items.name: Khalil Mack
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Chargers “still do not appear eager to sell players” ahead of the NFL trade deadline.
items.analysis: Fowler said he spoke to multiple executives around the league this week, and the general sentiment is that the Chargers are not interested in making any moves. Fowler wonders aloud whether Khalil Mack, who has generated “a lot of interest,” could be had for a fourth- or fifth-round pick. Mack, 35, certainly makes sense for contending teams. The 0-7 Chargers do not qualify as such.

items.name: Daniel Jones
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Daniel Jones “maybe wants to” be traded away from the Colts.
items.analysis: Fowler says that multiple sources around the league, including multiple sources inside the Colts’ organization, believe Jones “should be trying to get out of Indy, or maybe wants to.” The Colts are entering a rebuild, with trade rumors swirling around multiple star players. Fowler closed the segment by hinting at the Vikings as a possible landing spot. Jones’ fantasy-scoring outlook might tick up a little bit were he to head back to Minnesota.

items.name: Jordan Elliott
items.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports that Jordan Elliott will work out for the Bears next week.
items.analysis: Elliott was released by the Titans a couple of weeks ago due to an “incident” at their facility. Schultz says that Titans coach Robert Saleh has been an “advocate” for Elliott despite the team releasing him. Should they bring him aboard, the Bears would further solidify their interior defensive line after recently acquiring Jeffery Simmons.

items.name: Brandon Aiyuk
items.headline: Brandon Aiyuk’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said talks between him and the 49ers are “to be continued.”
items.analysis: Aiyuk and Rosenhaus met with the 49ers’ “big bosses” today to discuss an amicable solution to their multi-year conflict. Aiyuk seeks reinstatement, but under league rules, he owes th e 49ers roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture. The two sides met today, but evidently, things were not resolved. The saga continues. Stay tuned.

items.name: Kenny Gainwell
items.headline: Kenny Gainwell (hip) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Bears.
items.analysis: Gainwell has been a little more involved in recent weeks, and coach Todd Bowles recently told reporters that they are getting closer to the 1A/1B usage that they envisioned when they signed him. Gainwell will again play sidekick to Bucky Irving this week.

items.name: Tristan Wirfs
items.headline: Tristan Wirfs (toe) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Bears.
items.analysis: The Buccaneers will have their starting left tackle on hand when they take on the Bears’ ascending defensive line in Week 9. Wirfs is one of the best offensive tackles in football. Having him on the field is always a plus for Baker Mayfield.

items.name: George Pickens
items.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Colts.
items.analysis: Earlier today, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he is “hopeful” that Pickens will be available for this weekend’s game against the Colts. Pickens ended up being limited in practice all week and appears to be truly questionable to play. If active, he is a WR2 against a beatable Colts defense.

items.name: Rashee Rice
items.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) is not on the Chiefs’ final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Jets.
items.analysis: Rice posted a 7/53/1 receiving line against the Broncos last week. He got in a limited session on Wednesday before upgrading to full on Thursday. He seems to be recovering effectively from his summer knee procedure and in-season hamstring injury. Rice is a borderline WR1/2 for this weekend’s game against the Jets.

items.name: Travis Kelce
items.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) is not on the Chiefs’ final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Jets.
items.analysis: Kelce caught 5-of-7 targets for 67 yards, playing through the ankle injury last week against the Broncos, looking slightly hobbled. Kelce was limited to begin the week, but got in two full practices over the last two days. He remains firmly in the TE1 tier for Week 9 against the Jets.

items.name: Christian Darrisaw
items.headline: Christian Darrisaw (shoulder) practiced in full on Friday.
items.analysis: Darrisaw is now firmly on track to play in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game against the Bills, who field a tough, talented defensive line. Having Darrisaw on the field will be helpful for pocket passer Carson Wentz.

items.name: Quenton Nelson
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that “the plan” is for Quenton Nelson to avoid injured reserve after undergoing a procedure to remove cartilage fragments from his knee.
items.analysis: If the Seahawks were to place Nelson on short-term injured reserve, he would be required to miss at least four games. The Seahawks face the Cardinals this week, the Raiders next and then go on bye. Nelson could have a chance to play in Week 12 against the 49ers. His availability that week will likely just come down to how the recovery is going. His loss is unfortunate.

items.name: Michael Wilson
items.headline: Michael Wilson (NIR-rest/ribs) is not on the final injury report for Week 9 against the Seahawks.
items.analysis: Wilson caught 8-of-15 targets for 111 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals’ Week 8 win over the Cowboys while playing through a pair of broken ribs. The Cardinals kept him limited all week. He should be good to go for WR2 duties against the Seahawks’ elite defense this week.

items.name: Treylon Burks
items.headline: Commanders ruled out Treylon Burks (foot) for Week 9 against the Rams.
items.analysis: The Commanders’ wide receiver corps continues to lose players. Burks and Dyami Brown (calf) will both be sidelined this weekend, leaving Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams and Chig Okonkwo to operate as the top pass catchers.

items.name: Talanoa Hufanga
items.headline: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Panthers.
items.analysis: The Broncos’ talented safety might need another week to get his ankle healthy. Hufanga only logged two limited practice sessions this week. He has been sidelined since mid-October.

items.name: Pat Bryant
items.headline: Pat Bryant (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Panthers.
items.analysis: Bryant is expected to be activated from injured reserve by Saturday, but the team has officially listed him as questionable. He makes for a boom-bust FLEX in his first game back. The Broncos’ passing offense has struggled this season. Perhaps Bryant’s return lifts it up.

items.name: Dion Dawkins
items.headline: Dion Dawkins (ribs) did not practice on Friday.
items.analysis: Dawkins and starting LG Alec Anderson (ankle) have now missed two practices this week. This is concerning. The Bills face the Vikings’ elite, blitz-based defense in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game. Hopefully, the extra day off helps them return in time.

items.name: Keon Coleman
items.headline: Keon Coleman (shoulder) was limited on Friday.
items.analysis: Coleman’s fantasy-scoring outlook has been hurt by his teammate’s improving health. At this point, Coleman is more so a single-game DFS FLEX rather than a starter in 12-team re-draft formats. He should be good to go for Week 9’s Monday Night Football game though.

items.name: DJ Moore
items.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) was limited on Friday.
items.analysis: The Bills are managing Moore’s AC joint sprain fairly well. He should be expected to play in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game against the Vikings. Although it is a tough matchup, Moore remains the WR2 tier in this week’s final game.

items.name: Dalton Kincaid
items.headline: Dalton Kincaid (chest) practiced in full on Friday.
items.analysis: Kincaid remained limited in all three practices last week, so today’s return to full participation is great to see. The Vikings’ blitz-based defense often requires tight ends to stay in line to block, which could hurt Kincaid’s route volume. Regardless, he is too talented to be removed from the TE1 ranks.

items.name: David Njoku
items.headline: David Njoku (fibula) is doubtful to play in Week 9 against the Texans.
items.analysis: Njoku was limited all week, though he apparently is not ready to return from injured reserve. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats. The Chargers will likely employ a three-player rotation whenever he returns.

items.name: Reed Blankenship
items.headline: Texans ruled out Reed Blankenship (consussion/hand) for Week 9 against the Chargers.
items.analysis: The Texans will be without Blankenship this week, but they get Jalen Pitre (shoulder) back. The Texans’ defense has underperformed this year, as has the Chargers’ offense. Perhaps one of the units can facilitate a get-right outing for the other.

items.name: Christian Kirk
items.headline: 49ers ruled out Christian Kirk (knee) for Week 9 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: At this point, Kirk probably does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues. He returned from his lengthy calf injury only to injure his knee. It’s a tough break for the veteran wide receiver.

items.name: Demarcus Robinson
items.headline: Demarcus Robinson (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: If Robinson can make his return from injured reserve with Mike Evans (Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Christian Kirk (knee) sidelined, Robinson could end up returning WR3 value against the Raiders this week. Wide receiver-needy fantasy managers should add him now.

items.name: Deebo Samuel
items.headline: 49ers ruled out Deebo Samuel (hamstring) for Week 9 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Samuel, Mike Evans (Achilles) and Christian Kirk (knee) are all sidelined, potentially leaving Demarcus Robinson (ankle) as a featured receiver if he can play. Samuel can continue to be stashed on benches in 12-team leagues, though his return timeline remains somewhat opaque.

items.name: Mike Evans
items.headline: 49ers ruled out Mike Evans (Achilles) for Week 9 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Evans is dealing with tendinitis in his Achilles tendon that initially cropped up in Week 6. When speaking with the media earlier this week, general manager John Lynch said the team hopes to get Evans back in the “coming weeks,” which means he should tentatively be considered questionable to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys.

items.name: Nick Bosa
items.headline: Nick Bosa (calf/knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: Bosa strained his calf while going through his pre-practice warm-up routine before Week 3’s Thursday practice, and has not played since. He has also dealt with knee tendinitis. Bosa is finally cleared to return following the 49ers’ Week 8 bye.

items.name: Christian McCaffrey
items.headline: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: McCaffrey injured his hamstring in Week 7. The 49ers were on bye in Week 8, giving him extra time to rest. McCaffrey then sat out on Wednesday before practicing in a limited capacity on Thursday. He should be in fantasy football lineups this week, facing a soft Raiders run defense, but Kaelon Black could mix in for 8-10 touches, potentially warranting FLEX consideration.

items.name: Terrance Ferguson
items.headline: Rams ruled out Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) for Week 9 against the Commanders.
items.analysis: Ferguson was set to make his return from injured reserve, having rehabilitated his early-season ankle injury. Unfortunately, he strained his hamstring in practice today and has now been ruled out. With Colby Parkinson (ribs) questionable, Tyler Higbee sneaks back into the TE1 conversation.

items.name: Drew Lock
items.headline: Drew Lock (elbow) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Lock has dealt with an injury in his throwing-arm elbow for multiple weeks. He was limited at each Week 9 practice, but told reporters that he was feeling good late on Wednesday. It is tough to say whether this will impact him on game day, but he warrants QB2 treatment against the Cardinals’ soft defense.

items.name: Rashid Shaheed
items.headline: Seahawks ruled out Rashid Shaheed (knee) for Week 9 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: The Seahawks will again be without their speedy, underused wide receiver. Fortunately, Tory Horton (hand) was removed from the injury report and will play this week. He will catch passes thrown by Drew Lock (elbow).

items.name: Quenton Nelson
items.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Quenton Nelson (knee) will have a minor procedure and is week-to-week.
items.analysis: Apparently, Nelson was dealing with this knee issue when Seattle acquired for him, and he recently “aggravated it to some degree.” FOX 59’s Mike Chappell notes that Nelson was never listed on the Colts’ injury report this season. This is a bummer for the Seahawks, who acquired Nelson as a win-now move. Nelson will not play in Week 9 against the Cardinals, and the Seahawks also ruled out LT Charles Cross (ankle), DT Leonard Williams (stinger) and LB Uchenna Nwosu (ankle).

items.name: Mason Taylor
items.headline: Mason Taylor (back) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: Taylor’s contributions are far too volatile for him to be trusted in 12-team formats, but his presence hurts rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq’s fantasy-scoring outlook. Taylor does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

items.name: Sione Vaki
items.headline: Sione Vaki (ankle) is questionable for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Vaki and Lions RB3 Jacob Saylors (neck) are both questionable. Vaki did not practice on Friday, having apparently suffered a new injury. Saylors was limited all week. Jahmyr Gibbs should handle his normal, sizable workload.

items.name: Cade Mays
items.headline: Lions ruled out Cade Mays (ankle) for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Brutal. Mays returned from injured reserve in Week 7 due to a preseason wrist injury. He injured his ankle in Week 8. The Lions ruled out S Kerby Joseph (knee) and CB D.J. Reed (hip), yet S Brian Branch (concussion) will play.

items.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
items.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: St. Brown rarely misses games due to injuries. Fantasy managers should remain optimistic about his availability. The Lions’ No. 1 wide receiver remained limited all week. Although it might hurt to take hits, we expect St. Brown to suit up this weekend. Regardless, keeping it locked to Rotoworld is a must. Updates will be provided as they roll in.

items.name: Jaylen Wright
items.headline: Jaylen Wright (quad) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Wright and Dolphins RB3 Kaytron Allen (quad) are both questionable in this one, though Allen upgraded to full participation on Friday while Wright remained limited. Wright is barely worthy of stashing in 12-team leagues.

items.name: Jaelan Phillips
items.headline: Panthers ruled out Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) for Week 9 against the Broncos.
items.analysis: Phillips did not practice at all this week, after sitting out the Panthers’ last two games. Losing a key edge rusher will make things harder for the Panthers’ defense. Bo Nix should have decently comfortable pockets, though.

items.name: Malik Nabers
items.headline: Malik Nabers (knee) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Eagles.
items.analysis: The Giants have smartly limited Nabers’ practice participation levels at times this season, allowing him to play very well while returning from last year’s season-ending knee injury. Nabers belongs in fantasy football lineups in this divisional showdown, as usual.

items.name: Cam Skattebo
items.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is doubtful to play in Week 9 against the Eagles.
items.analysis: Giants coach John Harbaugh told reporters earlier this week that Skattebo is day-to-day. Unfortunately, Skattebo only got in one limited session on Friday. Fantasy managers should expect Devin Singletary to get the start this week. He can be treated as a volume-based FLEX.

items.name: Jihaad Campbell
items.headline: Eagles ruled out Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) for Week 9 against the Giants.
items.analysis: Campbell will now miss another game, beset by upper-leg injuries. The Eagles also ruled out DBs Michael Carter (abdomen) and Jonathan Jones (hamstring). The Eagles still have talented players available, but the defense is a little banged up.

items.name: Jake Elliott
items.headline: Jake Elliott (ankle) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Giants.
items.analysis: The Eagles’ kicker practiced in full today, which was good to see. Given the state of the Eagles’ offense, he may not have many field goal attempts this week, though. Kickers tend to benefit from playing on teams with stellar offenses. The Eagles no longer have one.

items.name: Dontayvion Wicks
items.headline: Eagles ruled out Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) for Week 9 against the Giants.
items.analysis: Wicks and DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will both miss this weekend’s game, before taking the week off next week as well. The Eagles go on bye in Week 10. Hopefully, the added rest will allow Wicks to be healthy down the stretch.

items.name: Saquon Barkley
items.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) is not on the final injury report for Week 9 against the Giants.
items.analysis: Barkley will again play through his hamstring and back injuries. Touchdowns have helped offset Barkley’s moderate yardage totals, and the offense will now be led by Joe Milton. Barkley’s role and talent keep him in the high-end RB2 tier, though an apex outcome is perhaps unlikely, given the state of the Eagles’ offense.

items.name: DeVonta Smith
items.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Giants.
items.analysis: As expected, Smith will miss another week after not being able to practice due to his ankle troubles. The 27-year-old wideout could be an option after the Week 10 bye, but nothing is certain. The Eagles’ passing attack should be completely avoided for their divisional showdown with New York.

items.name: Christian Watson
items.headline: Christian Watson is off the injury report for Week 9 against the Patriots.
items.analysis: Watson got in a pair of limited practices after leaving in Week 8 against the Panthers with a rib injury that required a trip to the hospital. The 6-foot-4 wideout is a WR1 for the upcoming battle against New England.

items.name: Micah Parsons
items.headline: Micah Parsons (knee) was ruled out for Week 9 against the Patriots.
items.analysis: Parsons was cleared to resume individual activities but was never likely to play against the Pats this week. The next chance for Parsons to play will be Week 10 against the Vikings, and there’s at least a smidgen of optimism he could be back for that contest.

items.name: MarShawn Lloyd
items.headline: MarShawn Lloyd (knee) is questionable for Week 9 against the Patriots.
items.analysis: Lloyd popped up on Thursday’s injury report with the knee issue, and now appears to be a game-time decision. Chris Brooks (ankle) is also questionable for the Week 9 tilt, so there could be depth issues for the Pack behind Josh Jacobs, who has struggled in his return to action as well.

items.name: Alvin Kamara
items.headline: Alvin Kamara has no injury designation for Week 9 against the Browns.
items.analysis: Kamara was limited due to rest and a back injury, but unsurprisingly, he’ll be good to go for Sunday’s contest against the Browns. The Saints’ run game is a disaster, but Kamara should be involved enough in the pass game to make him a decent FLEX play for that contest.

items.name: Derrick Brown
items.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that the NFL’s defensive tackle market “has been hot,” and teams “might” try to trade for Derrick Brown.
items.analysis: The Panthers are “not actively looking to move” Brown, but Breer says they have considered it. Other defensive tackles on other teams who have come up in trade talks include Grover Stewart, Davon Godchaux, Nathan Shepherd, Christian Barmore and Bobby Brown. The Dolphins have told teams they are not interested in trading away Zach Sieler.

items.name: Jauan Jennings
items.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) was not seen practicing on Friday.
items.analysis: Jennings was limited yesterday, which could mean he injured his calf during the Vikings’ Thursday practice. If this is the case, he is probably unlikely to suit up for his team’s Monday Night Football game against the Bills.

items.name: Josh Downs
items.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that Josh Downs “leads the wide receiver market” ahead of the NFL trade deadline.
items.analysis: Downs’ 2026 season has fallen short of expectations, but perhaps he has a chance to rebound. Breer believes acquiring Downs would “probably” cost a fourth-round pick. He is “one of a number of receivers on the market” at the moment, with the Chiefs and Steelers among the teams looking for help at the position. Breer adds that the 49ers are “open” to adding a wide receiver as well, but with their positional health improving, San Francisco is “less desperate than they were a couple of weeks ago.” The Steelers’ wide receiver corps might be too muddled for Downs to meaningfully increase his productivity, but landing in Kansas City or San Francisco would likely be good for him.

items.name: Emeka Egbuka
items.headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) is listed as questionable for Week 9 against the Bears.
items.analysis: Egbuka was able to get in another full practice Friday after getting the same Thursday, so it seems like he’s on the right side of the questionable tag, even with coach Todd Bowles suggesting he’ll be a game-time decision. The 24-year-old wideout is on the WR2/WR3 range for the Sunday Night Football showdown against Chicago if he is able to go.

items.name: Denzel Boston
items.headline: Denzel Boston (calf) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Boston will once again play through a lower-body injury. The rookie downfield wide receiver has played unproductively as of late, but he remains a threat to rip off a long gain. He will be catching passes from Shedeur Sanders this weekend. Hopefully, the two form a strong connection quickly.

items.name: KaVontae Turpin
items.headline: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) was ruled out for Week 9 against the Colts.
items.analysis: This will be a third-straight missed game for Turpin as he battles his rib issue. The 30-year-old has just seven targets on the season, but will again be missed by Dallas in the return game. Malachi Lawrence has also been ruled out by the Cowboys due to his ankle injury.

items.name: Jake Ferguson
items.headline: Jake Ferguson (ankle) is listed as questionable for Week 9 against the Colts.
items.analysis: Ferguson wasn’t able to practice Wednesday or Thursday, but he was able to get in a limited session Friday to give him at least a chance to play Friday. Luke Schoonmaker (groin) was also listed as questionable with limited practices all week. If Ferguson is able to play, he’s in the TE2 vicinity against Indianapolis.

items.name: Brian Thomas
items.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that the Jaguars “have been less inclined” to trade away Brian Thomas.
items.analysis: Breer and NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe put out similar reports today, indicating that the Jaguars are now hesitant to trade away Thomas. Per Breer, Thomas is not the best fit for coach Liam Coen’s scheme, but he “brings a downfield element that’s really important in keeping defenses honest against the run, and opening things up underneath for Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington.” Wolfe echoed Breer’s downfield sentiment and added that when the Jaguars traded away Tyson Campbell last year, it had a negative impact on the locker room — and Jaguars brass has “learned from it.” Thomas and Travis Hunter are reportedly close friends, and Thomas is liked in the locker room. It sounds like the formerly productive wide receiver might be staying put. Breer lists the Chiefs and Steelers, and the 49ers to a lesser degree, as the teams known to be seeking wide receiver help.

items.name: Kyle Monangai
items.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) returned to practice Friday.
items.analysis: The Bears are calling the tailback questionable for Week 9 against the Buccaneers. It’s the first time that Monangai has been able to practice picking up the injury a month ago against the Jets. It seems extremely unlikely that the 24-year-old will be able to play against Tampa Bay on Sunday night, but he appears to be on track to return after the Week 10 bye for the final stretch. Malik Muhammed and Tyrique Stevenson are also questionable for the Sunday Night showdown.

items.name: Jonathan Taylor
items.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that the Giants are serious suitors for Jonathan Taylor, while the Broncos and Vikings might be less inclined to acquire him.
items.analysis: All three teams have inquired about Taylor’s trade cost. Per Breer, the Colts either want a first-round pick or a draft pick package similar to what the Panthers received for Christian McCaffrey in 2023. The 49ers handed over 2023 second-, third- and fourth-round picks, and a 2024 fifth-rounder to acquire him. None of the three suitors have met either asking price yet. That said, the Giants have reportedly offered enough for Breer to label them “a serious suitor.” Stay tuned.

items.name: Colby Parkinson
items.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Commanders.
items.analysis: Parkinson sat out on Wednesday and Thursday. His Friday participation level has not yet been released, but he is probably on the wrong side of questionable at this time. Parkinson does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues, especially with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) expected to play.

items.name: Jordan Whittington
items.headline: Jordan Whittington (back) is questionable for Week 9 against the Commanders.
items.analysis: Whittington has just two catches on the season, and with head coach Sean McVay suggesting he wants to get Tutu Atwell more involved, it seems unlikely Whittington will have a role as more than a returner even if he can play against Washington come Sunday. Trent McDuffie (back) is also questionable for that contest, and won’t practice Friday.

items.name: Kelvin Banks
items.headline: Kelvin Banks (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Browns.
items.analysis: Banks, the Saints’ talented left tackle, has a chance to return from injured reserve this week. He underwent surgery earlier this year to address a high-ankle sprain. Banks’ backup, Asim Richards (thum), is also questionable to play. Hopefully, at least one of them is good to go.

items.name: Terrance Ferguson
items.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters that Terrance Ferguson (ankle) is expected to play in Week 9 against the Commanders.
items.analysis: Ferguson will be able to play for the first time since he suffered his medial ankle sprain in Week 3. The second-year tight end offers some volatility, but there’s no denying that there’s upside in his profile. Just don’t be shocked if it isn’t on full display just yet in Week 9.

items.name: Myles Garrett
items.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters Friday that Myles Garrett (knee) is expected to play against the Commanders in Week 9.
items.analysis: Garrett will need to come off injured reserve, with the Rams likely making that transaction closer to gametime. The 30-year-old has been as good as any defensive player in football, and for the first time he’ll get to be on the same field as Aaron Donald as teammates. Best of luck, Commanders’ offensive line.

items.name: Jordyn Tyson
items.headline: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Browns.
items.analysis: We do not yet know Tyson’s participation level at Friday’s practice, but he remained limited on Wednesday and Thursday. It seems like he may need another week before he makes his NFL debut, but we don’t know for sure. If active, Tyson would be FLEX-viable. It is possible the team initially keeps him on a snap count.

items.name: CJ Donaldson
items.headline: CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Browns.
items.analysis: Donaldson wasn’t able to practice again Friday, and the 22-year-old tailback won’t be available for the Week 9 skirmish against Cleveland. Alvin Kamara will likely be the top option — and would have been even if Donaldson could play — in that contest, assuming his back injury allows him to play, of course. This is not a great situation, folks.

items.name: Harold Fannin
items.headline: Harold Fannin was removed from the injury report Friday prior to Week 9 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Fanning popped up on the report with a groin injury, and there was some added concern because that’s the injury that slowed him during his rookie campaign. The removal brings a sigh of relief for fantasy managers, and Fannin could be in for a big day — at least in terms of targets — with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback for Sunday against New Orleans.

items.name: Deshaun Watson
items.headline: Deshaun Watson (concussion) will not start in Week 9 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Head coach Todd Monken said Watson will be questionable for Sunday’s game, but has already said Shedeur Sanders will make his first start of the season. Watson missed Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices but was upgraded to a limited participant on Friday, although he has yet to clear concussion protocol. The decision to start Sanders likely stems from him working with the first-team offense during the week and the unlikelihood of Watson clearing protocol in time for Sunday’s game.

items.name: Shedeur Sanders
items.headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said Shedeur Sanders will start in Week 9 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Sanders will draw the start as Deshaun Watson (concussion) has yet to clear protocol in time to be ready for Sunday’s game. Interestingly, Watson is still expected to be listed as questionable, per Monken, but Sanders will draw the start. We are assuming this decision is based on Sanders taking first-team reps after Watson missed each of the first two days of practice, but this is a nice opportunity for Sanders to show whatever growth he has made since a tough rookie season in which he threw for 1,440 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 interceptions in eight games played. He’ll be on the low-end QB2 radar on the road against the Saints, who rank 16th in fantasy points allowed to opposing QBs this season.

items.name: Hunter Henry
items.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) has been ruled questionable for Week 9 against the Packers.
items.analysis: The Patriots are down A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) on top of their other skill-position issues, so if Henry can go, he could see a considerable amount of targets against the Packers. He didn’t practice Wednesday or Thursday, however, so it seems unlikely. Eli Raridon is inline to be the top tight end option if Henry can’t play.

items.name: TreVeyon Henderson
items.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Packers.
items.analysis: It seemed pretty obvious that Henderson wasn’t going to play Sunday after it was announced the second-year runner was dealing with “neurological symptoms” but it’s now official. There are much bigger things than football going on in his life. While he gets better, Corey Kiner should be the backup running back behind Rhamondre Stevenson going forward.

items.name: Bryce Young
items.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Bryce Young (ankle) will play in Week 9 against the Broncos.
items.analysis: Young never really felt like he was at risk of missing this week. Despite dealing with an ankle injury, the Panthers’ QB1 was listed as a full participant in practice throughout the week and will be good to go despite what appears to be a minor ankle injury. Young draws a tough Week 9 matchup at home against the Broncos and has thrown two touchdowns and three interceptions in his last two games, and has completed below 60 percent of his passes in his last three outings. He’ll be a risky QB2 this week.

items.name: A.J. Brown
items.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Packers.
items.analysis: Brown was unable to practice again Friday, and the 29-year-old will not be able to roll against the Green Bay secondary. It’s a second-consecutive missed game for Brown, who has played in just three games since his blockbuster deal to the Patriots prior to the season. DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams will be Drake Maye’s top wideout targets for the game against Green Bay. Not ideal.

items.name: Zonovan Knight
items.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Bam Knight (concussion) will not play in Week 9 against the Seahawks.
items.analysis: LaFleur also ruled out OL Jon Gaines II (ankle) and OT Jayden Williams (knee). Knight has been a DNP all week after suffering a concussion in Week 8’s win over the Cowboys and will officially be sidelined for Week 9. His absence, along with Jeremiyah Love’s (ankle) could create a bell cow role for Tyler Allgeier, who totaled 191 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns in last week’s win, while fourth-year vet Evan Hull could also work into the mix. Allgeier’s volume alone will put him in the RB2 conversation this week despite the tough matchup.

items.name: Myles Garrett
items.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Myles Garrett (knee) “is on track to be activated ahead of Sunday vs. the Commanders.”
items.analysis: Garrett has practiced all week and will likely be activated in the next 24 to 48 hours. The star pass-rusher who was acquired by the Rams in a blockbuster trade this offseason played in just one game for the Rams this season and did not record a tackle. Now, after undergoing knee surgery to correct a nagging injury, Garrett is all but set to return against the Commanders after missing seven straight games. His return will provide a much-needed boost to a Rams defense that ranks near the bottom of the league in sacks (12) through the first half of the season.

items.name: Malik Nabers
items.headline: Malik Nabers (knee) returned to practice on Friday.
items.analysis: Nabers was a surprise DNP with a knee injury on Thursday, but said after practice that he expected to play. His return to the field on Friday suggests he will be good to go for Sunday’s game against the Eagles, but we will still check in with a final status when the Giants announce player designations for the weekend. Assuming he is good to go, Nabers should be treated as a normal must-start receiver against a down-bad Eagles team.

items.name: DJ Turner
items.headline: DJ Turner (heel) will play in the Bengals’ Week 9 game against the Falcons.
items.analysis: After being upgraded to a full participant in Thursday’s practice, Turner was officially removed from the injury report on Friday, meaning he will be good to go for Sunday’s international tilt against the Falcons. Turner has allowed 16 receptions for 133 yards and one touchdown on 26 targets this season, per PFF, earning a coverage grade of 72.9.

items.name: Breece Hall
items.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) will play in Week 9 against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: This comes a day after Hall said he expects to play, so this news isn’t all too surprising. Hall’s return could somewhat complicate the Jets’ backfield situation on Sunday, however, as Braelon Allen has played well in Hall’s absence, making a strong case for more touches even when Hall is healthy. Glenn declined to get into how he plans to divvy up his running backs’ touches next week, saying “both guys will play,” when asked about his plans. This was already shaping up to be a tough fantasy matchup on the road against the Chiefs, but a potential backfield split would only further complicate matters. Until we see how things shake out, both Hall and Allen should be viewed as mid-to-low-end RB2s.

items.name: Kadyn Proctor
items.headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said Kadyn Proctor cleared concussion protocol and will play in Week 9 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Proctor missed last week’s game against the Patriots with a brain injury, but will be back in his normal left guard position for this week’s game against the Lions. In six games this season, Proctor has appeared on more than 350 offensive snaps, earning a PFF grade of 64.8 while allowing one sack and 13 pressures.

items.name: Jacoby Brissett
items.headline: The Ravens and Cardinals finalized a trade on Friday that sends Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore.
items.analysis: We already knew this deal would be done, but the two sides made things official on Friday. The Ravens will receive Brissett, along with a 2027 fifth-round pick from the Cardinals in exchange for a 2027 4th-round pick and a 2028 7th-round pick. Brissett will immediately step into a starting role for the Ravens when they face the Chargers in Week 10 and should provide an immediate upgrade over Joe Fagnano, who struggled mightily in his first career start against the Jaguars.

items.name: Garrett Wilson
items.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Garrett Wilson (concussion) will not play in Week 9 against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: Wilson has not practiced this week and has now been ruled out for Sunday’s game against the Chiefs. Wilson has caught 43 passes for 527 yards and three touchdowns this season and saw 12 targets in last week’s loss to the Raiders. His absence means both Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper should see expanded roles, but both players will be hard to trust as anything more than WR3s against a stout Chiefs defense. In addition to Wilson, the Jets also ruled out LB Trevin Wallace (groin) for Week 9.

items.name: TreVeyon Henderson
items.headline: TreVeyon Henderson released a statement saying that he was dealing with an “unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days.”
items.analysis: This certainly sounds like a scary situation for Henderson, whose absence has been the subject of speculation for nearly two weeks. Henderson said that the results of “comprehensive medical testing have come back positive and reassuring, but he continues to work with specialists and physical therapists. Henderson said these issues have affected his “strength, coordination, and some of [his] physical functions,” while adding that he is working to return to full health. While we don’t want to speculate too much, it doesn’t sound like Henderson will be back anytime soon. Hopefully we will get more clarity on his situation soon, but our thoughts are with him and his continued recovery.

items.name: George Pickens
items.headline: Speaking on 105.3 The Fan, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said he is “hopeful” George Pickens (hamstring) will play in Week 9 against the Colts.
items.analysis: Pickens has been limited in each of the Cowboys’ first two practices to start the week, which would seem to be a good sign for his Week 9 availability. We’ll get a better sense of where things stand when the Cowboys release their final injury report on Friday and give Pickens a designation heading into the weekend, but Schottenheimer’s optimism is a good sign. Owner Jerry Jones advocated for Pickens getting the ball more this week after Week 8’s loss to the Cardinals, so if he is active, the star receiver could be primed for a bit of a squeaky wheel game in a plus matchup against the Colts.

items.name: Deshaun Watson
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Deshaun Watson (concussion) is “unlikely to start” in Week 9 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Watson has not practiced this week due to concussion symptoms he has been dealing with since Week 8’s loss to the Steelers. Unless he surprisingly clears concussion protocol this week, Watson will miss Week 9, paving the way for Shedeur Sanders to make his first start of the season. We will have official word on Watson’s status in a few hours, but at this point, it would be surprising if he does start.

items.name: Brandon Aiyuk
items.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Brandon Aiyuk owes the 49ers “roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture,” which could delay his return.
items.analysis: Pelissero calls this a “potential complication in [Aiyuk’s] efforts to secure his release by reporting to the facility Friday.” While it’s possible both sides reach a deal for Aiyuk to pay back that money, which would make this a non-issue, Pelissero said this could also end up going to arbitration, which may delay things. Aiyuk is scheduled to report to the 49ers’ facilities today, so we could have our answer in the next few hours about when this situation is resolved and Aiyuk has been granted his release. Aiyuk recently hired Drew Rosenhaus with the hopes of being reinstated into the league and with a new team soon. The 28-year-old last played in 2024.

items.name: James Pearce
items.headline: James Pearce is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Bengals.
items.analysis: Pearce’s status is related to a back injury that apparently flared up in Friday’s practice, per head coach Kevin Stefanski. Pearce was a full participant in practice, and teams said he will operate on a pitch count, so it seems highly unlikely he will be scratched on game day. In addition to Pearce, the Falcons also listed LB Yasir Abdullah (hamstring), WR Beaux Collins (hip), LB Divine Deablo (forearm), and OT Cameron Williams (ankle) as questionable for Week 9.

items.name: Brian Robinson
items.headline: Brian Robinson (hamstring) is questionable for the Falcons’ Week 9 game against the Bengals.
items.analysis: Robinson was briefly listed as questionable only for head coach Kevin Stefanski to rule him out shortly after the initial report. Robinson was limited in practice throughout the week, but the Falcons are opting to play it safe, likely hoping another week on the sidelines will lower the chances of re-injury. Rookie WR Zachariah Branch (hamstring) has also been ruled out for the game after picking up an injury in last week’s loss to the Buccaneers.

items.name: Mark Andrews
items.headline: Mark Andrews caught both targets for 19 yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Andrews, somewhat disgustingly, led the team in receiving with a modest 19 yards on a night undrafted free agent rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano threw for only 60 yards in his first career start. It remains difficult to start the veteran tight end, who has made more mental mistakes this season than he has receptions.

items.name: Zay Flowers
items.headline: Zay Flowers caught 3-of-6 targets for six yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars, adding 17 yards on three carries.
items.analysis: Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle did what he could to overcome undrafted free agent rookie Joe Fagnano under center, routinely putting Flowers in Motion across the formation to generate some level of misdirection for an offense with zero ability to attack downfield. That included three rush attempts and a completion thrown by running back Derrick Henry, but it wasn’t enough to salvage a usable fantasy week for the electric receiver. Fantasy managers can rest easy knowing help is on the way in the form of veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who was signed earlier in the week and will likely make his team debut when the Ravens take on the Chargers in Week 10. Flowers will return to upside WR2 range with the change at quarterback.

items.name: Derrick Henry
items.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 17 times for 57 yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle did everything in his power to overcome an undrafted free agent rookie quarterback in his first professional start, going so far as to call numerous direct snaps to Henry and a Henry pass attempt, but it ultimately proved futile. Things appeared to be trending in the right direction as the Ravens played the Jaguars to a tightly contested game through the first 29 minutes before Parker Washington broke the game open with a 50-yard touchdown in the final minute before the break. Things got nasty for Henry after the half as he managed only two additional yards after bruising his way to 55 first half yards. Henry will return to RB1 status in fantasy circles in Week 10 when the Ravens take on the Chargers.

items.name: Justice Hill
items.headline: Justice Hill rushed nine times for 85 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars, adding seven yards on three receptions.
items.analysis: Hill became the first running back to amass more than 75 yards against the Jaguars since the start of the 2025 regular season with a 65-yard touchdown with the game well out of hand in the second half. It was an otherwise poor showing for the entirety of the Baltimore offense with a rookie undrafted free agent starting his first NFL game. Hill remains nothing more than a desperation FLEX ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Chargers.

items.name: Joe Fagnano
items.headline: Joe Fagnano completed 10-of-18 passes for 60 yards and two interceptions in the Ravens’ 33-10, Week 9 loss to the Jaguars, adding 13 yards on three carries.
items.analysis: Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle did everything he could to scheme around a starting undrafted free agent rookie quarterback in his first NFL start, calling numerous exotic looks to include direct snaps to Derrick Henry, a Henry pass attempt, quick outs to Zay Flowers, Flowers rush attempts, and flea flickers, but it wasn’t enough to overcome poor execution, consistently off-target throws, and a lack of downfield ability. The Ravens also committed numerous pre-snap penalties as they continue to lead the league in that area through nine weeks, which killed multiple drives. Fagnano managed only 25 pass yards in the first half, finishing with a ridiculous 60 yards, while both interceptions came in the second half with the team in desperation mode. Fagnano leaves his first, and likely last, NFL start with a sour taste in his mouth, as he likely retreats to backup duties following the signing of veteran Jacoby Brissett earlier in the week.

items.name: Brenton Strange
items.headline: Brenton Strange caught both targets for 22 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
items.analysis: Strange was overshadowed by the 52-yard reception from fellow tight end Nate Boerkircher on the team’s opening possession, but he made a really nice grab in triple coverage over the middle of the field to set up the team’s second score of the game. Strange remains unlikely to see consistent volume for as long as the Jaguars continue to so handily control games, something that appears likely to continue given the team holds the weakest strength of schedule for the remainder of the regular season. Fantasy managers likely have better options ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Titans.

items.name: Parker Washington
items.headline: Parker Washington caught 2-of-7 targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
items.analysis: Both of Washington’s receptions came before the break, the second of which was a 50-yard touchdown on a double-move slant against Cover-0 with under one minute remaining before the half. Washington remains one of the most efficient receivers in the league but consistently positive game scripts have left the overall pass volume lacking, particularly in the second half this season. He remains an upside WR2 ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Titans.

items.name: Jakobi Meyers
items.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 4-of-6 targets for 65 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
items.analysis: All four of Meyers’ receptions came before the half in what remained a tighter game until just before the half, when alpha wide receiver Parker Washington took a simple slant for a 50-yard touchdown with under a minute remaining before the break. As has been the case on numerous occasions this season, Jacksonville coasted in the second half, limiting overall pass volume after the break. Meyers narrowly missed his first touchdown since Week 3 as he was tackled at the one on the team’s first possession. He remains a viable FLEX option ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Titans.

items.name: Chris Rodriguez
items.headline: Chris Rodriguez rushed 10 times for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens, adding 13 yards on two receptions.
items.analysis: Rodriguez split time with lead back Bhayshul Tuten in the first half before soaking up most of the backfield work in the third quarter. Both backs would then cede primary duties to special team ace Ameer Abdullah in the fourth quarter when the game was well in hand. Rodriguez has seen his fantasy value plummet of late with the emergence of Tuten as a borderline workhorse, a situation that was heavily influenced by Tuten’s lack of practice ahead of Thursday Night Football. The long week appears likely to provide the time needed for Tuten to return to full strength, leaving Rodriguez as a touchdown-dependent FLEX when the Jaguars face the Titans in Week 10.

items.name: Bhayshul Tuten
items.headline: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 12 times for 29 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
items.analysis: Tuten started after failing to practice in any capacity this week, capping off the opening drive with a score from one yard out. He would split time with Chris Rodriguez for the rest of the first half before giving way to the combination of Rodriguez and special teams ace Ameer Abdullah for the bulk of the second half with the game in hand. Tuten should see his volume tick back up toward lead back territory when the Jaguars face off against the Titans in Week 10, where he will return to RB2 status.

items.name: Trevor Lawrence
items.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 16-of-26 passes for 242 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ 33-10, Week 9 win over the Ravens.
items.analysis: It was business as usual for Lawrence and the Jaguars, who won their eighth game by 20 or more points since the start of the 2025 season, the most in the league during that span. Lawrence looked sharp throughout, starting things off with a touchdown drive on their opening possession that was sparked by a 52-yard completion to tight end Nate Boerkircher. He would hit Parker Washington on a slant for a 50-yard touchdown in the final minute before the half to push the lead to 17-3, with a flurry of second half field goals enough to chase the reeling Ravens from the field. In standard Jacksonville fashion, positive game script capped Lawrence’s aerial volume, something fantasy managers have both gotten used to through the mid way point in the season and will likely see continue considering the Jaguars hold the league’s softest remaining strength of schedule. The win pushes the Jaguars to 6-2 and extends their lead in the AFC South ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the one-win Titans, where Lawrence will remain a back end QB1 due to lack of volume.

items.name: Lamar Jackson
items.headline: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reports that the Ravens are willing to make Lamar Jackson the highest-paid player in NFL history.
items.analysis: Well, that’s good, because it will assuredly take a record-setting deal to keep him in a Ravens uniform. Jackson has an $84.34 million salary cap hit next season, so the team has to do something with his contract. Jackson has a no-trade clause and a no-franchise tag clause — he possesses a ton of leverage. Per Palmer, the two sides will not negotiate a new deal in-season, so they will try to get something done between the end of the season and the beginning of free agency, which starts in March 2027.

items.name: Michael Wilson
items.headline: Michael Wilson (NIR-rest/ribs) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Wilson will face the Seahawks this weekend, barring a setback. It’s a tough matchup, but Wilson’s target volume keeps him worth of remaining in starting lineups. Wilson showed decent chemistry with Gardner Minshew last week, which was nice to see, now that Jacoby Brissett is headed to the Ravens.

items.name: Rashid Shaheed
items.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Shaheed seems likely to miss another week, though he could technically still turn things around tomorrow. Seahawks LT Charles Cross (ankle) also remains sidelined on Thursday, and LG Quenton Nelson (knee) was downgraded to a non-participant. Hopefully, Nelson’s absence is precautionary.

items.name: Drew Lock
items.headline: Drew Lock (elbow) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Lock has been dealing with an injury in his throwing arm since Week 7, but he told reporters that he is feeling good now. Lock played very well as Sam Darnold’s replacement earlier this year. As long as the elbow holds up, Lock should be expected to do so again. He is a viable QB2.

items.name: Jordyn Tyson
items.headline: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: The Saints’ first-round rookie is now on the wrong side of questionable. It would have been nice to see him practice in full today. That said, New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill commented positively on Tyson’s performance, saying Tyson “does not look limited.”

items.name: Alvin Kamara
items.headline: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: The way the team listed Kamara indicates that the back injury will not keep him from playing, but he is clearly still hurt. Kamara has been entirely ineffective this season and can only be viewed as a touchdown-dependent FLEX. CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) was unable to practice today.

items.name: Myles Garrett
items.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) limited again on Thursday.
items.analysis: Garrett has a chance to face the Commanders this week, but he still belongs in the questionable column at this time. Rams CB1 Trent McDuffie (back) and S Kam Curl (foot) both missed practice for the second time this week.

items.name: Matthew Stafford
items.headline: Matthew Stafford (right elbow) practiced in full on Thursday.
items.analysis: Stafford has downplayed inquiries regarding his throwing-arm injury, saying he’s been icing his elbow post-game and post-practice for a while now — and he called out the beat reporters for missing it. Lingering elbow soreness isn’t exactly reassuring, but at least he is practicing fully. Stafford should be good to go for the Rams’ Week 9 game against the Commanders, but this is obviously worth monitoring.

items.name: David Njoku
items.headline: David Njoku (fibula) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Njoku’s return is probably a good thing for the offense as a whole, but the Chargers’ tight end rotation makes for a fantasy-unfriendly situation. Njoku does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats. Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) remains sidelined.

items.name: Treylon Burks
items.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: The Commanders’ thin wide receiver corps could get thinner. Burks, the team’s top downfield receiver, is on the wrong side of questionable for this week’s game against the Rams. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

items.name: Adam Randall
items.headline: Ravens did not activate Adam Randall (neck) from injured reserve for Week 9 against the Jaguars.
items.analysis: The Ravens’ rookie running back will have to wait to make his debut. The Ravens declared QB Kedon Slovis, WR Elijah Sarratt, OL Emery Jones Jr., DL Aeneas Peebles, CB Nate Wiggins and S Jaylinn Hawkins inactive. Hawkins is dealing with a knee injury and Wiggins, the Ravens’ No. 1 cornerback, is listed with a stinger and an illness. Slovis will serve as the emergency third quarterback. Austin Reed is the QB2. Ravens RG Vega Ioane (knee) will play.

items.name: Travon Walker
items.headline: Travon Walker (ribs) is active for Week 9 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: The Jaguars’ No. 2 edge rusher will play through his ribs injury tonight. He apparently got hurt during Tuesday’s practice, but is good to go two days later. The Jaguars declared WR CJ Williams, CB Alijah Huzzie, S Cam’Ron Silmon-Craig and DE Wesley Williams inactive for Week 9 against the Ravens.

items.name: Moro Ojomo
items.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that the Eagles have received “a ton of interest” on the trade market for Moro Ojomo.
items.analysis: Ojomo is in a contract year, and per Breer, the Eagles have told interested parties that they would like to keep him beyond this year. With both Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis signed for multiple seasons, investing heavily in another defensive tackle might be cost-prohibitive. Perhaps the Eagles are simply trying to drive up Ojomo’s trade value. Stay tuned.

items.name: Tony Pollard
items.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer thinks the Titans might be willing to trade away Tony Pollard in exchange for a fourth-round pick.
items.analysis: Breer believes a fourth-round pick “seems like a lot” to give up for an aging running back who is set to enter free agency at the end of the year. So, Pollard might end up staying in Tennessee. Breer adds that the Titans could also consider trading away Calvin Ridley for a worse Day 3 pick, but he isn’t sure if the team is eager to get rid of pass catchers while they are attempting to develop their young quarterback.

items.name: Bhayshul Tuten
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) is “good to go” after completing his pre-game workout for Week 9 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: The Jaguars have routinely killed the clock with their efficient ground game this season, oftentimes pulling Trevor Lawrence early. With the Ravens starting QB Joe Fagnano (ankle) tonight, the Jaguars should again enjoy a run-heavy game script, expectedly playing with a lead. Tuten is an RB1, having avoided suffering a setback this week.

items.name: Cam Skattebo
items.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: At this point, Devin Singletary should be considered the tentative starter for the Giants’ Week 9 game against the Eagles. Singletary could handle a sizable workload, though he was buried on the depth chart as the No. 3 running back for a reason. Singletary warrants volume-based FLEX status if Skattebo cannot play this week.

items.name: Malik Nabers
items.headline: Malik Nabers (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Nabers worked with trainers today instead of practicing with his teammates. He told reporters after practicing that he is “good” to go for Week 9 against the Eagles. We believe him. The Giants have managed his reps at times during the practice week this year.

items.name: Dontayvion Wicks
items.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: At this point, fantasy managers should expect Wicks to take the field next in Week 11, following the Eagles’ Week 10 bye. He does not need to be held on 12-team rosters at this time.

items.name: Jake Elliott
items.headline: Jake Elliott (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Even if Elliott is active for the Eagles’ Week 9 game against the Giants, he makes for an uncomfortable start. The offense is struggling with so many starters ailing.

items.name: DeVonta Smith
items.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Smith will almost certainly miss the Eagles’ Week 9 game against the Giants. Philadelphia goes on bye next week, so fantasy managers will likely have to wait until Week 11 to get Smith back in their lineups. Stay tuned.

items.name: Demarcus Robinson
items.headline: Demarcus Robinson (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Robinson may still need more time before taking the field on game day, but his continued practice participation, albeit limited, is a good sign overall. Given the state of the 49ers’ wide receiver corps, if active, Robinson could handle a decent workload.

items.name: Christian Darrisaw
items.headline: Christian Darrisaw (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: The Vikings’ left tackle is on track to play in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game against the Bills. His likely presence is good news. The Bills field a fairly strong defensive line.

items.name: Jauan Jennings
items.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Jennings has been the subject of trade rumors. Since is able to practice, even in a limited capacity, this injury is unlikely to alter a potential suitor’s interest. Regardless, Jennings is not on the FLEX radar this week.

items.name: Dion Dawkins
items.headline: Dion Dawkins (ribs) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Dawkins, the Bills’ left tackle, and LG Alec Anderson (ankle) were both absent today. They have an extra day to rest, since the Bills face the Vikings in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game. Hopefully, the extra time allows them to suit up against Minnesota’s elite defense.

items.name: Keon Coleman
items.headline: Keon Coleman (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Coleman was seen wearing a red non-contact jersey at today’s practice. His limited session to begin the week puts him on track to face the Vikings in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game. With DJ Moore (shoulder) back in the lineup, Coleman is just a WR4/FLEX. Joshua Palmer (hamstring) did not practice.

items.name: Dalton Kincaid
items.headline: Dalton Kincaid (chest) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Kincaid should be good to go for the Bills’ Monday Night Football game against the Vikings. It’s a tough matchup, and he could be asked to block more than usual. Still, Kincaid warrants TE1 treatment thanks to his talent, usage and quarterback.

items.name: DJ Moore
items.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: There was some concern that Moore may have injured his knee in Week 8 against the Ravens, but he is listed only with the same shoulder issue he has dealt with for weeks, which is good news. Moore should be treated as a WR2 in a very tough matchup against the Vikings on Monday Night Football.

items.name: Talanoa Hufanga
items.headline: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) resumed practicing on Thursday.
items.analysis: The Broncos’ safety now has a chance to play in Week 9 against the Panthers, though it is possible he still needs another week. Getting Hufanga back in the lineup will help improve a Broncos defense that has somewhat underperformed this year.

items.name: Rashee Rice
items.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) practiced in full on Thursday.
items.analysis: Rice is on track to face the Jets this weekend, as expected. The Chiefs’ embattled wide receiver also reportedly filed for bankruptcy this week, theoretically adding extra incentive to play well enough for a decent contract when he enters free agency next offseason. Rice is a fantasy football WR2.

items.name: Travis Kelce
items.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
items.analysis: This time last week, Kelce was still a limited participant. Today’s upgraded status is a good sign for his overall health. The Chiefs’ stalwart tight end earned eight targets last week despite the ailment. He can be treated as a fantasy football TE1 against the Jets this week.

items.name: Terrance Ferguson
items.headline: Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was spotted at practice Thursday.
items.analysis: Ferguson had his 21-day practice window open up, and it’s a positive sign that he’s been able to practice on back-to-back days. There’s no guarantee he’ll play in Week 9 against the Commanders, but even if he misses that contest, it seems likely the second-year tight end will be back for the second half of the campaign.

items.name: Jake Ferguson
items.headline: Jake Ferguson (ankle) did not participate in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: This makes two straight missed practices for Ferguson because of his ankle injury suffered in Week 8 versus the Cardinals. At this point, it seems unlikely that he’ll be able to play in Week 9 against the Colts, and there are better fantasy options even if he were to be able to go.

items.name: Bhayshul Tuten
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) “should be” good for Week 9 against the Ravens, barring any pre-game setbacks.
items.analysis: Tuten did not practice at all this week, though the Jaguars notably kept many injured players limited, so it is possible that his absences were mostly precautionary. Tuten injured his ankle and foot in Week 8 against the Colts, but still managed to total 159 scrimmage yards, two catches and two touchdowns. He is an RB1 if active.

items.name: George Pickens
items.headline: George Pickens (hamstring) was limited during Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Pickens was also limited during Wednesday’s session. The 25-year-old still seems to be on target to play in Week 9 against the Colts, but fantasy managers would obviously like to see Pickens get in a full session before that contest.

items.name: Myles Garrett
items.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) was able to practice again Thursday.
items.analysis: Garrett has now been able to participate in back-to-back practices. The 30-year-old star defender appears to be ready to roll for Week 9 against the Commanders, but a decision on Garrett’s availability likely won’t be made until Friday at the earliest.

items.name: Hunter Henry
items.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: It’s looking like rookie Eli Raridon will operate as the Patriots’ No. 1 tight end in Week 9 against the Packers. Henry has not participated in football activities since injuring his foot early in Week 8 against the Dolphins. Raridon would warrant streaming TE1 consideration if he gets the start.

items.name: Mack Hollins
items.headline: Mack Hollins (calf) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Hollins is firmly in the questionable column with one practice left in Week 9. If active, he would be a boom-bust FLEX. The Patriots’ healthy wide receivers have played well in Hollins’ absence, though the team would probably like to get their field-stretcher back in action before long.

items.name: A.J. Brown
items.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Brown seems highly unlikely to play in Week 9 against the Packers. The Patriots could shut him down for a little while, with the goal of getting his degenerative knee and early-season high-ankle sprain healed. For now, fantasy managers should make backup plans in the short term.

items.name: MarShawn Lloyd
items.headline: MarShawn Lloyd was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday’s practice due to a knee injury.
items.analysis: Lloyd was good to go for Wednesday’s session, so this appears to be a new issue. Chris Brooks was also limited by his ankle injury for a second-straight practice. Lloyd and Brooks — if healthy — will be the backups to Josh Jacobs for Week 9, and don’t offer much fantasy upside, if any.

items.name: Christian Watson
items.headline: Christian Watson (rib) was limited during Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: It’s back-to-back limited sessions for Watson. It’ll likely be a pain-tolerance issue for the wideout, but assuming he doesn’t suffer a setback in practice, he appears to be good for Week 9 against the Patriots and deserves WR1 consideration.

items.name: Denzel Boston
items.headline: Denzel Boston (calf) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Boston is on track to face the Saints this week, but lower-body injuries have limited his production since Week 4. The Browns are also likely to have Shedeur Sanders under center, adding an unknown variable to the mix as the two players hone their chemistry. Boston is likely just a boom-bust FLEX.

items.name: Harold Fannin
items.headline: Harold Fannin (groin) was added to the injury report on Thursday.
items.analysis: This is concerning. Fannin suffered a groin injury during his 2025 rookie season and underwent offseason surgery to address it. It is possible this is just general soreness, but fantasy managers must closely monitor his practice participation level tomorrow. KC Concepcion operates in a similar role and would directly benefit if Fanning is unable to play this week.

items.name: Tristan Wirfs
items.headline: Tristan Wirfs (toe) did not participate in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: It’s a new injury designation for Wirfs, so it seems likely that the ailment occurred during Wednesday’s practice. The Buccaneers already have offensive line issues, and anyone who saw the Bears ravage the Seahawks’ offensive line knows what that unit is capable of. It could be a long day for Baker Mayfield if Wirfs can’t go.

items.name: Kenny Gainwell
items.headline: Kenny Gainwell was a full participant in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Gainwell never seemed in danger of missing Week 9 against the Bears, but the 27-year-old should be just fine for the Week 9 bout against the Bears. He’s coming off a monster 140-yard performance against Atlanta, but keep in mind that Tampa Bay was basically a service academy school for that game with zero completions. He’s closer to FLEX than RB2.

items.name: Emeka Egbuka
items.headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) was a full participant in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: After only participating in drills on the side and being listed as a non-participant Wednesday, Egbuka was a full-go for Thursday’s session. The 24-year-old will likely need to get in one more full session before fantasy managers can fully trust the wideout for Week 9 against the Bears, but this is obviously a significant step in the right direction.

items.name: Mason Taylor
items.headline: Mason Taylor (back) practiced in full on Thursday.
items.analysis: Taylor is firmly on track to play in Week 9 against the Chiefs. He will operate as the team’s top tight end, keeping intriguing rookie Kenyon Sadiq in the TE2 tier.

items.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
items.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: It’d be nice to see the Sun God get in a full session, but the fact that the star wideout has been able to practice both days suggest he’ll be just fine for Week 9 against the Dolphins. He’ll be a high-end WR1 for that game and any other contest that St. Brown plays in.

items.name: Christian Kirk
items.headline: Christian Kirk (knee) was not spotted at the open portion of Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Kirk was limited Wednesday with his knee issue, and it’s possible he’ll get that designation again in the closed portion of practice. The 29-year-old still has a decent chance to play in Week 9 against the Raiders, but even with the litany of injuries for the 49ers in their receiving corps, it’s hard to trust Kirk from a fantasy perspective.

items.name: Tutu Atwell
items.headline: Rams OC Nate Scheelhaase wants to get Tutu Atwell more involved.
items.analysis: Atwell earned four targets last week, catching two for 52 yards. Increasing his workload could only mean one or two more targets, so Atwell does not need to be quickly picked up in 12-team formats. For those struggling at the wide receiver position, Atwell simply enters the boom-bust FLEX conversation.

items.name: Christian McCaffrey
items.headline: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) was able to participate in Wednesday’s practice.
items.analysis: A rare bit of good news on the injury front for the 49ers. McCaffrey was given the day off Wednesday, but even if this is just a limited session, it’s a good start for what could be a a Week 9 date against the Raiders that sees the tailback get a smorgasbord of touches due to the issues involving several injured receivers.

items.name: Deebo Samuel
items.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) was not seen at Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Neither Samuel nor Mike Evans (Achilles) was seen at the practice, and the same goes for Christian Kirk (knee). Kirk still has a chance to play, but it seems very unlikely that Brock Purdy will have Samuel lined out wide for Week 9 against the Raiders. His next chance to play will be Week 10 against the Cowboys, barring something unforeseeable.

items.name: Mike Evans
items.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) was not present at Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Evans wasn’t spotted at practice, nor was Deebo Samuel (hamstring). Neither player is expected to play against the Raiders on Thursday, and Thursday’s missed practice seems to clinch that. The 49ers’ receiving crops are in dire straits, with Christian Kirk also not practicing with his knee injury.

items.name: TreVeyon Henderson
items.headline: ESPN’s Mike Reiss believes TreVeyon Henderson’s illness might be related to the “adversity” he has faced this season.
items.analysis: Reiss was asked about Henderson’s status during his weekly appearance on the local radio show, Toucher & Hardy. According to Reiss, Henderson has faced a lot of new challenges this season, including recurring ankle issues and limited playing time, and the adversity has been tough for Henderson to deal with. Some might remember that similar reports surfaced regarding Bucky Irving, beset by multiple injuries, last season. Henderson might need more time before he resumes playing. Stay tuned. He was officially listed as a non-participant on Thursday.

items.name: Drew Lock
items.headline: Drew Lock told reporters that his elbow “felt good” after Wednesday’s practice.
items.analysis: “It’s doing good. I’m excited to be back out there,” Lock said. “Felt great to get under center, rip some balls yesterday. Feels good.” Lock noted that he’ll go through a normal week of practice, and assuming there’s no setbacks, he’ll be under center in place of Sam Darnold (rib/quad) for Week 9 against the Cardinals. If Lock can’t go, it’ll be Jalen Milroe.

items.name: Kyle Monangai
items.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not participate in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: It’s back-to-back missed practices for the 24-year-old ahead of Week 9’s contest against the Buccaneers. It seems more than likely that Monangai comes back for Week 10 after the bye, but if he can get a full session in, there’s a chance he rolls against Tampa Bay come Sunday.

items.name: Breece Hall
items.headline: Breece Hall (quad) said he is ready to go for Week 9 against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: We expect to see Hall listed as a full participant on today’s injury report. An update will be provided if that is not the case. Earlier today, Jets OC Frank Reich discussed Hall and Braelon Allen’s expected usage, saying having the two players is “a great problem to have,” referring to the duo as “two No. 1 backs.” That said, Reich added that Hall “is obviously the bell cow,” but the backfield usage will be a “mix” of both players. Jets coach Aaron Glenn will reportedly share his ideal backfield split with Reich, who will work with the position coaches to make it happen. Hall likely belongs in the high-end RB2 tier while Allen remains FLEX-viable.

items.name: Zonovan Knight
items.headline: Bam Knight (concussion) was not spotted at Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: It appears it’ll be another DNP for Knight as he entered the concussion protocol following Sunday’s win over the Cowboys in Week 8. The 25-year-old tailback seems unlikely to be able to go in Week 9 against the Seahawks, but there should be further updates on Knight’s status soon.

items.name: DJ Turner
items.headline: DJ Turner (heel) practiced in full on Thursday.
items.analysis: The Bengals No. 1 cornerback is firmly on track to play in Week 9 against the Falcons. While Drake London would get a matchup boost if Turner were to sit out, Turner’s presence does not drop London out of the WR1 tier.

items.name: Omarion Hampton
items.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh indicated that Omarion Hampton will get more touches.
items.analysis: Harbaugh reportedly made comments to this effect earlier in the week. When asked for his thoughts on the matter, OC Mike McDaniel said he is “excited about someone dictating the rotation” and added that Hampton has “had a really great week of prep.” Hampton hasn’t scored double-digit half-PPR points since Week 4. Whether the potential usage increase can get him back to 10.0-plus points remains to be seen, but this week’s comments are at least somewhat encouraging.

items.name: Saquon Barkley
items.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
items.analysis: Barkley is again on track to play through his injuries on game day. The Eagles’ offensive centerpiece totaled 54 scrimmage yards, one catch and one touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 8 loss to the Commanders. He may have trouble solidifying a spot in the RB1 tier, given the state of the Eagles’ offense, but he remains a high-end RB2 at worst, based on talent and usage.

items.name: Zavier Scott
items.headline: Bears placed RB Zavier Scott (thumb) on injured reserve
items.analysis: Scott has not played on offense at all this season, but he has successfully carved out a role on special teams. According to the Chicago Tribune’s Brad Biggs, the Bears have reason to believe that Scott’s injured reserve stint “will be on the shorter side.”

items.name: Jaylen Wright
items.headline: Jaylen Wright (quad) resumed practicing on Thursday.
items.analysis: Wright is on track to be available for the Dolphins’ Week 9 game against the Lions, although he is mostly functioning as an infrequently used backup rusher while also serving as the team’s top returner. He is a mid-tier bench stash at this time.

items.name: Malik Nabers
items.headline: Malik Nabers (undisclosed) was seen working off to the side with trainers on Thursday.
items.analysis: The Giants have limited Nabers’ practice reps from time to time this season. Although he may end up being listed as a non-participant, we are not currently concerned about his Week 9 availability. The Giants’ No. 1 wide receiver is fully dressed in his typical practice attire. An update will be provided when more info is released.

items.name: Kyler Murray
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Kyler Murray (hamstring) “will be ‘week-to-week’ now.”
items.analysis: Murray reportedly experienced soreness in his hamstring following the Vikings’ Week 8 loss to the Lions. Carson Wentz will start for the Vikings’ Week 9 Monday Night Football game against the Bills, and potentially longer. If Wentz plays well, Murray could be relegated to the backup role. Murray does not necessarily need to be stashed on benches in two-quarterback leagues at this time. This situation is not ideal for him.

items.name: Carson Wentz
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Carson Wentz will start for the Vikings in Week 9 against the Bills.
