https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce should be good to go for the Chiefs’ Week 7 game against the Seahawks. At 37 years old, he does not need to practice fully in order to play, though it would be nice to see him upgrade to full participation tomorrow. If active, he is a locked-in TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce played through an ankle issue in Week 6, catching five passes for 53 yards. Despite not playing at full health, he was still second on the team in targets. Kelce starts out the week as a limited practice participant and it would be a surprise if he misses National Tight End Day this week against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce caught 5-of-6 targets for 53 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce was in and out of the lineup in the first half while dealing with a lingering ankle issue. Though he clearly wasn’t 100 percent, Kelce was second on the team (behind Xavier Worthy) in targets and had a 24-yard catch and run reception in the second half. Kelce, who now has nine catches over his past three games, should see more looks from Patrick Mahomes for as long as Rashee Rice (hamstring) is sidelined. He’ll be a top-15 fantasy play in Week 7 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce caught 2-of-4 targets for 15 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 4 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce was held in check throughout the entirety of this one and has been targeted just six times in his last two games. Were it not for an 11-yard score in last week’s win over the Dolphins, we would be looking at back-to-back disappointing fantasy weeks for the future Hall of Famer. Kelce and the Chiefs are now heading into their bye week. He could see an increase in targets with Rashee Rice (hamstring) and Tyquan Thornton (ankle) both at risk of missing multiple weeks, but Kelce now has three games on his 2026 ledger with five or fewer targets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce caught 2-of-2 targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 3 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Both Kelce’s catches and targets were his fewest of the young season, though he made them count on an afternoon where Patrick Mahomes dropped back only 25 times. Kelce notched a 48-yard catch-and-run on the first offensive play of the game, then finished off the Chiefs’ last real drive with an 11-yard touchdown grab in the back of the end zone. Why he went so long between looks can be a question for another day. Sitting on 231 yards receiving through the Chiefs’ first three contests, Kelce will remain a strong TE1 for Week 4 in Vegas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Darrisaw (shoulder) practiced in full on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Darrisaw is now firmly on track to play in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game against the Bills, who field a tough, talented defensive line. Having Darrisaw on the field will be helpful for pocket passer Carson Wentz.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Darrisaw (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The Vikings’ left tackle is on track to play in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game against the Bills. His likely presence is good news. The Bills field a fairly strong defensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Darrisaw (concussion) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Darrisaw suffered a concussion in Week 4 against the Dolphins and was unable to play in Week 5 against the Saints. The Vikings were on bye in Week 6, giving him more than two weeks to get ready for Week 7. Vikings RT Brian O’Neill (knee) was limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Vikings LT Christian Darrisaw (concussion) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 5 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: He did not practice all week with the concussion. Brian O’Neill is questionable. Ryan Van Demark will likely play left tackle for Darrisaw, while 2026 third-rounder Caleb Tiernan is the likely reserve if O’Neill can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Vikings LT Christian Darrisaw (concussion) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Darrisaw is on the wrong side of questionable, having logged consecutive absences to begin Week 5. With Vikings LG Donovan Jackson (knee) out, Kyler Murray could be looking over his shoulder quite often against the Saints this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said LT Christian Darrisaw (concussion) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: O’Connell also said that RT Brian O’Neill (undisclosed) will be limited. The Vikings recently placed LG Donovan Jackson (knee) on injured reserve. The offensive line is very banged up at the moment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said LT Christian Darrisaw cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol in Week 4 against the Dolphins, but later experienced symptoms.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Darrisaw was in and out of the Vikings’ Week 4 win over the Dolphins. Now, we know why. The Vikings’ left tackle will have to clear it in order for him to play in Week 5 against the Saints. Vikings LG Donovan Jackson was forced from the game with a knee injury. This line is ailing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Vikings LT Christian Darrisaw (knee) said he feels “the best” he has felt in two years.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Darrisaw suffered a multi-ligament tear in his left knee in October 2024 and struggled in his return last year. He told reporters today that he thinks he “turned the corner this offseason.” The Vikings plan to give him regular rest days during training camp and the regular season, but he believes he is on track to be a full-time player once again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Vikings restructured WR Justin Jefferson’s contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: This comes from NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero. In hopes of getting under the cap before the start of the new league year, the Vikings will restructure the deals of both Jefferson and LT Christian Darrisaw, likely by converting portions of their base salaries into guaranteed money. The Vikings rank last in the league in available cap space, per OverTheCap.com, and will likely restructure a few more deals in the coming days to get to a point where they have money to spend in free agency.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Vikings placed LT Christian Darrisaw (knee) on injured reserve
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Darrisaw tore his left ACL and MCL in October 2024. He retook the field for the first time in Week 3 this season, following the injury, but the knee continued to bother him. He allowed 18 quarterback pressures in 10 games this season. Hopefully, he can put the knee injury behind him with another offseason of rest and rehab.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that “the plan” is for Quenton Nelson to avoid injured reserve after undergoing a procedure to remove cartilage fragments from his knee.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: If the Seahawks were to place Nelson on short-term injured reserve, he would be required to miss at least four games. The Seahawks face the Cardinals this week, the Raiders next and then go on bye. Nelson could have a chance to play in Week 12 against the 49ers. His availability that week will likely just come down to how the recovery is going. His loss is unfortunate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Quenton Nelson (knee) will have a minor procedure and is week-to-week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Apparently, Nelson was dealing with this knee issue when Seattle acquired for him, and he recently “aggravated it to some degree.” FOX 59’s Mike Chappell notes that Nelson was never listed on the Colts’ injury report this season. This is a bummer for the Seahawks, who acquired Nelson as a win-now move. Nelson will not play in Week 9 against the Cardinals, and the Seahawks also ruled out LT Charles Cross (ankle), DT Leonard Williams (stinger) and LB Uchenna Nwosu (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Shaheed seems likely to miss another week, though he could technically still turn things around tomorrow. Seahawks LT Charles Cross (ankle) also remains sidelined on Thursday, and LG Quenton Nelson (knee) was downgraded to a non-participant. Hopefully, Nelson’s absence is precautionary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Seahawks acquired Quenton Nelson from the Colts in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: With the Colts’ season all but over, the team could trade away a series of key player as they look toward a total tear down/rebuild scenario following the 2026 season. That includes Nelson, an eight-time Pro Bowler who now has a chance to compete for a title now that he’s out of Indianapolis. Nelson will join a Seattle offensive line that ranks 21st in pass blocking win rate and 27th in run blocking win rate. His addition should be a boon for Sam Darnold and the Seahawks’ pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Packers, Vikings, Seahawks, and Broncos are “among the teams interested” in trading for Jonathan Taylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: As Rap notes, the Colts view Taylor as a pillar of the franchise. Even if they are forced to rebuild the roster, they could want him there as the centerpiece of the next iteration of the offense. On the other hand, Taylor will turn 28 at the end of the season and the Colts face a lengthy teardown process without their 2027 first-round selection. Taylor will likely be past his prime by the time they are competitive again. Rapoport also named DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson as potential trade candidates if the Colts’ struggles continue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: ESPN’s Stephen Holder listed QuentonNelson and DeForest Buckner as potential trade options for the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Holder writes that “trade speculation is swirling” around Buckner and notes that Nelson is in the final year of his deal, potentially providing motivation for the Colts to move him. Neither player had much to say when asked about a potential trade, but per Holder, “it is widely expected that significant organizational changes might be coming after the eventual hire of a new general manager.” Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Jonathan Taylor said he would “definitely love to be a Colt for life,” as he enters the final year of his contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Taylor, 27, has totaled more than 320 offensive touches in each of the last two seasons. His current $14 million annual salary makes him the seventh-highest-paid running back in the league. Taylor has set multiple Colts records, operating as the centerpiece of Indianapolis’ offense for years. FOX 59’s Mike Chappell writes that it is “uncertain whether there’s a mutual desire to keep Taylor in Indy beyond 2025.” Multiple Colts stars, including DTs DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart, OG Quenton Nelson and WR Josh Downs, are also entering the final year of their deal. Chappell believes owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon “might believe it’s more prudent to allow the upcoming season to run its course rather than reinvest in lucrative contracts.” Time will tell.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Colts LG Quenton Nelson returned to Week 2 against the Broncos after suffering an apparent leg injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Nelson was the downfield blocker on a delayed Tyler Warren screen pass when he was hurt. Broncos S Talanoa Hufanga went low on Nelson, which resulted in Nelson driving his quad-knee area into the diving Hufanga. Nelson immediately grabbed just above his knee as he went down. He then limped off the field under his own power and was seen talking to teammates with his helmet on, along the sideline. He returned on the following drive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Colts LG Quenton Nelson (ankle) is questionable for Week 17 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Nelson was able to practice on Friday, though only in a limited capacity. He appears to be on the right side of questionable but will need to make it through pre-game warmups before being cleared. Tanor Bortolini would likely take his spot in the lineup if he is ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Colts listed OG Quenton Nelson (ankle) as questionable for Week 18 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Nelson was a limited participant in back-to-back practices to close out the week and should have a chance to suit up in what’s arguably the Colts’ biggest game of the season. In addition to Nelson, the Colts also listed center Ryan Kelly (ankle), cornerback Kenny Moore (back), and running back Zack Moss (forearm) as questionable heading into the weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson (NIR-rest/ribs) is not on the final injury report for Week 9 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson caught 8-of-15 targets for 111 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals’ Week 8 win over the Cowboys while playing through a pair of broken ribs. The Cardinals kept him limited all week. He should be good to go for WR2 duties against the Seahawks’ elite defense this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson (NIR-rest/ribs) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson will face the Seahawks this weekend, barring a setback. It’s a tough matchup, but Wilson’s target volume keeps him worth of remaining in starting lineups. Wilson showed decent chemistry with Gardner Minshew last week, which was nice to see, now that Jacoby Brissett is headed to the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson said he is playing with two broken ribs after the Cardinals’ Week 8 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson started the week off by practicing in a non-contact jersey. Now we know why. Wilson told reporters post-game that the Cardinals’ organization has changed his life, and he doesn’t believe in “taking, taking, taking,” adding that if he “can muster up the strength to go play, even at 60 percent,” he’s going to. Wilson will be in the WR3 ranks against the Seahawks next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson caught 8-of-15 targets for 111 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s Week 8 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: He added a key 17-yard end around in overtime to help set up the go-ahead field goal. Wilson got off to an obscenely slow start with Jacoby Brissett, notching all but 25 of these yards as Minshew Mania took over in the second half. Wilson managed several back shoulder balls and almost caught another of his targets down to the two-yard line before a successful challenge revealed he did not hold on to the ball. It’s unclear how much better Minshew will actually make things, but the Cardinals might as well ride the hot hand. Wilson’s role should have him in the WR3 ranks even if the matchup won’t be this good again in Week 9 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Michael Wilson (ribs) is “good to go” for Arizona’s Week 8 game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: He’ll get cleared off Arizona’s injury report later today. Wilson is in a nice spot in one of the games with the highest over/under total on the slate against Dallas, but may run into Joey Porter Jr. shadow coverage. Still, even with how things have trended of late, this feels like a spot where Wilson has to be started in the majority of leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson (ribs) was limited in practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: It was the second consecutive day in which Wilson practiced with a yellow non-contact jersey after stating Wednesday that the team was simply being overly cautious. Wilson appears on track to maintain a high-volume role in the pass-heavy Cardinals offense in Week 8 against the Cowboys, where he will be a borderline WR1, if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson (ribs) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson was on the practice field wearing a non-contact jersey on Wednesday. He is dealing with a rib injury, presumably suffered in the Cardinals’ Week 7 loss to the Broncos. He will be limited as long as he wears the non-contact jersey and ideally finishes the week without it in order to play in Week 8 against the Cowboys. Kendrick Bourne suddenly becomes the WR1 if Wilson cannot go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson caught 4-of-8 targets for 55 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 7 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Jacoby Brissett once again tried to get Wilson going downfield, but the best he could muster was 16 yards on their longest connection. Without a long play to juice the box score, Wilson was held under 10 PPR points for the third week in a row. All three of those games have been on the heels of the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade, or his one-game absence leading into the transaction. The target totals have held steady, but the production is lacking. The good news for Wilson is that he gets the Cowboys in Week 8. Facing one of the league’s worst pass defenses, Wilson will stick in the WR2 ranks next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson caught 4-of-7 targets for 32 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 6 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson’s day would have looked a lot different if a would-be 36-yard touchdown pass from Jacoby Brissett had not glanced off Wilson’s fingertips while he dove for it in the end zone. He had another 30-yarder go off his hands on the following drive, and had a five-yard catch overturned by a penalty. The disappointing box score results could allow fantasy managers to send a successful buy-low offer. Wilson is a WR2/3 next week against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: ArizonaCardinals.com’s Darren Urban believes Carson Beck won’t start in the “immediate future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Cardinals fans appear to be pining for the team to bench Jacoby Brissett and start the rookie in the coming weeks as another season circles the drain for Arizona. Beck so far has been the Cards’ emergency third quarterback. Urban said there remains a “chance Beck is made the backup this week or next and allow him to come on in relief if the situation presents itself. I don’t see Beck starting in the immediate future, but it does feel his time grows closer, and if the offense continues to sputter, that would be understandable.” Brissett this season ranks 15th in passing yards. He’s thrown nine touchdowns to five interceptions and ranks 30th out of 37 qualifying QBs in adjusted yards per attempt. He won’t be a viable fantasy play this week against a tough Rams coverage unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Commanders ruled out Treylon Burks (foot) for Week 9 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: The Commanders’ wide receiver corps continues to lose players. Burks and Dyami Brown (calf) will both be sidelined this weekend, leaving Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams and Chig Okonkwo to operate as the top pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: The Commanders’ thin wide receiver corps could get thinner. Burks, the team’s top downfield receiver, is on the wrong side of questionable for this week’s game against the Rams. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks was limited-DNP-limited due to the foot injury last week, but played through it for five targets in the Commanders’ Week 8 win over the Eagles. He starts out this week as a DNP as the Commanders manage his injury. Given he already played a game with the injury, Burks is still likely to play in Week 9, though he will need to get a practice in later this week to feel better about his chances of playing against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks caught 3-of-5 targets for 81 yards in the Commanders’ Week 8 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: A 53-yard reception toward the end of the third quarter did the bulk of the damage for Burks, who continues to give the Commanders their best deep option in the absence of Terry McLaurin. That doesn’t necessarily mean he carries weekly fantasy value considering the poor state of a Washington offense that got its first win in a Jayden Daniels start since 5 October of 2025. Burks is likely best left on the waiver wire ahead of a Week 9 meeting with the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) is active for Week 8 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: The team’s Week 7 bye apparently afforded Burks enough time to overcome the foot injury sustained late in the fourth quarter of Washington’s Week 6 loss, confirming previous reports that indicated Burks would be active after entering the weekend listed as questionable. Expect Burks to operate as a starter alongside veteran Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams, the latter two of whom carry greater upside against the inside-funnel Philadelphia defense. Inactive for the Commanders are QB Athan Kaliakmanis, CB Fabian Moreau, CB Isaac Yiadom, G Tanoa Togiai, DT Daron Payne, and DT Javon Kinlaw.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Treylon Burks (foot) is expected to play in Week 8 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks was limited in Friday’s practice before being listed as questionable. With Terry McLaurin done for the year, Burks is one of several role players for the Commanders who will be asked to step up in the back half of 2026. Burks has nine catches for 152 yards and two scores in five appearances this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) is questionable for Washington’s Week 8 game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: The rare limited-DNP-limited injury report shows up here after Burks suffered a late foot injury in Week 6’s Monday night football. Burks probably is best considered truly questionable at this point. If he’s absent, it could help Antonio Williams get into the 80 percent snap range.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks downgraded from a limited showing Wednesday to a “DNP” Thursday, indicating he might be headed toward an absence when the Commanders take on the Eagles on Sunday Night Football. Considering the team is already without Terry McLaurin, who was lost for the season in Week 6, this would appear to be setting up for the best chance for rookie Antonio Williams to finally break out in Washington. Fantasy managers will want to confirm the status of Burks on the team’s final injury report Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks was limited due to a foot injury; this is notable with the Commanders coming out of a bye week. With Terry McLaurin out for the season, Burks has the opportunity to earn an increased role in the receiving corps. Fantasy managers don’t need to roster the 26-year-old yet, but Dyami Brown and Antonio Williams could see a boost in targets if Burks sits out Week 8 against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: ESPN’s John Keim reports Terry McLaurin’s knee injury is considered “significant.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Washington head coach Dan Quinn said after the team’s Monday night loss to the 49ers that there was “fear” McLaurin could be lost for the long-term after going down with a non-contact injury and was carted to the locker room. McLaurin has functioned as the team’s lone downfield threat for much of the season, and could be replaced with Treylon Burks, who on Monday night caught four balls for 66 yards before sustaining a late-game injury. Antonio Williams and Dyami Brown could also see an increase in routes and targets if McLaurin is sidelined for a while. Look for Chig Okonkwo to see an uptick in targets too. Okonkwo had seven grabs for 69 yards against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: The Broncos’ talented safety might need another week to get his ankle healthy. Hufanga only logged two limited practice sessions this week. He has been sidelined since mid-October.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: The Broncos’ safety now has a chance to play in Week 9 against the Panthers, though it is possible he still needs another week. Getting Hufanga back in the lineup will help improve a Broncos defense that has somewhat underperformed this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: Broncos ruled out Jonah Elliss (ankle) for Week 7 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: Reporting from earlier this week indicates Ellis could be sidelined for a few weeks. Broncos S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) was also ruled out this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: Riley Moss (ribs) is questionable for the Broncos’ Week 6 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: Moss missed Week 5 due to a rib injury but has a chance to return Thursday against the Seahawks after three straight limited practices this week. CB Patrick Surtain (ankle) and S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) did not practice all week and were ruled out, as expected.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Talanoa Hufanga is expected to miss “about 2-3 weeks” with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: The former second-team All-Pro safety left last week’s game against the Chargers with the injury. Hufanga has been one of the biggest havoc creators in the league this year with one forced fumble and two interceptions, one of which was returned for a touchdown. His absence will be a big blow to the Broncos’ defense, which is already without Patrick Surtain II, Jonathon Cooper, and potentially Riley Moss for their Week 6 matchup against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: Broncos CB Riley Moss (ribs) was listed as a limited practice participant on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: Moss was ruled out of Week 5 against the Chargers but has a chance to play Week 6 against the Seahawks with back-to-back limited practice listings. Meanwhile, S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) was a DNP for the second straight day. With Patrick Surtain (ankle) still out in the short term, the Broncos’ banged-up secondary may have a tough time against Jaxon Smith-Njigba and company on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) did not practice on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: It was an estimated session, but one that probably bodes pretty prescient since Hufanga left Week 5’s game with the ankle injury and was ruled out. Riley Moss (ribs) was listed as limited and would appear to have a chance to come back after being ruled out for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: NFL Insider James Palmer reports Broncos S Talanoa Hufanga is “100% healthy and moving well.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: Palmer dropped some quick-hitting notes on Monday’s camp practice, singling out Hufanga as fully healthy. Hufanga agreed to a three-year contract with the Broncos this offseason after coming off consecutive season-ending injuries in 2023 and 2024, the former of which was a torn ACL and the latter being a torn ligament in his wrist. He’ll look to regain his high-level play with the Broncos after earning first-team All-Pro honors in his last fully healthy season in 2022 while with the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: Broncos agreed to terms with S Talanoa Hufanga, formerly of the 49ers, on a three-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: The deal is worth up to $45 million. Hufanga was a rising star coming out of his second NFL season. He started all 17 games in 2022 and totaled two sacks, nine pass breakups, and four interceptions, one of which was returned for a touchdown. Hufanga then tore his ACL 10 games into the 2023 season. His recovery lasted into the following season and he also missed time with a wrist injury, limiting him to just seven appearances. With a clean bill of health heading into 2025, Hufanga will look to get back on track as part of a Denver defense that ranked third in points allowed last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.headline: 49ers activated S Talanoa Hufanga (wrist) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/talanoa-hu.analysis: Hufanga bolsters an already sharp secondary, although the absence of DE Nick Bosa could place additional strain on the second level with a lessened ability to generate organic pressure up front. Expect Hufanga to step back into his starting safety role after missing all but two games this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Pat Bryant (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Bryant is expected to be activated from injured reserve by Saturday, but the team has officially listed him as questionable. He makes for a boom-bust FLEX in his first game back. The Broncos’ passing offense has struggled this season. Perhaps Bryant’s return lifts it up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Pat Bryant (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Bryant’s 21-day practice window has been opened, and it begins with a full session, putting him on track to play in Week 9 against the Panthers. The Broncos’ passing game has severely underperformed expectations. Bryant does not necessarily need to be added in 12-team formats, though he could ultimately compete for No. 2 wide receiver duties.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: The Denver Gazette’s Chris Tomasson said “indications point to Broncos WR Pat Bryant returning to practice this week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Bryant has missed the Broncos’ last four games after being placed on injured reserve with an ankle injury. The 23-year-old receiver is eligible to return whenever the Broncos deem him ready to do so, and his practicing this week would mean the team has opened his 21-day return window. Bryant has caught nine passes for 133 yards and one touchdown and was third among Broncos receivers in routes run (91) through the first four weeks of the season. He could make for an interesting stash in deeper leagues, but fantasy managers shouldn’t rush to put him in their lineups whenever he does return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Broncos placed Pat Bryant on injured reserve with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Bryant will be eligible to return from injured reserve in Week 9, when the Broncos face the Panthers. The Broncos go on bye in Week 10, though, so if he isn’t feeling ready to play, they could hold him out until they face the division-rival Raiders in Week 11. Bryant’s absence could create more opportunities for Courtland Sutton and Marvin Mims, but Jaylen Waddle may end up hogging targets instead.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Broncos WR Pat Bryant will miss “a few weeks” after suffering a sprained ankle in Week 4’s loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Bryant was carted from the field in the second half of Sunday’s game after taking a big hit over the middle. The 23-year-old receiver currently ranks third among Broncos receivers with 91 routes run and has played 55 percent of his snaps out wide. Troy Franklin or Marvin Mims could be in line to see more snaps while Bryant is sidelined, but it’s hard to imagine either player becoming valuable fantasy assets at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Pat Bryant was carted off with an apparent leg injury in Week 4 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: He’s questionable to return. Bryant took a big hit over the middle on a second half reception against the Niners and was down on the turf for some time before being helped onto the cart. Looking dejected, Bryant was taken to the locker room. The oft-injured Bryant could be facing yet another extended absence. That would likely boost playing time and targets for Courtland Sutton and possibly Marvin Mims.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Pat Bryant caught both targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 3 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Bryant also added a successful two-point reception in the third quarter to give him a usable fantasy week for the first time in 2026. He continues to play well behind Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle in an offense that has yet to find its footing with a new offensive play caller. He’ll be a difficult start in Week 4 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Pat Bryant caught 4-of-6 targets for 42 yards in the Broncos’ Week 1 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: The good news for fantasy managers is that Bryant played well ahead of both Marvin Mims and Troy Franklin, rewarding those who took a late-round dart through on the talented second-year receiver. That’s about where the good news ended on this night considering the Broncos managed only 176 yards of total offense. While better days are likely ahead for Bryant, there is likely to be mounting pressure from the outside for offensive coordinator Davis Webb to relinquish play calling duties back to head coach Sean Payton. Until, or unless, that happens, Bryant appears likely to remain an upside WR4. That begins in Week 2 when the Broncos face the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano believes Pat Bryant “might force his way into a bigger role than expected.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Graziano mentioned Bryant’s strong offseason as a reason to believe he could see more work in his second season. Bryant appeared to be gaining traction late in his rookie campaign before injuries brought his season to an underwhelming end. He finished the year with 31 grabs for 378 yards and one score. Bryant will top out as the Broncos’ No. 3 receiver to start the year, but he could push Courtland Sutton for targets and routes as the season progresses. His usage in Week 1 will be an important storyline for fantasy managers to monitor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.headline: Broncos listed Marvin Mims, Jr. as a starting receiver for Week 1.
https://www.nbcsports.com/patrick-bryant.analysis: Mims gets a starting slot alongside Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle for the Broncos’ season opener against Kansas City. It’s quite the stunner after Pat Bryant — listed as a second-team wideout — drew consistent praise from Denver coaches this offseason both as an intermediate and downfield pass catcher. Mims, who has been used primarily as a gadget guy, was targeted on 20 percent of his routes last season and ended the year with 322 yards over 15 games. Bryant’s usage will be something to monitor in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.headline: Dion Dawkins (ribs) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.analysis: Dawkins and starting LG Alec Anderson (ankle) have now missed two practices this week. This is concerning. The Bills face the Vikings’ elite, blitz-based defense in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game. Hopefully, the extra day off helps them return in time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.headline: Dion Dawkins (ribs) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.analysis: Dawkins, the Bills’ left tackle, and LG Alec Anderson (ankle) were both absent today. They have an extra day to rest, since the Bills face the Vikings in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game. Hopefully, the extra time allows them to suit up against Minnesota’s elite defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.headline: Bills declared DE Greg Rousseau, OT Dion Dawkins, DE Joey Bosa, WR Brandin Cooks, S Jordan Poyer, DT DaQuan Jones, and LB Terrel Bernard inactive for Week 18 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.analysis: The Bills’ game has little meaning with the team having locked up a playoff spot. They will either be the fifth or sixth seed, depending on the outcome of this game and the Texans’ game. The team might believe that they can beat the Jets without many of their starters, but we wouldn’t expect many starters to play key snaps here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.headline: Bills LT Dion Dawkins (illness) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.analysis: Players typically play through illnesses, but it would be nice to see Dawkins practice tomorrow after sitting out on Wednesday and Thursday. The Bills’ offensive line is tasked with fending off the Browns’ elite pass-rush unit this week. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.headline: Dion Dawkins cleared concussion protocol and will play in Week 14 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.analysis: Dawkins was out of the non-contact jersey on Thursday and is now on track to play on Sunday against the Bengals. While Dawkins will be back in action after one game away, head coach Sean McDermott said EDGE Joey Bosa and LB Terrel Bernard would be out in Week 14, while WR Joshua Palmer will be listed as doubtful.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.headline: Dion Dawkins (concussion) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.analysis: He did, however, shed his non-contact jersey, so he may be closer to clearing concussion protocol. Dawkins and Spencer Brown (shoulder, limited for the second day in a row) are both trending towards playing on Sunday, or at least hitting the questionable line on Friday. It would do wonders for Buffalo’s offense to have their bookend tackles back on Sunday against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.headline: Bills LT Dion Dawkins (concussion) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.analysis: Bills RT Spencer Brown (shoulder) also upgraded to limited. Both players were sidelined for the entirety of Week 13. The Bills face the Bengals’ pushover pass-rush unit in Week 14. Although the offense can likely get by without their starting offensive tackles, having them on the field would give Buffalo a significant edge in the trenches. Bills LB Terrel Bernard (elbow) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.headline: Bills LT Dion Dawkins (concussion) will not play in Week 13 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.analysis: Head coach Sean McDermott also ruled out RT Spencer Brown (shoulder), LB Terrel Bernard (elbow), and WR Curtis Samuel (elbow/knee), for Sunday’s contest. With both bookend tackles sidelined, the Bills will likely roll with Ryan Van Demark at left tackle and Chase Lundt at right tackle, which could make life tough for Josh Allen against a defense that has the fourth-highest blitz rate and fifth-highest sack total (34) this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.headline: Bills LT Dion Dawkins (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.analysis: Dawkins appears unlikely to suit up in Week 13 against the Steelers after entering the NFL’s concussion protocol and missing Wednesday’s practice. That would leave the Buffalo offense without both starting tackles against an aggressive Steelers pass rush. It could mean another outing full of pressures and hits for Josh Allen, who was banged up last week against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.headline: ESPN reports that the “NFL is introducing the Protector of the Year Award, which will be given to the league’s best offensive lineman.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dion-dawki.analysis: NFL executive vice president of football operations Troy Vincent credits Bills LT Dion Dawkins and retired OT Andrew Whitworth for the award’s creation. Per ESPN, the “winner will be decided by a panel that includes a number of former offensive line greats.” Whitworth adds that Protector of the Year Award “isn’t just about stats—it’s about the mindset, grit, and leadership it takes to be the foundation of a football team.” The phrasing indicates that all offensive line positions will be eligible for the award, not just the high-value left tackle position that stars in today’s pass-heavy league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman (shoulder) was limited on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman’s fantasy-scoring outlook has been hurt by his teammate’s improving health. At this point, Coleman is more so a single-game DFS FLEX rather than a starter in 12-team re-draft formats. He should be good to go for Week 9’s Monday Night Football game though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman was seen wearing a red non-contact jersey at today’s practice. His limited session to begin the week puts him on track to face the Vikings in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game. With DJ Moore (shoulder) back in the lineup, Coleman is just a WR4/FLEX. Joshua Palmer (hamstring) did not practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman caught 4-of-6 targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 6 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman’s six targets tied for second-most on the Bills with Khalil Shakir, who also found the end zone in this one. Coleman scored on an impressive 12-yard play by Josh Allen, who appeared ready to take off and run with the ball before spotting Coleman open in the end zone and flipping a shovel pass to him for the score. Coleman has now scored in three straight games and has been targeted six or more times in two of his last three. With the Bills now heading into their Week 7 bye, Coleman could face more target competition when they return in Week 8 against the Ravens if DJ Moore (shoulder) is active. Moore was questionable entering this week and ruled out 90 minutes before kickoff, so it wouldn’t be surprising if he was a full-go after the bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman caught 1-of-2 targets for seven yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 5 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman was largely erased by the lockdown corner play of the Rams but had a receiving line also heavily influenced by a ground-heavy game plan from a Bills team that attempted only 19 passes in almost 70 minutes of football. It was quite the letdown fantasy performance for managers looking to take advantage of the absences of both DJ Moore and Joshua Palmer. Coleman is a borderline FLEX play in Week 6 against the Raiders, pending the status of Moore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Joshua Palmer (shoulder) was added to the injury report on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Palmer seemingly injured his shoulder in practice today. The Bills may already be without WR DJ Moore (shoulder) on Monday night. While Palmer is not relevant in 12-team leagues, his potential absence would improve Keon Coleman’s stock.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 5 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman should be good to go for the Bills’ Monday Night Football game against the Rams this week. He had a career day in Week 4, with a 6/116/1 receiving line. We have seen Coleman produce solid outings in the past, so caution is advised if one is to consider believing the hype. That said, he rose to the occasion last week and could do so again in what should be a high-scoring game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman caught 6-of-7 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 4 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: This was the best game we’ve seen from Coleman in a long time. Not only did he show up in the box score, but two of his catches were unbelievable sideline grabs that showed the type of hands that made him an intriguing draft pick out of Florida State. He played on 46 of the team’s 59 snaps and ran a route on 31 of their 40 dropbacks. With D.J. Moore leaving this game with a shoulder injury, Coleman is a priority add on waiver wires before next week’s game against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said WR Keon Coleman (ankle) “should be good to play” for Buffalo’s Week 4 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman was limited on Thursday after a Wednesday DNP and apparently will avoid a questionable tag. He was questionable last week and played through the injury, though he doesn’t draw enough targets to be fantasy-relevant outside of the deepest leagues at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman missed two practices last week before getting in a limited session on Friday. He still suited up and caught one of his two targets for a 37-yard gain. He will likely see a very limited number of reps in practice again this week. Coleman is not on the fantasy radar for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman caught 1-of-2 targets for 37 yards in the Bills’ Week 3 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman was questionable to play with an ankle injury, but he was out there for 32 of the team’s 66 snaps, which was the third-most among wide receivers. His lone catch was a busted coverage down the sideline where a better throw from Josh Allen could have led to a touchdown. Coleman is playing better football this season, but he remains just an end-of-bench flyer if either DJ Moore or Khalil Shakir were to suffer an injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) was limited on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: The Bills are managing Moore’s AC joint sprain fairly well. He should be expected to play in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game against the Vikings. Although it is a tough matchup, Moore remains the WR2 tier in this week’s final game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: There was some concern that Moore may have injured his knee in Week 8 against the Ravens, but he is listed only with the same shoulder issue he has dealt with for weeks, which is good news. Moore should be treated as a WR2 in a very tough matchup against the Vikings on Monday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore caught 4-of-7 targets for 82 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 8 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore’s 82 receiving yards trailed only Dalton Kincaid (86). Playing in his first game since Week 4, Moore did not appear to be slowed at all by his injured shoulder and bounced back quickly on a play where he appeared to land hard on the turf. Moore hauled in an impressive 49-yard grab in the third quarter on a drive that helped set up James Cook for a five-yard rushing touchdown, and found the end zone himself in the fourth quarter on an 11-yard score that gave Josh Allen the Bills’ franchise record for career touchdown passes. The seven targets Moore saw were on par with what have come to expect from him pre-injury, which is a good sign for him going forward. He appeared to suffer a minor knee injury near the end of the game, but said afterward it wasn’t too serious. That will be something to monitor, but assuming he’s good to go, Moore will be on the WR2 radar next week on the road against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) is active for the Bills’ Week 8 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore and TE Dalton Kincaid are both officially active, giving the Bills two of their top playmakers in what projects as one of the best matchups of the Week 8 slate against the Ravens. Moore returns for his first game since Week 4 and has caught 12 passes for 178 yards and one touchdown on 19 targets. He’ll profile as a fringe WR1/WR2 at home. The Bills declared WR Skyler Bell, CB Dee Alford, S Jalon Kilgore, LB Mike Danna, OG Ar’maj Reed-Adams, OT Spencer Brown, and DL Greg Gaines inactive for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports DJ Moore (shoulder) is expected to play in Week 8 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore missed the Bills’ previous two games but had the bye week to get healthy. He was limited in practice throughout the week before being listed as questionable. He’s likely still not at full strength, but fantasy managers can’t be too concerned given the game environment. The Bills’ matchup with Baltimore has all of the makings of a shootout. Moore was also operating as Josh Allen’s clear No. 1 receiver before aggravating his shoulder injury. Moore is a strong WR2 option for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said DJ Moore (shoulder) is questionable for Buffalo’s Week 8 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore has practiced with a non-contact jersey on, in a limited fashion, both of the first two days of the practice week after coming off bye. He got in a third limited session on Friday. This isn’t exactly an exciting run-out after the bye, but Moore probably is on the optimistic side of questionable and any fantasy player that is breathing should be elevated in a game projected to have Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson at quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) was limited in practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: The consecutive limited showings seems to indicate Moore is on track to return from a two-game absence, something we should get further fidelity on after Friday’s practice. There remains a possibility that Moore carries a questionable designation into the weekend if he is unable to upgrade to a full participant Friday, leaving fantasy managers hopeful yet uncertain as we near the weekend. Moore would return to a WR2 profile when the Bills take on the Ravens, if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said DJ Moore (shoulder) will practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore missed the Bills’ past two games because of the recurring shoulder injury. He got in one limited practice in Week 6. The team listed him as questionable but ultimately held him out. A Week 7 bye could not have come at a better time, and he now appears likely to return for Buffalo’s upcoming date with the Ravens. In a likely shootout with Baltimore, Moore will be back in the WR2 mix once he gets the green light to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) is inactive for Week 6 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore was considered legitimately questionable entering the weekend after logging only one practice. He will now miss a second straight game with the shoulder injury he suffered in Week 4, paving the way for Keon Coleman to again see significant snaps. While Moore is out, Josh Palmer, who was questionable with his own shoulder injury, is active. The Bills declared DT Ed Oliver, LB Mike Danna, and OG Ar’ma Reed-Adams inactive for Sunday’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: The Athletic’s Joe Buscaglia notes that Moore resumed practicing today after sitting out on Wednesday and Thursday. He did the same thing last week before being labeled questionable and ultimately ruled out on game day. It looks like he’s a game-time decision again this week. If active, he can be started as a WR2, but re-injury remains a risk.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (chest) practiced in full on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid remained limited in all three practices last week, so today’s return to full participation is great to see. The Vikings’ blitz-based defense often requires tight ends to stay in line to block, which could hurt Kincaid’s route volume. Regardless, he is too talented to be removed from the TE1 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid should be good to go for the Bills’ Monday Night Football game against the Vikings. It’s a tough matchup, and he could be asked to block more than usual. Still, Kincaid warrants TE1 treatment thanks to his talent, usage and quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 4-of-6 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 8 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Playing through a chest injury that he suffered in Week 6, Kincaid didn’t appear to be slowed at all in what was a strong outing against the Ravens. Kincaid ripped off a 40-yard gain in the fourth quarter to help set up an eventual touchdown pass to DJ Moore, and on the following drive, he broke free down the right sideline to haul in a 23-yard touchdown reception of his own. Kincaid dropped what appeared to be a walk-in touchdown earlier in the game, which could have resulted in a much bigger fantasy day, but fantasy managers won’t be mad at this output. He has now drawn eight and six targets in his last two games and will be in the TE1 mix next week when the Bills take on the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid is active for the Bills’ Week 8 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: It was reported shortly before inactives were announced that Kincaid was expected to play. Now that he’s officially active, he will join DJ Moore, who is returning from a shoulder injury, to face a stingy Ravens defense. Despite some highly volatile performances this season, Kincaid will be in the TE1 mix this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports Dalton Kincaid (chest) is expected to play in Week 8 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid got banged up late in Week 6 and then got a bye week to rest up. He was limited in all three practices this week before being listed as questionable for Week 8. Kincaid will play a part-time role, per usual, but his elite efficiency has been enough to keep him in the TE1 mix so far. Playing in a shootout with the Ravens, he’ll remain in the top 12 tight ends this week as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said Dalton Kincaid (chest) is questionable for Buffalo’s Week 8 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid was limited in all three practices this week. We’d imagine he’s on the optimistic side of questionable, though it’s not altogether great news that he wound up on the questionable line after a bye week to heal up. Kincaid will have to be started if active in what projects as a scoring bonanza against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid briefly left the Bills’ Week 6 game against the Raiders with this injury, though it was called a rib issue at the time. He returned to the contest in the fourth quarter. Buffalo then got a well-timed Week 7 bye. A limited session today is nothing out of the ordinary for Kincaid. We fully expect him to play in Week 8 against the Ravens. In what could be the best game environment of the week, Kincaid remains a solid TE1 option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 7-of-8 targets for 38 yards in the Bills’ Week 6 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid did nearly all of his damage in the short area of the field, but his fantasy managers will take any kind of volume they can get after a three-week stretch where Kincaid saw a dismal seven combined targets. Kincaid’s eight targets led all Bills pass-catchers in this one, and were it not for an 18-yard touchdown taken off the board by a holding penalty, he could have been in line for a much bigger day. It’s far too early to say that Kincaid is “back,” but fantasy managers can at least be happy with a decent day of production. The Bills are now entering their bye week, but Kincaid will be boom-or-bust TE1 in Week 8 against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (ribs) returned in the fourth quarter of Week 6’s game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: With the game tied at 23-23, Kincaid returned to the field with the Bills attempting to take the lead. Whatever he’s dealing with appears to be minor at this point, so he’ll likely attempt to gut out the remainder if this one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (ribs) is questionable to return in Week 6’s game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid exited in the third quarter and went to the blue medical tent before eventually heading for the locker room. Kincaid could be seen holding his ribs while running a route earlier in the game and was in the midst of a good performance. We will check back in with any updates we receive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku (fibula) is doubtful to play in Week 9 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku was limited all week, though he apparently is not ready to return from injured reserve. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats. The Chargers will likely employ a three-player rotation whenever he returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku (fibula) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku’s return is probably a good thing for the offense as a whole, but the Chargers’ tight end rotation makes for a fantasy-unfriendly situation. Njoku does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats. Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku (fibula) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku had his practice window opened this week, giving the Chargers 21 days to activate him off injured reserve. He has been out since Week 3 and is now nearing a return, getting in limited work with a fibula injury on Wednesday. WR Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) was a DNP on Wednesday. Neither Njoku nor Thompson need to be on fantasy rosters just yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: Jim Harbaugh said the team will open the 21-day practice window for David Njoku this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku has been on the shelf since being placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 3, with the potential to return following five missed games plus the team’s Week 7 bye. The team will have 21 days to activate him from short-term injured reserve, meaning Njoku is not guaranteed to be activated in time for Week 9 against the Texans. Fantasy managers that have held Njoku through his time on injured reserve can continue patiently waiting for his return while those in shallower leagues can consider adding him from waivers before he is activated.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: Chargers placed TE David Njoku (fibula) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku was unable to put any weight on his right leg and was carted from the field in Sunday’s loss to the Raiders. Njoku has caught six passes for 67 scoreless yards for the Chargers in his first two games with the team and led all tight ends on the roster with 25 routes run. He’ll have to miss at least the next four games now that he’s landed on IR, but we should have a better sense of his return timeline in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku suffered an apparent leg injury in the second quarter of Week 2 against the Raiders and was carted off the field.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: The team officially called it a knee injury and listed him as questionable to return. Njoku was unable to put weight on his right leg and had to be helped onto the cart. Several Chargers players came to the cart to see him off the field. It looks like his day is done, even if the team is calling him questionable. Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden will see an uptick in routes going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: David Njoku caught all five of his targets for 58 yards in the Chargers’ Week 1 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Njoku logged a pass route on 19 of the team’s 31 drop backs and was third on the Chargers in targets. Oronde Gadsden, meanwhile, ran a grand total of seven routes and caught both of his targets for 32 yards. Charlie Kolar, listed as the team’s No. 1 tight end in August, was not targeted on 13 routes against Arizona. Njoku should have some deep league value as the team’s TE1 in Week 2 against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: The Chargers listed Charlie Kolar as the No. 1 tight end on their Week 1 depth chart.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Way back in late May, the Athletic’s Daniel Popper suggested Kolar, who signed a three-year, $24.3 million contract with the Bolts this spring, would enter the season as LA’s top tight end “because of his complete skill set.” Week 1 usage will tell us a lot about how offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will use his tight ends, but for now it seems Kolar will lead the group in Week 1 against the Cardinals. David Njoku and Oronde Gadsden II, however, could see more pass game involvement depending on how many routes they run in a given week, and whether the Chargers go run-heavy against an opponent. None of the Chargers’ tight ends are particularly appealing fantasy plays for Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: Chargers TE Charlie Kolar caught 1-of-1 targets for nine yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: Kolar earned QB Justin Herbert’s first target of the night on a short out route to the left. Kolar secured the pass but stumbled and was brought down just shy of the first-down marker. PFF’s Nathan Jahnke notes that Kolar shared the field with TE David Njoku on two of the first three plays, but Kolar remained on the field for the Chargers’ first 11 personnel package. Kolar looks like the Chargers’ No. 1 tight end. He was a talented prospect but has contributed sparingly as a receiver in the NFL to this point, making him a coin-toss TE2 for fantasy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.headline: Chargers TE Oronde Gadsden caught 2-of-3 targets for 21 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-njok.analysis: The second-year incumbent tight end is seemingly behind the Chargers’ free agent signee veteran TEs Charlie Kolar and David Njoku. Neither Kolar nor Njoku suited up this evening. Gadsden can still be viewed as a TE2/3 in best ball formats, but his current role could be undesirable for re-draft purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.headline: Texans ruled out Reed Blankenship (consussion/hand) for Week 9 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.analysis: The Texans will be without Blankenship this week, but they get Jalen Pitre (shoulder) back. The Texans’ defense has underperformed this year, as has the Chargers’ offense. Perhaps one of the units can facilitate a get-right outing for the other.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.headline: Reed Blankenship (consussion/hand) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.analysis: Blankenship has been dealing with a concussion since Week 6 and still has it listed as an injury designation nearly three weeks later. He is also listed with a hand injury. Blankenship will need to progress through concussion protocol to have a chance at playing in Week 9; he is on the wrong side of questionable for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.headline: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports David Montgomery (groin) will not play in Week 7 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.analysis: This will be the second game in a row that Montgomery has missed due to the groin injury he suffered in Week 5. Woody Marks, who totaled 17 touches in last week’s win over the Jaguars will again lead the Texans’ backfield. He has averaged 18.0 touches per game over the last two weeks and will be a volume-based RB2 with a chance at significant upside. Safeties Jalen Pitre (AC joint) and S Reed Blankenship (concussion) will also miss this week’s game against the Giants, putting the Texans down a handful of starters with one game left before their Week 8 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.headline: Reed Blankenship (concussion) was ruled out of Houston’s Week 6 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.analysis: Blankenship suffered the concussion near the end of the first half and was carted off with a towel over his head. MJ Stewart took over at safety for a suddenly-ordinary Texans defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.headline: Texans agreed to terms with S Reed Blankenship, formerly of the Eagles, on a three-year, $24.8 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.analysis: Blankenship made the Eagles’ roster as a UDFA in 2022. He served as a backup during his rookie season before earning a starting role in 2023. Blankenship never gave up that job and went on to start 46 reglar season games plus five postseason contests during his time in Philly. Blankenship broke up four passes and intercepted one in 2025. He will slot into a starting role on an elite Houston defense this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.headline: Eagles CB Darius Slay (concussion) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.analysis: Slay missed Week 13 with the concussion after failing to return to practice at any point in the week. Even a limited session on Wednesday would put him on track to return for Week 14. Safety Reed Blankenship suffered a concussion of his own on Sunday and did not practice today. He will likely miss Philly’s upcoming matchup with the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.headline: Eagles S Reed Blankenship suffered a concussion in Week 13 against the Ravens and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.analysis: Blankenship was ruled out at the end of the third quarter after heading to the locker room with the brain injury. The veteran safety signed a one-year extension in the offseason and has been giving the Eagles their money’s worth and then some. He has three interceptions, five pass breakups, and a fumble recovery this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.headline: Eagles signed S Reed Blankenship to a one-year contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.analysis: Blankenship was in the final year of his deal but will now be under contract through 2025. The former UDFA from the 2022 class has appeared in 25 games for the Eagles over the last two years and started in all 15 games he appeared in last season. In his brief career, Blankenship has totaled four interceptions and one fumble recovery and earned a PFF coverage grade of 78.0 last season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.headline: Eagles S Reed Blankenship (groin) is not participating in Saturday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.analysis: Blankenship is in danger of missing the Eagles’ Wild Card game against the Buccaneers with a groin injury. He missed practice on Saturday and head coach Nick Sirianni said he would be a game-time decision. If Blankenship cannot go, Avonte Maddox is likely to step up in his place.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.headline: Eagles S Reed Blankenship (concussion) is questionable to return to Week 14 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.analysis: Blankenship took the brunt of an attempted tackle attempt to the head in the second quarter of the team’s Week 14 game against the Cowboys. He was removed from the game by the independent neurologist and was ruled questionable to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: 49ers ruled out Christian Kirk (knee) for Week 9 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: At this point, Kirk probably does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues. He returned from his lengthy calf injury only to injure his knee. It’s a tough break for the veteran wide receiver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (knee) was not spotted at the open portion of Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk was limited Wednesday with his knee issue, and it’s possible he’ll get that designation again in the closed portion of practice. The 29-year-old still has a decent chance to play in Week 9 against the Raiders, but even with the litany of injuries for the 49ers in their receiving corps, it’s hard to trust Kirk from a fantasy perspective.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk comes out of the 49ers’ bye as a limited practice participant due to a knee issue. He was not targeted in Week 7 after returning off a calf injury and should remain off fantasy rosters even if he plays in Week 9 against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk was not targeted in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk was activated off the injured list this week after missing the first six games of the season with a calf injury. He played on just 20 of the team’s 66 snaps and ran a route on 14 of their 43 dropbacks. Kirk was always likely to be eased back into things, and the 49ers have a bye next week to get him more up to speed. That being said, he doesn’t figure to be a huge part of this passing game if the 49ers can get more of their receivers back healthy after the bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: 49ers activated Christian Kirk (calf) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The 49ers would normally have Kirk on a pitch count for his first game of the year. With their top four receivers unavailable for today’s game, Kirk may be thrust into a full-time role right away. He will be in the mix for WR1 duties in San Francisco alongside Brandin Cooks and Jordan Watkins. Kirk is a long-shot FLEX option for his first game as a 49er.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) is questionable for San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: We’ve heard worse desperation options than “most accomplished 49ers wideout on paper playing with Brock Purdy and George Kittle as Mike Evans sits.” Kirk probably factors in the WR3/WR4 calculus after being activated from injured reserve Saturday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk is on track to make his 2026 debut this week in the 49ers’ game against the Falcons. As strange as it sounds, Kirk has a chance to vault into the 49ers’ No. 1 wide receiver role with Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) expected to sit out this week. Kirk should be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) was a full participant in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk was limited all of last week but starts out this week listed as a full participant for the 49ers’ Wednesday walkthrough practice. He remains on injured reserve, but head coach Kyle Shanahan said Kirk is a “possibility” for Week 7. A full practice listing is a good start and Kirk could see WR3 volume immediately with Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel dealing with injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said Christian Kirk is a “possibility” for Week 7.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk has been on injured reserve with a calf injury but could return to the Niners’ injury-ravaged receivers room this Sunday against the pass-funnel Falcons defense. “He had two good practices (last week). It was just his first two practices of the year,” Shanahan said of Kirk, who last year had 239 yards and a touchdown in 13 regular season games for the Texans. “We were down on wideouts, so it was still something we discussed, but we decided to give it another week.” If Kirk returns and plays something close to a full complement of snaps against Atlanta, he could function as the team’s No. 1 receiver with Mike Evans (Achilles) seemingly unlikely to suit up. Kirk should be rostered in most 12-team leagues and all deeper formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) won’t play in San Francisco’s Week 6 game against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: He won’t be activated off injured reserve for this one, but he did practice three times this week and he may be a consideration for Week 7’s game if things continue to trend in this direction. This means Brandin Cooks should operate as San Francisco’s No. 2 wideout assuming Mike Evans plays.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarcus-r.headline: Demarcus Robinson (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Raiders.

They could get a small boost with Christian Kirk a candidate to be activated from injured reserve ahead of Monday’s game, although Mike Evans is also listed as questionable.
