McCaffrey then sat out on Wednesday before practicing in a limited capacity on Thursday. He should be in fantasy football lineups this week, facing a soft Raiders run defense, but Kaelon Black could mix in for 8-10 touches, potentially warranting FLEX consideration.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) was able to participate in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: A rare bit of good news on the injury front for the 49ers. McCaffrey was given the day off Wednesday. Even though today’s activity only resulted in a limited session, it’s a good start for what could be a Week 9 date against the Raiders that sees the tailback get a smorgasbord of touches due to the issues involving several injured receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said more than a week ago that McCaffrey has a “mild” hamstring strain. Hamstring strains can be finicky. If Kaelon Black is available, add him immediately. McCaffrey still has a chance to play in Week 9 against the Raiders’ soft run defense, but he is ever so slightly in the questionable column at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Kyle Shanahan said Christian McCaffrey has a “mild” hamstring strain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: That explains McCaffrey’s brief departure in the team’s Week 7 loss to the Falcons, when the veteran alpha missed most of the second quarter but returned for the second half. 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan added that he believes McCaffrey will be fine when the team comes out of their Week 8 bye. “We’re pretty optimistic,” he said Monday. Fantasy managers appear to have dodged a bullet with the first-round fantasy powerhouse but will want to continue to monitor reports from the team through their bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey rushed seven times for 39 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 7 loss to the Falcons, adding 61 receiving yards on six catches.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey scored a touchdown on the first drive of the game and had six touches, which seemed to set the tone for a massive workload. However, he also picked up a thigh injury on that drive and didn’t return again until the third quarter. The 49ers seemed to give him a few extra breaks in the second half, but McCaffrey didn’t look any less explosive. He was also half a yard away from catching a touchdown pass in the fourth quarter, but he was ruled down short of the end zone, and then Brock Purdy threw a touchdown pass to Kyle Juszczyk on the next play. The 49ers have a bye next week, so we doubt McCaffrey’s thigh injury will be an issue when we see them next in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey (thigh) returned to the game in Week 7 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey was injured on the first drive of the game when the 49ers scored a touchdown. The training staff was working on his thigh before he jogged into the locker room in the second quarter and was listed as questionable to return. It was a 14-3 49ers lead when McCaffrey went into the locker room, and it’s 19-14 in favor of the Falcons now, so the team is going to see if their star running back can get them back in front.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey is questionable to return to Week 7 against the Falcons with a thigh injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey was used heavily on the first drive with the 49ers down so many offensive players, and he came out of that drive with a touchdown but also a thigh injury. The trainers worked on him on the sideline for two drives before finally bringing him into the medical tent. The 49ers do have a bye next week, so they could try to get him back into the game, but they are also up 14-3 at this point, so the Falcons will likely need to get the game closer. Kaelon Black will continue to see a workhorse role while CMC is sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey rushed 16 times for 64 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 6 win over the Commanders, adding 53 yards on nine receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey set a season high with 25 touches and 26 opportunities in a game played without Deebo Samuel and in which Mike Evans departed just before the half with an aggravation of his Achilles injury. The veteran workhorse back again proved how high his ceiling can be with such a robust role through the air. A second-quarter fumble was his first lost fumble since 2024, a stretch spanning over 500 touches since he last lost a fumble. McCaffrey remains an elite RB1 despite a difficult matchup on the ground against the Falcons in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey rushed 11 times for 68 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 5 win over the Seahawks, adding three receptions for 15 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey’s lone touchdown came on an 11-yard touchdown run immediately after the 49ers had recovered a fumble by Emanuel Wilson. He hasn’t had the gaudy yardage totals we’re accustomed to seeing, but fantasy managers won’t be mad at this performance. While McCaffrey has yet to rush for 100 yards in a game this season, he’s gone for 80-plus yards from scrimmage in three of five games and has scored in four straight. He continues to be the only fantasy-relevant running back on the Niners and is set up to smash in Week 6 against the Commanders on Monday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey had 15 rushes for 52 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 4 win against the Broncos, adding three catches for 18 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Denver’s defense focused on slowing down McCaffrey and the Niners’ run game. That forced Brock Purdy and the offense into a more pass-heavy approach. CMC surprisingly was not all that involved in the passing attack against a Broncos defense that has been generous to pass catchers out of the backfield this season. He saved his fantasy day with a goal line plunge in the second half. Kaelon Black, meanwhile, saw six carries on the day. McCaffrey will be a top-5 option in Week 5 against the Seahawks.

Unfortunately, he strained his hamstring in practice today and has now been ruled out. With Colby Parkinson (ribs) questionable, Tyler Higbee sneaks back into the TE1 conversation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters that Terrance Ferguson (ankle) is expected to play in Week 9 against the Commanders.

The second-year tight end offers some volatility, but there’s no denying that there’s upside in his profile. Just don’t be shocked if it isn’t on full display just yet in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was spotted at practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson had his 21-day practice window open up, and it’s a positive sign that he’s been able to practice on back-to-back days. There’s no guarantee he’ll play in Week 9 against the Commanders, but even if he misses that contest, it seems likely the second-year tight end will be back for the second half of the campaign.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams opened Terrance Ferguson’s (ankle) 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Rams coach Sean McVay told reporters that Ferguson will be limited today. The Rams could get their top receiving tight end back on the field this week, but they have slow-played his rehab thus far. It would be unsurprising to see him sit out this weekend. He should be added where available, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Terrance Ferguson (ankle) will not be designated to return from injured reserve this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported last week that Ferguson’s return was still going to take “some time.” That doesn’t make it sound like he’s awfully close to getting back on the field. Tyler Higbee leads the Rams’ tight end room in routes since Ferguson went down, but his production has vanished over the past two weeks. Colby Parkinson scored in Week 6 and Davis Allen found the end zone twice last week. Higbee remains the best fantasy option of the bunch, but he’s nothing more than a low-end TE2 for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Terrance Ferguson (ankle) “will take some time” to come off injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson is eligible to come off injured reserve next week, but Schefter reports that a source told him Ferguson’s recovery “will take some time.” The Rams placed Davante Adams on injured reserve this week and are in desperate need of pass-catching help behind Puka Nacua. Ferguson is a rising receiving tight end for the Rams, but has been on injured reserve since suffering an ankle injury in Week 3. Though he is a good IR stash for fantasy purposes, Ferguson is going to take longer than the minimum four weeks to return. Without a good timeline for return, he can be released from fantasy rosters in dire need of more immediate help during bye weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams placed Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This escalated quickly. Ferguson briefly returned in Week 3 after getting X-rays on his injured ankle, but he was ultimately unable to continue. Ferguson can be kept on squads possessing an injured reserve spot, but dropping him for a needed starter makes sense. He will be eligible to return in Week 8 against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams ruled out Terrance Ferguson (ankle) for Week 4 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson suffered the ankle injury in Week 3 against the Broncos and was taken to the locker room for X-rays. He was cleared to return, but only did so briefly. The intriguing youngster remains a worthwhile hold, but he could end up being questionable to play next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was held out of Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Coach Sean McVay said earlier this week that Ferguson was unlikely to play against the Eagles, and this certainly puts him on the “out” trajectory. The timing could not possibly be worse, as Ferguson was finally producing a little bit, and Puka Nacua (groin) is now set to return. That makes Ferguson a shaky hold in standard-sized 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay said TE Terrance Ferguson (ankle) will likely miss Week 4 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson briefly departed after injuring his ankle in the team’s Sunday Night Football loss to the Broncos, returning for two snaps prior to departing again after his lone reception of the evening. The ankle injury now appears likely to cost the talented young tight end at least one game, with the potential for the absence to linger if the sprain is “more high than low.” McVay also relayed that fellow tight end Colby Parkinson suffered an AC sprain and is considered day-to-day. Veteran Tyler Higbee would be in line to operate as the primary receiving tight end after amassing 62 yards and a touchdown on eight receptions in Week 3, should both miss. Higbee should be added in all formats as a potential TE1 in the immediate future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock (elbow) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Lock has dealt with an injury in his throwing-arm elbow for multiple weeks. He was limited at each Week 9 practice, but told reporters that he was feeling good late on Wednesday. It is tough to say whether this will impact him on game day, but he warrants QB2 treatment against the Cardinals’ soft defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock (elbow) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Lock has been dealing with an injury in his throwing arm since Week 7, but he told reporters that he is feeling good now. Lock played very well as Sam Darnold’s replacement earlier this year. As long as the elbow holds up, Lock should be expected to do so again. He is a viable QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock told reporters that his elbow “felt good” after Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: “It’s doing good. I’m excited to be back out there,” Lock said. “Felt great to get under center, rip some balls yesterday. Feels good.” Lock noted that he’ll go through a normal week of practice, and assuming there’s no setbacks, he’ll be under center in place of Sam Darnold (rib/quad) for Week 9 against the Cardinals. If Lock can’t go, it’ll be Jalen Milroe.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock (elbow) was limited in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Despite being listed as limited with a right elbow injury, Lock is expected to start in place of Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) in Week 9 against the Cardinals. Lock has been dealing with the elbow injury for a couple weeks and was the emergency third quarterback in Week 8 as a result. Fantasy managers can still expect Lock to start, but if the injury is not healed, Jalen Milroe is the next quarterback up for the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock will start for the Seahawks in Week 9 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Sam Darnold is considered week-to-week with a quad injury. Lock himself is only barely healthy, having been relegated to emergency QB3 duties because of an elbow issue for the past two games. He’s clearly close enough to full strength if Mike Macdonald is willing to name him the starter on Wednesday. He did note that Jalen Milroe will also get some reps in practice this week. Lock threw for 422 yards and four touchdowns in a little under two full games earlier in the year. Facing a weak Arizona defense, Lock is in the QB2 mix for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock (right elbow) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: The Seahawks’ backup quarterback is dealing with an injury in his throwing arm, so any calls for Sam Darnold’s benching will have to quiet down. Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (hip), LB DeMarcus Lawrence (knee) and LB Uchenna Nwosu (hip) are questionable. The Seahawks ruled out Chazz Surratt (calf) and LB DrakeThomas (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold’s starting quarterback job is not in jeopardy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: The Seahawks’ head coach stood by his quarterback today, saying Darnold is “definitely part of the solution” to the offense’s recent struggles. Darnold returned somewhat quickly from a glute tendon strain a couple of weeks ago. One wonders if he is still rounding back into form following the early-season ailment. Backup Drew Lock played well in his stead, but the Seahawks believe their Super Bowl-winning quarterback should keep his job. That makes sense to us. He’s a QB2 next week against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said QB Sam Darnold (glute) will resume practicing, but won’t take every rep on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: This means Darnold will likely be listed as a limited participant today. The plan is to ramp him up as the week goes on, and Macdonald said the team would like to have a decision by Friday on whether Darnold will face the Commanders this week. The Seahawks’ quarterback has been sidelined since straining a glute tendon in Week 1. He will probably need to be treated as a QB2 with QB1 upside in his first game back, but his practice participation will clarify his readiness.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Seahawks QB Sam Darnold (glute) “has a chance” to play in Week 3 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: To be clear, Rapoport’s tone was controlled and cautionary here. Darnold can only be considered questionable, at best. The Seahawks’ quarterback “is healing faster than anyone had imagined,” but Rapoport adds that the team wants to be “cautious” with him. Backup QB Drew Lock should probably be viewed as the presumptive Week 3 starter at this time, but it sounds like Darnold can reasonably be expected to play in Week 4 at the latest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold (glute) is on track to practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: FOX Sports’ Megan Olivi reported on Sunday that the Seahawks “are aiming” to have Darnold play in Week 3 against the Commanders. It goes without saying that Darnold will need to get a few days of practice in if he hopes to suit up, making this a big week for the Seahawks’ QB1 as he looks to get back on the field. Darnold’s injury wasn’t as severe as the team initially feared when he exited in Week 1 against the Patriots, but with a game against the 0-2 Commanders on the horizon, it’s possible the team doesn’t look to rush him back to the field if he’s not close to 100 percent. His practice status will be worth monitoring throughout the week, but if he’s held out, Drew Lock will make at least one more start in what should be a plus matchup for fantasy managers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Seahawks ruled out Rashid Shaheed (knee) for Week 9 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: The Seahawks will again be without their speedy, underused wide receiver. Fortunately, Tory Horton (hand) was removed from the injury report and will play this week. He will catch passes thrown by Drew Lock (elbow).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed seems likely to miss another week, though he could technically still turn things around tomorrow. Seahawks LT Charles Cross (ankle) also remains sidelined on Thursday, and LG Quenton Nelson (knee) was downgraded to a non-participant. Hopefully, Nelson’s absence is precautionary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) did not practice in Wednesday’s walkthrough.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Also not practicing is OT Charles Cross (ankle). Both missed Week 8 against the Bears and are still out with their respective injuries to open the week. They will need to practice in some fashion to have a chance at returning for the Seahawks offense in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Seahawks ruled out Rashid Shaheed (knee) for Week 8 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed reportedly avoided a major injury in the collision with teammate Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the end zone in Week 7, an injury that will claim at least one game from the veteran speedster. There’s not really a ton of fantasy value behind Smith-Njigba in Seattle, although veteran Cooper Kupp could see a target or two trickle his way in Shaheed’s absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) remained sidelined for Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed is now firmly on the wrong side of questionable heading into Monday evening’s game against the Bears. If he was in your third receiver or second FLEX spot in a 14-team league, it is time to start making other plans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed received positive news on his knee injury that caused him to leave Sunday’s blowout win over the Chiefs, but there’s a pretty good chance that he’s going to miss at least Week 8’s game against Chicago on Monday. Assuming that’s the case, it will lead to more snaps for Tory Horton both as a receiver and as the primary returner.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said the “early returns are positive” on Rashid Shaheed’s knee injury he suffered in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Macdonald didn’t elaborate on how much time Shaheed could miss, if any, but it doesn’t sound like this is expected to be a long-term injury based on what he had to say on Monday. Shaheed’s impact is largely felt in the punt and kick return game, as he has just 16 receptions for 163 scoreless yards on the season for Seattle. We will update his practice status throughout the week, but Shaheed won’t have any fantasy relevance even if he does suit up next week against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) is questionable to return in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed was involved in a collision with teammate Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the end zone on an interception in the waning moments of the first half and did not retake the field out of the break. Tory Horton received the kickoff to begin the second half, after which Shaheed was deemed questionable to return with a knee injury. Expect Cooper Kupp and Horton to see a small bump in opportunity behind Smith-Njigba for the remainder of the game. Shaheed caught 2-of-3 targets for one yard prior to departing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (hip) is not on the Seahawks’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: The Seahawks’ sporadic producer will be on the field against the Chiefs this week. Shaheed has been involved as a receiver and as a rusher, scoring touchdowns in consecutive weeks. He offers a low floor, but he makes for a viable FLEX starter this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (hip) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed will be good to go for the Seahawks’ Week 7 game against the Chiefs, barring a setback. Unfortunately, his terribly volatile performances keep him in the boom-bust FLEX tier despite four teams being on bye. For what it’s worth, this could be a fantasy-friendly game environment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor (back) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor’s contributions are far too volatile for him to be trusted in 12-team formats, but his presence hurts rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq’s fantasy-scoring outlook. Taylor does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor (back) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor is firmly on track to play in Week 9 against the Chiefs. He will operate as the team’s top tight end, keeping intriguing rookie Kenyon Sadiq in the TE2 tier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: It’s likely a maintenance day for Taylor, who tallied three catches on five targets in Week 8. He has been running ahead of rookie Kenyon Sadiq in recent weeks, though his own fantasy has been hit or miss. Taylor has been held under 40 yards in three of his past four appearances. He erupted for 62 yards and two scores in the fourth. Barring a setback in practice, Taylor will be a low-end TE2 for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 3-of-5 targets for 19 yards in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor’s five targets were third on the team behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell, while fellow seam stretcher Kenyon Sadiq mustered only two looks. Taylor has become a weekly volume presence in an offense that attempts a lot of passes, but he has not established a particularly high floor while his spiked week odds remain practically nonexistent. He’s a TE2 by the letter of the law but not one we would be looking to start in Week 9 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 5-of-6 targets for 62 yards and two touchdowns in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor got off to a hot start on National Tight Ends Day by mossing Dolphins cornerback Jason Marshall Jr in the end zone. Not content with just one score, Taylor double-dipped with a leaping touchdown catch late in the fourth quarter. He also scored the two-point conversion after the play. Taylor is running well ahead of first-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq right now and there’s no reason to expect anything different in Week 8 versus the Raiders. Taylor will be in the TE2 mix next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 4-of-6 targets for 33 yards in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor is now up to 7/57 in two games since returning from his thumb injury. First-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq, who missed most of Week 5 with a concussion, is 3/15 during the same timespan. This Jets tight end targets battle figures to oscillate back and forth, but Taylor is the preferred option for the time being. It’s still not resulting in more than desperation TE2 value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Kenyon Sadiq remains in the league’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: The good news is that Sadiq was able to practice in a limited capacity on Wednesday. Sadiq suffered the head injury in Week 5 against Cleveland and did not return to action. Mason Taylor led the team’s tight ends with a 59 percent route rate against the Browns, catching all three of his targets for 23 yards. If Sadiq remains in the protocol tomorrow, he would be a long shot to play in Week 6. Taylor in that case would be a desperation streaming option in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 3-of-3 targets for 24 yards in the Jets’ Week 5 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Active for the first time since Week 2, Taylor caught the second most balls on the team as Kenyon Sadiq departed with a third quarter concussion. Those are awful developments for Sadiq managers, but almost certainly not enough to create TE2 value for Taylor, even if Sadiq misses Week 6 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Jets TE Mason Taylor (thumb) is practicing in full for Week 5 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor’s return could be problematic for rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq. Sadiq posted a 7/105/1 receiving line two weeks ago before goose-egging last week. Taylor is not a serious receiving threat, but he can eat into Sadiq’s snap share. Sadiq likely remains a viable TE1, but his volatility just increased a tad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Breece Hall (quad) will not play in Week 4 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Hall was initially mentioned as being week-to-week when he was diagnosed with his quad injury, so he was never really considered a candidate to play in Week 4 despite the team waiting until the end of the week to rule him out. With Hall out, the Jets will look to Braelon Allen to handle most of the backfield duties. Allen will profile as a solid RB2 candidate with a chance for more upside in what could be a high-volume day against the Bears. In addition to Hall, the Jets also ruled out OG Dylan Parham (knee), TE Mason Taylor (thumb), and LB Kiko Mauigoa (quad) for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Sione Vaki (ankle) is questionable for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: Vaki and Lions RB3 Jacob Saylors (neck) are both questionable. Vaki did not practice on Friday, having apparently suffered a new injury. Saylors was limited all week. Jahmyr Gibbs should handle his normal, sizable workload.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Sione Vaki had 11 rushes for 65 yards in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings, adding one catch for five yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: It was the first time this year Vaki has seen more than six carries. The Lions went ultra run-heavy in this one to combat the Vikings’ vexing blitz scheme, which led to 35 carries on the day. Vaki should be stashed in most formats in cae Jahmyr Gibbs misses any time in the coming weeks. Vaki would be a potential 20-touch weekly option in such a scenario.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: A DNP to open the week would normally be concerning, but Dan Campbell told reporters earlier today that he was going to get a lot of players “off their feet” during today’s practice. Gibbs appeared to injure his leg while awkwardly sliding to the ground on his final carry of Week 7. The fact that he isn’t listed with a leg injury on today’s report is also a good sign. Sione Vaki is the next man up if Gibbs can’t play this week, but we aren’t overly concerned quite yet. Tomorrow’s injury report will be more telling.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Isiah Pacheco (back) could return in early December.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: According to Rapoport, Pacheco “had surgery to remove a body that was pressing on a nerve in his back.” The 27-year-old back is looking at a 12-week recovery, but if all goes well, he could return for the final month of the season. If the Lions don’t add anybody to their backfield in the coming days/weeks, Sione Vaki and Jacob Saylors will continue to serve as the primary backups behind Jahmyr Gibbs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Lions HC Dan Campbell said Jacob Saylors and Sione Vaki could both push for RB2 touches behind Jahmyr Gibbs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: It’s hard to imagine either Vaki or Saylors having meaningful fantasy value at this point in the season, but it sounds like both will be on the field while Isiah Pacheco (back) is sidelined for at least the first four games of the season. Judging by how Campbell sounded when discussing each player, it sounded like Saylors might be closer to the official RB2, but Campbell didn’t mince words when he said, “I see Vaki getting some reps, too.” Fantasy managers interested in taking a shot on a Lions running back not named Jahmyr Gibbs can consider both Saylors and Vaki as late-round dart throws until we see how their snap shares look in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: The Athletic’s Colton Pouncy believes Sione Vaki has an opportunity to cut into Isiah Pacheco’s touches.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: Vaki was “quietly putting together an excellent training camp last year when healthy” per Pouncy and the 2024 fourth-round pick could cut into Pacheco’s touches if Pacheco continues to not look like the 2022-2023 vintage. Vaki has just seven carries in his first two seasons in the league, but has been active 27 games as a core special teams contributor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Lions declared RB Sione Vaki, LB Zach Cunningham, OL Equakun Kingsley, DL Mekhi Wingo, and DL Chris Smith inactive for Week 4 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: Vaki has missed each of the Lions’ first four games with a groin injury. He did not practice this week and does not appear to be close to returning.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Lions RB Sione Vaki (hamstring) is doubtful for Detroit’s Week 2 game against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: Vaki got in three limited practices this week, but looks unlikely to be available. When healthy, he’s debatably the RB3 on the team, in a heat with Craig Reynolds.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Lions declared RB Sione Vaki, S Thomas Harper, LB Trevor Nowaske, DL Chris Smith, DL Mekhi Wingo, and DL Tyrus Wheat inactive for Week 1 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: Vaki is dealing with a hamstring issue and was ruled out on the final injury report. The Lions are fairly healthy heading into Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.headline: Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press reports Sione Vaki (hamstring) could miss the Lions’ Week 1 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sione-vaki.analysis: Vaki has been dealing with a hamstring injury for the better part of the preseason. The Lions’ fourth-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, Vaki serves as the RB4 and contributes on special teams. The 24-year-old running back isn’t expected to go on injured reserve, according to Birkett, but could miss Week 1 against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions ruled out Cade Mays (ankle) for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Brutal. Mays returned from injured reserve in Week 7 due to a preseason wrist injury. He injured his ankle in Week 8. The Lions ruled out S Kerby Joseph (knee) and CB D.J. Reed (hip), yet S Brian Branch (concussion) will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Cade Mays (ankle) is questionable to return in Week 8 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Mays went down with the injury in the second quarter. His absence will make it even tougher for the Detroit offense to navigate the Vikings’ complex blitzing schemes. Mays has dealt with injuries for much of the past month.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Cade Mays (wrist) is active for Week 7 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Detroit will get back it’s highly-paid free agent acquisition from this past offseason after a preseason wrist injury. The Lions declared TE Jackson Meeks, S Bishop Fitzgerald, C Seth McLaughlin, DL Mekhi Wingo, and DE Ahmed Hassanein inactive against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions activated Brian Branch from the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: The team also activated center Cade Mays from the reserve/injured list. Week 7 will be the first game of the year for both players. Branch tore his Achilles in Week 14 last year and has been out ever since. Currently in last place in the NFC North, the Lions desperately needed this infusion of talent to get their season back on track.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Cade Mays (wrist) is questionable for Detroit’s Week 7 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Questionable but fully expected to play after three full practices, Mays should add some more teeth to the Lions’ run game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions C Cade Mays (wrist) is practicing in full ahead of Week 7’s game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Mays seems likely to be activated off injured reserve ahead of the game given Dan Campbell’s public statements on the matter, him giving a presser today, and the trend to full sessions following the team’s Week 6 bye. It should be an upgrade for Detroit’s offensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions ruled out C Cade Mays (wrist) for Week 5 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Mays and S Brian Branch (Achilles) are not yet ready to return from their injuries. Starting CB Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring) has been ruled out as well, and DL Tyleik Williams (foot) is questionable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions activated C Cade Mays’ (wrist) 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: This is a big deal for fantasy purposes. The Lions signed Mays to a three-year, $25 million contract this offseason, shoring up their center position with a reliable prime-age starter. Mays injured his wrist early in August, so he has not yet taken the field on game day with his new team. The Lions’ permissive defense continues to put the offense into pass-heavy game scripts. Getting Mays back on the field will fortify Jared Goff’s protection. He was limited on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions place S Brian Branch on the reserve/physically unable to perform list with an Achilles injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Branch ruptured an Achilles tendon in Week 14 last year. He is still recovering. The Lions also placed C Cade Mays (wrist) on the injured reserve/designated for return list due to his summer injury. Both players will be eligible to return after missing four games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions HC Dan Campbell said C Cade Mays (wrist) will miss a “significant amount of time.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: The Lions sought to upgrade at center this offseason and went out and signed Mays to a three-year, $25 million contract. Now, the 27-year-old lineman is expected to be sidelined for the next 8-10 weeks after fracturing a small bone in his wrist , per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. Campbell said that the injury is not believed to be season-ending, but it’s still a major blow to the offensive line. Former second-round pick Juice Scruggs came over in the David Montgomery trade and has played center before, so he will presumably get the first crack at taking over in Mays’ absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown rarely misses games due to injuries. Fantasy managers should remain optimistic about his availability. The Lions’ No. 1 wide receiver remained limited all week. Although it might hurt to take hits, we expect St. Brown to suit up this weekend. Regardless, keeping it locked to Rotoworld is a must. Updates will be provided as they roll in.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: It’d be nice to see the Sun God get in a full session, but the fact that the star wideout has been able to practice both days suggest he’ll be just fine for Week 9 against the Dolphins. He’ll be a high-end WR1 for that game and any other contest that St. Brown plays in.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown briefly left the Lions’ Week 8 win over the Vikings but managed to finish the game. A limited session today means the rib injury should be a non-issue by Sunday. The Lions should have no issues picking apart Miami’s atrocious defense this week. Per usual. St. Brown will be a high-end WR1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 7-of-8 targets for 46 yards in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown added ten yards on a carry, which was actually a running catch on a play in which St. Brown lined up fifteen yards behind the line of scrimmage and got a running start like you might see in the CFL. He had a touchdown catch called back in the first half and had to go to the locker room with what looked to be a knee issue. It was only the second time this season St. Brown was held to less than 60 yards. He came into Week 8 ranked fourth in expected fantasy points per game. St. Brown takes on the Dolphins in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) will play in Week 8 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown started the week off with an absence before logging consecutive full sessions to end the week or preparations, ultimately removed from the injury report entirely heading into the weekend. He should be good to go for a normal workload against the stingy Minnesota defense, where fantasy managers can start him with confidence as a WR1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) practiced in full Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: The upgrade from “DNP” to a full session indicates St. Brown will be fine for a normal workload when the Lions face off against the Vikings Sunday, easing fantasy managers’ collective minds after the star receiver was not present at practice Wednesday. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his status on Friday’s injury report, but it certainly appears as if the team will have their veteran alpha for the divisional tilt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: Lions head coach Dan Campbell told reporters on Monday that St. Brown would likely miss today’s practice, so this isn’t much of a surprise. Campbell also told reporters that St. Brown “should be good” for Week 8, so we’re not panicking just yet. St. Brown is one of the few players who can suit up after missing an entire week of practice. Even a DNP tomorrow wouldn’t be the end of the world. For now, fantasy managers can treat St. Brown as a WR1, but a backup plan should be in place. Jameson Williams would vault into the WR1 ranks if St. Brown misses Week 8 versus the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Lions head coach Dan Campbell said Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) “should be good” to play in Week 8 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: St. Brown is dealing with what sounds like a minor ankle injury after Week 7’s win over the Packers. Campbell said he could likely be held out of practice on Wednesday before the team begins ramping him up on Thursday, but tempered any optimism by adding, “We’ll see when we get there.” The 4-2 Lions are playing host to the undefeated Vikings in a game that could end up deciding the winners of the NFC North later in the season. Unless this injury is more serious than Campbell is letting on, we would expect St. Brown to be on the field and operating as a high-end WR1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 9-of-11 targets for 153 yards in the Lions’ Week 7 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: The Sun God didn’t find the end zone in this one, but he did rip off multiple big gains, which included plays of 28 and 40 yards on the Lions’ first two drives — both of which ended with points. St. Brown’s 11 targets led all Lions’ pass-catchers in this one, and his 153 receiving yards are good for the fifth-most he has had in any game in his career. It’s the first time in his career that ARSB has gone for 140-plus yards but failed to score a touchdown, but this was easily one of his best games to date this season. St. Brown hasn’t scored since Week 3’s game against the Jets, but he has gone for 69 or more yards in each of his last three games while seeing 11 targets in every outing. He continues to be as steady a fantasy asset as there is at receiver, and will be in the WR1 mix in Week 8 against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 6-of-11 targets for 69 yards in the Lions’ Week 5 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/amon-ra-st.analysis: Lions coach Dan Campbell tasked St. Brown with punt return duties (2/36) after Tom Kennedy got hurt. While St. Brown looked great weaving through traffic, his first return nearly ended in a lost fumble, but a teammate dove on the loose ball, bailing him out after it was punched out of St. Brown possession. St. Brown nearly had a 43-yard touchdown on a sideline play-action shot on the Lions’ seventh drive, but he couldn’t quite get his hands on it. He almost bagged short scores via out routes on the Lions’ eighth and ninth drives, but his coverage defender effectively challenged the pass on the first and the pass was just out of his reach on the second. He had a nice 36-yard catch-and-run on the eighth drive and nearly nabbed another explosive gain on the sixth drive, but Sam LaPorta accidentally knocked him down 11 yards downfield after St. Brown leapt over a downed Cardinals defender. He had another fumble recovered by a teammate after snagging a pass on a crosser. The Lions’ stud wide receiver will be an elite WR1 against the Packers following the Lions’ Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (quad) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright and Dolphins RB3 Kaytron Allen (quad) are both questionable in this one, though Allen upgraded to full participation on Friday while Wright remained limited. Wright is barely worthy of stashing in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (quad) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright is on track to be available for the Dolphins’ Week 9 game against the Lions, although he is mostly functioning as an infrequently used backup rusher while also serving as the team’s top returner. He is a mid-tier bench stash at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (quad) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Dolphins RB3 Kaytron Allen (quad) was limited. At some point, Allen might get a chance to overtake Wright for the No. 2 role, though Wright remains a capable special teams contributor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright rushed two times for five yards in the Dolphins’ Week 8 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright failed to catch his lone target and returned five kicks for 142 yards. Wright is just a bench stash at this point, with Ollie Gordon operating in a featured offensive role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot/quad) is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright is a mediocre bench stash at this point, with Ollie Gordon playing well in the lead role. Wright does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats, though he may be able to slightly improve his efficiency if his health continues to improve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright rushed six times for eight yards in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright managed just six touches, even with Miami running the ball 41 times today. Wright is the only running back seeing work outside of Ollie Gordon, but the latter is pushing for workhorse status, leaving Wright without much to do. He is somewhere well beyond the RB4 ranks for his Week 8 matchup with New England.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot) will play in Week 7 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright has rushed 14 times for 28 scoreless yards this season and has yet to receive a target in the four games he has appeared in. Fellow running back Ollie Gordon has emerged as the unquestioned RB1 for the Dolphins since the team lost De’Von Achane (knee) in Week 3. Wright is well off the fantasy radar at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot) remained limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright played through this listing ahead of Week 5, but it appears that he simply won’t shake it this year. It makes him hard to trust him as someone who could suddenly usurp the lead role from Ollie Gordon, but we’d be surprised if he didn’t play in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: The Dolphins’ speedy back will likely serve as a change-of-pace option behind Ollie Gordon, who has outplayed Wright since De’Von Achane’s season-ending knee injury. Wright does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright rushed six times for 11 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright entered the day questionable with a foot injury and wound up playing nine offensive snaps with special teams mixed in. The 23-year-old is the clear backup to Ollie Gordon for now, he is best left off fantasy rosters.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Panthers ruled out Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) for Week 9 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips did not practice at all this week, after sitting out the Panthers’ last two games. Losing a key edge rusher will make things harder for the Panthers’ defense. Bo Nix should have decently comfortable pockets, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) will not play in Week 8 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Carolina also ruled out left guard Damien Lewis, who is dealing with a knee issue. Phillips also missed last week’s game because of a hamstring injury. The hope is that the mini-bye after Thursday Night Football is enough to get him back for Week 9. Phillips has 2.5 sacks this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Panthers declared EDGE Jaelan Phillips, TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, QB Haynes King, RB AJ Dillon, C Sam Hecht, OT Stone Forsythe, and EDGE TeRah Edwards inactive for Week 7 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips is a big loss, but it’s an otherwise quiet list for the Panthers vs. a more-injured and undermanned Bucs squad. Phillips is week to week after pulling his hammy in Week 6 against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) is questionable to return to Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips came into this game questionable with a hamstring injury but was able to suit up. Unfortunately, he got hurt early in the first quarter and is unlikely to return. Considering he had the bye week to heal and is not 100 percent, it seems likely that the EDGE rusher will miss some time with the injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Taylor Moton (blood clots) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Moton is tentatively on track to make his return from injured reserve this week. Meanwhile, RT Monroe Freeling (knee) sat out on Wednesday. Panthers DT Tershawn Wharton (neck) is practicing in full, while EDGE Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) was limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said he is “hopeful” Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) will be able to play in Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips went down with a hamstring injury late in Sunday’s game against the Lions and didn’t return to the field. For a player with Phillips’ injury history, there were immediate concerns regarding the severity of the injury, but with a Week 5 bye on tap, the hope is Phillips won’t miss much time, if any. Phillips has totaled two sacks in his first four games of the season. In addition to Phillips, the team is also hopeful that OT Monroe Freeling (knee) will be able to return in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Devin Lloyd (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Lloyd was one of the Panthers’ premier free agent additions this offseason, and he’s already proven to be worth the investment. Lloyd terrorized the Falcons in Week 2 with a sack and two interceptions, one of which was a pick-six. Fellow free agent acquisition Jaelan Phillips was also absent from practice today. He is dealing with a back injury. Though the Browns aren’t a particularly good offense right now, it would still be a massive boon for them if Lloyd and Phillips are out for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Panthers agreed to terms with EDGE Jaelan Phillips, formerly of the Eagles, on a four-year, $120 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the deal includes an eye-popping $80 million guaranteed. The Eagles were reportedly working to retain the 27-year-old (in May) pass rusher, but got outbid by the typically free-spending Panthers. A former Dolphin who flourished during his eight-game trade cameo for the Eagles last season, Phillips finally stayed healthy last year after an injury marred 2023-24 run. That’s a concern going forward, but Phillips is a pass-rushing difference maker when on the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports “Philly isn’t done trying” to re-sign Jaelan Phillips before the legal tampering period begins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: It sounds like the Eagles are making a push to re-sign Phillips before the legal tampering period begins on Monday. Phillips, whom the Eagles acquired at last year’s trade deadline, totaled 28 tackles, two sacks, and one fumble recovery in his eight games with the team last season, and is believed to have a strong market should he become available. While the soon-to-be 27-year-old dealt with two serious injuries in 2023 and 2024, he managed to play in all 17 regular season games in 2025 and is a clear difference maker for any defense he’s on.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Odafe Oweh, Jaelan Phillips, Trey Hendrickson and Boye Mafe are on Dallas’ “radar” in the coming days.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: The Cowboys lost out on the Maxx Crosby trade sweepstakes and will have to pivot — they reportedly had some interest in Hendrickson at the deadline. Oweh probably makes more sense as a younger upside swing, and this is the third of four NFC East teams in on Jaelan Phillips that we’ve heard about.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers (knee) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: The Giants have smartly limited Nabers’ practice participation levels at times this season, allowing him to play very well while returning from last year’s season-ending knee injury. Nabers belongs in fantasy football lineups in this divisional showdown, as usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers (knee) returned to practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers was a surprise DNP with a knee injury on Thursday, but said after practice that he expected to play. His return to the field on Friday suggests he will be good to go for Sunday’s game against the Eagles, but we will still check in with a final status when the Giants announce player designations for the weekend. Assuming he is good to go, Nabers should be treated as a normal must-start receiver against a down-bad Eagles team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers worked with trainers today instead of practicing with his teammates. He told reporters after practicing that he is “good” to go for Week 9 against the Eagles. We believe him. The Giants have managed his reps at times during the practice week this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers (undisclosed) was seen working off to the side with trainers on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: The Giants have limited Nabers’ practice reps from time to time this season. Although he may end up being listed as a non-participant, we are not currently concerned about his Week 9 availability. The Giants’ No. 1 wide receiver is fully dressed in his typical practice attire. An update will be provided when more info is released.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers caught 7-of-11 targets for 111 yards in New York’s Week 7 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: He toasted Derek Stingley Jr. a few times and found a 42-yarder early on in the proceedings. Nabers didn’t come close to scoring, but that was mostly a result of Houston’s bad run defense being an easy mark. He’ll retain WR1 status once he’s back from New York’s Week 8 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: SNY TV’s Connor Hughes believes the Giants will stick with J.J. McCarthy as the starter “for the foreseeable future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: According to Hughes, “this is the player they targeted and wanted” as their quarterback the minute Jaxson Dart (knee) got hurt. Hughes acknowledges that coach John Harbaugh could eventually bench McCarthy later in the year, but it will take more than a bad “game or two” for that to happen. In the meantime, the weekly fantasy football outlooks for Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are more volatile than they were with Jameis Winston at the helm. Selling high could make sense. Hughes adds that McCarthy would have to play like a top-10 quarterback to make the coaching staff consider him for the starting role next season. That outcome seems highly unlikely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers caught 12-of-15 targets for 165 yards in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers was once again heavily involved in the Giants’ passing game, getting the first offensive touch for New York. He saw 15 targets and tallied 165 scoreless yards on the day, with over half of this yardage coming with J.J. McCarthy in the fourth quarter. It’s the third straight 100-yard game for Nabers, who is now fully ramped up from his torn ACL last year. The Giants may be debating between Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy as the starting quarterback for next week. Regardless of the starter, Nabers sees enough volume to be a borderline WR1 for Week 7 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers caught 11-of-20 targets for 121 yards and one touchdown in the Giants’ Week 5 tie with the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers saw 15 of his targets come in the second half after the Giants opted to abandon a mostly useless ground game in a game they trailed for most of the afternoon. Nabers came up with multiple big plays as the Giants mounted their comeback attempt, with his biggest coming on a leaping 17-yard touchdown in the end zone to tie the game at 27-27 with under two minutes to go in the game. Nabers had a key drop on a screen pass in overtime that had a chance to set up a big gain, but he made up for it later in the game with a 28-yard gain as the Giants were trying to position themselves for a potential game-winning field goal attempt. Nabers has now gone for 100-plus yards in back-to-back weeks and has found the end zone in both of those games. He seems to finally be hitting his stride after a slow start to the season, and will profile as a high-end WR2 in next week’s game against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Giants coach John Harbaugh said Malik Nabers (knee) will be “ready to play” on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: It was presumed that Nabers would play after sitting out Wednesday with soreness in his surgically repaired knee. Though this is just our speculation, the Giants may take it easier on their star receiver this week after he hauled in 6/112/1 against the Cardinals in Week 4. He remains on the WR2 line in what has been (when not facing the Cardinals) a rough offense with Jameis Winston under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers (knee) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers is currently going through route running drills with his position group, putting him on track to play in Week 5 against the Commanders. Nabers sat out yesterday, citing extra soreness in his surgically repaired knee, but told ESPN’s Jordan Raanan that he usually feels better as the week progresses. A WR1 finish is in play this week, assuming he is active. He was later listed as limited on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is doubtful to play in Week 9 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Giants coach John Harbaugh told reporters earlier this week that Skattebo is day-to-day. Unfortunately, Skattebo only got in one limited session on Friday. Fantasy managers should expect Devin Singletary to get the start this week. He can be treated as a volume-based FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: At this point, Devin Singletary should be considered the tentative starter for the Giants’ Week 9 game against the Eagles. Singletary could handle a sizable workload, though he was buried on the depth chart as the No. 3 running back for a reason. Singletary warrants volume-based FLEX status if Skattebo cannot play this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Giants coach John Harbaugh said Cam Skattebo (hamstring) remains day-to-day.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan reports that Skattebo once again worked with trainers off to the side at today’s practice. He will be listed as a non-participant. With Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) on injured reserve, Devin Singletary is tentatively in line to start in Week 9 against the Eagles. He would likely be an RB3/FLEX if Skattebo cannot play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) was seen working with trainers on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: The Giants won’t release their first injury report for the week until Wednesday, but in the team’s first practice after its bye week, Skattebo was seen working off to the side with trainers. Skattebo injured his hamstring late on a 42-yard run in overtime in Week 7’s win over the Texans, but said he expected to be okay after the bye. While that may still be the case, fantasy managers will want to check his practice status throughout the week to see if he’s at risk of missing Week 9’s game against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo told ESPN’s Dan Graziano that he thinks he will be okay after suffering a hamstring injury in the Giants’ Week 7 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Skattebo appeared to have tweaked his hammy on a 42-yard run in overtime that had a chance to be the game-winning run for the Giants. Despite the scare, Skattebo said he expects to be okay, especially with the Giants set to enter their Week 8 bye. His status will be one to monitor when the Giants resume practicing ahead of Week 9’s game against the Eagles, but for now, it doesn’t sound like there’s too much to be worried about here. Skattebo rushed 17 times for 124 yards and a touchdown last week after failing to see a touch in Week 6 following his costly Week 5 fumble against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo rushed 17 times for 124 yards and a touchdown in New York’s Week 7 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Skattebo looked rejuvenated after his benching, bulldozing a few Houston tacklers on his touchdown run that ended with a backflip. He did pull up late on a 42-yarder that could have sealed the game, and he seemed to be gesturing towards his hamstring on the sideline. We don’t have a full update on that as the Giants quickly closed out the game thereafter, but Skattebo will get a bye week to heal up as we try to figure out how this Giants backfield will sort itself out. Skattebo’s fantasy value looks to have bounced back to some real extent today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Cam Skattebo “is expected to resume his role as the team’s lead back” in Week 7 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Skattebo was benched for his fumbling issues last week. He did not touch the ball once, while Najee Harris, Tyrone Tracy, and Devin Singletary all got a few opportunities. The team then cut Harris a few days after Sunday’s loss. After a week in the doghouse, Skattebo appears to be back as the team’s top runner, though we still expect a committee approach from John Harbaugh. Rapoport even said that it’s unclear who will draw the start, so we aren’t sold on Skattebo as a safe fantasy option this week. At best, he’s a high-risk RB3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan believes Cam Skattebo “will be back in the mix” in Week 7 against the Texans, likely in “some sort of timeshare with Tyrone Tracy and Devin Singletary.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Sigh. Three-player backfields are generally fantasy-unfriendly situations, and this one is no different. Skattebo is a capable dual-threat player who has seemingly been limited by the significant ankle injury he suffered last year. The Giants could get him more involved in the passing game, but Tracy can contribute there as well, muddying that opportunity. Singletary would not be a contributor for many NFL teams, but lucky him, he’s a New York Giant. Skattebo and Tracy are viable FLEX options, though both are likely touchdown-dependent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: SNY TV’s Connor Hughes believes the Giants will likely try to trade for a running back, and Cam Skattebo is unlikely to return to his prior role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Hughes makes clear that he thinks Skattebo’s time as the clear-cut lead back is over, recapping coach John Harbaugh’s offseason attempts to acquire a bellcow, while noting that Skattebo is currently in the doghouse. Hughes believes Skattebo is a nice complementary player who can function as a physical change-of-pace option. The biggest issue the Giants face in replacing him is cost. He thinks a player like Jonathan Taylor will cost a Day 2 pick, at least, and he is not sure Taylor is worth that, given the Giants’ long-term plans for the 2027 draft capital they’ve accrued via various personnel moves. Trading away Kayvon Thibodeaux is an option, but doing so is challenging with Brian Burns (knee) out for the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Giants released Najee Harris.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: The move comes a couple days after Harris criticized the New York coaching staff for its handling of the backfield touch distribution. “It’s hard to get into a rhythm with one or two plays...if you’re getting a play here and then get taken out for a series, there’s nothing you could do,” Harris said after the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints. “I’ve never been through none of this before.” Harris had 31 rushes for 99 scoreless yards before getting the boot. With Harris gone, Cam Skattebo could get another chance to see increased playing time after being all but benched last week. Tyrone Tracy, who led the team in rushing attempts against New Orleans, could be the de facto lead back for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.headline: Eagles ruled out Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) for Week 9 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.analysis: Campbell will now miss another game, beset by upper-leg injuries. The Eagles also ruled out DBs Michael Carter (abdomen) and Jonathan Jones (hamstring). The Eagles still have talented players available, but the defense is a little banged up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.headline: Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.analysis: Campbell missed the Eagles’ Week 8 game against the Commanders after not practicing all of last week due to hamstring and quad injuries. He starts out this week DNP, along with DBs Michael Carter (abdomen) and Jonathan Jones (hamstring) on the defensive side of the ball. All three will need some kind of practice later in the week to have a chance at reinforcing the Eagles defense in Week 9 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.headline: Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 8 game against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.analysis: Campbell didn’t practice all week and his availability for Week 9 is likely in question as well. Campbell has 49 tackles in seven starts this season despite spending a few early October weeks as an injury report fixtures. IDP leaguers will need to make other plans this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.headline: Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) did not participate in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.analysis: Campbell came out of the Eagles’ Week 7 loss to the Cowboys dealing with hamstring and quad injuries. He starts out the week as an estimated DNP. Campbell will likely need to practice in some capacity in order to play Week 8 against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.headline: Zack Baun (concussion) is not on Philadelphia’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.analysis: He cleared concussion protocol and will, judging by online comments about the Eagles offense, spend 40 minutes Sunday morning throwing himself at Jaguars running backs who are trying to kill clock. Jihaad Campbell (knee) was also cleared.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.headline: Eagles LB Zack Baun (concussion) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.analysis: This is Baun’s second limited practice this week. Fellow LB Jihaad Campbell (knee) resumed practicing in a limited capacity, but EDGE Jonathan Greenard (ankle) and S Marcus Epps (groin) remain sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.headline: Zack Baun (concussion) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.analysis: Baun entered the league’s concussion protocol last week and was unable to practice at all. His return means he is making progress through the protocol and should be able to play in Week 5. On the other hand, fellow lineback Jihaad Campbell is not expected to practice with an unknown injury. It’s still a net positive injury report for Philly, but far from ideal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.headline: Eagles LB Jihaad Campbell (shoulder) is expected to be ready for training camp after undergoing shoulder surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.analysis: Campbell also underwent surgery to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder back in March 2025. He dealt with a triceps injury in-season last year. Per Eagles DC Vic Fangio, Campbell is doing well and might have a chance to participate in a limited capacity later in organized team activities. Campbell totaled 62 tackles, 14 quarterback pressures, two pass breakups and one interception in his rookie season last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.headline: Eagles RB Will Shipley (oblique) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.analysis: Shipley should resume No. 2 running back duties and can be stashed as a high-upside player in re-draft formats. Stud RT Lane Johnson (stinger) practiced in full on Thursday and Friday. The Eagles lost star OLB Nolan Smith (triceps) to injured reserve earlier this week. He will be eligible to return after missing four games. They got good news on LB Zack Baun (knee), LB Jihaad Campbell (triceps) and backup QB Tanner McKee (right thumb), though. All three are good to go. Unfortunately, CB Adoree’ Jackson (groin) is doubtful.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.headline: Eagles LB Zack Baun (knee) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jihaad-cam.analysis: Baun, LB Jihaad Campbell (triceps) and Adoree’ Jackson (groin) all took the day off on Wednesday, which was slightly alarming given the Eagles’ other defensive injuries. Eagles OLB Nolan Smith (triceps) and CB Jakorian Bennett were placed on injured reserve yesterday. Baun, Campbell and Jackson should all be good to go for Week 4, barring setbacks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.headline: Jake Elliott (ankle) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.analysis: The Eagles’ kicker practiced in full today, which was good to see. Given the state of the Eagles’ offense, he may not have many field goal attempts this week, though. Kickers tend to benefit from playing on teams with stellar offenses. The Eagles no longer have one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.headline: Jake Elliott (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.analysis: Even if Elliott is active for the Eagles’ Week 9 game against the Giants, he makes for an uncomfortable start. The offense is struggling with so many starters ailing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.headline: Jake Elliot (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.analysis: Elliot was listed as a limited participant for the Eagles’ Wednesday practice. The 31-year-old has made 6-of-7 field goals this season and all 17 extra points. He is still trending to play in Week 9, but if the Eagles add another kicker sometime this week, that would indicate Elliot’s ankle injury is a real issue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.headline: Eagles and K Jake Elliott agreed to a reworked contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.analysis: Per NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, Elliott’s base salary went down from $6 million to $5 million. In turn, the Eagles guaranteed all of the money. Elliott struggled in 2025, hitting on just 20-of-27 field goal attempts. Four of his misses came from 50+ yards out. This season could be a make-or-break campaign for Elliott.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.headline: Jake Elliott missed his only field goal attempt and made all three of his extra point attempts in the Eagles’ Week 12 loss against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.analysis: Elliott narrowly missed on a 52-yard attempt in the second half as the Eagles choked away a big lead to the Cowboys. He’s now missed three of his 14 field goal tries on the season. The Eagles’ red zone aggressiveness and use of the tush push near the goal line makes Elliott a dicey weekly bet for fantasy purposes. Elliott has one or zero field goal attempts in eight games this season. He should remain on waiver wires in Week 13 against Chicago.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.headline: Eagles signed K Jake Elliott to a four-year, $24 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.analysis: Per ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the deal ties Elliott with Justin Tucker for the crown of highest-paid kicker in NFL history. Elliott went 30-of-32 on field goal tries this year, with only one of his two misses coming from inside 50 yards. He hit all but one of his 46 PATs. The veteran kicker also takes kickoffs for Philly. Despite the Eagles’ downturn in 2023, Elliott was a top-five fantasy kicker. He will rank among the league’s top fantasy options at the position heading into 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.headline: Eagles restructured K Jake Elliott’s contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.analysis: The Eagles save $2.492 million against the cap with the restructuring of Elliott’s deal. The veteran kicker converted on 20-of-23 field goal attempts for the Eagles last season and has converted on 89.3% of his field goal attempts since 2021.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.headline: K Jake Elliott (ankle) is off Philadelphia’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.analysis: He’ll be Philadelphia’s kicker for Week 6’s game against the Cowboys after missing Week 5. He’s not a terrible streamer, but Dallas’ defense has been imposing enough that it’s hard to call him an easy streamer for Week 6 if he was dropped in your league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.headline: Jake Elliott (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.analysis: Elliott did kick at Eagles practice per several reporters on the scene with video evidence. There’s been no mention of Elliott’s status in interviews so far. Cameron Dicker is the backup Eagles kicker and would get another go against the Cowboys if Elliott can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.headline: Jake Elliott (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-ellio.analysis: Elliott missed Week 5 after going down with an injury in the ankle of his kicking leg. Rookie kicker Cameron Dicker took his place in Week 5. Dickerson nailed both of his extra points and both of his field goals. If Elliott misses another week, Dickerson is a solid streaming option at kicker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Eagles ruled out Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) for Week 9 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks and DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will both miss this weekend’s game, before taking the week off next week as well. The Eagles go on bye in Week 10. Hopefully, the added rest will allow Wicks to be healthy down the stretch.
