https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: At this point, fantasy managers should expect Wicks to take the field next in Week 11, following the Eagles’ Week 10 bye. He does not need to be held on 12-team rosters at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was not seen at the start of Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks hasn’t played or practiced since Week 6. It doesn’t look like he has much of a shot at suiting up this week. With a Week 10 bye up next, fantasy managers in even the deepest of leagues can cut Wicks loose.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 8 game against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: He didn’t practice all week and has not practiced since the build up to Week 6. As with colleague DeVonta Smith, Wicks enters next week questionable to play and with the Eagles having a Week 10 bye, we wouldn’t be surprised if Wicks sat that game out as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was not spotted at Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks has not practiced since before Week 6’s loss to the Panthers and should be seen as doubtful heading into Friday’s practice session. We’d be surprised if he played in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Both Smith and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were estimated DNPs for the Eagles’ walkthrough. Both players missed Week 7 against the Cowboys and start off on the wrong side of questionable to open Week 8. Smith and Wicks will need to at least get a limited practice session in before they can be considered as potential fantasy options against the Commanders. With Britain Covey (knee) also DNP, the receiving corps is sparse. If neither can go, Darius Cooper and Hollywood Brown get a boost from the WR group while TE Dallas Goedert becomes the No. 1 pass-catcher in the Eagles offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) has been ruled out for Week 7 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) also sidelined, life will not be easy for Tanner McKee on Monday evening, even in a plus matchup. Wicks drew some summer hype as a well-paid reclamation project for the Eagles, but he has caught more than three passes only two times all season and has not reached 70 yards since Week 2. He is a poor hold in 12-team leagues with five-man benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Eagles ruled out DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) for Week 7 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: The Eagles will be without their top two receivers but got good news Saturday with the removal of Dallas Goedert from the injury report. Saquon Barkley is listed as questionable and appears to be a true game-time decision. Considering the low involvement of the backfield in the pass game this season, Goedert stands to benefit the most from the absences at wide receiver. He can be started as an upside TE1 in a solid on-paper matchup against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks has been banged up for weeks, and the Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane said Wicks might miss the Eagles’ Week 7 game against the Cowboys. Hopefully, he resumes practicing tomorrow. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks swaps out his multi-week hamstring injury for an ankle injury. He managed to play through it in Week 6 against the Panthers after meeting with the training staff. We expect him to face the Cowboys on Monday night, but he is just a boom-bust FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) is not on the final injury report for Week 9 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley will again play through his hamstring and back injuries. Touchdowns have helped offset Barkley’s moderate yardage totals, and the offense will now be led by Joe Milton. Barkley’s role and talent keep him in the high-end RB2 tier, though an apex outcome is perhaps unlikely, given the state of the Eagles’ offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley is again on track to play through his injuries on game day. The Eagles’ offensive centerpiece totaled 54 scrimmage yards, one catch and one touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 8 loss to the Commanders. He may have trouble solidifying a spot in the RB1 tier, given the state of the Eagles’ offense, but he remains a high-end RB2 at worst, based on talent and usage.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) was not seen at the start of Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley played through the pair of injuries last week, turning 13 carries into 30 yards and a score. While this could just be maintenance for a banged-up veteran, the Eagles are waving the white flag on 2026 by starting Joe Milton at quarterback. If they’re worried about making Barkley’s injuries worse, the team may simply shut him down for the year at some point. Elijah Mitchell is the next man up for Philly if Barkley doesn’t play in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley said the Eagles informed him that they don’t intend to trade him ahead of the NFL trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Speaking with the media early Monday morning, Barkley said he was informed that the team would not be trading him despite falling to 2-6 on the season after Sunday night’s loss to Washington. Barkley rushed 13 times for 30 yards and a touchdown in the loss while catching one pass for another 24 yards. The soon-to-be 30-year-old back could have decent trade value for the Eagles in what is shaping up to be a lost season, but it sounds like he’s in the team’s future plans heading into 2027. Barkley is playing through injuries and has just 56 carries for 274 yards and two touchdowns this season, and has caught seven passes for another 41 yards. Assuming he can get in another week of practice this week, he’ll be a fringe RB1/RB2 in Week 9 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley rushed 13 times for 30 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 8 loss to the Commanders, adding 24 yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley showed clear limitations as he played through hamstring and back injuries, routinely spotted on the sideline riding the stationary bike and getting stretched out by trainers as he rotated with Elijah Mitchell. The Philadelphia offense remained largely ineffective as they gained only 268 yards of total offense, while Barkley’s longest carry of the game went for only five yards against a solid Washington run defense. Fantasy managers will want to consider their alternatives when the Eagles face the Giants in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Saquon Barkley “will not be traded before next week’s trade deadline.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Though teams can change their minds in very short periods of time, Rapoport’s wording on this matter is rather definitive. Sitting at 2-5 with Jalen Hurts out for the year, it makes sense for the Eagles to be sellers at the trade deadline. Players including Dallas Goedert, Riq Woolen, and Hollywood Brown have also been the subject of trade rumors. All three are more likely than Barkley to land with new teams over the next week. Barring a change of heart from GM Howie Roseman, Barkley will continue to be the focal point of a failing offense for the remainder of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring, back) was removed from the injury report Friday and will play in Week 8 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley gave a cryptic response when asked if he would play earlier in the day, ultimately ready to gut out multiple injuries as the Eagles continue to trudge forward in an injury-decimated season. The veteran back added that the injuries are both something he will need to manage throughout the game but that he feels as if he can play through them. That leaves fantasy managers in a sticky situation, likely forced to start Barkley if he’s on the roster. Barkley is a middling RB2 in a difficult matchup on the ground against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) was spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: After being a DNP in each of the Eagles’ first two practices of the week, it’s far too early to be confident that Barkley will suit up on Sunday night against the Commanders. That said, his return to the field is still an encouraging sign for the Eagles, whose backfield is suddenly among the most banged up in the league. We will check back in when the Eagles announce Barkley’s Week 8 status, but it wouldn’t be surprising if this ends up being a game-time decision, which could prove frustrating for fantasy managers. We should know more on his availability in the next few hours.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) was not spotted at Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: This doesn’t look ideal. Barkley practiced all week leading up to his return, and at this point he doesn’t even have a limited session ahead of Sunday’s game with the Commanders. There’s probably not a zero percent chance that Barkley is playing, but at this point the best Barkley-reliant managers can likely hope for is a questionable tag on Friday. Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue would be in line to form some sort of committee if Barkley can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) did not participate in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley was predictably a non-participant after re-aggravating his hamstring injury and additionally injuring his back in Week 7 against the Cowboys. Despite the injuries, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported that Barkley said his hamstring “came out great” and he doesn’t believe his back will keep him out. With every other Eagles running back suffering long-term injuries, Barkley is attempting to gut out his injury issues. Given his re-aggravation last week, it is well within the range of outcomes for Barkley to see limited snaps in Week 8 against the Commanders. His motivation to play makes us think he is on track to be active on Sunday but Barkley is a risky RB2 as he deals with injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: As expected, Smith will miss another week after not being able to practice due to his ankle troubles. The 27-year-old wideout could be an option after the Week 10 bye, but nothing is certain. The Eagles’ passing attack should be completely avoided for their divisional showdown with New York.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith will almost certainly miss the Eagles’ Week 9 game against the Giants. Philadelphia goes on bye next week, so fantasy managers will likely have to wait until Week 11 to get Smith back in their lineups. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) was not seen at the start of Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith has been out since Week 6, which was his first game back from a two-week absence. In the middle of a lost season, there’s no reason for the Eagles to rush their star receiver back. We don’t expect him to play this week and it’s possible he’s out for a while longer. Makai Lemon will likely operate as the team’s WR1 once again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: Eagles declared WR DeVonta Smith, LB Jihaad Campbell, WR Dontayvion Wicks, CB Jonathan Jones, OL Jake Majors , and WR Britain Covey inactive for Week 8 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: The Eagles continue to trudge on without key contributors as they enter Week 8 down their top two wide receivers and starting quarterback. Running back Saquon Barkley is active after being removed from the injury report Friday, with Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue on hand for change of pace duties. Covey’s absence is primarily a hit to the Philadelphia special teams unit, who will continue to require alternate contributions to kick returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 8 game against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: He has not practiced since Week 6. It’s hard to count on Smith to be up for Week 9, though we obviously can’t say anything beyond him being questionable. The Eagles have a Week 10 bye and it might be preferable for them at this point if Smith sat through that — though that is just our speculation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith was not spotted at practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Assuming there’s not a non-media practice portion that adds him to the report, Smith will enter Friday as fairly unlikely to play. We’ll see if he can get on the practice field on Friday. A limited session might get him on to the questionable line. Smith last practiced ahead of Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Both Smith and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were estimated DNPs for the Eagles’ walkthrough. Both players missed Week 7 against the Cowboys and start off on the wrong side of questionable to open Week 8. Smith and Wicks will need to at least get a limited practice session in before they can be considered as potential fantasy options against the Commanders. With Britain Covey (knee) also DNP, the receiving corps is sparse. If neither can go, Darius Cooper and Hollywood Brown get a boost from the WR group while TE Dallas Goedert becomes the No. 1 pass-catcher in the Eagles offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: Eagles ruled out DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) for Week 7 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: The Eagles will be without their top two receivers but got good news Saturday with the removal of Dallas Goedert from the injury report. Saquon Barkley is listed as questionable and appears to be a true game-time decision. Considering the low involvement of the backfield in the pass game this season, Goedert stands to benefit the most from the absences at wide receiver. He can be started as an upside TE1 in a solid on-paper matchup against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane said he got “the sense” that DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will not play in Week 7 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Like Thursday, Smith was sidelined for Friday’s practice. The Eagles have been managing his practice reps and pulled him out for multiple drives in their Week 6 loss to the Panthers. The Eagles face the Cowboys on Monday night, giving Smith an extra day to rest. Consider him highly questionable to play at this time. McLane adds that Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) could also sit out this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: The Eagles held Smith out for multiple drives in Week 6 against the Panthers, in his first game back from a multi-week hamstring injury. He was also dealing with a toe issue. The latter injury is now behind him, and we suspect that his day off today is just a veteran maintenance day. He should be good to go for the Eagles’ Week 7 game against the Cowboys on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson is off the injury report for Week 9 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson got in a pair of limited practices after leaving in Week 8 against the Panthers with a rib injury that required a trip to the hospital. The 6-foot-4 wideout is a WR1 for the upcoming battle against New England.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (rib) was limited during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: It’s back-to-back limited sessions for Watson. It’ll likely be a pain-tolerance issue for the wideout, but assuming he doesn’t suffer a setback in practice, he appears to be good for Week 9 against the Patriots and deserves WR1 consideration.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (rib) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson famously left for the hospital in the middle of Week 8’s win over the Panthers, only to return after halftime like a WWE performer. The fact that they’re letting him practice in any capacity today means he should be able to play through the issue in Week 9. We’d expect him to wear a flak jacket for at least a few weeks. Barring a setback in practice, Watson will be a high-variance WR1 for his matchup with the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught 8-of-10 targets for 113 yards in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The fact that Watson was able to even play in the second half was incredible, as the 27-year-old was forced to be examined at the hospital following a chest injury. He didn’t do much after putting up 100 yards in the first half, but again, that’s not really the story here. Watson told reporters after the game that he was coughing up blood and suffered a fractured rib before returning. Assuming no setbacks, he’s a WR1 candidate for Week 9 against the Patriots, but keep in mind Christian Gonzalez — on top of this injury — can make things difficult.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (chest) returned to action in Week 8 against the Panthers in the third quarter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson went to the hospital to have his chest injury examined, but obviously checked out well if the Packers were willing to reinsert him into a game where they were leading by two scores. It’s a sigh of relief for fantasy managers, as Watson has been sensational Thursday night with six catches for 100 yards in just one half thus far.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson is questionable to return in Week 8 against the Panthers with a chest injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson was hurt on a deep pass in the middle of the second quarter, and went to the locker room to be evaluated and will head to the hospital to be further examined. The 27-year-old was playing well prior to the injury with six catches for 100 yards on his seven targets. Matthew Golden will be the primary wideout target for Jordan Love if Watson can’t return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (ankle) is not on the Packers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson remained limited through the first two practices this week. We do not yet know his Friday participation level, but he seems to be ready for action. Watson belongs in the WR1 tier against a Lions’ pass defense that has freely surrendered big plays this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson appears to just be being managed at this point as Matt LaFleur said there are no concerns on him playing in Week 7. Two limited sessions are often a starting point for a questionable listing, but we’d be surprised if it got that far with Watson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Matt LaFleur said he has no concerns about Christian Watson’s ankle injury ahead of the Packers’ Week 7 game against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The same is true of Matthew Golden, who is dealing with a shoulder issue. Both players were estimated as limited participants for Wednesday’s walkthrough. It doesn’t look like either wideout is at risk of missing the Packers’ upcoming shootout with Detroit. Watson is currently fifth in the league in receiving yards at 538. Golden is sixth at 501. Both players hold a spot in the WR1 ranks heading into Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The Packers held a walkthrough today, so Watson’s status is only an estimate from the team. Given his lengthy injury history, fantasy managers should keep an eye on Green Bay’s injury report tomorrow, though we suspect this isn’t a major issue for Watson. Assuming he gets up to a full practice at some point this week, Watson will be a borderline WR1 for Week 7 versus Detroit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Micah Parsons (knee) was ruled out for Week 9 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons was cleared to resume individual activities but was never likely to play against the Pats this week. The next chance for Parsons to play will be Week 10 against the Vikings, and there’s at least a smidgen of optimism he could be back for that contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Micah Parsons (knee) is a “full go” to do individual work at practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: That doesn’t mean Parsons is a “full go” for Week 9 against the Patriots, however, as the pass rusher comes back from a season-ending knee injury in 2025. Parsons could return soon for a Green Bay defense that ranks 12th in pressure rate and 16th in quick pressure rate on the season. Look for the team to ease Parsons into action to make sure he’s OK for the final stretch of the regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said he expects Micah Parsons (knee) to practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons is not expected to suit up in Week 9 against the Patriots, but this is the next step in his recovery as he looks to return to the field. On Sunday, it was reported that the Packers were targeting a Week 12 return for Parsons, which would mean he plays on Thanksgiving Eve against the Rams if all goes according to plan.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Micah Parsons (knee) is targeting a Week 12 return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons is still working his way back from the torn ACL he suffered late in the 2025 season. Per Rapoport, Parsons is expected to return to practice this week, meaning he will be designated to return from injured reserve in the coming days. He will then ramp up for a few weeks before hopefully returning in Week 12 against the Rams. Green Bay’s Week 11 bye will give him some extra time to get fully up to speed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Micah Parsons (knee) is expected to practice next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: If Parsons returns to practice next week, the Packers will have a 21-day window where he can practice before activating him to the 53-man roster. Pelissero also reported that Parsons’ most likely return date is in Week 11 against the Rams. Including the playoffs, Green Bay is 5-8 since Parsons tore his ACL last December.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said “there’s a chance” Micah Parsons (knee) practices next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: When asked about Parsons’ chances of practicing next week, LaFleur said, “I sure hope so.” He followed that up with, “I’m saying there’s a chance.” Parsons opened the season on the PUP list after an ACL tear late last season. The Packers have a Thursday game for Week 8, leading to a mini-bye where Parsons’ door to practice is at least cracked open.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Packers EDGE Micah Parsons (knee) still isn’t practicing.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: The Packers play the Cowboys on Sunday Night Football on NBC and Peacock in Week 6, but Parsons still isn’t practicing. According to Pelissero, it’s unlikely the 27-year-old defensive end plays before Green Bay’s matchup with the Patriots in Week 9 at the earliest. The Packers’ defense has certainly struggled without Parsons, but they have enough offensive firepower to win shootouts, which only adds to the fantasy floor for Jordan Love and Green Bay’s skill players.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers EDGE Micah Parsons (knee) isn’t expected to practice next week and could return in November, reports the Ringer’s Tom Pelissero.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons is coming back from tearing his ACL late last season. The 27-year-old defensive end didn’t practice this week and isn’t expected to practice next week, according to Pelissero. Parsons hasn’t had any setbacks in his rehab, but still isn’t ready for the Packers to open the 21-day window for him to practice before he’s activated. Pelissero points out that it could be November before Parsons is ready for game action. Green Bay is 1-2 this year and 1-8 without Parsons in the lineup over the last two years (including playoffs).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers HC Matt LaFleur said Micah Parsons (knee) will not practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: Parsons is nearing a return, but the star pass-rusher isn’t ready to get on the field just yet. LaFleur did say that Parsons has not suffered any setbacks in his recovery, while adding that this is “just part of the process.” Parsons’ return window can be opened at any time, which would then give the Packers a 21-day window to ramp him up before activating him from IR.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.headline: Packers placed Micah Parsons (knee) on the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/micah-pars.analysis: This move was expected. Parsons himself said a few weeks ago that a Week 6 return was his “most optimistic” timeline. A spot on the reserve PUP list means Parsons must miss at least the first four months of the season. He is still recovering from the torn ACL he suffered in Week 15 of the 2025 season. Parsons should still be a force on the defensive front when he’s back, but that won’t happen until at least October.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: MarShawn Lloyd (knee) is questionable for Week 9 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: Lloyd popped up on Thursday’s injury report with the knee issue, and now appears to be a game-time decision. Chris Brooks (ankle) is also questionable for the Week 9 tilt, so there could be depth issues for the Pack behind Josh Jacobs, who has struggled in his return to action as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: MarShawn Lloyd was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday’s practice due to a knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: Lloyd was good to go for Wednesday’s session, so this appears to be a new issue. Chris Brooks was also limited by his ankle injury for a second-straight practice. Lloyd and Brooks — if healthy — will be the backups to Josh Jacobs for Week 9, and don’t offer much fantasy upside, if any.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: Josh Jacobs rushed 21 times for 39 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers, adding six catches for 13 yards and another score.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: Jacobs’ fantasy game was salvaged with two scores, but the tailback didn’t look particularly spry in the process. He had a long gain of just six, and there was almost no burst even against the porous Panthers’ run defense. He was involved in the passing game, but again, outside of his four-yard receiving score, there really wasn’t much there. It’s clear this is Jacobs’ backfield despite the scuffles, as MarShawn Lloyd had just three touches in the contest for seven yards. He’s a volatile low-end RB1 candidate for Week 9 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: Pierre Strong rushed 11 times for 28 yards in the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys, adding 39 yards on five receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: Strong’s 17 opportunities handily led the backfield on a night MarShawn Lloyd was in and out of the game due to an early injury scare. Even so, he managed only 2.8 yards per carry. With Josh Jacobs expected to be activated off the commissioner’s exempt list on Monday, Strong, Lloyd, and Kaleb Johnson can safely be returned to the waiver wire from whence they came.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: MarShawn Lloyd rushed 10 times for 31 yards and a two touchdowns in the Packers’ Week 5 win over the Bears, adding a six-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: Although he notched a receiving score in Week 2, these were the first two rushing touchdowns of Lloyd’s career. Awesome stuff, though a player who was averaging 2.7 yards per carry coming into this afternoon saw that number sit at just 3.1 against the Bears. The Pack also got journeyman Pierre Strong involved in their increasingly frustrating backfield committee. Strong was mostly just absorbing Chris Brooks’ (ankle, injured reserve) lost work, but that of course means Lloyd wasn’t seeing a bigger workload. Although the scores are nice, Lloyd is still lacking an RB2 profile heading into Week 6. He will be a low-upside FLEX vs. the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: Chris Brooks (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: Brooks suffered the ankle injury in Week 4. He went down in the first half and did not return. Brooks underwent testing on his ankle after the game, though the exact nature of his injury has yet to be reported. He does appear to be on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5. If he can’t go, MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson will split the backfield. Johnson led the team in carries last week but also gave up a goal line fumble. We expect Lloyd to get the start versus Chicago on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Chris Brooks is undergoing tests on his ankle.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: Brooks left the Packers’ Week 4 win over the Bucs with an ankle injury in the first half. He did not return after the break and LaFleur didn’t have any definitive answers about the injury on Monday. It sounds like his status for Week 5 is very much up in the air. After coughing up a goal line fumble, Kaleb Johnson would likely take a backseat to MarShawn Lloyd once again. Lloyd has some low-end RB3 appeal as the potential lead back, but this is ultimately a backfield to avoid for fantasy purposes if possible.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: MarShawn Lloyd played on 22.7 percent of the offensive snaps in the Packers’ Week 3 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: The Packers largely played in a trailing game script last night. Lloyd does not have meaningful access to passing down snaps, logging just one snap on third down and none in the two-minute drill, making him mostly dependent on decent rushing workloads. He played 45.5 percent of the red zone snaps and took the lone snap inside the five-yard line, but was held out of the end zone. Lloyd’s six touches led the backfield, but are hardly enough to keep him locked in 12-team FLEX spots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: Kaleb Johnson rushed four times for six yards in the Packers’ Week 3 loss to the Falcons, adding 10 yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: The two backs combined for the only eight running back rush attempts on a night the Packers’ offensive line was completely manhandled by an aggressive and athletic Atlanta front. Lloyd took his four carries for 11 yards while Johnson managed only six on his four totes. Both backs were targeted three times through the air, with Johnson going for 10 yards on one reception and Lloyd managing just seven yards on two grabs. This backfield is a complete mess amidst Josh Jacobs’ absence and mounting injuries along the offensive line, with neither back anywhere near a usable fantasy asset ahead of a Week 4 road matchup with the pass-funnel Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.headline: MarShawn Lloyd rushed six times for 20 yards in the Packers’ Week 2 win over the Jets, adding six yards receiving and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marshawn-lloyd.analysis: Perhaps more importantly, Lloyd lost a key fumble in the second half and then was barely on the field after that. The 25-year-old had plenty of trouble earning yards in the running game, but he was wide open on a well-designed screen pass in the first half for a touchdown catch. Lloyd played on just 16 of the Packers’ 53 snaps and handled seven of their 19 carries. This is a confusing committee that isn’t giving any running back real value, and Josh Jacobs could return at some point near the middle of the season. Fantasy managers in shallow leagues don’t need to hold onto Lloyd, and others could look to trade him away on the back of his receiving touchdown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara has no injury designation for Week 9 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara was limited due to rest and a back injury, but unsurprisingly, he’ll be good to go for Sunday’s contest against the Browns. The Saints’ run game is a disaster, but Kamara should be involved enough in the pass game to make him a decent FLEX play for that contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: The way the team listed Kamara indicates that the back injury will not keep him from playing, but he is clearly still hurt. Kamara has been entirely ineffective this season and can only be viewed as a touchdown-dependent FLEX. CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) was unable to practice today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Donaldson aggravated a shoulder injury in Week 7 against the Steelers and did not return. He also entered the league’s concussion protocol after the game. A limited session today means he’s making progress on both fronts. He should be good to go for Week 9. The same is true of Alvin Kamara, who got a rest day today, despite his back injury also being noted on the report. Both backs will mix in behind Kendre Miller on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara rushed six times for five yards in the Saints’ Week 8 loss to the Steelers, adding seven receptions for 57 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Tyler Shough ended up leading the Saints with seven rushing yards. Yikes. Kamara was effective as a receiver out of the backfield, but to say that New Orleans struggled to run the ball is quite the understatement as they finished with 18 yards on 17 attempts. The good news for fantasy managers that used Kamara is that he was effective out of the backfield as a receiver, but it’s a modest day for the 31-year-old. Kamara and the Saints will try and get something going after a bye against the Browns in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was removed from the injury report for Week 7’s game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara was still listed as limited in Friday’s practice, but the Saints feel confident enough in his health to clear him for Week 7. Kamara found the end zone last week on a 31-yard reception, but has largely been inefficient with his touches this season. He seen 14 opportunities to Kendre Miller’s 30 over the last two weeks and will be hard to trust as anything more than a touchdown-dependent RB3 against the Steelers. The only players on the Saints carrying injury designations into the weekend are guard Cesar Ruiz (knee) and DL Nathan Sheperd (illness). Both are listed as questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: He’s played through this listing for a few weeks now, and though he’ll sometimes get dinged up in game, appears no worse for the wear. Kendre Miller feels like the more viable back in a normal game script right now, with Kamara playing more on passing downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara has been playing through the back issue for several weeks. He is expected to do so again this week. Kamara is part of a three-back committee, and he isn’t the leader of the trio, but that didn’t stop him from finding the end zone on nine touches last week. With a limited receiving role to go along with his shrinking rushing workload, he’s barely in the RB3 mix for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara rushed seven times for 34 yards in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants, adding two receptions for 35 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: The Saints deployed a committee backfield once again for Week 6. Kamara was the third running back into the game for the Saints, but was the only one to score a touchdown. He briefly went to the medical tent after falling on his hip in the first half but re-entered the game soon after. Kamara caught a swing pass from Tyler Shough and tip-toed away from the sideline to score from 17 yards out in the third quarter. With that catch, he became the sixth player in NFL history with 5,000 yards receiving and 5,000 yards rushing in his career. Despite the touchdown and milestone, Kamara was still third in running back snaps and is a touchdown-dependent FLEX play for Week 7 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Saints declared RB Alvin Kamara (back) active for Week 6 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara is active after NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported he would be expected to play in Week 6. He played through the back injury last week and is part of a rough running back committee in the Saints backfield. Kamara is in the RB4 ranks for fantasy purposes. Also active is Chris Olave (illness). The Saints declared QB Zach Wilson, EDGE Anfernee Jennings, S Mike Reid, LB Kaden Elliss, DT Nathan Shepherd, and DT John Ridgeway inactive for Week 6 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Alvin Kamara (back) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara played through the back issue last week, though he only saw five touches. He has fallen behind Kendre Miller in the pecking order for carries, and even CJ Donaldson is pushing him for work on passing downs. Kamara is barely an RB4 for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that the NFL’s defensive tackle market “has been hot,” and teams “might” try to trade for Derrick Brown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.analysis: The Panthers are “not actively looking to move” Brown, but Breer says they have considered it. Other defensive tackles on other teams who have come up in trade talks include Grover Stewart, Davon Godchaux, Nathan Shepherd, Christian Barmore and Bobby Brown. The Dolphins have told teams they are not interested in trading away Zach Sieler.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.headline: Panthers DE Derrick Brown (elbow) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.analysis: Brown appeared on Thursday’s injury report as a limited participant on Thursday, but successfully practiced in full on Friday. The Panthers’ star defender should have a fruitful outing against an injury-depleted Saints offensive line missing OT Taliese Fuaga (ankle) and C/OG Erik McCoy, who is on injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.headline: Panthers DE Derrick Brown (elbow) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.analysis: Mid-week additions to the injury report are concerning, particularly for a team’s lynchpin defender. Brown is a difference-maker as both a pass rusher and run defender, boasting 16 quarterback pressures, four sacks and 20 tackles. Whether the Saints can exploit his potential absence on Sunday is up for debate, but having him on the field is certainly ideal for Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.headline: Panthers DT Derrick Brown left Carolina’s Week 8 against the Bills with a knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.analysis: Brown limped off the field late in the fourth quarter with a knee injury and was in the blue medical tent for a while. He seemed to be in good spirits on the sideline afterward, but he was listed as questionable to return. The Panthers are down 40-9, so they likely just wanted to hold their best defender out with the Packers on deck next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.headline: Panthers DE Derrick Brown “has continued to impress this summer and should be a force” in his return from last year’s season-ending knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.analysis: Brown was sidelined for the entirety of the 2024 season after undergoing surgery to repair a meniscus tear that he suffered in Week 1. Brown has been a “high-impact player” for years, notably setting the defensive linemen record for tackles in a single season (103) in 2023. The Athletic’s Jeff Howe reports, “judging by conversations with those around him this season, it doesn’t sound like there’s any dropoff in sight.” Brown was held out of preseason play due to a separate rib/oblique issue, but there are no indications that Brown’s Week 1 availability is in question. The Panthers’ defensive leader will have a busy day, attempting to contain the Jaguars’ three-deep rushing attack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.headline: Panthers GM Dan Morgan said Derrick Brown (knee) is “cleared for all activity.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.analysis: Of course, the caveat is that the Panthers “will be smart” with the Pro Bowl defensive lineman. Brown’s status for the season doesn’t look to be in any doubt after his season-ending meniscus injury in Week 1 last year, but he’ll likely have plenty of off-days in training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.headline: Panthers HC Dave Canales said the team is taking it “week to week” with Derrick Brown’s (knee) recovery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.analysis: Brown suffered a season-ending meniscus injury in Week 1 of last season and said earlier this offseason that his goal is to be ready for Week 1. How that plays out is anybody’s guess, but it’s clear the Panthers are in no rush to put their star defensive tackle back on the field until he’s at 100 percent. Brown racked up a career-high 103 tackles in 2023 and received a lucrative four-year, $96 million contract last offseason for his efforts. His return, coupled with the additions of top-100 draft picks Nic Scourton and Princely Umanmielen, should go a long way in bolstering a Panthers defense that finished dead last in points and yards allowed last season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports that the Panthers will be “seeking big-name players in free agency,” particularly on defense.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.analysis: Graziano suggests the Panthers “might be one of the teams willing to spend big to lure defensive tackle Milton Williams away from the Super Bowl champion Eagles.” The Panthers will also attempt to bolster their edge rush and Graziano lists Saints defensive end Chase Young as an “intriguing option.” Adding Williams and Young to a defensive line featuring Derrick Brown and Jadeveon Clowney could help turn around Carolina’s dire 2024 defense. Safeties Jevon Holland and Camryn Bynum are also reportedly on the Panthers’ short list of preferred defenders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports Panthers DL Derrick Brown (knee) could miss the remainder of the regular season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.analysis: Brown in Week 1 against the Saints sustained an injury to his meniscus. He’ll require surgery and could be out for much of the season. It’s a brutal blow to a Carolina defense that was shredded by Derek Carr and the Saints on opening day. Without Brown, the Panthers almost certainly have the NFL’s worst pass rush.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.headline: Panthers signed DT Derrick Brown to a four-year, $96 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-br.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Brown — who had one year remaining on his contract — will get around $63 million in guarantees with the new deal. The seventh overall pick in the 2020 NFL Draft, Brown, 25, set an NFL record for defensive lineman with 103 tackles in 2023; his missed tackle rate was among the league’s lowest among defensive linemen. He has functioned as a run stuffer in the Carolina defense. Pro Football Focus graded Brown as last year’s No. 2 defensive lineman behind Quinnen Williams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) was not seen practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings was limited yesterday, which could mean he injured his calf during the Vikings’ Thursday practice. If this is the case, he is probably unlikely to suit up for his team’s Monday Night Football game against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings has been the subject of trade rumors. Since is able to practice, even in a limited capacity, this injury is unlikely to alter a potential suitor’s interest. Regardless, Jennings is not on the FLEX radar this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams must find a way to trade for a wide receiver before the November 10th deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: The Rams’ resources are thin. They already traded away their 2027 first- and second-round picks, their 2028 second-round pick and their 2029 third-round pick. They also have just $8,000 in 2026 salary cap space, so restructuring the potential new add’s deal would be required. Atkins believes the Rams should consider Josh Downs as the top option due to his ability to beat man coverage and contribute as a returner. Other options, according to Atkins, include Calvin Ridley, Keenan Allen and Jauan Jennings, “for the likely cost of a Day 3 pick.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter named Calvin Ridley as a potential trade candidate.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Schefter threw out several names, many of whom have already been bandied about as trade candidates. Among the lesser-discussed options, he included Jerry Jeudy and Jauan Jennings in addition to Ridley. All three are veteran wideouts who have simply disappeared in the current iterations of their respective offenses. Even with new landing spots in the cards for the trio, none of them are worth holding onto in standard fantasy leagues. Ridley has five catches for 81 yards this year. He is expected to play through his hip injury today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Juan Jennings caught 2-of-3 targets for 34 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings caught a 20-yard pass, his longest reception of the season. He was targeted three times, nearly catching a long touchdown from Kyler Murray in the second quarter, but failing to haul it in. Jennings is outside of the top-three pass-catching options for the Vikings and is irrelevant for fantasy purposes in this role. Fantasy managers should keep an eye on him in case he is traded, but Jennings does not need to be in fantasy lineups heading in to Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jauan Jennings “would be a name for me to keep an eye on” for the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings has been a major disappointment in Minnesota, falling behind Tai Felton on the depth chart. A small stakes trade could make sense for the 49ers, who are down to hoping Brandin Cooks can provide for Brock Purdy in a major rash of injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Tai Felton caught 2-of-3 targets for 27 yards in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jordan Addison missed this game with an ankle injury and the Vikings deployed Felton as their WR2 over Jauan Jennings. Jennings ran fewer routes and failed to catch his only target. Felton wasn’t awfully productive either, but it’s good to see the former third-round pick picking up more work in his second season. He will return to a rotational role, assuming Addison is cleared to play after the Vikings’ Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings caught 1-of-1 targets for eight yards in the Vikings’ Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings simply isn’t meaningfully involved in the Vikings’ game plan. That is unlikely to change in Week 5 against the Saints, especially with the Vikings’ offensive line getting banged up in Week 4. Jennings could be asked to contribute more as a run blocker next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Jauan Jennings caught 1-of-2 targets for one yard in the Vikings’ Week 3 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings hasn’t been part of the Minnesota passing attack through three weeks. Against the Bucs Jennings ran the second most pass routes on the Vikings, behind only Jordan Addison. The low-volume Vikings passing offense likely can’t support more than one fantasy viable pass catcher per week. Jennings should remain on waivers for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said Jauan Jennings (personal) is expected to return for Week 3.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jauan-jenn.analysis: Jennings was targeted just once in Week 1. It could be argued that we’re not sure what his target count would look like in a normal Vikings game given how quickly Kyler Murray got hurt, but there’s never been a normal Vikings game anyway. Jennings is best monitored from the waiver wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that Josh Downs “leads the wide receiver market” ahead of the NFL trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Downs’ 2026 season has fallen short of expectations, but perhaps he has a chance to rebound. Breer believes acquiring Downs would “probably” cost a fourth-round pick. He is “one of a number of receivers on the market” at the moment, with the Chiefs and Steelers among the teams looking for help at the position. Breer adds that the 49ers are “open” to adding a wide receiver as well, but with their positional health improving, San Francisco is “less desperate than they were a couple of weeks ago.” The Steelers’ wide receiver corps might be too muddled for Downs to meaningfully increase his productivity, but landing in Kansas City or San Francisco would likely be good for him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams must find a way to trade for a wide receiver before the November 10th deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: The Rams’ resources are thin. They already traded away their 2027 first- and second-round picks, their 2028 second-round pick and their 2029 third-round pick. They also have just $8,000 in 2026 salary cap space, so restructuring the potential new add’s deal would be required. Atkins believes the Rams should consider Josh Downs as the top option due to his ability to beat man coverage and contribute as a returner. Other options, according to Atkins, include Calvin Ridley, Keenan Allen and Jauan Jennings, “for the likely cost of a Day 3 pick.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: A to Z Sports’ Charles Goldman reports that if the Chiefs trade for a wide receiver, the team “would like to acquire a long-term fixture rather than a one-year rental.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Chiefs coach Andy Reid told reporters today that general manager Brett Veach has been constantly sharing potential trade targets with the coaching staff for about a month. According to Goldman, the Chiefs could also target additions along the offensive and defensive lines, but he believes the team would “likely have to acquire a receiver through other means” before focusing on the trenches. There aren’t many free agency options right now, though, so it is unclear how this scenario would play out. Goldman notes that Josh Downs and Brian Thomas Jr. “have surfaced in trade discussions.” He does not think the Chiefs will make a move before Sunday, though a move early next week, before the November 10th trade deadline, is still possible.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs caught 4-of-5 targets for 23 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 8 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Downs’ score was something of a pity touchdown in a game the Colts were trailing 35-0 at the 3:59 mark of the third quarter. Jacksonville’s defense had a rare mixup, and Downs was roaming free in the end zone. Amazingly, it was his first touchdown of the year. That speaks to just how dire things have been for Downs in an offense with an ineffective Daniel Jones and ageless Keenan Allen. Downs, who of course must be held responsible for his own mediocre play, will have no shot at a 2026 fantasy revival unless he’s subject to a change-of-scenery trade ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said he “wouldn’t be surprised” if the Chiefs trade for a wide receiver.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Rapoport then named Josh Downs and Brian Thomas Jr. as players to keep an eye on. Both wideouts are in the midst of down years and their teams have already leaked that they are on the trade block. Thomas Jr. would hopefully unlock the once-vaunted Patrick Mahomes deep ball. Downs, on the other hand, would be another underneath weapon for a passing attack that his simply asking too much of Rashee Rice right now. Both players’ fantasy stock would skyrocket via a trade.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Colts want a third-round pick for Josh Downs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: The Colts are already the league’s biggest sellers ahead of the trade deadline and they’re not done yet. While they get plenty of interest in Downs, a third-round pick might be too much to ask after his slow start to the year. Downs has 26 catches for 307 yards as we approach the midway point of the season. Downs is also set to become a free agent in the spring, meaning that he might play only a handful of games for his new team. On the other hand, his disappointing season can largely be written off as the product of a failing offense. Fantasy managers should at least hold onto Downs until the trade deadline, even if he’s barely a WR3 as things stand right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Josh Downs will play in Week 8 against the Jaguars despite his trade request.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Steichen confirmed that Downs did indeed request a trade, but that won’t stop him from being on the field this week against the Jaguars. The Colts appear to be in full sell mode after trading away OG Quenton Nelson and DT DeForest Buckner earlier this week. Downs has been on the practice field this week and profiles as a fringe WR3/WR4 after a string of tough outings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs has requested a trade.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Downs was cagey when asked on Wednesday morning whether he had officially asked for his ticket out of Indianapolis, but Fowler maintains the wideout has requested the Colts trade him before the NFL’s trade deadline. That could very well happen in the coming days with the miserable Colts in fire sale mode, having dealt Quenton Nelson to Seattle and DeForest Buckner to the Niners. Downs, who has 26 receptions for 307 scoreless yards this season, would make sense as a trade target for the wideout-needy Chiefs, the Steelers, and perhaps the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts could trade Josh Downs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Schefter listed out DeForest Buckner, Grover Stewart, and Downs as players that could potentially be on the move as the Colts continue what from all outside appearances looks to be a fire sale. He thinks Buckner will be the next player on the move and likely go for less than Quenton Nelson. Downs certainly hasn’t impressed with his opportunity this season, but he’s a valuable receiver and Indianapolis didn’t exactly but him in an ideal scenario with Alec Pierce hurt and Keenan Allen playing alongside him while Daniel Jones struggles to regain his 2025 form.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.headline: Josh Downs caught 2-of-4 targets for 18 yards in the Colts’ Week 7 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-downs.analysis: Downs’ four targets were the most on the team, though he caught just two for 18 yards. His lack of red zone usage and deep targets cap his ability to get explosive plays or touchdowns. He led all Colts wideouts with 52 snaps, tallying seven more than second-place Laquon Treadwell. Even with Tyler Warren (groin) out, Downs is losing middle-of-the-field targets to Keenan Allen. Given his low output with both Warren and Alec Pierce out, Downs is a low-ceiling WR4/FLEX play for Week 8 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) is listed as questionable for Week 9 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Egbuka was able to get in another full practice Friday after getting the same Thursday, so it seems like he’s on the right side of the questionable tag, even with coach Todd Bowles suggesting he’ll be a game-time decision. The 24-year-old wideout is on the WR2/WR3 range for the Sunday Night Football showdown against Chicago if he is able to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) was a full participant in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: After only participating in drills on the side and being listed as a non-participant Wednesday, Egbuka was a full-go for Thursday’s session. The 24-year-old will likely need to get in one more full session before fantasy managers can fully trust the wideout for Week 9 against the Bears, but this is obviously a significant step in the right direction.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Egbuka missed Week 7 with a concussion and a foot injury. He cleared the league’s concussion protocol last week, but the foot issue kept him on ice. A DNP today suggests he will miss another week. However, head coach Todd Bowles told reporters Egbuka worked off to the side today. The team will see how he feels tomorrow. That leaves the door open for him to play, but fantasy managers should at least have backup options in place. If he does suit up, Egbuka would be a high-risk WR3 versus Chicago.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Emeka Egbuka (foot) will not play in Week 8 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Bowles said Egbuka did clear concussion protocol, but the foot injury he has been dealing with for the last two weeks will officially sideline him for this week’s game against the Falcons. Hopefully this isn’t any kind of a major setback for Egbuka, who shed his non-contact jersey in Thursday’s practice and was limited in the first two practices to start the week. Ted Hurst will again operate as the Buccaneers’ primary outside target but shouldn’t be trusted as anything more than a risky WR4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: After being limited in back-to-back practices to start the week, and shedding his non-contact jersey on Thursday, Egbuka being a DNP on Friday is a notable setback. Buccaneers beat writer Greg Auman speculated that Egbuka will “be ruled out again” for Week 8’s game against the Falcons, but we’ll wait for official word from the team before drawing conclusions. That said, the Bucs could again have Ted Hurst operating as their primary outside threat.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: The Tampa Bay Times’ Rick Stroud reports Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) shed his non-contact jersey for Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: There’s a good chance Egbuka has been upgraded to a full participant in practice, meaning he is making his way through the league’s concussion protocol. He remains on track to play this week after missing Week 7. With Baker Mayfield back under center, Egbuka may be able to turn around his season after a rather quiet start to the year. He is in the WR2 mix for Week 8 versus the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Egbuka logged one limited practice on Friday last week but was ruled out shortly after. It looks like he is trending in the right direction for Week 8, but the Bucs’ next two injury reports will be more revealing. Assuming all goes well, Egbuka should be back in the WR2 ranks with Baker Mayfield under center and playing well in Tampa Bay’s Week 7 demolition of the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Buccaneers ruled out Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) for Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Just minutes after head coach Todd Bowles said the team would list Egbuka as doubtful, the official injury report listed him as out, despite his limited participation in Friday’s practice. Egbuka was unable to clear concussion protocol in time to be active for this week, and will now set his sights on returning in Week 8 in time to face the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Buccaneers head coach said Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) will be doubtful for Week 7’s game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Bowles said Egbuka remains in concussion protocol and initially said “I’d say he’s out [for Week 7], too,” before saying the second-year receiver would be listed as doubtful. Fantasy managers holding out hope that Egbuka will suit up for Sunday’s game against the Panthers should ensure their backup plan is in place, as players listed as doubtful seldom end up playing on game day. Assuming he’s out, Ted Hurst could be tasked with operating as the Bucs’ WR1. Hurst has caught 11-of-22 targets for 168 yards and one touchdown this season but wouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a WR3/FLEX play even with Baker Mayfield (thumb) back under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.headline: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) was seen practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/emeka-egbuka/0.analysis: Egbuka missed the first two practices of the week, but could have a shot at suiting up after appearing on the practice field Friday. Head coach Todd Bowles should give an update on Egbuka shortly after practice, so we’ll check back on his official status once we have word on his Week 7 availability. Whether or not he has a chance to play will largely depend on the team’s independent neurologists clearing him from the league’s concussion protocol.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (calf) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston will once again play through a lower-body injury. The rookie downfield wide receiver has played unproductively as of late, but he remains a threat to rip off a long gain. He will be catching passes from Shedeur Sanders this weekend. Hopefully, the two form a strong connection quickly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (calf) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston is on track to face the Saints this week, but lower-body injuries have limited his production since Week 4. The Browns are also likely to have Shedeur Sanders under center, adding an unknown variable to the mix as the two players hone their chemistry. Boston is likely just a boom-bust FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (calf) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: A limited designation for the first practice of the week is usually nothing to worry about. We’ll assume as much for now. Boston has been racking up targets and air yards without much to show for it in his box scores over the past month. He hasn’t eclipsed 50 yards in a game since Week 4. A date with New Orleans’ struggling defense should help him get back on track as a WR3 for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston caught 6-of-11 targets for 37 yards in the Browns’ Week 8 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: The good news is that Boston’s route tree wasn’t limited to deep shots, but the bad news is that the production did not follow. The rookie was second on the team in targets, played the most snaps, and ran the second-most routes of any receiver, but the Browns’ passing attack could never get going. Boston was close to a bigger day after he made a great one-handed catch in the end zone, but he could only get one foot in bounds. He’ll continue to be a boom-or-bust option but has a chance to boom against the Saints next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston caught 3-of-8 targets for 25 yards in the Browns’ Week 7 win against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston was third in targets among Browns pass catchers and saw lots and lots of air yards from Deshaun Watson, who nearly connected with Boston for two long touchdowns on the day. So it goes with a high-variance downfield option like Boston, who now has three straight quiet outings. With a 45 percent air yards share headed into Week 7, Boston will certainly have his big box scores in the coming weeks. Predicting when that might happen will be tough for fantasy managers. He should be a flex play in Week 8 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: He’ll be on the WR3 line in a good matchup against the Titans. Boston finally had a clunker last week against Baltimore, but he’s been remarkably consistent otherwise and should find easier footing against Tennessee’s rough back seven.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: The Browns’ rookie field-stretcher played through his foot injury last week against the Ravens, posting just a 1/15 receiving line. Ostensibly, the foot is bothering him, but he still has a chance to suit up in Week 7 against the Titans. Hopefully, Boston upgrades to full participation tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston played through the injury last week, catching just 1-of-5 targets for 15 yards. The foot injury could be bugging him. Fortunately, he did not appear to suffer any setbacks. Boston is a WR3/FLEX against the Titans in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston caught 1-of-5 targets for 15 yards in the Browns’ Week 6 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: This was the worst game of Boston’s young career. After going for 40-plus yards in his first five games to start the season, the promising rookie was blanketed in coverage all afternoon and managed just one reception as a result. Boston may have had a chance at scoring were it not for a pass near the right side of the end zone sailing too far out of bounds for him to bring both feet down, but scoring opportunities were hard to come by in this one. Boston will be back on the fantasy radar as a WR3 next week against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: He’ll be a usable WR3 against the Ravens this week. Boston has returned at least 41 yards in every start this year while hitting a deep gain seemingly weekly. The 22-year-old should be Cleveland’s No. 1 target again this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) was ruled out for Week 9 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: This will be a third-straight missed game for Turpin as he battles his rib issue. The 30-year-old has just seven targets on the season, but will again be missed by Dallas in the return game. Malachi Lawrence has also been ruled out by the Cowboys due to his ankle injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) was ruled out for Week 8 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Week 8 will mark the second consecutive absence for the veteran kick returner, with little-to-no impact on the offensive pieces around him considering he has played more than 12 offensive snaps only once all season. Fantasy managers are more interested in the potential status of George Pickens, who is listed as questionable. If Pickens can’t go, Ryan Flournoy could see a slight uptick in opportunities on the perimeter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Pickens played through a minor shoulder injury last week, but the hamstring designation is new. He was still a limited practice participant, indicating neither injury should be an issue for his Week 8 status. Meanwhile, WR/KR KaVontae Turpin (ribs) was an estimated DNP in practice after not playing last week. The Cowboys may be missing Turpin again as a kick returner and gadget player on offense, but Pickens should still be the WR2 for Sunday against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that the Giants are serious suitors for Jonathan Taylor, while the Broncos and Vikings might be less inclined to acquire him.

The 49ers handed over 2023 second-, third- and fourth-round picks, and a 2024 fifth-rounder to acquire him. None of the three suitors have met either asking price yet. That said, the Giants have reportedly offered enough for Breer to label them “a serious suitor.” Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Jonathan Taylor said he has not requested a trade.

For now, fantasy managers can keep Taylor in their lineups, as there’s been no indication that Taylor will be put on ice to protect his trade value.

Daniel Jones’s name has also come up, though it’s hard to imagine another team paying even a late-round pick for his services given how dreadful he has been this year. All signs point to Taylor being moved early next week, but it’s clear the Colts are going to play hardball in trade talks. We still suspect he’s playing for a new team by Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Jonathan Taylor remains on the Colts roster.

That could be the Vikings, Bengals, Seahawks, or another contending team in need of backfield help.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: DNVR Broncos’ Zac Stevens reports that the Broncos are “going to try” to trade for Jonathan Taylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Stevens said that this trade “could happen at any moment,” telling Broncos Country that they “might not want to go to sleep.” While this could be hyperbole, it sounds like Stevens is saying the trade could go down tonight. Stevens said he’s had conversations with multiple people on the matter, and the Broncos “know that this is not the time to wait and develop” young running backs. Stevens closed by reminding viewers that the Broncos were very interested in Breece Hall at one point, and added that there are likely other backup plans that the Broncos could be considering.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Jonathan Taylor rushed eight times for 23 yards in the Colts’ Week 8 loss to the Jaguars, adding four receptions for 24 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: With the Colts losing 28-0 at halftime and 42-7 going into the fourth quarter, there simply wasn’t any run to be established. Daniel Jones also short-circuited two drives with interceptions, further limiting volume in a game where it was already exceedingly difficult to come by. You could question why Taylor even played at all as trade rumors swirl ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline, but that will be a bigger question mark in Week 9 against the Cowboys. That’s a far better matchup than the Jaguars, so even if Taylor remains in limbo, you will have no choice but to fire him up for what could be his final game in a Colts uniform.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Jordan Schultz reports the Vikings, Giants, Broncos, Bengals and Packers are amongst the teams that have “checked in” on a potential Jonathan Taylor trade.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: The Vikings dots have been getting connected for a while now, so it’s not surprising to see something of a confirmation they are interested. The Giants and Bengals also make all the sense in the world. Green Bay would be a fit, as well, though it would be a bit surprising to see the Broncos add to their running back surplus. Taylor, of course, would blow their other backs out of the water. There’s enough smoke here to believe a fire might break out, but the Colts can probably be taken at their word that it would take an overpay to pry away what amounts to their franchise player right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts “would seek a similar compensation package” to the Christian McCaffrey trade for Jonathan Taylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: The Panthers netted second-, third-, fourth-, and fifth-round picks for McCaffrey when they sent him to San Francisco in 2022. Indy reportedly turned down an offer of a second-round selection plus another pick for Taylor, meaning they have their eyes set on the full compensation that Carolina landed. The fact that the Colts abruptly changed their stance on trading Taylor at all this weekend suggests it’s only a matter of time before a deal gets done. They have until November 10th, the Tuesday after Week 9, to find a trade partner.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts are open to trading RB Jonathan Taylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Multiple teams are interested in acquiring the 27-year-old Taylor and talks are active and ongoing, according to Schefter. The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reported that the Colts already turned down an offer for Taylor that included a 2027 second-round pick and another pick. While previous reports stated the Colts weren’t interested in trading Taylor, who signed an extension before the season, Indianapolis appears to be holding out for the best offer they can get. Taylor would see a slight boost in fantasy value if acquired by another team while Seth McGowan would likely take over the Colts’ backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Jonathan Taylor will play in Week 8 against the Jaguars.
