https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Steichen said Taylor will see a full workload despite being the subject of trade rumors for a Colts team that will clearly be sellers at the deadline. Taylor is healthy and not on the injury report, so this is strictly an update to inform fantasy managers they can start him with confidence this week. Taylor remains a high-end RB1 as long as his normal workload remains intact.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson sat out on Wednesday and Thursday. His Friday participation level has not yet been released, but he is probably on the wrong side of questionable at this time. Parkinson does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues, especially with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) expected to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Rams head coach Sean McVay announced Parkinson would be a DNP on Wednesday. The 27-year-old has been dealing with a rib injury since Week 7, missing the Rams’ Week 8 game against the Chargers. Starting out DNP puts him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 9 against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Rams declared TE Colby Parkinson, QB Ty Simpson, LS Joe Cardona, OT Keagan Trost, and DE Desjuan Johnson inactive for Week 8 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson will miss at least one game with a rib injury he sustained last week against the Raiders. His absence could have a big impact on playing time for both Davis Allen — who had two touchdown grabs last week — and Tyler Higbee, the de facto TE1 in the LA offense. Both tight ends are better options against the Chargers with Parkinson sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is questionable for Week 8 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson gutted out an injury to his midsection against the Raiders a week ago when he was in and out of the lineup while clearly dealing with significant discomfort. He was unable to practice through Thursday this week, prompting the questionable designation ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the Chargers. Already down multiple primary pass catchers, the Rams could see further concentration of volume should Parkinson miss, a situation that could also pave the way for Davis Allen to see an uptick in opportunities in the 12- and 13-personnel-heavy Rams offense. Fantasy managers likely won’t get further updates on Parkinson’s status before the team releases inactives 90-minutes prior to first kick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson will have one more chance to get back no the practice field Friday to avoid an injury designation entering the weekend. The veteran tight end was in and out of the team’s Week 7 game with the injury but managed to finish it, apparently feeling much worse after the adrenaline wore off. Fantasy managers of Parkinson and Tyler Higbee will want to track Parkinson’s status closely to end the week. An absence from Parkinson could also bring Davis Allen into the fantasy spotlight after the young tight end scored twice against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson has meaningfully contributed to the Rams’ offense in each of the last two weeks, but he is now at risk of missing his team’s Week 8 game against the Chargers. Were Parkinson to sit out on Sunday, Tyler Higbee would likely benefit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson caught 5-of-6 targets for 48 yards in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson was in and out of the game with various injuries, picking up a new ailment on seemingly every reception. Parkinson logged 16 pass routes while Tyler Higbee led the team’s tight ends with 18 routes. Davis Allen, meanwhile, ran a route on 12 of the Rams’ drop backs and caught two touchdowns from Matthew Stafford. Parkinson should be a viable desperation option in deeper formats next week against the Chargers if the Rams keep using three tight end sets at a high rate. He has ten receptions over his past two outings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson caught 5-of-6 targets for 31 yards and one touchdown in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson played effectively against the Cardinals’ zone coverage this afternoon. He bagged a first down after finding a soft spot downfield on the Rams’ fourth drive, and deftly hurdled a defender on a one-yard gain a few plays later. His touchdown occurred on the Rams’ final possession and required post-catch effort, barreling through contact and extending for the score. Parkinson is a touchdown-dependent TE2 against the Raiders in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Davis Allen (foot) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: He got in a limited session and the Rams apparently trust him to play despite a pair of missed practices on Wednesday and Thursday. Colby Parkinson (shoulder) also avoided the final report. Tyler Higbee is the Rams tight end you should be using at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Davis Allen (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Allen remains out, and Parkinson (shoulder) remains limited. Tyler Higbee has played productively in the Rams’ No. 1 tight end role, and he should be expected to do so again this week against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Jordan Whittington (back) is questionable for Week 9 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Whittington has just two catches on the season, and with head coach Sean McVay suggesting he wants to get Tutu Atwell more involved, it seems unlikely Whittington will have a role as more than a returner even if he can play against Washington come Sunday. Trent McDuffie (back) is also questionable for that contest, and won’t practice Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams WR Jordan Whittington (quad) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Whittington is WR Puka Nacua’s (hip) direct backup, so he will be out there running a decent number of routes. Whittington has, however, never managed to establish himself as a reliable contributor. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues. Rams TE Colby Parkinson (knee) will be questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams WR Jordan Whittington (quad) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It is unclear whether the Rams will get their backup wide receiver back. Whittington cannot be treated as a reliable FLEX starter if he plays in place of WR Puka Nacua (hip) this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Jordan Whittington (quad) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Whittington missed Week 2 with the quad injury and doesn’t look likely to return this week. Xavier Smith and Konata Mumpfield each ran a little over half of the routes last week, though they combined for just three targets. With Tutu Atwell also in the mix for the WR2 role, there isn’t a clear fantasy winner here despite the bevy of injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams WR Puka Nacua (groin) is questionable for Week 2 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nacua did not practice for the second consecutive day Saturday, prompting the questionable designation for Monday Night Football. The issue is now being called a groin ailment and is reportedly unrelated to the psoas injury he dealt with during the offseason. Fantasy managers will want to start making alternate plans for their first-round pick considering the Rams don’t play until the final game of the week. Jordan Whittington is listed as doubtful with a quad injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams WR Jordan Whittington (quad) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Whittington is WR1 Puka Nacua’s direct backup, and Nacua appeared on the injury report today with a hip injury. Neither player practiced. This situation is worth monitoring closely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: The Athletic’s Jourdan Rodrigue believes the Rams may take a committee approach to the WR3 role this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Rodrigue listed WR Konata Mumpfield and WR Jordan Whittington as candidates for the gig, notably excluding rookie WR CJ Daniels. Daniels was viewed as the potential WR3 due to his blocking ability earlier this year. Rodrigue says it is instead Whittington who could serve as the “3B” blocker. Mumpfield reportedly “looks the part” as the “3A” receiving component. Will he return fantasy value reliably? Probably not. Earlier this month, Rodrigue’s colleague, Nate Atkins, said Mumpfield could be the next man up on the perimeter if WRs Puka Nacua or Davante Adams miss time. Rodrigue’s comments seemingly confirm this.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Jordan Whittington was not targeted in Los Angeles’ NFC Championship loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: From Weeks 1-12, the 2024 sixth-round pick was Los Angeles’ No. 3 receiver and played 52.4 percent of the Rams’ snaps. His fantasy relevancy peaked when the Rams headed to London without Puka Nacua and Whittington managed to reward managers with a 2/9 dud. Over the final five games of the season, dealing with a knee injury, he managed just 44 offensive snaps. Whittington isn’t a must-hold in dynasty leagues at this point, but it’s possible he was simply not himself while trying to play hurt. Either way, it’s hard to imagine much of a 2026 fantasy role for him here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams TE Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) is questionable to play in the Wild Card Round against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Rams WR Jordan Whittington (knee) was initially listed as questionable, but later ruled out. Ferguson earned four targets in each of his last two games, catching five for 87 yards and two touchdowns. Having him on the field would be great for the Rams’ creative tight end usage. Whittington serves only as a rotational weapon at wide receiver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rams TE Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ferguson followed up his Tuesday DNP with another DNP on Wednesday. WR Jordan Whittington (knee) and OL Kevin Dotson (ankle) also remained out. Official injury statuses will come out on Thursday but all three players are on the wrong side of questionable for the Wild Card round against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kelvin-ban.headline: Kelvin Banks (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kelvin-ban.analysis: Banks, the Saints’ talented left tackle, has a chance to return from injured reserve this week. He underwent surgery earlier this year to address a high-ankle sprain. Banks’ backup, Asim Richards (thum), is also questionable to play. Hopefully, at least one of them is good to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kelvin-ban.headline: Saints opened Kelvin Banks’ (ankle) 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kelvin-ban.analysis: This is a big deal. The Saints’ left tackle earned PFWA All-Rookie Team honors last year. He suffered what was reportedly a “severe” high-ankle sprain earlier this season and underwent surgery to correct the issue. He was initially expected to return sometime in December, but apparently his rehab went very well. Banks is not guaranteed to suit up in Week 9 against the Browns, but he should retake the field soon enough. Banks’ impending return will boost both the Saints’ pass game and run game. Banks was officially limited at Wednesday’s practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kelvin-ban.headline: Saints placed Kelvin Banks (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kelvin-ban.analysis: The team signed long snapper Cal Adomitis and reached an injury settlement with running back Audric Estime in corresponding moves. Banks is undergoing surgery for a severe high-ankle sprain. He could return later this year, but the team will be without their starting left tackle for at least four games, and likely much longer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kelvin-ban.headline: Saints T Kelvin Banks is expected to undergo ankle surgery after tests revealed a “severe” high-ankle sprain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kelvin-ban.analysis: He’s out indefinitely and this will be a major blow for the Saints offense. There’s a chance he returns at some point later this season. He almost undoubtedly will end up on injured reserve in the next few days. Banks had a 73.5 PFF grade last year as one of the brighter rookie tackles of the class of 2025. Asim Richards would seem like the likely short-term replacement.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kelvin-ban.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Saints believe LT Kelvin Banks suffered a high-ankle sprain in Week 2’s win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kelvin-ban.analysis: Banks will undergo an MRI to confirm the severity of the injury, but the second-year tackle is likely looking at a 4-6 week absence if the MRI doesn’t reveal any additional damage. Banks has started all 19 games he has appeared in for the Saints since being drafted last year. He was replaced by fourth-year tackle Asim Richards in Sunday’s win over the Ravens, who allowed two pressures on the 15 pass-blocking snaps he was in on.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kelvin-ban.headline: Saints LT Kelvin Banks (ankle) will not return in Week 2 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kelvin-ban.analysis: Banks was carted from the field in the third quarter with what was originally called a lower-leg injury after Ravens EDGE Mike Green collided with Banks’ legs on his way to sack Tyler Shough. The No. 9 overall pick of the 2025 NFL Draft has started every game he’s appeared in since being drafted and was replaced by Asim Richards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kelvin-ban.headline: The Times-Picayune’s Matthew Paras reports that Saints OT Trevor Penning took snaps at left guard during organized team activities.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kelvin-ban.analysis: Saints first-round rookie OT Kelvin Banks Jr. is already taking repetitions at left tackle, which pushes last year’s first-round pick and starting left tackle Taliese Fuaga over to the right tackle position. Penning, who manned the right tackle spot last year, will now evidently kick inside to left guard. Penning has failed to developed into a reliable pass protector through three NFL seasons but respectably earned a 70.1 PFF run-blocking grade last season. The Saints’ offensive line is rounding into form as an above-average unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kelvin-ban.headline: Saints signed No. 9 overall pick OT Kelvin Banks Jr. to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kelvin-ban.analysis: The youngster banks $27.7 million with pen now put to paper. Banks will settle in as a handsomely paid blocker for one of Derek Carr or Tyler Shough, pending the former’s shoulder health. The former Texas tackle allowed just four career sacks in his three college seasons. The Saints also signed LB Danny Stutsman, CB Quincy Riley, RB Devin Neal, TE Moliki Matavao and EDGE Fadil Diggs to four-year contracts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kelvin-ban.headline: Saints selected Texas OT Kelvin Banks Jr. with the No. 9 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kelvin-ban.analysis: Banks Jr. (6’5/315) was considered the top offensive tackle from the 2022 prep cycle according to On3, and proved that evaluation correct by receiving FWAA Freshman All-American accolades after starting all 13 games at LT for Texas. The mountainous Longhorn recorded 930-plus snaps in each of the last two seasons while allowing just one sack in each campaign. Bolstered by a sterling 0.9 percent pressure rate allowed, the reigning Outland Trophy winner is one of only four 2025 NFL Draft tackles to record 80th-plus percentile grades in both the run and pass phases of the game. His 10 3/8th-inch hands allow him to bully smaller Edge rushers, while Banks Jr,’s 32-inch vertical (93rd) and 8.25 Relative Athletic Score solidifies his testing profile despite his non-ideal 33.5-inch arms. He’s quick enough to ride rushers past the pocket and fires out of his stance with well-timed punches. His wide hand placement on pass sets allows rushers to get in his chest, and he can get ahead of himself on pull blocks. Banks does keep his feet churning and torques his body into his run blocking. He is a projectable tackle who is also agile enough to move inside should his attempt at playing OT falter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kelvin-ban.headline: Texas has received a verbal commitment from 2022 five-star OT Kelvin Banks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kelvin-ban.analysis: Banks (6'5/300) had previously committed to Oregon, but de-committed from the school on December 6th following Mario Cristobal’s decision to leave for Miami. Now Banks, a Humble, Texas native, has committed to Texas, which marks a tremendous signing for head coach Steve Sarkisian. Banks the the no. 2 rated offensive tackle of the 2022 recruiting class according to 247Sports’ composite rankings, and is the no. 15 overall player in the nation. Already possessing excellent size, Banks should fit in nicely at Texas, Banks is built to play Power Five football. He was a Texas District 21-6a first-team selection at offensive tackle as both a sophomore and junior in 2019 and 2020.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters Friday that Myles Garrett (knee) is expected to play against the Commanders in Week 9.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett will need to come off injured reserve, with the Rams likely making that transaction closer to gametime. The 30-year-old has been as good as any defensive player in football, and for the first time he’ll get to be on the same field as Aaron Donald as teammates. Best of luck, Commanders’ offensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Myles Garrett (knee) “is on track to be activated ahead of Sunday vs. the Commanders.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett has practiced all week and will likely be activated in the next 24 to 48 hours. The star pass-rusher who was acquired by the Rams in a blockbuster trade this offseason played in just one game for the Rams this season and did not record a tackle. Now, after undergoing knee surgery to correct a nagging injury, Garrett is all but set to return against the Commanders after missing seven straight games. His return will provide a much-needed boost to a Rams defense that ranks near the bottom of the league in sacks (12) through the first half of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) limited again on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett has a chance to face the Commanders this week, but he still belongs in the questionable column at this time. Rams CB1 Trent McDuffie (back) and S Kam Curl (foot) both missed practice for the second time this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) was able to practice again Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett has now been able to participate in back-to-back practices. The 30-year-old star defender appears to be ready to roll for Week 9 against the Commanders, but a decision on Garrett’s availability likely won’t be made until Friday at the earliest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Myles Garrett (knee) will practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Rams coach Sean McVay told reporters that Garrett will be limited today. The team could still give him another couple of weeks to ramp up, but he at least has a chance to play in Week 9 against the Commanders. Garrett underwent surgery on his injured knee back in September.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Sean McVay said Rams will open the 21-day practice window for Myles Garrett.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett will reportedly retake the practice field this week as he looks to make his return from injured reserve, a welcome sight for fans and the team, alike. Garrett played only 40 defensive snaps in Week 1 before suffering the injury that would cost him the following seven games. His eventual return will bolster a defense that has been underperforming preseason expectations, bringing a jolt to a team currently stuck at .500 with a 4-4 record. We’ll know more of the timing of his activation throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Myles Garrett (knee) will not be designated to return from injured reserve this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: There was hope within the organization late last week that Garrett could get back on the practice field today. That will have to wait at least one more week. Garrett hasn’t played since Week 1 because of a knee issue that required surgery. His absence will make life for Jayden Daniels substantially easier in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Rams are hopeful Myles Garrett (knee) returns to practice at least next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Rapoport didn’t go as far as to say they hope he is back for Week 8’s game against the Commanders, but it’s at least on the table. Garrett is currently on injured reserve, so we’ll know if he’s making progress if they open his practice window next week. The reigning DPOY has been out since Week 1 after undergoing surgery on his knee.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said EDGE Myles Garrett (knee) won’t have his 21-day practice window opened this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett went on injured reserve after Week 1 and is therefore eligible to have his 21-day practice window for activation off IR opened this week. However, McVay said the 30-year-old pass-rusher won’t have his window opened, indicating Garrett is not ready to practice yet and it will still be some time before we see him back on the field. His initial timeline after undergoing a knee scope was roughly six weeks. It’s been four weeks so far, but Garrett could still hit the six-week return timeline if his practice window is opened next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Myles Garrett “was given a timeline of roughly six weeks for his recovery from knee surgery.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/myles-garr.analysis: Garrett attempted to play through the knee issue in Week 1 but was clearly bothered by the balky knee. He underwent a knee scope shortly after the Rams’ opener and was placed on injured reserve. It was initially expected to be closer to a four-week absence for the reigning Defensive Player of the Year. Now he’ll miss a bit longer than that, and Rapoport added that the team will be cautious with his return, so he could be sidelined beyond even the six-week timeline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: We do not yet know Tyson’s participation level at Friday’s practice, but he remained limited on Wednesday and Thursday. It seems like he may need another week before he makes his NFL debut, but we don’t know for sure. If active, Tyson would be FLEX-viable. It is possible the team initially keeps him on a snap count.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: The Saints’ first-round rookie is now on the wrong side of questionable. It would have been nice to see him practice in full today. That said, New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill commented positively on Tyson’s performance, saying Tyson “does not look limited.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints designated Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson aggravated his nagging hamstring late in the offseason and was placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 1. He will practice for the first time today. NewOrleans.Football’s Nick Underhill said it’s possible Tyson plays this week, though he immediately mentioned a potential snap count for the rookie. The Saints likely want to ramp Tyson up slowly to avoid another setback. He was limited in Wednesday’s session. Tyson should be stashed in every fantasy format, but managers can’t count on him as even a FLEX play for at least one more week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said the team is still deciding when it will open Jordyn Tyson’s (hamstring) 21-day return window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: When Tyson landed on injured reserve, the initial belief was that he would return sometime after the Saints’ bye week. Whether that is in Week 9 or the coming weeks is still to be determined, but we wouldn’t expect him to take the field the same week the team opens his return window. That said, opening that window for a return is the first step in getting Tyson back on the field. If he takes the field Wednesday, Tyson would then have 21 days to practice before the team would need to officially activate him from injured reserve. We could still be a few weeks away from seeing the the rookie first-rounder in action, but hopefully we get an encouraging update on his progression this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints general manager Mickey Loomis said Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) won’t practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Loomis said Tyson is “improving” in his long rehab from a major preseason hamstring injury. Tyson, who traveled with the Saints to France for their Week 7 game against the Steelers, could still be a couple weeks away as the team takes a cautious approach to his recovery. In the meantime, Bryce Lance will operate as the Saints’ No. 2 wideout behind Chris Olave. Lance over the past two weeks has a 13 percent target share and a 20 percent air yards share in the pass-first New Orleans offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) traveled with the team to Paris for Week 7’s game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: The Saints have not opened Tyson’s 21-day window for return, but the fact that he traveled with the team suggests his window could be opened later this week, which would allow him to begin practicing with the team. There’s some belief that Tyson could return in Week 9 after the Saints’ bye week, but the team hasn’t committed to a return date for him just yet. We wouldn’t expect Tyson to suit up this week against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: When asked if Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) could resume practicing for Week 6 against the Giants, Saints coach Kellen Moore said, “not right now.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson was officially a non-participant to begin the week, as expected. Moore adds that Tyson is “progressing well,” and New Orleans Football’s Mike Triplett said there is “an expectation that he’ll return to practice soon.” Tyson should be rostered in 12-team formats, but fantasy managers must, unfortunately, remain patient.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is “weeks away from return.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: The Saints’ offense has managed just fine without Tyson, but it doesn’t sound like it will get a boost from the rookie first-rounder any time soon. According to Schefter, Tyson is “making progress and feeling good,” but the earliest we may see him is Week 7. That said, due to the Saints playing Week 7 in Paris, Schefter also notes that “the most logical” return date for Tyson could be Week 9 after the team’s bye week. Fantasy managers stashing Tyson will need to continue doing so for the next several weeks, and even when he’s active, it could take a few games for him to see a full assortment of snaps. We can expect Devaughn Vele to continue operating as the Saints’ WR2 behind Chris Olave until Tyson returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said that “at the moment,” he does not expect WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) to begin practicing next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson is currently on injured reserve and will be eligible to join his teammates on the practice field next week. Moore added, “but we shall see” at the end of his statement, making it at least possible for Tyson to resume practicing in Week 5. For now, Week 6 could be more likely. Once activated from injured reserve, Tyson will have a 21-day window to continue rehabbing, if need be.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints placed Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson has been dealing with hamstring issues since his senior season at Arizona State. The issue flared up during training camp and he is now expected to be sidelined for roughly two months, as of two weeks ago. With an international game in Week 7 and a bye the following week, a Week 9 return looks like the most likely outcome for the rookie. He could still put up strong fantasy numbers in the second half of the season, but it’s hard to justify holding him in leagues with shallow benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Donaldson wasn’t able to practice again Friday, and the 22-year-old tailback won’t be available for the Week 9 skirmish against Cleveland. Alvin Kamara will likely be the top option — and would have been even if Donaldson could play — in that contest, assuming his back injury allows him to play, of course. This is not a great situation, folks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: The way the team listed Kamara indicates that the back injury will not keep him from playing, but he is clearly still hurt. Kamara has been entirely ineffective this season and can only be viewed as a touchdown-dependent FLEX. CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) was unable to practice today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Donaldson aggravated a shoulder injury in Week 7 against the Steelers and did not return. He also entered the league’s concussion protocol after the game. A limited session today means he’s making progress on both fronts. He should be good to go for Week 9. The same is true of Alvin Kamara, who got a rest day today, despite his back injury also being noted on the report. Both backs will mix in behind Kendre Miller on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Donaldson is the third member of the Saints’ backfield committee. While he will get a few touches this week, he is not getting enough work for fantasy relevance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: The pass-protecting back looks likely to continue to mix in and limit snaps for the fantasy-valuable members of the backfield in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: A limited practice to start the week is usually maintenance. Donaldson looked good last week, running for 39 yards on six attempts, though he did commit one fumble. Donaldson is one of three backs seeing work for the Saints, and none of them have made a strong case to get more touches. Donaldson is a weak FLEX option for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson rushed six times for 39 yards and a fumble in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: A messy Saints committee backfield had Donaldson get the second-most snaps among New Orleans running backs against the Giants. He and Alvin Kamara were the passing-down backs while Donaldson also had a 17-yard run, the longest run by a Saints running back on the day. His first-career touchdown was called back in the third quarter after he was ruled down just shy of the goal line. The 22-year-old rookie has had a surprisingly high utilization early in the season and will continue to be involved while Travis Etienne is out. Despite this, his fantasy impact will mainly be to dilute Kamara and Kendre Miller’s fantasy values. Donaldson should only be rostered in the deepest of leagues heading into Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson rushed four times for 13 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings, adding one catch for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Alvin Kamara entered this game with a back injury and played just eight snaps in the second half, freeing up some extra work for Donaldson. He led the team in snaps, but Kendre Miller was the top option between the tackles, seeing 10 carries, one of which went for a touchdown. Even if Kamara remains on the injury report for Week 6, Donaldson won’t crack the FLEX rankings versus the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Kamara briefly left the Saints’ Week 4 game against the Falcons to deal with a knee injury. Today, he is sidelined by a back injury. It’s perhaps unsurprising for a 31-year-old player who has clearly lost a step at this point in his career. He is backed up by Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson. Either player can be stashed in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: Saints placed Travis Etienne on injured reserve with a hamstring injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: This is a tough break. The Saints’ high-priced free agent signee will be sidelined for at least four games. Their Week 8 bye makes him eligible to return in Week 9. Veteran RB Alvin Kamara is the next man up, followed by RB Kendre Miller. Both should be rostered in 12-team leagues. Kamara will likely get the first crack at the starting job, but he has struggled to play efficiently this season, and coach Kellen Moore gave RB CJ Donaldson the backfield’s first green zone touch last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Deshaun Watson (concussion) will not start in Week 9 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Head coach Todd Monken said Watson will be questionable for Sunday’s game, but has already said Shedeur Sanders will make his first start of the season. Watson missed Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices but was upgraded to a limited participant on Friday, although he has yet to clear concussion protocol. The decision to start Sanders likely stems from him working with the first-team offense during the week and the unlikelihood of Watson clearing protocol in time for Sunday’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Deshaun Watson (concussion) is “unlikely to start” in Week 9 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Watson has not practiced this week due to concussion symptoms he has been dealing with since Week 8’s loss to the Steelers. Unless he surprisingly clears concussion protocol this week, Watson will miss Week 9, paving the way for Shedeur Sanders to make his first start of the season. We will have official word on Watson’s status in a few hours, but at this point, it would be surprising if he does start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Deshaun Watson (concussion) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Cleveland’s Mary Kay Cabot indicated yesterday that Shedeur Sanders is seemingly slated to start in Week 9 against the Saints. If that ends up being the case, and Sanders can play well enough, it might be possible for him to steal the starting job from Watson this week. Sanders would be QB2-viable against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Cleveland.com’s Mary Kay Cabot said the “vibe” is that Shedeur Sanders will start in Week 9 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Cabot said it would be a challenge for Deshaun Watson to clear the NFL’s concussion protocol by Saturday and suit up for Sunday’s game. Watson suffered a head injury in Week 8 against the Steelers and reported concussion symptoms on Tuesday, according to the Browns. Sanders in 2025 was the most inaccurate quarterback in the league and struggled to support fantasy-relevant pass catchers. Harold Fannin could see a boost with Sanders under center after Sanders targeted the tight end relentlessly during his 2025 starts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Browns placed Deshaun Watson in the NFL’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Watson took a hit to the head in the first half of the Browns’ Week 8 loss to the Steelers. He was evaluated for a brain injury and re-entered the game. He then reported concussion-like symptoms on Tuesday and entered the protocol on Wednesday. It would be somewhat surprising if Watson is able to clear the protocol in time for the Browns’ Week 9 matchup against the Saints. That would likely mean Shedeur Sanders would get the starting nod against New Orleans. Sanders should only be rostered in superflex formats for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Deshaun Watson completed 27-of-39 passes for 324 yards in the Browns’ 27-6, Week 8 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: The Browns were never really a threat to win this game. The Steelers only led 7-0 at the end of the first quarter, but the Browns gained nine total yards in that quarter. Even when the Browns were able to keep the game close, the Steelers always seemed to answer with a big defensive play, and Watson was sacked eight times. With the Browns trailing by two touchdowns for the entire second half, Watson was able to air it out, but of his 324 yards, 240 of them came to Harold Fannin Jr. and the two running backs. Despite the high yardage totals, it wasn’t really a great showing for Watson, who seemed flustered in the pocket and struggled to connect with his wide receivers. Things could get easier against the Saints next week though, so he remains on the QB2 radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Deshaun Watson cleared concussion evaluation and is back in the game in Week 8 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Watson was evaluated after taking a hit to the head on the first drive. Shedeur Sanders played the end of the first drive, which ended in a Browns fumble, and now Watson is back in the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Deshaun Watson is being evaluated for a concussion in Week 8 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Watson was sacked on the second play of the game and then hit as he threw on the next play. The facemask of Steelers defender Jaquan Brisker hit the side of Watson’s helmet, and Watson was pulled into the blue tent for evaluation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Deshaun Watson completed 25-of-36 attempts for 308 yards and an interception in the Browns’ 27-24, Week 7 win against the Titans, adding three rushes for 19 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Watson again led the Browns to a heart-stopping fourth quarter comeback after the Titans tied the game late in the fourth quarter. Watson connected with Harold Fannin for a long gain that put the Browns in field goal range before they won the game at the buzzer. Watson targeted KC Concepcion a team high ten times, mostly on well-designed short area passes. He was seven percent over his expected completion rate — one of his best rates of the 2026 season. Watson rushed for a touchdown in the second half after being flushed out of the pocket; it was his first rushing score of the season. Watson, who now has two straight games without a passing score, should remain in superflex lineups next week against a pass-funnel Pittsburgh defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.headline: Deshaun Watson completed 16-of-26 passes for 164 yards in the Browns’ 13-10, Week 6 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deshaun-wa.analysis: Watson has now taken 13 sacks over the last two weeks. The Browns’ QB1 was under pressure all afternoon by the Ravens, but found himself in position to lead a game-winning drive with 1:59 left on the game clock. Watson started the drive with a nine-yard completion to Jaleel McLaughlin, but came up big on a third-and-five when he found Jerry Jeudy for a 33-yard gain to move into Ravens territory and position his team for the game-winning field goal attempt. Three plays later, Andre Szmyt, who missed the go-ahead field goal earlier in the game, converted on a 37-yard try to propel the Browns into first place in the AFC North. It wasn’t a pretty game for Watson, but that’s nothing new. He has thrown for just 319 yards and one touchdown in his last two games and has just two touchdowns in his last three games. He shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a low-end QB2 in next week’s road game against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said Shedeur Sanders will start in Week 9 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.analysis: Sanders will draw the start as Deshaun Watson (concussion) has yet to clear protocol in time to be ready for Sunday’s game. Interestingly, Watson is still expected to be listed as questionable, per Monken, but Sanders will draw the start. We are assuming this decision is based on Sanders taking first-team reps after Watson missed each of the first two days of practice, but this is a nice opportunity for Sanders to show whatever growth he has made since a tough rookie season in which he threw for 1,440 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 interceptions in eight games played. He’ll be on the low-end QB2 radar on the road against the Saints, who rank 16th in fantasy points allowed to opposing QBs this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.headline: Deshaun Watson (concussion) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.analysis: Cleveland’s Mary Kay Cabot indicated yesterday that Shedeur Sanders is seemingly slated to start in Week 9 against the Saints. If that ends up being the case, and Sanders can play well enough, it might be possible for him to steal the starting job from Watson this week. Sanders would be QB2-viable against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.headline: Cleveland.com’s Mary Kay Cabot said the “vibe” is that Shedeur Sanders will start in Week 9 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.analysis: Cabot said it would be a challenge for Deshaun Watson to clear the NFL’s concussion protocol by Saturday and suit up for Sunday’s game. Watson suffered a head injury in Week 8 against the Steelers and reported concussion symptoms on Tuesday, according to the Browns. Sanders in 2025 was the most inaccurate quarterback in the league and struggled to support fantasy-relevant pass catchers. Harold Fannin could see a boost with Sanders under center after Sanders targeted the tight end relentlessly during his 2025 starts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.headline: Browns placed Deshaun Watson in the NFL’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.analysis: Watson took a hit to the head in the first half of the Browns’ Week 8 loss to the Steelers. He was evaluated for a brain injury and re-entered the game. He then reported concussion-like symptoms on Tuesday and entered the protocol on Wednesday. It would be somewhat surprising if Watson is able to clear the protocol in time for the Browns’ Week 9 matchup against the Saints. That would likely mean Shedeur Sanders would get the starting nod against New Orleans. Sanders should only be rostered in superflex formats for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter said Shedeur Sanders could start in Week 3 if Deshaun Watson plays poorly in Week 2.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.analysis: Schefter said it “feels like Shedeur’s time is coming” if Watson bombs in the Browns’ Week 2 matchup with the Bucs following his Week 1 collapse against Jacksonville. Sanders, in that scenario, would be under center for the Browns’ home opener against the Panthers in Week 3. Sanders, who is slightly more accurate than Watson in the short and intermediate areas, would be an upgrade for Harold Fannin and KC Concepcion. He would likely be a downgrade for downfield air yards eater Denzel Boston.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports “the belief is that the first two games would serve as a natural evaluation point” for Deshaun Watson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.analysis: The Browns open the year with a two-game road trip before returning to Cleveland for their home opener next week. Watson was a disaster in Week 1, turning the ball over twice while throwing for 205 yards and one score. Another showing like that versus the Bucs this week and he could be sent to the bench. Shedeur Sanders would then draw the start against Carolina in Week 3. It’s unlikely the Browns offense turns things around under Sanders, but things truly cannot get worse than they are right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said he’s confident in Deshaun Watson’s downfield passing ability.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.analysis: Monken has stressed explosive plays as an important part of the Cleveland offense headed into the 2026 regular season. “Obviously having explosive players helps that,” Monken said. “Being able to scheme it up against certain looks and then being able to execute because your protection has to hold up when you get those opportunities. I’m confident in Deshaun and our ability to push the ball down the field, otherwise we wouldn’t be starting him.” That confidence might be misplaced considering Watson completed just 1-of-6 attempts for 20 yards and an interception on downfield passes in the preseason and was among the league’s worst deep ball passers in 2024, when he threw downfield on a career-low 27 percent of his attempts. Once an elite deep ball thrower, Watson will look to regain form coming off two torn Achilles, entering his age-30 season. Perhaps rookie WR Denzel Boston will be a boon for Watson’s downfield game in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.headline: Browns HC Todd Monken said it’s possible QB Taylen Green will be active for Week 1 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.analysis: When speaking with the media on Monday, Monken said, “There could be a package where we have (Green)” on the field. Monken also suggested he would prefer to not have three QBs active on game day , which could mean Shedeur Sanders would be a healthy scratch. Even if this were to happen, we shouldn’t assume this means Sanders is behind Green on the depth chart. As long as Deshaun Watson is in the QB1 seat, the Browns’ weekly game plan won’t include Sanders, while Green’s explosiveness on the ground could add another element to the offense in select packages, making him a more valuable option on game days. If Watson were to miss time due to injury or lose the starting job, we would still expect Sanders to be the next man up, with Green continuing to serve in select packages.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.headline: Shedeur Sanders will start the season as the QB2 for the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.analysis: Multiple outlets reported on Monday that Deshaun Watson would be the starter for Week 1 against the Jaguars, with Sanders as the backup. Sanders was solid in his second preseason game, completing 9-of-11 passes for 74 yards, a touchdown, and an interception in one half of play, but this camp battle was always expected to work in Watson’s favor, barring an obvious breakout by Sanders in camp. While it’s not the result Sanders and his fantasy managers hoped for, Watson’s job is anything but secure. He’ll start in Week 1, but the veteran QB will likely be evaluated on a week-to-week basis, meaning head coach Todd Monken could turn the job over to Sanders at any point in time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Browns plan to name Deshaun Watson as their starter for Week 1 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/shedeur-sa.analysis: This is coming from multiple reports, per Schultz. We’ll eventually get word from head coach Todd Monken on the decision, but it sounds like Watson, who was the favorite to win the battle entering training camp, will get the first crack at the starting job. Watson completed 16-of-27 passes for no touchdowns and one interception in his two preseason appearances, and struggled in last week’s outing against the Bills while playing with backups. Despite being booed off the field after a disappointing performance in front of a home crowd, the 30-year-old vet, who is in the final year of a five-year, $230 million fully guaranteed contract, will get the chance to show he can lead the Browns in 2026. Watson shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a low-end QB2 for fantasy purposes, but he has some exciting offensive weapons to throw to in Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion, and Harold Fannin.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) has been ruled questionable for Week 9 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: The Patriots are down A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) on top of their other skill-position issues, so if Henry can go, he could see a considerable amount of targets against the Packers. He didn’t practice Wednesday or Thursday, however, so it seems unlikely. Eli Raridon is inline to be the top tight end option if Henry can’t play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: It’s looking like rookie Eli Raridon will operate as the Patriots’ No. 1 tight end in Week 9 against the Packers. Henry has not participated in football activities since injuring his foot early in Week 8 against the Dolphins. Raridon would warrant streaming TE1 consideration if he gets the start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) was not seen at the start of Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Henry could ultimately get in a limited session later in the day, but this certainly looks like a DNP. The veteran tight end injured his foot early in the Pats’ Week 8 win over the Dolphins and did not return. Rookie Eli Raridon will take his spot in the lineup if Henry is unable to play this week. Raridon is averaging an impressive 13.3 yards per catch while mixing in behind Henry this year. He would immediately be in the TE2 mix if Henry is ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry did not return to the Patriots’ Week 8 win over the Dolphins after suffering a foot injury in the second quarter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: This is particularly unfortunate because Henry was playing well early on, catching 3-of-3 targets for 30 yards. Drake Maye told reporters after the game that he is “worried” about his No. 1 tight end, but added that Henry was “walking around fine” with “a smile on his face” in the locker room post-game. Eli Raridon will be a streaming TE1 against the Packers next week if Henry cannot play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry (foot) was taken back to the locker room after briefly returning in Week 8 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Henry briefly returned to the sideline after halftime, where he tested out his injured left foot. Evidently, the sideline testing did not go well. Henry was then taken right back to the locker room by the Patriots’ training staff. If the Patriots do end up ruling him out, as we expect, he will finish the day having caught 3-of-3 targets for 30 yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry exited Week 8 against the Dolphins after suffering an apparent foot injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Henry seemingly suffered the injury after catching a four-yard pass on the Patriots’ fourth drive. He ran a quick out route and hauled in the catch as he was sliding to the ground. A Dolphins defender touched him down, fairly forcefully. Henry’s left foot may have gotten trapped underneath him in the process. Henry removed his left cleat during a brief trip to the blue medical tent before slowly walking to the locker room for further examination.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry caught all seven targets for 71 yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Henry operated as the clear safety blanket for quarterback Drake Maye, the latter of whom was under constant duress in the face of unrelenting pressure from Dennis Allen’s Bears defense. The team was largely unable to move the football on the ground and fell into an early hole, leading to Josh McDaniels utilizing the short passing game as an extension of the run. That’s where Henry made his presence felt, although it was rookie tight end Eli Raridon that caught the touchdown at the position. Week 7 goes down as the first game with more than a modest five targets for the veteran tight end, who has quickly become a difficult weekly start in a more crowded New England pass offense. Fantasy managers might want to consider alternatives when the Patriots face the downtrodden Dolphins in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry caught 4-of-5 targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: It’s a fairly standard Henry box score, though the 48 yards were actually his second most of the season. The touchdown was his second, as well as second in as many weeks. Henry took advantage of a Jets communication breakdown near the goal line. By now we know Henry is a perfectly fine option if you find yourself in a streamer or second FLEX pinch, but he is not making a move on TE1 status heading into Week 7 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Eli Raridon caught 5-of-5 targets for 57 yards in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Raridon, who was out last week, was very much involved in the revived New England passing attack. Hunter Henry, meanwhile, had three grabs for 44 yards and a touchdown. The Patriots have used two tight end sets at a high rate when Raridon is healthy. Unless Henry misses time, Raridon should remain on waiver wires in most 12-team formats. He had been targeted on ten percent of his routes headed into Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry caught 3-of-4 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Henry was third on the team in targets and caught one of Drake Maye’s four touchdown tosses on the day. Henry has seen better involvement in the Pats offense of late; against the Bills in Week 4 he caught all five of his targets for 62 yards. The resurgence of the Patriots passing attack has made Henry viable as a streaming option. He’ll be in play next week against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: It seemed pretty obvious that Henderson wasn’t going to play Sunday after it was announced the second-year runner was dealing with “neurological symptoms” but it’s now official. There are much bigger things than football going on in his life. While he gets better, Corey Kiner should be the backup running back behind Rhamondre Stevenson going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson released a statement saying that he was dealing with an “unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: This certainly sounds like a scary situation for Henderson, whose absence has been the subject of speculation for nearly two weeks. Henderson said that the results of “comprehensive medical testing have come back positive and reassuring, but he continues to work with specialists and physical therapists. Henderson said these issues have affected his “strength, coordination, and some of [his] physical functions,” while adding that he is working to return to full health. While we don’t want to speculate too much, it doesn’t sound like Henderson will be back anytime soon. Hopefully we will get more clarity on his situation soon, but our thoughts are with him and his continued recovery.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: ESPN’s Mike Reiss believes TreVeyon Henderson’s illness might be related to the “adversity” he has faced this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Reiss was asked about Henderson’s status during his weekly appearance on the local radio show, Toucher & Hardy. According to Reiss, Henderson has faced a lot of new challenges this season, including recurring ankle issues and limited playing time, and the adversity has been tough for Henderson to deal with. Some might remember that similar reports surfaced regarding Bucky Irving, beset by multiple injuries, last season. Henderson might need more time before he resumes playing. Stay tuned. He was officially listed as a non-participant on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: It’s rare for a player to miss even one game with an illness. It’s even more unheard of for them to miss the next practice. It’s possible Henderson is dealing with something more severe than the flu or a stomach bug. If he isn’t able to play in Week 9, Rhamondre Stevenson will handle the bulk of the backfield touches once again. He touched the ball 22 times on Sunday and would be in line for a similar workload against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was ruled out for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson first popped on the injury report with a missed practice Thursday before maintaining that status to end the week, ultimately unable to play through the ailment while being ruled out Saturday. Rhamondre Stevenson steps into a potential workhorse role against the downtrodden Dolphins, where he will be an upside RB2 in Week 8. Expect the team to elevate another back from their practice squad ahead of Sunday’s game to play behind Stevenson and Corey Kiner, the latter of whom is expected to serve as the primary change of pace option with Henderson out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) is questionable for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson missed practice Thursday with an illness, ultimately drawing the questionable tag for the team’s Week 8 divisional clash with the Dolphins. That places fantasy managers in a precarious position considering the team plays in the afternoon portion of the Sunday slate. It would be prudent to make alternate plans at FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Illnesses typically don’t hold back NFL players, so we’d be surprised if Henderson missed time, but it is worth noting that it was a Thursday addition to the report. Because of that, if he missed Friday, it wouldn’t be surprising if he was listed as questionable. We’d still expect him to play either way.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson rushed three times for nine yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears, adding 14 yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson continues to play second, or third, fiddle behind Rhamondre Stevenson when the Patriots are forced into “gotta have it” mode, with Stevenson the back most trusted in key situations. The Patriots fell into an early hole and were playing catch-up throughout against the Bears, something that could help to explain the lowly opportunity total for the back widely considered the more explosive of the two. Furthermore, the team continued to rotate Corey Kiner through the opportunity pecking order, placing another sizable dent in the weekly floor of Henderson. Although he could find more opportunities in a softer matchup in Week 8, he’ll be a difficult click to insert into fantasy lineups against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is not on the final injury report for Week 7 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson will be active for the Patriots’ Thursday Night Football game, but his usage is up in the air. Patriots coach Mike Vrabel got RB Corey Kiner going late last week after Henderson fumbled. The Patriots won’t simply discard their former second-round pick, so he remains FLEX-viable, but he may be playing with a very limited touch count.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: It’s been a stunningly quick recovery from what looked to be a high-ankle sprain that could sideline him. Henderson has practiced in full both days this week. We’re not concerned that he won’t play, but after fumble problems struck last week and Corey Kiner closed out the Jets in the fourth quarter, we do have slightly lowered expectations for his Thursday night stat line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Bryce Young (ankle) will play in Week 9 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young never really felt like he was at risk of missing this week. Despite dealing with an ankle injury, the Panthers’ QB1 was listed as a full participant in practice throughout the week and will be good to go despite what appears to be a minor ankle injury. Young draws a tough Week 9 matchup at home against the Broncos and has thrown two touchdowns and three interceptions in his last two games, and has completed below 60 percent of his passes in his last three outings. He’ll be a risky QB2 this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said after Week 8’s loss to the Packers that Young’s knee injury could be limiting his mobility. The team didn’t list the knee issue on this week’'s injury report, instead adding an ankle injury to the mix. It’s not something that will prevent Young from playing on Sunday, but another lingering ailment could further hamper his mobility. Already in the midst of a two-game slump, Young is back in the middle of the QB2 ranks for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Bryce Young’s knee injury may be limiting his mobility.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young declined to get into details about his knee injury after Thursday night’s loss to the Packers, saying, “Everyone’s dealing with something; it’s no excuse,” when speaking with the media after the game. Canales didn’t seem overly concerned about Young’s injury after the game, but did acknowledge that he didn’t appear to have the “quick, make you miss” aspect to his game against the Packers. Young was listed on the Panthers’ injury report throughout the week, but was also a full participant in practice. Young’s knee could be partly to blame for the six sacks he took in Thursday’s loss, and his health will be one to monitor in the weeks ahead, especially with the team already past its Week 5 bye. Assuming he’s good to go in Week 9, Young will face an uphill battle against a stout Broncos defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 23-of-41 passes for 209 yards with a touchdown and an interception in the Panthers’ 27-19, Week 8 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Those who believe that sacks are a quarterback stat might change their mind watching the Panthers block Thursday night. The 25-year-old had no time to throw and couldn’t get out of the pocket while taking six sacks and being pressured on what seemed like every throw. That’s not to say that Young was completely a victim of his circumstance; he struggled with accuracy and couldn’t get the ball downfield in another ugly performance for the 25-year-old sans a 26-yard passing score to Jalen Coker in the middle of the fourth. Things won’t get any easier on paper in Week 9, as Young and the Panthers face the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Panthers listed Bryce Young (knee) as a full participant on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young was listed with the same knee injury last Friday but remained a full participant and was good to go in Week 7. Whatever issue he’s dealing with appears minor, especially if the team is still listing him as a full participant. At this point, there’s no reason to think he won’t be active for Week 8’s game against the Packers on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 14-of-27 passes for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the Panthers’ Week 7 game against the Bucs, also losing a fumble-six.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: With the Panthers somehow losing 43-6 in the fourth quarter, Young gave way to Kenny Pickett for the final 10:11. Pickett immediately engineered a garbage time touchdown drive. This was by far Young’s worst performance of what had so far been a legitimate breakout campaign, as he short-circuited one drive after another and set up Bucs short fields with turnovers. The fumble-six was the most costly mistake, but Young’s second interception was probably his worst throw. He was fooled by the coverage under pressure and threw the ball right to Tykee Smith. Young’s first pick came after Jalen Coker fell down. In between all the miscues, Young could get nothing going with either Coker or Tetairoa McMillan. It was hard to see this coming — especially against the Bucs — but it is even harder to see it continuing for Thursday’s short-week date with the Packers. With that contest likely to feature shootout game script, Young will remain in the low-end QB1 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young (knee) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: It’s the first time we’ve seen Young o the injury report with this knee issue, though a full practice today is nothing to worry about. He will be good to go for his date with the Bucs. Young is currently the QB4 by fantasy points per game. Even if he does cool down this week, Young should be in most starting fantasy lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 20-of-39 passes for 281 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ 25-14, Week 6 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: This game was never quite as easy as many thought it would be given Philadelphia’s injuries. Young looked pretty good, but he was often under pressure, and the Panthers continued to make things harder on themselves with 13 penalties for 149 yards. A few of those really killed the momentum on some Panthers drives. Still, Young made enough big throws and receivers were schemed open into space repeatedly throughout the day. We’d expect that to continue next week against a Bucs defense that might not be as talented as this Eagles one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 29-of-41 passes for 329 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 4 win over the Lions, adding three yards on three carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: The NFL’s passing leader through four weeks, pending Monday Night Football, took complete advantage of a defense still working to find their identity through the first month of play, leaning on his top option in Tetairoa McMillan throughout. Young now leads the league in passing and can only be caught by Tyler Shough on Monday Night Football, while only Kirk Cousins and Brock Purdy have more touchdown passes than Young’s nine. Even more impressive was the fact that he did what he did to the Lions without two of his top three receivers with both Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette out of action in Week 4. Young and the Panthers head to their Week 5 bye at 2-2 and alone atop the NFC South, soon to be joined by the winner on Monday night. He’ll be a legitimate QB1 when he returns to action against the Eagles in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Panthers QB Bryce Young (knee) is practicing in full for Week 4 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young visited the blue medical tent a couple of times after taking a cleat to the knee in Week 3 against the Browns. He reportedly underwent imaging to assess the injury. We never received an official follow-up report, but he is practicing in full already, so the imaging evidently checked out just fine. After years of frustrating performances, Young is suddenly a low-end QB1 against an injury-impacted Lions pass defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown was unable to practice again Friday, and the 29-year-old will not be able to roll against the Green Bay secondary. It’s a second-consecutive missed game for Brown, who has played in just three games since his blockbuster deal to the Patriots prior to the season. DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams will be Drake Maye’s top wideout targets for the game against Green Bay. Not ideal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown seems highly unlikely to play in Week 9 against the Packers. The Patriots could shut him down for a little while, with the goal of getting his degenerative knee and early-season high-ankle sprain healed. For now, fantasy managers should make backup plans in the short term.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown’s recurring knee issue flared up during practice last week. He was downgraded to a DNP on Thursday and Friday. The Pats then ruled him out over the weekend. Brown has been dealing with this injury for years, and it was something the Pats acknowledged when they traded for him in the offseason. It wouldn’t be surprising for the team to give him multiple weeks off in preparation for a playoff run. Head coach Mike Vrabel sidestepped a question about putting Brown back on injured reserve. At a minimum, we’re not expecting Brown to suit up this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said “we’ll see” when asked if A.J. Brown (knee) could practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: This is basically a non-answer from Vrabel, who said the team will see how Brown progresses through the week and how he responds to treatment. Brown missed Week 8’s game against the Dolphins after he suffered what was described as a flare up” of a knee issue that has plagued him for some time. It’s far too early to assume Brown will be able to go in Week 9 against the Packers given the timing of his injury last week, so his status will be one to keep an eye on throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (knee) was ruled out for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: This was always thought to be the case after Brown missed Thursday and Friday with a “flare up” of an existing knee injury, the same issue that ultimately saw the Rams back out of trade negotiations this offseason. Brown’s absence comes at a horrible time for a team already without Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs, leaving only DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism as healthy wide receivers on the active roster. Fantasy managers in a bind could consider taking a shot on upside through Williams’ downfield role against a Dolphins team bleeding explosive passing through the first seven weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said A.J. Brown (knee) is questionable for New England’s Week 8 game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: This feels like a very optimistic questionable after Brown missed the last two practices of the week with a new knee tweak. Brown-reliant managers should be making contingency plans ready for Sunday. “We’ll see when he comes in tomorrow, and we’ll make a decision,” Vrabel said.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (knee) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown has now missed back-to-back practices and is at serious risk of missing Week 8’s game against the Dolphins. Brown’s knee injury was reported as a “flare-up” from a previous knee injury, which is never a good sign for a player. Brown has been dealing with injuries like this for a few years but has always found a way to play through them. While it’s possible he ends up doing so again this week, fantasy managers should begin considering other options in the event he is held out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (knee) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: The downgrade in participation raises serious questions surrounding his potential availability when the Patriots face the Dolphins in Week 8. Brown had been mostly limited in practice since being activated from injured reserve due to a separate ankle issue, with the absence Thursday marking the first fully missed practice in that window. Fantasy managers will want to monitor his status Friday as they make plans for their weekend ahead. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported Thursday that the veteran receiver’s absence is due to a “flare up” of a previous knee injury, placing his status for Sunday in doubt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Setting Brown’s drops aside, Brown still looked like he was working his way back from his high-ankle sprain last week against the Bears. He was laboring through his routes at times, particularly downfield. Targets should continue flowing his way, but Brown is perhaps best viewed as a volume-driven WR2 against the Dolphins in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown caught 3-of-6 targets for 48 yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown has not yet clicked with his new team after going down with injury in Week 1 and spending the subsequent four games on injured reserve. He committed yet another drop against the Bears after three drops the week prior, this time on what would have been a long gain down the left sideline. Brown’s burst off the line and at the top of routes appears to remain hampered, something both the Patriots and Brown’s fantasy managers hope will remedy in short order. You can’t really sit Brown at this point, but fantasy managers have to be growing impatient of their first or second-round selection. Brown remains a teeth-gritting start ahead of a Week 8 matchup with the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Bam Knight (concussion) will not play in Week 9 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: LaFleur also ruled out OL Jon Gaines II (ankle) and OT Jayden Williams (knee). Knight has been a DNP all week after suffering a concussion in Week 8’s win over the Cowboys and will officially be sidelined for Week 9.
