His absence, along with Jeremiyah Love’s (ankle) could create a bell cow role for Tyler Allgeier, who totaled 191 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns in last week’s win, while fourth-year vet Evan Hull could also work into the mix. Allgeier’s volume alone will put him in the RB2 conversation this week despite the tough matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Bam Knight (concussion) was not spotted at Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: It appears it’ll be another DNP for Knight as he entered the concussion protocol following Sunday’s win over the Cowboys in Week 8. The 25-year-old tailback seems unlikely to be able to go in Week 9 against the Seahawks, but there should be further updates on Knight’s status soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Bam Knight (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Knight entered concussion protocol after a hit to the head in Week 8 against the Cowboys. Starting out as a DNP this week means he still has a few steps to go to clear protocol by Sunday. Unless he can progress through protocol quickly, Knight is on the wrong side of questionable for Week 9 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Bam Knight is in the league’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Knight will need to clear protocol if he hopes to suit up in time to play in Week 9 against the Seahawks. The former UDFA has turned in a solid season thus far for the Cardinals, rushing for 28-168-0 while adding another six receptions for 43 additional yards. With Jeremiyah Love (ankle) likely to miss time, Knight could again find himself in a split with Tyler Allgeier when he returns. The Cardinals will likely need to address their running back room at some point in the week with Allgeier currently being the only healthy back on the roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: FOX’s Pam Oliver reports Zonovan Knight (head) left Arizona’s Week 8 game against the Cowboys and won’t return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: She got word from Mike LaFleur that Knight would be out. Knight wasn’t officially given an injury declaration as of yet, but it was a fairly textbook shoulder-to-the-head that caused a fumble towards the waning moments of the second half. Knight had 18 total yards on three carries and one catch before leaving. We would be surprised, given how brutal the hit he took looked, if he were available for Week 9. This leaves Tyler Allgeier as the lone healthy back for the second half of this game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Tyler Allgeier (toe) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Allgeier popped up on the injury report with a toe issue as rookie Jeremiyah Love (ankle) returned to practice in a limited fashion. Though we don’t know the severity of Allgeier’s injury, it may be worth keeping Bam Knight rostered despite Love’s return. If Allgeier cannot play in Week 8 against the Cowboys, Knight will get another week of fantasy viability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will be limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: We were hoping to see Love practice in full after taking two weeks off. While today’s limited session puts him on track to play in Week 8 against the Cowboys, Bam Knight and Tyler Allgeier are still worth stashing on benches, just in case. The Cardinals are finally handling Love’s recovery patiently, after giving him far too many touches early in the preseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Bam Knight rushed seven times for 48 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 7 loss to the Broncos, adding three catches for 15 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Knight only saw one fewer carry than Tyler Allgeier. His 29-yard scamper in the first quarter alone was enough to best Allgeier’s mark of 19 yards. Knight had a chance to get in the end zone on a strike from Jacoby Brissett, but he dropped the would-be touchdown and Arizona had to settle for a field goal. It’s unclear if Jeremiyah Love will be back next week. If he isn’t, Knight will once again operate as the 1B in this backfield, putting him in the RB3/4 mix versus Dallas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Bam Knight will handle “a lot of work” on early downs with Jeremiyah Love (ankle) sidelined.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: LaFleur simply does not believe that any one running back can handle a full-time role and remain healthy, so he employs a committee approach. Although Tyler Allgeier sits ahead of Knight on the depth chart, LaFleur said he views Allgeier as a reliable complementary running back who excels in pass protection and short-yardage. Knight will be the team’s lead rusher on early downs and can be started in the FLEX against the Broncos this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will not play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Things have been trending in this direction all week, but LaFleur officially confirmed on Friday that Love will miss a second straight game. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will likely split duties again in Week 7 after seeing a near 50/50 split in the touch distribution last week, with Allgeier’s 19 touches narrowly edging out Knight’s 17. Both Allgeier and Knight are fringe RB2/RB3 plays against a stout Broncos defense. In addition to Love the Cardinals also ruled out DT Walter Nolen III (ankle), S Andrew Wiggins (ankle), and OG Jo Gaines II (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-turner-.headline: DJ Turner (heel) will play in the Bengals’ Week 9 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-turner-.analysis: After being upgraded to a full participant in Thursday’s practice, Turner was officially removed from the injury report on Friday, meaning he will be good to go for Sunday’s international tilt against the Falcons. Turner has allowed 16 receptions for 133 yards and one touchdown on 26 targets this season, per PFF, earning a coverage grade of 72.9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-turner-.headline: DJ Turner (heel) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-turner-.analysis: The Bengals No. 1 cornerback is firmly on track to play in Week 9 against the Falcons. While Drake London would get a matchup boost if Turner were to sit out, Turner’s presence does not drop London out of the WR1 tier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-turner-.headline: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said DJ Turner is day-to-day with a heel injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-turner-.analysis: Turner was initially believed to have suffered an ankle injury in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans, but it was later ruled to be a heel injury. According to Taylor, the fourth-year corner has a chance to suit up in Week 9 when the Bengals take on the Falcons in Madrid, so his status will be one to keep an eye on throughout the week. Turner has earned a PFF coverage grade of 72.9 this season, allowing opposing receivers to catch 16-of-26 targets for 132 yards and one touchdown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-turner-.headline: DJ Turner (ankle) was ruled out in Week 8 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-turner-.analysis: Turner went down with an apparent ankle injury at the start of the fourth quarter. He was quickly ruled out, indicating the injury is major enough to put his status in question beyond this week. Josh Newton entered the game for Turner and allowed a go-ahead touchdown. Drake London will be set up for a nice fantasy WR1 game in Week 9 against the Bengals if Turner misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-turner-.headline: Bengals CB DJ Turner (hamstring) will play in Week 1 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-turner-.analysis: Turner popped up on Thursday’s injury report with the hamstring issue, but head coach Zac Taylor said the fourth-year corner will be good to go for Sunday’s game. Turner posted career highs in pass breakups (18) and interceptions (2) last season while earning a PFF coverage grade of 78.1. The Bengals will rely heavily on him in Week 1 to slow down Baker Mayfield and a revamped Buccaneers passing game. While Turner is healthy and good to go, Taylor said DE Shemar Stewart (knee) is doubtful, making him unlikely to play in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-turner-.headline: Bengals CB DJ Turner (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-turner-.analysis: Defensive injuries aren’t always notable. This one is. Turner, 25, is an up-and-coming star defender, capable of challenging No. 1 wide receivers. If he is absent on Sunday, Buccaneers wide receivers will have a far easier time getting open.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-turner-.headline: The Athletic’s Paul Dehner reports the Bengals will have extension talks with CBs DJ Turner and Dax Hill.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-turner-.analysis: Turner had a 78.1 PFF coverage grade last year in a career-high 974 snaps and is entering the final year of his rookie deal, while Hill is entering his fifth-year option offseason having moved into the slot more often last year. Turner would appear to be the more important player to extend, but the Bengals are definitely still in “keep as many good pieces from last year’s defense as possible” mode.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-turner-.headline: Bengals coach Zac Taylor said DJ Turner (clavicle) will be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-turner-.analysis: He has “the potential to be gone for the year” and the Bengals are looking to add options in the secondary per Taylor. Turner had some big plays in Week 11’s loss to the Chargers and was just starting to round in to form. It’s a tough loss for a defense that is already best described as beleaguered.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-turner-.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Bengals fear CB DJ Turner suffered a fractured clavicle in Week 11’s loss to the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-turner-.analysis: According to Rapoport, Turner will seek a second opinion on his injury, but the second-year corner “is likely out for the season.” Turner has started every game for the Bengals this season, earning a PFF coverage grade of 68.4 while allowing 21 receptions for 253 yards on 39 targets. He has yet to allow a touchdown this season and has broken up eight passes, per PFF. His loss would be a tough one for a Bengals defense that is already struggling to slow its opponents.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-turner-.headline: Bengals selected Michigan CB DJ Turner with the No. 60 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-turner-.analysis: The IMG Academy product was an unheralded three-star prospect who spent two years working his way up the Wolverines’ depth chart before finally breaking into the lineup in 2021. That year he earned Honorable Mention All-American honors with a sterling 54.8 passer rating when targeted and 83.8 PFF coverage grade. Turner (5’11/178) raised his level of play last year by recording 11 PBU with a 46.5 completion rate en route to Second Team All-Big Ten status. What he lacks in size, he makes up for with savvy, technique, and speed. And by speed, we’re talking a ludicrous 4.26s which was the fastest time at the 2023 Combine. Turner backed his rare speed score with a 38.5 vertical (88th%) and 10’11” broad jump (96th%) for a very projectable 9.59 RAS. A true worker bee, he can trigger in a snap and accelerates like a roadster when he’s trailing. While he’s still filling out his frame, the biggest concern NFL teams have is does Turner have enough strength to hold up physically on the outside against bigger wideouts despite his lean upper body? While he spent most of his Michigan tenure on the boundary, Turner will need to improve his play strength to win consistently in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) will play in Week 9 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: This comes a day after Hall said he expects to play, so this news isn’t all too surprising. Hall’s return could somewhat complicate the Jets’ backfield situation on Sunday, however, as Braelon Allen has played well in Hall’s absence, making a strong case for more touches even when Hall is healthy. Glenn declined to get into how he plans to divvy up his running backs’ touches next week, saying “both guys will play,” when asked about his plans. This was already shaping up to be a tough fantasy matchup on the road against the Chiefs, but a potential backfield split would only further complicate matters. Until we see how things shake out, both Hall and Allen should be viewed as mid-to-low-end RB2s.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall (quad) said he is ready to go for Week 9 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: We expect to see Hall listed as a full participant on today’s injury report. An update will be provided if that is not the case. Earlier today, Jets OC Frank Reich discussed Hall and Braelon Allen’s expected usage, saying having the two players is “a great problem to have,” referring to the duo as “two No. 1 backs.” That said, Reich added that Hall “is obviously the bell cow,” but the backfield usage will be a “mix” of both players. Jets coach Aaron Glenn will reportedly share his ideal backfield split with Reich, who will work with the position coaches to make it happen. Hall likely belongs in the high-end RB2 tier while Allen remains FLEX-viable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall (quad) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Hall is expected to return this week, but a full practice might be required before the team gives him the go-ahead. Hall logged three limited practices last week before being ruled out on Sunday. Barring a setback, we’re still expecting Hall to ramp up to a full session over the next two days. Assuming he does, Hall will likely split work with Braelon Allen, who has been extremely effective as the Jets’ workhorse running back in his absence. Both backs will sit in the RB3 ranks for their Week 9 date with the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) is “trending in the right direction.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Hall, barring setbacks in practice, should be OK for Week 9 against the Chiefs. What his workload will look like is another question entirely. Braelon Allen has established himself as an efficient, tough runner over the past few weeks, and could remain the Jets’ lead rusher while Hall takes on most pass-catching opportunities. Though Hall should have some kind of floor in Week 9, he probably doesn’t have much of a ceiling unless the Jets decided to phase out Allen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich said he “assumes” Breece Hall will remain the team’s lead back when he returns from injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn has knocked down suggestions that the Jets would trade Hall before the league’s trade deadline, as Braelon Allen continues as one of the NFL’s most productive rushers. When asked about how the backfield might look when Hall returns from his quad injury, Reich seemed to say Hall would remain the de facto lead runner. “Well, that’s obviously coach’s decision, but they’re both the guy … I mean, that’s a good problem to have,” Reich said. “That’s coach’s decision, but to me … Breece is our guy. I’m assuming Breece is our guy, you know what I mean? He’s one of the best in the NFL, but I think what’s been so excited is like, oh my gosh, we’ve got two of them. I mean, we’ve got two. This Braelon guy, he’s a beast as well.” Allen this season ranks third among running backs in rushing success rate; 11th in rush yards over expected per attempt; eighth in yards after contact per rush; and over the past three weeks he ranks eighth among RBs in expected fantasy points per game, proving the haters wrong along the way. Hall is expected to return to action this week against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Breece Hall (quad) is “now good to go and should play next week” against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: It was reported on Sunday that Hall was “hoping for next week,” which is now here, as the Jets prepare to take on the Chiefs in Kansas City. After logging a week of limited practices and entering last weekend as questionable, Hall was still scratched from Week 8’s game against the Raiders, leading some to believe he had suffered a setback in his recovery. Hopefully that was more of a case of the Jets exercising caution with their RB1, especially with Braelon Allen playing well in his absence. Hall’s status will still be one to monitor, but this is a very optimistic report on him to start the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said “we’re in the business of keeping good players” when asked if the team would consider trading Breece Hall before the deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: The Jets are 2-6 and Braelon Allen has put together a solid few weeks in Hall’s absence. As a result, there has been some speculation as to whether or not the Jets would consider moving Hall, who has missed the last five games with a quad injury. In addition to saying the Jets are “in the business of keeping good players,” Glenn also was sure to remind the media that Hall is “one of our better players,” suggesting there are no plans to move the 25-year-old back at this year’s deadline. If he’s able to play next week against the Chiefs, Hall would fall somewhere in the RB2 ranks in his return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: DNVR Broncos’ Zac Stevens reports that the Broncos are “going to try” to trade for Jonathan Taylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Stevens said that this trade “could happen at any moment,” telling Broncos Country that they “might not want to go to sleep.” While this could be hyperbole, it sounds like Stevens is saying the trade could go down tonight. Stevens said he’s had conversations with multiple people on the matter, and the Broncos “know that this is not the time to wait and develop” young running backs. Stevens closed by reminding viewers that the Broncos were very interested in Breece Hall at one point, and added that there are likely other backup plans that the Broncos could be considering.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall (quad) is inactive for Week 8 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Hall seems to have suffered a rather serious setback with the quad injury that has been dogging him since September. This is easily said in hindsight, but it would seem Gang Green did not handle the issue particularly well. Hall is supposedly “hoping for next week,” but we would consider him on the wrong side of questionable until further notice. Isaiah Davis will serve as Braelon Allen’s breather back. Joining Hall on the shelf are EDGE David Bailey, WR Tim Patrick, CB Nahshon Wright, ED David Bailey, OL Kohl Levao and OL Max Mitchell.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Breece Hall (quad) is “hoping for next week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported an hour ago that Braelon Allen will get the start, but he didn’t explicitly rule out Hall for Week 8. Fowler’s report makes things relatively black and white. Hall will miss today’s game versus the Raiders. He got in three practices this week before being listed as questionable on Friday. Though a Week 9 return is on the table, the Jets’ failure to put Hall on IR, only for him to miss at least five games, suggests his injury is worse than they initially expected. It’s possible he’s held out beyond today’s game. Braelon Allen will continue to dominate the Jets’ backfield touches until Hall returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kadyn-proctor/.headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said Kadyn Proctor cleared concussion protocol and will play in Week 9 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kadyn-proctor/.analysis: Proctor missed last week’s game against the Patriots with a brain injury, but will be back in his normal left guard position for this week’s game against the Lions. In six games this season, Proctor has appeared on more than 350 offensive snaps, earning a PFF grade of 64.8 while allowing one sack and 13 pressures.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kadyn-proctor/.headline: Kadyn Proctor (concussion) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kadyn-proctor/.analysis: The Dolphins’ starting left guard should make his return this week after sitting out in Week 8 against the Patriots. Proctor’s presence will help stabilize the pocket for Malik Willis.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kadyn-proctor/.headline: Dolphins HC Jeff Hafley said No. 12 overall pick OT Kadyn Proctor “can excel at both tackle and guard.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/kadyn-proctor/.analysis: “We could see him getting some work at guard or tackle,” Hafley told reporters. “We’ll all talk more about it and sort it out.” Proctor played almost exclusively left tackle in his final season at Alabama but apparently showed the Miami brass enough to gain excitement about a potential multi-faceted offensive lineman. New offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik has long showed a propensity to run to set up the pass since his time with the Texans, with it now appearing more likely that Proctor takes the bulk of his snaps at right guard after being a bulldozer in the run game in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kadyn-proctor/.headline: Dolphins traded back with the Cowboys to select Alabama OT Kadyn Proctor with the No. 12 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kadyn-proctor/.analysis: In addition to the No. 12 overall pick, the Dolphins also acquired the No. 177 and No. 180 overall picks from the Cowboys. Proctor (6’6"/352) anchored Alabama’s offensive line at left tackle in 2025, logging 901 snaps with 882 of them coming on the blindside and turning in his busiest collegiate season to date. He was notably sturdy in pass protection, allowing 21 pressures on 584 pass-block snaps with only 2 sacks attributed, translating to an 84.2 PFF pass-block grade and a solid 98.0 efficiency rating on traditional protections and 97.5 on true pass sets where Alabama asked him to win one-on-one. In the run game, Proctor paired that pass-proficiency with a mauling mentality, earning an 81.1 PFF run-block grade. Across all phases he was disciplined, committing just 2 penalties on the year and a modest 2.3% blown-block rate, helping stabilize an Alabama unit that had trouble running the ball. He checked out well athletically at the Combine with a 32.5” vertical (94th%) and 9.26 overall RAS score. The mammoth Proctor is rugged in the run game (0.6% blown run block rate), effective in pass pro, and the kind of reliable, high-volume anchor who has the traits to become a long term contributor, whether it is at guard or tackle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kadyn-proctor/.headline: Iowa received a verbal commitment from five-star 2023 OT Kadyn Proctor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kadyn-proctor/.analysis: The commitment of Proctor (6'8/330) to the Hawkeyes is a monumental move for head coach Kirk Ferentz and the program. The No. 2 ranked OT recruit in the country has opted to stay home and play for his hometown Hawkeyes, becoming the seventh in-state recruit of the 2023 class to commit to the program. Proctor brings enormous size to the OT position and is expected to spend most of his time on the left side of the line. The three-sport athlete also participates in basketball, along with track and field, and placed fifth as a junior at the Iowa State Track and Field Championship in May 2022. Prior to committing to Iowa, Proctor had also received offers from Alabama, Arkansas, Auburn, Florida, Florida, State, Georiga, and several other big-name programs. 247Sports.com’s Allen Trieu has already comped him to NFL star LT Trent Williams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kadyn-proctor/.headline: 2023 five-star T Kadyn Proctor set his official visits for the summer.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kadyn-proctor/.analysis: Proctor (6'8/330) has the ideal size for the tackle position and has been heavily recruited by schools across the nation. His visits are very reflective of that. He will be visiting Arkansas State, Alabama, Penn State, and Oregon in June with a visit to Michigan on Labor Day weekend. He won’t be taking a visit to home state school Iowa and for good reason. “I have been to Iowa 10 or more times, so I will be taking officials out of state just to have those other experiences.” They are safely in the mix for the five-star recruit and number six overall player per the On3 Consensus, who is described as a “physically developed tackle who excels as a mauling run blocker.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: The Ravens and Cardinals finalized a trade on Friday that sends Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: We already knew this deal would be done, but the two sides made things official on Friday. The Ravens will receive Brissett, along with a 2027 fifth-round pick from the Cardinals in exchange for a 2027 4th-round pick and a 2028 7th-round pick. Brissett will immediately step into a starting role for the Ravens when they face the Chargers in Week 10 and should provide an immediate upgrade over Joe Fagnano, who struggled mightily in his first career start against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that the Ravens are acquiring Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals in a deal that is expected to be completed this weekend.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Schefter adds that this trade will not be completed in time for Brissett to play in Week 9’s Thursday Night Football game for the Ravens, but he will make his debut in Week 10 against the Chargers. Brissett’s impending arrival in Baltimore immediately stabilizes the pass-catching corps’ fantasy value. The trade compensation has not yet been revealed, but we expect to know more soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett will serve as the Cardinals’ emergency QB3 in Week 9 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: After holding out part of the offseason for a new deal that was fitting for a starting QB in the league, Brissett now finds himself as the QB3 of the Cardinals entering Week 9. There’s a good chance this is the end of the road for Brissett as far as his time with the Cardinals is concerned, as a handful of dire QB situations around the league could warrant a trade to a contender who is looking to upgrade at QB before the trade deadline. Brissett was solid last season for a three-win Cardinals team, throwing for 3,366 yards, 23 touchdowns, and eight interceptions in 12 starts. He currently sports a 1,719-10-7 line this season but has struggled in his last three starts, throwing just one touchdown to two interceptions. With Brissett being demoted to QB3, rookie Carson Beck will be elevated to QB2 on game days, and draws ever closer to making his first career start at some point in the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 10-of-23 passes for 119 yards and an interception before being benched for Gardner Minshew in the third quarter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: He took four sacks, including back-to-back sacks to kill a third-quarter drive, before being replaced. Brissett hasn’t necessarily played this poorly all season, but we’d been getting plenty of questions at press conferences about if he’d remain the starter so we’re ultimately unsurprised by this move. Minshew took over and we assume Carson Beck will also be mentioned ahead of Week 9. Full Mike LaFleur press conference coverage to come, naturally.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 27-of-48 passes for 272 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals’ 30-16, Week 7 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Brissett struggled to get the deep ball going in this game and was largely stuck dinking and dunking his way down the field. He averaged a measly 5.7 yards per attempt while completing 56.3 percent of his passes. Brissett hasn’t averaged seven yards per attempt in a game since Week 1. Even worse is the fact that he’s taking bone-crushing hits more than ever. Brissett injured his non-throwing hand while taking a sack late in the second quarter but never missed any time with the issue. We expect him to make an appearance on the injury report this week. Head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters after the game that Brissett remains the starter, meaning he’ll take on a terrible Dallas defense next week. He will be a priority streamer for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 24-of-35 passes for 218 yards and one touchdown in the Cardinals’ 18-16, Week 6 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Brissett threw an interception to Rams S Quentin Lake while targeting Trey McBride on the Cardinals’ third play from scrimmage but managed to play mistake-free and touchdown-free football from there on out. Brissett took zero sacks for the first time this season and linked up with four different players for explosive gains. That said, the box score results obviously disappoint. Brissett nearly linked up with Michael Wilson for a 36-yard touchdown on the Cardinals’ seventh drive, but the ball glanced off Wilson’s fingertips as he dove for it in the end zone. The drive ultimately resulted in a field goal, as did five others. Brissett will be a high-end QB2 against the Broncos in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: ArizonaCardinals.com’s Darren Urban believes Carson Beck won’t start in the “immediate future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Cardinals fans appear to be pining for the team to bench Jacoby Brissett and start the rookie in the coming weeks as another season circles the drain for Arizona. Beck so far has been the Cards’ emergency third quarterback. Urban said there remains a “chance Beck is made the backup this week or next and allow him to come on in relief if the situation presents itself. I don’t see Beck starting in the immediate future, but it does feel his time grows closer, and if the offense continues to sputter, that would be understandable.” Brissett this season ranks 15th in passing yards. He’s thrown nine touchdowns to five interceptions and ranks 30th out of 37 qualifying QBs in adjusted yards per attempt. He won’t be a viable fantasy play this week against a tough Rams coverage unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 29-of-47 passes for 292 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in the Cardinals’ 21-45, Week 5 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Brissett also rushed twice for 19 yards and nearly scored on a trick play via a seven-yard reception. He was stopped at the Lions’ two-yard line. Brissett guided the Cardinals to a 14-play scoring drive on their first possession, which he capped off with a two-yard touchdown strike to backup TE Teagan Quitoriano. The bottom dropped out after that. The Cardinals racked up five straight drives ending a punt, with Brissett only managing to break the dreary streak by throwing an interception. Brissett managed to salvage his box score with another Quitoriano score, and a juggling touchdown catch secured by Trey McBride. Brissett also coaxed a few big plays out of fellow backup TE Elijah Higgins. Apparently, the veteran quarterback is ready to target more towering pass catchers with Marvin Harrison Jr. now a Texan. Brissett is a borderline QB1/2 with a shaky floor in Week 6 against the Rams. Coach Mike LaFleur said post-game that he is not considering a quarterback change.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 21-of-35 passes for 166 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions in the Cardinals’ 36-24, Week 4 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Brissett added four carries for 18 yards. Entering the proceedings with just one pick through three starts, Brissett tossed two in the first half before “adding” a walk-off pick-six on the game’s final play. Trailing 30-24, the Cardinals had a 4th-and-goal from the Giants’ four-yard line. Then a pressured Brissett threw it right to Deonte Banks after Michael Wilson cut off his route in the end zone. It was a brutal end to a brutal game, one where Brissett took a pair of sacks in addition to his giveaways. He did find the beleaguered Marvin Harrison Jr. for a 12-yard score against man-to-man coverage on the game’s opening drive, but that opening drive score went down as MHJ’s only reception. The duo did draw a late DPI to set up their ill-faded goal-line series. Averaging a miserable 4.7 yards per attempt on 115 throws over his past three starts, Brissett could get the Carson Beck chatter going in the desert sooner rather than later. That being said, the Lions are a plus Week 5 matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 38-of-52 passes for 280 yards and two touchdowns in the Cardinals’ 36-30, Week 3 loss to the 49ers, adding four carries for four yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Brissett and the Cardinals offense had difficulty navigating penalties and finishing drives in the first half, playing catch-up for much of the second half. The offense wore down the 49ers’ banged-up defensive line over time, with Brissett tossing a pair of touchdowns and sneaking in another from the one-yard line to bring the Cardinals close in the fourth quarter. Though he couldn’t complete the comeback, Brissett’s fantasy production with 52 passing attempts is a good sign for Cardinals pass-catchers moving forward. However, they won’t be in as much of a pass-happy game script against the Giants in Week 4; Brissett is a fantasy QB2 for next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Garrett Wilson (concussion) will not play in Week 9 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson has not practiced this week and has now been ruled out for Sunday’s game against the Chiefs. Wilson has caught 43 passes for 527 yards and three touchdowns this season and saw 12 targets in last week’s loss to the Raiders. His absence means both Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper should see expanded roles, but both players will be hard to trust as anything more than WR3s against a stout Chiefs defense. In addition to Wilson, the Jets also ruled out LB Trevin Wallace (groin) for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson (concussion) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson did not practice on Wednesday and will go down as a DNP today as well. He is a long-shot to suit up for the Jets’ Week 9 game against the Chiefs. His absence will free up targets for Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. The two have alternated spike weeks and zeroes over their past two games. Now both should have stable fantasy floors for at least one game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Jets placed Garrett Wilson in the NFL’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: He was officially a DNP for Wednesday’s practice. Wilson sustained a head injury in Week 8 against the Raiders and now appears to be a long shot for Week 9. Wilson this season has accounted for 27 percent of the Jets’ targets and 38 percent of the team’s air yards. His absence would make both Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper flex-viable for Week 9, along with Mason Taylor. Cooper is coming off a game in which he saw no targets while running a route on 75 percent of the Jets’ drop backs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 6-of-12 targets for 83 yards in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Fresh off a three-target fiasco that prompted trade request denials from the Jets’ No. 1 wideout, Wilson was jammed the ball early and often. It was a clear, intentional commitment from Geno Smith and the Jets’ coaching staff. It still couldn’t prevent Wilson from once again getting out-shined by one of his positional mates, this time Adonai Mitchell. AD contributed an explosive 7/142/1 on nine looks. That’s now three 100-yard performances by Jets wideouts over the past three weeks with zero of them coming from Wilson. He still commands the most defensive attention, making life easier for Mitchell and rookie Omar Cooper Jr. Despite those frustrations and Wilson’s relative struggles, he will remain a must start for Week 9 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports WR Garrett Wilson won’t be traded.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson told reporters this week that he hasn’t requested a trade. Now Schefter reports, citing a “well-placed” source, that there’s “no way” the Jets will trade the 26-year-old wide receiver before the trade deadline. Wilson was held to two catches and 26 yards in Week 7, but remains in the WR2 mix heading into Week 8’s matchup against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson told reporters he has not requested a trade.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson said he loves it in New York. He then immediately added, “Do I love it more than I love winning? Nah, to be completely honest, but I’m hopeful.” It’s hard to blame Wilson. The Jets are 24-51 since drafting Wilson and he has routinely caught passes from some of the league’s worst quarterbacks. The offense has been better under Geno Smith this year, but the team is still struggling to win games. Wilson could likely force his way out of New York if he wanted to, but it sounds like he’s content to go down with the ship again this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 2-of-3 targets for 26 yards in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: The Dolphins shut down Wilson, opting to let Omar Cooper Jr. and Mason Taylor beat them through the air. The duo combined for 177 yards and three touchdowns while Wilson was stuck with decoy duties. Wilson was spotted screaming at Geno Smith in the fourth quarter after Smith took a back-breaking sack on third down at the goal line. Wilson downplayed the altercation after the game, saying he was “collaborating” and then noting that he wasn’t even talking to Geno. He was. With several young players taking on larger roles in the Jets’ offense, Wilson’s role as the team’s unquestioned WR1 on the team has taken a hit. Still, he should at least stay in the fantasy WR2 mix for his Week 8 date with the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 4-of-6 targets for 44 yards in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson’s second quietest effort of the season came as he dealt with Christian Gonzalez’s stingy coverage and first-round rookie teammate Omar Cooper Jr. returning from his ankle injury. With Adonai Mitchell (finger) likely — hopefully — soon returning from his marathon absence, Wilson is set to have a lot more target competition in the Jets’ receiver corps, but those extra bodies should also create more space for the Jets’ No. 1. Wilson remains a high-end WR2 heading into next week’s plus matchup with the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 7-of-11 targets for 104 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 5 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: The 100-yard effort was Wilson’s second in three weeks. It was no easy feat on a rainy afternoon in Jersey where Geno Smith completed only 17 passes. Wilson’s score was a 32-yarder where he spun out of a tackle for a catch-and-run house call. In addition to the 100-yard efforts, Wilson now has a score in three of his past four appearances. It’s like Wilson’s lost 2025 never happened, which is exactly what the Jets and fantasy managers were hoping for. A weekly fixture in the low-end WR1 ranks, Wilson has a Week 6 date with the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 3-of-4 targets for 27 yards in the Jets’ Week 4 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: No one on the Jets offense got home for fantasy purposes as the Bears held on to the ball for several long drives in the second half. The Jets possessed the ball for just 17 minutes on the day. Wilson’s four targets led the New York offense, as Geno Smith was limited to a mere 15 pass attempts. Wilson continues to dominate air yards and targets in the Jets offense and should remain in all lineups next week against Cleveland.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: James Pearce is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: Pearce’s status is not injury-related. This likely has more to do with whether or not head coach Kevin Stefanski believes Pearce is in enough shape to play a game after being sidelined for eight weeks due to his suspension. Pearce was a full participant in practice, and teams said he will operate on a pitch count, so it seems highly unlikely he will be scratched on game day. In addition to Pearce, the Falcons also listed LB Yasir Abdullah (hamstring), WR Beaux Collins (hip), LB Divine Deablo (forearm), and OT Cameron Williams (ankle) as questionable for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: Falcons DE James Pearce returned from his eight-game suspension and is eligible to play in Week 9 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: Pearce is eligible to play in Week 9 against the Bengals and will likely join the team when it flies to Madrid for the international matchup. Pearce’s return should provide a nice spark to the 17th-ranked Falcons’ defense after the 2025 first-rounder racked up 10.5 sacks and 10 TFLs as a rookie while totaling 26 tackles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said James Pearce Jr. (suspension) will be added back to the Falcons 53-man roster next week when eligible.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: “He’s done everything that we have asked, everything that he has been allowed to do, he’s done a great job,” Stefanski said while saying that Pearce would play in Madrid against the Bengals. Pearce was suspended after violating the league’s personal conduct policy for three felonies and one misdemeanor for his role in a car chase with ex-girlfriend, WNBA player Rickea Jackson. Pearce’s felony charges were aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police and resisting an officer with violence to his or her person.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: ESPN’s Marc Raimondi reports that the NFL suspended Falcons EDGE James Pearce for the first eight regular season games.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: The NFL determined that Pearce violated the league’s Personal Conduct Policy. He will be suspended without pay, but is allowed to participate in all preseason activities, including games. The suspension begins on August 30th, and he will be eligible for reinstatement on November 2nd. The Falcons go on bye in Week 11, so Week 9 marks his earliest possible return to the field. Pearce was arrested in February and initially charged with three felonies and one misdemeanor, including aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police, and resisting an officer with violence to his or her person.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: The Athletic’s Josh Kendall believes the NFL is “likely” to suspend Falcons EDGE James Pearce Jr.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: Atlanta “appears to be waiting” on the league to decide how they want to punish Pearce. Cameron Sutton was suspended eight games in 2024 for a similar incident, which Kendall mentions and certainly could serve as a blueprint for how this plays out. Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said they have not received any communication from the league on this subject. It certainly would be surprising if Pearce weren’t eventually suspended to some extent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: Fox5 Atlanta’s Justin Felder reports James Pearce will be in attendance for Falcons minicamp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: Pearce is in the middle of an ongoing legal situation stemming from a February arrest that resulted in him being charged with three felonies and one misdemeanor. The 22-year-old pass-rusher recently entered a pre-trial intervention program that can result in all charges being dismissed if he meets the conditions of the program, and the league is reportedly “closely monitoring all developments” with Pearce. We don’t yet know if the league plans to hand down a suspension to Pearce, but it wouldn’t be surprising if some disciplinary action was taken after everything is resolved in his case.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the NFL is “closely monitoring all developments” in Falcons EDGE James Pearce Jr.'s legal situation.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: From Rapoport, “Earlier today, Pearce entered into a six-month pre-trial intervention program that, if conditions are met, will result in all charges being dismissed.” Pearce was initially charged with a misdemeanor and three felonies: aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police, and resisting an officer with violence to his or her person. This deal would allow him to walk away with no jail time and no admission of guilt. The NFL could still suspend him at some point, but it does look like he has avoided career-altering legal trouble.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Falcons DE James Pearce is not expected to attend the team’s voluntary offseason workout program.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: This does not come as a surprise, as Pearce is currently facing charges for three felonies, including aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, stemming from a February arrest in which he reportedly used his vehicle to collide with another vehicle during a domestic incident with WNBA player Rickea Jackson. The team has remained non-committal about when Pearce could return, but it’s possible they will opt to keep him away from the facilities until this matter is resolved.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski and GM Ian Cunningham were non-committal on EDGE James Pearce Jr. reporting to the first day of the spring program on April 7.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: Pearce was charged with three felonies and one misdemeanor for his role in a car chase with ex-girlfriend, WNBA player Rickea Jackson. Pearce’s felony charges were aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police and resisting an officer with violence to his or her person. Stefanski said “we’re working through it” and Cunningham said it was an “ongoing legal matter” while adding he’s “not gonna touch on that right now.” Pearce’s status with the team continues to be up in the air.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.headline: ESPN’s Marc Raimondi reports that Falcons EDGE James Pearce is being charged with 3 felonies and one misdemeanor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-pear.analysis: Pearce’s felony charges include “aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police and resisting an officer with violence to his or her person.” His fourth arrest charge of felony aggravated stalking was changed to a misdemeanor. Per Raimondi, “Pearce allegedly followed the car of [WNBA player Rickea] Jackson, his ex-girlfriend, and repeatedly used his vehicle to collide with hers as she attempted to reach the Doral (Florida) police station.” A police chase allegedly ensued. After crashing his vehicle, Pearce fled on foot but was eventually caught and arrested. Pearce’s 2026 availability appears to be up in the air.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.headline: Brian Robinson (hamstring) is questionable for the Falcons’ Week 9 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.analysis: Robinson was briefly listed as questionable only for head coach Kevin Stefanski to rule him out shortly after the initial report. Robinson was limited in practice throughout the week, but the Falcons are opting to play it safe, likely hoping another week on the sidelines will lower the chances of re-injury. Rookie WR Zachariah Branch (hamstring) has also been ruled out for the game after picking up an injury in last week’s loss to the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.headline: Brian Robinson (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.analysis: Robinson should be good to go for Week 9, though we won’t get official word on his status until tomorrow. He’ll reclaim the RB2 role in Atlanta once he gets cleared for action. Robinson will be a touchdown-or-bust RB4 if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.headline: Brian Robinson (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.analysis: Robinson has missed the past two weeks with the hamstring issue. A limited session today puts him on track to return to the lineup against the Bengals on Sunday. Robinson had at least seven carries in every game before going down in Week 6. He will be in the RB4 mix if he gets the green light for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.headline: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) will not play in Week 8 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.analysis: Robinson will miss a second straight game with his hamstring injury, which positions Khalil Herbert to again serve as the backup to Bijan Robinson. Herbert rushed two times for nine yards in last week’s win over the 49ers while adding one reception for 19 additional yards. He will not be on the streaming radar this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.headline: Brian Robinson (hamstring) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.analysis: He hasn’t practiced since before Week 6 and looks likely to be ruled out again on Friday. Khalil Herbert ran in Robinson’s place as the backup last week and would handle those duties again against Tampa on Sunday if Robinson is ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.headline: Brian Robinson (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.analysis: Bijan Robinson handled 20 carries and five targets with his backup, Brian Robinson, sidelined in Week 7. The backup should be considered questionable to play at this time, though he could make a late-week return. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.headline: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) won’t play in Atlanta’s Week 7 game against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.analysis: Bijan should get a larger-than-usual workload this week against San Francisco. The Falcons only have two running backs on the 53-man roster so it may be Khalil Herbert or Jam Miller filling in as (Bijan) Robinson’s backup on Sunday. Herbert seems like the logical choice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.headline: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.analysis: The Falcons’ No. 2 running back was limited yesterday. This series of events suggests Robinson strained his hamstring on Wednesday, putting him on the wrong side of questionable for the Falcons’ Week 6 game against the 49ers. Bijan Robinson would handle a few extra touches in Robinson’s absence. The team does not have a third running back on the active roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.headline: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.analysis: Robinson is the immediate backup to Bijan Robinson in the Falcons’ backfield, seeing his best usage in run-heavy game scripts. He was limited with a hamstring injury on Wednesday but is still trending to play Week 7 against the 49ers, barring setbacks. Also limited was Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). Both players are depth options at best behind the Falcons’ star-studded skill players.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.headline: Brian Robinson, Jr. had two rushes for one yard in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears, adding two catches for nine yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-robi.analysis: With the Falcons down by three touchdowns and abandoning the run game in the second half, Robinson had little chance of paying off as a Week 6 flex in the usually run-first Atlanta offense. Chicago snuffed out the Falcons run game and forced Michael Penix to try to beat them through the air. Robinson will be a game-script sensitive RB3 option in Week 7 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught both targets for 19 yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews, somewhat disgustingly, led the team in receiving with a modest 19 yards on a night undrafted free agent rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano threw for only 60 yards in his first career start. It remains difficult to start the veteran tight end, who has made more mental mistakes this season than he has receptions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews (hand) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews has been playing through the hand injury for a few weeks without any issues. He logged three full practices this week. With Joe Fagnano making his first career start for the Ravens tomorrow, we wouldn’t advise playing any Ravens outside of Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews (hand) was listed as a full participant on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: That keeps the veteran tight end on track to suit up in Week 9 against the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football. Andrews has struggled to return usable fantasy weeks throughout his age-31 season, with the team now down to their third, potentially fourth, quarterback for Thursday’s game. he can safely be left on fantasy benches on the short week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 3-of-4 targets for 14 yards in the Ravens’ Week 8 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: It was another day at the office for Andrews, who has now gone six straight games with 28 or fewer receiving yards. Any hope that he might see a slight increase in production with Lamar Jackson back under center can be put aside after Jackson suffered a severe injury to his throwing hand that will require surgery and force him to go on injured reserve. Andrews isn’t on the fantasy radar heading into Week 9 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 3-of-4 targets for 23 yards in the Ravens’ Week 7 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: It was business as usual for Andrews, who can be consistently relied on for a solid 20-yard game. Andrews has gone for 28 or fewer yards in five straight games and will not be on the fantasy radar in Week 8 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 1-of-3 targets for four yards in the Ravens’ Week 6 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews ran 11 more routes than rookie tight end Josh Cuevas but was out-targeted by Cuevas 5-to-3. Andrews continues to underwhelm in the passing game and has now failed to surpass 28 yards in four straight games. He can be left on waivers ahead of Week 7’s game against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 4-of-6 targets for 28 yards in the Ravens’ Week 5 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews dropped a would-be touchdown on the team’s opening possession on a ball that went through his hands in the end zone. He would then fumble on the following possession, which Jessie Bates returned for a touchdown to force the Ravens into catch-up mode for the remainder of the game. Luckily for him, late heroics from Tyler Huntley and Derrick Henry had the team escaping with a victory. Andrews has not looked great to start the 2026 season, having not eclipsed 50 yards through five games. He’ll remain a shaky fantasy start in Week 6 when the Ravens host the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews (hand) is practicing in full for Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews practiced in full with the hand injury last week before posting a 5/27/1 receiving line. He should be good to go again this week, though he is a low-end TE1, with backup QB Tyler Huntley likely starting in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 5-of-6 targets for 27 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 4 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews continues to see most of his work come in the short area of the field. He’s gone for less than 30 yards in each of his last two games, but did manage to haul in a three-yard score in the second quarter of Sunday’s win for his first touchdown of 2026. Lamar Jackson also missed Andrews in the end zone on a high throw earlier in the game, but he remains a very touchdown-dependent option as far as fantasy is concerned. He’s a boom-or-bust play in Week 5 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews (hand) is practicing in full for Week 4 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: The Ravens seemingly forgot about Andrews when they first posted their injury report, only noting his injury and status in a post 40 minutes after the initial run. In their defense, Andrews has been pretty forgettable this year, catching 13 passes for 122 scoreless yards. The hand injury shouldn’t be an issue this week, but he’s still stuck in the TE2 ranks versus Tennessee.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers caught 3-of-6 targets for six yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars, adding 17 yards on three carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle did what he could to overcome undrafted free agent rookie Joe Fagnano under center, routinely putting Flowers in Motion across the formation to generate some level of misdirection for an offense with zero ability to attack downfield. That included three rush attempts and a completion thrown by running back Derrick Henry, but it wasn’t enough to salvage a usable fantasy week for the electric receiver. Fantasy managers can rest easy knowing help is on the way in the form of veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who was signed earlier in the week and will likely make his team debut when the Ravens take on the Chargers in Week 10. Flowers will return to upside WR2 range with the change at quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers caught 0-of-5 targets in the Ravens’ Week 8 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Lamar Jackson exited after one play due to a thumb injury. Midway through the second quarter, backup Tyler Huntley left the game with a toe injury, forcing Flowers into a nightmare situation with rookie UDFA Joe Fagnano under center. Flowers saw four of his five targets come from Fagnano but was unable to convert any of them into catches, even if they were within his range to do so. With the Ravens now set to face the Jaguars on a short week, and Fagnano possibly set to make his first career start, Flowers needs to be adjusted down to WR3 rankings. With a full week to install a game plan with Fagnano, it’s fair to assume he’ll offer more than the donut we saw here today, but the Ravens’ offense, which was already struggling with Huntley under center, is unlikely to fare any better with Fagnano.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers caught 8-of-11 targets for 137 yards and one touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 7 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers’ biggest play of the day came on the Ravens’ opening drive. The star receiver turned a screen pass on third-and-nine upfield for a 48-yard touchdown to give the Ravens an early lead on what would be their only touchdown drive of the day. Despite another low-scoring day for the Ravens’ offense, Flowers continues to be one of the most profitable wide receivers in fantasy. He’s averaged over 10 targets per game in three starts by Tyler Huntley and has caught six or more passes in his last four games. With Lamar Jackson (ankle) expected back for Week 8’s game against the Bills, things are looking up for Flowers and the Ravens’ offense as a whole. The good news for Flowers’ managers, however, is that he’s a must-start regardless of who is under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers caught 6-of-11 targets for 66 yards in the Ravens’ Week 6 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers has yet to find the end zone in back-to-back games with Tyler Huntley under center, but the 10 targets per game he has averaged over that span is still encouraging. Flowers led the Ravens in targets by a wide margin in this week’s loss, with his biggest play coming on a 31-yard reception in the third quarter. Scoring opportunities were scarce in this one, as the Ravens managed just 10 points on their first two drives and were shut out for the rest of the game. Flowers will be in the WR1 conversation next week against the Bengals if Lamar Jackson (ankle) makes the start, but would be more of a WR2 if Huntley gets the nod for a third straight week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers (toe) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Perhaps feeling a bit wistful after spending a little of every week of the season on the injury report, Flowers got re-added Thursday with a limited session. He was limited again on Friday but is expected to play. There’s no further word on how serious this toe injury was, but he’s doing enough on the field in his limited time so far this year that nobody is seriously benching Flowers anyway.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers (toe) was added to the injury report on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers played through a foot injury last week, catching 8-of-9 targets for 53 yards and rushing once for 13 yards. This injury could be related, but we really don’t know. Flowers’ productivity took a hit with Tyler Huntley running the offense last week. Huntley is currently in line to start again, though Lamar Jackson’s (ankle) status is still up in the air. If the toe injury limits Flowers, that further complicates things, but he still must be started if active. Hopefully, he practices tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers caught 8-of-9 targets for 53 yards in the Ravens’ Week 5 win over the Falcons, adding 13 yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers was largely confined to short area work with Tyler Huntley under center and also saw a 26-yard reception erased from his ledger due to a 29-yard pass interference penalty on the play. It was a weird situation in which the penalty yardage was greater than his reception. Fantasy managers might be forced to continue waiting on the return of Lamar Jackson after it was reported this week that the All Pro starter could be forced to miss another week. Flowers is a locked-in WR2 against the Browns in Week 6 with Huntley under center and an elite WR1 should Jackson return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Ravens declared QB Lamar Jackson, OLB Trey Hendrickson, C Cam Jurgens, G Andrew Vorhees, WR Elijah Sarratt, and DT Aeneas Peebles inactive for Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Jackson had already been ruled out earlier in the week and reportedly could be looking at a multi-game absence due to an ankle injury suffered before halftime in Week 4. Tyler Huntley will start under center for the Ravens as they look to subdue the momentum of the Falcons, who have won both games started by Michael Penix. Wide receiver Zay Flowers is officially active for Sunday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Zay Flowers (foot) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers was limited in practice throughout the week but never appeared at risk of missing Sunday night’s game. The bigger issue for him will be the absence of Lamar Jackson. Flowers has been the most efficient receiver in the league on a per-route basis this year. That will come back to Earth sans Jackson, but he remains on the WR1/2 border, even with Tyler Huntley under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.headline: Zay Flowers (foot) is questionable for Baltimore’s Week 5 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zay-flower.analysis: Flowers got in three limited sessions while dealing with the foot injury. He loses ceiling with Tyler Huntley under center, but remains a rock solid low-end WR1 in terms of how much volume he amasses in this passing attack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 17 times for 57 yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle did everything in his power to overcome an undrafted free agent rookie quarterback in his first professional start, going so far as numerous direct snaps to Henry and a Henry pass attempt, but it ultimately proved futile. Things appeared to be trending in the right direction as the Ravens played the Jaguars to a tightly contested game through the first 29 minutes before Parker Washington broke the game open with a 50-yard touchdown in the final minute before the break. Things got nasty for Henry after the half as he managed only two additional yards after bruising his way to 55 first half yards. Henry will return to RB1 status in fantasy circles in Week 10 when the Ravens take on the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 11 times for 53 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 8 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Playing more than half of the game with emergency QB Joe Fagnano under center didn’t do much to help Henry or the Ravens’ offense. Fortunately, after being gifted a short field in the first quarter following an interception by Josh Allen, Henry was able to convert the opportunity into a two-yard rushing touchdown two plays later. It was Henry’s first rushing touchdown since Week 4, but he’s shaping up to be little more than a volume-based RB2 in Week 9 against the Jaguars if Fagnano is forced to start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 17 times for 45 yards in the Ravens’ Week 7 loss to the Bengals, adding one reception for four additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Henry has rushed 34 times for 93 scoreless yards in his last two games, and has seen 10 of those carries go for zero yards or a loss. Injuries to the Ravens’ offensive line continue to plague the running game, and the loss of rookie RG Vega Ioane (knee) in the first quarter didn’t do anything to help the Ravens’ rushing woes. Henry has just one touchdown in the three starts by Tyler Huntley and has just six carries inside his opponents’ 10-yard line over that span. Baltimore’s sluggish offense under Huntley hasn’t boded well for Henry’s fantasy upside, but with Lamar Jackson (ankle) expected back for Week 8’s game against the Bills, Henry should be in line for more scoring opportunities. He will be a fringe RB1 next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 17 times for 58 scoreless yards in the Ravens’ Week 6 loss to the Browns, adding one reception for two additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Henry continues to struggle on the ground, as this marks the third time in four games that he has been held under 4.0 YPC. In fairness to the Big Dog, he averaged less than one yard before contact per attempt in this one, and six of his 17 rush attempts went for no gain or a loss of yards. Henry totaled 28 rushing yards on his first two carries on a drive that eventually ended with a Ravens touchdown, but yards were hard to come by the rest of the way. He’s now gone two-straight weeks without a rushing touchdown, but will hopefully be in better position to score next week against the Bengals if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is back under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 24 times for 102 yards in the Ravens’ Week 5 win over the Falcons, adding 18 yards and a touchdown on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Henry also tacked on a successful two-point conversion to further pad his counting stats. The King erupted for 59 yards in the first half before being largely held in check for the final two quarters with the Ravens playing from behind. He would watch from the sidelines for the duration of the team’s final possession in the two-minute drill but came on the field to tie the game with a two-point conversion on a direct snap. The Falcons were no match for Henry in the extra frame, with the bruising back tacking on an additional 32 yards on the ground on the team’s lone overtime possession. Henry continues to turn back the clock while notching his eighth touchdown in five appearances, having scored in every game to start the season. He remains an elite RB1 ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 23 times for 73 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 4 win over the Titans, adding two receptions for six additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: This week marks the second straight game in which Henry averaged less than 4.0 YPC. Fortunately for fantasy managers, he did manage to find the end zone on a five-yard score on the Ravens’ first drive and was relied on heavily in the second half when Lamar Jackson exited the game with an ankle injury. This wasn’t a flashy game for Henry, who was held to three or fewer yards on 16 of his 23 rush attempts. That said, he continues to be the only Ravens RB of note and remains in the RB1 mix for next week’s game against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 26 times for 89 yards and two touchdowns in the Ravens’ Week 3 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Fantasy managers won’t balk at the production Henry provided their lineups in Sunday’s win over the Cowboys, but the Big Dog was largely bottled up against a suddenly stingy defensive front. Henry’s longest run came on a 29-yard burst in the third quarter that helped set up a Chris Moore receiving touchdown, but that run also accounted for 32.6 percent of Henry’s yards on the ground. He averaged a very underwhelming 2.4 YPC on his other 25 carries on the day and was tackled for a three-yard loss on a fourth-and-goal from the Cowboys’ one-yard line. The good news is Henry remains the unquestioned bell cow in the Ravens’ backfield, and he has a Week 4 revenge game against the Titans on tap. He’ll be a must start RB1 in what should be a plus matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 16 times for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 2 loss to the Saints, adding three receptions for 19 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Henry didn’t provide his signature explosive plays in this one, with his longest carry of the afternoon coming on an eight-yard run. On the Ravens’ second drive of the game, Henry turned seven touches into 45 yards from scrimmage, thanks in part to a screen pass he took for 19 yards, and capped the drive with a one-yard score to give the Ravens an early 7-0 lead. He averaged a respectable 4.3 YPC on the day, but the Saints were able to hold Henry in check for much of the afternoon. That said, fantasy managers won’t be mad at the production. He gets a plus matchup next week on the road against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Derrick Henry rushed 24 times for 144 yards and three touchdowns in the Ravens’ Week 1 win over the Colts, adding one reception for 19 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: Age continues to be just a number for Henry. The 32-year-old bell cow handled 24 of the backfield’s 30 carries on Sunday, averaging an impressive 6.0 YPC while ripping off four gains of 10-plus yards. Henry did his part to keep the Ravens on schedule all afternoon, and wound up finding the end zone three times on Sunday. His first score, which came on a four-yard plunge in the first quarter, was followed by a 32-yard score in the second quarter, in which Henry shook off two tackles on his way into the end zone. He would add a third score early in the fourth quarter for good measure while pushing the Ravens’ lead to 38-16. It’s only one game, but Henry doesn’t look like he’s lost a step heading into his 11th season. He’ll be on the RB1 radar in Week 2 in a plus matchup against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.headline: Ravens RB Derrick Henry said he “would like to finish [his] playing career with [the] Ravens.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derrick-he.analysis: In an appearance for the Up & Adams show, Henry said, “when I hang it up, Baltimore is the last place I want to be.” The 32-year-old later followed up on social media by saying he “would like” to finish his career with the Ravens, but clarifying he “never said anything about retiring.” Henry is still producing at a high level and is not headed for retirement just yet. However, when he does consider retirement, he hopes to close out his career with the Ravens. Henry has produced 3,516 rushing yards and 32 rushing touchdowns in two seasons with the Ravens and is currently under contract through 2027.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.headline: Justice Hill rushed nine times for 85 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars, adding seven yards on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.analysis: Hill became the first running back to amass more than 75 yards against the Jaguars since the start of the 2025 regular season with a 65-yard touchdown with the game well out of hand in the second half. It was an otherwise poor showing for the entirety of the Baltimore offense with a rookie undrafted free agent starting his first NFL game. Hill remains nothing more than desperation FLEX ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.headline: Justice Hill (groin) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.analysis: Hill saw eight targets in a blowout loss last week. Third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano peppered him with check-downs, though Hill only managed four catches. With Fagnano making his first career start tomorrow, Hill should continue to rack up targets in Week 9. He’s in the RB4 mix in PPR leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.headline: Justice Hill (groin) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.analysis: The fact he was listed as limited and not a “DNP” likely signals a more modest injury and we would expect Hill to suit up when the Ravens take on the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football in Week 9. Either way, fantasy managers likely have better options at the position.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.headline: Justice Hill rushed three times for 15 yards in the Ravens’ Week 8 loss to the Bills, adding four receptions for 20 yards on eight targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.analysis: Hill nearly turned into a surprise PPR scam this week with rookie UDFA Joe Fagnano under center for two-and-a-half quarters of play. Hill’s eight targets led all Ravens players, but his 20 receiving yards were largely buoyed by back-to-back receptions during a two-minute drill when the Ravens were facing second and third and longs. Despite the high-volume day, it’s hard to rely on anybody in this offense, which could have dark days ahead with Lamar Jackson (thumb) out for the foreseeable future and Tyler Huntley also dealing with a toe injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.headline: Ravens placed Adam Randall on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.analysis: Cornerback Bilhal Kone was also placed on IR. Both players can return after four games. Randall was likely parked behind Justice Hill as the Ravens’ RB3 heading into the season. That role now belongs to Rasheen Ali, at least until Randall is back in action. He played in the team’s final preseason game and the team has not said what this injury is yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.headline: The Athletic’s Jeff Zrebiec believes the Ravens see Justice Hill “as a good complement to Derrick Henry and really value his ability out of the backfield and in blitz pickup.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.analysis: Hill ended 2025 on injured reserve because of a neck issue.
