He was reportedly a cut candidate during the offseason and the team selected Clemson running back Adam Randall on Day Three of the draft. It seemed possible that the team planned on replacing Hill this year, but Zrebiec shot that idea down, at least for the start of the season. Zrebiec answered, “I can’t see that happening from the jump,” in reference to a question about Randall opening the season as Baltimore’s backup running back. Hill caught 21 passes for 169 yards and a touchdown in 10 games last year. He also punched in a pair of touchdowns on the ground despite running just 18 times. His ceiling is extremely limited, even in the event of a Henry injury, but Hill should have some standalone RB4 value in PPR leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.headline: The Athletic’s Jeff Zrebiec reports Justice Hill has “been mentioned as a potential salary-cap cut.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.analysis: Hill has a $3.8 million cap figure, of which the Ravens can save $3.1 million with a release. He missed the final six weeks of the season with a long-term neck injury, and turns 29 next November. Zrebiec brought up this idea in mentioning that the Ravens could chase a running back in the lower rounds of the draft to add to the room behind Derrick Henry.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.headline: Ravens coach John Harbaugh said Justice Hill (neck) could return in “3-4 weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.analysis: Rasheen Ali will continue as the Ravens third-down back in the meantime, per Harbaugh. Keaton Mitchell is probably a better second Ravens back to roster at this point for most fantasy leagues than Ali. Hill can be dropped in all shallow formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.headline: Justice Hill (neck) will not play in Week 13 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.analysis: Hill was a mid-week addition to the injury report, going from a normal practice on Monday to a DNP because of the neck issue on Tuesday. He previously missed time with a toe injury. Keaton Mitchell will continue to operate as the change-of-pace back this week. Mitchell is worth a look in large-field DFS contests for the Thanksgiving slate, but redraft managers can leave him on the waiver wire for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.headline: Ravens RB Justice Hill (neck) did not participate in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justice-hi.analysis: Hill pops up on the injury report with a neck issue. It is presumably new, given he was not on the injury report Monday. A new neck injury is cause for concern in terms of game status and Hill is in jeopardy of missing the Ravens’ Thanksgiving game against the Bengals. If he does miss, Keaton Mitchell will get a bump in pass-catching duties.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-fagnan.headline: Joe Fagnano completed 10-of-18 passes for 60 yards and two interceptions in the Ravens’ 33-10, Week 9 loss to the Jaguars, adding 13 yards on three carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-fagnan.analysis: Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle did everything he could to scheme around a starting undrafted free agent rookie quarterback in his first NFL start, calling numerous exotic looks to include direct snaps to Derrick Henry, a Henry pass attempt, quick outs to Zay Flowers, Flowers rush attempts, and flea flickers, but it wasn’t enough to overcome poor execution, consistently off-target throws, and a lack of downfield ability. The Ravens also committed numerous pre-snap penalties as they continue to lead the league in that area through nine weeks, which killed multiple drives. Fagnano managed only 25 pass yards in the first half, finishing with a ridiculous 60 yards, while both interceptions came in the second half with the team in desperation mode. Fagnano leaves his first, and likely last, NFL start with a sour taste in his mouth, as he likely retreats to backup duties following the signing of veteran Jacoby Brissett earlier in the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-fagnan.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Joe Fagnano will start in Week 9 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-fagnan.analysis: The 25-year-old rookie UDFA will make the starting lineup on Thursday night against the Jaguars’ top-flight defense under the lights. Fagnano predictably struggled in the two-and-a-half quarters he played against the Bills last week, throwing for just 91 yards on 10-of-21 passes while also throwing a pick and taking three sacks. While it’s possible a short week of prep as the team’s QB1 could yield marginally better results, this projects to be a tough matchup for Fagnano and the rest of the Ravens’ offensive players. Fagnano will not be on the fantasy radar this week, and Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers will both be docked a few spots in fantasy rankings due to the downgrade at QB.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-fagnan.headline: Joe Fagnano was seen wearing an ankle guard/brace during Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-fagnan.analysis: Head coach Jesse Minter said on Monday that Fagnano was “dealing with some things physically,” but the rookie UDFA is still expected to make his first career start on Thursday against the Jaguars. Fagnano was wearing the guard/brace on his right ankle, but was on the field practicing with the team. The Ravens recently signed Austin Reed and Kedon Slovis to the practice squad, with Reed looking like the most likely backup to Fagnano on Thursday night. Hopefully the Ravens aren’t forced to go to fourth QB in less than a week, but Fagnano clearly isn’t operating at 100 percent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-fagnan.headline: Ravens signed QB Kedon Slovis from the Packers practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-fagnan.analysis: Slovis could, unbelievably, get the start Thursday night against the Jaguars with Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) out, and Joe Fagnano (ankle) iffy to suit up. If Fagnano can play, Slovis would presumably serve as Baltimore’s backup. Fagnano completed 48 percent of his passes for 91 yards and a pick last week against the Bills. Look for the Ravens to be ultra run-heavy against Jacksonville, one of the league’s best run defenses. It will be tough to trust anyone in the Ravens offense as a viable fantasy option for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-fagnan.headline: Jesse Minter said Joe Fagnano (ankle) is “dealing with some things physically” but has a chance to start in Week 9.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-fagnan.analysis: Whelp, that isn’t exactly a ringing endorsement for the rookie quarterback’s chances of starting under center for the Ravens when they host the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football to kick off Week 9. The team lost both Lamar Jackson to a season-ending thumb injury and backup Tyler Huntley to a turf toe injury in their Week 8 loss to the Bills, now in desperate need of a viable quarterback option as they fight for their playoff lives. It is possible the team addresses the position through trade with just over a week until the trade deadline, although that is unlikely to help them on a short week. More to come in what quickly became a dire situation in Baltimore. Fagnano was officially listed as limited on the team’s estimated practice report Monday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-fagnan.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Lamar Jackson is “likely out for the season” after suffering a thumb injury in Week 8’s loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-fagnan.analysis: Head coach Jesse Minter didn’t dismiss the possibility of this being a season-ending injury for Jackson when asked about it after the game, but the optics on the field weren’t good, and the team wasted little time announcing he would undergo surgery and be placed on injured reserve. It wouldn’t be at all surprising to learn in the days ahead that Jackson’s season is over, but the team will likely wait until after he has his surgery to make any formal announcement. With Jackson and Tyler Huntley (toe) both being sidelined, rookie UDFA Joe Fagnano is slated to start on the short week on Thursday against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-fagnan.headline: The Athletic’s Jeff Zrebiec reports that Joe Fagnano (undisclosed) said he thinks he is healthy enough to play in Week 9 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-fagnan.analysis: According to Zrebiec, Fagnano “was hobbled by game’s end, after he took a low and penalized hit” from Bills DL Ed Oliver. Fagnano said he and the team will have to wait and “see” how he is feeling in the coming days, noting that “you’re always going to have bumps and bruises” after a football game. Lamar Jackson (thumb) is already headed to injured reserve and Tyler Huntley will undergo an MRI tomorrow to assess a potential turf toe injury. Zrebiec rightly writes that the Ravens “will almost certainly have to bring in at least one quarterback, if not two,” this week. He lists Anthony Richardson and Tua Tagovailoa as potential trade targets. At this point, it is unclear who will start for the Ravens on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-fagnan.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Tyler Huntley is believed to have suffered a turf toe injury and will undergo an MRI on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-fagnan.analysis: Tomorrow’s MRI should clarify whether Huntley will miss time. In the meantime, Lamar Jackson will be placed on injured reserve with what could be a season-ending thumb injury. This leaves rookie Joe Fagnano as the team’s potential starter for the Ravens’ Week 9 Thursday Night Football game against the Jaguars, though Fagnano reportedly got a little banged up today, too. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-fagnan.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (thumb) will undergo surgery and be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-fagnan.analysis: When asked if this is a potentially season-ending injury for Jackson, Minter’s response was, “We’ll see.” After seeing Jackson’s injury on replay, it was easy to assume the Ravens’ QB1 would be looking at another multi-week absence, but this sounds like the worst-case scenario. If Jackson doesn’t land on season-ending IR, he would be required to miss at least four games before he could even consider a return. Adding insult to injury, the Ravens also lost backup Tyler Huntley in this game to a toe injury, meaning rookie UDFA Joe Fagnano could be in line to start on Thursday night against the Jaguars in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-fagnan.headline: Joe Fagnano completed 10-of-21 passes for 91 yards and an interception in the Ravens’ 36-10, Week 8 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-fagnan.analysis: Injuries to Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) resulted in Fagnano getting on the field with nearly half of the second quarter left to be played. The rookie UDFA performed as expected, completing fewer than 50 percent of his passes while taking three sacks and committing two turnovers. Fagnano looked a little more poised in the second half, with one of his throws resulting in a 22-yard completion to Rashod Bateman, but the Ravens’ QB room is in shambles heading into a short week. With Jackson likely to miss an extended period of time, and Huntley at risk of missing at least one game due to the short week, it’s possible Fagnano will draw the start at home against the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football. It goes without saying that he can’t be trusted in any fantasy format, and he would put a serious cap on the upside of all of the Ravens’ key fantasy assets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught both targets for 22 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Strange was overshadowed by the 52-yard reception from fellow tight end Nate Boerkircher on the team’s opening possession, but he made a really nice grab in triple coverage over the middle of the field to set up the team’s second score of the game. Strange remains unlikely to see consistent volume for as long as the Jaguars continue to so handily control games, something that appears likely to continue given the team holds the weakest strength of schedule for the remainder of the regular season. Fantasy managers likely have better options ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 2-of-2 targets for 55 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 8 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Strange had a 46-yard first quarter catch-and-run that went down as the Jags’ longest gain of the day in a 42-7 demolition of the pathetic Colts. Strange was really rumbling, looking out of gas at the end of his journey. Strange actually tied for the team lead in receiving yards, but that’s because Trevor Lawrence attempted all of 14 passes. Strange has done enough to keep himself in the TE2 mix, but he is not an ideal TE1 streamer heading into a short-week Thursday night date vs. a Ravens team that will be without Lamar Jackson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 5-of-7 targets for 44 yards in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: The Jaguars did have a tight end touchdown, but unfortunately for fantasy managers it went to Nate Boerkircher on a ridiculous one-handed stab on a pop pass at the goal line. Strange has now gone for 23 targets in three games and appears to be crowding out Brian Thomas Jr. He’s a reasonable low-end TE1, albeit one on bye next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 7-of-8 targets for 68 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: After a quiet three games to start the year, Strange has heated up over the past two weeks. He led the team with seven catches last week and did so again today in London. Strange had seven catches in his first three games combined. He can’t be expected to pace the Jags in receiving, but Strange is back on the TE1/2 border for his Week 6 date with Houston.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 7-of-8 targets for 95 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 4 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Strange was Trevor Lawrence’s primary target against a Bengals defense that has struggled against tight ends. Many of his targets were middle-of-the-field intermediate passes as he tallied 95 total receiving yards on the day. The Jaguars offense has a variety of pass-catchers that can find success based on defensive matchup. The game environment aligned perfectly for Strange, who rarely came off the field with 53 total snaps. The Eagles are a tougher matchup for tight ends, but Strange is a good streamer option in the high-end TE2 territory for a Week 5 matchup in London.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 3-of-5 targets for 32 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers dominated looks from Trevor Lawrence on a low-volume day for the Jacksonville offense. Strange played his usual role as a check down option for Lawrence, rumbling for yards after the catch on two of his three grabs. Strange, with seven catches on the year, could be a streaming play in Week 4 against the Bengals if the game turns into a shootout.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught both of his targets for 17 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 2 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Strange ran a pass route on 30 of the team’s 36 drop backs but was invisible for most of the game. For now Strange can be treated as a desperation streamer in 12-team formats ahead of the Jags’ Week 3 matchup against the Patriots. He should remain on waiver wires in 10-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 2-of-3 targets for 23 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 1 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Strange operated as the Jaguars’ primary receiving tight end, seeing three targets on the day. In a loaded passing attack, he still found opportunity in what was a very fantasy-friendly offense. Strange caught a 14-yard touchdown in the second quarter and was mostly quiet in a second half where the Jaguars were already up by four scores. The Jaguars wide receivers will take much of Lawrence’s targets but Strange has a role over the middle of the field; he profiles as TE2 for Week 2 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Jaguars signed Brenton Strange to a three-year contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Per NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, the deal is worth “up to” $48 million. A chunk of that figure is presumably based on incentives. The contract includes $25 million guaranteed. Strange posted a minor breakout in 2024 with 411 yards on 40 grabs. He upped the ante in 2025 to 46 catches for 540 yards despite missing five games. Strange was heading into the final year of his rookie deal before this extension and the team spent multiple draft picks on tight ends, making it look like they were considering letting him walk next offseason. Instead, Nate Boerkircher and Tanner Koziol will primarily see the field for heavy offensive looks, something the team talked about after the draft. Strange will sit on the TE1/2 border in early fantasy drafts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes Brenton Strange will be a “key piece of everything the Jaguars do on offense” in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Shipley said the Jaguars drafting Texas A&M TE Nate Boerkircher and Houston TE Tanner Koziol in the 2026 draft does not mean the Jaguars coaching staff has a smaller role planned for Strange, who last season 46 catches, 540 yards, and three touchdowns as the team’s TE1. Shipley expected Strange’s pass game involvement to grow as the Jaguars deploy more tight end-heavy offensive sets. The Jaguars, Shipley said, are “clearly hoping that injecting the [tight end] room with talent should allow Strange to produce at an even higher level than before.” Last season Strange was targeted on 21 percent of his routes, which ranked 25th out of 58 qualifying tight ends. Though he’ll likely be the team’s third or fourth option in the passing game, Strange should be a viable fantasy option in 12 and 14-team leagues this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 2-of-7 targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Both of Washington’s receptions came before the break, the second of which was a 50-yard touchdown on a double-move slant against Cover-0 with under one minute remaining before the half. Washington remains one of the most efficient receivers in the league but consistently positive game scripts have left the overall pass volume lacking, particularly in the second half this season. He remains an upside WR2 ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 1-of-2 targets for 16 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 8 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Washington also added a 10-yard rush. Extremely disappointing volume coming out of the Jaguars’ bye week, but no Jag commanded more than three targets in a contest where Trevor Lawrence attempted only 14 throws before taking a fourth quarter breather in a 42-7 blowout. Washington is going to be subject to this kind of risk when the deep-and-dangerous Jags take on more overmatched foes, including now for Week 9 as the Ravens come to town for Thursday Night Football with their No. 2 or 3 quarterback under center. You always fire up Washington as a WR2, but he’s probably not going to stuff the stat sheet on Thursday evening.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 4-of-11 targets for 64 yards in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: A lot of these incompletions were balls Washington got a hand on but couldn’t quite reel in as was breaking to the sideline. Washington displayed his speed and shiftiness on a 27-yard catch-and-run in the second quarter where he cut through both Texans linebackers for a big gain. He is a fantasy WR2 as the Jaguars enter their bye week. Washington is #onpace for a near-1,200 yard season with 14 touchdowns even after this dud.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 6-of-9 targets for 124 yards and two touchdowns in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Coming off a pair of quiet weeks, Washington paid off for fantasy managers early with a 51-yard score in the first quarter. It was somehow nowhere close to his best play of the day. Washington scored his second touchdown on a falling, one-handed grab in the end zone from 27 yards out near the end of the game. The grab was reminiscent of Odell Beckham’s famous touchdown catch. Washington remains the most talented and most involved receiver on the Jags. He will be a high-end WR2 versus the Texans next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 1-of-3 targets for 7 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 4 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Washington also added three yards with one carry on the ground. After a hot start to the season, Washington was relatively quiet against the Bengals. The Jaguars receivers combined for just 11 of Trevor Lawrence’s 23 targets and Washington saw three of those. His first reception came in the fourth quarter on a 40-yard catch-and-run that would have sealed the game, but was called back after replay showed he stepped out of bounds after seven yards. Game script and the Bengals’ tight end weaknesses played a factor in this game, with Brenton Strange the primary target on the day. Washington should still be the Jaguars’ No. 1 receiver and is a fantasy WR2 for Week 5 against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: It’s Washington’s second touchdown in the Jags’ first three games of the season. Washington caught his touchdown against the Patriots after having an acrobatic touchdown grab called back on a penalty. Having established himself as the team’s clear-cut WR1 — well ahead of Brian Thomas, who had one target in Week 3 — Washington will have a rock solid weekly floor with ceiling to spare in shootout game scripts. Washington should remain in all lineups next week against a middling Bengals defense, in what could be a high-scoring affair between two potent offenses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 8-of-12 targets for 98 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 2 loss against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Trevor Lawrence, as always, targeted Washington heavily, as no other Jacksonville pass catcher saw more than eight targets on the day. Washington came within half a yard of a touchdown in the first half after scoring in Week 1 against the Browns. Clearly the team’s No. 1 wideout, Washington should have a rock-solid weekly floor with upside to spare, especially when the Jaguars have to operate a more pass-heavy offense. Washington will be a top-15 play next week against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 5-of-6 targets for 83 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 1 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Washington saw elite usage in the first half, making the first Jacksonville catch of the game and ending the Jaguars’ first drive with a diving 30-yard touchdown reception. He followed it up with a one-handed sideline catch on the second drive and tallied five receptions in the first half. His usage was that of a legitimate No. 1 wide receiver for the Jaguars’ fantasy-friendly offense. The game was out of hand in the second half, leading to no more receptions the rest of the day, but fantasy managers will be happy with Washington’s utilization and production as he adds to his elite box scores from the end of last season. Washington is a fantasy WR2 heading into Week 2 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports the Jaguars are “unlikely” to extend Parker Washington before Week 1.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Per Wolfe, the Jags explored a deal similar to that of Michael Wilson, who just landed a three-year, $75 million extension. The two sides couldn’t agree to terms, and Washington will now start his contract year. It’s a highly risky move for a largely unheralded player who caught lightning in a bottle at the end of last year. Washington caught 29 passes for 507 yards and three touchdowns in his final five games, including one postseason appearance. If he repeats anything close to those numbers over a full season this year, Washington will make far more than Wilson as a free agent next offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Jaguars HC Liam Coen said Parker Washington will “absolutely” be the team’s punt returner to start the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Coen also noted that Washington is “the guy right now,” suggesting that his role as the returner could change at some point in the year. Washington returned 25 punts for the Jaguars last season and racked up 341 return yards and two touchdowns on those returns. Coen said the Jaguars will hope to get Travis Hunter involved as the punt returner at some point, but Washington will start the season in the role. Washington profiles as a solid WR2 to start the fantasy season after going for 58-847-5 last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 4-of-6 targets for 65 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: All four of Meyers’ receptions came before the half in what remained a tighter game until just before the half, when alpha wide receiver Parker Washington took a simple slant for a 50-yard touchdown with under a minute remaining before the break. As has been the case on numerous occasions this season, Jacksonville coasted in the second half, limiting overall pass volume after the break. Meyers narrowly missed his first touchdown since Week 3 as he was tackled at the one on the team’s first possession. He remains a viable FLEX option ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) is not on the final injury report for Week 9 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: The Jaguars keep many of their injured players limited all week, Meyers included. The move was likely just a conservative measure, given the short practice week. The Jaguars will likely take a run-heavy approach against a Ravens team playing with their QB3. Meyers is just a FLEX, given the expected game script.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: The veteran receiver played through both ailments in Week 8 but was limited to only 54 percent of the team’s offensive snaps in a blowout win. Fantasy managers will want to monitor his status in the coming days, with the expectation that he continues to play through the injuries against the Ravens on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 2-of-3 targets for 24 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 8 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers wasn’t the only Jags pass catcher to post an empty box score in a 42-7 obliteration where Trevor Lawrence attempted only 14 passes, though he’s now been held to two or fewer receptions in 4-of-7 games. For a supposed “floor” player, that is not going to cut it, especially since Meyers is not the ceiling threat in this offense. With volume likely to remain in short supply for Thursday’s short-week tilt with the Lamar Jackson-less Ravens, Meyers is not a compelling WR3 for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle/hamstring) is active for Jacksonville’s Week 8 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: As expected based on the morning reporting. Meyers can be trusted as a WR4/FLEX mix against the Colts. Inactive for the Jaguars are S Antonio Johnson (knee), WR CJ Williams, CB Alijah Huzzie, LB Jamal Hill, DE Wesley Williams and DT Albert Regis.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jakobi Meyers (ankle/hamstring) is “good to go” for Week 8 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers was limited in the Jags’ first two practices of the week before being downgraded to a DNP on Friday. The team listed him as questionable, though the DNP was likely maintenance in hindsight. Meyers has topped three catches or 50 yards in just two games this year. He did, however, see 10 targets in the Jags’ Week 6 loss to the Texans before their bye. Meyers is in the WR4 mix for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring, ankle) did not practice Friday and is questionable to play in Week 8 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers managed back-to-back limited sessions to begin the week of preparation but was downgraded to a “DNP” Friday, ultimately drawing the questionable tag for Week 8 against the Colts. An absence could require additional offensive snaps for two-way player Travis Hunter and a slight uptick in route rate for Brian Thomas Jr and Josh Cameron. This is one to monitor for fantasy managers of all Jacksonville pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers has put together a pair of limited sessions out of the bye and seems likely to play against the Colts in Week 8. Brian Thomas Jr.'s disappearing act has left Meyers capable of putting up WR3 lines, but the Colts may not be opponent enough to force that kind of production out of Meyers this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: The hamstring issue is new, but it’s not one we expected to prevent Meyers from playing. A limited practice this early in the week is typically maintenance, especially midway through the season. Meyers will remains a fantasy WR4 for his Week 8 matchup with the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 5-of-10 targets for 83 yards in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: It’s his highest target total of the season and the first time Meyers has managed 10 targets since Week 14 of the 2025 season. No touchdown here, but Meyers is a fine real-life third receiver who has mostly been left to the FLEX life in Jacksonville. He enters the bye as someone who can be dropped in shallow leagues in a roster crunch, but also someone solidly in the top 50 wideouts in the league on a good offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez rushed 10 times for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens, adding 13 yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez split time with lead back Bayshul Tuten in the first half before soaking up most of the backfield work in the third quarter. Both backs would then cede primary duties to special team ace Ameer Abdullah in the fourth quarter when the game was well in hand. Rodriguez has seen his fantasy value plummet of late with the emergence of Tuten as a borderline workhorse, a situation that was heavily influenced by Tuten’s lack of practice ahead of Thursday Night Football. The long week appears likely to provide the time needed for Tuten to return to full strength, leaving Rodriguez as a touchdown-dependent FLEX when the Jaguars face the Titans in Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez (hand) is not on the final injury report for Week 9 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez remained limited all week, as did many Jaguars on the Week 9 injury report. It seems likely that the team simply took a conservative approach to their Thursday Night Football preparation. Rodriguez could end up being the Jaguars’ starter this week, with Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) labeled a game-time decision after failing to practice all week. Rodriguez warrants RB2 treatment if this is the case. Add him everywhere.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Liam Coen said Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) will be a game-time decision for Week 9 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Tuten did not practice on Tuesday. Coen told reporters he would get in a limited session today. Tuten himself told Coen he feels better today and he toughed it out through the injury on Sunday. He appears to be on the right side of questionable for Thursday’s contest, but fantasy managers will want to check inactives before kickoff to be sure. If he can’t go, Chris Rodriguez will get the bulk of the carries for the Jags.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez (hand) was limited on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: This appears to be a non-issue as the veteran change of pace back should be fine for Thursday Night Football against the Ravens. Of greater concern was the absence of lead back Bayshul Tuten, something fantasy managers of both players will want to monitor as Thursday draw nearer. Rodriguez would seemingly be in line for a featured role if Tuten is unable to play on a short week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez rushed six times for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 8 win over the Colts, adding a 17-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez was still getting out-snapped and out-produced by a percolating Bhayshul Tuten, but he managed to contribute a 28-yard score in a blowout victory. Rodriguez hit the hole then emerged to an abandoned mall of a Colts defense. With the Jaguars heading on the road for a short-week Thursday night date with a Ravens team operating without Lamar Jackson, expect lots of “get me out of here” Jags rushes in Baltimore, locking Rodriguez in as a Week 9 FLEX play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez rushed 11 times for 55 yards in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: He failed to catch his only target. Rodriguez was churning out success rate on the regular in the first half. The Jaguars curiously went away from him in the second half, as he played just 21-of-70 snaps and had only one carry after halftime. He’s not a must-hold through the bye week, but this game is the proof-of-concept that he can be an effective weapon for the Jaguars if they want to use him as a between-the-tackles pounder.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez rushed two times for five yards in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez was all but phased out of the rotation in this game. His most notable touch was a goal line carry which he was stuffed on and then fumbled the ball away. He was called down on the field. Even though replay clearly showed him losing the ball, there was no clear recovery and the refs didn’t bother overturning the non-fumble. Rodriguez may still be the occasional touchdown vulture, but his role has been reduced to the point where fantasy managers can safely cut ties with him on the next run of waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez rushed six times for 35 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 4 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez entered the game frequently when the Jaguars entered Bengals territory. He has a hold on short-yardage opportunities while also getting some red zone looks, but Bhayshul Tuten is the clear lead back. Rodriguez was out-snapped 36-to-15 but salvaged his fantasy day with a 25-yard rushing touchdown in the fourth quarter. He is a handcuff for fantasy purposes heading into Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez had eight rushes for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez remained the second option in the Jaguars backfield behind Bhayshul Tuten, but stole a short score from Tuten in the blowout victory. Through three games Rodriguez has been a between the tackles option who has next to no involvement in the passing game. He would only be fantasy viable if Tuten misses time this season. For now C-Rod is a decent stash as a contingency option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Jaguars HC Liam Coen said he “fully anticipates” more snaps for LeQuin Allen on third down.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Allen played on just one offensive snap in last week’s win over the Browns, but led the Jaguars in third-down snaps (146) last season. Despite all the snaps he saw on third down as a rookie, Allen never materialized into a viable fantasy option. Whether or not that changes this season is to be determined, but any additional snaps he receives on third down would come at the expense of Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez, after Rodriguez led the way with five third-down snaps last week. While Allen seeing additional work in these situations could be problematic for fantasy managers, they shouldn’t let that deter them from starting Tuten in Week 2 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 12 times for 29 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten started after failing to practice in any capacity this week, capping off the opening drive with a score from one yard out. He would split time with Chris Rodriguez for the rest of the first half before giving way to the combination of Rodriguez and special teams ace Ameer Abdullah for the bulk of the second half with the game in hand. Tuten should see his volume tick back up toward lead back territory when the Jaguars face off against the Titans in Week 10, where he will return to RB2 status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) is “good to go” after completing his pre-game workout for Week 9 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: The Jaguars have routinely killed the clock with their efficient ground game this season, oftentimes pulling Trevor Lawrence early. With the Ravens starting QB Joe Fagnano (ankle) tonight, the Jaguars should again enjoy a run-heavy game script, expectedly playing with a lead. Tuten is an RB1, having avoided suffering a setback this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) “should be” good for Week 9 against the Ravens, barring any pre-game setbacks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten did not practice at all this week, though the Jaguars notably kept many injured players limited, so it is possible that his absences were mostly precautionary. Tuten injured his ankle and foot in Week 8 against the Colts, but still managed to total 159 scrimmage yards, two catches and two touchdowns. He is an RB1 if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Jaguars coach Liam Coen told reporters earlier today that Tuten will be a game-time decision for this week’s Thursday Night Football game. He also told reporters that Tuten would get in a limited session today. Unfortunately, that did not happen. Tuten logged his third DNP of the week instead. Conversely, Chris Rodriguez (hand) logged three limited sessions and was removed from the injury report. As things currently stand, Tuten is on the wrong side of questionable, while Rodriguez appears to be the likely starter. Rodriguez should be added in all 10- and 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Liam Coen said Bhayshul Tuten (foot/ankle) will be a game-time decision for Week 9 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten did not practice on Tuesday. Coen told reporters he would get in a limited session today. Tuten himself told Coen he feels better today and he toughed it out through the injury on Sunday. He appears to be on the right side of questionable for Thursday’s contest, but fantasy managers will want to check inactives before kickoff to be sure. If he can’t go, Chris Rodriguez will get the bulk of the carries for the Jags.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) was not spotted at Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: After being an estimated DNP on Monday, Tuten was not spotted at Tuesday’s practice. With the Jaguars playing Thursday, this is a bit concerning for his Week 9 availability, as he will likely need to get in a limited practice on Wednesday if he hopes to suit up. In the event he can’t go, Chris Rodriguez, who ran for 41 yards and a touchdown on six carries last week, would be in line to handle a significant workload against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) was listed as a “DNP” on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten briefly left the team’s Week 8 win in the first quarter but returned to amass 159 total yards and two touchdowns against the overmatched Colts. Fantasy managers will want to track his status closely as the team makes a quick turn to face the Ravens on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 16 times for 104 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 8 win over the Colts, adding two receptions for 55 yards and a second score.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: It was a red letter day for the second-year pro, who: 1. Posted a new career high in rushing. 2. Posted a new career high in receiving. 3. Posted just his second two-touchdown outing. No. 3 is perhaps the most notable since Tuten’s first two-score day came heading into the Jags’ Week 7 bye. Tuten is taking off in fantasy even as Chris Rodriguez Jr. remains involved. It’s due in part to the fact that the Jags are dominating game script and dictating tempo, but Tuten is also just genuinely running well. Today that included even after he had to get an ankle taped. That will be something to monitor heading into Thursday’s short-week date with the Ravens, but Tuten should be good to go as a high-end RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 12 times for 39 yards in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans, adding four catches for 48 yards and two touchdowns on his only four targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: The Jaguars looked like they were in control with their run game early in this one, but Tuten sputtered out in the second half, where he managed just six carries for 18 yards with the Jaguars curiously going away from Chris Rodriguez Jr. Tuten played 40-of-72 snaps with Rodriguez having a big day on the ground. It feels good that his “down” games are like this, and he also had a rushing touchdown pulled off the board after what appeared to be a phantom holding flag was thrown. Tuten enters the Week 7 bye as an RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 22 times for 72 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles, adding two catches for 24 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: The Jags’ offense struggled to execute at a basic level in this game, and Tuten may have been hurt the most by errors. Their first goal line sequence of the day started with a Chris Rodriguez near-fumble. After two incomplete passes, Liam Coen dialed up a jet sweep for Tuten that was blown up for a loss of six yards. The Jags’ next goal line sequence featured a pair of delay of game penalties followed by an incomplete pass on fourth down. Tuten got the full workhorse treatment in this game, ceding just two carries and one catch to his backups. He unfortunately could not make much of the touches. Tuten will be a high-end RB2 if this role persists into his Week 6 matchup versus the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 16-of-26 passes for 242 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ 33-10, Week 9 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: It was business as usual for Lawrence and the Jaguars, who won their eighth game by 20 or more points since the start of the 2025 season, the most in the league during that span. Lawrence looked sharp throughout, starting things off with a touchdown drive on their opening possession that was sparked by a 52-yard completion to tight end Nate Boerkircher. He would hit Parker Washington on a slant for a 50-yard touchdown in the final minute before the half to push the lead to 17-3, with a flurry of second half field goals enough to chase the reeling Ravens from the field. In standard Jacksonville fashion, positive game script capped Lawrence’s aerial volume, something fantasy managers have both gotten used to through the mid way point in the season and will likely see continue considering the Jaguars hold the league’s softest remaining strength of schedule. The win pushes the Jaguars to 6-2 and extends their lead in the AFC South ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the one-win Titans, where Lawrence will remain a back end QB1 due to lack of volume.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 10-of-14 passes for 210 yards and three touchdowns in the Jaguars’ 42-7, Week 8 win over the Colts, adding three rushes for 10 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: This came in only three quarters of work, as Lawrence spent the fourth frame on the bench with the Jags demolishing the quitting Colts. Unfortunately for fantasy managers, early breathers have been a theme for Lawrence this season as his well-rounded team keeps blowing out less impressive sides. Rather unbelievably, that could now include the Ravens for Week 9, as Baltimore appears down to its No. 3 quarterback for the sides’ short-week Thursday night tilt. That won’t be enough to force Lawrence out of starting lineups, but he can’t be expected to single-handedly win matchups in that environment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 24-of-41 passes for 306 yards, four touchdowns and one interception in Jacksonville’s 34-31, Week 6 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: It could have been more, had Liam Coen not settled for a game-tying field goal on fourth-and-short with less than four minutes left in the game. It also could have been more had Lawrence not thrown an end-zone pick to Calen Bullock. At the end of the day, the screen game was dealing and Lawrence was hitting all sorts of in-breakers against a beleaguered Texans secondary. He enters the bye week as a sure-fire QB1 with 1,174 passing yards and 10 throwing touchdowns in his first five games. Last year’s rushing touchdowns appear to have vanished as the Jaguars have gotten better in the red zone, but Lawrence is still playing exceptional football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 24-of-39 passes for 331 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Jaguars’ 19-17, Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: Lawrence gave fantasy managers what they needed with a solid box score, but he was not the reason the Jags won this game. Lawrence struggled under pressure, throwing one ugly interception while putting the ball on the ground twice via sack-fumbles. Both were recovered by the Jags. The offense was also a catastrophe in the red zone, though a series of penalties and bizarre play calls are largely to blame there. Down by one with eight seconds left, it looked like the team’s struggles on offense would be too much to overcome. Instead, Ameer Abdullah returned a kickoff 53 yards to set up a walkoff field goal from Cam Little. If the Jags can clean things up after an uncharacteristically sloppy game, Lawrence will remain a mid-range QB1 for Week 6 versus the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 18-of-23 passes for 227 yards and one touchdown in the Jaguars’ 22-17, Week 4 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: The Jaguars offensive operation was far from clean against the Bengals; the team as a whole tallied 10 penalties for 100 yards by halftime. Lawrence was sacked four times behind a struggling offensive line but still put together an efficient game. He found Brian Thomas Jr. for the game’s first touchdown as time wound down in the first half and found tight end Brenton Strange for seven of his 18 completions. Despite a relatively pedestrian showing, Lawrence comes away with zero turnovers and the win. He will be a top-12 fantasy option for Week 5 against the Eagles in London.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 19-of-29 attempts for 182 yards and three touchdowns in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots, adding four rushes for 25 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: Lawrence’s big statistical day could have been bigger if he hadn’t inexplicably taken a knee at the one yard line on a QB rush with about eight minutes left in the fourth quarter. Bhayshul Tuten would go on to score a rushing touchdown a few plays later. Lawrence picked apart of the New England secondary with very little pressure in his face, targeting former Patriots WR Jakobi Meyers heavily and connecting with three different pass catchers for touchdowns — including Parker Washington, who had another score called back. Lawrence, with one of the highest weekly floors in the game, will again be a top-12 QB option in Week 4 against Bengals in what should be a high-scoring game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 17-of-29 attempts for 189 yards and one interception in the Jaguars’ Week 2 loss against the Broncos, adding two rushes for six yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: The Jaguars were relatively run-heavy against Denver a week after the Broncos were shredded by Ken Walker and the Chiefs. Lawrence mostly checked down in this one, targeting Parker Washington a team-high 12 times. Brian Thomas, Jr., meanwhile, had two untimely drops, one that appeared to frustrate Lawrence. Lawrence’s interception came on a poor throw to Washington near the sideline. He’ll look to bounce back next week against a stingy New England secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 18-of-23 passes for 245 yards and four touchdowns in the Jaguars’ 34-10, Week 1 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: It was a monstrous offensive showing from the Jaguars, led by Lawrence and his four passing touchdowns. He opened scoring with a 30-yard touchdown throw to Parker Washington in the first quarter, tossing two more scores in the first half. Lawrence flexed his mobility with a lob on the run to Jakobi Meyers for a 32-yard touchdown in the third quarter. With a comfortable lead, Lawrence rested in the fourth quarter, finishing with a whopping 0.72 EPA per play. Nick Mullens tallied three kneel-downs in relief. Liam Coen’s offense will generate many fantasy opportunities across the board, especially when operating as efficiently as it did Week 1. Lawrence built upon his solid 2025 season with an all-star showing Week 1 against the Browns and should be a low-end fantasy QB1 for Week 2 against a tougher Broncos defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence said he is more confident in his “progressions, adjustments, when to kill a play and what to call instead.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: According to ESPN’s Michael DiRocco, Lawrence’s offseason “was about gaining a graduate-level understanding” of coach Liam Coen’s offense. Last season, Lawrence was rehabbing an injury while attempting to change his footwork and adjust to a new play caller. He is now calmer and “can play more freely the way he did in the second half of last season.” Lawrence was the overall QB1 in total scoring from Weeks 9-18. If Lawrence and his pass catchers can carry the momentum into 2026, Lawrence can once again finish as an elite QB1, this time from Week 1 onward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Jaguars HC Liam Coen said he is “trending toward” playing the starters in Friday’s preseason game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: The Jaguars didn’t play any starters in last week’s preseason game against the Saints, but Coen said that because they couldn’t do a padded practice on Monday with the Panthers, he may consider playing his starters a bit on Friday in order to get some “good (players) on good (players)” facing one another. If the Jaguars do play their starters this week, it will be their only taste of preseason action, as Coen has already said he won’t be playing them in the third preseason game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reports that the Ravens are willing to make Lamar Jackson the highest-paid player in NFL history.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Well, that’s good, because it will assuredly take a record-setting deal to keep him in a Ravens uniform. Jackson has an $84.34 million salary cap hit next season, so the team has to do something with his contract. Jackson has a no-trade clause and a no-franchise tag clause — he possesses a ton of leverage. Per Palmer, the two sides will not negotiate a new deal in-season, so they will try to get something done between the end of the season and the beginning of free agency, which starts in March 2027.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Lamar Jackson is “likely out for the season” after suffering a thumb injury in Week 8’s loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Head coach Jesse Minter didn’t dismiss the possibility of this being a season-ending injury for Jackson when asked about it after the game, but the optics on the field weren’t good, and the team wasted little time announcing he would undergo surgery and be placed on injured reserve. It wouldn’t be at all surprising to learn in the days ahead that Jackson’s season is over, but the team will likely wait until after he has his surgery to make any formal announcement. With Jackson and Tyler Huntley (toe) both being sidelined, rookie UDFA Joe Fagnano is slated to start on the short week on Thursday against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (thumb) will undergo surgery and be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: When asked if this is a potentially season-ending injury for Jackson, Minter’s response was, “We’ll see.” After seeing Jackson’s injury on replay, it was easy to assume the Ravens’ QB1 would be looking at another multi-week absence, but this sounds like the worst-case scenario. If Jackson doesn’t land on season-ending IR, he would be required to miss at least four games before he could even consider a return. Adding insult to injury, the Ravens also lost backup Tyler Huntley in this game to a toe injury, meaning rookie UDFA Joe Fagnano could be in line to start on Thursday night against the Jaguars in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Lamar Jackson (thumb) will not return in Week 8’s game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Jackson’s day officially ends after one play. The two-time MVP injured the thumb on his throwing hand on his first and only dropback of the day and immediately went to the locker room. The urgency with which Jackson was ushered from the field, coupled with how quickly he was ruled out, suggests this could be a serious enough injury that will result in another multi-game absence for Jackson. Tyler Huntley will be under center for the remainder of Week 8’s game against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Lamar Jackson (thumb) is questionable to return in Week 8 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Shortly after he exited the field the team announced that Jackson was questionable to return after suffering a thumb injury on his throwing hand. Tyler Huntley immediately took over for Jackson, as the Ravens’ offense went three-and-out on their first drive of the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Lamar Jackson (hand) exited in the first quarter of Week 8’s game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Jackson dropped back to pass on the Ravens’ first offensive play of the game and immediately headed for the sideline after hitting his hand on Bills LB Greg Rousseau. The injury was to Jackson’s throwing hand and appeared to be to his thumb, judging by what we could see on slow-motion replay. Trainers covered Jackson’s hand with a towel and immediately ushered him to the locker room. We will check back in when we receive more information on his status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe said Lamar Jackson (ankle) “won’t be 100 percent” in Week 8 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: The good news, per Wolfe, is that Jackson will still be able to move despite playing on a bum ankle. Jackson told reporters the pain is “bearable” earlier in the week, which didn’t exactly inspire confidence from Ravens fans and fantasy managers. On the other hand, if Jackson is out there, we expect him to be mobile enough to lead a top-flight offense. A date with the Bills, which features the highest game total of the week, should also create an incredible environment for fantasy production. He is back at the top of the QB1 mix for a likely shootout with the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (ankle) will play in Baltimore’s Week 8 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: “We do think we will have Lamar this game,” Minter said. Jackson practiced in full on Friday and has missed the last three weeks with his high-ankle sprain. He was officially cleared off the injury report. Jackson told reporters that he feels like “I’m no longer a statue.” Jackson will be “safe” to use as a QB1 against the Bills in what profiles as a fantasy points bonanza.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) practiced in full Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: It’s the second consecutive full practice for Jackson, who is attempting to return from a three-game absence to face the Bills in Week 8. The two full sessions were also his first such practices since injuring his ankle, a positive development toward an active status in a marquee matchup. He’ll have one more opportunity to maintain his level of participation, which would likely keep him off the injury report heading into the weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: It’s Jackson’s first full practice since suffering the ankle injury in Week 4. Even with the many twists and turns in this latest injury saga, we’re comfortable assuming Jackson will play this week. The fact that he was held out this long hopefully means that he’s close to 100 percent healthy. Facing a likely shootout with the Bills, Jackson projects for the second-most fantasy points at his position, behind only Josh Allen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford (right elbow) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford has downplayed inquiries regarding his throwing-arm injury, saying he’s been icing his elbow post-game and post-practice for a while now — and he called out the beat reporters for missing it. Lingering elbow soreness isn’t exactly reassuring, but at least he is practicing fully. Stafford should be good to go for the Rams’ Week 9 game against the Commanders, but this is obviously worth monitoring.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 17-of-25 attempts for 157 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford wasn’t asked to do much against the Chargers, as the Rams once again went ultra run-heavy with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined. Averaging a meager 6.3 yards per attempt, Stafford mostly checked down to his short-area targets. His touchdown came on a well-designed screen pass to Puka Nacua. Stafford will have some fantasy appeal in Week 9 against the pass-funnel Washington defense. Coming into Week 8, Stafford ranked 13th in expected fantasy points per game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 23-of-29 attempts for 195 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: It was a fairly clean game for Stafford against a Raiders defense that rarely pressures the passer and has proven vulnerable in the intermediate and deep areas of the field. Stafford picked apart the Vegas secondary in the first half, with heavy three tight end-set usage and a more run-heavy game plan than usual with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined. The Rams had 35 rushing attempts to 29 passes on the day. Stafford connected with Puka Nacua for one score and Davis Allen for two others. Though Stafford’s ceiling is going to be lower with Adams out, he profiles as a safe option in Week 8 against the Chargers. He now has six multi-touchdown games this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 25-of-33 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns in the Rams’ 16-18, Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: The Cardinals’ pass rush was disruptive, hitting Stafford seven times and sacking him twice. Stafford lost a fumble on a two-point conversion, but the box score only shows a failed two-point try, evidently saving fantasy managers two fantasy points. Stafford later fumbled after getting spooked by a pass-rushing ghost. A Rams lineman recovered it, but it derailed an otherwise effective, tempo-based drive. Stafford engineered a touchdown drive at the tail end of the game, connecting with Puka Nacua on a 42-yarder and a 16-yarder, before Colby Parkinson barreled into the end zone for the score. Stafford should return to the QB1 tier against the Raiders in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 40-of-54 passes for 383 yards and three touchdowns in the Rams’ 37-34, Week 5 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: It was the third consecutive game in which Stafford attempted 51 passes or more in what has become the most voluminous passing offense in the league. The two powerhouses felt each other out throughout the first half as only 20 combined points per scored before the break. Things would get aggressive for the final 30 minutes as seven combined touchdowns were scored on nine second half possessions, four of which were accounted for by the Rams. Stafford directed a whopping 24 targets toward alpha wide receiver Puka Nacua, who set a career high with 17 receptions in a short-area role. The reigning MVP returned an instant classic performance against the 2024 MVP, ultimately coming up short in overtime following a blocked field goal attempt from Harrison Mevis. The Rams fall to 2-3 ahead of a home matchup against the more forgiving Cardinals in Week 6. Stafford is once again a fantasy QB1 in that matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 32-of-51 passes for 316 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions in the Rams’ 24-20, Week 4 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford put the Rams behind the eight ball with a pair of first half interceptions but was better after the break as the Rams slowly erased a 20-10 deficit. Not that he was amazing, but with the Eagles finishing an inconceivable 0-12 on third down, Stafford needed to make just enough plays, and that’s what he did despite leaving some meat on the bone. It was forgivable on a rainy day in Philly, though Stafford now has at least one interception in all four of his starts. In fact, he has as many scores (six) as picks. Hopefully that trend reverses with Puka Nacua back in the lineup, though the schedule is not lightening up with the Rams hosting the Bills for Monday Night Football in Week 5. That should nevertheless be a fantasy football bonanza.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 30-of-55 passes for 390 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Rams’ 30-26, Week 3 loss to the Broncos, adding 13 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: The Rams stormed out to a 16-0 lead they would take into the break but two unanswered scores and two-point conversions from the Broncos saw the game knotted at 16 heading into the fourth quarter, which is where the scoring really took off. Stafford and the Rams appeared to be in control of the game until a Talanoa Hufanga pick-six off Stafford, making 33 career pick-sixes thrown to give him a record he would otherwise not like to have on his ledger. Stafford answered on the following possession on a 48-yard strike to Konata Mumpfield, only for the Broncos to answer back with a Bo Nix rushing score with 47 seconds left to play. Stafford worked more magic to get the team into the red zone, marching the field with only one timeout with a chance to win on the final play of the game. Hufanga ultimately won the play with his second interception off Stafford, sending the Rams to a 1-2 record. Stafford also became the first quarterback in NFL history to throw for 20,000 yards for two different franchises in the loss. Stafford remains a locked-in QB1 in fantasy circles ahead of a Week 4 showdown with the Eagles on the road.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said he’s “not sure” if Puka Nacua (groin) will play in Week 3.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: McVay said he’s “hopeful” Nacua, who missed Monday night’s game against the Giants, will be able to suit up against Denver next week. The Rams offense was fine without Nacua on Monday against an injury-ravaged Giants team. LA had the week’s fourth highest EPA per play on the way to a 28-6 win. Another game with Nacua sidelined will mean more target domination for Davante Adams and more involvement for Terrance Ferguson, who caught 6-of-9 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown against New York.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 22-of-31 passes for 327 yards, four touchdowns, and one interception in the Rams’ 28-6, Week 2 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: It was an inspiring effort from the 38-year-old quarterback while playing without his top option through the air in Puka Nacua. Stafford locked onto Davante Adams, the latter of whom turned 10 targets into eight receptions for 195 yards and two touchdowns, on his way to a 22nd career game with four touchdown passes. He also moved into sixth on the all-time passing touchdown leaderboard, overtaking Philip Rivers with the four-touchdown performance. The Rams shook off their travel woes in convincing fashion to move to 1-1 ahead of road meeting with the Broncos in Week 3, where Stafford will remain a locked-in QB1 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 15-of-25 passes for 155 yards with an interception in the Rams’ 27-7, Week 1 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford didn’t get much time to enjoy Australia, and likely won’t leave this contest with fond memories. He completed just 4-of-11 passes in the first half and didn’t do much better in the final 30 minutes, and outside of a 41-yard connection with Puka Nacua, he just couldn’t get the ball downfield. He was also stuffed on a fourth-and-goal run at the goal line to cement the poor day. Credit the 49ers’ defense, but it’s fair to call this a disappointing season debut for the reigning MVP. Expect a rebound in Week 2 against the Giants in a Monday Night Football contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Ravens did not activate Adam Randall (neck) from injured reserve for Week 9 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: The Ravens’ rookie running back will have to wait to make his debut. The Ravens declared QB Kedon Slovis, WR Elijah Sarratt, OL Emery Jones Jr., DL Aeneas Peebles, CB Nate Wiggins and S Jaylinn Hawkins inactive. Hawkins is dealing with a knee injury and Wiggins, the Ravens’ No. 1 cornerback, is listed with a stinger and an illness. Slovis will serve as the emergency third quarterback. Austin Reed is the QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Adam Randall (neck) is questionable for Week 9 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: Randall is currently on injured reserve, so the Ravens will have to activate him tomorrow afternoon if they plan on him playing. He will compete with Rasheen Ali for the RB3 role if he’s ready to return to the field this week. There isn’t any fantasy value to be had here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Ravens designated Adam Randall to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: Randall was placed on injured reserve at the end of training camp with an undisclosed injury. The team now has three weeks to officially activate him from injured reserve. Once healthy, Randall will be contending with Rasheen Ali for the Ravens’ rarely used RB3 role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Ravens placed Adam Randall on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: Cornerback Bilhal Kone was also placed on IR. Both players can return after four games. Randall was likely parked behind Justice Hill as the Ravens’ RB3 heading into the season. That role now belongs to Rasheen Ali, at least until Randall is back in action. He played in the team’s final preseason game and the team has not said what this injury is yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: The Athletic’s Jeff Zrebiec believes the Ravens see Justice Hill “as a good complement to Derrick Henry and really value his ability out of the backfield and in blitz pickup.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: Hill ended 2025 on injured reserve because of a neck issue. He was reportedly a cut candidate during the offseason and the team selected Clemson running back Adam Randall on Day Three of the draft. It seemed possible that the team planned on replacing Hill this year, but Zrebiec shot that idea down, at least for the start of the season. Zrebiec answered, “I can’t see that happening from the jump,” in reference to a question about Randall opening the season as Baltimore’s backup running back. Hill caught 21 passes for 169 yards and a touchdown in 10 games last year. He also punched in a pair of touchdowns on the ground despite running just 18 times. His ceiling is extremely limited, even in the event of a Henry injury, but Hill should have some standalone RB4 value in PPR leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Ravens signed fifth-round pick RB Adam Randall to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: Per Spotrac, the deal is worth $4.62 million and includes a $379,480 signing bonus. Randall is the team owner, Steve Bisciotti’s first handpicked player. He converted from wide receiver to running back for Clemson’s 2025 season and posted a 168/814/10 rushing line and a 36/254/3 receiving line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Ravens’ Ryan Mink reports that team owner Steve Bisciotti was allowed to draft a player for the first time ever this year and chose former Clemson RB Adam Randall.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: The Ravens drafted Randall with the No. 174 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft’s fifth round yesterday. Bisciotti has been the Ravens’ majority owner since 2004 and was reportedly “begging” general manager Eric DeCosta for the chance to draft a rookie this year. According to DeCosta, Bisciotti “did his research and studied the tape, talked to people.” Bisciotti notably has a really good relationship with Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney. Swinney moved Randall (6’3/232) from wide receiver to running back for the 2025 season after Randall showcased shifty moves when given the chance to run the ball and contribute as a returner late in 2024. Whether Randall can earn the No. 2 or No. 3 running back role remains to be seen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Ravens selected Clemson RB Adam Randall with the No. 174 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: Randall could be the next big-bodied WR-to-RB convert to earn an NFL roster spot. He suffered a torn ACL during a 2022 spring practice and recovered in time to resume playing in Week 3 that year. Randall’s splash plays in the run game and return game late in 2024 inspired coach Dabo Swinney to move Randall from WR to RB for the 2025 season. Built to handle a three-down workload, Randall, 21, measured 6’3/232 at the NFL Scouting Combine. In his lone season at running back, Randall produced a 168/814/10 rushing line and a 36/254/3 receiving line. Randall is still learning how to play running back, so he comes with a very low floor, but his frame and dual-threat profile make him a name to know for fantasy purposes. He will likely get a crack at replacing Keaton Mitchell’s part-time role as a rookie.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Clemson freshman WR Adam Randall is rehabbing well from his torn ACL.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: Randall (6'3/198) suffered a torn ACL on April 6th during spring practice. He is reportedly doing well in his rehab and head coach Dabo Swinney said that he expects Randall to return at some point this season. A four-star recruit from this year’s class, it’s unlikely Randall makes much of an impact even if he does return to the field this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.headline: Clemson incoming freshman WR Adam Randall has torn his ACL in spring practice, will undergo surgery later this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adam-randall/0.analysis: It’s a big blow for the Tigers, who are losing their top receiver Justyn Ross to the draft. Randall (6'2"/215) was a four-star recruit in the 2022 class, the 17th ranked WR and the fourth ranked player from South Carolina. He could have helped jolt a disappointing passing game for Clemson, but he’ll miss his true freshman season and almost certainly medical redshirt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.headline: Travon Walker (ribs) is active for Week 9 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.analysis: The Jaguars’ No. 2 edge rusher will play through his ribs injury tonight. He apparently got hurt during Tuesday’s practice, but is good to go two days later. The Jaguars declared WR CJ Williams, CB Alijah Huzzie, S Cam’Ron Silmon-Craig and DE Wesley Williams inactive for Week 9 against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.headline: Travon Walker (ribs) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.analysis: Walker was added to the Jaguars’ injury report on Tuesday, apparently having suffered a ribs injury in practice. The Jaguars’ No. 2 edge rusher might not be needed to win an expectedly lopsided affair, but having him on the field will certainly be helpful for the Jaguars D/ST.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.headline: Jaguars signed EDGE Travon Walker to a four-year, $110 million extension through 2030.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.analysis: The deal includes $50 million at signing and $77 million in total guarantees. Walker, 25, has sacked opposing quarterbacks 29 times in regular season games over his four-year career. He banked four sacks last year, plus 42 quarterback pressures and a career-high 13.0 percent quarterback pressure rate. Fellow Jaguars EDGE Josh Hines-Allen is under contract through 2028. Today’s deal keeps the starting EDGE duo intact long-term.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.headline: ESPN’s Michael DiRocco reports the Jaguars have had preliminary discussions about extensions for WR Parker Washington, TE Brenton Strange, and EDGE Travon Walker.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.analysis: It was pointed out by John Shipley a few days ago that Wan’Dale Robinson’s free agent contract might be a starting point for the Washington extension. Walker is entering his final season under his rookie contract’s fifth-year option. Strange and Washington are both on the final year of their rookie contracts.
