The Jaguars have been uncharacteristically (and probably smartly, given their success last year) quiet in free agency, so perhaps they’re just focusing on locking up their core.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes that the Jaguars could use the 2026 NFL Draft to “boost” their defensive line.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.analysis: The front office could invest heavily in the defensive line, which currently includes three projected starters who have just one year remaining on their contracts. Former No. 1 overall pick, EDGE Travon Walker, is among them and is coming off a four-sack season, matching his 2022 rookie season total. He recorded 10 in 2024 and 11 in 2023. The team could draft an EDGE to groom behind Walker just in case they don’t complete an extension before the season. The Jaguars’ projected starting DTs are Arik Armstead, 32, and DaVon Hamilton, 29. Both players are scheduled to enter free agency next offseason. Given their age, it is reasonable to assume the Jaguars draft at least one interior defender in April. The team is returning every member of their offensive line this year. Shipley believes the Jaguars will use “at least one pick on a developmental offensive lineman.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.headline: Jaguars EDGE Travon Walker (knee) is practicing in full for Week 15 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.analysis: Walker returned to practice for two limited sessions last week and played off a questionable tag on Sunday. Potentially facing the Brady Cook-led Jets, Walker should be able to return with a sack or two in Week 15.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.headline: Jaguars declared WR Parker Washington (hip) inactive for Jacksonville’s Week 14 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.analysis: As expected based on earlier reporting, Washington will be scratched. He’s droppable if you have a late move you need to get in ahead of Sunday kickoff. Also inactive for the Jaguars are: S Andrew Wingard (concussion), Yasir Abdullah, OL Walker Little (concussion), TE Johnny Mundt, DL Emmanuel Ogbah and DL Austin Johnson. DL Travon Walker (knee), S Eric Murray (neck) and Arik Armstead (hand) are playing despite questionable tags in a huge game for the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.headline: Jaguars EDGE Travon Walker (knee) is questionable for Jacksonville’s Week 14 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.analysis: Walker hasn’t played since Week 11, but was able to get in two limited sessions this week and appears to be trending towards a return in a must-win AFC South top-of-division showdown with the Colts. The pass rusher has had a somewhat disappointing year to this point with just 2.5 sacks in nine games. Arik Armstead (hand) and Eric Murray (neck) are also questionable for Jacksonville.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.headline: Jaguars EDGE Travon Walker (knee) is practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.analysis: Almost undoubtedly a limited session after missing most of the last two weeks. The Jaguars are likely checking just how much Walker can give them ahead of Sunday’s massive top-of-AFC-South showdown with the Colts. It’s his first practice since ahead of Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.headline: Jaguars EDGE Travon Walker (knee) won’t play in Jacksonville’s Week 13 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travon-wal.analysis: Walker hasn’t practiced at all the last two weeks and will enter the Week 14 conversation on the questionable line. Walker has just 2.5 sacks in nine games this year and has been a bit of a disappointment after back-to-back 10-sack years in 2023 and 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/moro-ojomo.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that the Eagles have received “a ton of interest” on the trade market for Moro Ojomo.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/moro-ojomo.analysis: Ojomo is in a contract year, and per Breer, the Eagles have told interested parties that they would like to keep him beyond this year. With both Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis signed for multiple seasons, investing heavily in another defensive tackle might be cost-prohibitive. Perhaps the Eagles are simply trying to drive up Ojomo’s trade value. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/moro-ojomo.headline: Eagles DL Moro Ojomo and WR Tyrie Cleveland were both backboarded from Thursday’s preseason game against the Browns with neck injuries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/moro-ojomo.analysis: Scary, though both players were reported to have feeling in their extremities. The backboard is usually “just” a precaution, though it obviously always denotes a potentially serious situation. Thankfully in this case, it would seem both players have avoided truly serious injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/moro-ojomo.headline: Eagles selected Texas DT Moro Ojomo with the No. 249 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/moro-ojomo.analysis: Ojomo (6’2.625/292) is an interesting evaluation. Even with five years of college on his resume, he is still only 21. A trim 292 pounds, Ojomo played all over the line in Austin, utilizing his 88th percentile explosion and his class-best wingspan. Ojomo is regularly at full extension, providing a brick wall effect in the running game thanks to good get off. He underperformed on the stat sheet, along with most of the Longhorns defenses during his time there. Due to his lack of mass, he may be moved out to three tech. His strength will never be penetration or pass rush, though he is quick enough he doesn’t have a good understanding of how to get around a blocker. Ojomo is a good run stopper that will free up his linebackers to make a play around him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer thinks the Titans might be willing to trade away Tony Pollard in exchange for a fourth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Breer believes a fourth-round pick “seems like a lot” to give up for an aging running back who is set to enter free agency at the end of the year. So, Pollard might end up staying in Tennessee. Breer adds that the Titans could also consider trading away Calvin Ridley for a worse Day 3 pick, but he isn’t sure if the team is eager to get rid of pass catchers while they are attempting to develop their young quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard rushed 21 times for 117 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 8 loss to the Bengals, adding three receptions for 20 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard had his second-straight multi-touchdown game, scoring the first touchdown of the game on a 40-yard scamper with multiple missed tackles and a stiff-arm in the first quarter. With Tyjae Spears out, Pollard was the only Titans running back that got touches. He recovered his own fumble in the second half and added a one-yard score in the third quarter. He was also dropped for a safety in the third quarter on a head-scratching delayed hand-off to give the Bengals two points. Pollard enters the Titans’ Week 9 bye with several trade rumors swirling; if he is still in Tennessee, Pollard is a fantasy RB2 for Week 10.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: With two DNPs to start the week, Spears looks unlikely to play on Sunday. He also missed Week 7 with the knee issue. Tony Pollard racked up 28 touches and scored three rushing touchdowns. While we’re not banking on another multi-score outing anytime soon, his role alone is worth an RB2 ranking if Spears remains out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard had 25 rushes for 129 yards and three touchdowns in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns, adding three catches for 26 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard, whose last big game before Sunday was against these same Browns in 2025, scored two first quarter touchdowns against a Cleveland rush defense that seemed uninterested in tackling Pollard. He scored a third rushing touchdown in the fourth quarter, and could have had a fourth score if not for a Browns goal line stand. Pollard has seen big workloads with Tyjae Spears (knee) sidelined but hadn’t done much with the opportunity before Sunday. The Titans offense operated quickly, using no-huddle through much of the game. That created more play volume that benefited Pollard and the rest of the Titans offense. As long as Spears remains sidelined, Pollard should remain in 12-team lineups next week against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Titans declared RB Tyjae Spears, WR Calvin Ridley, RB Nick Singleton, TE Kylen Granson, T Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, DT Jackie Marshall, and CB Jaylon Jones inactive for Week 7 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: As Spears’ knee injury lingers, Tony Pollard continues to see a nice but ultimately meaningless workload in the Tennessee backfield. Pollard has seen at least 14 carries in every game since Week 2, though he only has eight receptions on the season. His lack of involvement in the pass game means Pollard will be a touchdown-dependent flex play in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard rushed 19 times for 76 yards in the Titans’ Week 6 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard was targeted only once, finishing without a reception. Pollard has somewhat surprisingly banished No. 2 Tyjae Spears to pure breather back status, but the Titans’ overall play volume and touchdown opportunities are so limited that he is still struggling to achieve weekly RB2 status. He has nevertheless shored up his RB3/FLEX floor. That is where you will find him in the Week 7 ranks against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard rushed 14 times for 52 yards in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard looks like he could be a legitimate NFL running back somewhere, but it sure can’t happen on this offense. He’s cleared 14 carries and 48 yards in each of his last four games and has just one touchdown to show for it. It’s fringe low-end RB2 land for Pollard, as usual, against the Colts next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (foot) is not on Tennessee’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard will take on the 0-4 Texans, who have had some trouble handling the run, and should be a viable low-end RB2 this week. He continues to get Wednesday vet days while dealing with this foot injury, but doesn’t seem to be in any real danger of missing time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (foot) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: During Weeks 3-4, Pollard took Wednesdays off, rehabbing an ankle injury. He would resume practicing on Thursday and suit up on Sunday. Now, with his new foot issue, he appears to be on the same practice plan. Expect him to play in Week 5 against the Texans. Pollard was a full participant on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: The Titans have given Pollard Wednesday off in back-to-back weeks. He was removed from the injury report entirely on Friday both times. This week should be no different. Pollard has 39 touches over the past two weeks. Even on a struggling Titans offense, that’s enough work to put him on the RB2/3 border for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins (calf) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Hollins is firmly in the questionable column with one practice left in Week 9. If active, he would be a boom-bust FLEX. The Patriots’ healthy wide receivers have played well in Hollins’ absence, though the team would probably like to get their field-stretcher back in action before long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Mack Hollins (calf) will return to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Hollins has been on injured reserve for a month with a calf injury. With a full practice today he’ll have a good chance of suiting up in Week 9 against the Packers. Hollins will likely function as Drake Maye’s primary downfield option if A.J. Brown remains sidelined. Hollins’ return dings the fantasy prospects of DeMario Douglas, who has an 18 percent target share and a 19 percent air yards share over the team’s past three games. Hollins will be flex viable in deeper formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Patriots place Mack Hollins on injured reserve with a calf injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: The Patriots snuck Hollins onto the injured reserve list over the weekend. He will be eligible to return after sitting out for four games. The Patriots also placed FB Reggie Gilliam on injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins (calf) will not play in New England’s Week 5 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: It sounds like Efton Chism, Kyle Williams, and Demario Douglas will all work more than usual next to Romeo Doubs in Week 5. Chism might be the most interesting FLEX play of the three after putting up 2/42/1 in relief of Hollins against the Patriots, though all of them have cases.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins (calf) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Normally a wind-sprinter and a blocking specialist, Hollins became shockingly important at work after A.J. Brown went on IR with an ankle injury. He currently leads the team in targets, tied with Romeo Doubs at 20 apiece. Hollins holds the lead outright in catches (15) and yards (209). His absence would free up downfield opportunities for Kyle Williams. Efton Chism and Demario Douglas would likely see an uptick in routes as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Hollins injured his calf in Week 4 and was listed as questionable to return. He immediately went to the locker room and did not return. Hollins is unlikely to play in Week 5. Romeo Doubs finally broke out last week with six catches for 58 yards and two scores. He will be in line for another sizable role once Hollins is ruled out. Kyle Williams will take on a starting role, though he is only worth a stash in deeper fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Speaking Monday, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel did not have an update on Mack Hollins’ calf injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Vrabel said he’ll have more information on Hollins shortly, but added that Hollins may miss a few days of practice. Hollins exited Week 4’s game against the Bills with a non-contact injury, leaving the field with a 3-53-0 line on four targerts. Hollins has seen 13 targets over the last two weeks while running the third-most routes (45) of any receiver. We’ll likely know more about the severity of his injury soon, but he could be at risk of missing Week 5’s game against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins is questionable to return with a calf injury
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Hollins went down when he cut to the sideline on an out route. He had to hobble off the field and was immediately taken into the locker room. The Patriots have not ruled him out yet, but we’d be surprised if he returned today. Romeo Doubs should continue to see the vast majority of targets. Hollins had 53 yards receiving on 3-of-4 targets before getting hurt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: Mack Hollins caught 6-of-9 targets for 87 yards in the Patriots’ Week 3 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Hollins looked the part of Drake Maye’s top option against Jacksonville, dominating air yards and easily leading all pass catchers in targets. Hollins manhandled much smaller Jaguars defensive backs throughout the game and nearly came down with a long play that would have put him over 100 yards on the day. Hollins, who had just two grabs last week against the Steelers, could have some flex viability in Week 4 against the Bills, especially if Maye and the Pats are once again chasing points in the second half.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports A.J. Brown (ankle) is expected to miss 6-8 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mack-holli.analysis: Schefter and other reporters previously called it a 4-6 week injury, which now seems unlikely. Schefter did add that Brown is moving “pretty well” and could come back on the faster side of his updated timeline. Still, it looks like Brown will miss at least half of the regular season. Romeo Doubs will operate as the team’s No. 1 receiver until he returns, though it will likely be a group effort to replace Browns’ production. Mack Hollins and Demario Douglas will also be more involved.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.headline: Rams OC Nate Scheelhaase wants to get Tutu Atwell more involved.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.analysis: Atwell earned four targets last week, catching two for 52 yards. Increasing his workload could only mean one or two more targets, so Atwell does not need to be quickly picked up in 12-team formats. For those struggling at the wide receiver position, Atwell simply enters the boom-bust FLEX conversation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.headline: Tutu Atwell caught 2-of-4 targets for 52 yards in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.analysis: Atwell made the biggest play of the day for the Rams, catching a perfectly placed 40 yard pass from Matthew Stafford. Atwell was second on the team in targets behind Puka Nacua, who had 12 targets on the day. Atwell should remain on waiver wires ahead of the Rams’ Week 9 game against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.headline: Rams declared WR Tutu Atwell, WR CJ Daniels, OL Bill Murray, TE Max Klare and QB Ty Simpson inactive for Week 1 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.analysis: The Rams acquired Atwell via trade in August. Although he already knows the system, coach Sean McVay evidently feels that Atwell is unnecessary for this one. Incumbent QB Stetson Bennett has officially defeated Simpson for the QB2 job. Simpson is inactive, but has been labeled the emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.headline: Rams acquired WR Tutu Atwell from the Dolphins in exchange for RB Jarquez Hunter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.analysis: Back with his old team, Atwell is highly unlikely to warrant FLEX treatment this season, but he provides the Rams with a speed element that the offense was somewhat lacking. The move also indicates that TE Terrance Ferguson will not be asked to stretch the field as much as he did last year, freeing him up for a potential breakout campaign. Last week, The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reported that Hunter has had a good training camp, showing “many of the rushing skills that had the Rams enamored enough to trade up and draft him in the fourth round last year.” He will likely compete for the No. 2 running back job in Miami.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.headline: Dolphins signed WR Tutu Atwell, formerly of the Rams, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.analysis: This will be Atwell’s first time playing for a team other than the Rams, who drafted him in the 2021 NFL Draft’s second round. Atwell spent time on injured reserve last season, dealing with a hamstring injury. Although he is unlikely to be a full-time, fantasy-relevant player with the Dolphins, his speed will help stretch the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.headline: Rams declared WR Tutu Atwell, CB Derion Kendrick, RB Jarquez Hunter, TE Nick Vannett, OL Beux Limmer, QB Stetson Bennette, and DE Larrell Murchison inactive for Sunday’s NFC Championship Game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.analysis: Atwell is again a healthy scratch for the playoffs. The Rams did not have a player listed on their final injury report for the week and enter a tough road environment at near full strength as they look to win their third conference championship game under Sean McVay.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.headline: Rams declared WR Tutu Atwell, CB Derion Kendrick, RB Jarquez Hunter, S Tanner Ingle, TE Nick Vannett and OT DJ Humphries inactive for the Divisional Round against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.analysis: Typically a valuable, role-playing field stretcher, Atwell just hasn’t been able to crack the Rams’ loaded skill corps rotation this season. Now 26 years old, it’s possible healthy-scratched Atwell has played his final game for the Rams as he heads to free agency this spring.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Tutu Atwell (hamstring) will be activated from injured reserve this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.analysis: Atwell has been back at practice for a few weeks and is finally ready to return to action. He will play a part-time role on offense unless something happens to Puka Nacua or Davante Adams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.headline: Rams WR Tutu Atwell (hamstring) will not be activated off injured reserve for Week 14 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.analysis: Atwell remains on injured reserve despite practicing fully for two weeks. The team evidently feels comfortable with their current wide receiver corps, and we can’t really blame them. Still, keeping Atwell’s downfield speed on injured reserve rather than wielding it on occasional shot plays is surprising. It remains to be seen whether he will return for Week 15 against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said he’d like to get Tutu Atwell (hamstring/IR) active “if that fits for the collective relative to the 48, there’s a lot of factors for that.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tutu-atwel.analysis: Atwell surprisingly carried no injury status for Week 13, but was not activated from injured reserve. Xavier Smith, who returns kicks, was up and managed a 3/83 day in Atwell’s absence. It doesn’t sound like the Rams are all that fussed about the $10 million Atwell getting back. He’s droppable in all but the deepest fantasy leagues based on this update.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh indicated that Omarion Hampton will get more touches.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Harbaugh reportedly made comments to this effect earlier in the week. When asked for his thoughts on the matter, OC Mike McDaniel said he is “excited about someone dictating the rotation” and added that Hampton has “had a really great week of prep.” Hampton hasn’t scored double-digit half-PPR points since Week 4. Whether the potential usage increase can get him back to 10.0-plus points remains to be seen, but this week’s comments are at least somewhat encouraging.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton had nine rushes for 20 yards in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams, adding two catches for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: It was business as usual for the plodding Hampton, who breaks no tackles and does nothing beyond what is blocked for him. Hampton, who now has less than 50 rushing yards in five games this season, was third in pass routes among LA running backs on the day and tied with Keaton Mitchell with three targets. Hampton’s role doesn’t offer much: Coming into Week 8, he ranked 31st among running backs in expected fantasy points per game (and 37th in actual fantasy points per game). With no ceiling of which to speak, Hampton should stay on benches in Week 9 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: The Athletic’s Noah Furtado reports the Chargers will try to “simplify” the team’s offense in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Justin Herbert and the flailing Chargers skill position players have appeared almost comically confused about all the pre-snap motion OC Mike McDaniel uses. That came through in the team’s embarrassing Week 6 loss to the Chiefs when players were bumping into each other during pre-snap motion calls from Herbert. Head coach Jim Harbaugh acknowledged the team is considering narrowing the offensive playbook during their bye week. “Definitely looking at volume and where you can make it to where the players can understand,” Harbaugh said when asked about how Chargers players were adjusting to McDaniel’s complex offense. The Chargers have used pre-snap motion on 74 percent of their snaps, the fourth highest rate in the NFL. Last year they used motion on 56 percent of their snaps. Hopefully these adjustments lead to some production for the NFL’s worst offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton had seven rushes for 18 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs, adding four catches for 21 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Hampton was his usual plodding self in this one, with a long rush of four yards in another depressing outing for the LA offense. Kimani Vidal, meanwhile had seven rushes for 21 yards and got much of his work in the first quarter. Keaton Mitchell had just two carries and did not catch his lone target. Hampton led the backfield in routes and targets on the day. His diminishing role and his lack of efficiency has made Hampton nothing more than a touchdown-dependent desperation flex option this year. The Chargers have a bye in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed 14 times for 33 yards in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Webster’s defines plodding as whatever this was. Hampton picked up a literal third of his yards on one 11-yard carry, and while much of the blame goes to the sheer lack of bodies on the offensive line, it was still mightily unimpressive. Hampton is at best a dart-throw FLEX for Week 6 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel said he has not lost “any faith” in Omarion Hampton.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: “I don’t see any change in terms of the depth chart at all. I felt I was underutilizing a strength,” McDaniel said about the increased usage of Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal. McDaniel’s statement is good for Hampton in the sense that we know Hampton will retain a reasonable role. And it’s bad because McDaniel is all but confirming the pecking order will remain the same. Expect more low-end RB2/FLEX nonsense from Hampton.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed nine times for 45 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Hampton’s late touchdown that still left the Chargers down by 10 in the middle of the fourth quarter is the only positive of the day. Los Angeles clearly isn’t enamored with the second-year tailback — or at the very best, is concerned about keeping him healthy — right now, and he was clearly in a timeshare again with Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal. He’s at best a FLEX play for Week 5 against the tough Denver defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed 15 times for 56 yards in a Week 3 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: The Chargers were missing two starting interior linemen and decided that running up the gut was not going to work for them. Understandably so. Hampton was held to just 3.7 yards per carry and didn’t seem to break any tackles in the interior of the Bills’ defensive line. Mike McDaniel decided to use Keaton Mitchell on the perimeter at the start of the game, but the Bills adjusted to take that away. At the end of the day, Hampton had 15 carries to Mitchell’s eight, but Hampton played 29 snaps, while Mitchell played 26 and ran a route on double the amount of dropbacks that Hampton did. This is a problematic timeshare in an offense that doesn’t look very good right now. Hampton remains a low-end RB2 who is touchdown dependent, which means he’s probably an RB3 next week against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed 23 times for 94 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 2 loss to the Raiders, adding two catches for 21 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Hampton was a workhorse in this game, picking up what was blocked but not much more. He had a solid outing going until late in the fourth quarter when Nakobe Dean knocked the football out of his hands and into the waiting arms of Jeremy Chinn. A lengthy return put the Raiders in scoring position and all but ended the game. Fantasy managers won’t be too bothered by the blunder today, but it could result in the team giving more work to Keaton Mitchell, who only touched the ball six times. Hampton will be near the top of the RB2 ranks for Week 3 versus the Bills despite seeing an RB1 workload today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton had 12 rushes for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 1 loss against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Hampton got away with it thanks to a first half touchdown plunge before the LA offense imploded following Ladd McConkey’s chest injury. Hampton was not targeted on 17 pass routes while Keaton Mitchell saw one target on 13 routes. Mitchell had four rushes on the day. Mike McDaniel’s offense collapsed immediately after the Bolts marched downfield on their first drive of the game, making it hard to tell exactly how Hampton (and Mitchell) will be used in neutral game script. That the Chargers were dominated by the Cardinals could be a bad sign for everyone in the Chargers offense, including Hampton. He’ll be a top-20 option next week against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.headline: Bears placed RB Zavier Scott (thumb) on injured reserve
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.analysis: Scott has not played on offense at all this season, but he has successfully carved out a role on special teams. According to the Chicago Tribune’s Brad Biggs, the Bears have reason to believe that Scott’s injured reserve stint “will be on the shorter side.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.headline: Bears signed RB Zavier Scott to their active roster from the practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.analysis: The Bears had run out of elevations with him, so had to sign him to the roster to have him active for Week 8. Scott has played 46 special teams snaps and 0 offensive snaps so far and does not need to be rostered for fantasy purposes. It’s hard to not read this as bad news about Kyle Monangai’s health in the short term, but we’re trying.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.headline: Vikings waived Zavier Scott.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.analysis: Scott signed his ERFA tender with Minnesota this offseason but was ultimately beaten out for the RB3 job by rookie Demond Claiborne. He is a candidate to sign with the Vikings practice squad after rosters settle. Claiborne is officially a name to know in deeper leagues, though he remains parked behind Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.headline: Vikings re-signed exclusive rights free agent Zavier Scott to a one-year deal.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.analysis: Scott managed a 32/114 line on the ground, adding 14 catches for 98 yards and a score on 16 targets, as Minnesota’s third-string back last year. He’s currently in line for the No. 2 role behind Jordan Mason with Aaron Jones expected to be released or traded. Scott probably doesn’t have much standalone fantasy value right now, but his first year certainly showed he has something to offer in the passing game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.headline: Vikings RB Jordan Mason (ankle) is not on the injury report for Week 18 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.analysis: Mason is in line to start this week with RB Aaron Jones (hip) having been ruled out. The Packers have already locked up a playoff spot. The Vikings are simply trying to get a better read on QB J.J. McCarthy. Mason is on the RB3/FLEX radar this week. He will likely cede passing down snaps to No. 3 RB Zavier Scott.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.headline: Vikings RB Jordan Mason (ankle) practiced fully on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.analysis: With RB Aaron Jones (hip) sidelined by a hip injury, Mason has a chance to start. Vikings No. 3 RB Zavier Scott would likely play in passing situations, if this is indeed, the case. Mason would be on the RB3/FLEX radar. The Vikings face the playoff-bound Packers in Week 18.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.headline: Aaron Jones (ankle) returned to the Vikings’ Week 16 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.analysis: Jones left in the first quarter with an ankle issue and was listed as questionable. Jordan Mason also suffered an ankle injury and was taken to the locker room on a cart. Assuming he remains out, Jones and Zavier Scott will split the backfield for the remainder of the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.headline: Aaron Jones (ankle) is questionable to return in Week 16 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.analysis: Jordan Mason left for the locker room with an ankle injury of his own. That leaves Zavier Scott as the only active running back on the Vikings’ roster. Fullback C.J. Ham will likely see an uptick in snaps as well. Scott will get three quarters of workhorse duties if both Mason and Jones remain out today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.headline: Aaron Jones is believed to be day-to-day after suffering a shoulder injury in Week 13’s loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.analysis: According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, Jones “is likely to be considered day-to-day” with his injury. Jones exited in the third quarter of Sunday’s shutout loss to the Seahawks and didn’t return to the field. The phrasing in Schefter’s report suggests the Vikings are still waiting to get a final word on Jones’ injury, but it sounds like he avoided the worst. If he is day-to-day, Jones will have a chance to suit up in Week 14 when the Vikings face the Commanders this week, but if he’s unable to go, we can expect Jordan Mason to step into a lead role with Zavier Scott likely working in on passing downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.headline: Zavier Scott had three rushes for 17 yards in the Vikings’ Week 13 loss against the Seahawks, adding one catch for four yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zavier-sco.analysis: Scott could see an increased role in Week 14 if Aaron Jones misses time with the shoulder injury he sustained in the second half of the team’s loss against Seattle. Jones has a history of shoulder ailments and was quickly pulled from the game. Jordan Mason would likely take over as the Vikings’ lead back, but it could be Scott who takes on the pass-catching tole with Jones sidelined. Scott had a six-catch game in Week 3 with Jones out. He should be picked up in deeper leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Kyler Murray (hamstring) “will be ‘week-to-week’ now.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: Murray reportedly experienced soreness in his hamstring following the Vikings’ Week 8 loss to the Lions. Carson Wentz will start for the Vikings’ Week 9 Monday Night Football game against the Bills, and potentially longer. If Wentz plays well, Murray could be relegated to the backup role. Murray does not necessarily need to be stashed on benches in two-quarterback leagues at this time. This situation is not ideal for him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Carson Wentz is “trending toward” starting in Week 9 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: Kyler Murray suffered a hamstring injury in Week 8, but even Schefter alluded to the idea that this would be a soft benching for Murray. Schefter added that it “looks like there’s a question at the quarterback position” for Minnesota. Healthy or not, it sounds like Wentz is going to be under center versus Buffalo. Wentz made one start earlier in the season while Murray was sidelined with a concussion. He only threw for 133 yards on 19 attempts, but Wentz found the end zone three times. Murray hasn’t thrown three passing touchdowns in a game since the end of the 2024 season. Wentz’s gunslinging style will likely be a win for fantasy managers hoping to get more out of Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, especially in a potential shootout with the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: The Athletic’s Ted Nguyen said Kyler Murray has been “constantly late on his reads,” leading to misfires.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: Nguyen studied Murray’s film in the Minnesota offense and noted the veteran is often late to recognize an open pass catcher. That could be related to Murray’s clear discomfort in Kevin O’Connell’s offense, as Nguyen noted. “When his first read doesn’t open up, he holds the ball and runs backward,” leading to drive-killing sacks. That’s exactly what unfolded a few times in high-leverage situations against the Lions in Week 8. Justin Jefferson on Sunday appeared frustrated by Kyler’s inability to make the proper reads on critical downs. All of this has an outsized impact on Murray’s fantasy prospects. He now ranks 31st among QBs in expected fantasy points per game, below Bo Nix and Daniel Jones.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said Kyler Murray is dealing with a sore hamstring and will undergo further evaluation.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: Murray appeared to be slowed a bit by an injury in Week 8’s loss to the Lions, so this news isn’t all too surprising. O’Connell said Murray will go “through a full eval” of everything to determine the severity of his injury, but didn’t suggest this will cost Murray any time as the Vikings prepare to face the Bills next Monday night. That said, we know how these types of injuries can linger and lead to some missed time, so we won’t jump to assume Murray is in the clear for Week 9. In the event he can’t go, Carson Wentz would be in line to draw the start against Buffalo.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Kyler Murray completed 17-of-29 attempts for 210 yards and two touchdowns in the Vikings’ Week 8 loss to the Lions, adding four rushes for 35 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: It was Murray’s best game as a Viking, and it came against a Detroit defense that was down a half dozen starters by the fourth quarter. Murray for once had a positive drop back EPA and eclipsed 200 passing yards for the third time this season in the run-heavy Minnesota offense. Murray’s best throw of the day came on a 51-yard bomb to Jordan Addison over double coverage. Murray has a couple well-times runs in high leverage situations too. His performance against the injury-riddled Lions secondary could be a good sign for Justin Jefferson and Addison going forward. They’ll face off against a vulnerable Buffalo secondary in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: The Athletic’s Alec Lewis believes Kyler Murray is still “acclimating to the [Vikings’] progression-based passing game.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: Minnesota’s offensive ineptitude has reached stunning levels in recent weeks, including last Sunday against the Colts, when Murray had 150 yards and a touchdown while completing 58 percent of his pass attempts. “We’ll continue to get better,” Murray said Sunday night. “I know we will. I know we keep saying that, but I felt like we moved the ball well (against the Colts). We’ve just got to put the ball in the end zone.” The Vikings, who rank 25th in pass rate over expected this season, have operated conservatively on offense while their defense dismantles opponents week in and week out. As Lewis pointed out, the 2026 Vikings are the first team in a century to win five straight games with five or fewer TDs over that span. Murray through Week 7 ranks 28th out of 40 qualifying QBs in EPA per pass attempt and 33rd in fantasy points per drop back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Kyler Murray completed 14-of-24 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ 16-10, Week 6 win over the Colts, adding five carries for 39 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: The story of the Vikings season has been a vaunted defense with a mediocre offense. That remained true in Week 7, with the Minnesota offense scoring just one touchdown on a Kyler Murray five-yard toss to T.J. Hockenson. Murray averaged 6.3 yards per attempt and struggled to connect with open receivers much of the day. He added 39 yards as a rusher, most of those coming on a 35-yard scamper prior to his passing touchdown. Murray came up limping after a second quarter play but did not miss any plays and finished the game. He threw an end zone interception in the second quarter, but the defender was ruled out of bounds. On the flip side, Murray nearly had Jauan Jennings for a long passing touchdown in the second quarter, but Jennings failed to haul it in. Murray is a high-variance fantasy quarterback due to his rushing upside, but his passing ability remains poor and caps his ceiling. He will be in the fantasy QB2 ranks for a soft Week 8 matchup against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Kyler Murray completed 24-of-30 passes for 229 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ 23-13, Week 5 win over the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: Murray was extremely active on the ground, addnig 51 yards on 10 rush attempts. His deep ball, on the other hand, remains a work in progress. His lone touchdown of the day came on a dime to Justin Jefferson on the back of the end zone. He was hesitant to even pull the trigger on deep shots at other times, even when his receiver was wide open. Murray is largely a game-manager right now, but that’s enough to win football games when the Minnesota defense is simply shutting down every opponent they face. Murray will be a mid-range QB2 when he returns to take on the Colts after a Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Kyler Murray completed 27-of-37 passes for 247 yards in the Vikings’ 15-10, Week 4 win over the Dolphins, adding six rushes for 16 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: The Dolphins’ pass rush made life tougher than expected for the Vikings’ signal caller. Murray managed to turn a few extended plays into successful scrambles, but he also took four sacks, at times simply holding the ball too long. As the game progressed, Murray locked in on T.J. Hockenson when the pass rush was closing in, linking up with him 13 times for 119 yards. The duo should have shared a late touchdown, but Hockenson smartly downed himself at the Dolphins’ five-yard line, so Murray could kneel out the clock from there. Murray will be a high-end QB2 against the Saints next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.headline: Kyler Murray completed 15-of-29 attempts for 168 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Vikings’ Week 3 win against the Bucs, adding two rushes for 17 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyler-murr.analysis: In his first action since sustaining a concussion in Week 1, Murray wasn’t asked to do much in this one. He was about four percent below his expected pass rate on the day with an average depth of target of 9.4 yards. Murray targeted Jordan Addison heavily after Justin Jefferson left the game with an ankle injury, connecting with Addison on a 41-yard score and narrowly missing the speedy downfield wideout for another touchdown. Murray took three sacks and avoided a handful of other sacks against a Tampa front seven missing key players. Murray likely won’t be a 12-team starting play in Week 4 against the Dolphins even if Jefferson suits up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-wentz/0.headline: Minnesota Vikings QB Carson Wentz will start in Week 2 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-wentz/0.analysis: Wentz played serviceably last week after starting QB Kyler Murray suffered a concussion. The Bears’ pass defense looks like a unit worth targeting in fantasy. https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-wentz/0.headline: Carson Wentz completed 12-of-19 passes for 133 yards and three touchdowns in the Vikings’ 39-22, Week 1 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-wentz/0.analysis: Kyler Murray took a brutal shot to the head in the first quarter and was quickly ruled out with a concussion. Wentz’s production came in fits and starts, but he did ultimately bring the Vikings back from a 12-point deficit. Minnesota’s defense then put the pressure on Jordan Love and forced back-to-back turnovers that gave Wentz the ball in the red zone. Jordan Mason scored a touchdown on the first drive and Wentz put an exclamation point on the day with a short touchdown toss to Jefferson on the second. Assuming Murray misses Week 2, Wentz will be in the QB2 mix for Superflex players. He faces a Bears defense that just gave up 37 points to the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grady-jarr.headline: Grady Jarrett (groin) did not practice in Wednesday’s walkthrough.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grady-jarr.headline: Bears declared DT Grady Jarrett, K Cairo Santos, LB Ruben Hyppolite II, G Luke Newman, LB Noah Sewell, WR Jahdae Walker, and QB Case Keenum inactive for Week 7 against the Saints.

With the weather making this likely to be a run-heavy game, Jarrett being out is a slight bump for Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grady-jarr.analysis: Rapoport notes Bears DT Grady Jarrett (knee) is also expected to play. Swift was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice before being downgraded to limited sessions on the following two days. The team then listed him as questionable. Swift told reporters after Friday’s practice that the limited days were simply maintenance. He has been dealing with a myriad of injuries this year but has yet to miss any time. Swift should get plenty of work as a home favorite versus the Saints this week, vaulting him up the RB2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grady-jarr.headline: Bears RB D’Andre Swift (hip) is active for Week 4 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grady-jarr.analysis: For the second straight week, Swift will suit up on game day after a trio of limited practice sessions. The Bears’ starting running back totaled 13 carries and three targets despite playing through a quad injury last week. He’s caught three passes in every game this season. Fantasy managers should expect 15 or so touches for him against the Raiders today. He’s a back-end RB2. The Bears declared CB Kyler Gordon, DT Grady Jarrett, LB TJ Edwards, RT Darnell Wright, TE Colston Loveland, DT Chris Williams and QB Case Keenum inactive for Week 4 against the Raiders. Loveland’s absence does not alter TE Cole Kmet’s projected workload enough to put Kmet on the TE1 radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grady-jarr.headline: Bears ruled out CB Jaylon Johnson (groin) for Week 3 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grady-jarr.analysis: It’s unclear why the Bears have not yet placed Johnson on injured reserve, but that could occur on Saturday. The star cornerback is expected to undergo surgery after suffering what is believed to be a season-ending groin injury. Bears slot CB Kyler Gordon, LB T.J. Edwards and backup CB Jaylon Jones are all sidelined by hamstring injuries. Bears DL Grady Jarrett (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3, but the Cowboys should be able to pass and run as they please against this depleted unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grady-jarr.headline: Bears DT Grady Jarrett (knee) is questionable for Chicago’s Week 2 game against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grady-jarr.analysis: Jarrett was able to get in a limited session on Friday after missing each of the first two practices of the week. Jarrett played 46 of the 56 snaps in Week 1 and will likely be dialed back a little even if he is active in Week 2. Andrew Billings and Chris Williams will pick up more slack against Detroit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grady-jarr.headline: Bears CB Kyler Gordon (hamstring) and DT Grady Jarrett (knee) were estimated non-participants in Wednesday’s walk-through practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grady-jarr.analysis: Gordon and Jarrett were the only non-participants for Chicago on Wednesday. Gordon has been rehabbing a hamstring strain since last month and missed Week 1. Meanwhile, Jarrett is dealing with a knee injury from Monday’s loss to the Vikings. Wednesday’s injury report is an estimate, so Bears fans can stay tuned later in the week to see if the defenders practice in time for Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grady-jarr.headline: Bears signed DT Grady Jarrett to a three-year, $43.5 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grady-jarr.analysis: $28.5 million of this is fully guaranteed at signing. It’s kind of surprising with this kind of market developing this quickly that the Falcons weren’t able to trade Jarrett, but it is understandable given how much they’re focusing on ignoring moving on from Kirk Cousins. Jarrett will slot in next to Gervon Dexter on the Bears interior, and Chicago has now spent heavily on their offensive and defensive lines this offseason in hopes of winning in the trenches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grady-jarr.headline: Falcons released DT Grady Jarrett.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grady-jarr.analysis: Jarrett, a two-time Pro Bowler, has spent his entire 10-year career with the Falcons. The veteran tackle was set to enter the final year of his deal, but the Falcons opted to release Garrett in a move that will save them $16.250 million against the cap in 2025. Jarrett, 32, totaled 53 tackles and 2.5 sacks while also putting up nine TFLs last season. After a torn ACL ended his 2023 campaign, he bounced back nicely in 2024 and should have a strong market as a free agent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/grady-jarr.headline: Troy Andersen (knee) was removed from the Falcons’ injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Saints.

The Falcons will have two of their top defenders in place against a Saints offense that has already lost Rashid Shaheed for the season and is expected to be without Chris Olave (concussion). Center Drew Dalman (ankle) is also questionable for Week 10 but was a full participant in Friday’s practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.headline: Seahawks signed Leonard Williams to a three-year, $90 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.analysis: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler was first on the news, followed by contract details from Ian Rapoport. Seattle acquired Williams from the Giants during the 2023 season. In his two full seasons as a Seahawk, Williams has totaled 18 regular season sacks plus one during the team’s postseason last year. He is now one of the five highest-paid defensive tackles on an annual basis. Williams will be under contract through the 2029 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.headline: Seahawks restructured Leonard Williams’ contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.analysis: According to Seahawks beat writer Corbin Smith, the team converted $18.745 million of Williams’ 2025 salary into a bonus while tacking on two void years to the end of his deal. The move freed up just over $14 million in cap space for the Seahawks, who will still need to make additional moves to get under the cap before the start of next season. Williams is coming off one of his best years as a pro after totaling 64 tackles, 11 sacks, and a career-high 16 TFLs in 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.headline: Seahawks EDGE Leonard Williams did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.analysis: Williams popped up on the practice report with a new foot injury, listed as a non-participant for Wednesday. https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.headline: Seahawks LB Boye Mafe (knee) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.analysis: Mafe led a lengthy injury report for the Seahawks front seven. LB Uchenna Nwosu (knee) remains out with an MCL sprain while LB Jerome Baker (hamstring) and DE Leonard Williams (knee) also did not participate in practice. It is still early in the week, but Mike Macdonald’s defense hopes to get back key contributors before Week 3 against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.headline: Seahawks agreed to terms with DT Leonard Williams on a three-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.analysis: Per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, the deal is worth $21.5 million per year. Williams was the Seahawks’ big move at the trade deadline. Though the team fell just short of making the playoffs, it wasn’t because the move didn’t work out. Williams racked up four sacks and nine TFLs in 10 games with the Seahawks. Those are solid numbers for any player, let alone an interior pass-rusher. Having already invested a second and a fifth-round pick to acquire Williams, there was no way the Seahawks were letting him walk in free agency just a few months later. He will now return to Seattle with defensive guru Mike Macdonald as his head coach.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.headline: Seahawks DT Leonard Williams (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/leonard-wi.analysis: Williams was acquired by Seattle at the trade deadline, playing in five games for the Seahawks. He was listed with a new ankle injury on Wednesday, not practicing to start the week. LB Jordyn Brooks (ankle), who left Week 13 early, also did not participate. Both Williams and Brooks are major contributors to the Seahawks defense and nursing ankle issues that could keep them out for Week 14 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reggie-vir.headline: Reggie Virgil (back) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reggie-vir.analysis: Virgil practiced fully after colliding with the goalpost in the Cardinals’ Week 8 win over the Cowboys. It’s a good sign that his back is not a major issue heading into the week. He’s in line to play in Week 9 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reggie-vir.headline: Reggie Virgil (undisclosed) was carted off after colliding with a goalpost in Arizona’s Week 8 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reggie-vir.analysis: Virgil was never officially listed on the injury report, but he was carted off. It was not a head-on collision with the post — our conjecture would be that it seemed to be a shoulder injury — but it didn’t look great and Virgil never returned. It was one of two targets Virgil collected.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reggie-vir.headline: Cardinals selected Texas Tech WR Reggie Virgil with the No. 143 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reggie-vir.analysis: Virgil (6’3/187) spent his first three seasons at Miami (Ohio) before transferring to Texas Tech in 2025. He earned second-eam All-MAC honors in 2024, posting a 41/816/9 receiving line and leading his team in receiving touchdowns. He posted a 57/705/6 receiving line after transferring, leading the Red Raiders in receptions. Virgil notably took both of his 2025 season rushing attempts for touchdowns. He recorded seven special teams tackles at Miami, a skill that could help him earn a spot on the active roster as a rookie.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: ESPN’s Rob Demovsky reports Josh Jacobs is “operating under the assumption” he won’t miss more games despite additional allegations of abuse against him.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Jacobs is facing additional allegations of verbal and physical abuse that could jeopardize his playing status moving forward. He told Demovsky that he is “operating under the assumption that he won’t have to sit out any more games than the six he already missed while on the NFL commissioner exempt list.” Jacobs has defended himself against the allegations after his attorneys also dismissed the claims. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said earlier this week he expects Jacobs to remain on the roster as the league reviews this round of allegations. Jacobs has missed six games on the Commissioner’s Exempt List and will continue to play while the NFL looks into the new claims.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said he expects Josh Jacobs to remain on the roster while the league investigates multiple allegations of domestic violence against him.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: This doesn’t come as much of a surprise, given that NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported on Sunday that Jacobs is “going to continue to play” while the league reviews this latest round of allegations. The league is not only reviewing these latest allegations, but is also looking into whether or not Jacobs was “upfront” with them about the initial allegations that led to him being placed on the Commissioner’s Exempt list. Barring an unexpected development this week, we would expect Jacobs to be on the field against the Patriots this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Josh Jacobs is “going to continue to play, but it is possible that he gets a suspension” at the end of the league’s investigation into several claims of domestic violence against him.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: A public records request revealed three additional accusations of domestic violence against Jacobs over the weekend. That is on top of the initial incident in which Jacobs ultimately pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property. The NFL put out a statement saying they will continue to look into Jacobs’ situation. Even though Jacobs was removed from the Commissioner’s Exempt List two weeks ago, the league’s investigation was still ongoing. Rapoport notes that the league is also looking into whether Jacobs was “upfront” with them about his disturbing legal situation. Of note, Jacobs’ team pushed to have video of the most recent incident sealed from public access while the league actively sought to have it released. Rapoport makes it sound like it may take some time for a suspension to be announced, but it’s more likely than not that Jacobs is suspended because of the most recent revelations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: NBC 26 Northeast Wisconsin reports “newly released records show additional women contacted the Hobart/Lawrence (Wisconsin) Police Department to report alleged physical incidents involving Josh Jacobs.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: The Wisconsin television station received “heavily redacted” police reports on Friday evening, though they included allegations from three other women. There are multiple extremely disturbing allegations of physical violence. One alleged incident took place in January 2022. The accuser “contacted investigators in June after learning about the May investigation, telling police the allegations sounded similar to her prior experience with Jacobs.” She also said the incident had “never been reported to law enforcement, (and that she) contacted police when she believed her alleged experience with Jacobs could be relevant to the case.” The allegations highlight the folly of the NFL’s apparent wish that the situation would just go away. It has not, and now it is quite possible, if not likely, that Jacobs ends up suspended for the remainder of the 2026 season. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Josh Jacobs rushed 21 times for 39 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 8 win over the Panthers, adding six catches for 13 yards and another score.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Jacobs’ fantasy game was salvaged with two scores, but the tailback didn’t look particularly spry in the process. He had a long gain of just six, and there was almost no burst even against the porous Panthers’ run defense. He was involved in the passing game, but again, outside of his four-yard receiving score, there really wasn’t much there. It’s clear this is Jacobs’ backfield despite the scuffles, as MarShawn Lloyd had just three touches in the contest for seven yards. He’s a volatile low-end RB1 candidate for Week 9 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Josh Jacobs rushed 11 times for 36 yards in the Packers’ Week 7 loss to the Lions, adding five receptions for 55 additional yards and one touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Jacobs saw 18 opportunities come his way in his return from the Commissioner’s Exempt List. He played on 35 offensive snaps compared to MarShawn Lloyd’s 22, but did little to solve the Packers’ woes in the run game. Jacobs managed a forgettable 36 yards on the ground on 11 carries, but was solid in the passing game. His biggest play came in the third quarter when he turned a short pass from Jordan Love upfield for a 25-yard touchdown, tightroping along the sidelines as he attempted to stay in bounds and reach the end zone. Head coach Matt LaFleur suggested Jacobs would be “limited” to about 30 plays in his first game of the season, but his 35 snaps are on par with the 36.8 snaps per game he averaged last season. We would certainly expect him to handle more of the rushing work in the weeks ahead, but this felt like a fairly normal day for Jacobs. He will be a fringe RB1/RB2 play next week against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Josh Jacobs is expected to get “a normal allotment of reps for a starter” in Week 7 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Packers OC Adam Stenavich told reporters Jacobs looked “great” in practice earlier this week, so we’re going to assume he’s in football shape and ready to go for Week 7. Given Garafolo’s reporting, Jacobs is already back on the RB1/2 border for a potential shootout with Detroit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Josh Jacobs is on track to play in Week 7 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: LaFleur said Jacobs’ Week 7 status depends on how he gets through Friday’s practice. The 28-year-old back has looked “great” in practice this week, per an earlier quote from OC Adam Stenavich, and seems to be trending toward a return after a six-week stay on the Commissioner’s Exempt List. At this point, we would be surprised if Jacobs didn’t play this week against the Lions, but it’s too early to assume he will see his normal workload in his first game back. Even if he doesn’t get a full assortment of touches, we would still expect Jacobs to get enough work to justify starting him at RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Packers OC Adam Stenavich said Josh Jacobs “will help for sure” and that he “looks great.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Matt LaFleur did not publicly commit to playing Jacobs ahead of Week 7’s date with the Lions, but his offensive coordinator — who also said he’d “provide a spark for our offense” — seemed to let the cat out of the bag that Jacobs will be involved in some way. Whether that’s a start or as part of a committee remains in some limbo, but we’d be surprised if Jacobs wasn’t involved in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said he is undecided on whether or not Josh Jacobs will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: LaFleur said Jacobs will log a full week of practice but also pointed out that the 28-year-old back has “missed the exposure to football” over the last several months while on the commissioner’s exempt list. Jacobs was reinstated by the league late last week and is eligible to play immediately, but whether or not he will be active next week is to be determined. We’ll see how this week unfolds, but it would be a bit surprising if Jacobs was inactive in a pivotal NFC North matcup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/art-maulet/000.headline: Arthur Maulet retired after nine seasons in the NFL.
https://www.nbcsports.com/art-maulet/000.analysis: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports that Maulet is retiring. The 33-year-old slot cornerback began his career with the Saints and Colts and ended it with the Lions, but made the bulk of his impact from 2019-2024 with the Jets, Steelers, and Ravens. Maulet made major noise as a hard-hitting cornerback in the AFC North, going from the Steelers to the Ravens in 2023 and starting a playoff game for Mike Macdonald’s historic Ravens defense. He retires with five career interceptions and five sacks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/art-maulet/000.headline: Texans signed CB Arthur Maulet to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/art-maulet/000.analysis: Maulet was released by the Ravens in March before landing in Houston on a one-year contract. He was held to just three appearances in 2024 due to multiple knee injuries and a calf injury, requiring two trips to injured reserve, but looked spry in workout videos released earlier Monday on X. Maulet should serve in a reserve role behind established starters Derek Stingley, Kamari Lassiter, and Jalen Pitre.

https://www.nbcsports.com/art-maulet/000.headline: Ravens released CB Arthur Maulet.
https://www.nbcsports.com/art-maulet/000.analysis: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports the Ravens are planning to release Maulet after an injury-riddled 2024. He had a strong 2023 as the Ravens’ slot corner, re-signing with the team last offseason. However, he hit injured reserve to begin the 2024 season and played just three games. The 31-year-old will look for a new home as a rotational defensive back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/art-maulet/000.headline: Ravens CB Nate Wiggins (shoulder/illness) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/art-maulet/000.analysis: Ravens CB Arthur Maulet (neck) will also play in Week 9. Starter CB Marlon Humphrey (knee) was limited all week and is now labeled as questionable. Backup Jalyn Armour-Davis (knee) was a healthy participant on Wednesday and Thursday but showed up on the Friday injury report as a DNP. He is also questionable to play in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/art-maulet/000.headline: Ravens activated CB Arthur Maulet from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/art-maulet/000.analysis: Maulet has played between 348 and 481 defensive snaps for each of the last five seasons with the Jets, Steelers, and Ravens. He’ll be a nice depth piece for Baltimore’s secondary, and perhaps elevate into an even bigger role if Marlon Humphrey’s MNF knee injury is serious.

https://www.nbcsports.com/art-maulet/000.headline: Ravens agreed to terms with CB Arthur Maulet on a two-year deal.
https://www.nbcsports.com/art-maulet/000.analysis: Maulet initially joined the Ravens on a one-year deal prior to the 2023 season. He thrived in a nickel role for the Ravens’ top defense, notching two sacks, five tackles for loss and an interception. Maulet now returns on a two-year deal for a Ravens defense that lost much personnel, including defensive coordinator Mike Macdonald. Expect Maulet to return to a nickel role under new defensive coordinator Zach Orr.

https://www.nbcsports.com/art-maulet/000.headline: The Athletic’s Jeff Zrebiec reports Ravens CB Ar’Darius Washington (chest) was placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/art-maulet/000.analysis: Washington was Baltimore’s starting slot CB for the first two weeks of the season. He joined the Ravens as a 2021 UDFA and earned a big role after the preseason injury to Marlon Humphrey, but now Baltimore’s secondary is even thinner. CB Arthur Maulet is likely next man up. C Sam Mustipher was signed to the 53-man roster in a corresponding move.

https://www.nbcsports.com/art-maulet/000.headline: Ravens signed CB Art Maulet, formerly of the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/art-maulet/000.analysis: The Ravens have undergone somewhat of a secondary transformation as their once formidable depth chart has aged. Maulet should compete for a depth role primarily as the nickel corner in Baltimore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/art-maulet/000.headline: Steelers released CB Art Maulet.
https://www.nbcsports.com/art-maulet/000.analysis: Maulet, whose played the past two seasons in Pittsburgh, has three interceptions over six NFL seasons. In 2022, he set a career high with 59 tackles for the Steelers, including two tackles for a loss. Maulet will likely sign with another team before training camps start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/art-maulet/000.headline: Steelers re-signed CB Art Maulet to a two-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/art-maulet/000.analysis: Maulet will turn 29 this summer and joined the Steelers last season after spending a couple years with the Jets. He played 35% of the Steelers’ defensive snaps as a nickel corner and will again compete for that job this upcoming campaign.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adrian-mar.headline: Seahawks signed QB Adrian Martinez to the practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adrian-mar.analysis: Martinez has bounced around the 49ers and Jets in the NFL, while winning MVP in the UFL in 2024. He worked out for the Ravens earlier this week but now joins the Seahawks as depth with Sam Darnold (quad) banged up and set to miss Week 9 against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adrian-mar.headline: Ravens worked out QB Adrian Martinez, formerly of the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adrian-mar.analysis: Martinez, who played four seasons at Nebraska and one at Kansas State in college, was the UFL MVP in 2024. He’s had stints with the Jets and 49ers, appearing in one NFL game. The Ravens are shoring up their QB room after Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) went down in Week 8. The Ravens on Tuesday signed journeyman QB Kedon Slovis.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adrian-mar.headline: Jets signed QB Adrian Martinez, formerly of the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adrian-mar.analysis: Martinez already spent time on both the Jets and 49ers’ rosters this year. Jets QB Tyrod Taylor (groin) and QB Justin Fields (knee) were unable to practice on Wednesday. Martinez’s return provides the team with a backup option behind QB Brady Cook for the Jets’ Week 15 game against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adrian-mar.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Adrian Martinez will be the backup to Mac Jones in Week 3 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adrian-mar.analysis: This means Brock Purdy will be inactive, as expected. Kyle Shanahan put on a brave face and floated the idea of Purdy being the backup earlier this week, but that was a lie even Shanny himself couldn’t believe. Purdy will stay on the bench for another week as he nurses toe and shoulder injuries. He is reportedly eying a Week 4 return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adrian-mar.headline: 49ers signed WR Russell Gage Jr. to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adrian-mar.analysis: The 49ers bolster their wide receiver depth with availability concerns swirling around Brandon Aiyuk (knee), Jauan Jennings (calf, contract) and Demarcus Robinson (suspension). Gage should not be expected to return flex value in Week 1. The 49ers also released S Richie Grant, while QB Adrian Martinez, RB Sincere McCormick and WR Marquez Valdes-Scantling were signed to the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adrian-mar.headline: Jets waived QB Adrian Martinez.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adrian-mar.analysis: Martinez is a practice squad candidate, but the Jets may choose to go with Brady Cook as the third quarterback behind Josh Fields and Tyrod Taylor. New York also waived LB Jamin Davis, DE Michael Fletcher, T Liam Forandel, T Samuel Jackson, TE Zach Kuntz, DB Tanner McCalister and RB Lawrance Toafili.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adrian-mar.headline: Lions signed Nebraska QB Adrian Martinez.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adrian-mar.analysis: A former four-year starter at Nebraska, Martinez (6’2/221) transferred to Kansas State for his final season and turned in a solid 2022 campaign for the Wildcats. Martinez’s athleticism (9.46 RAS) jumps off the tape and is undeniably the best part of his game. With 2,928 rushing yards and 45 touchdowns for his career, Martinez’s pro day 40-time of 4.55 all but confirmed the speed and athleticism we’ve witnessed over the last several years. His athleticism allows him to make plays off script and evade pursuing tacklers to extend plays, but his already inconsistent accuracy falls apart on the run. If the quarterback thing doesn’t work out for Martinez, a switch to receiver could extend his stay in the NFL. An exciting player with the ball in his hands whose size would complement such a switch, Martinez is the kind of athlete teams should want to develop.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adrian-mar.headline: Kansas State senior QB Adrian Martinez (shoulder) is back throwing passes in training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adrian-mar.analysis: Martinez (6-foot-2, 212-pounds) missed all of spring practice after undergoing surgery on his throwing shoulder, so it’s great to see him out there throwing passes in drills as summer camp opened. The all-time Nebraska leader in total offense has accrued 10,792 total yards over his four-year career. When asked about how Martinez is looking, HC Chris Klieman said “[He’s] been really sharp. He’s done a nice job, he continues to learn what we’re doing. He’s continuing to absorb more and more of the playbook and feeling more and more comfortable with the offensive scheme. We’re seeing some really, really good things throwing the ball, running the ball and getting us in the right play.” Martinez is on track to start in KSU’s season opener against South Dakota.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adrian-mar.headline: Kansas State redshirt junior QB Adrian Martinez spoke about why he left Nebraska.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adrian-mar.analysis: After a 3-9 season with the Huskers, there are a number of reasons why Martinez (6'2"/212) might have wanted to move on. The biggest one for him: winning. “The narratives I’m fighting against, well, I haven’t been to a bowl game and I haven’t had a winning season,” Martinez spoke candidly. “I play quarterback and often times you get associated with those kinds of things and I want to win.” Outside of a couple of seasons in the 2000’s, that’s been par for the course in Lincoln and Martinez experienced that for four seasons. He projects to be the starter in Manhattan, where the Wildcats have had a winning record in 10 of the last 13 seasons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adrian-mar.headline: Kansas State redshirt junior QB Adrian Martinez will begin throwing in May.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adrian-mar.analysis: Kansas State head coach Chris Klieman announced Martinez (6'2"/212) will not be throwing in spring practice as he recovers from off-season shoulder surgery. He said his quarterback will participate in other parts of practice, including footwork drills and mental reps, but throwing is off-limits until May. After four years at Nebraska, Martinez became one of the big-name QBs that entered the transfer portal and will enter his first season at K-State. If there are no setbacks, he should be the starter in September.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (back) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie played through a groin injury in Week 8 and seemingly picked up a new back injury during the game. Rams head coach Sean McVay said McDuffie will be a DNP Wednesday, indicating the 26-year-old’s back issue is more than a minor flare-up. It’s possible he is getting the day off to rest the groin and back injuries, but Rams fans should keep an eye on his practice status the rest of the week. It’s safe to say McDuffie is truly questionable for Week 9 against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said he did not have an official update on Trent McDuffie (back), adding, “he looks like he’s feeling OK.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie missed Weeks 6-7 with a groin injury that he suffered in practice. He played through a questionable tag this week after three straight limited practices. Until we get an official update, McDuffie should probably be considered questionable to play in Week 9 against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (groin) is questionable for Week 8 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie has missed the previous two games as he tends to a groin injury suffered ahead of Week 6. He made it back to the practice field this week but was unable to prove healthy enough to avoid the questionable designation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (groin) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: This is McDuffie’s first practice since he injured his groin during a Week 6 practice. He will be limited on the official injury report. Rams LB Nate Landman (concussion) will be listed as a full participant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Rams declared CB Trent McDuffie, QB Ty Simpson, LB Nate Landman, OL Bill Murray, OL Keagan Trost and TE Max Klare inactive for Week 7 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie injured his groin during a Week 6 practice. The Rams have listed him as questionable to play despite the fact that he has not yet resumed practicing. He was playing extremely well prior to the injury. His loss is consequential.
