The Rams elevated LB Eric Kendricks and CB Cam Lampkin to the active roster for today’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (groin) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie has not practiced since straining his groin in Week 6’s Thursday practice. Labeling him as questionable to play seems like a formality before a game-day inactive listing, but only the Rams’ staffers know for sure. The Rams ruled out LB Nate Landman (concussion). Practice squad LB Eric Kendricks will be promoted to the active roster for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (groin) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie, the Rams’ No. 1 cornerback, and LB Nate Landman (concussion) were both sidelined today. Both players are on the wrong side of questionable for the Rams’ Week 7 game against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (groin) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie injured his groin during last Thursday’s practice and did not play in Week 6 against the Cardinals. He starts out this week not practicing, putting him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 7. Also not practicing was LB Nate Landman (concussion). The Rams defense continues to lose players to injury; the Raiders face this defense in Week 7 and could see more fruitful fantasy performances than usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Rams declared CB Trent McDuffie, WR CJ Daniels, WR Tutu Atwell, QB Ty Simpson, DL Larrell Murchison and OL Bill Murray inactive for Week 6 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie injured his groin during Thursday’s practice and was unable to participate on Friday. Losing their top cornerback may not cost them the game, but it certainly makes it easier for Cardinals pass catchers to produce fantasy points. The Rams also activated OL Keagan Trost from injured reserve and promoted CB Cam Lampkin from the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (groin) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie reportedly injured his groin during Thursday’s practice, and is now questionable to play. Frankly, the Rams can probably get by without their No. 1 cornerback this week, though obviously it would be preferable to have him out there. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle played through a questionable tag with this injury last week, catching 3-of-6 targets for 39 yards and one touchdown against the Chiefs. He apparently made it through the contest without re-injuring himself and can be started as a WR3 this week against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle caught 3-of-6 targets for 39 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 8 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Starting with the positive, Waddle found the end zone for the second time this year and got going over the middle of the field with a 35-yard missile from Nix early in the second quarter. It’s his longest catch since Week 2, when he erupted for 138 yards on eight receptions, including a 49-yarder. On the downside, Waddle managed a pedestrian 19 percent target share and finished third on the team in receiving. He found the end zone and still scored a grand total of 12.9 PPR points. The Broncos’ offense is still a work in progress, even if today was a step in the right direction. Waddle will get another week in the WR3 mix when the Broncos take on the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (shoulder) is active for Week 8 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Left tackle Garrett Boles and EDGE Zach Allen are also active. All Broncos players who were questionable for Week 8 are active. After a disappointing two months to start the year, Waddle is at the back of the WR3 ranks for Week 8. Inactive for the Broncos are S Talana Hufanga, QB Sam Ehlinger, OL Gavin Ortega, DL Jordan Jackson, DL Tyler Oneydim, OL Kage Casey, and TE Dallen Bentley.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jaylen Waddle (chest) is “trending toward playing” in Week 8 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle suffered the chest injury late in the Broncos’ Week 7 win over the Cardinals and a doomed trick play. He was leveled by Josh Sweat several yards behind the line of scrimmage. The Broncos held him out of Wednesday’s practice before giving him two limited sessions and a questionable tag. Though we suspect he is on some form of a snap count, it looks like Waddle is giving it a go. Already struggling to put up WR3 fantasy numbers, we’re regarding him as a high-risk FLEX play versus Kansas City.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) is questionable for Denver’s Week 8 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle got in two limited sessions after missing practice on Wednesday. It feels like he’s on the optimistic side of questionable given the trend line, though of course you would have preferred to see a full session somewhere in here. It’s also possible he winds up on a snap count, so we’ll see if any insiders dig up anything on that this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle aggravated an existing chest injury on a trick play late in the fourth quarter of Week 7. A return to the practice field, in any capacity, Thursday keeps the door open for him to be available to play the Chiefs in Week 8, although fantasy managers are likely looking for an excuse to bench the over-hyped receiver. It would be prudent to look at other viable options in a difficult matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Earlier today, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that Waddle’s status for Week 8 against the Chiefs has not been determined. The Broncos’ No. 1 wide receiver aggravated his preexisting chest injury in Week 7 against the Cardinals. Backup plans should be made at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Jaylen Waddle suffered a chest injury and his Week 8 status has not been determined.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle left Sunday’s game against the Cardinals with the chest injury. It was, according to Rapoport, an “aggravation of his previous chest injury.” Waddle could try to practice later this week, but would appear to be iffy unless he can log a practice session by Friday. If Waddle is sidelined this week against the Chiefs, Courtland Sutton would likely see more targets and become an interesting flex option against a tough KC secondary. Sutton over the past four weeks leads Denver in air yards and has the second most targets behind Waddle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle left Week 7’s game against the Cardinals with an apparent chest injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Up by 14, Sean Payton dialed up a trick play for Waddle, giving him a pitch as Waddle came across the formation. Waddle bobbled the ball and was clobbered by Josh Sweat. He writhed in pain while holding his left shoulder. Trainers came onto the field and eventually walked him into the locker room. With less than four minutes on the clock at the time of his departure, we don’t expect to see him again today. Waddle’s day ends with four catches for 48 yards on seven targets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) is not on the Broncos’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle upgraded to full on Friday after logging two limited sessions to begin the week. The Broncos’ No. 1 wide receiver has struggled to deliver usable stat lines with Bo Nix intent on checking down. The Cardinals’ pass defense could facilitate a bounce-back game for Waddle, but he remains a WR3/FLEX at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cody-white.headline: Raiders released WR Cody White.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cody-white.analysis: Tight end Carter Runyon was activated from injured reserve in a corresponding move. White has eight catches for 112 yards and three scores this year. He also contributes on special teams. The Raiders could ultimately sign him to their practice squad and promote him to the game-day roster this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cody-white.headline: Raiders WR Jalen Nailor (concussion) did not participate in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cody-white.analysis: Nailor will almost assuredly sit out the Raiders’ Week 5 game against the Patriots. Fellow WR Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) is practicing in full, and WR Cody White (ankle) remains limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cody-white.headline: Raiders WR Jalen Nailor (concussion) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cody-white.analysis: Nailor suffered a concussion against the Chiefs in Week 4 and starts out the week not practicing. This indicates he is on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5 against the Patriots. Fellow WR Cody White (ankle) was limited as well, though Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) returned to practice, giving the Raiders some reinforcement with Nailor still in concussion protocol.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cody-white.headline: Raiders placed WR Jack Bech (forearm) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cody-white.analysis: He’ll miss at least the next four weeks. Bech had five catches for 48 yards and a touchdown in the first two weeks of the season, but played just 11 snaps in Week 3 before fracturing his forearm. The Raiders signed Cody White — he of the three touchdowns in the last two weeks — to the active roster as his replacement.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cody-white.headline: Cody White caught 1-of-3 targets for four yards and one touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 3 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cody-white.analysis: White has likely earned himself a roster spot with three touchdowns in two weeks. He scored via an in-breaking route on the Raiders’ eighth possession, operating as the apparent checkdown in the progression. He is not yet worth stashing, but take note of his productivity.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cody-white.headline: Cody White caught both of his targets for 24 yards and two touchdowns in the Raiders’ Week 2 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cody-white.analysis: White last caught multiple passes in a game in Week 9 of the 2024 season. He had only done that three times throughout his five-year career before today. White got on the board in the third quarter with a hard-fought grab in the end zone. His second score was much easier. The Chargers simply forgot to cover him on a play-action pass in the red zone, resulting in the easiest of his three career scores. White only ran seven routes in this game and is primarily a special teamer. He isn’t a viable fantasy option for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cody-white.headline: Seahawks re-signed WR Cody White.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cody-white.analysis: White appeared in 10 games for the Seahawks last year. He caught three passes for 90 yards and a touchdown. With Jake Bobo also under contract for the 2026 season, most of White’s reps will come on special teams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cody-white.headline: Seahawks released CB Shaquill Griffin.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cody-white.analysis: Griffin was immediately signed to the Seahawks’ practice squad. The team signed wide receiver Cody White from their practice squad to the active roster in a corresponding move. They made the opposite pair of moves last week. This is what peak roster management looks like.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cody-white.headline: Seahawks CB Devon Witherspoon (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cody-white.analysis: Seahawks S Julian Love (groin) was also downgraded to a non-participant after practicing in a limited capacity on Wednesday. Fellow Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (ankle) was recently placed on injured reserve. With the secondary in such rough shape, the Seahawks signed CB Shaquill Griffin from the practice squad. The team correspondingly released WR Cody White before immediately signing him to the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cody-white.headline: Seahawks WR Jake Bobo (concussion) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cody-white.analysis: Bobo entered concussion protocol after the Seahawks’ final preseason game. He is still working his way back, but a limited practice indicates he has a chance to play Week 1. Also limited at wide receiver were Cody White (shoulder) and Dareke Young (hamstring), while Tory Horton (ankle) was a full participant and is on track to play against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis (groin) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis did the same during Week 8 practices and ended up running just once against the Patriots. Hopefully, the groin injury continues to improve and his rushing usage returns. Willis remains a QB2 this week against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 21-of-32 passes for 211 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in the Dolphins’ 19-24, Week 8 loss to the Patriots, adding one rush for two yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis practiced in full this week despite being listed with a groin injury. Perhaps the soft tissue issue made him play a little more restrained than we would have liked him to. The Dolphins’ quarterback continues to hold the ball too long. He took five sacks today. His interception was not totally his fault. He was hit by a pass rusher, altering the pass’s trajectory, which bounced off a defensive lineman’s helmet before flying 29 yards downfield, where a Patriots defender picked it off. Willis had another interception called back due to defensive offsides, which was lucky. The Dolphins’ young wide receivers are learning the ropes and could help him churn out usable fantasy line as the season progresses. Willis will be a high-end QB2 against the Lions in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis (groin) is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: While we are happy to see Willis practicing in full, we are slightly unhappy to see that he has a new injury. The Dolphins’ quarterback has already dealt with toe and right thumb injuries this season. Willis remains a viable QB2 starter against the Patriots, but this is worth monitoring.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 14-of-21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns in the Dolphins’ 28-28, Week 7 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis also added 37 yards and a touchdown on eight rush attempts. It was, by far, his best performance as a Dolphin. It was also the first win for both Willis and first-year head coach Jeff Hafley. Willis picked apart the Jets for chunk play after chunk play. His biggest play of the day was a 63-yard completion to Caleb Douglas, though nearly all of those yards came after the catch. He had already connected with Douglas earlier in the game for his first touchdown of the day. Things will be a lot tougher for Willis and the Miami offense when they take on the Patriots next week. Despite the strong showing today, Willis will remain buried in the QB2 ranks for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis (right thumb) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: ESPN’s Marcel Louis-Jacques reports that Willis received treatment for his thumb injury on his right, throwing hand, though he did not share what exactly the injury is. Hopefully, it is nothing serious. If his ball placement is impacted, the Jets’ D/ST would benefit. Willis is a volatile QB2 against them this week. Willis underwent surgery on his left thumb in August 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Malik “is our quarterback.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: “Malik needs to be better, but that’s not the headline -- we all need to be better ... everything in the pass game has to be better.. It’s the receivers, it’s the tight ends, it’s the protection,” Hafley continued. Willis is by all statistical measures one of the weakest quarterbacks in the league with his arm, but at least he’s skimping some superflex QB2 value with his legs. There’s not much reason for the Dolphins to bench him either way, as they have nobody they pressingly need to evaluate. Willis should return after the Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 15-of-27 passes for 137 yards, one touchdown, two interceptions and a fumble in the Dolphins’ 31-24, Week 5 loss to the Bengals, adding eight rushes for 74 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis had a poor passing day, finishing the first quarter completing 0-of-4 passes. He threw a pair of second quarter interceptions to Jordan Battle, the first coming off a tip and the second on a cross-body throw and poor decision. He also fumbled and recovered a snap in the two-minute drill while a potential third interception was dropped in the endzone in the second half. Willis recovered with a touchdown throw to Kevin Coleman in the fourth quarter but fumbled deep in the Dolphins’ own territory late in the game. He capped off his day with a quick goal-line rushing score at the end of the game but it was too little, too late. Between his decision-making and lack of ball security, Willis had a poor game but good fantasy production due to his rushing output. Willis is a fantasy QB2 heading into a Week 6 Dolphins bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 9-of-17 passes for 85 yards in the Dolphins’ 10-15, Week 4 loss to the Vikings, adding two rushes for 11 yards and one fumble lost.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis’ biggest plays of the day are the ones that didn’t count. Willis rolled out of the pocket, escaping pressure, on the Dolphins’ third drive and hit Chris Bell downfield for what could have been a 68-yard touchdown. Unfortunately, the officials determined that the tiniest edge of Bell’s right cleat grazed the sideline pre-catch, during the scramble drill, negating the play altogether. Heartbreaking. Willis also had a 10-yard scramble called back due to holding on the Dolphins’ fifth drive. He attempted a running fadeaway pass 25 yards downfield to Bell on 3rd-and-8 on the Dolphins’ ninth drive, but the catch was contested and ultimately fell incomplete. He is a QB2 against the Bengals next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said increasing Malik Willis’ designed run rate will be discussed game by game, “when we need him to.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Hafley’s full quote is fairly non-committal. The first-year head coach was asked whether Willis could receive more designed rushes with De’Von Achane (knee) out for the year. Hafley said the game planning in that regard will “go game by game,” and be employed “situationally when we need him to.” For those hoping that Willis will consistently be involved in the run game, those outings could come, but the occurrences could be volatile. Willis remains a QB2 at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 20-of-36 passes for 210 yards and an interception in the Dolphins’ 24-10, Week 3 loss to the Dolphins, adding nine carries for 56 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis also lost a fumble late in the second quarter. Willis made some of his best throws of the season this afternoon, though the two turnovers were also his first of the year. He also missed impressive rookie Chris Bell on what could have been a pair long-ish touchdowns. He was at least running more after combining for just eight carries between Weeks 1 and 2. That is going to remain a must, especially now with De’Von Achane being waylaid with a serious knee injury. That will further change the face of this undermanned offense, and make things even harder for Willis in this no-win setup. Despite his intriguing young wideouts, he will be difficult to trust as a superflex option vs. the Vikings’ blitz-happy defense in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/caleb-downs/00.headline: Caleb Downs (concussion/ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/caleb-downs/00.analysis: The Cowboys’ rookie safety and slot defensive back is very banged up. He is firmly on the wrong side of questionable for Week 9 against the Colts at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/caleb-downs/00.headline: Cowboys signed No. 11 overall pick S Caleb Downs to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/caleb-downs/00.analysis: Downs is expected to be an immediate starter for a Cowboys defense that ranked 32nd in points allowed last season, while also allowing the highest yards per attempt. Downs is a versatile defender who excelled in both pass coverage and against the run while at Ohio State. He is one of six Cowboys to ink their rookie deals, with pass rusher Malachi Lawrence the only one yet to put pen to paper.

https://www.nbcsports.com/caleb-downs/00.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Eagles WR Makai Lemon was “definitely” in the mix for the Rams at pick No. 13.
https://www.nbcsports.com/caleb-downs/00.analysis: Per Fowler, Jets TE Kenyon Sadiq “was also believed to be part of the Rams’ first-round conversation at some point,” along with Cowboys S Caleb Downs. Both the former USC wide receiver and the former Oregon tight end were available when the Rams were on the clock. The former Ohio State safety was taken two picks earlier. The Rams are slated to pick 29th in Rounds 2 and 3 today. Given their interest in Lemon, a slot/Z-receiver, and Sadiq, a receiving tight end, it would be unsurprising to see them draft a pass catcher today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/caleb-downs/00.headline: Cowboys traded up with the Dolphins to select S Caleb Downs at No. 11 overall in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/caleb-downs/00.analysis: Downs will join one of the NFL’s worst coverage units in Dallas. The Cowboys in 2025 allowed the league’s third highest drop back EPA and the second highest drop back success rate, regularly getting carved up by opposing quarterbacks. Caleb Downs (6’0/206) enters the 2026 NFL Draft cycle with one of the most bankable defensive résumés in the class, pairing elite coverage metrics with high-level run support and professional tackling technique. He allowed just 9 completions on 20 targets (45.0%) for 72 yards with 0 TDs allowed, 2 INT, and a staggering 7.0 passer rating allowed, making him one of the most efficient safeties in college football. His versatility is reflected in his 365 coverage snaps, where he aligned deep, rotated into the slot, and triggered downhill against the run, posting 6 run stops, 11 havoc plays and an 83.7 run defense grade. Downs’ diagnostic skills show up in the tape and the data (89.6 cover grade) as he consistently undercuts intermediate routes and rarely bites on play-action, allowing only 0.22 yards per coverage snap. Physically, he’s not a height/length outlier, but his short-area burst, clean feet, and immediate trigger allow him to win both in space and in traffic. Downs’ value comes from certainty, he’s a plug-and-play NFL starter with Pro Bowl floor traits and one of the safest defensive evaluations this class has to offer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/caleb-downs/00.headline: FOX Sports’ Ralph Vacchiano reports that Commanders head coach Dan Quinn is a big fan of Ohio State LB Sonny Styles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/caleb-downs/00.analysis: Vacchiano adds that the team knows they need a wide receiver and “did a lot of work on” Ohio State WR Carnell Tate. Both players took top-30 visits with the Commanders and are viewed as potential top-10 picks. The pick could simply come down to which player is on the board when the team picks at No. 7 overall. The Commanders focused on improving the pass defense in free agency, but they could still benefit from adding a player like Styles. Vacchiano notes, Ohio State S Caleb Downs “might be in the mix, too.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/caleb-downs/00.headline: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan believes that Giants head coach John Harbaugh “is going to want to” draft Notre Dame RB Jeremiyah Love if he is available with the No. 5 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/caleb-downs/00.analysis: Giants general manager Joe Schoen views Love as “an offensive weapon,” not just as a running back, so he may not disagree with Harbaugh in this scenario. That said, Raanan reminds viewers that Harbaugh is ultimately “running the show” in New York. The Giants are also interested in Ohio State LB Sonny Styles and Ohio State S Caleb Downs. Per Raanan, trading back into the Nos. 6-10 range before drafting Downs might be the “perfect scenario” for the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/caleb-downs/00.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said he “would not be surprised” if the Commanders draft the best defender available with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/caleb-downs/00.analysis: Rapoport cautioned viewers, saying he is not making any predictions, before listing Ohio State S Caleb Downs, Ohio State LB Sonny Styles and Miami EDGE Rueben Bain Jr. as potential options. An ESPN report from earlier this month indicated the Commanders are focused on improving the pass defense this year. Adding any of the three players listed above would go a long way toward that end.

https://www.nbcsports.com/caleb-downs/00.headline: NFL Network’s Daniel Jeremiah believes Ohio State WR Carnell Tate, LB Arvell Reese and LB Sonny Styles could be drafted in the 2026 NFL Draft’s top-10 picks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/caleb-downs/00.analysis: Jeremiah also thinks Ohio State S Caleb Downs’ odds of being drafted in the top 10 are greater than 50.0 percent. He adds that Ohio State DT Kayden McDonald will be drafted between picks 25 and 35. Jeremiah’s colleague, Ian Rapoport, said last week that he believes Tate will be drafted in the top 15. Sounds like his stock is ticking upward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/caleb-downs/00.headline: Ohio State S Caleb Downs declared for the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/caleb-downs/00.analysis: Downs began his college career at Alabama in 2023. He transferred to Ohio State the following season and helped the Buckeyes win the 2024 College Football Playoff Championship. In 2023, he was a second-team All-American, the SEC Freshman of the Year and first-team All-SEC. In both 2024 and 2025, Downs was a Unanimous All-American, the Big Ten Defensive Back of the Year and earned first-team All-Big Ten honors. In 2025 alone, he won the Lott Trophy and Jim Thorpe Award. The Athletic’s James Boyd notes Downs is Colts WR Josh Downs’ younger brother and “is widely considered to be a potential top-10 pick.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/caleb-downs/00.headline: Alabama received a verbal commitment from 2023 five-star S Caleb Downs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/caleb-downs/00.analysis: Downs (6'0"/185) is ranked as the 12th player in the class, and is the top safety. He chose Bama over hometown Georgia, Ohio State, Notre Dame and Clemson. Athleticism, intelligence, size, agility, pursuit, coverage, he checks all the boxes. Downs work ethic and leadership also standout. He’s the brother of star UNC WR Josh, and both his uncle and father made it to the NFL. He racked up 77 tackles, one sack, 11 PBU’s and an incredible five picks in 2021. Physical traits, mental traits, pedigree, production, Downs has it all, which makes it no surprise he’s the top ranked safety in the class.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wat.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Jaylen Watson will undergo season-ending shoulder surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wat.analysis: This is an unfortunate loss. Watson is the Rams’ No. 2 perimeter cornerback, and No. 1 cornerback Trent McDuffie has been slowed by a groin injury in recent weeks. Watson signed a three-year, $51 million contract with the Rams this offseason. Hopefully, Watson makes a full recovery in time for next season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wat.headline: Aaron Donald (back) practiced in full on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wat.analysis: This is a good sign for Donald. Meanwhile, CB Jaylen Watson (shoulder) remained limited and star S Quentin Lake (hip) remained sidelined. Watson starts in the No. 2 perimeter cornerback role, while Lake serves as the primary nickel cornerback and part-time safety. Missing either player would be notable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wat.headline: Aaron Donald (back) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wat.analysis: The Rams face the Bills in Week 5’s Monday Night Football game, so this is Los Angeles’ first practice. Donald is on track to play, though the team could be cautious with his return. Rams CB Jaylen Watson (shoulder) will also be limited today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wat.headline: Rams agreed to terms with CB Jaylen Watson, formerly of the Rams, on a three-year, $51 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wat.analysis: $34 million of it is guaranteed per Mike Garafolo. The Rams now have two of Kansas City’s three main cornerbacks from the 2025 season. Watson had a career-best 74.1 PFF defense grade for the Chiefs in 2025, but Kansas City almost never retains cornerbacks and prefers to keep churning the roster with youth. Watson figures to be one of Los Angeles’ main outside corners in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wat.headline: The Athletic’s Jesse Newell believes CB Jaylen Watson is “likely to be out of the Chiefs’ price range” this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wat.analysis: Watson is a former seventh-rounder who has started 21 games for the Chiefs over the last two seasons. The 27-year-old corner is expected to be one of the top available free agents on the market next month, and allowed just 35 catches for 447 scoreless yards on 59 targets last season, per PFF. Watson has played exclusively on the outside since entering the league in 2022 and hasn’t allowed a receiving touchdown since 2023.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wat.headline: Chiefs placed CB Trent McDuffie (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wat.analysis: Fellow cornerback Jaylen Watson is joining him on injured reserve. With nothing left to play for, the Chiefs are packing it in for the year. McDuffie leads the team in pass breakups at six. Watson is one behind him. Down their top two corners, Kansas City will be an easy target for Bo Nix this week. Fantasy managers can feel free to fire Nix up as a QB1 one last time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wat.headline: Chiefs CB Trent McDuffie (knee) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wat.analysis: McDuffie is listed as DNP for the second straight day. He has been dealing with the knee issue since Week 14 and may not play the rest of this season with the Chiefs eliminated from playoff contention. Fellow CB Jaylen Watson (groin) was also DNP for the second straight day. Both are on the wrong side of questionable with a Christmas game against the Broncos on the horizon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wat.headline: Chiefs activated CB Jaylen Watson (ankle) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wat.analysis: After practicing in full this week, Watson is good to go for Kansas City’s Divisional Round matchup with the Texans. Watson played nearly every snap of the Chiefs’ first five games before going down with the ankle injury. He had six pass breakups and 21 total tackles through six appearances. Watson’s return will bolster an already-strong Kansas City defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wat.headline: Chiefs CB Jaylen Watson (ankle/IR) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wat.analysis: Watson injured his ankle in Week 7’s win over the 49ers, and the Chiefs struggled to find decent cornerback play next to Trent McDuffie in his stead. Watson had a 74.2 PFF coverage grade in 221 coverage snaps this season. Andy Reid said he was “in good shape” and said “he has a chance of playing” earlier today. The full practice would certainly seem to suggest he has a good chance of being active on Saturday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wat.headline: Chiefs designated CB Jaylen Watson for return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wat.analysis: According to Fox Sports’ Jordan Schultz, Watson will practice on Friday with the team and may return in time for the start of the Chiefs’ postseason. The third-year corner suffered a broken fibula in late October and was believed to be lost for the season. Now on the mend, the Chiefs will get a major boost to their secondary if Watson is able to return. Before suffering his injury, Watson had allowed just 15 receptions for 192 scoreless yards on 28 targets in six games while earning a PFF coverage grade of 74.2. The Chiefs already have a bye during the Wild Card round of the playoffs, meaning Watson wouldn’t return until the weekend of January 18th, giving him more than two weeks to practice and continue healing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kentavius-.headline: Bears placed Kentavius Street on injured reserve with a knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kentavius-.analysis: The Bears’ backup defensive tackle suffered a knee injury in Week 8 against the Seahawks. Whether he has a chance to return this season has not yet been reported. The Bears also signed TE Stephen Carlson to the active roster and DL Earnest Brown to the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kentavius-.headline: Bears agreed to terms with DL Kentavius Street, formerly of the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kentavius-.analysis: Street has spent the past three seasons as a rotational pass rusher for the Falcons. He notched three tackles for loss, including two sacks, in seven games last season. The Bears add Street for depth on the defensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kentavius-.headline: Falcons DL Kentavius Street (shoulder) is out for the rest of Week 14 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kentavius-.analysis: Street left in the third quarter against the Buccaneers with an apparent shoulder injury. The Falcons’ defensive line was already banged up, but now loses Street for the game as well. The injuries are piling up in the trenches for the Falcons with multiple offensive and defensive lineman missing Week 14.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kentavius-.headline: Falcons acquired Kentavius Street and a 2025 seventh-round pick from the Eagles in exchange for a conditional 2024 sixth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kentavius-.analysis: The Falcons lost Grady Jarrett to a torn ACL and will now look to replace him — at least to some degree — with Street. This may not be the last move the Falcons make before the trade deadline, as they’ve also been rumored to be in on Commanders EDGE rusher Montez Sweat. Street has played in eight games for the Eagles this season, totaling two tackles on the year. He tallied a career-high 3.5 sacks in 2022 with the Saints and should be a serviceable pass rusher alongside Calais Campbell. The conditional sixth-round pick is contingent on Street playing at least six games for the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kentavius-.headline: Eagles signed DL Kentavius Street, formerly of the Saints, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kentavius-.analysis: Street started out with the 49ers before becoming a Saint last offseason. He’s played in all 17 games in each of the last two years for the 49ers and Saints, adding 6.5 sacks as a rotational lineman. Street should be part of the plan to replace Javon Hargrave for the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kentavius-.headline: Saints signed DT Kentavius Street.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kentavius-.analysis: Street was a restricted free agent not tendered an offer by the 49ers. Although in theory he offers some pass-rushing upside, Street was too frequently washed out in San Francisco. He earned poor marks across the board from Pro Football Focus. Turning 26 in May, Street will be working with a strong defensive coach in Dennis Allen. The Saints’ aggressive scheme could put him in advantageous pass-rushing spots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kentavius-.headline: 49ers did not tender restricted free agent Kentavius Street, making him a free agent.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kentavius-.analysis: The 49ers selected Street in the fourth round of the 2018 draft, and he emerged in 2021 as a decent pass rusher, recording 19 tackles, three sacks, four hits, and 12 hurries. Street played in all 20 of the 49ers games, including the playoffs. He also played on Special Teams in kick blocking packages. Entering his age-26 season, Street is likely to find another home as a rotational lineman and Special Teams contributor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kentavius-.headline: 49ers placed DT Kentavius Street (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kentavius-.analysis: The 49ers activated LB Kwon Alexander (pec) off injured reserve in a corresponding roster move. Street recorded four tackles in three games this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kentavius-.headline: 49ers activated LB Kwon Alexander (pec) off injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kentavius-.analysis: The team placed DT Kentavius Street (knee) on injured reserve in a corresponding roster move. Alexander’s return to the lineup is great news for the defense’s chances of slowing down Dalvin Cook and company. The 49ers quietly allowed at least 100 rushing yards in 12-of-16 games this season. Alexander’s presence is also bad news for Kyle Rudolph and company. The 49ers boast the type of freaky-athletic LBs in Alexander (PFF’s No. 9 LB in coverage) and Fred Warner (No. 11) to force Kirk Cousins to have to work outside the numbers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kentavius-.headline: 49ers activated DL Kentavius Street (knee) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kentavius-.analysis: Street was selected in the fourth round of the 2018 draft, but has yet to play a regular season snap. The 49ers placed DL D.J. Jones on the injured reserve in a corresponding roster move.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-conn.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said James Conner (ankle) will not return from injured reserve this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-conn.analysis: LaFleur could only say the team was taking things “week to week” when asked if Conner will play this year. It sounds like the veteran running back may ultimately miss the entire season. With Jeremiyah Love on IR, Tyler Allgeier will handle the bulk of the backfield touches versus Seattle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-conn.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said James Conner could “potentially” return this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-conn.analysis: Conner has been on injured reserve all season while continuing to work his way back from the brutal foot/ankle injury he suffered last season. If he does return, Conner will join a fairly crowded backfield and would be nearly impossible to trust in fantasy as long as Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier are both healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-conn.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said it’s still not “the right time” for James Conner (ankle) to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-conn.analysis: Same goes for TE Tip Reiman (ankle). LaFleur said he does not check in with the medical staff about them “on the daily,” but he “knows they’re doing well.” Neither player needs to be rostered in 12-team formats. Conner may be fantasy-relevant later in the year, but a lot would have to go wrong beforehand for that to be the case.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-conn.headline: Cardinals placed James Conner on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-conn.analysis: Conner will miss at least four games to start the year as he continues to work his way back from the ankle injury that ended his 2025 season. The team can designate him to return after Week 4. With Jeremiyah Love also banged up, Tyler Allgeier could be in for a hefty workload early in the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-conn.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said it’s “too early to tell” if James Conner (ankle) will play in Week 1.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-conn.analysis: Conner suffered a season-ending ankle injury early in the 2025 season. He avoided the PUP list to start training camp but has yet to participate in 11-on-11 drills. With the season nearly two weeks away, it certainly doesn’t look like Conner will be available for Week 1. Trey Benson is on injured reserve and Jeremiyah Love is on the mend with an ankle issue of his own. It’s possible Tyler Allgeier earns a three-down role to open the season, making him a priority target for ZeroRB drafters.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-conn.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said there’s no timeline for James Conner (ankle) to return to 11-on-11 work.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-conn.analysis: It doesn’t sound like Conner has a great chance of being available for Week 1, and if he’s not yet able to fully practice it’s certainly on the table for Conner to start the year on injured reserve or the reserve/PUP list. Conner took a paycut this offseason and is due $2.35 million guaranteed in 2026 after suffering a season-ending injury in Week 3 last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-conn.headline: ESPN’s Josh Weinfuss projects the Cardinals to keep four running backs on their 53-player roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-conn.analysis: The four running backs are Jeremiyah Love, Tyler Allgeier, James Conner, Trey Benson. Given the recent draft capital and financial investments in Love and Allgeier, those two are obviously locks to make the final squad. Conner, 31, and Benson, 24, seem like reasonable trade candidates. Both players’ seasons ended prematurely due to injury. Conner has one year left on his deal. Benson has two. Love should take over the starting role soon enough, but perhaps the RB2 battle could take a while to sort through. Weinfuss believes “Conner and Benson won’t roll over easily and give their jobs away.” If they do indeed keep four running backs, and one player were to miss time, this might make for a tough waiver wire read.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-conn.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano writes, “it feels like one of the Cardinals’ six RBs has to go.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-conn.analysis: Graziano could only be referring to James Conner and Trey Benson. He noted that Conner took a pay cut this offseason, which could signal that he’s still in the Cardinals’ plans, making a Benson deal potentially more likely. That seems unlikely, though, considering Arizona brought in Tyler Allgeier and Jeremiyah Love this offseason. Conner is still working off to the side with trainers at practice as he recovers from ankle surgery, but if he can return to the practice field soon then a trade could be in his future. Graziano mentioned the Bengals and Giants as teams that could be looking for running back help.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-conn.headline: Cardinals RB James Conner (ankle) was seen working with trainers at organized team activities on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-conn.analysis: Conner suffered a season-ending ankle injury in Week 3 last year. Earlier this offseason, he agreed to a revised contract that pays him $2.35 million this year. The Cardinals signed RB Tyler Allgeier to a two-year, $12.25 million deal one day later, before spending the No. 3 overall pick on former Notre Dame RB Jeremiyah Love. If Conner can resume practicing soon, it might increase the odds of a running back-needy team acquiring him via trade.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-conn.headline: Cardinals selected RB Jeremiyah Love with the No. 3 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-conn.analysis: Love will enter a crowded backfield alongside trusted veteran James Conner and free agent signing Tyler Allgeier. Love’s draft capital and his standout ability will give him a good shot at taking on lead back duties to start the 2026 season, though Allgeier and Conner will be involved. Love will be running behind one of the NFL’s worst offensive lines. A two-year starter for the Fighting Irish, 21-year-old (in May) Love (6’0/212) was without peer in this year’s running back draft class. Totaling 40 touchdowns in 28 games over the past two seasons, Love’s explosiveness is unmatched. His 52.9 percent breakaway rate in 2025 ranked No. 1 in the power four conferences, while his average 4.50 yards after contact trailed only one player nationally. Those fancy stats underscore a rare blend of vision, burst and contact balance. Although Love is indeed a home run hitter, he’s also a complete offensive weapon. His final year in South Bend saw him add to his ground statistics with 27 receptions for 280 yards and three scores, posting a superb 1.83 yards per route run. It was production that stressed linebackers in space. Love’s overall elusiveness spike from 2024 to 2025 reflects a runner who not only dodges the first hit but finishes with authority, combining lateral twitch with downhill violence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-ada.headline: Cardinals designated Isaiah Adams (ankle) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-ada.analysis: The Cardinals’ offensive line has been slowed by injuries this season. Adams’ return is good news. It is unclear whether he will be able to play this week, but he will be back within 21 days at the very least.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-ada.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Isaiah Adams (ankle) will not play in Week 5 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-ada.analysis: Jon Gaines will take his spot at right guard. Gaines drew the start in Week 1 while Adams was sidelined with a knee injury, so it’s not a major shakeup for the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-ada.headline: Cardinals declared CB Garrett Williams, QB Carson Beck, OL Josh Fryar, WR Reggie Virgil and DL Andrew Billings inactive for Week 2 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-ada.analysis: Williams is not yet ready to return from his season-ending Achilles tendon rupture. On the plus side, DT Roy Lopez (groin) will play this week, and RG Isaiah Adams (knee) will make his 2026 debut. Beck will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the division rival Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-ada.headline: Cardinals CB Garrett Williams (Achilles) will not play in Week 1 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-ada.analysis: The Cardinals will also be without S Dadrion Taylor-Demerson (ribs) and RG Isaiah Adams (knee). Williams is working his way back from a torn Achilles he suffered in Week 16 of last season. He was able to avoid the PUP list to start the season and has been a limited participant in practice all week, but head coach Mike LaFleur is opting to give him at least one more week of rest before putting him on the field. We’ll see if he’s able to suit up in Week 2 when the Cardinals play host to the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-ada.headline: Cardinals guard Isaiah Adams is facing charges for possessing a weapon by crime, possessing a restricted or prohibited firearm without a license, possessing a loaded firearm, and possessing a prohibited device.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-ada.analysis: Adams turned himself in to Toronto police on Sunday. Per ESPN’s Josh Weinfuss, he is still expected to report to training camp. Adams was expected to compete for a starting job at right guard this summer, but the off-field concerns could see him shuffled to the bench for the start of the season. A 2024 third-round pick, Adams made 11 starts in 2025 and five starts as a rookie.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-ada.headline: Cardinals OG Isaiah Adams exited Week 10 against the Jets with a back injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-ada.analysis: The backups offensive lineman is now questionable to return. While his absence may not immediately be felt, it could be an issue if the Cardinals’ line thins out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-ada.headline: Cardinals selected Illinois OG Isaiah Adams with the No. 71 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-ada.analysis: After joining Illinois out of JUCO, Adams (6'4/315) immediately slid into the lineup as the starting left guard and became a fixture there, recording 962 snaps with a team-leading 120.5 knockdowns while earning the second-highest PFF run-blocking grade among Big Ten guards (80.2) in 2022. For the first time in school history, Illinois was named a semi-finalist for the coveted Joe Moore Award, which is given to the best offensive line in the country each year. Signs were pointing up heading into 2023, with Adams looking like a brick wall at LG for the first two games against Toledo and Kansas, posting 83rd+ percentile pass block grades with zero pressures. Adams (6’042/315) performed every drill and test available at the combine, showing above average in every rubric with the exception of his 24.5-inch vertical and 22 bench reps being the only substandard tests he performed. Adams doesn’t move with a burst or lateral fluidity, which can expose his average quickness when playing tackle against freaky Big Ten edge rushers. When he’s locked inside at guard and just has to take on defenders within his space, he looks far more natural and is very difficult for even the most brutish three-techs to overpower when engaged.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: David Montgomery (groin) will not play in Week 9 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Per head coach DeMeco Ryans, Montgomery remains week-to-week. He did not practice today and we assume he won’t get on the field in any capacity this week. Woody Marks will make another start. Facing a down-horrific Chargers squad, Marks should finally get going after two underwhelming starts in Montgomery’s absence. He is a locked-in RB2 for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: David Montgomery (groin) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Montgomery could still need more time to recover from his Week 5 groin injury. Woody Marks should be expected to start against the Chargers this weekend, at this time. Montgomery technically still has a chance to resume practicing this week, but today likely would have served as the first ramp-up session if he had a good chance of playing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans did not have an update on David Montgomery’s groin injury when speaking with the media on Monday
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Montgomery, who missed the Texans’ last two games with his injury, is coming off the team’s Week 8 bye, and there was some hope he might be able to get on the field for Week 9’s game against the Chargers. While that may still be the case, it’s possible we will need to wait until Wednesday, when the team releases its first injury report, to see how Montgomery is trending heading into the weekend. The 29-year-old running back has struggled mightily this season even when healthy, rushing for 138 yards and two touchdowns on 52 carries while averaging a dismal 2.7 YPC. Even if he is active against the Chargers, Montgomery would be hard to trust as anything more than an RB3/Flex play given his performance pre-injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports David Montgomery (groin) will not play in Week 7 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: This will be the second game in a row that Montgomery has missed due to the groin injury he suffered in Week 5. Woody Marks, who totaled 17 touches in last week’s win over the Jaguars will again lead the Texans’ backfield. He has averaged 18.0 touches per game over the last two weeks and will be a volume-based RB2 with a chance at significant upside. Safeties Jalen Pitre (AC joint) and S Reed Blankenship (concussion) will also miss this week’s game against the Giants, putting the Texans down a handful of starters with one game left before their Week 8 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports that David Montgomery (groin) is not expected to play in Week 7 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Like we said yesterday, Montgomery is still seemingly in the week-to-week camp. Woody Marks and Dare Ogunbowale will likely split backfield touches this week. The Texans used both Marks and Jawhar Jordan last week, but Jordan suffered an injured reserve-worthy injury. Marks should be in starting lineups, but he may be more of a FLEX than a reliable RB2. Ogunbowale is a low-floor PPR dart throw.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: David Montgomery (groin) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: We were told early last week that Montgomery is week-to-week. Today’s absence suggests he is still week-to-week and will likely be ruled out again on Friday, though we do not know that for sure. We will provide an update before then if his status changes. In the meantime, Woody Marks will get the start again this week, potentially with less touch competition. Jawhar Jordan totaled 50 yards and a touchdown on seven total touches last week, but was surprisingly placed on injured reserve today. Dare Ogunbowale remains a receiving factor, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: Texans ruled out David Montgomery (groin) for Week 6 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: We already knew that Montgomery was considered week-to-week, so this is unsurprising. Woody Marks will start for however long Montgomery is sidelined. The Jaguars field one of the NFL’s best run defenses, but Marks ceded just one snap to Dare Ogunbowale last week. Theoretically, he should remain in a near-full-time role, elevating him to the RB2/FLEX tier despite the tough matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said David Montgomery will be week-to-week with the groin injury he suffered in Week 5 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Ryans said Woody Marks “will carry the load” for the team while Montgomery is sidelined. It’s been a tough start to the season for Montgomery, who scored three times in Week 1 but has been locked out of the end zone ever since while averaging a career-low 3.5 yards per touch. Marks has been slightly more efficient than Montgomery this season, but the Texans’ running game as a whole has left much to be desired. Marks’ expected workload makes him worth a waiver wire claim where available, but fantasy managers shouldn’t expect anything more than RB3 levels of production at this time. The Texans will take on the Jaguars in London in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said David Montgomery (groin) may miss “some time.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: It sounds like Montgomery is in danger of missing both the Jaguars and Giants games before Houston’s Week 8 bye, assuming this is just a mild injury. Woody Marks will take over as Houston’s lead back for the time being and could be in for sizable role given how no other back received a snap or touch once Montgomery went down in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: David Montgomery (groin) will not return to Houston’s Week 5 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: He finishes with five carries for 11 yards. Initially questionable to return in the second quarter, Montgomery was ruled out after halftime. This could open some major space for Woody Marks to have a strong role going forward. We’ll keep an eye out for updates after the game, but it doesn’t look good for Montgomery.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Ravens S Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) will not play in Week 9 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Cornerback Nate Wiggins is questionable with an illness. He did not practice today. Hawkins missed Week 8 with the knee issue and wasn’t able to practice once this week. The Ravens play on Thursday this week and then get an extended break until Monday of Week 10, when they’ll take on the Chargers. The extra time off might help Hawkins get back on the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) is out for Week 8 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Hawkins was unable to practice all week as he tends to a knee injury, ultimately ruled out for Week 8 Friday. It will go down as his second consecutive absence, with his next opportunity to take the field to come in Week 9 against the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) missed practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Hawkins was absent for the second consecutive day, requiring some level of participation Friday to avoid a designation for the team’s showdown against the Bills in Week 8. The team got good news on other fronts as Lamar Jackson, Ioane Vega, Kyle Hamilton, and Roquan Smith were all present Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Kyle Hamilton (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Neither did fellow Ravens safety Jaylinn Hawkins, who is also dealing with a knee injury. Ravens coach Jesse Minter said a few of his players were dealing with “after game type things” when asked about Hamilton, so it doesn’t sound like this is a major issue. Still, with multiple members of the secondary banged up, this is a situation to monitor throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Ravens agreed to terms with S Jaylinn Hawkins, formerly of the Patriots, on a two-year, $10 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Hawkins signed with the Pats as a backup two years ago. He was elevated to a starting role in 2025 and put some of his best play on tape. Hawkins totaled six pass breakups, four interceptions, and 1.5 sacks across 15 games. He will likely serve as Jesse Minter’s third safety in Baltimore’s new defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Patriots released S Jabrill Peppers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Peppers has $4.32 million in guaranteed money remaining on his contract for this season. The 29-year-old safety started 26 games over the last three seasons with the Patriots. New England could be looking to start Jaylinn Hawkins and rookie Craig Woodson now, according to ESPN’s Mike Reiss.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Patriots re-signed S Jaylinn Hawkins to a one-year, $2.25 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Hawkins will handle backup safety duties while primarily contributing on special teams. He earned a 69.5 PFF special teams grade last year, though he does not return punts nor kicks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Chargers claimed S Jaylinn Hawkins off waivers from the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Hawkins was primarily a special teams contributor for Atlanta to start the season. He saw a handful of defensive snaps in each of his first three games but has only played on defense one time in the past three weeks. Per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, the Chargers were not the only team to put in a claim on Hawkins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: The Falcons waived S Jaylinn Hawkins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Hawkins was a 2020 fourth-round pick by the Falcons, starting 16 games in 2022. He has four career interceptions and was in the last year of his rookie contract, but Hawkins has now been cut loose by Atlanta.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.headline: Falcons placed rookie S Jaylinn Hawkins on the reserve/COVID list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylinn-ha.analysis: Hawkins (6'0/208) was a highly recruited wide receiver in high school but transitioned to Cal’s secondary after a redshirt year. He was a three-year starter and earned an All-Pac 12 honorable mention as a redshirt senior. He has racked up 10 interceptions over the last three seasons, but he is a below-average tackler and makes too many gambles for a free safety. Hawkins was a projected undrafted free agent and The Athletic’s Dane Brugler’s 30th ranked safety in the 2020 NFL Draft.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-mck.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports that Tanner McKee will not start in Week 9 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-mck.analysis: Joe Milton will start for the Eagles against the Giants this week. McKee’s time under center lasted three games. Unfortunately, he never once threw for more than 215 yards or threw multiple touchdowns. McKee can be dropped in two-quarterback leagues. Milton is a volatile QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-mck.headline: Nick Sirianni said “Tanner (McKee) is our guy” when asked about the team’s quarterback situation.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-mck.analysis: Speaking to media Monday following the team’s sixth consecutive loss, Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni expressed confidence in his 26 year old quarterback, saying, “Tanner is out guy.” He was asked directly if he was considering a change at quarterback following McKee’s third straight loss, quickly putting those rumors to rest. McKee appears to be the team’s starting quarterback, at least in the immediate future, as they limp past the half way point of the regular season with a Week 9 meeting against the division rival Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-mck.headline: Tanner McKee completed 23-of-34 passes for 212 yards and one interception in the Eagles’ 27-10, Week 8 loss to the Commanders, adding 25 yards on four carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-mck.analysis: The Eagles scored the first 10 points of the game as they looked to be in control early. Things quickly went south following numerous mental mistakes, penalties, and poor execution, eventually leading to the Commanders scoring 27 straight to send Philadelphia to their sixth consecutive loss. The Eagles continue to have no downfield ability while playing through mounting injuries, with their longest play of the game coming on the final play from scrimmage on a meaningless down. That leaves very little room for error with things like penalties, drops, and sacks, all of which were present in Week 8. McKee and the Eagles limp into another divisional matchup in Week 9 against the Giants, where McKee will carry negligible fantasy value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-mck.headline: Tanner McKee completed 23-of-35 passes for 211 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Eagles’ 38-21, Week 7 loss to the Cowboys, adding one yard on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-mck.analysis: McKee looked to be comfortable in the pocket to start but things quickly unravelled, with the veteran backup unable to improve upon a 21-yard completion to rookie Makai Lemon in the first quarter as he remained incapable of attacking downfield. Lemon would also be the recipient of McKee’s lone touchdown toss, marking the second consecutive start with just one touchdown pass in relief of Jalen Hurts. The offense looked far more functional while Saquon Barkley was on the field, but the veteran back was in and out of the lineup from the second quarter through the fourth, before ultimately being deemed questionable to return and missing the final frame. The Eagles drop their fifth straight for the first time since 2016 as they fall further behind the Giants for the division lead. McKee is not worth rostering ahead of a Week 8 divisional tilt against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-mck.headline: Tanner McKee completed 26-of-45 passes for 215 yards and one touchdown in the Eagles’ 25-14 Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-mck.analysis: The very first play of the game was a play-action pass where McKee was sacked for an 11-yard loss. That began what was a rough first half for McKee, but he made some nice throws in the second half, including a beautiful over-the-shoulder throw to DeVonta Smith for a touchdown. When McKee wasn’t under pressure, he was happy to stand in the pocket and take shots down the field, which helped Smith and Dallas Goedert put together usable fantasy days, but McKee obviously does not avoid pressure in the pocket the way that Jalen Hurts does. He could put together a solid day next week against a vulnerable Cowboys defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-mck.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Eagles will decide whether to place Jalen Hurts (blood clot) on short-term injured reserve on Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-mck.analysis: Fowler reportedly spoke to “some people who are hopeful” that Hurts can avoid injured reserve. He described the situation as being “very much touch and go” and said Tanner McKee will “probably” start multiple games. The Eagles go on bye in Week 10, so if Hurts does land on injured reserve, the Eagles’ Week 11 game against the Steelers would be his earliest possible return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-mck.headline: Speaking on the Pat McAfee Show, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said he “would describe” Jalen Hurts’ (blood clot) status as being “out indefinitely.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-mck.analysis: Hurts’ blood clot was initially a superficial issue in his calf. Unfortunately, the clot has moved and the situation now appears to be quite serious and, per Rapoport, “scary.” Rapoport said Hurts will now undergo treatment, “which, a lot of times, is blood thinners.” If that treatment option is deemed necessary, Hurts would not be allowed to play. Rapoport believes Hurts will be sidelined in Week 6 “and likely beyond.” Tanner McKee is his replacement.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-mck.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Tanner McKee will start for the Eagles until Jalen Hurts’ (superficial blood clot) “medical situation is solved.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-mck.analysis: McKee, 26, is a towering pocket passer (6'6/231) with 97 career dropbacks. He has two career starts and has made appearances in two other contests, averaging 6.8 yards per attempt and a 73.8 percent adjusted completion rate. McKee was the subject of trade rumors last offseason, but luckily, the Eagles kept him. He faces a Panthers secondary missing its two starting perimeter cornerbacks, though he has almost exactly 72 hours to get himself ready and the Eagles’ pass-catching corps is banged up. He is a viable QB2 in superflex formats, but he offers a wide range of potential outcomes. McKee is backed up by rookie Cole Payton. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo thinks the team could reunite with Andy Dalton, whom they released last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-mck.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo believes the Eagles could re-sign Andy Dalton.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-mck.analysis: Dalton is “an option” for the Eagles, who are down to two available quarterbacks this week, Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton, with Jalen Hurts having been ruled out preemptively due to a superficial blood clot in his calf. The Eagles released Dalton last week. A few teams have reportedly checked in with Dalton since his release, “though there’s familiarity and a clear role in Philly for him if he decides to return.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-mck.headline: Jalen Hurts has a “superficial blood clot” and will not play in Week 6 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tanner-mck.analysis: The Eagles released an official statement announcing the news. Per their statement, Hurts took a cleat to the calf in Week 4. He went in for treatment the following Thursday and an ultrasound revealed the blood clot. Doctors ultimately cleared him to play in Week 5. He continued to receive treatment over the next two days. After practice on Wednesday (yesterday), a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot. The team has now ruled him out for Week 6 as they determine the next course of action. They didn’t comment on how long Hurts will be out, but it’s possible this is a long-term issue for the veteran quarterback. Tanner McKee will draw the start versus Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports that Joe Milton will be the Eagles’ starting quarterback in Week 9 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: Milton, 26, has spent time with three different teams since the Patriots drafted him in the 2024 NFL Draft’s sixth round. He is a towering, mobile, cannon-armed quarterback with enticing traits. His erratic play can also be frustrating. Milton can be added in two-quarterback leagues, though his range of potential outcomes in his first start is extremely wide. He replaces Tanner McKee after a three-game starting stint.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Eagles signed Joe Milton, formerly of the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: Milton will join Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton on the Eagles’ 53-man roster. This move comes a day after it was revealed that Jalen Hurts would be out indefinitely due to a superficial blood clot that could sideline him for the next several weeks. Milton will likely serve as the Eagles’ emergency third QB on game days and seems unlikely to see any playing time at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Cowboys signed QB Joe Milton to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: Milton initially made the 53-man roster but was let go after the initial wave of waiver claims. He went unclaimed when waivers ran Tuesday and now returns to the Cowboys on the practice squad. With Sam Howell winning the QB2 job, Milton will be QB3 heading into the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Joe Milton was not claimed on waivers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: He’ll likely catch on with a practice squad in the next day or two, perhaps with the Cowboys again. Milton had initially made the 53-man roster in Dallas but lost his spot when they claimed Emari Demercado off waivers. The 26-year-old has an arm that was made to play quarterback and a decision-making process that was made to play quarterback in 1975.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Sam Howell and Joe Milton will compete for the No. 2 quarterback job this summer.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: This is mostly just a housekeeping item for dynasty managers, but re-draft managers can still file it away for a potential rainy day in Dallas. Things could change via the 2026 NFL Draft, but these two are set to duke it out for now. Milton flubbed his second-half opportunity in Week 18 last year, perhaps prompting the Cowboys to search for a more reliable No. 2 option. The team certainly has a type. Both Howell and Milton possess very strong arms, which should allow the Cowboys to continue attacking downfield if starting QB Dak Prescott were to miss time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Joe Milton III completed 7-of-13 passes for 73 yards and an interception in the Cowboys’ 34-17, Week 18 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: A year after destroying the Bills’ backups in the final game of the 2024-25 season, Milton failed to deliver the same kind of fireworks here. He started the second half for the Cowboys and led five drives, only one of which resulted in points. He’ll finish the season 15-of-24 for 183 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, while adding four rushes for 45 yards. He will return as Dak Prescott’s backup in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Dak Prescott completed 19-of-31 passes for 188 yards and two interceptions in the Cowboys’ 44-24, Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: He was benched with eight minutes left in the game and Dallas down by 27 points, Joe Milton led a touchdown drive with things out of hand. Both of Prescott’s picks were pretty weird, one of them by dropping edge player Deondrea Tillman. He was hit hard today, taking 14 pressures in 38 dropbacks per PFF. Obviously, this wasn’t the QB1 game you were promised — it didn’t look like the Cowboys had a real answer for their easy underneath stuff getting poached. Prescott will look to rebound in Week 9 against the Cardinals and should remain on the QB1 line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Dak Prescott completed 31-of-40 passes for 251 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the Cowboys’ 31-14 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: Testing the limits of what an all-Jake Ferguson offense could deliver to the world, one of Prescott’s picks deflected off George Pickens’ hands, and the other got him benched for Joe Milton in a 17-point deficit the Cowboys were obviously not overcoming. (Milton went 3-of-5 for 41 yards and a pick of his own.) The pass offense lost a lot of oomph without Lamb, and now Prescott gets to deal with an absolutely livid Packers front seven on Sunday night next week. If Lamb misses Week 4, it would be hard to fire up Prescott as more than a borderline QB1. The Dallas defense has forced plenty of passing situations for the Cowboys, as Prescott has 126 pass attempts in three games, but it would be a tough sell against a great defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Joe Milton completed 9-of-18 passes for 122 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Cowboys’ preseason game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: At one point, Milton was 3-of-10 passing. The second-year quarterback who took a sack for a safety on his team’s opening drive looked as erratic as we’ve seen during his time as a pro, and ended the day with an absurd 15.2 ADOT. Milton missed his intended target all night, with PFF attributing just one of his incompletions to a dropped pass. His best play on the night came on a 49-yard completion to Jonathan Mingo, but it’s hard to ignore what we’ve witnessed from Milton through two preseason games. He’s completed 26-of-47 passes (55.3 percent) for one touchdown and two interceptions, and has taken three sacks on 10 pressures. Thankfully for the Cowboys, Dak Prescott is healthy, but it may be time for the Cowboys to explore additional depth behind their QB1 after Milton appears to have reverted to the player we saw for parts of six college seasons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.headline: Joe Milton completed 17-of-29 passes for 143 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Cowboys’ 31-21 preseason loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joe-milton/000.analysis: Milton also rushed for 22 yards on five carries. The 2024 sixth-round pick drew that start in Saturday’s exhibition, and limited mistakes for most of the evening, taking just one sack while throwing an interception that bounced off his receiver’s hands. His lone touchdown pass came on a seven-yard completion to Rivaldo Fairweather, who broke free from his defender in the end zone. Known for his rocket arm and erratic accuracy, Milton continues to impress when given the opportunity and should be in line for more playing time next Saturday when the Cowboys play host to the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold (quad) will not play in Week 9 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Per Macdonald, Darnold also suffered a rib injury early in the team’s Week 8 loss to the Bears, though that doesn’t appear to be the reason he’s out this week. Darnold is considered week-to-week. Per Macdonald, he won’t go on injured reserve. It’s possible this quad issue is related to the glute issue that sidelined Darnold earlier in the season. Either way, Darnold’s health concerns are now becoming an issue for a Seahawks team that was already struggling to live up to the hype. Drew Lock will draw the start versus Arizona this week. He’ll likely start in Week 10 as well. With two successful appearances under his belt this year, Lock is a somewhat safe QB2 bet for Superflex managers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Sam Darnold completed 17-of-34 passes for 188 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Seahawks’ 34-17, Week 8 loss to the Bears, adding 20 yards on two rushes.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Darnold really struggled through consistent pressure from Dennis Allen’s aggressive defensive front as the Seahawks gained just 252 yards of total offense. Things looked manageable in the first half while Darnold leaned heavily on alpha wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, feeding his top option for 92 yards before the break. Allen’s second half adjustments all but removed JSN from the offense, holding him to just 26 yards after the break. Week 8 went down as only the third game of the 2026 season in which Darnold threw multiple touchdowns, leaving him outside QB2 range and on waiver wires ahead of a Week 9 meeting with the Cardinals.
