https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Sam Darnold completed 20-of-28 passes for 257 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Seahawks’ 20-3, Week 7 win over the Chiefs, adding 17 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Darnold continued to flaunt his connection with wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba with zero regard to the naysayers, feeding his alpha 12 targets on 28 pass attempts, the latter of whom accounted for 150 of the 257 pass yards for Darnold. As you probably guessed, Smith-Njigba was also the recipient of Darnold’s lone touchdown throw, which was a dime down the left sideline on a corner route that the veteran signal caller dropped into the bread basket. The two would connect on another similar play later in the same quarter in which Smith-Njigba was forced out at the two, with the result of that drive Darnold’s interception in the end zone. Darnold continues to do just enough for his team and not enough for fantasy managers that thought they could grab cheap production late in drafts. He’s better sent back to the waiver wire than inserted into starting lineups. The Seahawks next face the Bears on the second half of back-to-back Monday Night Football games, where Darnold remains a shaky fantasy option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold’s starting quarterback job is not in jeopardy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: The Seahawks’ head coach stood by his quarterback today, saying Darnold is “definitely part of the solution” to the offense’s recent struggles. Darnold returned somewhat quickly from a glute tendon strain a couple of weeks ago. One wonders if he is still rounding back into form following the early-season ailment. Backup Drew Lock played well in his stead, but the Seahawks believe their Super Bowl-winning quarterback should keep his job. That makes sense to us. He’s a QB2 next week against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Sam Darnold completed 27-of-51 passes for 278 yards and two interceptions in the Seahawks’ 17-14, Week 6 loss to the Broncos, adding 19 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: The Seahawks struggled to move the football throughout against the tenacious situational play calling from Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph, scoring only three points until just over five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. A late-game surge saw them punch on in and a successful two-point conversion drew the team within three points. They would stop the Broncos on the subsequent possession but an interception in Denver territory put the game in jeopardy. The defense would do their job and force a three-and-out that took only 15 seconds off the clock, giving the ball back to Darnold to lead a two-minute drill to send the game to overtime through a chip shot field goal. Darnold would throw his second interception in overtime, watching from the sideline as the Broncos walked it off with a 53-yard Will Lutz field goal. The loss sends the Seahawks to 3-3, matching the total number of losses from a season ago through only six weeks of the 2026 season. The Seahawks have work to do to make up ground in the NFC West, now 2.5 games behind the undefeated 49ers through the first third of the regular season. Darnold and the Seahawks now have a long week to prepare for the now-undefeated Chiefs at home in Week 7, where Darnold will be a fringe QB2 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Sam Darnold completed 18-of-29 passes for 195 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Seahawks’ 32-29, Week 5 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: It was a rough outing for Darnold, who was picked off on his first pass attempt of the day and absorbed a season-high five sacks. His lone touchdown pass came on a 16-yard pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Darnold completed a short two-yard pass to JSN, who turned it upfield for the score to give the Seahawks the 23-21 lead with just over five minutes left in the third quarter. On the Seahawks’ final drive of the game, Darnold found JSN for a 35-yard completion, but three straight incompletions, including an uncharacteristic drop by JSN, put the Seahawks in a fourth-and-10 situation that they were unable to convert after Cooper Kupp came up a yard short on his second reception of the night. Darnold has now thrown seven touchdowns and six interceptions in his last three games since returning from injury, and now faces a short week to get ready for the Broncos on Thursday night. He profiles as a mid-to-low-end QB2 in what could be a tough road matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Sam Darnold completed 13-of-22 passes for 168 yards with two touchdowns and an interception in the Seahawks’ 30-23, Week 5 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Darnold’s first pass of the game was intercepted on a throw to the flat that should have gone basically anywhere else. He connected on a screen pass with Emanuel Wilson for his first score, and found Tory Horton on a short slant for his second. The 29-year-old wasn’t close to his best, but could enough against the less-than-spectacular Chargers’ defense. He’ll have a marquee matchup in Week 5 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Sam Darnold completed 31-of-45 passes for 379 yards with four touchdowns and two interceptions in the Seahawks’ 33-31, Week 3 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: It was his first action since leaving in the first series of Week 1 against the Patriots with his hip/glute injury. Darnold’s first interception was a doink off a defensive lineman that landed in the hands of Sonny Styles. The second was an egregious offering that resulted in a pick six. Outside of that, the 29-year-old played relatively well, with two touchdown throws to Jaxon Smith-Njigba and another pair to Cooper Kupp and Eric Saubert. He’ll look to limit the turnovers and find JSN more often in Week 4 against the Chargers at home.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold (glute) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Darnold upgraded to full participation yesterday, so today’s news tracks. In an interview on the Rich Eisen Show earlier today, Seahawks WR Smith-Njigba basically let slip that Darnold would be back, but Eisen let him out of the situation with only a soft follow-up. Darnold can be started as a borderline QB1/2 against a fantasy-friendly Commanders defense in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.headline: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold (glute) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-darnol.analysis: Darnold said today that he is “striving” to play in Week 3 against the Commanders. It sounds like his striding is going well, too. The Seahawks’ starting quarterback is now seemingly on track to play on Sunday. Darnold’s strained glute tendon has healed faster than expected. If active, he can be treated as a high-end QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Packers designated Chris Brooks (ankle) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Brooks is back at practice and could be officially activated from IR ahead of the Packers’ Week 9 matchup with the Patriots. He would likely take Pierre Strong’s spot in the lineup as Green Bay’s RB3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Packers placed RB Chris Brooks (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Brooks had been the most consistent contributor to a Green Bay backfield working to find their way in the absence of Josh Jacobs. The team appears likely to utilize journeyman Pierre Strong as the preferred passing down specialist, likely keeping the backfield in a maddening timeshare without Brooks. None are worthy of legitimate fantasy interest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Chris Brooks (ankle) will not play in Green Bay’s Week 5 game against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: This was foreshadowed a bit by the appearance of Pierre Strong Jr. on the roster. It’s unclear how the Packers will handle third-down reps between Strong, Kaleb Johnson, and MarShawn Lloyd on Sunday. Strong was on the field for 138 passes of his 192 snaps in 2024 with the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Chris Brooks (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Matt LaFleur said earlier this morning that they were going to “give him another day and see where he’s at tomorrow and make a decision after that.” It sounds like there’s still a chance Brooks could play in Week 5, but he’ll likely be on the questionable line on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Chris Brooks (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Brooks suffered the ankle injury in Week 4. He went down in the first half and did not return. Brooks underwent testing on his ankle after the game, though the exact nature of his injury has yet to be reported. He does appear to be on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5. If he can’t go, MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson will split the backfield. Johnson led the team in carries last week but also gave up a goal line fumble. We expect Lloyd to get the start versus Chicago on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Chris Brooks is undergoing tests on his ankle.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Brooks left the Packers’ Week 4 win over the Bucs with an ankle injury in the first half. He did not return after the break and LaFleur didn’t have any definitive answers about the injury on Monday. It sounds like his status for Week 5 is very much up in the air. After coughing up a goal line fumble, Kaleb Johnson would likely take a backseat to MarShawn Lloyd once again. Lloyd has some low-end RB3 appeal as the potential lead back, but this is ultimately a backfield to avoid for fantasy purposes if possible.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Chris Brooks rushed four times for 30 yards in the Packers’ Week 4 win over the Bucs, adding one catch for five yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Brooks was third among the Packers’ three running backs in snaps and touches. That could change next week with Kaleb Johnson coughing up a goal line fumble in this game. Still, Brooks would only jump to RB2 on the depth chart. He is seeing enough work to remove most of the fantasy value from Johnson and Lloyd but doesn’t have much fantasy value of his own. Green Bay’s backfield remains a mess headed into Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Chris Brooks rushed four times for 11 yards in the Packers’ Week 2 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: He added one catch for 15 yards. While those stats are not impressive, Brooks also played on 24 of the team’s 53 snaps, which was the most of any Green Bay running back. After Marshawn Lloyd fumbled in the second half, it was Brooks who saw the next red zone carries and also Brooks who caught a crucial pass in overtime to set up the game-winning field goal. This has all the makings of a confusing committee, but Brooks needs to be on radars in deeper formats until Josh Jacobs returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports that the Brown County District Attorney “has formally charged Packers RB Josh Jacobs with two misdemeanors related to his May arrest.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Pelissero reminds us that Jacobs was “originally booked on five charges, including felony strangulation.” He now faces “reduced charges of misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property.” The NFL continues to monitor all developments in the matter, which remains under review. Jacobs could end up being suspended. His backups are RB MarShawn Lloyd, who has performed well all spring and summer, and RB Chris Brooks. Lloyd should be a priority in drafts at this time. According to The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman, the police department’s full incident report indicates that the department is in possession of a video showing Jacobs striking a woman after throwing her to the ground.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.headline: Packers RB MarShawn Lloyd rushed five times for 15 yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Broncos, adding one reception for 11 yards and one touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christophe.analysis: Lloyd played on 5-of-7 snaps during the first drive, giving way to RB Chris Brooks for third- and fourth-and-inches. Lloyd looks fast and powerful and can be treated as a high-end bench stash with potential standalone value. His touchdown occurred on a nifty catch-and-run play over the middle. Starting RB Josh Jacobs (groin) did not play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-campb.headline: Jack Campbell said he has full movement in his lower body.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-campb.analysis: Campbell, who was carted off with a frightening neck injury in Week 8 against the Vikings, said in a statement that he is recovering. “I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time,” Campbell’s statement reads, in part. “I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better.” Campbell is likely out for the rest of the season, a blow to a Detroit defense that has struggled against both the pass and the run this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-campb.headline: Lions head coach Dan Campbell said the team has received “positive” news on Jack Campbell after he suffered a neck injury in Week 8’s win over the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-campb.analysis: The team has opted to not disclose any further details of Campbell’s injury, but this is obviously good news for the fourth-year linebacker. Campbell suffered a scary neck injury in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s win and was eventually carted from the field after being down on the ground for several minutes. While the early reports are encouraging, it’s possible Campbell avoided the worst-case scenario but could still face a months-long journey back to the field. We will be sure to provide any updates as they come our way.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-campb.headline: Jack Campbell (neck) will remain in a local hospital tonight for continued evaluation and monitoring.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-campb.analysis: This update comes straight from the Lions’ organization. Campbell was taken to a local hospital shortly after being taken off the field on a stretcher. He is reportedly resting now. The team will provide further updates as it has them. We hope he recovers quickly and completely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-campb.headline: Jack Campbell was carted off in Week 8 with an apparent neck injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-campb.analysis: Campbell’s neck bent awkwardly on a tackle in the fourth quarter. He immediately went limp, and after more than ten minutes, he was carted off with what appeared to be a neck injury. The standout linebacker could be looking at an extended absence. We will update his status as we get more information.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-campb.headline: Lions signed LB Jack Campbell to a four-year extension through 2030.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-campb.analysis: Campbell, 25, was set to enter free agency in 2027 after the Lions declined to exercise Campbell’s fifth-year option in April. Instead, the team’s leader in tackles will stick around. Campbell’s 110 tackles are 42 more than the next closest Lions defender. He also banked 17 quarterback pressures, five sacks and two pass breakups. The deal is reportedly worth $81 million.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-campb.headline: Lions declined to pick up LB Jack Campbell’s fifth-year option.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-campb.analysis: The fifth-year option and franchise tag grouping of positions strikes again. Campbell would have received $21.9 million if Detroit picked up the option due to the amount of pure EDGE players that are factored into the equation — it’s essentially the same reason why the Packers declined Quay Walker’s fifth-year option last year and lost him in free agency. The Lions reportedly were trying to strike a long-term extension with Campbell — this doesn’t seem like a true signal on that so much as the natural outcome of not wanting to head into negotiations with that figure over Brad Holmes’ head.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-campb.headline: Lions GM Brad Holmes said the team has already discussed picking up the fifth-year option for Jahmyr Gibbs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-campb.analysis: Speaking during the Lions’ pre-draft press conference, Holmes said the Lions have not exercised the options for Gibbs or LB Jack Campbell, who also has a fifth-year option the team needs to decide on. Both Gibbs and Campbell are safe bets to have their options picked up, which would keep them under contract through 2027. While Gibbs emerged as one of the top backs in the league and totaled 1,800-plus yards from scrimmage in each of the last two seasons, Campbell earned First-team All-Pro honors in 2025, finishing the year with 175 tackles, five sacks, three forced fumbles, and nine TFLs. We would expect both players to have their options picked up in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-campb.headline: Lions signed No. 18 overall pick Jack Campbell to a four-year contract with a fifth-year option.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-campb.analysis: Campbell figures to start next to Alex Anzalone for the Lions this year, though perhaps Malcolm Rodriguez will make a move up the rankings in his first offseason with the team. Campbell should be an IDP starter from the jump assuming he stays healthy in training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-campb.headline: Lions selected Iowa LB Jack Campbell with the No. 18 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-campb.analysis: A unanimous All-American who brought home Big Ten Defensive Player of the Year accolades, Campbell (6’5/249) was named the 2022 Butkus Award recipient given to the top linebacker in the country. He plays the position with a cerebral approach befitting a three-time Academic All-Big Ten student and is a savant at diagnosing play flow. The rangy MLB rarely lets rushers escape his grasp, which is reflected in his superb 8.9% missed tackle rate and 107 run stops over the last two seasons. The mechanics with which he plays the game are unassailable, but his length can hurt him in coverage and in change of direction situations. Campbell is at his best scraping and challenging ball carriers at the point of attack, though his 31.875” arms hurt his ability to out-leverage massive linemen. His Combine performance was near-perfect, with Campbell posting 97th+ percentile results in jumping and agility testing to go with a 92nd percentile 1.58s 10-yard dash to combine for an eye-popping 9.98 RAS. His play style and athleticism are reminiscent of former Boise State LB Leighton Vander Esch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-campb.headline: Iowa senior LB Jack Campbell recorded a solid 2021 season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-campb.analysis: Campbell (6'5/243) is a linebacker to watch in 2022, and his numbers back up that statement. Last season, Campbell recorded 140 total tackles (57 solo) with five passes defended, two interceptions, one touchdown, two fumble recoveries, one forced fumble and one sack. According to Pro Football Focus, Campbell totaled 45 run stops last season -- the most by a Power Five linebacker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: Tyler Huntley (toe) is out for the remainder of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: Further evaluation of Huntley’s toe injury showed it was a season ender. That leaves the Ravens desperate at quarterback for the remainder of the season. Against the Jaguars on Thursday night the team is likely to start Joe Fagnano. It’s unclear who will serve as the team’s backup quarterback this week or going forward. Zay Flowers goes from an elite weekly fantasy option to something closer to a WR3 in this degraded offensive environment. Derrick Henry’s prospects take a major knock too.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Tyler Huntley (toe) could be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: The decision on whether or not to place Huntley on injured reserve could come in the next few days as the Ravens prepare to play the Jaguars on Thursday. With Lamar Jackson (thumb) expected to be placed on IR and possibly be out for the rest of the season, Huntley landing on IR would mean the Ravens would be starting their third-string QB (or worse) for at least the next four weeks. Rookie UDFA Joe Fagnano has already been named as the starter for Thursday’s game against the Jaguars, but was seen sporting an ankle brace in Tuesday’s practice. While he’s expected to play through it, the Ravens could be forced to play either Austin Reed or Kedon Slovis, who signed with the team earlier this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Tyler Huntley is going to miss “extended time” after suffering a turf toe injury in Week 8’s loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: Even in the best-case scenario, Huntley felt like a long shot to play in Thursday night’s game against the Jaguars, but it sounds like this is going to be a multi-week absence. An MRI will confirm the severity of his injury in the days ahead, but for now, rookie UDFA Joe Fagnano is expected to draw the start against the Jags for the 4-4 Ravens. Lamar Jackson, who will be placed on IR in the coming days, will undergo surgery to repair the thumb he dislocated in Sunday’s game, meaning the Ravens will bring in a veteran QB through a trade or free agency in the near future. It should go without saying, but all of the Ravens’ key fantasy assets will receive a noticeable downgrade with Jackson and Huntley both out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: The Athletic’s Jeff Zrebiec reports that Joe Fagnano (undisclosed) said he thinks he is healthy enough to play in Week 9 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: According to Zrebiec, Fagnano “was hobbled by game’s end, after he took a low and penalized hit” from Bills DL Ed Oliver. Fagnano said he and the team will have to wait and “see” how he is feeling in the coming days, noting that “you’re always going to have bumps and bruises” after a football game. Lamar Jackson (thumb) is already headed to injured reserve and Tyler Huntley will undergo an MRI tomorrow to assess a potential turf toe injury. Zrebiec rightly writes that the Ravens “will almost certainly have to bring in at least one quarterback, if not two,” this week. He lists Anthony Richardson and Tua Tagovailoa as potential trade targets. At this point, it is unclear who will start for the Ravens on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Tyler Huntley is believed to have suffered a turf toe injury and will undergo an MRI on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: Tomorrow’s MRI should clarify whether Huntley will miss time. In the meantime, Lamar Jackson will be placed on injured reserve with what could be a season-ending thumb injury. This leaves rookie Joe Fagnano as the team’s potential starter for the Ravens’ Week 9 Thursday Night Football game against the Jaguars, though Fagnano reportedly got a little banged up today, too. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (thumb) will undergo surgery and be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: When asked if this is a potentially season-ending injury for Jackson, Minter’s response was, “We’ll see.” After seeing Jackson’s injury on replay, it was easy to assume the Ravens’ QB1 would be looking at another multi-week absence, but this sounds like the worst-case scenario. If Jackson doesn’t land on season-ending IR, he would be required to miss at least four games before he could even consider a return. Adding insult to injury, the Ravens also lost backup Tyler Huntley in this game to a toe injury, meaning rookie UDFA Joe Fagnano could be in line to start on Thursday night against the Jaguars in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: Tyler Huntley (toe) will not return in Week 8 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: Emergency QB3 Joe Fagnano will finish this one out after Huntley was ruled out during halftime. The Ravens’ QB2 completed 2-of-4 passes for zero yards in relief of Lamar Jackson, who exited after the first play of the game due to a thumb injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: Tyler Huntley (toe) questionable to return in Week 8 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: Huntley suffered a toe injury on a sack/fumble in the second quarter and was replaced by emergency QB3 Joe Fagnano. Huntley is eligible to return to the game if the team clears him to do so, despite some initial confusion that he would be unable to return after the Ravens were forced to put in their emergency QB.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: ESPN’s Jamison Hensley believes only Lamar Jackson (ankle) knows when he’ll be able to play again.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: Jackson surprisingly missed the Ravens’ Week 7 loss to the Bengals with his lingering ankle injury, which has been described as neither high nor low. “If Jackson’s injury history has taught the football world anything, his timeline to return can be complicated and an extended absence can derail the Ravens’ season,” Hensley said. “But ultimately, the only one who truly knows when Jackson will return is Jackson himself.” NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said on Tuesday that he expected Jackson to suit up in Week 8 against the Bills. We likely won’t be sure of that until pre-game warmups. Tyler Huntley would continue as Baltimore’s starter if Jackson remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.headline: Tyler Huntley completed 23-of-34 passes for 298 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Ravens’ 35-13, Week 7 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-hunt.analysis: This makes it two straight games where Huntley and the Ravens failed to score in the second half. Huntley was solid in the first half, throwing for 227-1-0 on 21 passes, with his lone touchdown pass coming on a 48-yard screen pass to Zay Flowers on the Ravens’ opening drive. He would lead the Ravens on two drives that ended in field goals in the second quarter, but the Ravens struggled mightily in the second half as the Bengals rallied for 35 unanswered points. At one point, Huntley had the Ravens in position for a short field goal to go up 16-14, but passed on the points and opted to go for it on fourth-and-two, which resulted in an incomplete pass to tight end Josh Cuevas. It was reported during the game that Lamar Jackson (ankle) would be back for Week 8’s game against the Ravens. Now sitting at 4-3 on the year, it goes without saying that the Ravens are in desperate need of Jackson in what is shaping up to be a highly competitive AFC North division.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakorian-b.headline: Eagles waived CB Jakorian Bennett.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakorian-b.analysis: Bennett was acquired by the Eagles in a swap with the Raiders before the start of last season. The 26-year-old played 98 defensive snaps in two seasons for Philly, spending all of the 2026 season on injured reserve with a knee injury. The Eagles now waive Bennett from injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakorian-b.headline: Eagles placed OLB Nolan Smith on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakorian-b.analysis: Smith reportedly re-injured the triceps muscle that he tore during Super Bowl LIX. He underwent surgery to repair the torn tissue this offseason. The Eagles believe Smith will not require surgery and hope to have him back “around” their Week 9 bye. Players placed on injured reserve are eligible to return after missing four games. The Eagles also placed CB Jakorian Bennett and WR Darius Cooper on injured reserve with undisclosed injuries. Both players are likewise expected to avoid surgery and are expected to return around Week 9. The Eagles signed S Marcus Epps, TE Cameron Latu, and CB Parry Nickerson to the active roster, and LB Lance Dixon, DB Eli Ricks, and WR Quez Watkins to the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakorian-b.headline: Raiders traded CB Jakorian Bennett to the Eagles for DT Thomas Booker.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakorian-b.analysis: The move should be considered a depth move for both franchises as neither player were expected to open the 2025 season as starters. That said, the move makes sense for both teams as it addresses relative weaknesses. We should see more trades go down as teams work through their respective depth charts as we inch closer to the start of the regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakorian-b.headline: Raiders placed CB Jakorian Bennett (shoulder) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakorian-b.analysis: Bennett is eligible to return in Week 17, so there’s a chance his season is over, as the Raiders will be well out of playoff contention by that time. Bennett has earned a PFF coverage grade of 61.0 this season, but has allowed just 18 receptions for 176 and no touchdowns on 37 targets. In addition to him being out for Week 13, the Raiders will also be down Nate Hobbs (ankle), leaving them without their top two corners vs. the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakorian-b.headline: Raiders CB Nate Hobbs (ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakorian-b.analysis: Both Hobbs and No. 1 perimeter CB Jakorian Bennett (shoulder) remain sidelined, putting them on the wrong side of questionable for the Raiders’ Week 13 Friday night game against the Chiefs. Hobbs and Bennett are two of the Raiders’ best players. The defense cannot afford to be without them.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakorian-b.headline: Raiders CB Nate Hobbs (ankle) did not participate in Tuesday’s walk-through.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakorian-b.analysis: Also out was CB Jakorian Bennett (shoulder). The Raiders secondary struggled without either cornerback in Week 12 against the Broncos and both are trending out again. Hobbs and/or Bennett will need to practice later in the week in order to play Friday, but for now, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs are slated for an extremely favorable matchup in Week 13.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakorian-b.headline: Raiders CB Jakorian Bennett (shoulder) is out for Week 12 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakorian-b.analysis: Fellow cornerback Nate Hobbs is out with an ankle issue. Jack Jones returned to practice on Friday and will presumably be listed as questionable. Down at least two starting corners, the Raiders are as good of a matchup as Bo Nix could ask for.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakorian-b.headline: Raiders CB Jakorian Bennett (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakorian-b.analysis: Raiders slot CB Nate Hobbs (ankle) and No. 2 perimeter CB Jack Jones (back) were also unable to practice on Wednesday. The development pushes the Broncos’ ascending rookie QB Bo Nix firmly into the QB1 ranks. His pass catchers are likewise on the rise this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakorian-b.headline: Raiders CB Jakorian Bennett exited Week 7 against the Rams with an apparent leg injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakorian-b.analysis: Update: Bennett has returned to play. Bennett’s seven forced incompletions tie for the fifth-most in the NFL. Decamerion Richardson takes over for Bennett and will attempt to mitigate the loss as much as possible.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakorian-b.headline: Raiders traded up with the Texans to select Maryland CB Jakorian Bennett with the No. 104 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakorian-b.analysis: The Raiders moved up five spots but traded back from pick No. 174 to pick No. 203 later in the draft. Bennett (5’11/188) didn’t start until his senior year of high school and had to go the JuCo route for two years in order to build his value. He became a starter in 2021 and was highly productive over the next two seasons, racking up 29 PBU, five interceptions, and allowing a 47% completion rate while twice earning Honorable Mention All-Big Ten recognition. Bennett substantially raised his profile during the pre-draft evaluation process, running a blinding 4.30s 40-yard dash that is a 99.6th percentile time along with a 40.5” vertical (96th%) and 11’01” broad jump (98th%) for a 9.59 RAS. He has enough juice and fluidity to turn and run in lockstep with speedsters but is vulnerable to manipulation after receivers get him striding, then break off their routes. He’s constantly raking at the ball and plays scrappy to overcome size limitations, Bennett has the skills to compete for meaningful reps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-car.headline: Saints released K Daniel Carlson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-car.analysis: Carlson has converted 8-of-12 field goals this season and is 16-for-18 on PATs. The veteran kicker who is known for his big leg has seen all four of his misses come on distances of 50-plus yards, but that was more than enough for the Saints to look in a different direction. Practice squad kicker Charlie Smyth, who converted 12 of his 16 field goal attempts for the Saints last season has a chance to be the next man up when the Saints take on the Browns in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-car.headline: Saints signed K Daniel Carlson, formerly of the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-car.analysis: It would appear that the winner of the kicking competition that took place in training camp between Tanner Brown and Charlie Smyth is the man who wasn’t there. Carlson, who has remained unsigned since his contract with the Raiders expired at the end of last season, is now expected to take over as the Saints’ starting kicker for the season. Currently the 10th-most accurate kicker in NFL history, Carlson converted 22-of-27 field goal attempts last season, with three of his misses coming from 50-plus yards. Carlson still possesses one of the biggest legs in the league and should benefit from kicking in the friendly confines of the Superdome this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-car.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports K Daniel Carlson (groin) will kick in Week 8 against the Lions, barring setback.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-car.analysis: Carlson was deemed a true game-time decision but appears to be up to the task to kick on Monday night. Groin injuries can be tricky for a kicker, which could influence Josh McDaniels’ tendencies near the outer portions of field goal range tonight. Even so, the Raiders have struggled in the red zone to the tune of a 41.67 percent red zone touchdown rate, meaning Carlson could still find his way into field goal attempts against the stout Lions defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-car.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports Daniel Carlson (groin) “figures to be a game-time decision” for the Raiders’ Week 8 matchup against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-car.analysis: The name to know here is James McCourt. McCourt is the kicker the Raiders promoted from the practice squad prior to Monday night’s contest against the Lions. Fantasy managers who weren’t prepared to be without Carlson could conceivably pivot to McCourt if they need a few points from a kicker to push them across the finish line this week. Fantasy managers don’t need to react just yet, as Carlson’s status will be confirmed in the coming hours, but if he can’t go, McCourt is almost certainly available in every league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-car.headline: Raiders signed K Daniel Carlson to a four-year, $18.4 million extension through 2025.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-car.analysis: Carlson is playing 2021 on the restricted free agent tender. After flaming out with the Vikings, Carlson has found a long-term home with Vegas. He’s 27-of-30 (90%) on field goals this season and has missed just two of his 25 extra points. At $4.6 million per year, Carlson is the league’s third-highest paid kicker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-car.headline: Raiders re-signed K Daniel Carlson to a one-year, $3.384 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-car.analysis: This is Carlson officially signing his second round restricted free agent tender. Carlson converted 94.3 percent of his 2020 field goal attempts after he was a far worse 73.1 percent in 2019. Carlson was 4-of-4 beyond 50 yards last season as he quietly finished as fantasy’s fourth highest scoring kicker thanks largely to the NFL’s seventh most attempts. He’ll likely be overdrafted in seasonal leagues this season. Coach Jon Gruden evidently believes the 26-year-old is his “kicker of the future.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-car.headline: Raiders extended a second-round tender to restricted free agent K Daniel Carlson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-car.analysis: No team is giving up a second-rounder for the kicker. Carlson set the Raiders’ franchise record with 144 points last season. The Mike Zimmer castoff was a stunningly consistent waiver wire pickup in 2020 fantasy leagues, finishing the year as the game’s third highest scoring kicker with a hefty 2.2 field goal attempts per game -- the sixth highest mark in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-car.headline: Raiders re-signed K Daniel Carlson to a one-year, $750,000 contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-car.analysis: Carlson was an exclusive rights free agent. The 25-year-old was not particularly good last season, converting just 19-of-26 field goal attempts (73.1 percent). He will probably face training camp competition.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-car.headline: Raiders signed K Daniel Carlson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-car.analysis: The Raiders are moving on from Matthew McCrane as they wait on Mike Nugent (hip) to get healthy. A fifth-round rookie out of Auburn, Carlson was cut by the Vikings following a disastrous two-week stint. The Raiders are getting their tank on, and Carlson was good in the SEC, so they are taking a no-risk gamble as they play for draft position and wait on Nugent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-car.headline: Raiders re-signed K Daniel Carlson to a one-year, $570,000 contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-car.analysis: Carlson was an exclusive rights free agent. Signed last October, Carlson ended up converting 94.1 percent of his field goal attempts. It was an excellent bounce back after his NFL career got off to a horrid start with the Vikings. Carlson was the No. 167 overall pick of last year’s draft.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-loop.headline: Ravens placed K Tyler Loop (groin) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-loop.analysis: Loop will be sidelined for at least the next four weeks after suffering a right groin injury in Sunday’s loss to the Bills. The second-year kicker competed for the starting kicker job in camp and has struggled during parts of this season. He has converted on 13 of his 17 field goal attempts this year, with his four misses all coming from inside 50 yards. Veteran Jake Moody is set to take over in Loop’s absence when the Ravens face the Jaguars on Thursday night. Loop will be eligible to return in Week 14 when the Ravens play host to the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-loop.headline: Jesse Minter said the team is considering injured reserve for Tyler Loop (undisclosed).
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-loop.analysis: Loop suffered an undisclosed injury in the Week 8 loss to the Bills, something that is reportedly serious enough to warrant injured reserve consideration. When asked if Jake Moody would be kicking on Thursday Night Football against the Jaguars, Minter replied with a simple, “At this point, yes.” The Ravens were dealt numerous injury issues in their loss to the Bills as they lost both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley, with third string rookie Joe Fagnano also emerging dinged up after taking numerous hard sacks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-loop.headline: Ravens signed Jake Moody to the team’s practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-loop.analysis: Moody could serve as competition for Tyler Loop after Loop’s early-season struggles. Loop has made 10 of his 13 field goal attempts and all 16 of his extra points through Week 6. Moody — a career 78 percent kicker — competed with Loop for starting duties ahead of the regular season. Whoever ends up kicking for Baltimore will be fantasy relevant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-loop.headline: Tyler Loop made 1-of-2 field goals and all three extra-point attempts in the Ravens’ Week 18 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-loop.analysis: Loop has been one of the best kickers in football even as a rookie, but his season ends on a dour note as he missed what would have been a game-winning field goal with no time remaining. The 24-year-old shouldn’t have any issues with job security to open 2026 even with the miss, and he’ll be worthy of fantasy consideration in leagues that still employ kickers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-loop.headline: Tyler Loop converted all three of his field goals and one of his two extra point attempts in the Ravens’ Week 14 loss against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-loop.analysis: Loop has been excellent all season, making 25 of his 27 field goal tries. He hasn’t missed a field goal since Week 5 against the Texans. Loop will be a top-10 fantasy option in Week 15 against the Bengals. The Ravens are averaging 2.1 field goal tries per game, the 11th highest mark in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.headline: Giants signed CB Greg Newsome to a three-year, $46 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.analysis: Newsome signed a one-year $8 million contract with the Giants this offseason and is now being rewarded for his strong play during the first half of this season. The 26-year-old corner has allowed just 174 receiving yards on 26 targets this season, per PFF, earning a coverage grade of 66.1. He has been one of the league’s better outside corners this season and will now be under contract with the Giants through the 2029 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.headline: Jevón Holland (concussion) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.analysis: Holland, the Giants’ starting free safety, and Tyler Nubin (neck), the Giants’ starting strong safety, are both questionable to play. Meanwhile, starting perimeter CB Greg Newsome (concussion) has been ruled out. Expect the Texans’ passing offense to stay hot this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.headline: Jevón Holland (concussion) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.analysis: Holland, the team’s top safety, and Greg Newsome (concussion), the team’s top cornerback, were both sidelined today. Giants LB Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) was also sidelined. The Giants are tasked with containing a Texans’ passing offense that ties for the league lead in explosive pass plays this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.headline: Giants agreed to terms with CB Greg Newsome, formerly of the Jaguars, on a one-year, $10 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.analysis: Newsome was traded to the Jaguars last October and started 11 games for them. The former first-round pick allowed opposing receivers to go for 48-582-5 against him on 73 targets, and has struggled over the last two seasons after a strong first three years in the league. Newsome played almost exclusively on the outside last season, but has shown enough versatility throughout his career to play both outside and in the slot. Newsome will make for a nice addition to a secondary that just lost Cor’Dale Flott to the Titans on the first day of legal tampering.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports that the Jaguars “plan to play” Travis Hunter as a full-time cornerback and part-time wide receiver in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.analysis: Per Wolfe, the Jaguars believe Hunter can be an “elite” cornerback, while still being “an impact player” on offense. For fantasy purposes, this is unfortunate. Hunter may be stuck rotating in as a contributor in three-wide receiver sets, which would make him frustratingly unreliable, though head coach Liam Coen will likely try to scheme up ways to get the ball in his hands. On the plus side, Wolfe said Hunter will be “full-go” by Week 1. The Jaguars are reportedly expected to let one of their free agent cornerbacks, Montaric Brown or Greg Newsome, walk in free agency.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.headline: Jaguars CB Greg Newsome suffered an ankle injury in Jacksonville’s Week 11 game against the Chargers and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.analysis: Only recently back from injury, Newsome didn’t make it very long before landing back on the shelf. He has been replaced by Christian Braswell.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.headline: Jaguars HC Liam Coen said Greg Newsome will have “an opportunity to play” in Week 6 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.analysis: Speaking with the media on Friday, Coen said there’s some crossover between what the Jaguars do defensively and what Newsome did with the Browns that should put Newsome in line to see some snaps. Whether or not he draws the start is to be determined, but it doesn’t sound like the Jaguars will waste too much time getting Newsome on the field in a meaningful capacity, especially after they traded starting corner Tyson Campbell to acquire him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.headline: Browns acquired CB Tyson Campbell and the Eagles’ 2026 seventh-round pick from the Jaguars in exchange for CB Greg Newsome and the Jets’ 2026 sixth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Browns and Jaguars will be swapping late-round picks in addition to the cornerbacks. Campbell signed a four-year, $76.5 million extension in the 2024 offseason with the Jaguars and is now under contract through 2028 for Cleveland. He has six interceptions and 42 passes defended through his five-year career, but has missed 11 games over the last two seasons. The Jaguars swap him out for Greg Newsome, who is in the last season of his rookie deal. Newsome held a top-45 PFF coverage grade each of his first three seasons and has three interceptions and 37 passes defended through four total seasons. The Jags have flexibility at corner with Travis Hunter mixing in for snaps; his usage won’t decrease with Newsome joining him on the outside. Meanwhile, the Browns opt for Campbell’s long-term deal over negotiating a Newsome extension.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.headline: Greg Newsome (hamstring) is questionable for Week 5’s game against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.analysis: Newsome popped up on Thursday’s injury report with a hamstring and will officially be questionable entering the week. It’s never a good sign when a player is a late addition to the injury report, and the Browns will need all hands on deck if they hope to slow the receiving duo of Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison. If he’s unable to go, backup Myles Harden appears next in line to receive snaps. In addition to Newsome, RT Jack Conklin (elbow), who hasn’t played since Week 1, is also questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.headline: Browns CB Greg Newsome (hamstring) was limited in practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-newso.analysis: We never love to see a mid-week downgrade and unfortunately that’s what happened with Newsome today. It’s possible this is a blip, but it also could be a mid-practice injury that sends him to the inactives for Week 5. We’ll check in on him again tomorrow. If Newsome were out, it would increase the appeal of Minnesota’s wideout room as Cleveland’s depth corners behind Denzel Ward and Newsome are not well-regarded.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.headline: Bills released DB C.J. Gardner-Johnson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.analysis: Shortly after being reinstated from suspension for a spitting incident in Week 6 against the Raiders, Gardner-Johnson is now in search of a new home. The 28-year-old safety started all six games he appeared in for the Bills this season, earning a PFF defensive grade of 55.2 while allowing 11 receptions for 132 yards and a touchdown on 15 targets. Gardner-Johnson has played for four different teams since 2024 and is now free to sign with anyone willing to take on the 28-year-old vet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.headline: Bills S C.J. Gardner-Johnson has been suspended one game for an act of unsportsmanlike conduct in Week 6’s game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.analysis: Gardner-Johnson was caught on tape spitting at/in the direction of Raiders TE Brock Bowers after the two were seen jawing at one another after a play. Gardner-Johnson will be suspended without pay when the Bills return from their bye to play the Ravens in Week 8. He has tallied 25 tackles, two pass breakups, and one interception this season while earning a PFF grade of 55.2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.headline: C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected in the second quarter of the Bills’ Week 6 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.analysis: Instant replay showed Gardner-Johnson spitting in the direction of Brock Bowers and other Raiders players after he was seen jawing with Bowers after a play. The veteran defensive back was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct and immediately disqualified from the game, and will likely be facing a fine and suspension later in the week. The 28-year-old DB has started all five games he has appeared in this season, and entered the day with 25 tackles, two pass breakups, and one interception.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Bills S C.J. Gardner-Johnson has a calf strain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.analysis: Gardner-Johnson was carted off with a scary-looking injury that appeared to be near his Achilles. It looks as if he’s avoided the worst-case scenario, though we still wouldn’t be surprised if he missed a lot of time. The team should have further updates soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.headline: Bills S C.J. Gardner-Johnson (leg) was carted to the locker room on Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.analysis: Gardner-Johnson appeared to suffer a non-contact lower leg injury. He went down on the practice field and grabbed at his leg near his Achilles. The 28-year-old safety couldn’t put any pressure on his right leg as he was helped off the field. Gardner-Johnson had a towel over his head as he was carted to the locker room. Buffalo lacks safety depth behind Gardner-Johnson as fifth-round rookie Jalon Kilgore could be next up if this injury indeed turns out to be significant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.headline: Bills signed S C.J. Gardner-Johnson, formerly of the Bears, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.analysis: Gardner-Johnson can make up to $6 million this year. The 28-year-old safety allowed a career-high 71.4 percent catch rate playing for both the Texans and Bears last season. He also forced four incompletions, intercepted two passes, recorded 51 solo tackles and notched three TFLs. He may help fill former Bills CB Taron Johnson’s vacated slot cornerback role. The Bills traded Johnson to the Raiders on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.headline: Bears signed CB C.J. Gardner-Johnson, formerly of the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.analysis: Gardner-Johnson will reunite with Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen, who coached him in New Orleans from 2019 to 2021. The mercurial cornerback will join a Chicago defense that has allowed the NFL’s fourth highest drop back success rate and the second highest completion rate over expected this season. Look for Gardner-Johnson, who has 18 interceptions over 77 NFL games, to primarily play slot corner in Chicago.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.headline: Ravens released C.J. Gardner-Johnson from their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.analysis: The 27-year-old safety asked for his release after the Ravens traded for Alohi Gilman.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.headline: Ravens signed S C.J. Gardner-Johnson to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.analysis: The Texans released Gardner-Johnson after Week 3 and much came out about him freelancing, blowing assignments, and complaining about his role. The Ravens defense is at a juncture where they’d probably take that if it came with some competent NFL-level play, too.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.headline: Texans released S C.J. Gardner-Johnson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.analysis: What was your favorite moment of the Gardner-Johnson era in Houston? He did play 96 percent of the snaps for the Texans in three weeks, so it’s a loss. NBC’s Aaron Wilson reports there was “friction behind the scenes” behind the release, with Gardner-Johnson “complaining about his role, wanting to blitz more, per league sources, and even communicating that he wanted to be traded.” M.J. Stewart will take over at safety for the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.headline: Commanders placed DT Javon Kinlaw (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.analysis: Kinlaw was ruled out for Sunday’s game against the Eagles and will now miss at least the next four games after landing on IR. Kinlaw has tallied 13 tackles and one sack for the Commanders this season and will be eligible to return in Week 13 when the Commanders take on the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.headline: Javon Kinlaw (knee) will not play in Washington’s Week 8 game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.analysis: He didn’t practice all week after Dan Quinn acknowledged it would be “tough” for him to play. An IR stint probably is in play on Saturday, if not, Kinlaw will probably start Week 9 on the questionable line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.headline: Javon Kinlaw (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.analysis: Kinlaw is dealing with a knee issue. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Wednesday it will “likely be tough” for the 29-year-old defensive tackle to play Sunday. We can expect Kinlaw to be on the wrong side of questionable for Week 8 against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.headline: Commanders DT Javon Kinlaw (back/shoulder) is not on Washington’s final Week 3 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.analysis: He was limited on Thursday and practiced in full today to avoid the questionable line. The 28-year-old defensive tackle can look forward to a Sunday of trying to stop Jadarian Price runs right up the gut.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.headline: Commanders DT Javon Kinlaw (back/shoulder) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.analysis: Kinlaw dealt with a back injury last week but played in Week 2. He came out of the loss against the Cowboys with an additional injury to the shoulder. Kinlaw’s status for Week 3 is in question as he sits out of practice with back and shoulder issues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.headline: Commanders HC Dan Quinn said RG Sam Cosmi is in concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.analysis: Cosmi will need to clear concussion protocol in time to play in Week 3’s home opener against the Seahawks. Cosmi took a hard helmet-to-helmet shot from teammate Kaytron Allen while trying to make a block and immediately went down on the field for several minutes. Rookie sixth-rounder Matt Gulbin took over in his absence and could be in line to draw the start for him next week if Cosmi is unable to play. Quinn also said DT Javon Kinlaw suffered a shoulder injury and LT Brandon Coleman suffered a finger injury in the loss.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.headline: Commanders DT Daron Payne was ejected from Week 10 against the Lions after committing an unnecessary roughness penalty.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.analysis: Payne was flagged after a hard-fought 13-yard touchdown run made by Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs. Payne can be clearly seen punching Lions WR Amon-Ra St. Brown on the left side of his facemask. Astonishingly, Commanders DT Javon Kinlaw was not ejected after striking a referee in the forehead, though he was penalized, after Payne was ejected. The Commanders also may have lost CB Trey Amos, who entered the game with a hip injury, and required two trainers’ assistance to leave the field after injuring his ankle on the play. Amos is currently questionable to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.headline: Commanders agreed to terms with DT Javon Kinlaw, formerly of the Jets, on a three-year, $45 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.analysis: Kinlaw will get $30 million in guaranteed money on this deal. A former 49er who was drafted No. 14 overall in 2020 reunites with general manager Adam Peters, who has already added two other former 49ers to the roster this offseason. Kinlaw signed a one-year deal with the Jets last offseason and posted career highs in tackles (40) and sacks (4.5) in his age-27-season. Turning 28 in October, Kinlaw could make for a nice addition if he’s able to live up to the potential that once made him the 14th pick in the draft.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.headline: Jets agreed to terms with DT Javon Kinlaw, formerly of the 49ers, on a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.analysis: With his career derailed by his 2021 ACL tear, Kinlaw started just six games last season, though he did appear in all 17. He notched a career-high four sacks but earned horrid PFF pass-rushing marks in the process. Going on 27, Kinlaw isn’t exactly young and projectable. It’s a flier that is unlikely to pan out for Gang Green.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.headline: 49ers declined to exercise DL Javon Kinlaw’s fifth-year option.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javon-kinl.analysis: Kinlaw has played just 10 regular season games in two years and has yet to rebound from a 2021 ACL tear to become the same player he was as a prospect. Declining the option was a formality. The 49ers brought in Javon Hargrave to take Kinlaw’s place in the starting lineup this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.headline: Commanders placed RB Jeremy McNichols (foot) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.analysis: McNichols is believed to have suffered a severe foot injury in Sunday night’s win over the Eagles. While he is still seeking additional opinions, it was reported on Monday that he is expected to miss multiple months, which could mean this is a season-ender. McNichols has spent the last three seasons with the Commanders, contributing primarily on special teams while also mixing in for an occasional offensive play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jeremy McNichols is undergoing additional testing to determine the severity of the foot injury he suffered in Week 8’s win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.analysis: McNichols’ injury is believed to be “significant,” according to Schefter. The 30-year-old journeyman was recently activated from injured reserve after missing the first five weeks of the season with a quad injury and could now be looking at another extended absence. He has rushed 10 times for 34 scoreless yards this season and has been a reliable role player and special teams contributor for the Commanders since joining the team in 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.headline: Commanders activated Jeremy McNichols (quad) off injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.analysis: He’ll likely be Washington’s third-string back tonight, but one thing that two years and five weeks of Dan Quinn being in charge have taught us is that no one ever expects that Jeremy McNichols takeover until it’s too late. The backfield mix in Washington is weak and anyone could emerge in a post-'Bill’ world.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.headline: Austin Ekeler (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.analysis: Ekeler and Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) are both ailing, though the latter player sat out entirely. Rachaad White (shoulder) and Jeremy McNichols (quad) are both practicing in full. Croskey-Merritt is the only fantasy-relevant Commanders running back at this time, assuming he is good to go on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.headline: Commanders placed RB Jeremy McNichols (quad) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.analysis: McNichols will start the season sidelined with a linger quad injury he suffered in mid-August. Used primarily as a pass-catching back, McNichols could see playing time later this season if Rachaad White or Jacory Croskey-Merritt miss any time. He will miss at least the first four games of the season and should remain on waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Jeremy McNichols (quad) will be sidelined a few weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.analysis: McNichols probably is no higher than fourth on the depth chart in Washington behind ‘Bill,’ Rachaad White, and Kaytron Allen. Missing time due to injury doesn’t bode well for him making the initial 53-man roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.headline: Commanders RB Jeremy McNichols (quad) is out Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.analysis: This is the second straight practice McNichols has missed with the quad issue. He’s slated to function as Washington’s No. 3 back behind some combination of Rachaad White and Jacory Croskey-Merritt this season. McNichols was efficient in 2025, averaging five yards per carry on 44 rushes in Washington.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.headline: Last Man Standig’s Ben Standig reports that Commanders RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (soft tissue) sat out the team’s three-week organized team activities program.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.analysis: Whether Croskey-Merritt can participate in the Commanders’ three-day mandatory minicamp, from June 16-18, is unknown. That said, Standig believes RB coach Anthony Lynn’s “positivity is notable.” Lynn thinks the team can take Croskey-Merritt’s game “to another level and get him potentially in the lead role.” To do this, Croskey-Merritt must take on more responsibility in the passing game this summer. Lynn adds that the young back’s “hands are very good, his movement skills are very good, and there’s no reason why he couldn’t win routes.” The staff is happy with its new-look backfield, but Standing writes that RBs Rachaad White, Jeremy McNichols and Jerome Ford “are not high-volume playmaking threats,” like “Bill” is, and rookie RB Allen is still getting up to speed. Once Croskey-Merritt arrives, he must prove that he can meaningfully contribute as a receiver and as a pass protector. Doing so would unlock a fantasy-friendly role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.headline: Commanders re-signed RB Jeremy McNichols to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.analysis: McNichols is the third running back to sign with Washington in recent days. The 30-year-old vet has been used sparingly over the last two seasons with the Commanders, but has totaled 705 yards from scrimmage and five touchdowns on 133 touches. McNichols would likely have a camp battle with Jerome Ford to play on passing downs on the current depth chart, meaning he could be in some risk of starting off the year on the practice squad. But after playing 34 games with the Commanders the last two years, we think it’s clear the current administration thinks highly of him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.headline: Jeremy McNichols rushed one time for three yards in the Commanders’ Week 18 win over the Eagles, adding one reception for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.analysis: McNichols spent the season as the Commanders’ pass-catching back after Austin Ekeler tore his Achilles at the beginning of the season. He broke several tackles on a Beast Mode-esque 60-yard touchdown run in Week 3; that run was his only rushing touchdown and accounted for 27 percent of his rushing yards for the season. McNichols totaled 44 carries for 221 yards and a touchdown on the ground but often saw more passing-down snaps than rushing snaps, adding 25 receptions for 196 yards through the air. He will be a free agent heading into the offseason and could find a home as a pass-catching depth piece for a team’s backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adetomiwa-.headline: Colts signed DT Adetomiwa Adebawore to a two-year, $35 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adetomiwa-.analysis: Adebawore, 25, is in the midst of a breakout season for the Colts. After setting career highs in tackles (36), TFLs (5), and sacks (4.0) last season, the fourth-year pro has already tallied four sacks and four TFLs in his first eight games of this season. While the Colts are in the middle of a rebuild, the decision to sign Adebawore to an extension means he’s one of the players they hope to build around in the years ahead. He is now under contract through the 2028 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adetomiwa-.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the Colts have told teams they won’t move Adetomiwa Adebawore.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adetomiwa-.analysis: Adebawore, a fourth-round pick in 2023, played under 200 snaps in each of his first two seasons and was a pass-rush specialist in 2025. In 2026, he’s taken a step forward, with an 81.8 PFF grade buoyed by an 86.3 pass rush grade. It would be reasonable to expect the Colts to try to extend a player like this, but they sure didn’t seem to have any urgency to do it before the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adetomiwa-.headline: Colts selected Northwestern DT Adetomiwa Adebawore with the No. 110 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/adetomiwa-.analysis: Despite lacking the desired length for edge work and having a three-tech frame, Adebawore (6’2/282) is one of the great athletic marvels from the 2023 NFL Draft class. His 4.49s 40-yard dash is the 10th fastest edge time in the history of the NFL Scouting Combine. If that weren’t impressive enough, he did it at 282 pounds which is 20+ pounds heavier than every single one of the 10 edge players ahead of him on that list (Amare Barno #1 All Time - 4.37). Though he had been a primary edge for his first three years on Northwestern’s campus, last year he logged 261 reps in the B-Gap compared to 440 on the outside. Adeboware’s 80.3 PFF pass rush grade is very solid, but there’s plenty of room for improvement in the run game as Adebawore missed 25.5% of his tackle attempts this year. A success story who bulldozed his way through just about every OL put in front of him last season, He was being considered as a likely mid-Day 3 pedestrian contributor before he took over the Senior Bowl’s 1-on-1 blocking sessions. While there is still some question about whether he plays three tech or edge, Adebawore has tantalizing traits that cannot be taught with an athletic profile of a faster, more agile Ed Oliver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Cardinals placed Jeremiyah Love (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: The new injury Love picked up in Week 8’s win over the Cowboys has been diagnosed as a high-ankle sprain and will sideline Love for a minimum of four weeks. Love, who has been dealing with multiple ankle injuries this season, has had a tough start to his NFL career. In six career games he’s rushed for 268 yards and one touchdown on 76 carries, while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and another score. His injury comes as Bam Knight is in the league’s concussion protocol, leaving Tyler Allgeier and Evan Hull as the only two healthy backs on the Cardinals’ 53-man roster. Allgeier could be in line for a significant role in Week 9 against the Seahawks if Knight is unable to clear protocol, and veteran Jerome Ford could also be promoted from the practice squad in the coming days. Love will not be eligible to return until Week 13 against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love is dealing with a new ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: According to LaFleur, the injury is to “a new portion of the ankle” that Love hadn’t previously injured. LaFleur didn’t dismiss the possibility of Love being placed on injured reserve, suggesting he would wait until Wednesday to decide if that is on the table. A tough rookie season only gets tougher for Love, who sounds like he will be at risk of missing more time even if he isn’t an IR candidate. Meanwhile, Bam Knight, who left Week 8’s game with a concussion, is in the league’s protocol, making Tyler Allgeier the only healthy back on the roster entering Week 9 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) left Arizona’s Week 8 game against the Cowboys and is questionable to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: His right ankle was rolled up on at the end of a running play and Love immediately slammed his helmet after walking off. He later went to the locker room with trainers and then was officially dubbed questionable. Not great. Love finished with nine carries for 23 yards, including a fourth-and-1 go at the goalline that he didn’t convert. We’ll see what reports say after the game but given Love has already missed time with ankle injuries this year, it’s hard to be optimistic about his status for next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will play in Week 8 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: After missing the last two games with an ankle injury, Love will return to the Cardinals in what could be a three-way split after the recent emergence of Bam Knight. Love was averaging 16.2 opportunities per game before being sidelined, with most of that work coming on the ground. With only two top-24 PPR performances to his name so far this season, he shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a boom-or-bust RB2 against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) was listed as a limited participant in practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: That’s a second straight limited session for Love. The Cardinals are taking this slowly with the 21-year-old ahead of a potential return in Week 8 against the Cowboys, but fantasy managers will obviously need to pay close attention to how much he practices Friday and his injury designation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will be limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: We were hoping to see Love practice in full after taking two weeks off. While today’s limited session puts him on track to play in Week 8 against the Cowboys, Bam Knight and Tyler Allgeier are still worth stashing on benches, just in case. The Cardinals are finally handling Love’s recovery patiently, after giving him far too many touches early in the preseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is expected to practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: This news comes from head coach Mike LaFleur, who spoke with the media on Monday. After missing the last two games with a nagging ankle issue, Love’s return to the field in any capacity suggests he could have a chance to suit up in Week 8 against the Cowboys. Love’s ankle injury slowed his production through the first five weeks of the season, with the rookie saying at one point that he would “probably just hinder the team” if he had to play through it. Love’s status will be one to watch throughout the week, but even if he’s active, he’ll likely be forced to split touches with either Tyler Allgeier or Bam Knight, who has been solid in Love’s absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will not play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Things have been trending in this direction all week, but LaFleur officially confirmed on Friday that Love will miss a second straight game. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will likely split duties again in Week 7 after seeing a near 50/50 split in the touch distribution last week, with Allgeier’s 19 touches narrowly edging out Knight’s 17. Both Allgeier and Knight are fringe RB2/RB3 plays against a stout Broncos defense. In addition to Love the Cardinals also ruled out DT Walter Nolen III (ankle), S Andrew Wiggins (ankle), and OG Jo Gaines II (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is not expected to play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Love didn’t practice on Wednesday and Thursday after missing Week 6. It doesn’t sound like he will practice at all this week. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will split the backfield again this week. Allgeier out-carried Knight 18-15 last week, but Knight was far more effective, running for 80 yards in total. Allgeier posted just 38 yards. He still figures to be the lead runner this week, but Allgeier shine as a plug-and-play RB2 is waning headed into Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Love starts out not practicing for the second straight week due to an ankle injury. He missed Week 6 against the Rams and a DNP Wednesday puts him on the wrong side of questionable to play in Week 7 against the Broncos. Love will need to practice in some capacity to have a chance of playing this week, but Tyler Allgeier is back in the RB2 range if Love cannot go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.headline: Ravens signed QB Kedon Slovis from the Packers practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.analysis: Slovis could, unbelievably, get the start Thursday night against the Jaguars with Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) out, and Joe Fagnano (ankle) iffy to suit up. If Fagnano can play, Slovis would presumably serve as Baltimore’s backup. Fagnano completed 48 percent of his passes for 91 yards and a pick last week against the Bills. Look for the Ravens to be ultra run-heavy against Jacksonville, one of the league’s best run defenses. It will be tough to trust anyone in the Ravens offense as a viable fantasy option for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.headline: Cardinals waived QB Kedon Slovis.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.analysis: Slovis needed to unseat QB Gardner Minshew or QB Carson Beck to make the roster. He was unable to do so. He could return to Arizona via the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.headline: Cardinals ruled out QB Carson Beck (rib) for the team’s preseason Week 1 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.analysis: According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Beck suffered a rib injury in the Cardinals’ Hall of Fame game against the Panthers. Despite feeling “soreness,” he managed to practice this week. The Cardinals “decided to keep him out tonight as a precaution and to allow more time to heal.” This pours a little cold water on Beck’s moderate hype, but the reporting suggests that the injury is not overly concerning. Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett will start, and presumably be relieved by QB Kedon Slovis at some point. No word yet on QB Gardner Minshew’s potential involvement tonight.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.headline: When asked about the Cardinals’ starting quarterback job, general manager Monti Ossenfort said, “we’ll see how that room looks by the time we get in August.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.analysis: This doesn’t tell us a whole lot. Readers might recall that the 2026 NFL Draft is next week, and the Cardinals hosted Alabama QB Ty Simpson for a top-30 visit yesterday. If the Cardinals do not draft a rookie quarterback, Jacoby Brissett will likely be the default starter, with only Gardner Minshew and Kedon Slovis joining him on the roster at this time. If that is the case, the pass catchers likely stand to benefit. Brissett was able to distribute the ball effectively last year. Rolling with a developmental rookie could hurt the receiving outlooks for TE Trey McBride, WR Michael Wilson and WR Marvin Harrison Jr.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.headline: Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett exited Week 12 against the Jaguars after suffering an apparent injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.analysis: Brissett was hurt on a third-quarter scramble. The Cardinals’ quarterback was trotting out of bounds after picking up a short gain on the ground when Jaguars LB Devin Lloyd lowered his shoulder, hitting Brissett hard, up high, from the left side. Brissett remained down after the play, and eventually made his way to the blue medical tent. He was replaced by QB Kedon Slovis.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.headline: Cardinals signed QB Kedon Slovis.
