https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.analysis: Slovis returns to his home state of Arizona after three preseason appearances with the Texans. He completed 27-of-43 passes for 233 yards, one touchdown and one interception and rushed three times for seven yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.headline: Texans released QB Kedon Slovis.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.analysis: Slovis was unable to make the Texans to the surprise of absolutely no one. The 24-year-old is a candidate for the practice squad of Houston or another team looking for signal-caller depth.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.headline: Texans signed OG Braeden Daniels, formerly of the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.analysis: Daniels’ 2023 rookie season was derailed by a torn rotator cuff. His new landing spot will hopefully allow him to compete for a backup role for a Texans’ squad that was likewise hit by significant injuries last year. Also signed by the Texans on Thursday were TE Cole Fotheringham, WR Xavier Johnson, S Mark Perry and QB Kedon Slovis.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.headline: Colts signed BYU QB Kedon Slovis.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.analysis: Slovis’ (6’2/223) career began at USC in 2019, but after losing the starting job to former No. 1 overall prospect Jaxson Dart in 2021, he made the jump to Pittsburgh in 2022 to replace Kenny Pickett. A down season at Pitt in which he threw for 2397-10-9 led to him transferring to BYU in 2023, where he nearly replicated those numbers (1716-12-6) over eight games played. Slovis ran a 4.55 at the NFL Scouting Combine, but his speed didn’t lead to much production as a dual threat, as he managed just 242 career rushing yards in college per PFF. Slovis could get a chance to earn a spot on the practice squad but we wouldn’t expect much more at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.headline: Pittsburgh junior quarterback Kedon Slovis could raise his draft stock once more in 2022.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kedon-slovis/0.analysis: Slovis (6'3/205) was considered one of the top quarterbacks in the nation ahead of the 2022 college football season, but fell off as turmoil built up at USC and head coach Clay Helton was fired. Not all of the misfortune should be pinned on Slovis, who could experience a resurgence as he transitions from an Air Raid system to more of a pro-style system at Pitt. Anthony Treash of Pro Football Focus recently released his Top 10 QB list, pinning Slovis as the ninth-best quarterback in all of college football. It will be interesting to see if that holds true in the fall.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said the team’s backfield touch distribution will be a “moving target.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Mike Washington, Jr. in Week 8 against the Jets took over as the team’s lead rusher, logging 25 carries to just two carries for Ashton Jeanty. While Kubiak said after the game that Jeanty would remain a part of the offense, it’s clear the Raiders are willing to experiment with backfield touches. “You see where your team is at and who’s playing the best ball at the time. It’s a 17-game regular season where things change every week. They’ve been changing at guard, they change up front defensively, they change at corner,” Kubiak said. “That’s the NFL. We have a young roster and we’re going to give guys opportunities and see what fits us best. But your 11, whether you’re playing really well or not playing well at all, it’s always going to change a little bit.” The Raiders through Week 8 rank dead last in EPA per rush and second to last in rushing success rate. Jeanty should remain viable as long as he’s the team’s primary pass catcher out of the backfield. Jeanty ranks fifth among all RBs in expected fantasy points per game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty rushed two times for nine yards in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets, adding three receptions for 64 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Jeanty was benched as the Raiders’ early-down back, getting out-carried 25-2 by Mike Washington Jr. For his part, Washington was not effective, churning up just 3.3 yards per carry and getting stoned on a bevy of goal-line handles. Speaking afterward, coach Klint Kubiak said the move was his call but that "(Jeanty) is still going to be a big part of our team.” Jeanty made waves during the week when he said the Jets could not tackle. Rather than let the struggling second-year back prove his theory on the field, the Raiders made the takedown themselves for the Jets. While it’s clear Jeanty is now in a true timeshare, we do also take Kubiak at his word that Jeanty will remain a “big part” of the team, almost certainly with double-digit carries more weeks than not. The question is if he can keep catching enough passes to hold RB2 status. Washington is now the preferred short-yardage back, but his failures in Sunday’s highest-leverage spots could keep the door ajar for Jeanty.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty had eight rushes for 15 yards in the Raiders’ Week 7 loss to the Rams, adding eight catches for 61 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Among the least efficient rushers in the game, Jeanty again struggled to get anything going on the ground behind a middling Vegas offensive line. He did almost all of his damage through the air, turning eight targets into 61 yards and a late score in garbage time. He ran a route on 20 of the team’s 35 drop backs against the Rams and ranked second among Raiders pass catchers in targets. Mike Washington had six carries on the day. Jeanty, with at least six targets in six of his seven games this season, can maintain RB2 status as long as he’s catching passes out of the backfield. He gets the Jets in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Mike Washington (foot/back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Dang. This suggests Washington suffered one or both injuries yesterday in practice. He is firmly in the questionable camp and may have only a long shot at suiting up in Week 7 against the Rams. Without him, Ashton Jeanty should handle a solid workload. Dylan Laube could end up serving as the No. 2 running back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty rushed 10 times for 22 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills, adding four receptions for 36 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Jeanty, who is dealing with a foot/ankle injury, wasn’t effective on the ground, but that didn’t stop him from scoring his first rushing touchdown of the season. Jeanty punched in a one-yard score in the first quarter of Sunday’s game to give the Raiders an early 7-3 lead, but averaged a disappointing 2.2 YPC overall. He did manage a solid 4-36-0 receiving line on six targets, with two of his four receptions coming on the Raiders’ third drive of the game. Jeanty appeared on 15 more snaps than Mike Washington and out-touched him 14 to 10. While he continues to struggle from an efficiency standpoint, Jeanty’s volume will make him a low-end RB1 next week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty (foot) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: The Raiders’ starting running back is good to go for what should be a fantasy-friendly game environment. The Raiders encouragingly stopped listing Jeanty with an ankle injury this week. Hopefully, his remaining plantar fasciitis issue subsides before long as well. Jeanty is a low-end RB1 in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty (foot) said he is feeling “great” and “ready to go” for Week 6 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: The quotes read a tad bit more enthusiastically than Jeanty did while speaking to media members at his locker, but this is still good to hear. Jeanty has been dealing with an ankle injury for a long time, but the team took that injury off the weekly practice report this week. He is now listed only with the foot injury after experiencing “a flare-up of plantar fasciitis” last Friday. Jeanty is a low-end RB1 against the Bills this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty (foot) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Jeanty’s previous ankle designation was removed from the injury report and he was a full practice participant on Wednesday. His practice participation lines up with Raiders coach Klint Kubiak saying the 22-year-old running back was starting to “feel a lot better.” Though there were rumors of the Raiders resting Jeanty for a week, he is trending to play in Week 6 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Ashton Jeanty (foot/ankle) is starting to “feel a lot better.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Kubiak also shot down the idea of the Raiders resting Jeanty for a week, despite it being reported earlier today that the Raiders were considering giving him a week off to recover at some point. Jeanty has been dreadfully inefficient this year, averaging a meager 3.3 yards per carry, though the team’s subpar offensive line also deserves some of the blame. For fantasy purposes, his workload has been the big draw. He is averaging 22 touches per game through five weeks. Even if the foot and ankle injuries continue to bother him, Jeanty has to be treated as a mid-range RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty had 10 rushes for 27 yards in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots, adding three catches for 50 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Most of Jeanty’s production against New England came on a 31-yard catch and run in the third quarter. Battling through foot and ankle injuries, Jeanty looked hobbled from the start and struggled to break tackles or outrun Patriots defenders to the edge. Most Raiders starters rested in the fourth quarter of a lopsided loss. Jeanty still doesn’t have a rushing touchdown on the season and hasn’t had 100 rushing yards in a game since Week 1 against the Dolphins. Until Jeanty is fully healthy he probably won’t provide much in the way of upside, including next week against a decent Buffalo run defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.headline: AJ Barner caught 2-of-5 targets for 23 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 8 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.analysis: Barner is far from fantasy consideration having only one game through eight appearances with more than a modest five targets while failing to notch a single receiving touchdown. Fantasy managers can safely return him to the waiver wire in all formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.headline: AJ Barner caught 4-of-5 targets for 42 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 7 win over the Chiefs, adding four yards on three carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.analysis: All three carries for Barner were tush push plays that resulted in first downs in key situations, while his five targets tied his second most of the young season. Even so, that was not enough to return a usable fantasy week outside of tight end premium leagues, keeping Barner best left on the bench or returned to the waiver wire, regardless of the severity of Rashid Shaheed’s injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.headline: AJ Barner caught 3-of-5 targets for 20 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 5 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.analysis: Barner continues to be a non-factor in the Seahawks’ passing game. Outside of a Week 3 game against the Commanders in which he went for 5-69-0 on nine targets, Barner has totaled 53 yards in his other four games combined and has yet to find the end zone this season. Barner won’t be on the streaming radar in Week 6, even with four teams on bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.headline: AJ Barner caught 1-of-3 targets for 12 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 4 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.analysis: After a solid effort against the the Commanders where he caught five passes for 69 yards, Barner was once again a non-factor in this one. The 24-year-old is clearly the top tight end in the passing attack, but outside of Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the rest of the options just haven’t done much. He’ll be a boom or bust TE1 for Week 5 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.headline: AJ Barner caught 5-of-9 targets for 69 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 3 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.analysis: It was easily Barner’s best receiving day of the year, although he was unable to find the end zone. His nine targets were second on the team behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s 14, and it’s clear he and Sam Darnold have more of a connection than he did with Drew Lock. Barner will be on the TE1 precipice for Week 4 against the Chargers, but this was encouraging.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.headline: AJ Barner caught 1-of-1 targets for eight yards in the Seahawks’ Week 2 win over the Cardinals, adding one rush for one yard and one touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.analysis: Up 24-7 on 4th-and-goal with just over three minutes left in the game, the Seahawks started a fresh set of downs from the Cardinals’ three-yard line. Both RB George Holani and RB Emanuel Wilson were given chances to punch it in before Seahawks OC Brian Fleury dialed up a Tush Push play for Barner on 4th-and-goal. Barner jumped up and across the line, bringing his fantasy stat line from something unusable to something we can live with. He remains a boom-bust TE1 against the Commanders next week. Seahawks TE2 Elijah Arroyo nabbed a 17-yard pass on a post route, but that was it for him. So far, the Seahawks’ reported uptick in usage for the tight end position has not panned out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.headline: A.J. Barner caught both of his targets for 13 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 1 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.analysis: Barner also had a tush push attempt that was called back by a penalty. With Jaxon Smith-Njigba soaking up 11 targets on just 24 team pass attempts, there wasn’t much volume to go around for the rest of the Seattle pass-catchers. Barner only topped four catches in 20 combined regular and postseason appearances last year. If Week 1 is any indication, he won’t be putting up big box scores very often this season either. He will barely crack the TE2 ranks when Seattle takes on Arizona next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.headline: Seahawks TE AJ Barner (oblique) is practicing in full for Week 1 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.analysis: The Seahawks’ starting tight end is firmly on track to play in the 2026 season opener on Wednesday night. Barner is reportedly set to handle a bigger role than he did last year, when he finished as the PPR TE14. He can only be viewed as a borderline TE1/2 early on, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.headline: The Athletic’s Andrew Destin believes Seahawks TE AJ Barner “will likely see an uptick in production, as should backup TE Elijah Arroyo” this year.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.analysis: Destin notes that new Seahawks OC Brian Fleury served as the 49ers’ TE coach for four seasons “and is expected to feature the position prominently.” Aside from that, and an increase in shifts and motion, he thinks the offense is “going to look very similar” to last year. Barner underwent two offseason surgeries, one of which was to address a nagging ankle injury that Barner said he initially suffered during the 2024 Senior Bowl before the Seahawks drafted him. After turning in the PPR TE14 performance last season, Barner might have a shot to crack the position’s top 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler believes AJ Barner is an “ascending” player in the Seahawks offense.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-barner/.analysis: Fowlers said the team expects Barner to be more involved as a pass catcher in 2026 after recording 52 receptions for 519 yards and six touchdowns last season (while being targeted on 19 percent of his routes). Barner, following multiple offseason surgeries to clean up nagging injuries, is fully healthy and ready for a more prominent role in Seattle’s offense. New Seahawks offensive coordinator Brian Fleury, meanwhile, is expected to use plenty of two tight end sets in 2026, meaning TE Elijah Arroyo could see an increase in snaps and routes. Barner has a little bit of extra hidden upside as the Seahawks’ primary tush push option near the goal line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tory Horton caught 3-of-6 targets for 26 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 8 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Horton took more massive hits than he had receptions in this one, with Sam Darnold placing him in harms way on more than one occasion. He was already fighting through nagging injuries entering the contest but gave it a go with Rashid Shaheed ruled out, with this game likely doing nothing to help him in that regard. Despite finishing second on the team in receiving behind alpha Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Horton is not a startable fantasy asset ahead of a Week 9 meeting with the division rival Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tory Horton caught his only target for a six-yard touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 4 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Horton’s lone catch was a six-yard slant from Sam Darnold. The 23-year-old wideout has just four catches in his first two games, and clearly is well behind the top three wideouts in the passing game. Whether that should be — with all due respect to Cooper Kupp (held without a catch Sunday) and Rashid Shaheed (one reception) is a different question. For now, Horton is off the radar for Week 5 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tory Horton caught all three targets for 48 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 3 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It was only three catches, but it was a reminder that Horton looked like he was on his way to being a relevant player before his injuries as a rookie last year. With Cooper Kupp no longer close to an elite option and Rashid Shaheed a non-factor thus far, one can’t help but wonder if Horton will get more opportunities now that he’s healthy. Fantasy managers should at least keep an eye on him, but shouldn’t have him in a lineup for Week 4 against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Seahawks WR Tory Horton (hamstring) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Horton’s return boosts QB Drew Lock’s passing outlook, though Horton is not worth starting in 12-team FLEX spots, operating in the Seahawks WR4 role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Seahawks WR Tory Horton (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Horton missed Week 1, dealing with a hamstring injury from training camp. He now finally gets in a full practice, opening Week 2 with a full participation designation. The Seahawks are preparing for the 23-year-old to return against the Cardinals, though Horton is best left off fantasy rosters with Drew Lock the starting quarterback for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Seahawks WR Tory Horton (hamstring) is inactive for Week 1 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Horton got in some limited practices earlier this week as he deals with a hamstring injury. He will miss opening week against the Patriots, boosting Rashid Shaheed for some deep targets in Week 1. Also inactive for the Seahawks are S Nick Emmanwori, G Beau Stephens, QB Jalen Milroe, TE Nick Kallerup, S Ty Okada, and DE Mike Morris. Milroe will serve as the emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tory Horton (hamstring) is questionable for Seattle’s Week 1 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Even if Horton does play, he’s unlikely to be more than the fourth receiver behind Rashid Shaheed, Cooper Kupp and all-world Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The second-year receiver looked great early in 2025 but has dealt with a ton of injuries ever since, leading the Seahawks to their midseason trade for Shaheed last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Seahawks WR Tory Horton (hamstring) was limited in practice Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It was the second straight day with the same level of participation for the second-year receiver, who could be headed for a game-day injury designation for the team’s season opener. We were kept in the dark regarding Horton’s ailment after he missed the final three weeks of camp, with a hamstring injury now labeled as the cause. Although Jake Bobo’s season-ending ACL tear all but guaranteed Horton a spot on game-day rosters, he remains unlikely to contribute meaningful counting stats playing behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Rashid Shaheed, and Cooper Kupp. Second-year undrafted free agent Montorie Foster Jr would be in line to serve as the team’s fourth receiver on Wednesday should Horton be unable to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Seahawks WR Tory Horton (hamstring) was limited on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Now we know what has kept Horton sidelined since mid-August. Although the speedy wide receiver has resumed practicing, which is a good sign, he is not guaranteed to suit up. If active, he is likely only relevant in single-game DFS contests.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said WR Tory Horton’s (undisclosed) “injury isn’t a long-term thing.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Frankly, it is tough to trust this statement. The Seahawks kept things quiet almost all offseason about Horton’s season-ending shin injury. They do not have to disclose anything until Week 1 practices begin. Were he to miss time in the regular season, WR Rashid Shaheed might be able to earn an extra target or two, operating as the team’s uncontested field stretcher.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Cooper Kupp caught 1-of-3 targets for seven yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 8 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp was unable to take advantage of the absence of fellow receiver Rashid Shaheed but did cash in for his second touchdown of the season. Kupp’s days of consistent fantasy production are long behind him as the Seahawks head into a Week 9 divisional meeting against the Cardinals approaching must-win territory.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Cooper Kupp caught both targets for 20 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 7 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp saw sparse usage as Jaxon Smith-Njigba went off in the first half and the team transitioned to a run-heavy approach while playing with a lead after the break. Fellow receiver Rashid Shaheed departed with a knee injury following a collision with Smith-Njigba in the end zone at the end of the second quarter, which is something managers will will want to monitor ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the Bears on Monday Night Football. Kupp could work his way into the FLEX discussion if Shaheed misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Cooper Kupp caught 5-of-10 targets for 50 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 6 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp’s 10 targets finished second on the team behind alpha Jaxon Smith-Njigba but were largely a product of 51 Sam Darnold pass attempts in game that had all the ingredients for increased pass volume, including an inability to run the football, negative game script, and overtime. It continues to appear as if Kupp’s fantasy-relevant days are far behind him, with the veteran best left on the waiver wire ahead of a Week 7 showdown against the Chiefs on deck.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Cooper Kupp caught 4-of-5 targets for 46 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 3 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp took advantage of the Commanders double-teaming Jaxon Smith-Njigba and walked into the end zone on the fourth touchdown throw from Sam Darnold. It’s his first score of the season, and it’s a season high in receiving yards for the former star. Kupp will try and build on this in Week 4 in a matchup against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp will be available for QB Sam Darnold (glute), who makes his return from his Week 1 injury. Kupp is a mild FLEX option, facing a soft Commanders’ coverage unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp will not be fantasy-relevant in 12-team managed leagues this week, but he could be an option in single-game DFS tournaments. If QB Sam Darnold (glute) can play, he will appreciate having Kupp on the field with him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp also opened last week with a limited practice due to the back injury before getting in two full practices and playing in Week 2. His limited designation Wednesday is likely a continuation of veteran workload management for his back; fantasy managers should not be surprised to see the 33-year-old limited on Wednesdays this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Cooper Kupp caught 2-of-2 targets for 20 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 2 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp got involved on the Seahawks’ fifth and sixth drives, but was quiet outside of that. The 33-year-old wide receiver entered the game with a back injury, though he logged two full practice sessions, so it is unlikely to have meaningfully impacted him. He nabbed his second reception during the Seahawks’ two-minute drill at the end of the first half, but he was unable to get out of bounds, allowing precious seconds to tick away. Kupp is a WR5/FLEX against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) is not on the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: Kupp, 33, is good to go against the Cardinals. He was limited on Wednesday, but upgraded to full on Thursday and Friday. With QB Drew Lock under center, Kupp’s outlook is a little more volatile. He should be viewed as just a boom-bust FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.headline: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp (back) practiced in full on Thursday,
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-kup.analysis: The 33-year-old wide receiver should play in Week 2 against the Cardinals, although he is just a boom-bust FLEX starter at this point. Kupp does not need to be in 12-team lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 6-of-11 targets for 118 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 8 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba was the entire offense in the first half, accumulating 92 yards through the air while the rest of the offense managed only two, including his receiving touchdown. Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen made adjustments after the break that confined JSN to only 26 additional yards the rest of the way. Smith-Njigba now has seven 100-yard receiving games in eight appearances as he extended his league-leading yardage totals, clear and away the top overall wide receiver in fantasy circles. That position will not change ahead of a Week 9 meeting with the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 9-of-12 targets for 150 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 7 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Is there anyone in the league doing it better than Smith-Njigba at the moment? The reigning receiving leader put on an absolute show in this one, making two nearly identical bread basket catches down the left sideline in the second quarter, the first of which he snuck inside the pylon for his touchdown. He was forced out at the two on the second, resulting in an end zone interception from Sam Darnold two plays later. Those two long receptions before the break helped push Smith-Njigba to 126 yards and a touchdown before halftime, and he added an additional 24 yards on three more receptions in the final two frames as the Seahawks transitioned to a more ground-heavy attack while playing with the lead. Fantasy’s early-season cheat code has now gone over 100 yards in six of seven games while notching a league-leading eight receiving touchdowns. It goes without saying, but Smith-Njigba remains the overall WR1 in a solid matchup against the Bears in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 12-of-16 targets for 134 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 6 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba overcame a sluggish first half to extend his stranglehold on the overall WR1 in fantasy circles with a dominant second half and overtime period. While the 51 pass attempts from Sam Darnold were highly uncharacteristic of this Seattle offense, a complete inability to run the football paired with a negative script to form the perfect environment for Smith-Njigba to set a season high in targets and receptions. Smith-Njigba has now gone over 100 yards in five of six appearances to start the 2026 regular season and is in a good spot to continue that dominance when the Seahawks host the Chiefs in Week 7, where he remains a top-tier WR1 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) has no injury designation ahead of the Seahawks’ Week 6 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba played through an ankle injury in Week 5 and was limited in practice this week before getting a full designation on Wednesday. Despite the short week ahead of a Thursday matchup against the Broncos, he is off the injury report and good to go. Smith-Njigba is once again a top-three wide receiver option for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) was listed as a limited practice participant on Tuesday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Smith-Njigba gets a second-straight “limited” practice designation. The Seahawks have technically not practiced yet this week but it is notably the 24-year-old receiver gets back-to-back limited designations. With a Thursday matchup against the Broncos on the horizon for Week 6, the Seahawks are leaving the door open for Smith-Njigba to play; he battled the ankle injury in Week 5 and the short week makes this a tougher evaluation. For now, we still expect Smith-Njigba to play against the Broncos on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Seahawks listed Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) as limited on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: With the Seahawks preparing to face the Broncos on a short week, it would be a bit more concerning if JSN were listed as a DNP. The team listing him as limited on the first day of the week is encouraging after he clearly battled through an ankle injury in Week 5’s loss to the 49ers. Smith-Njigba still topped 100 receiving yards for the fourth time this season and made several big plays despite being in visible pain. We’ll continue to update his practice status throughout the week, but as long as he’s active come Thursday, JSN should be in your fantasy lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 5-of-8 targets for 102 yards and one touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 5 loss to the 49ers, adding one rush for 16 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: JSN appeared to be playing through a bit of an ankle injury in this one, but he looked perfectly fine when he turned what would have been a short two-yard reception upfield for a 16-yard touchdown in the third quarter. In the fourth quarter, as the Seahawks were attempting a comeback, JSN hauled in a 35-yard reception, evading multiple defenders to get the Seahawks to the 50-yard line. A few plays later, he would drop a wide-open pass that may have set the Seahawks up for a game-winning field goal opportunity, but JSN did his part to keep the Seahawks in what proved to be a sloppy game for the offense as a whole. He’s gone for 100-plus yards in four of his first five games of the season and will look for his fifth 100-yard game on Thursday night when the Seahawks visit the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 5-of-6 targets for 78 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 4 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: For the first time this year, Smith-Njigba was held out of the end zone. It was a quiet day fore the star wideout, but if 78 yards is your worst day (so far), well, you’ve had a pretty good season. JSN and fantasy managers will hope for a return to the end zone and a little more volume against the 49ers in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 10-of-14 targets for 128 yards and two touchdowns in the Seahawks’ Week 3 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: Goodness gracious. Smith-Njigba did have a drop, but it was yet another dominant effort for the 24-year-old. His first touchdown saw him fake a fade route only to comeback to the pylon for an easy six, and then he and Sam Darnold connected for a second time on a pass over the middle in the end zone. That’s already six touchdowns in three games for the 24-year-old, and he’s reached the century mark in all three contests. On top of that, he also completed a 14-yard pass. Asking for this kind of red-zone production every week is tough, but he’s more than capable of these kind of fireworks. Obviously. JSN will be a WR1 and then some for Week 4 against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 9-of-11 targets for 155 yards and three touchdowns in the Seahawks’ Week 2 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaxon-smit.analysis: On the Seahawks’ second play from scrimmage, a Cardinals safety somehow failed to pick up Smith-Njigba, streaking down the right sideline, after he snuck right past CB Will Johnson. Seahawks QB Drew Lock noticed and fired a perfect pass to Smith-Njigba in stride, leading to the Seahawks’ wide receiver’s longest career gain. The rest of the day played out similarly, with Smith-Njigba routing up defenders right and left. He scored again on the Seahawks’ seventh drive, leaping past a diving cornerback to make the catch in the end zone. Lock linked up with him again for a third score in the back of the end zone, threading the ball past a linebacker in the end zone as Smith-Njigba broke left on a crosser, dusting Cardinals S Budda Baker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Zach Charbonnet rushed six times for 23 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 8 loss to the Bears, adding six yards on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet drew the start but saw four fewer opportunities than rookie Jadarian Price, the latter of whom led the team in rush yards and touches. Expect the two to continue operating in a near-even timeshare moving forward, leaving Charbonnet in shaky FLEX territory ahead of a Week 9 meeting with the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) and Jadarian Price (chest) are active for Week 8 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet makes his season debut after a suffering a torn ACL late in the 2025 season while Price returns from short-term injure reserve due to a chest injury. Emmanuel Wilson and George Holani had held down the backfield in the absence of the two top backs, leaving an uncertain situation regarding expected backfield utilization when the Seahawks take on the Bears in a marquee matchup. Inactive for the Seahawks are QB Drew Lock, LB Uchenna Nwosu, WR Rashid Shaheed, RB Velus Jones Jr., OT Charles Cross, G Beau Stephens, and NT Brandon Pili.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Seahawks plan to activate Jadarian Price from injured reserve and that he will play in Week 8 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Price and Zach Charbonnet will both make their returns from injured reserve tonight, putting the Seahawks’ backfield at full strength heading into a pivotal NFC matchup. It’s hard to know how the touches will be spread out in this one, which makes both backs hard to trust on Monday night against the Bears. Price averaged 11.5 carries per game in his two full games played this season, but Charbonnet should eat into that somewhat. Fantasy managers looking to play either Seattle running back in this one should temper expectations until we have more data to go on in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) is expected to be active for Week 8 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: The team has yet to activate Charbonnet from injured reserve but removed him from the injury report Saturday, leaving only the procedural step in the way of his season debut. He likely returns to a limited role as the team manages his reps in his first game since tearing his ACL in 2025. Rookie Jadarian price is also expected to play after being removed from the injury report. He, too, will need to be activated from injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) was downgraded to “limited” for Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: It’s not particularly concerning — this is probably part of a pre-established practice plan as Charbonnet completes his injury comeback — but Jadarian Price’s Friday return to full practice certainly has our attention. Now even if Charbonnet does manage to make his 2026 debut on Monday evening against the Bears, he could have even more company in Seattle’s crowded backfield. Both backs returning would make all three of Charbonnet, Price and Emanuel Wilson shaky FLEX plays. We will receive official game designations on Saturday afternoon. Until then, hang tight.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) was a full participant during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: It’s obviously a positive development for Charbonnet, who appears to be on track for his season debut against the Bears in Week 8. Fantasy managers just have to keep in mind that the rug was pulled from underneath last week when the Seahawks ruled the tailback out late in the week. Jadarian Price (chest) was a limited participant, but fantasy managers who want to use a Seattle tailback on Monday night won’t have clarity until Saturday at the earliest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald declined to say whether or not Zach Charbonnet (knee) would play in Week 8 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Macdonald said the team will continue to stick to their plan regarding Charbonnet’s return. The 25-year-old running back was activated from the PUP list last week, only to be ruled out before the weekend as the Seahawks were preparing to face the Chiefs. It’s worth noting that Charbonnet was a full participant in practice last week, so we would assume he will log another full week of practices this week. Should the Seahawks opt to sideline Charbonnet next week, Emanuel Wilson would again assume the role as lead back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks declared RB Zach Charbonnet, QB Drew Lock, LB Drake Thomas, RB Robert Henry Jr., LB Chazz Surratt, LB Connor O’Toole, and G Beau Stevens inactive for Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Lock will serve as the emergency quarterback while the team will have to wait another week for the season debut of Zach Charbonnet. The Seahawks look to make up ground in the NFC West following the loss from the 49ers against one of two remaining undefeated teams in the league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks ruled out Zach Charbonnet (knee) for Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald told reporters that Charbonnet has not suffered a setback. He just isn’t ready yet. Many teams might rush a player of his caliber back, now that he is practicing in full, but the Seahawks are smartly taking the long view with Charbonnet’s health. Emanuel Wilson will function as the team’s leading rusher while George Holani plays on passing downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks activated Zach Charbonnet (knee) from the reserve/physically unable to perform list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet underwent ACL reconstruction after suffering his season-ending knee injury in the Seahawks’ Divisional Round win over the 49ers. He will make his 2026 debut in Week 7 against the Chiefs, facing his former teammate, Kenneth Walker. Charbonnet’s expected workload is unknown, though he could handle enough touches to be FLEX-viable. As long as he stays healthy, Charbonnet should advance to the RB2 ranks in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Jadarian Price rushed 10 times for 29 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 8 loss to the Bears, adding eight yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: It was Zach Charbonnet that drew the start for the Seahawks in his first game since tearing his ACL last year, but it was the talented rookie that led the team in opportunities. Price was making his first appearance since hitting injure reserve with a chest injury suffered in Week 2, and while he led the team in yardage and carries, George Holani remained involved in clear passing situations and Charbonnet is liable to see his role continue to grow with each healthy game. Price will be a shaky FLEX option in a better matchup against the Cardinals in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Seahawks plan to activate Jadarian Price from injured reserve and that he will play in Week 8 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: Price and Zach Charbonnet will both make their returns from injured reserve tonight, putting the Seahawks’ backfield at full strength heading into a pivotal NFC matchup. It’s hard to know how the touches will be spread out in this one, which makes both backs hard to trust on Monday night against the Bears. Price averaged 11.5 carries per game in his two full games played this season, but Charbonnet should eat into that somewhat. Fantasy managers looking to play either Seattle running back in this one should temper expectations until we have more data to go on in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Seahawks removed Jadarian Price (chest) from the injury report Saturday and he is expected to play in Week 8 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: The team has yet to activate him from injured reserve, a procedural move that is expected to come before they take the field in Week 8 against the Bears on Monday Night Football. Zach Charbonnet is also expected to be activated from injured reserve, giving the team their top two backs for the first time this season. No word yet on an expected snap count for either, although Price would seem to be in line to serve as the top option in the backfield considering it will be Charbonnet’s season debut.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Jadarian Price (chest) was upgraded to “full” for Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: Price was upgraded to full while Zach Charbonnet (knee) was downgraded to limited. That is probably part of a pre-planned process with Charbonnet, but as of Friday evening, we suppose Price is now technically closer to returning than his veteran backfield mate. As it is, both players now seem more likely than not to suit up, which would make for an extremely chaotic fantasy situation with Emanuel Wilson still in the fold. With the Seahawks playing on Monday evening, we will receive official game designations Saturday afternoon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Jadarian Price (chest) was a limited participant during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: Price gets in the limited session after coach Mike Macdonald said that it was realistic that the tailback could be back Monday night against the Bears in Week 8. Zach Charbonnet was a full participant Thursday, so the Seattle backfield could finally be at full strength — or close to it, anyway — for the stretch. That’s nice for the Seahawks, but creates a lot of confusion from a fantasy perspective.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said it’s “realistic” that Jadarian Price (chest/IR) could return in Week 8.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: With Zach Charbonnet’s status also in some doubt, Seattle’s backfield situation likely won’t be sorted out until Saturday (or MNF inactives), but if Price is back that’s probably the end of Emmanuel Wilson’s short-term RB2 ride. We’ll keep an eye on the situation. Wilson-reliant managers might want to consider alternative arrangements for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Seahawks coach Mike MacDonald said the team would designate Jadarian Price (chest) to return from injured reserve this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: Price has missed the minimum four games and being immediately designated to return should have him making his debut sooner rather than later. Of course, with Zach Charbonnet also returning to the fold soon, this could be a split backfield rather than the RB2 zone that Price looked to be opening the year in. Price probably will only reach the FLEX ranks when active until we see what the touch counts look like; perhaps he could have a Blake Corum-ish role if all goes well for the Seahawks offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Seahawks placed RB Jadarian Price (chest) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: Price reportedly aggravated a chest injury during the team’s Wednesday practice and will now miss the next four games, at minimum, as he tends to the injury. The backfield will be left in the hands of Emanuel Wilson and George Holani in Week 4 against the Chargers but should get reinforcements in short order with Zach Charbonnet set to resume practicing. Price’s season continues to trend poorly for fantasy managers that invested a mid-round pick in his services this summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Seahawks rule out Jadarian Price (chest) for Week 4 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: Price reportedly aggravated his chest injury on Wednesday. That is unfortunate. With Price out of the picture against the Chargers, and Zach Charbonnet (knee) still rehabbing, burly RB Emanuel Wilson and receiving specialist RB George Holani will split backfield reps. Wilson can be started as a volume-based RB2/FLEX while Holani is FLEX-viable in PPR formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.headline: Jadarian Price (chest) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jadarian-p.analysis: It’s possible that this is just a precautionary rest day, but those typically occur on Wednesdays. Price should be viewed as questionable to play in Week 4 against the Chargers. Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald favorite, Zach Charbonnet (knee), returned as a limited participant. Backup RB Emanuel Wilson would likely get the start if Price and Charbonnet are both out this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Kalif Raymond caught 2-of-3 targets for 14 yards in the Bears’ Week 8 win over the Seahawks, adding 39 yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Raymond’s lone “carry” came on a third-and-long in the fourth quarter in a three-point game, with the play ruled a rush attempt following a slightly backwards toss on a quick swing pass to the perimeter. Raymond did the rest as he turned on the jets for a 39-yard gain to the five, which D’Andre Swift would punch in for the second of his three rushing scores on the evening. Raymond remains unlikely to match his early-season exploits but can be stashed in case of injury to Luther Burden, Rome Odunze, or Colston Loveland.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Kalif Raymond caught both of his targets for 18 yards in the Bears’ Week 6 win against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Raymond ran a pass route on 18 of the Bears’ 45 drop backs and didn’t see a target until the second half. He has been mostly phased out of the team’s passing offense since profiling as Chicago’s de facto WR1 over the first couple games of the season. Raymond, who has just 30 receiving yards over his past three games, can be left on the waiver wire ahead of Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Kalif Raymond caught 3-of-4 targets for six yards in the Bears’ Week 5 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Raymond’s fast start to the season has now been erased to the tune of just five catches for 12 yards over the past two weeks. Even with Caleb Williams (hamstring) looking likely to return for Week 6 against the Falcons, Raymond’s brief moment in the 2026 fantasy sun has come and gone.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Kalif Raymond caught 6-of-7 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 3 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Raymond has now led the Bears in receiving in two of the team’s first three games, with Week 3 his best performance yet on the back of a 41-yard touchdown through busted coverage. It isn’t likely the career role player will lead the team in receiving throughout the season, but the early returns on investment must have fantasy managers ecstatic for those that either drafted him in the final round or scooped him off the wire following Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Kalif Raymond caught 5-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Bears’ Week 2 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: For whatever reason, Raymond again lead the Bears’ receiver corps in production, though Luther Burden did out-target him on fewer snaps. Cold comfort. Although Raymond out-snapped Burden, he was on the field 16 fewer plays than Rome Odunze. Pro Football Focus’ Nathan Jahnke charted Raymond as seeing more time in “12" personnel than his sophomore teammate. We would like to say this is bound to change going forward, but coach Ben Johnson had no problem featuring veteran Olamide Zaccheaus in 2025. Raymond is struggling to create WR4 value of his own, but he is certainly hampering Burden and Odunze’s production ahead of Week 3 against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Kalif Raymond caught 8-of-9 targets for 89 yards in the Bears’ Week 1 win against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Raymond, who ran a route on 23 of 40 Caleb Williams drop backs, led the Bears in targets, catches, and receiving yards, while Colston Loveland went catchless and Luther Burden was an afterthought. Raymond’s route participation suggests he’ll be a rotational player in the run-first Chicago offense. That should make him a risky option in any sort of fantasy league. Even so, it’s clear Raymond has taken something similar to the D.J. Moore role and could be useful in fantasy this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: The Chicago Tribune’s Sean Hammond reports that Bears WR Rome Odunze exited practice early on Thursday after suffering an apparent leg injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Per Hammond, Odunze “came up hobbling during an install period at the start of practice,” with what appeared to be a right leg injury. Apparently, Odunze “wasn’t overly concerned” and tried to continue practicing, but Bears trainers removed him from the field. That last bit is encouraging. Hopefully, Odunze’s Week 1 availability has not been jeopardized. Bears TE Colston Loveland and WR Luther Burden would benefit if Odunze cannot play. Odunze is backed up by WR Kalif Raymond.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: The Athletic’s Kevin Fishbain believes the “expectation” is that Kalif Raymond will be the team’s No. 3 receiver.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Jahdae Walker could position himself as the No. 3 with a second-year jump, and third-round pick Zavion Thomas is also in the mix. This room will probably split the snaps enough to make them unappealing from a fantasy perspective, but it’s possible someone emerges as a WR4-type.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Bears signed WR Kalif Raymond, formerly of the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Raymond was mostly a role player and a special teams standout during his five years in Detroit. Last season Raymond had 24 receptions for 289 yards and a touchdown while drawing three starts for the run-heavy Lions. In Chicago, Raymond — entering his age-32 season — will likely function as a role player in Ben Johnson’s run-centric offense. He could see starter’s snaps if the Bears struggle with receiver injuries in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Isaac TeSlaa caught his only target for 18 yards in the Lions’ Week 18 win over the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: TeSlaa emerged as a primary option for the Lions in Week 13 after Amon-Ra St. Brown departed with injury, finishing off the back half of his rookie season as the clear WR3 for the Lions. That effectively shifted Kalif Raymond into a situational role, something likely to carry forward into the 2026 season. TeSlaa ends his rookie year with 16 catches for 239 yards, flashing abilities in the red zone through six touchdowns. Although unlikely to immediately see his role grow while playing alongside St. Brown and Jameson Williams, TeSlaa appears likely to step into a bigger role when one of the main receivers goes down. That gives him legitimate best ball upside considering he will be playing for an offense that has finished in the top five in scoring in each of the previous four seasons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden caught 7-of-9 targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 8 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: Burden’s opening drive score was the first touchdown surrendered by the Seahawks on an opening possession in the previous 26 games, finishing tied with tight end Colston Loveland for the team lead in targets while catching the only passing score from quarterback Caleb Williams. He continues to operate as the team’s top option through the air in a role that is most malleable, which can either be concentrated on the short areas against zone or extended in the vertical against man. Burden is a WR2 in a pass-funnel matchup against the Buccaneers in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden caught all four targets for 130 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 7 win over the Patriots, adding seven yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: Burden erupted on the scene with a 58-yard, catch-and-run reception on a crosser in the first quarter to set up a four-yard score for D’Andre Swift. He would tack on another 24 yards and his touchdown late in the second quarter to push him over the century mark in yards on an improbable touchdown reception, taking a quick screen to the house on third-and-17 with only 14 seconds remaining before the break. Burden would largely fall victim to a more reserved offensive stance after the Bears pushed their lead to 13 points on their first possession of the second half, adding just one additional reception in the final 30 minutes of play. That matters not to fantasy managers that had been waiting for a marquee performance from a player they chased up draft boards this summer. Burden appears to be heating up now further removed from the offseason injury he carried into the start of the regular season and can continue to be started as an upside WR2 ahead of a difficult matchup against the Seahawks in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden III caught all eight of his targets for 95 yards in the Bears’ Week 6 win against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: With Caleb Williams back from a hamstring injury, Burden led the Bears with eight targets and a season-high 95 yards, mostly on short over-the-middle passes from Williams. Burden’s long play was a 25-yard catch and run. That he ran a route on just 19 of the Bears’ 45 drop backs is something of a concern going forward. With that little route involvement, Burden will have to be hyper efficient if he’s going to be a WR2/3 in fantasy formats. He should remain in lineups next week against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden III caught 4-of-6 targets for 47 yards in the Bears’ Week 5 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: Burden “led” the Bears in receiving, but the fact that 47 yards was the team’s high-water mark tells you all you need to know about their offensive effectiveness this afternoon. Today was actually the first time in three games without Caleb Williams that Burden finished under 60 yards receiving, but he is still in dire need of his starting quarterback’s return. It appears that will be Week 6 against the Falcons, keeping Burden in the low-end WR2 mix despite his lack of spiked weeks through the season’s first five contests.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden III caught 4-of-6 targets for 63 yards in the Bears’ Week 4 win against the Jets, adding one rush for 11 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: It was a fine outing for Burden after he showed signs of life in Week 3’s win over the Eagles. Burden was second on the team in targets, trailing Rome Odunze’s seven looks from Tyson Bagent. He ran a few more pass routes than Kalif Raymond, who had two grabs for six yards. Chicago operating as a run-first team is going to necessarily limit Burden’s opportunities, but he should suffice as a WR3/4 in the coming weeks. That includes next week against a middling Green Bay secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden caught 7-of-11 targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 3 win over the Eagles, adding seven yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: Burden got the scoring started with a shovel-pass touchdown on the first possession of the game and continued to be the primary engine of the offense on a night the team was led by veteran journeyman Case Keenum. Head coach Ben Johnson handily outmatched his counterpart in Sean Mannion, keeping the offense in rhythm and unpredictable throughout. Burden should continue to improve upon his early-season returns for fantasy managers that chased him up draft boards this offseason, particularly once Caleb Williams returns to the starting roster in a few weeks. In the meantime, treat Burden as an upside WR2 ahead of a Week 4 meeting with the Jets in Chicago.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden caught 3-of-7 targets for 32 yards in the Bears’ Week 2 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: For the second straight week, Burden was out-produced by Kalif Raymond, who again led the receiver corps in production. D’Andre Swift “led” the entire team in receiving with five receptions for 54 scoreless yards. Burden is now sitting on eight catches for 95 yards through two weeks. It’s not the worst start anyone has ever seen, but fantasy managers were expecting better. It might not be coming in Week 3 if Caleb Williams’ hamstring injury costs him time against the Eagles, which seems highly likely. We are trying not to overreact to small-sample sizes, but Burden is definitely now more of a WR3 than WR2 heading into next Monday’s contest. That, of course, should still have him in most fantasy lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden caught all five of his targets for 63 yards in the Bears’ Week 1 win against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: Burden overcame a first quarter fumble on a bubble screen to finish second on the team in targets behind Kalif Raymond, who saw nine looks from Caleb Williams, just as everyone had predicted. While Burden’s 17 percent targets per route run was well below his 2025 rate, he should be more involved going forward in a Bears offense that might be trying to break the NFL’s single season scoring record, as head coach Ben Johnson mentioned in an August interview. Burden will be a top-30 PPR option next week against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Bears elevated WR Kaden Davis for Week 1 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: This wouldn’t be news under normal circumstances but takes on additional meaning with Rome Odunze listed questionable for Week 1. It is of particular note that the Bears already have five wide receivers on the active roster and still chose to elevate another. While recent reports seemed to indicate a sense of optimism regarding Odunze’s potential availability, he could be on the wrong side of questionable given the recent transaction. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his status when the team releases its inactives 90 minutes prior to first kick. Luther Burden and Colston Loveland would be in line to benefit greatly should Odunze be unable to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: The Chicago Tribune’s Sean Hammond reports that Bears WR Rome Odunze exited practice early on Thursday after suffering an apparent leg injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: Per Hammond, Odunze “came up hobbling during an install period at the start of practice,” with what appeared to be a right leg injury. Apparently, Odunze “wasn’t overly concerned” and tried to continue practicing, but Bears trainers removed him from the field. That last bit is encouraging. Hopefully, Odunze’s Week 1 availability has not been jeopardized. Bears TE Colston Loveland and WR Luther Burden would benefit if Odunze cannot play. Odunze is backed up by WR Kalif Raymond.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 4-of-6 targets for 87 yards in the Bears’ Week 8 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Odunze was almost nonexistent in the first half, catching his first pass, an 18-yard reception over the middle of the field, with just under five minutes remaining in the second quarter. The Bears exploited the attention paid to Luther Burden and Colston Loveland after the half, with Odunze catching three passes for chunk gains in the third quarter to help position the team for their sixth victory. Odunze remains unlikely to challenge for the team lead in targets on a weekly basis while playing alongside Burden and Loveland, but his big play ability keeps him in the FLEX discussion, for the time being. That could change in a more favorable matchup through the air in Week 9 against the Buccaneers, where Odunze will be a WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 4-of-5 targets for 69 yards in the Bears’ Week 7 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The yardage total goes down as Odunze’s second highest mark of the season as the third-year receiver was held out of the end zone for the seventh straight game to start the 2026 season. He did make three massive catches on third downs to help extend drives, making his mark felt more with quality than quantity. That doesn’t necessarily benefit fantasy managers that chased his big-play abilities this offseason as Odunze has largely been a fantasy dud outside of the Week 4 win over the Jets in which he returned 15.4 PPR points. He remains best left on fantasy benches ahead of another difficult test against the Seahawks in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 3-of-4 targets for 39 yards in the Bears’ Week 6 win against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Odunze, who led the Bears in pass routes on the day, was third in targets while Luther Burden and Colston Loveland had big days with Caleb Williams back under center. Odunze was seeing more targets and air yards with the Bears’ backups QBs under center, though he should remain a high-variance flex in Week 7 against the Patriots. Odunze leads the Chicago offense with a 35 percent air yards share this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 3-of-9 targets for 40 yards in the Bears’ Week 5 loss to the Packers, also losing a fumble.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Although the Bears were already losing 31-7, Odunze’s fourth quarter giveaway was an ill-advised decision on a fourth down catch-and-run where he had already secured a new set of downs. Odunze seemed to be extending the ball forward. Unnecessary. Like every Bears pass catcher, Odunze is treading fantasy water waiting for the return of Caleb Williams (hamstring). It appears that will be Week 6 against the Falcons, but Odunze’s returns have been uneven enough that not even Williams’ re-insertion under center will be enough to get Odunze above the mid-range WR3 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 6-of-7 targets for 94 yards in the Bears’ Week 4 win against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Tyson Bagent, making his first NFL start, locked on to his boundary wideout in the first half, hitting Odunze for a couple long gains, including a nicely-placed 37 yarder. Odunze was second on the team in targets behind Colston Loveland, who saw nine looks on the day. Odunze is leading the Bears offense in air yards and profiles as a high-variance weekly fantasy option in an offense that leans toward the run. Odunze will be a solid flex option in Week 5 against a Green Bay secondary that struggles against boundary receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 3-of-6 targets for 44 yards in the Bears’ Week 3 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Odunze continues to function as the deep threat in Ben Johnson’s offense, which spells trouble for his fantasy value in the immediate future considering the absence of Caleb Williams. Case Keenum got the start under center against the Eagles, and while he kept the offense on track through veteran savvy, his general lack of arm strength limited the offense to hefty rates of attacking the short-to-intermediate areas of the field. It is unclear whether Keenum or Tyson Bagent will draw the start in Week 4, but the decision could dictate whether Odunze can be inserted into fantasy rosters against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 3-of-4 targets for 43 yards in the Bears’ Week 2 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It was Odunze’s second quiet statline in as many weeks to begin the season. The difference this time, of course, was the Bears scored only three points after dropping 59 on the Panthers in Week 1. They did attempt 35 passes, 26 of which came from Caleb Williams before he injured his hamstring midway through the fourth quarter. If Williams misses Week 3 against the Eagles as is currently looking likely, it would be difficult to jam Odunze into the WR3 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 2-of-3 targets for 52 yards in the Bears’ Week 1 win against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Odunze came down with an impressive 47-yard contested catch near the end zone in the first half. He was quiet from there on out. Running a route on about 60 percent of the Bears’ drop backs, Odunze may have been limited by the calf injury that kept him out of practice for much of last week. Odunze will continue as a high-variance downfield option in a run-first Chicago offense next week against the Vikings. He should be treated as nothing more than a WR3 option in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze (calf) is active for Week 1 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Odunze missed some practice time this week with the calf issue and was considered questionable headed into the weekend. He could see his snaps and routes limited if the calf is still bothering him. Odunze should be considered a high-variance flex option with a frightening floor against the Panthers. Bears declared QB Tyson Bagent, QB Miller Moss, S Xavier Woods, OT Ozzy Trapilo, DE Jamree Kromah, and OL Jordan McFadden inactive for the team’s season opener.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Rome Odunze (calf) is expected to play in Week 1 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Odunze was limited by the calf issue throughout the week before being listed as questionable on Friday. He will suit up today but might not be at full strength. Odunze will be a high-risk WR3 for his 2026 opener. To no one’s surprise, Colston Loveland trails only Trey McBride in the tight end rankings, while Luther Burden is a speculative WR2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: D’Andre Swift rushed 27 times for 69 yards and three touchdowns in the Bears’ Week 8 win over the Seahawks, adding 10 yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Swift managers were sweating early as he alternated drives with Roschon Johnson. Those worries were swiftly erased as the veteran lead back played almost the entirety of the second half, scoring all three of his short yardage touchdowns after the break. The three trips to paint marked his second game with three touchdowns through the first eight weeks, now the only player in the league with multiple three-touchdown games. Swift will be a matchup-based RB2 when the Bears host the Buccaneers in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: D’Andre Swift rushed 22 times for 78 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 7 win over the Patriots, adding 12 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Swift shook off an early injury scare when he took a helmet directly to his knee to earn a season-high 26 opportunities in the absence of Kyle Monangai. This game had an entirely different feel than the previous game played without Monangai, during which Roschon Johnson was much more involved in a game the Bears held a 31-7 lead in the fourth quarter. The back-and-forth nature of Week 7 kept Swift on the field for more of the game, allowing him to return a legitimate RB1 performance on the backs of elite volume. Monangai could return as early as Week 8 considering the Bears now have 10 days until they play the Seahawks on Monday Night Football, potentially sending Swift back into the RB2 range in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: Bears ruled out Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) for Week 7 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Monangai will miss his third game in a row this week. Exactly two weeks ago, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported that Monangai’s turf toe injury would be an issue for 1-2 weeks. Technically, his statement remains accurate. This week’s Thursday Night Football game complicates things. If the Bears thought Monangai would miss four games, they likely would have put him on injured reserve, so he should, theoretically, be able to play in Week 8 against the Seahawks. Of course, nothing is guaranteed, and for those wondering, the Bears go on bye in Week 10. D’Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson have been splitting touches with Monangai sidelined. We do not yet know if Johnson will be punished for last week’s fumble though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: D’Andre Swift had 16 rushes for 44 yards and two touchdowns in the Bears’ Week 6 win against the Falcons, adding four catches for 26 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Swift again dominated backfield touches for Chicago with Kyle Monangai sidelined with injuries to his toe and hand. Roschon Johnson had 13 carries, with most of those coming after the Bears had raced out to a big lead (before that lead dwindled in the fourth quarter). Both of Swift’s touchdowns came inside the ten yard line. Swift should be locked in for at least 15 touches in Week 7 against the Patriots if Monangai remains sidelined. His involvement in the pass game provides a nice weekly PPR floor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: Bears ruled out Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) for Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Monangai is “trending in the right direction,” but remains week-to-week. D’Andre Swift should handle a sizable workload with Monangai sidelined. Roschon Johnson may be able to catch a few passes, but he makes for a shaky FLEX bet. Monangai should be stashed safely on fantasy football benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: D’Andre Swift rushed nine times for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 5 loss to the Packers, adding four receptions for 30 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Swift was the only Bear to find the end zone in a throwaway performance where Tyson Bagent was benched for the fourth quarter. It was still a disappointing statline with Kyle Monangai (toe) on the shelf, but there just wasn’t much Swift could do with Bagent failing to threaten the Packers’ defense and the Bears’ D struggling mightily. Swift also lost a ton of passing-game work and targets to fill-in No. 2 RB Roschon Johnson. That’s a potentially disturbing development heading into Week 6 against the Falcons, with or without Monangai in the lineup. Thankfully, Caleb Williams (hamstring) should be back, shoring up Swift’s value in the RB10-14 range.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: D’Andre Swift (hip/knee) is not on Chicago’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Despite an early-week DNP, Swift heads into the week in arguably a better position than he started it. We’re not sure how much workload he’ll handle with Kyle Monangai (foot) out, but it will certainly be a large majority of what the Bears do. Roschon Johnson figures to handle whatever Swift can’t, but isn’t a priority free agency pickup so much as a stash at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the “belief is that D’Andre Swift (hip/knee) should be able to go” in Week 5 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: We will get a better sense of Swift’s availability soon when the Bears release their final injury report of the week. After being a DNP in Wednesday’s practice, Swift was able to log a limited session on Thursday, which is a good sign for his availability with one practice left to go. Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe), who has yet to practice this week, could be at risk of missing Week 5, which could lead to a busy day for Swift, while Roschon Johnson would serve as the Bears’ RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: D’Andre Swift (hip/knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: It’s an upgrade from Wednesday’s DNP. Swift has been a constant presence on the midweek injury reports, but hasn’t seemed at any real risk of missing a game yet. We’d imagine he’s more likely than not to avoid a questionable tag again on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: D’Andre Swift (hip/knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Swift nursed this knee injury last week, but was active on game day, as usual. Bears RB2 Kyle Monangai took on 30 carries, functioning as the team’s offensive centerpiece after Swift lost a fumble in the second half. Perhaps Swift’s hip injury, which he apparently picked up in-game, contributed to Monangai’s increased involvement. Monangai injured his right thumb and suffered a toe injury, though he is expected to play in Week 5 against the Packers. Swift’s participation level is worth watching closely this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams completed 24-of-34 passes for 247 yards and one touchdown in the Bears’ 34-17, Week 8 win over the Seahawks, adding one yard on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams marched the Bears down the field for a 17-play opening possession touchdown, snapping a 26-game streak in which the Seahawks kept opponents out of the end zone on first possessions in the process. The two teams traded defensive stops for much of the remainder of the first half before the Bears opened the flood gates after the break, vaulting to a 6-2 record and now just half a game behind the Vikings for the lead in the NFC North. Williams’ ball placement was impeccable in this one, the most notable of which came just after the half on three absolute dimes to Rome Odunze for chunk gains.
