Two surging teams meet in Week 9 when the Bears host the pass-funnel Buccaneers on Sunday Night Football, where Williams will remain a back end QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams completed 22-of-33 passes for 308 yards and two touchdowns in the Bears’ 30-24, Week 7 win over the Patriots, adding 18 yards on five carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The enigmatic signal caller also took three sacks, the last of which almost placed the Bears in position to hand the keys to victory to the Patriots. Ben Johnson called a pass play on third-and-five with under two minutes to play in Patriots territory, placing another nod of support toward his franchise quarterback. Things turned dire when Williams took a sack that appeared to take the Bears out of field goal range in a six-point game, with veteran kicker Cairo Santos hitting a career-long 58-yard field goal to dispel the worries. That sequence of two plays displayed Johnson’s unrelenting trust in his players considering the 58-yard field goal was not only the longest of Santos’ 12-year career, but the third longest field goal in Soldier Field history. Either way, Williams and the Bears escaped with the victory and move to 5-2, now 1.5-games behind the Vikings for the division lead in the most competitive division in football. The Bears get a mini-bye ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the Seahawks on Monday Night Football, where Williams will remain a back-end QB1 in fantasy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams completed 30-of-36 attempts for 305 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 6 win against the Falcons, adding four rushes for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams was all the way back in this one, returning to action after three weeks on the sideline recovering from a hamstring injury. His only real miss of the day came on a ten yard throw to Colston Loveland that should have been an easy touchdown. Williams tormented the pass-funnel Atlanta defense with middle-of-the-field throws, along with typical out-of-structure passes to the sideline. It was an impressive outing against a Falcons defense giving up the league’s fifth lowest drop back success rate. Williams should remain in lineups in Week 7 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) is active for Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams will make his return to the starting lineup after being sidelined for a few weeks with a hamstring injury while the Bears declared RB Kyle Monangai, CB Tyrique Stevenson, LB T.J. Edwards, LB Keyshaun Elliott, OL Jordan McFadden, DL Jayden Loving, and QB Case Keenum inactive against Atlanta. Monongai’s absence should translate into another big workload for D’Andre Swift, facing a tough Falcons rush defense. Meanwhile, Tyson Bagent will serve as Williams’ backup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) will start in Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This was expected to be the case but is now confirmed by sources close to the team. Williams returns after missing the previous three games as the Bears look to claw their way back into contention in a crowded NFC North division. Consider it a sizable boost for all Chicago pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) posted a video to social media indicating he will play in Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Normally, social media posts don’t count for much. However, earlier today, Bears coach Ben Johnson said that the Bears should have more clarity on Williams’ status by the end of the day, after the medical team put Williams through “the final stress tests” in his return-to-play program. We are inferring that Williams’ social media post suggests he passed the final medical testing, though we have not officially received word that this is indeed the case. For now, we tentatively expect Williams to play on Sunday. He can be treated as a mid-to-low QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Bears are smartly taking a conservative approach with their franchise quarterback. Williams had a limited practice session last week and practiced fully this week. Bears coach Ben Johnson told reporters that the team should have more clarity by the end of the day on whether Williams has passed his return-to-play plan’s final stress tests. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Bears’ QB1 is seemingly on track to make his return this week, when his team takes on the Falcons. When speaking to reporters after practice, though, Williams said he does not know if he is going to play yet, adding that he still has a number of tests and protocols to go through before he’s cleared. If active, Williams could end up running a little less frequently than he did early in the year, perhaps playing cautiously in his first game back. Regardless, Williams is a low-end QB1 if he is indeed active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) practiced in full Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Technically, Williams was estimated as a full participant ahead of the Bears’ Week 6 game against the Falcons. We’ll see if Williams, who has missed the past three games, practices in full on Thursday. Either way he’s likely to be under center against the pass-funnel Atlanta defense in Week 6. He should be in all lineups if he’s active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said “all signs point” to Caleb Williams (hamstring) returning in Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Head coach Ben Johnson said on Sunday that Williams would be “close” to suiting up for Week 6, and he reportedly had a good workout before Week 5’s game against the Packers. Williams has missed the last three games with the hamstring injury he suffered in Week 2, but the Bears have managed to go 2-1 over that span. Williams logged one limited practice last week, after being a DNP on Wednesday and Thursday. If he can get on the practice field multiple days this week, it would be a good sign for his availability for next week’s game against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.headline: Kendrick Bourne suffered a fractured tibia in the Cardinals’ Week 8 win over the Cowboys, ending his season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.analysis: Shortly after head coach Mike LaFleur said Bourne’s injury could be season-ending, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Bourne suffered a fractured tibia that will sideline him for the next three months, effectively ending his season. Bourne caught 26 passes for 263 scoreless yards in his first season with the Cardinals. He remains under contract for the 2027 season, but the Cardinals can release him for a dead cap hit of $2.2 million.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Kendrick Bourne could be at risk of missing the remainder of the season after suffering an ankle injury in Week 8’s win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.analysis: It’s a tough break for Bourne, who was getting more involved with the offense following the trade of Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Texans. If his season is over, he finishes it with a 26-263-0 receiving line on 38 targets. He also topped 70 yards twice in the seven games he appeared in. Bourne signed a two-year, $10 million contract earlier this offseason but can be released by the Cardinals in exchange for a $2.2 million dead cap hit. It wouldn’t be surprising if the 10-year vet was playing elsewhere next season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.headline: FOX’s Pam Oliver reports Kendrick Bourne suffered a high-ankle sprain in Arizona’s Week 8 game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.analysis: Bourne limped to the sideline and later the locker room with trainers in a sequence towards the end of the half where the Cardinals lost three offensive skill players in just four plays. Bourne had a 29-yard catch before exiting. It seems likely he’ll miss multiple weeks and perhaps be a candidate for injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.headline: Kendrick Bourne caught 3-of-6 targets for nine yards in the Cardinals’ Week 7 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.analysis: Bourne and Jalen Brooks each saw six targets, though neither was awfully productive. Brooks went for 35 yards but only caught one pass. Bourne brought down half of his targets at a dreadful 1.5 yards per target. Bourne will hold a slight edge in the Week 8 rankings when Arizona takes on Dallas, but neither Arizona WR2 will be more than a desperation FLEX play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.headline: Kendrick Bourne caught 5-of-8 targets for 47 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 6 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.analysis: Bourne got going with a 15-yard catch-and-run on the Cardinals’ third drive. He earned a third-down end zone target from the Rams’ three-yard line, running an out route just inside the goal line, but he was unable to secure the pass, resulting in a close incompletion. He later bagged a tight-window catch on the Cardinals’ first drive after halftime, helping the offense down the field for one of their six field goal drives. The crafty veteran remains a PPR FLEX starter against the Broncos next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.headline: Kendrick Bourne caught 5-of-8 targets for 70 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 5 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.analysis: Bourne looks like a viable FLEX starter for those in need. His 70 receiving yards were a team high, and his eight targets trailed only Trey McBride (10). The journeyman receiver delivered two 20-plus-yard gains via post routes, the first coming on the Cardinals’ first drive and the second on the seventh. Jacoby Brissett tried to force another downfield shot to Bourne on the latter drive, but it didn’t work out. Bourne is running high-value routes in the center of the field, playing for a garbage-time team with a cannon-armed quarterback. The results could be volatile at times, but he is worth starting in the FLEX against the Rams next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.headline: Kendrick Bourne caught 2-of-3 targets for 22 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 3 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.analysis: Bourne operated as the Cardinals’ No. 3 wide receiver, seeing just three targets in a high-volume passing day. The team’s pass-catching hierarchy seems to have settled in, with Michael Wilson and Marvin Harrison operating as the top wide receivers and Trey McBride the top tight end. Bourne will get some looks behind this group but won’t be fantasy relevant without an injury ahead of him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.headline: Kendrick Bourne caught 2-of-3 targets for 11 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 2 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.analysis: Bourne earned his first target on the Cardinals’ fourth drive. The throw was a tad late, and Bourne’s hesitated while running his route, so the pass glanced off his hands in the flats. He caught the next two, but barely cleared double-digit yardage. Bourne does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.headline: Kendrick Bourne caught all eight of his targets for 75 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 1 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.analysis: Bourne led all Arizona wideouts in targets, catches, and yards. He ran a route on 82 percent of Cardinals dropbacks. Jacoby Brissett found Bourne in the short and intermediate areas throughout the first half — averaging a meager five air yards per target — while Michael Wilson and Marvin Harrison Jr. worked mainly downfield. Bourne could be an interesting waiver add this week in deeper PPR formats if his usage keeps up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.headline: Cardinals agreed to terms with WR Kendrick Bourne, formerly of the 49ers, on a two-year, $10 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.analysis: The deal has a max value of $12 million. Bourne has been a consistent depth receiver throughout his career, most recently catching 37 passes for 551 yards for the 49ers in 2025. He has cracked 500 yards three times in nine seasons, profiling best as WR3 or lower on the depth chart. He’ll be exactly that for the Cardinals, who are fortifying the pass-catchers behind Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson as they figure out their quarterback plans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eric-murra.headline: Jaguars S Eric Murray (elbow) will miss the remainder of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eric-murra.analysis: The Jaguars lost two starters on the defensive side of the ball in Sunday’s win over the Colts, with Murray and DT DaVon Hamilton (quad) both being dealt season-ending blows. Murray, 32, started all six games he appeared in for the Jags this season, totaling 15 tackles while earning a PFF coverage grade of 60.4. His loss, along with the loss of Hamilton, deals a substantial blow to the Jags’ run defense, as both players have been key contributors in stopping the ground game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eric-murra.headline: Jaguars S Eric Murray suffered an elbow injury in Jacksonville’s Week 8 game against the Colts and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eric-murra.analysis: Veteran Murray went down early and was ruled out in the first half. It leaves the Jags’ safety depth perilously low.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eric-murra.headline: Jaguars declared S Eric Murray, WR CJ Williams, CB Alijah Huzzie, CB Jaylon Jones, OL Daniel Faalele, DE Wesley Williams, and DT Albert Regis inactive for Week 5 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eric-murra.analysis: Murray was listed as doubtful on Friday because of a concussion. He returned to practice but couldn’t clear concussion protocol in time. Murray has started all four games this year, though we don’t think his absence will spark a revival of the Eagles’ passing attack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eric-murra.headline: Jaguars declared WR Parker Washington (hip) inactive for Jacksonville’s Week 14 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eric-murra.analysis: As expected based on earlier reporting, Washington will be scratched. He’s droppable if you have a late move you need to get in ahead of Sunday kickoff. Also inactive for the Jaguars are: S Andrew Wingard (concussion), Yasir Abdullah, OL Walker Little (concussion), TE Johnny Mundt, DL Emmanuel Ogbah and DL Austin Johnson. DL Travon Walker (knee), S Eric Murray (neck) and Arik Armstead (hand) are playing despite questionable tags in a huge game for the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eric-murra.headline: Jaguars EDGE Travon Walker (knee) is questionable for Jacksonville’s Week 14 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eric-murra.analysis: Walker hasn’t played since Week 11, but was able to get in two limited sessions this week and appears to be trending towards a return in a must-win AFC South top-of-division showdown with the Colts. The pass rusher has had a somewhat disappointing year to this point with just 2.5 sacks in nine games. Arik Armstead (hand) and Eric Murray (neck) are also questionable for Jacksonville.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eric-murra.headline: Jaguars agreed to terms with S Eric Murray, formerly of the Texans, to a three-year, $22.5 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eric-murra.analysis: This courtesy of former Jaguars back Maurice Jones-Drew, who added that Murray will get $12 million in guarantees. Murray has spent the last five years in Houston — he was playing on the team when Bill O’Brien was still the head coach. Entering his age-31 season, this is a strong contract for a player who spent two of the last three years as a reserve. Murray saw more playing time last year as the Texans moved Jalen Pitre to nickelback, and had a playoff pick-six of Justin Herbert. Signing him seems like an admission that the Jags will move on from Andre Cisco.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eric-murra.headline: Texans S Eric Murray (knee) is questionable to return in Week 6 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eric-murra.analysis: Murray left the game with a knee injury early in the second quarter, was examined in the medical tent, and then was taken into the locker room. There’s no word on the specific injury or the severity of it, but the Texans calling him questionable doesn’t inspire confidence that we’ll see him back on Sunday. That could lead to more opportunities downfield for Derek Carr, Chris Olave, and the Saints passing game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eric-murra.headline: Texans restructured S Eric Murray’s contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eric-murra.analysis: This marks the second-straight year in which Murray has restructured his deal with the Texans. Set to earn $3.75 million in base salary, the Texans are likely converting a portion of this into a bonus to free up a few million dollars in cap space. Murray is heading into his fourth season with the Texans and has appeared in 47 games for them since 2020.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eric-murra.headline: Texans S Eric Murray has agreed to a new two-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eric-murra.analysis: Signed for $5 million in 2022, Murray now has a two-year, $10 million deal. The starter of 25 games in Houston over the past two years, Murray has experience at corner but will continue to man safety under new head coach/former DC Lovie Smith. More versatile than good, Murray is not a particular asset in any one area.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eric-murra.headline: Texans DC Lovie Smith said he expects to keep Lonnie Johnson at safety.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/eric-murra.analysis: “Lonnie has position flexibility. I think it’s safe to say, we see Lonnie as a safety right now. He feels good about that. He’s got excellent size. He’s got a corner skillset, too. Really feel good about him fitting into our defense,” Smith said at his introductory press conference. The Texans drafted Johnson in 2019 to play corner but moved him to safety full-time last year. He was effective in a semi-regular role, posting 76 tackles despite playing only 64 percent of defensive snaps. With Eric Murray returning for at least another season, Johnson should continue to split playing time opposite Justin Reid.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: Gardner Minshew will start in Week 9 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: After leading a second-half comeback against the Cowboys in which he threw for 188 yards and three touchdowns on 17-of-23 passing, the move to Minshew felt inevitable. Now, the eighth-year journeyman will have a chance to make his first start for the Cardinals in what’s sure to be a tough road matchup against the Seahawks. Minshew has long proved his value as a serviceable backup in the league and should provide enough to keep the fantasy stocks of Trey McBride and Michael Wilson up, but he could be in for a tough outing against a top-flight Seahawks defense. He shouldn’t be treated as anything more than a desperation streamer in 2QB/superflex leagues, while Wilson’s expectations should fall somewhere in the WR3 range.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: Gardner Minshew completed 17-of-23 passes for 188 yards and three touchdowns in Arizona’s 33-30, Week 8 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: Minshew appeared to get better blocking and be more accurate and on-time with his passes than Jacoby Brissett. He also got a few major long gains from Tyler Allgeier en route to rallying the Cardinals from a 17-3 deficit. Minshew should have had a walkoff 13-yard touchdown pass to Michael Wilson with six seconds left, but kicker Chad Ryland missed the extra point. In overtime, after an initial three-and-out, Minshew completed just one pass as Wilson and Allgeier ran the Cardinals into field-goal range for the win. Hard to see how the Cardinals would bench Minshew after how this looked, though he certainly shouldn’t be considered a firm rest-of-season starter just yet. Minshew Mania will likely figure into the QB2 superflex mix in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter named Gardner Minshew and Mac Jones as potential trade candidates for the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: Jaxson Dart will miss the rest of the regular season, though there’s hope he could return for a postseason run. Schefter noted that Minshew played under Giants OC Matt Nagy in Kansas City, giving him some familiarity with the team’s scheme. He also mentioned that it will not be cheap to pry Jones away from the 49ers. Jimmy Garoppolo is out there as well. He is a free agent and is reportedly still interested in playing, “in the right situation.” For now, the Giants are going to roll with Jameis Winston. Jake Haener will back him up. They will likely add someone as an extra backup option, but Winston is an interesting QB2 for fantasy purposes until they make a bigger addition.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: Cardinals ruled out QB Carson Beck (rib) for the team’s preseason Week 1 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Beck suffered a rib injury in the Cardinals’ Hall of Fame game against the Panthers. Despite feeling “soreness,” he managed to practice this week. The Cardinals “decided to keep him out tonight as a precaution and to allow more time to heal.” This pours a little cold water on Beck’s moderate hype, but the reporting suggests that the injury is not overly concerning. Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett will start, and presumably be relieved by QB Kedon Slovis at some point. No word yet on QB Gardner Minshew’s potential involvement tonight.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that the Cardinals and QB Jacoby Brissett “reached agreement today on a reworked contract.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: Brissett was scheduled to make up to $4.88 this year, in the final year of his old deal. His new contract increases his compensation for this season, but he is still scheduled to hit free agency next offseason. The new deal includes a $15.5 million base salary. He can make up to $21 million via incentives. Things can always change in-season, but this appears to be clear-cut starter money — and it’s good news for Cardinals pass catchers. Although the Cardinals struggled to win games with Brissett under center last year, he was a very productive passer. Theoretically, he should be able to support TE Trey McBride and likely one of WR Marvin Harrison Jr. or WR Michael Wilson reliably. Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur confirmed that the plan is for Brissett to start in Week 1 against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: ESPN’s Josh Weinfuss reports that the Cardinals and QB Jacoby Brissett are “significantly” far apart on a reworked deal for this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: Brissett has one year left on his deal, which includes $1.5 million in guarantees. He can make up to $5.39 million. Fellow Cardinals QB Gardner Minshew signed a one-year deal with the team this offseason that netted him $5.14 million in guarantees. The front office also invested a third-round pick in rookie QB Carson Beck. It’s easy to see why Brissett is seeking increased financial security, but he may not have the leverage required to attain it. It is unknown whether Brissett will attend next week’s voluntary organized team activities. A mandatory minicamp for veterans and rookies is scheduled to take place June 8-10. Things could become even more contentious if he refuses to attend the mandatory events. Hopefully, the dispute will be resolved soon. Brissett, 33, showed last year that he has the ability to distribute the ball in a fantasy-friendly manner for Cardinals pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: When asked about the Cardinals’ starting quarterback job, general manager Monti Ossenfort said, “we’ll see how that room looks by the time we get in August.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: This doesn’t tell us a whole lot. Readers might recall that the 2026 NFL Draft is next week, and the Cardinals hosted Alabama QB Ty Simpson for a top-30 visit yesterday. If the Cardinals do not draft a rookie quarterback, Jacoby Brissett will likely be the default starter, with only Gardner Minshew and Kedon Slovis joining him on the roster at this time. If that is the case, the pass catchers likely stand to benefit. Brissett was able to distribute the ball effectively last year. Rolling with a developmental rookie could hurt the receiving outlooks for TE Trey McBride, WR Michael Wilson and WR Marvin Harrison Jr.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: Cardinals signed QB Gardner Minshew, formerly of the Chiefs, to a one-year, $8.25 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: Uncle Rico lands on his feet in Arizona with a chance to compete for the starting quarterback job with incumbent Jacoby Brissett during camp and preseason. The $8.25 million contract is far from “starter money,” but is still more than the average annual value of Brissett, making it likely the franchise is headed for a positional battle this offseason in the wake of Kyler Murray’s departure. At bare minimum, Minshew has proven to be a capable backup at the NFL level, having notched 47 starts across 63 appearances during his seven-year NFL career.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Gardner Minshew did not suffer a torn ACL and “already is back to full strength.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: Minshew was initially believed to have suffered a torn ACL in Week 16. The issue would have sidelined him for much of 2026, if not the entire season. Per Schefter, it was just a bone bruise that did not require surgery. Minshew did not suffer any long-term damage from the injury. Minshew will head into free agency with a clean bill of health. At just 29 years old, Minshew should have no issues finding another backup gig in the spring.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.headline: Chiefs placed QB Gardner Minshew (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/gardner-mi.analysis: Minshew received good news regarding his knee injury on Monday, but with just two weeks left in the regular season, it was apparent he would not be able to return in time to avoid the IR designation. The seventh-year signal-caller signed a one-year contract with the Chiefs this offseason but only appeared in two games. One of the better backups the league has to offer, Minshew should have no trouble finding a new home in 2026, given the current state of the quarterback landscape across the league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Ravens signed QB Austin Reed to the practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Reed spent time with the Ravens during training camp, and threw for 59 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in three brief appearances during the preseason. Reed will presumably be elevated to the 53-man roster ahead of Week 9’s game against the Jaguars, and could serve as Joe Fagnano’s backup for the foreseeable future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Ravens placed QB Skylar Thompson on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Thompson signed with the Ravens in the offseason but dealt with an undisclosed injury in training camp. He heads to injured reserve, likely ending his season; he and the team may reach an injury settlement in the coming days. The Ravens signed former UFL quarterback Austin Reed in his place. Reed figures to get some game time during preseason as the team’s fourth-string quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bears released RB Royce Freeman.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Freeman had only joined the Bears last week — the veteran will probably find a practice squad by the time the week is over. The Bears also waived DB Millard Bradford, DL Xavier Carlton, DB Alex Cook, LB Power Echols, DB Kaleb Hayes, QB Austin Reed, RB Ian Wheeler, and TE Joel Wilson. Additionally they released DB Tre Flowers and OL Joshua Miles, and placed DB Zah Frazier on the NFI list.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bears signed LB Micah Baskerville, OL Theo Benedet,TE Stephen Carlson, DL Byron Cowart, OL Jake Curhan, WR Collin Johnson, DB Quindell Johnson, LB Carl Jones, DL Jamree Kromah, DL Dashaun Mallory, DB Tarvarius Moore, QB Austin Reed, DB Reddy Steward and DB Ro Torrence to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Reed battled for the backup quarterback job despite being an UDFA out of Western Kentucky, and while he lost that competition to Tyson Bagent, he’ll stay in the organization.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bears waived/released QB Austin Reed, TE Brenden Bates, OL Theo Benedet, OL Jake Curhan, DL Jamree Kromah, DL Dashaun Mallory, LB Micah Baskerville, LB Carl Jones Jr., DB Leon Jones, DB Reddy Steward, DB Ro Torrence, LS Cameron Lyons, P Corliss Waitman, QB Brett Rypien, FB Khari Blasingame, WR Collin Johnson, OL Aviante Collins, DL Byron Cowart, DB Greg Stroman Jr., DB Adrian Colbert, DB Tarvarius Moore.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Reed signed with the Bears as a UDFA out of Western Kentucky but lost the QB2 battle to incumbent Tyson Bagent. Reed completed 75 percent of his passes in the preseason while throwing for 122 yards and a touchdown. It’s possible he returns as a member of the practice squad, but he won’t be threatening for a job any time soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bears signed Western Kentucky QB Austin Reed.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Reed (6'1"/220 pounds) threw for a whopping 71 touchdowns and ran for a dozen more in the same Western Kentucky offense that produced Patriots QB Bailey Zappe. Reed racked up nearly 16,000 passing yards over 51 collegiate games in the pass-first Hilltoppers offense. He’ll compete this summer to make the Bears roster and possibly serve as Caleb Williams’ backup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Western Kentucky graduate transfer QB Austin Reed has been named as the team’s starter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Reed (6'2/220) and the Hilltoppers will look to recreate the magic ushered in by Bailey Zappe last season after he shattered FBS passing records in his lone year at Western Kentucky last season. Tyson Helton’s air raid offense finished second in the nation in points per game last season (44.2) and amassed over 6,000 yards through the air in just 14 games. Reed beat out West Virginia transfer Jarret Doege for the starting role in camp, as he now sets his sights on an August 27th home matchup against Austin Peay.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said the team is weighing whether or not to open Jonathon Brooks (core) return window this week
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: Canales said the oft-injured Brooks still has “some things to clear recovery-wise” but noted that he could still have his practice window opened this week. Brooks suffered a core muscle injury in Week 2 against the Falcons and handled just 11 touches in his first two games of the year. Given his injury history, it’s hard to know how close he could truly be to dressing on game day, but even when he does return, we would still expect Chuba Hubbard to handle the majority of touches given how efficient he has been this season. In addition to Brooks, Canales said the team is also weighing when to open the return window for Xavier Legette, who has been sidelined since Week 2 with a knee injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jonathon Brooks is expected to have core muscle surgery and will be placed on IR.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: Brooks will be sidelined for at least six weeks. It opens the door for Chuba Hubbard to dominate the Carolina backfield for the next month and a half, with AJ Dillon chipping in as a breather back. Through two game Hubbard leads the Panthers backfield with 22 rushes for 102 yards. He’s run a route on 50 percent of the team’s drop backs and have five targets. The Panthers, meanwhile, have the second highest pass rate over expected through Week 2. Hubbard will be a locked-in top-20 option going forward. Dillon can be stashed in case Hubbard gets dinged up while Brooks is recovering.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Panthers coach Dave Canales said the team is “gathering information” on Jonathon Brooks’ groin injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: He’s undergoing tests to determine the severity. That’s not normally the sort of story that ends with “and Brooks played a full allotment of snaps in Week 3,” but we’ll see. The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports that Brooks is “considered week to week.” Brooks should be regarded as a drop candidate in shallow leagues on snaps and opportunities alone, but if he’s not healthy, that may expand to more leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Jonathon Brooks aggravated his groin injury in Week 2 against the Falcons and is considered “day to day.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: The good news is that this is unrelated to Brooks’ history of knee injuries and it sounds like he has a shot at suiting up for Week 3. The bad news is that Brooks originally suffered this groin injury during training camp and is still dealing with it two weeks into the season. Brooks only had five carries and one catch before exiting Week 2’s win over Atlanta. Even if he is healthy for next week’s game, Brooks is barely on the fantasy radar right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Jonathon Brooks (groin) is questionable to return in Week 2 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: Brooks went down on a routine tackle in the fourth quarter and was slow to get up. He eventually left for the locker room with a towel over his head. Brooks missed time late in training camp with the groin issue and it seemingly flared up against the Falcons. He had five carries for 16 yards before leaving the game. AJ Dillon will back up Chuba Hubbard if Brooks is unavailable for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Jonathon Brooks had four rushes for 14 yards in the Panthers’ Week 1 loss to the Bears, adding one catch for 48 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: In his first regular season action, Brooks played well behind lead back Chuba Hubbard, who finished the day with ten carries and three receptions. The highlight of Brooks’ day came on a sideline throw from Bryce Young that went for 48 yards. Brooks, coming off multiple major knee injuries, showed impressive burst and speed on the catch and run. That Hubbard was the team’s primary option inside the ten yard line is bad news for Brooks’ touchdown upside in the Carolina offense. For now he profiles as a bench stash in case Hubbard misses time this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Jonathon Brooks (groin) will play in Week 1 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: Brooks missed time late in camp with “general soreness” that was later revealed to be a minor groin issue. He was limited in practice this week, but that seems like nothing more than maintenance for a player who has barely played football over the past two seasons. Dave Canales is understandably keeping his workload light, even in practice. Brooks is expected to split carries with Chuba Hubbard in Week 1. He will be a high-risk FLEX play before we know what his role looks like.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Jonathon Brooks (groin) was seen practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: We’ll have a better sense of Brooks’ Week 1 availability in a few hours when the Panthers release their final injury report for the week, but the third-year back logged limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday and is trending in the right direction for Sunday’s game against the Bears. If he’s active, Brooks is expected to split touches with Chuba Hubbard, which could put a hard cap on both players’ upside in the season-opener.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Panthers RB Jonathon Brooks (groin) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: Now we know what Brooks has been dealing with for the past week or so. Beginning the week with a limited session is a good sign regarding his Week 1 availability, but obviously we hope to see him practice fully as soon as possible, given his extensive injury history. He could end up rotating in behind RB Chuba Hubbard if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.headline: Jonathon Brooks (soreness) was seen working off to the side with trainers on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathon-b.analysis: Head coach Dave Canales declined to provide an update on Brooks’ status Monday after saying last week that he was “very optimistic” that Brooks would play in Week 1 against the Bears. The Panthers won’t release their first official injury report until Wednesday, which should give us a better idea of where things stand for Brooks in the season opener. The 23-year-old back has had a strong training camp and is expected to split work with Chuba Hubbard if active. Both RBs should be viewed in the RB3 range for Week 1 if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) said he hopes to return after the Steelers’ Week 9 bye week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: Pittman has been on injured reserve since October 10th, and began running last week. While the veteran receiver said he hopes to return after the Steelers’ bye week, he also said that there’s “no time frame” for his return. Pittman’s foot injury was a reaggravation of a previous injury he had earlier in the season, so it wouldn’t be surprising if the Steelers exercised extreme caution to ensure it doesn’t flare up again when he returns. Pittman’s first season in Pittsburgh has been disappointing, to say the least. He has appeared in just three games and has totaled seven receptions for 89 scoreless yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Steelers placed WR Michael Pittman (foot) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: Pittman aggravated the foot injury that cost him Week 2 last week and will now miss four games, at minimum, while on injured reserve. Roman Wilson appears to be the primary beneficiary of Pittman’s absence and has seen six targets in each game this season while mostly playing a situational role. Wilson is a priority waiver addition over rookie Germie Bernard.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Michael Pittman re-aggravated his foot injury and will miss multiple weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: McCarthy told reporters the team is evaluating Pittman’s roster spot, meaning they could place him on injured reserve. He would miss at least four weeks while on IR. Pittman tried to play through the foot injury but only made it two weeks before aggravating the issue. He was spotted using a scooter to support his foot in the locker room on Wednesday. We suspect the Steelers will place him on IR to give Pittman enough time to fully recover. Germie Bernard will now operate as the team’s permanent WR3, with Roman Wilson taking on more work as the clear No. 2 receiver. Both players will be decent FLEX options for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: ESPN’s Brooke Pryor reports that Michael Pittman (foot) was in “the locker room with his left foot propped up on a scooter.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: Pittman has been playing through a foot injury this season and was seen participating in team stretches earlier today. Although the scooter use is alarming, this is likely just load management. Pittman is a boom-bust FLEX against the Colts this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Michael Pittman caught 2-of-4 targets for 15 yards in the Steelers’ Week 4 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: That makes two consecutive games with two receptions for the veteran X receiver, who continues to be handily outplayed by teammate Roman Wilson. Pittman brings his season total in receptions to seven after missing Week 2 with injury and remains largely confined to the short areas of the field. The Steelers made good on their promise to increase their 12-personnel utilization against the Browns, and it was Pittman who saw his route participation suffer the most. Pittman is quickly bordering drop candidate territory ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Michael Pittman caught 2-of-5 targets for 16 yards in the Steelers’ Week 3 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: Pittman was back in action after missing Week 2’s game with a foot injury. Despite being on the field for 28 routes, the veteran receiver struggled to make much of an impact, making two eight-yard receptions on back-to-back drives before fading into the distance. Pittman has caught 5-of-8 targets for 74 scoreless yards this season and shouldn’t be counted on for Week 4’s game against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Michael Pittman (foot) is active for Week 3 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: It was reported earlier on Sunday that Pittman was expected to suit up, so this isn’t much of a surprise. Despite being ready to go, Pittman will be hard to trust this week against a much-improved Bengals defense. He caught just three passes for 58 yards on three targets in his lone game this season and his best left on fantasy benches in most cases.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Michael Pittman (foot) is expected to play in Week 3 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: Pittman missed last week’s game with the foot issue and was limited in practice throughout this week. He was given a questionable designation on Friday. Pittman will return as the No. 2 receiver on a struggling offense, and he’s likely not back to full strength. Fantasy managers should keep him on the bench for at least one more game before getting him back into lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Michael Pittman (foot) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 3 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: He was limited in practice all three days this week with a foot injury that kept him out of Week 2. We’d say Pittman is on the optimistic side of questionable based on his participation status. If he’s out again, it would likely be Germie Bernard picking up the slack, as he did in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.headline: Michael Pittman (foot) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-pi.analysis: It seems like he’s trending towards playing, though Mike McCarthy seemed unsure about it earlier in the week. That’s two straight limited tags for Pittman. Friday will likely determine if he winds up with a questionable tag or not.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said Zachariah Branch (hamstring) will not play in Week 9 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Branch suffered a hamstring injury in Week 8’s shutout loss to the Buccaneers and will miss next week’s game against the Bengals in Madrid. The rookie third-rounder has caught just 10 passes for 64 scoreless yards this season and has also served as the Falcons’ primary kick and punt returner.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: It seemed like Branch would be in for a bigger role in Week 7 with Olamide Zaccheaus out with a shoulder injury. However, Branch ran a route on just 18 of 37 dropbacks and was only targeted twice. It doesn’t seem like he’s anywhere close to playing a large enough role for fantasy value and doesn’t need to be held through the bye weeks in redraft leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Falcons declared WR Olamide Zaccheaus, QB Jack Strand, QB Andy Dalton, RB Brian Robinson Jr., LB Divine Deablo, CB Avieon Terrell, and DB Billy Bowman Jr. inactive for Week 7 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) was ruled out earlier in the week, and Zaccheaus is dealing with a shoulder injury and will not be able to suit up for this one. That could mean more work in the receiving game for rookie Zachariah Branch, who might be worth a stash in deeper formats in case a solid game today earns him a bigger role moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch caught both of his targets for 14 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Branch’s primary duties still come on kick and punt returns, but Kevin Stefanski made it a point to get him more involved this week. He was held without a catch or even a target in Week 1. Branch isn’t on the fantasy radar yet, but dynasty managers can be pleased with his role taking a step in the right direction.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch had no targets in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: On one hand, no targets is bad. On the other hand, Branch played one more snap than Olamide Zaccheaus and ran only three fewer routes. This is not a passing attack that you want pieces of right now, but there is a chance that Branch could take the WR3 role by the middle of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) will play in Week 1 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Branch was limited by the hamstring issue for the first two practices of the week. He got up to a full practice on Friday and was cleared for Week 1. Branch will likely see a few designed touches in his NFL debut, but fantasy managers will want to wait until he overtakes Olamide Zaccheaus on the depth chart before getting him into their lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Falcons WR Zachariah Branch (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: The Falcons’ third-round rookie wide receiver could end up playing this week, but his inability to practice fully will keep him in a pure backup role. Branch does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Branch ran behind Olamide Zaccheaus for most of training camp. A light workload in practice heading into Week 1 all but guarantees he won’t threaten the veteran receiver for a starting role to open the year. Branch isn’t on the fantasy radar for his NFL debut versus the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: The Athletic’s Josh Kendall reports that Falcons WR Zachariah Branch is “looming” behind WR Olamide Zaccheaus for the starting slot role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: According to Kendall, “everyone in Atlanta can see” Branch’s ascension. The diminutive rookie has been “a standout in Atlanta from the moment he stepped on the practice field.” Zaccheaus is still taking most of the first-team snaps, so Branch may have to continue fighting for the starting role in-season. That said, the coaching staff plans to line up Branch at all three wide receiver spots. Obvious questions remain regarding Branch’s ability to play in the NFL at 5'10/180, but the youngster bench-pressed 225 pounds 20 times at the NFL Combine, so his strength is not in question. Even if Branch assumes a starting role, it will probably be tough for Branch to reliably return FLEX value, earning targets behind WR Drake London, TE Kyle Pitts and RB Bijan Robinson, but showing up with a few big performances is possible.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.headline: ESPN’s Marc Raimondi believes Falcons WR Zachariah Branch could start the season as a “gadget guy,” before later earning a starting role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zachariah-.analysis: Branch was a screen game dominator in college, with speed to spare. Raimondi thinks the Falcons will attempt to replicate his Georgia game early on, but Branch has a chance to become “the No. 3 guy, maybe even the No. 2 guy at some point.” Falcons WRs Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus sit in those two spots. Branch is unlikely to contribute meaningfully in fantasy early in the year, but he is worth keeping an eye on in-season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said the team is still deciding when it will open Travis Etienne’s (hamstring) 21-day return window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Etienne hasn’t played since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 3 against the Raiders. The 27-year-old back will need to have his 21-day return window opened before he can take the practice field, so we’ll see if Moore and the staff elect to designate him for a return ahead of Wednesday’s practice. Until that happens, Alvin Kamara, Kendre Miller, and CJ Donaldson will continue to operate as the Saints’ top options, with Kamara the likely leader in what has been an underwhelming backfield this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints placed Travis Etienne on injured reserve with a hamstring injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: This is a tough break. The Saints’ high-priced free agent signee will be sidelined for at least four games. Their Week 8 bye makes him eligible to return in Week 9. Veteran RB Alvin Kamara is the next man up, followed by RB Kendre Miller. Both should be rostered in 12-team leagues. Kamara will likely get the first crack at the starting job, but he has struggled to play efficiently this season, and coach Kellen Moore gave RB CJ Donaldson the backfield’s first green zone touch last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) “will miss time” and that a timeline for his return has not yet been determined.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: It’s unclear how much time Etienne will miss, but it wouldn’t be surprising if this became an injured reserve stint. Alvin Kamara could find himself in a more elevated role next week, perhaps with Kendre Miller joining him in a committee. Etienne exited Week 3’s loss to the Raiders with the injury after rushing for 57 yards on 13 carries. It had already been a tough scene for Etienne-reliant fantasy managers this year just based on how the results on the field were going; this won’t help.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints RB Travis Etienne exited Week 3 against the Raiders after suffering an apparent hamstring injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Etienne entered the game with a hamstring injury and appears to have aggravated it on an explosive run. The Saints’ starting running back broke off a 16-yard gain in the third quarter, setting up a Saints passing touchdown on the following play. Etienne could be seen grabbing at his left hamstring at the end of the run. He had mostly been limited to modest single-digit gains before that, rushing 13 times for 57 yards and catching 2-of-2 targets for 13 yards on the day. He seems highly unlikely to return. Etienne and the other veteran running backs notably ceded the first backfield touch inside the green zone to RB CJ Donaldson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints RB Travis Etienne (hamstring) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: We do not yet know today’s participation level, but Etienne logged two limited sessions to begin the week. Hopefully, we get a report pre-game revealing the injury’s severity, so we can better assess his potential usage. Given the Saints’ prior backfield workload splits and Etienne’s soft-tissue strain, he should probably be viewed as a low-end RB2/FLEX starter right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints RB Travis Etienne (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Etienne remains limited, which keeps him in the questionable camp for the Saints’ Week 3 game against the Raiders. Saints RB3 Kendre Miller was sidelined by an illness, but those rarely impact NFL players’ availability on game day. Veteran RB Alvin Kamara should be rostered wherever he is available.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints RB Travis Etienne (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Etienne begins the week with a limited session, which is either good or bad, depending on when the injury occurred. If this is a lingering issue from Sunday, Etienne should be considered likely to play. Limited practices early in the week are generally a good sign. However, if he suffered the injury during today’s practice, his Week 3 availability would be in jeopardy. Veteran Saints RB Alvin Kamara would likely get the start, but RB Kendre Miller would be FLEX-viable if Etienne sits.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Travis Etienne rushed eight times for 25 yards in the Saints’ Week 2 win over the Ravens, adding two receptions for 6 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Etienne tallied just two carries in the first half of this one while Alvin Kamara led the Saints backfield with 10 total touches through the first two quarters. Things would shift more in Etienne’s favor in the second half, as he out-snapped Kamara 21-to-7 while out-touching him 8-to-4. It was a disappointing outing overall, however, for the 27-year-old back, who has yet to find the end zone in his first two games and has managed just 109 yards from scrimmage on 26 touches. He’ll be hard to trust as anything more than an RB2/RB3 in next week’s game against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Alvin Kamara (knee) will play in Week 2 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Kamara was limited throughout practice last week and was ruled out with inactives. Moore said today that he could have played but needed more time on task, implying that limited preparation was the larger issue, not Kamara’s health. Travis Etienne split work with Kendre Miller last week. Kamara will presumably take on Miller’s role as the backup, though he could also eat into Etienne’s target total. Etienne caught seven balls in his Saints debut. If he loses that work, Etienne could fall out of the RB2 ranks entirely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.headline: Travis Etienne rushed nine times for 46 yards in the Saints’ Week 1 loss to the Lions, adding seven catches for 32 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-eti.analysis: Etienne was taken off the field a surprising amount, ceding nine carries to Kendre Miller and another two to CJ Donaldson. Donaldson also logged two targets. While his role on the ground was concerning for fantasy managers, a nine-target outing cushioned the blow slightly. In PPR leagues, Etienne did enough. Unless the Saints are going to play in overtime shootouts every week, Etienne will need to take on more rushing work to be a weekly RB2. With Alvin Kamara potentially returning next week, Etienne will sit on the RB2/3 border for his date with the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/yaya-diaby.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Buccaneers LB YaYa Diaby is dealing with a Grade 2 MCL sprain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/yaya-diaby.analysis: According to Rapoport, Diaby “should be back within a matter of weeks,” but it sounds like the fourth-year linebacker could avoid a stint on injured reserve. Diaby has totaled three sacks — all of which came in Week 7 against the Panthers- and also has 16 tackles and one interception this season. Diaby has started all eight games for the Bucs this year while playing on nearly 60 percent of the team’s defensive snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/yaya-diaby.headline: YaYa Diaby is believed to have suffered a sprained MCL after the Buccaneers’ Week 8 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/yaya-diaby.analysis: Diaby will undergo an MRI to confirm the severity of the injury, but according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, the team his hopeful that this injury will “not cause him to miss extended time.” Diaby has 16 tackles, three sacks, and one interception this season, with all three of his sacks coming in the Bucs’ Week 7 win over the Panthers. Even if he doesn’t miss too much time, it’s possible he’ll be sidelined for at least Week 9’s game against the Bears on Sunday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/yaya-diaby.headline: Bucs EDGE Yaya Diaby suffered a knee injury in Week 8 against the Falcons and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/yaya-diaby.analysis: Diaby went down in the first half and was ruled out before halftime. He was off to a slow start to the season before erupting for three sacks versus the Panthers last week. Diaby has started all eight Bucs games this year and has logged a snap share just under 60 percent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/yaya-diaby.headline: Bucs EDGE Yaya Diaby has been diagnosed with a high-ankle sprain and will be sidelined for 4-6 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/yaya-diaby.analysis: It’s good news in that it’s not a season-ending injury, but high-ankle issues are quite frequently season- altering issues. One silver lining here is that there are no current games to rush back for. Diaby might not be 100 percent by Week 1, but he will be much closer to it than most high-ankle sprain sufferers are when they return. Diaby notched 7.5 sacks as a third-round rookie last season, and profiles as a major part of the Bucs’ 2024 pass rush.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/yaya-diaby.headline: Buccaneers HC Todd Bowles said Yaya Diaby was carted off the field with an ankle injury during Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/yaya-diaby.analysis: We don’t know the severity of Diaby’s injury at this time, but his absence for any length of time would be a tough blow to the Buccaneers defense. As a rookie, Diaby totaled an impressive 12 TFLs and 7.5 sacks in 17 games on 515 snaps. The former third-rounder set the bar high heading into his second season and is expected to offer more contributions to a defense that finished as the fifth-best defense in points per game while ranking 10th in sacks. We’ll provide more on his injury when we have an update.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/yaya-diaby.headline: Buccaneers LB Shaquil Barrett (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday’s walkthrough.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/yaya-diaby.analysis: Barrett played in the Wild Card round against the Eagles, but is not dealing with an ankle issue that has him listed as a DNP for Wednesday’s walkthrough practice. Rookie Yaya Diaby (shoulder) joined Barrett as the other defender with a DNP listing. Both linebackers will have a chance to return to practice later in the week to prepare for the Divisional Round game against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/yaya-diaby.headline: Bucs selected Louisville EDGE YaYa Diaby with the No. 82 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/yaya-diaby.analysis: A former walk-on at Georgia Military College, Diaby (6’3/263) scrapped his way up through the collegiate ranks to have an impact in 2022 when he recorded 14.0 TFL (7th in ACC) and 9.0 sacks, which was the second-highest total in the ACC. His 34” arms and huge 10 ⅜” hands help him to leverage his natural strength when setting the edge and dislodge opposing linemen with his punch on the rush. Though Diaby only had one year of high-end production in college, his athletic traits are tantalizing. He ran a 4.51 40 (99th percentile) and a 1.51 10-yard split (99th percentile) to go with an outstanding 37” vertical (94th percentile) and 10’00” broad jump for a spectacular 9.86 RAS. He needs to avoid losing contain on run plays, refine his counters and expand his pass rush technique to take advantage of his intriguing potential. With some growth, Diaby could develop into a consistent 4-3 rotational defensive end who can bring pressure on demand.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyn-armo.headline: Chargers signed CB Jalyn Armour-Davis, formerly of the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyn-armo.analysis: Armour-Davis saw his 2025 season come to an end in Week 17 when he suffered a torn Achilles. The 27-year-old corner has spent the last 11 months rehabbing his injury and is now set to make his return for the winless Chargers. To the surprise of nobody, Armour-Davis is yet another player with ties to a Harbaugh brother, as he began his career playing under John Harbaugh with the Ravens from 2022 to 2024. Now, he’ll have a chance to play under Jim Harbaugh and could see playing time in the coming weeks once he gets up to speed. Armour-Davis allowed 24 receptions for 346 yards and two touchdowns on 31 targets last season while with the Titans, earning a PFF coverage grade up 49.6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyn-armo.headline: Titans ruled out C Lloyd Cushenberry (foot) for Week 13 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyn-armo.analysis: Cushenberry’s absence is unfortunate. The Jaguars’ pass rush has played well in recent weeks. The Titans also ruled out DT Shy Tuttle (concussion), S Xavier Woods (hamstring), S Kendell Brooks (concussion) and CB Jalyn Armour-Davis (Achilles). Armour-Davis’ injury is a bit concerning. He was downgraded to a DNP on Thursday. Hopefully, it is only a short-term issue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyn-armo.headline: Titans claimed CB Jalyn Armour-Davis off waivers from the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyn-armo.analysis: The Titans have been lacking this particular brand of body outside, so there’s a chance that Armour-Davis slides right into being their top backup behind L’Jarius Sneed, Amani Hooker, and Jarvis Brownlee. The Titans also claimed DB Samuel Womack from the Colts, OL Clay Webb from the Broncos, and LB Dorian Mausi from the Vikings on waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyn-armo.headline: Ravens waived CB Jalyn Armour-Davis.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyn-armo.analysis: The 2022 fourth-rounder pick played well in the preseason, notching a 84.7 PFF coverage grade in 49 coverage snaps. He’s only started three games in three years with Baltimore, but was a key special-teams player. Armour-Davis could draw waiver wire interest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyn-armo.headline: Ravens CB Nate Wiggins (shoulder/illness) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyn-armo.analysis: Ravens CB Arthur Maulet (neck) will also play in Week 9. Starter CB Marlon Humphrey (knee) was limited all week and is now labeled as questionable. Backup Jalyn Armour-Davis (knee) was a healthy participant on Wednesday and Thursday but showed up on the Friday injury report as a DNP. He is also questionable to play in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyn-armo.headline: Ravens selected Alabama CB Jalyn Armour-Davis with the No. 119 overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyn-armo.analysis: A first-year starter in 2021, Armour-Davis (6'0/197) finished with 32 tackles and three interceptions, resulting in All-SEC Second Team honors. He is coming into the draft as one of the more exciting prospects with all the traits you want in an NFL cornerback. Armour-Davis has the look of an elite corner with his size and athleticism. As a former 100-meter state champion, he has the speed to guard downfield and can stay on pace with the fastest receivers in the game. His 4.39 40-yard time shows that. He also displays impressive footwork, showing it off in press coverage where you see him mirror a receiver’s route almost perfectly, granting minimal separation and using his length to disrupt passes. There’s not much he needs to improve, except sometimes he can be a little hesitant on his first move. Although he has the athleticism to recover, it could hinder him slightly against top-tier talent. There is very little to nitpick on Armour-Davis, and he can become of the bigger sleepers in this draft.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyn-armo.headline: CBS Sports’ Chris Trapasso said Alabama DB Jalyn Armour-Davis “will be in my final top 100.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyn-armo.analysis: Armour-Davis (6'1/192) ran a 4.39 40-yard dash at the NFL Scouting Combine, and put on a solid showing at Alabama’s pro day. Armour-Davis won’t hear his name called in the first round, but he turned in a solid 2021 at Alabama after seeing limited action in 2019 and 2020 due to medical issues. Per PFF.com, Armour-Davis allowed 27 receptions for 290 yards and no touchdowns last season, while forcing three interceptions and breaking up three passes. Opposing quarterbacks had a 52.3 QBR when throwing in Armour-Davis’ direction, and he drew just two penalties on the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyn-armo.headline: Alabama CB Jalyn Armour-Davis will enter the draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyn-armo.analysis: Armour-Davis (6'0/165) will forgo his senior year and declare for the draft. He finished the season with three interceptions and four passes deflected for the Crimson Tide.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyn-armo.headline: Alabama HC Nick Saban did not offer a specific recovery timetable when asked about the status of redshirt freshman CB Jalyn Armour-Davis (knee).
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyn-armo.analysis: Armour-Davis (6'0/165) suffered a season-ending knee injury during pregame warmups for last September’s game against Arkansas State. He was not healthy enough to take part in spring practice, but if you were hoping for a concrete timetable from Coach Saban, no such luck. During a fundraiser on Wednesday, he said that “Jalyn’s got some medical issues now that he’s going to have to work through over the summer.” Saban figures to give us a little more information (maybe?) when preseason camps lurch to life in two months. Armour-Davis signed with Alabama as a four-star recruit in the 2018 class. He’s a developmental prospect at this early juncture in his career.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyn-armo.headline: Uncommitted four-star 2018 CB Jalyn Armour-Davis listed Florida, Auburn, LSU, Georgia, Florida State and USC as the finalists for his pledge.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalyn-armo.analysis: It is no real surprise that Armour-Davis has slotted four SEC programs among his finalists, as the 6-foot, 165-pounder hails from Mobile, Alabama. Auburn and Florida State have both hosted him for recent unofficial visits. Scout.com ranks Armour-Davis as the No. 1 prospect in the state and No. 152 overall. He told the outlet that he plans on making a commitment “pretty soon.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.headline: Jaguars DT DaVon Hamilton suffered a torn quad in Week 8’s win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.analysis: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport was the first to report the injury. This is expected to be a season-ender for Hamilton, who has totaled 16 tackles and a half sack this season. Hamilton has earned a 74.0 PFF defensive grade this season and is a key contributor top-five run defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.headline: Jaguars selected Ohio State DT Davon Hamilton with the No. 73 overall pick in the 2020 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.analysis: Hamilton (6’4/320) was a one-year starting nose tackle at Ohio State who earned third-team All-Big Ten honors as a redshirt senior. Before his breakout campaign in 2019, he was a rotational depth option for the Buckeyes, but improved conditioning and maturity led to career highs in sacks (6.0), TFLs (10.5), and tackles (28) last season. He wins with a bull rush on tape, which was backed up by a class-leading 31 bench press reps at the NFL Combine. He lacks the burst of an interior disruptor in the NFL, but Hamilton figures to compete for a starting defensive tackle job because of his strength and physical playing style.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.headline: NFL Media’s Lance Zierlein compares Ohio State DT DaVon Hamilton to former Bengals/Raiders DT Pat Sims.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.analysis: Hamilton (6'4/320) performed well at the NFL Scouting Combine, as he tallied an impressive 33 reps in the bench press and ran the 40 in 5.14 seconds. Just how high he goes in April’s draft will largely depend upon how teams view him as a pass rusher, with Hamilton having proven just how effective he can be against the run. “He flashes needed traits as both a one- and two-gapper, but better skill with his hand-fighting could help unlock quicker wins and clearer paths to the quarterback,” Zierlein wrote. “His draft stock could be tied to how teams view his upside as a pass rusher.” Hamilton projects to be an early Day 3 selection, with a shot at sneaking in late on Day 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.headline: Ohio State DL DaVon Hamilton posted 33 reps on the bench press at the NFL Scouting Combine.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.analysis: Those 33 reps from Hamilton (6'4/320) are the most of any defensive lineman at the combine, and the fourth most of all players who have participated so far. The defensive tackle was strong for the Buckeyes -- literally and figuratively -- with five sacks and 8.5 tackles for loss in 2019, and also helped plug the line to allow stars like Chase Young go to work. He’s viewed as a mid-round prospect at this point, but if a team believes he can get to the quarterback, it’s not hard to imagine he goes earlier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.headline: Ohio State DL Davon Hamilton has accepted his invitation to play in the 2020 Reese’s Senior Bowl.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.analysis: Hamilton (6'4/300) did a lot of the dirty work inside the tackles by occupying double-teams and bringing interior pressure that allowed Chase Young to run wild on opposing offenses. He posted 25 tackles, 16 solo, 5.0 sacks and 8.5 TFL this season and has 19 sacks over his Buckeye career. Hamilton has been in the Buckeye program for five years and is viewed as a potential Day 3 selection should he perform well in the CFB playoff and Senior Bowl practices.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.headline: Dave Biddle of 247Sports reports Ohio State redshirt freshman DL Devon Hamilton exited spring “locked in as Michael Hill’s backup at the 1-technique” after being “the biggest pleasant surprise of spring.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.analysis: The 6-foot-4, 300-pound Hamilton, a natural DT who has the versatility to play DE, went off for three sacks in the spring game at the Horseshoe. “Urban Meyer mentioned [Hamilton a] couple weeks ago as guy having a good spring,” Cleveland.com’s Doug Lesmerises wrote in a tweet during the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.headline: Ohio State redshirt sophomore DL Devon Hamilton is not participating in spring practice due to recent surgery to repair a broken foot.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.analysis: No word as to exactly when Hamilton underwent surgery, but regardless, his recovery has sidelined him for the spring. This past season, the 6-foot-4, 300-pounder recorded 10 tackles (2.5 for loss) and one fumble recovered over the course of nine games played. Scout.com ranked Hamilton as the No. 54 defensive tackle prospect in the 2015 class.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.headline: Ohio State HC Urban Meyer said that redshirt sophomore DL Davon Hamilton has been fighting through a back injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.analysis: Hamilton (6'4/300) has seen his playing time limited in part because of the injury and has recorded just eight tackles (2.0 for loss) on the year. This back issue is not the only health concern that the redshirt sophomore has had to deal with since the 2016 season, as he also underwent surgery to repair a broken foot during the offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo caught 2-of-4 targets for 32 yards in the Commanders’ Week 8 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo flashed his athletic ability with a full-stretch reception in the second half but it was not enough to overshadow a first quarter fumble. The spry veteran has now been held to four receptions or fewer in four of five appearances in the low volume Washington pass offense, unable to return consistent fantasy value through the absence of Terry McLaurin. He is best left on fantasy benches in a Week 9 matchup against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Terry McLaurin (knee) tore his patellar tendon and will miss the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: It’s another rough blow for Washington’s No. 1 wideout, who will now have missed most of the last two seasons with injuries with the book closed on a 15-catch, 230-yard 2026 season in just five games. Entering his age-32 season in 2027, McLaurin will be a release or restructure candidate with a $34 million cap hit. The Commanders could save $16 million by releasing him without getting into post-June 1 antics. In the short term fantasy calculus, Stefon Diggs will slide in as Washington’s No. 1 receiver and Chig Okonkwo will also get a boost. Antonio Williams figures to see more snaps going forward as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: ESPN’s John Keim reports Terry McLaurin’s knee injury is considered “significant.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Washington head coach Dan Quinn said after the team’s Monday night loss to the 49ers that there was “fear” McLaurin could be lost for the long-term after going down with a non-contact injury and was carted to the locker room. McLaurin has functioned as the team’s lone downfield threat for much of the season, and could be replaced with Treylon Burks, who on Monday night caught four balls for 66 yards before sustaining a late-game injury. Antonio Williams and Dyami Brown could also see an increase in routes and targets if McLaurin is sidelined for a while. Look for Chig Okonkwo to see an uptick in targets too. Okonkwo had seven grabs for 69 yards against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo caught all seven targets for 69 yards in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo was thrust into an increased role with the departure of lead wide receiver Terry McLaurin in the first quarter, operating as the primary option through the air for much of the game. Veteran wide receiver Stefon Diggs continued to operate in a situational role, making Okonkwo a priority start when the Commanders come out of their Week 7 bye to face the Eagles in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said he is hopeful Diggs will get some practice reps in later this week. Diggs missed Week 5 with the hamstring issue, and a DNP today puts him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 6, even if Quinn remains optimistic. Terry McLaurin and Chig Okonkwo led the team in receiving last week. McLaurin should pull away from Okonkwo as he puts more time between himself and the hamstring injury that previously knocked him out for a week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo caught 4-of-6 targets for 60 yards in the Commanders’ Week 5 tie with the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo caught two passes on the Commander’s opening and immediately topped his previous best game of the season. He hauled in passes of 11 and 23 yards on back-to-back catches before Jacory Croskey-Merritt ended the drive with a 33-yard touchdown run. Okonkwo would come up with a 25-yard reception later in the second quarter on a drive that ended with a Drew Stevens field goal, but was targeted just one time in the second half. It was an overall nice outing for Okonkwo, but fantasy managers shouldn’t rush to add him to their lineups. He’ll be a boom-or-bust streaming option in Week 6 against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) is not on the final injury report for Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo got in a full practice on Friday after consecutive limited sessions. With Stefon Diggs (hamstring) out, Terry McLaurin (hamstring) questionable and Jayden Daniels (elbow) returning, Okonkwo could warrant top-12 positional treatment this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: With Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs both absent for a second day in a row on Thursday, Okonkwo could catch some desperation TE1 steam on Friday. He seems on track to play and Jayden Daniels should provide a more reliable passing floor than he had last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
