https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonwko returned to the lineup last week after missing a handful of games with the hamstring injury. His limited designation today is likely just maintenance. With Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs banged up, he should see more work in Week 5. Okonkwo is in the TE2 mix for Sunday’s game versus the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo caught 2-of-4 targets for five yards in the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo was back in action today after missing the last two games with a hamstring issue. With Marcus Mariota exiting this game early because of an injury, the passing attack was out of whack from the jump. There wasn’t much of a chance to reinstall Okonkwo into the mix this week. The hope is that he will earn more work with Jayden Daniels potentially back in the lineup in Week 5, but fantasy managers will need to see it to believe it with Okonkwo.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs caught 3-of-6 targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 8 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Offensive coordinator David Blough ha made good on his promise not to increase the route participation or snap rate of the veteran receiver in the absence of Terry McLaurin, effectively keeping Diggs relegated to a situational role primarily from the slot. That has left Treylon Burks and rookie Antonio Williams to lead the team in routes the previous two weeks while limiting the true ceiling of Diggs in the process. Consider Diggs a touchdown-dependent FLEX option in a difficult matchup against the Rams in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hand/hamstring) is not on Washington’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: He should be a mid-range WR3 with Terry McLaurin out of the picture in Washington. Diggs practiced in full each of the last two sessions of the week after a Wednesday DNP.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hand/hamstring) practiced in full Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs shook of the absence Wednesday with a full showing Thursday, indicating he is tracking well to suit up when the Commanders face off against the Eagles on Sunday Night Football. The tam previously indicated that Diggs’ modest role would not grow in the absence of Terry McLaurin, potentially paving the way for rookie Antonio Williams to see an increase in role and opportunity in the second half of the season. Fantasy managers will want to confirm Diggs’ status on the final injury report Friday, but it appears as if he will be available in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hand/hamstring/rest) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn already said Diggs won’t practice Wednesday, so this is not a surprise. Quinn also confirmed the veteran will return to practice Thursday and the additional rest designation should stave off concerns of Diggs dealing with a long-term injury. He should be in the WR3/FLEX mix for Week 8 against the Eagles. Also not practicing for the Commanders was TE John Bates (shoulder).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Stefon Diggs will practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs won’t practice Wednesday with an undisclosed injury. He should be fine for Washington’s Week 8 matchup against the Eagles, however. Diggs could see a slightly bigger role in the Commanders offense with Terry McLaurin (knee) done for the year. Diggs drafters should keep an eye on the veteran’s practice status in the coming days. Diggs has been targeted on a team-high 28 percent of his pass routes in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said he doesn’t anticipate Stefon Diggs taking on a larger role with Terry McLaurin lost for the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Quinn did mention usage from “elsewhere” and the name “Antonio Williams” came up. Williams won’t be a buzzy waiver wire claim this week but could find himself in a reasonable WR3/WR4 sort of situation as the year unfolds.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Terry McLaurin (knee) tore his patellar tendon and will miss the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: It’s another rough blow for Washington’s No. 1 wideout, who will now have missed most of the last two seasons with injuries with the book closed on a 15-catch, 230-yard 2026 season in just five games. Entering his age-32 season in 2027, McLaurin will be a release or restructure candidate with a $34 million cap hit. The Commanders could save $16 million by releasing him without getting into post-June 1 antics. In the short term fantasy calculus, Stefon Diggs will slide in as Washington’s No. 1 receiver and Chig Okonkwo will also get a boost. Antonio Williams figures to see more snaps going forward as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs caught 6-of-7 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: While the end line looks good in the box score, the fact that Diggs continued to operate in a situational role following the departure of Terry McLaurin in the first quarter was somewhat concerning for the veteran receiver’s upside potential in McLaurin’s absence, although the fact that he came into the game listed as questionable with a hamstring injury could have influenced his snap rate. Either way, Diggs continues to produce when on the field, returning significant value for fantasy managers that invested a middle-round pick for his services this summer. Diggs will be an upside WR3 when the Commanders take on the division rival Eagles in Week 8 following their bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is active for Week 6 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs returns from a one-game absence due a hamstring injury. Although possible he sees his route participation curtailed, fantasy managers that made it this far are likely forced to ride with the veteran receiver in a solid schematic matchup against the zone-heavy 49ers. Inactive for the Commanders are QB Marcus Mariota, CB Fabian Moreau, CB Isaac Yiadom, OLB T.J. Magunranyanga, G Tanoa Togiai, and DE Charles Omenihu.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is questionable for Week 6 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs returned to the practice field Friday as a limited participant, following it with another practice with the same status a day later. The listed his as questionable for Monday Night Football against the 49ers as he attempts to return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Fantasy managers might be better off playing it safe considering the timing of the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Antonio Williams caught 5-of-7 targets for 54 yards in the Commanders’ Week 8 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Williams mostly operated in a short area role but added a 30-yard grab up the seam in the fourth quarter to pad his counting stats for fantasy managers hoping on a second-half rookie breakout. While the fantasy returns have yet to pop, managers can continue to hold the electric rookie in the hopes his role grows in the coming weeks. That said, he is likely best left on fantasy benches until his route structure improves.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Treylon Burks (foot) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Burks downgraded from a limited showing Wednesday to a “DNP” Thursday, indicating he might be headed toward an absence when the Commanders take on the Eagles on Sunday Night Football. Considering the team is already without Terry McLaurin, who was lost for the season in Week 6, this would appear to be setting up for the best chance for rookie Antonio Williams to finally break out in Washington. Fantasy managers will want to confirm the status of Burks on the team’s final injury report Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said he doesn’t anticipate Stefon Diggs taking on a larger role with Terry McLaurin lost for the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Quinn did mention usage from “elsewhere” and the name “Antonio Williams” came up. Williams won’t be a buzzy waiver wire claim this week but could find himself in a reasonable WR3/WR4 sort of situation as the year unfolds.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Terry McLaurin (knee) tore his patellar tendon and will miss the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: It’s another rough blow for Washington’s No. 1 wideout, who will now have missed most of the last two seasons with injuries with the book closed on a 15-catch, 230-yard 2026 season in just five games. Entering his age-32 season in 2027, McLaurin will be a release or restructure candidate with a $34 million cap hit. The Commanders could save $16 million by releasing him without getting into post-June 1 antics. In the short term fantasy calculus, Stefon Diggs will slide in as Washington’s No. 1 receiver and Chig Okonkwo will also get a boost. Antonio Williams figures to see more snaps going forward as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Antonio Williams caught 3-of-4 targets for 50 yards in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: While the yardage total looks solid on paper, the fact that Williams had only four targets in a game in which veteran wide receiver Terry McLaurin departed in the first quarter and quarterback Jayden Daniels attempted 40 passes is concerning. Williams continues to flash big play upside through a multitude of injuries to teammates but has yet to fully take advantage of the increase in opportunity, something fantasy managers will hope corrects when the Commanders come out of their bye to face the Eagles in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Terry McLaurin (hamstring) will “most likely” be a game-time decision for Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Keep it locked to Rotoworld, folks. Hopefully, we get word on McLaurin’s status on Saturday, but it appears as though we may have to wait until Sunday morning. Fowler adds that rookie WR Antonio Williams “could be a factor in the passing game regardless of whether McLaurin plays.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) will not play in Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Diggs did not practice this week and was ruled out by the team shortly after Friday’s practice concluded. His absence will give rookie Antonio Williams, who ran 30 routes last week, a chance to take on a bigger role. Williams tied for the team lead with eight targets in Week 4’s game against the Colts and could be treated as a desperation WR4/FLEX play. Fantasy managers considering Williams for their lineups may want to check the weather, as rain and wind are currently forecasted for the area, which could create a suboptimal environment for Washington’s passing game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Diggs didn’t appear to get hurt during the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts, but it looks like he felt something after the game. With Terry McLaurin also sidelined for today’s practice, Antonio Williams could be the Commanders’ No. 1 receiver in Week 5. He saw eight targets on Sunday, only one fewer than Diggs. The Commanders’ absurdly long injury report will be one to monitor as the week progresses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Antonio Williams caught 3-of-8 targets for 21 yards in the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: With Terry McLaurin out, Williams fully took over as the team’s No. 2 receiver. His eight targets were good for a 22 percent target share and he led the Commanders in routes. The bad news is that the offense struggled after Marcus Mariota went down with a knee injury. That happened in the first quarter, so Washington had a third-string quarterback under center for the majority of this game. If the role sticks, Williams could be a viable FLEX play once Jayden Daniels returns. The Commanders’ injury report will be one to watch heading into Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Antonio Williams caught 2-of-4 targets for 15 yards in the Commanders’ Week 3 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: The Commanders were able to put up an impressive 34 points — six of those coming on a pick six, but still — against the Seahawks, but Williams had little to do with it with a long gain of nine. The 2026 third-round pick has a chance to be a solid PPR play at some point, but Williams is much more of a dynasty option than a redraft one at this stage. He’ll likely be the third wideout for Washington in Week 4 against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White rushed 11 times for 55 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 8 win over the Eagles, adding five yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: White averaged just over two yards per carry on his first eight attempts before breaking loose for a 33-yard gain entering the final two minutes of the fourth quarter. He would find the end zone two plays later to salvage an otherwise underwhelming fantasy outing while operating in a three-way timeshare with Austin Ekeler and Jeremy McNichols. Although White’s fantasy value is clearly higher in the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt, his performance in Week 8 goes down as his first fantasy-viable start through the first eight weeks of the 2026 season. Fantasy managers are likely better off exploring alternatives ahead of a poor matchup against the Rams in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White rushed seven times for 27 yards in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers, adding 30 yards and a touchdown on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: The Commanders immediately found themselves in a negative game environment, managing just 17 offensive plays and 90 yards of total offense in the first half. While White found the end zone from nine yards out in the fourth quarter on an in-breaking route, the backfield split amongst White, Jeremy McNichols, and Austin Ekeler was troubling for fantasy managers looking to the former as a potential option with lead back Jacory Croskey-Merritt on injured reserve. White and the Commanders head to their bye week at a 1-4-1 record and some serious questions to answer, the least of which is the current state of their backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Commanders ruled out RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) for Week 6 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: No surprise here. Croskey-Merritt has been dealing with a groin injury since the start of the season. This week he couldn’t practice and has since been officially ruled out for the Commanders’ Monday Night Football matchup against the 49ers. Croskey-Merritt will get a two-week break with Washington on bye in Week 7. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler figure to handle the majority of the backfield touches in his absence with White being the preferred fantasy option between the two.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: Croskey-Merritt has played through multiple injuries this year. We still think he has a chance to face the 49ers in Week 6’s Monday Night Football game. Rachaad White (shoulder) sported a red non-contact jersey for the first time this week, and was downgraded to limited today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Austin Ekeler (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: Ekeler and Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) are both ailing, though the latter player sat out entirely. Rachaad White (shoulder) and Jeremy McNichols (quad) are both practicing in full. Croskey-Merritt is the only fantasy-relevant Commanders running back at this time, assuming he is good to go on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White rushed seven times for 18 yards in the Commanders’ Week 5 tie against the Giants, adding one reception for two additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: White continued to serve as the RB2 behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt and led the backfield with 11 snaps on third down. While his role remained largely the same, even with Austin Ekeler active, White offered nothing of fantasy value in this one. He saw only one target on the afternoon, and could continue to have his fantasy upside limited as long as Jayden Daniels is scrambling away from pressure rather than dumping it off to his checkdown options. Fantasy managers should avoid White in Week 6 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White (shoulder) will play in Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: In addition to White, the Commanders will also get RG Sam Cosmi back after missing the last two games with a concussion. White will likely return to his role as the team’s third-down/pass-catching back, but could be at risk of having Austin Ekeler eat into some of his workload. Fantasy managers hoping for White to return to the 10.3 touches/gm he was averaging before his injury may want to temper expectations and leave him on the bench while we wait to see how Ekeler is factored into the game plan.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White (shoulder) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: He looks to be on track to return to the backfield in Week 5. What percentage of carries that leaves him in a post-Ekeler world appears to be open to interpretation. We would not recommend starting him in any reasonably-sized league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: White injured his shoulder in Week 3. He did not practice once last week before being ruled out on Friday. A limited practice today puts him on track to suit up in Week 5. With Austin Ekeler now on the roster, White’s role as the team’s top back on passing situations could be at risk. Fantasy managers will want to leave him on the bench for another week, even if he is cleared to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White (shoulder) will not play in Washington’s Week 4 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: He didn’t practice at any point this week after suffering a shoulder injury in Week 3. He has to be considered questionable for Week 5 at this point. ‘Bill’ Croskey-Merritt figures to shoulder the majority of the workload for the Commanders this week and is a reasonable FLEX play against the Colts. Freshly-signed Austin Ekeler figures to handle third-down work.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Jayden Daniels completed 16-of-29 passes for 217 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ 27-10, Week 8 win over the Eagles, adding 23 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Daniels started the game going 4-of-10 passing in the first quarter, which included an interception that was called back due to penalty, two false start penalties in the red zone, and a missed field goal, causing the Commanders to quickly fall into a 10-point deficit. They would clean things up from there as they rattled off 27 unanswered points to improve to 2-4-1 as they chase the division-leading Giants. A 53-yard completion to Treylon Burks and 30-yard completions to Antonio Williams and Stefon Diggs gave the offense explosive plays in key situations during the final three frames to boost Daniels’ counting stats despite poor efficiency. The win was the first victory in a Daniels start since 5 October of the 2025 season as the Commanders saved their season, at least for the moment. They get a difficult matchup against the Rams in Week 9, where Daniels will remain a middling QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes it could make long-term sense for the Commanders to acquire Brian Thomas, Jr.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Shipley mentions the Commanders and Rams as wideout-desperate teams who might be interested in trading for Thomas before the NFL’s trade deadline. The Jaguars have apparently soured on the one-time burgeoning star in recent weeks; against the Texans in Week 6, Thomas ran a pass route on just 28 percent of the Jags’ drop backs and saw two targets. The Commanders, meanwhile, lost Terry McLaurin to a potentially long-term knee injury on Monday night. Thomas, per Shipley, “is not a trade that would make a ton of sense for a Commanders team that might be losing a ton of games and needs their picks to rebuild ... but it would make sense for a general manager who needs to keep his job to give his quarterback a familiar and talented target. Daniels was Thomas’ quarterback during their final seasons at LSU, and the connection between the two could go a long-way toward solving some of Washington’s long-term issues at the wide receiver position.” BTJ’s fantasy prospects would get a big boost if he were to land in Washington in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Jayden Daniels completed 29-of-40 passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns in the Commanders’ 23-17, Week 6 loss to the 49ers, adding 10 yards on four carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: The Commanders gained just 90 yards of total offense and ran just 17 offensive plays in the first half, taking a 20-3 deficit into the break. Two quick touchdown drives to end the third quarter and begin the fourth quarter had the team in position to pull off an improbable comeback but two critical errors from Daniels sank that effort. The first error occurred on fourth down in the red zone with just over two minutes to play, when the team was late to break the huddle and ended up taking their first timeout down by six. They would fail to convert but would get the ball back with no timeouts and 52 seconds left. Daniels then committed an intentional grounding penalty from the San Francisco 28 with 16 seconds left, which incurred a loss of down and a 10-second runoff on the clock. The game would end on the following play. That now makes consecutive contests with late-game clock mismanagement that cost the Commanders potential wins. Rumors continue to swirl about a potential coaching change as the Commanders limp into their bye at a 1-4-1 record.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Jayden Daniels completed 17-of-25 passes for 199 yards in the Commanders’ 27-27, Week 5 tie with the Giants, adding nine carries for 103 additional yards and two touchdowns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Daniels turned in one of the best games of his career on the ground on Sunday against the Giants. Daniels broke off an uncontested 38-yard touchdown run in the third quarter to put the Commanders up 19-6, and later broke free for a 26-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter to again extend the Commanders’ lead. Both runs came on scrambles where the Giants seemingly forgot Daniels was a threat to run at any moment, and Daniels made the most of his opportunities. With the Commanders in range for a game-winning field goal late in overtime, Daniels inexplicably took a sack with no timeouts left on what appeared to be an attempt to center the ball in time for the game-winning try. We’ll likely get an explanation from both Daniels and head coach Dan Quinn on that final play, but Washington snatched defeat from the jaws of victory to move to 1-3-1 on the season. Despite the late-game gaffe, Daniels looked on-point for most of the afternoon, but struggled at times against the blitz, as the Giants brought pressure in several key spots to force Daniels to get the ball out quick or throw it away. Daniels looked like the elite dual threat fantasy managers want to see, and will be firmly in the QB1 ranks in next week’s game against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports “there are doctors around the NFL who believe it’s a matter of when, not if, Jayden Daniels hurts his left elbow again.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Schefter immediately added the caveat that the “overwhelming opinion” among doctors was that playing with a brace was a viable option. Daniels reportedly contemplated surgery after dislocating his elbow for the second time in less than a year. He opted against it and missed two games. Daniels is now set to return for Week 5 against the Giants. The Commanders could scale back his rushing for the time being, but OC David Blough already dismissed the idea that the playbook would be limited because of Daniels’ elbow injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Jayden Daniels (elbow) is “not 100 percent” healthy yet.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Rapoport, typically cheery on the injury front, said that there are still “a lot of questions, going forward, for Jayden Daniels.” The bottom line is that Daniels is still rehabbing the elbow in his non-throwing arm. He should be able to throw and run effectively, putting him squarely in the QB1 tier, but re-injury risk remains a factor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Jayden Daniels (elbow) will start in Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Daniels appeared to be close to playing in Week 4 against the Colts before ultimately being ruled out. His being upgraded to a full participant in Thursday’s practice suggested he was a virtual lock to start in Week 5, barring any unexpected setbacks. Daniels will wear a brace on his left arm for the rest of the season in hopes of avoiding a three-peat of his dislocated elbow. Daniels will be without Stefon Diggs (hamstring) for Sunday’s game, and rainy/windy conditions are currently in the forecast. We’ll conservatively project him as a mid-to-low-end QB1 in what could be less-than-ideal conditions on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough said Jayden Daniels is a “full go” when asked if his elbow injury would create any limitations in the game plan.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Daniels is practicing in full and is expected to return to the lineup this week. He has suffered the same elbow dislocation twice in the past year, but his game-changing running ability is a big part of what makes Daniels a potential superstar quarterback. Blough might be more tactile with how he calls quarterback runs, but they will still be in the playbook this week. Daniels will be a low-end QB1 once he is officially cleared to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: ESPN’s John Keim reports Jayden Daniels (elbow) is expected to be a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo already reported that Daniels is expected to play in Week 5 and a full practice to open the week all but confirms his update. With Marcus Mariota also banged up, seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis would have been the next man up. He will back Daniels up as long as the latter doesn’t suffer any setbacks. The Commanders will likely dial back the designed runs for their franchise quarterback, but fantasy managers have to start him as a low-end QB1 as long as he’s on the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Jayden Daniels (elbow) is “on track” to start for the Commanders in Washington’s Week 5 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Washington will be trying to keep their season on the tracks after falling to 1-3 against the Colts while having to go to third-stringer Athan Kaliakmanis. It’s unsurprising that they’re rushing Daniels back. Even if you factor in an elevated chance of re-injury, Daniels probably clears the QB1 line for fantasy managers against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert caught 3-of-4 targets for 30 yards in the Eagles’ Week 8 loss to the Commanders, adding two yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert also committed a drop that was intercepted in the down performance, although the play in question was overturned through penalty. The veteran tight end continues to be limited by an ineffective offense with Tanner McKee under center in what has quickly become a lost season after the team’s sixth consecutive loss. Fantasy managers are likely better off looking for viable alternatives ahead of a Week 9 divisional clash with the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert caught 5-of-7 targets for 48 yards in the Eagles’ Week 7 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert has now returned consecutive games of middling production with Tanner McKee under center, which is a somewhat troubling realization considering DeVonta Smith missed both games and Dontayvion Wicks departed Week 6 with an injury before missing Week 7. Goedert’s fantasy value appears strictly tied to the state of a sinking Philadelphia ball club, now fighting through declining quarterback play in addition to poor offensive structure and shoddy play calling. Fantasy managers are likely forced to endure the middling production for lack of better options.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) was removed from the injury report Saturday and will play against the Cowboys in Week 7.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert reportedly aggravated his previous knee injury but got back on the practice field for a full session Saturday before being removed from the injury report. He could be stepping into a massive target share with both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks ruled out. Fantasy managers can start him as an upside TE1 in a great matchup against the Cowboys in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert is on the wrong side of questionable for the Eagles’ Week 7 Monday Night Football game against the Cowboys. The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane reports that as of Thursday, there was “optimism” about Goedert’s Week 7 availability. Hopefully, he resumes practicing tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert missed time with a knee injury earlier this year, but he was not on the injury report last week. This could just be a maintenance day, but it is worth keeping an eye on in the lead up to the Eagles’ Monday Night Football game against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert caught 6-of-8 targets for 61 yards in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Early in the game, when Tanner McKee was struggling to get anything going, he seemed locked onto Goedert. When the Panthers were up by multiple scores and the defense seemed to allow some more space in the secondary, McKee felt more confident in taking shots down the field to his receivers, which meant Goedert was quiet in the second half. Still, he was second on the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards and will be a low-end TE1 against the Cowboys next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert caught 6-of-9 targets for 38 yards in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert returned to the lineup after missing three games with a knee injury. Already without Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith, Goedert was immediately thrust into a high-usage role. He led the team in targets and catches, though much of his looks were simply check-downs. Even if that’s his role going forward, Goedert should catch enough passes to sustain borderline TE1 numbers until DeVonta Smith returns. He gets a date with the Panthers in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) is not on Philadelphia’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert got in a full session on Friday and is cleared. With DeVonta Smith down, he has some TE1 potential against the Jaguars on volume. He’s always been one of Jalen Hurts’ favorite red zone targets, and Saquon Barkley being down may lead the Eagles to throw more once the field condenses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert’s return cannot come soon enough. DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Hollywood Brown (ankle) remain sidelined, and Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) got hurt in today’s practice. If Goedert can play this week, he will vault right back into the TE1 tier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: It’s Goedert’s first practice since going down with a knee injury in Week 2. Even a limited session today puts him on track to suit up for Philly’s Week 5 game against the Jags. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) unlikely to play, Goedert could be in line for a large role right away. He will be on the TE1/2 border for Week 5 if he is cleared for action.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 6-of-9 targets for 57 yards in the Eagles’ Week 8 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon led the team in receiving for the second consecutive game without both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, although the returns were nothing to write home about in Week 8. Largely confined to a short area role, Lemon’s nine targets were mostly the product of the offense’s inability to attack downfield and carry weak per-target upside, a trend likely to continue for as long as Tanner McKee remains under center. That leaves fantasy managers in a precarious position heading into a Week 9 showdown against the Giants, where better options likely exist.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 7-of-8 targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 7 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon showed out with the best game of his career in the absence of both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, operating as the top option through the air throughout the game against the Cowboys. He started his night off with a 21-yard reception on the team’s first possession before adding a fourth quarter touchdown on a quick slant from four yards out. The uncertainty surrounding Smith’s injury could leave Lemon as the de facto lead receiver for a Week 8 divisional tilt against the Commanders, where his fantasy value will be strictly tied to the availability of the other receivers on the roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-6 targets for 19 yards in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Despite not lighting up the box score, Lemon was third on the team in targets and finished fourth in receptions. Initial reports had him playing on 52 of the team’s 64 snaps and running a route on 47 of their 52 dropbacks. That was the most routes of any receiver on the team. Some of this was because the team seemed to be easing DeVonta Smith back from injury, and Dontayvsion Wicks briefly left the game with an injury scare, but we also wouldn’t be surprised to see Lemon get more work in what is looking like a bit of a lost season in Philadelphia.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 5-of-7 targets for 43 yards in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: The good news is that Lemon set new season highs in targets, catches, and yards. The bad news: All of that resulted in a measly 9.3 PPR points. Lemon will hopefully continue to earn more opportunities as the season progresses, but DeVonta Smith’s return could just as easily stall the rookie’s progress. Lemon will be a WR4/5 if Smith remains out for Week 6 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) was added to the injury report on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Wicks was listed as a limited participant today, indicating that he strained his hamstring during Thursday’s practice. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) still sidelined, rookie WR Makai Lemon could be the de facto top receiver, though the team has struggled to use him effectively thus far. Hollywood Brown (ankle) also remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-6 targets for 27 yards in the Eagles’ Week 4 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon moved up a spot in the targets pecking order with DeVonta Smith sidelined, but it resulted in the same quiet box score he posted the first three weeks of his career. The No. 20 overall pick is now sitting on 10 receptions for a scoreless 65 yards through his first four NFL appearances. There has yet to be any light at the tunnel with regards to either his usage or the Eagles’ overall offensive environment. Even with byes beginning and injuries mounting, Lemon is not a recommended WR4 heading into Week 5 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-4 targets for 29 yards in the Eagles’ Week 3 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon was the target on the team’s first play from scrimmage, gaining a first down on a first down play for the Eagles for the first time all season. The offense would sputter throughout the game on their way to only 47 offensive plays run from scrimmage, capping the fantasy upside of all involved in the process. Lemon has yet to live up to his lofty draft capital through the first three games of his professional career, but he could be called on for heavier work with tight end Dallas Goedert nursing an MCL sprain. Things don’t get any easier with a matchup against the Rams on deck for Week 4, where Lemon can safely be left on fantasy benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught a 14-yard pass in the Eagles’ Week 2 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon also “added” a -5 yard rush. Lemon’s first quarter catch ended up going down as his only target of the afternoon. He’s now stuck on four catches for nine yards through his first two NFL contests, and is getting soundly out-targeted by Dontayvion Wicks. That’s with Darius Cooper mixing in. The Eagles are calling plays like Lemon has to be manufactured his touches. Two games is not a large sample size, but it is enough to know we can’t rely on Lemon as a WR4 for Week 3 in Chicago.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-4 targets for negative -5 yards in the Eagles’ Week 1 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: It’s possible things could’ve gone worse for Lemon in his debut, but not much worse. The rookie first-rounder saw two of his four targets come at/behind the line of scrimmage, with his longest target coming eight yards downfield. Lemon’s 28 routes run were good for third-most among Eagles receivers in this one, but we would expect him to see a little more work downfield going forward. Lemon remains a bench stash heading into Week 2’s game against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: ESPN’s Tim McManus believes “expectations should be tempered early” for Eagles WR Makai Lemon.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: It’s a reasonable assessment for a rookie who missed valuable spring and summer practice reps due to a recurring hamstring strain. Lemon reportedly admitted that he should have been “more professional off the field” regarding the injury, and Eagles WR coach Aaron Moorehead eventually told him to do “whatever” WR DeVonta Smith did during his own hamstring rehab program. Per McManus, “coaches say Lemon attacked the mental part of the game with high intensity as he waited to get healthy.” McManus believes Lemon should get playing time right away, but Smith and WR Dontayvion Wicks will “receive the bulk of targets while the rookie gets his footing.” Lemon must be safely stashed on benches at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 20-of-32 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns in the Broncos’ 28-24, Week 8 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Fittingly, Nix’s longest completion of the day was a dump-off to Jonah Coleman that the rookie turned into a 51-yard gain. Nix has two completions of 50+ yards this year. Both have gone to running backs on throws near or behind the line of scrimmage. On the other hand, when Nix did push the ball downfield versus Kansas City, he was largely effective. He completed 4-of-6 throws farther than nine yards downfield. It was a small step in the right direction after weeks of middling production on intermediate and downfield shots. Nix will look to build on this performance versus a beatable Carolina defense in Week 9. He will sit somewhere near the top of the QB2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 15-of-29 passes for 222 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ 30-16, Week 7 win over the Cardinals, adding seven carries for 74 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Per usual, Nix had a quiet day through the air, which is doubly true when you realize 52 of his yards and his lone touchdown came on an RJ Harvey screen. Nix struggled to get his deep ball going, missing several long shots that would have padded out an otherwise lacking box score. On the other hand, fantasy managers won’t be complaining after seeing his rushing line, which was largely the result of a 62-yard rushing touchdown late in the first half. Denver sent nearly all of their eligible pass catchers to the right side of the field, opening up a running lane big enough for at least one 18-wheeler. Facing a much stingier Chiefs defense in Week 8, we don’t expect another elite fantasy showing from Nix next week. He will be on the QB1/2 border for the AFC West showdown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Broncos coach Sean Payton said he has not considered removing Bo Nix from the starting job.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: “He is going to become the byproduct of all the finer things that get improved. The improved play from our offensive line; the more efficient we are relative to downs; running the football. That’s our job as coaches here,” Payton said. Nix has been one of the worst quarterbacks in the league through six starts and Jay Glazer passed along word yesterday that Payton changed the terminology that OC Davis Webb had put in this offseason back to what it was last season, which apparently did not help Nix out. He’ll be hard to trust even with a slapdash Cardinals defense on tap for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 17-of-27 passes for 107 yards in the Broncos’ 17-14, Week 6 win over the Seahawks, adding two yards on four carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Broncos managed just 168 yards of total offense on a night their defense carried them to victory in overtime. Nine of the Broncos’ 11 possessions, excluding the two kneel downs to end each half, ended in punts on drives that lasted five plays or fewer. Two second quarter touchdown drives had the Broncos playing with a lead for much of the game but they were otherwise unable to move the football with any consistency. An overtime interception by nickel corner Ja’Quan McMillian allowed for a game-winning, 53-yard field goal from kicker Will Lutz after the Broncos again failed to gain a first down. The win sends Denver to 4-2 while averaging only 18.7 points per game through six weeks. The team gets a scheduling gift with the Cardinals on deck in Week 7, although Nix cannot be treated as a starter-worthy fantasy asset outside of the deepest leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 16-of-127 passes for 123 yards with a touchdown in the Broncos’ 23-17, Week 5 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nix also added 10 yards on the ground on his four carries. He once again wasn’t able to get the ball downfield, with a long passing gain of 34 yards on a busted coverage. He was at least able to find Courtland Sutton for a short touchdown, but this was an ugly day for both signal-callers. Nix is no more than a QB2 for a matchup against the tough Seattle defense in Week 6, and it’s worth noting that game takes place Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 25-of-42 attempts for 214 yards and one touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers, adding two rushes for ten yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nix’s play — including missing easy intermediate throws in the first half — left Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb without answers, a common theme so far this season. His lone touchdown came on a garbage time score to Jaylen Waddle. Nix was in check-down mode throughout the game against the Niners, finishing with a 4.9 aDOT. He was 5 percent under his expected completion rate, targeting his running backs 12 times. Until Webb and Sean Payton figure out the offense, Nix will be a superflex-only fantasy option without much of a weekly ceiling. He gets the Chargers in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 17-of-34 passes for 186 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Broncos’ 30-26, Week 3 win over the Rams, adding seven yards and a touchdown on four carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Broncos were shut out in the first half amidst consistent struggles from Nix, who, for his part, turned in solid production in a third quarter that saw the Broncos knot the game at 16 through two touchdowns and successful two-point conversions. Nix and the Broncos would struggle to move the football again in the fourth quarter but a pick-six from safety Talanoa Hufanga gave them the lead with under five minutes to play. Stafford returned blows to send the Rams to a three-point lead before Nix’s game-winning score from one yard out. That final drive was aided by three key penalties to go against the Rams, the final of which was questionable, to put it kindly. Josh Wallace appeared to intercept Nix for the second time in the fourth quarter but a defensive pass interference penalty was called, giving the Broncos renewed life. Hufanga would intercept Stafford for a second time in the fourth quarter, this time in the end zone, to seal the victory for the Broncos as time expired. Nix and offensive coordinator Davis Webb have not looked good through three games despite the team’s 2-1 record, and will need to clean things up ahead of another NFC West showdown against the 49ers in Week 4. Nix is currently nothing more than a middling QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 22-of-31 attempts for 288 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Broncos’ Week 2 win against the Jaguars, adding five rushes for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It was an uneven day for Nix, who missed some routine throws and threw a bad pick in the end zone while targeting Courtland Sutton. He targeted Jaylen Waddle heavily and connected with Waddle for a 49-yard gain in the first half, regularly attacking the Jaguars secondary downfield. After taking far too many sacks in Week 1 against the Chiefs, Nix was not sacked against a solid Jaguars pass rush on Sunday. Nix’s lack of early-season rushing success has dinged his fantasy prospects a bit. He’s a fine superflex option for Week 3 against the Rams, however.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix called the Broncos’ Week 1 offensive performance “pretty pitiful.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nix during his postgame presser defended offensive play caller Davis Webb, who took over for head coach Sean Payton this offseason. “The players did not make it easy on [Webb] today,” said Nix, who completed 17-of-28 passes for 131 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in Monday night’s loss to Kansas City. “Pretty pitiful, actually.” Denver had the league’s second lowest drop back EPA of Week 1; only the Falcons were worse. Nix, meanwhile, ranked 28th out of 32 qualifying QBs in Week 1 accuracy. “We called exactly what we prepared for and what we wanted to get to and we just didn’t execute,” Nix said. “Then we were behind.” Webb and the Broncos will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a tough Jaguars defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 17-of-28 passes for 131 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Broncos’ 31-10, Week 1 loss to the Chiefs, adding two yards on three carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nix and the rest of the Denver offense struggled throughout against Steve Spagnuolo’s Kansas City defense, gaining fewer yards as a team (176) than opposing running back Kenneth Walker (191). Things seemed to be clicking early after the Broncos were able to knot the game at seven in the first quarter, but quickly fell apart under unrelenting pressure. The poor offensive showing is sure to draw criticism in the media considering it was the first game called by first-time offensive coordinator Davis Webb after head coach Sean Payton relinquished play calling duties this offseason. Whether that setup continues remains to be seen and we wouldn’t be shocked if Webb failed to make it through the first six weeks still calling plays. The Broncos hold the league’s most difficult schedule through the first six weeks, with games against Jaguars, Rams, 49ers, Chargers, and Seahawks on the immediate horizon. Nix could regain form against the pass-funnel Jaguars in Week 2, where he will be a back-end QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram failed to catch any of his three targets in the Broncos’ Week 8 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram was not a meaningful part of the Broncos’ offense, per usual. He has three catches for 15 yards over his past three appearances. It goes without saying, but Engram isn’t even on the TE2 radar for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram caught 1-of-3 targets for two yards in the Broncos’ Week 7 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram popped up with four catches for 43 yards and a touchdown in Week 1. He has one game with more than two catches for 17 yards since. This week was no different. Engram isn’t even in the TE2 mix for Week 8 versus the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram caught both targets for 13 yards in the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram has not seen more than five targets in a game this season and has been held out of the end zone since Week 1, making him a difficult start in fantasy leagues of all sizes. He can safely remain on the bench in an enticing matchup against the Cardinals in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram caught all four targets for 55 yards in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram did a large portion of his damage on a busted coverage that allowed him to pick up 34 yards and come just short of a receiving score. The 55 yards are a season high, and it’s encouraging to see more involvement after being a non-factor in the previous two weeks. Engram will hope to build on this effort in Week 6 against the Seahawks, but fantasy managers shouldn’t bet on it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram caught 1-of-5 targets for six yards in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram again had a good route rate but didn’t make the most of his short targets from Bo Nix. Engram, who now has five receptions through four games, is not a fantasy option in any format and should remain on waiver wires for now. He’s been targeted on just 11 percent of his routes this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram caught his lone target for 17 yards in the Broncos’ Week 2 win against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram followed up his four catch, 43 yard, one touchdown Week 1 performance with a dud against his former team. Engram ran a route on just 15 of Bo Nix’s 34 drop backs, a far lower rate than he had in Week 1 against the Chiefs. That kind of role and usage would mean Engram is unusable in fantasy formats. He should remain on waiver wires ahead of the Broncos’ Week 3 matchup against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Evan Engram caught 4-of-5 targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 1 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram’s trip to paint came from 19 yards out on the team’s second possession to knot the score at seven in the first quarter, which would be the last time the team would be within striking distance for the remainder of the game. Nix’s timing was continually thrown off while under mounting pressure from Steve Spanguolo’s Kansas City defense, resulting in numerous off-target throws. Engram managed to corral two such throws and turn otherwise poor passes into completions for his young quarterback. Regardless of the low yardage total, Engram managed to score for the second time wearing the Denver blue and orange after notching just one touchdown in his first year with the team in 2025. Engram remains a low-upside TE2 ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: The Denver Post’s Parker Gabriel believes “it would be a surprise” if Adam Trautman didn’t outsnap Evan Engram again in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: There’s been some mild hype for Engram again in the early offseason, but it’s hard to understand why the Broncos would have brought in Jaylen Waddle if they thought getting Engram more involved in the offense would have been a notable upgrade. Engram belongs in TE2 purgatory for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: The Denver Post’s Troy Renck believes readers should “buy” into Broncos TE Evan Engram’s performance at organized team activities.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: Engram is “making light work of linebackers in coverage with eye-widening catches,” which Renck thinks could suggest Engram is headed toward a bounce-back campaign. Renck also believes Engram will be more involved in the offense thanks to Davis Webb’s promotion to offensive coordinator. Webb recruited Engram, his former teammate, to join the Broncos last year. Renck also rightly believes new WR Jaylen Waddle will command safety attention, clearing out the middle of the field for Engram. However, he does not address the fact that Waddle represents a massive increase in target competition. Renck also spends the entire piece comparing Engram to a banana and asks whether said banana is ripe or stuck in a tailpipe. Seriously. Engram can be viewed as a potential TE2 candidate in best ball, but we fear a tailpipe scenario is in play for those hoping he produces a TE1 outcome.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.headline: Broncos general manager George Paton said the team wants to add to TE Evan Engram’s workload next year.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/evan-engra.analysis: The Broncos have also been heavily scouting the incoming tight end class. Per Paton, the group has “a nice variety of different types.” The team has hosted at least three tight ends on top-30 visits. Engram, 31, earned 77 targets last season. It is tough to envision him meaningfully increasing that number, but the Broncos obviously do not want to tip their hand ahead of next week’s draft, if they do intend to select a tight end. Paton adds that the team is “really honed in” on the players they expect to be available in the picks 45-75 range.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught all four of his targets for 53 yards in the Broncos’ Week 8 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Sutton’s 53 yards today are now a season-high, as are his four receptions. That, however, largely speaks to how unproductive he has been this year. Sutton has more games under 20 yards than over 40. He also has just one touchdown through eight games. His signs of life versus the Chiefs will keep him in the WR5 ranks for Week 9, but the ceiling remains nonexistent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Jaylen Waddle suffered a chest injury and his Week 8 status has not been determined.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Waddle left Sunday’s game against the Cardinals with the chest injury. It was, according to Rapoport, an “aggravation of his previous chest injury.” Waddle could try to practice later this week, but would appear to be iffy unless he can log a practice session by Friday. If Waddle is sidelined this week against the Chiefs, Courtland Sutton would likely see more targets and become an interesting flex option against a tough KC secondary. Sutton over the past four weeks leads Denver in air yards and has the second most targets behind Waddle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 3-of-5 targets for 45 yards in the Broncos’ Week 7 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Sutton’s 45 yards today were one shy of his season-high, which mostly speaks to how quiet the veteran wideout has been this year. He has only topped 25 yards twice and has just one touchdown to his name. Jaylen Waddle injured his chest late in this contest and could be out for Week 8. That would funnel a few more targets Sutton’s way, but it’s not like Waddle was putting up loads of counting stats that now shift to Sutton. Even if Waddle is out for Week 8 versus the Chiefs, Sutton would have a hard time pushing past the WR4 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 2-of-3 targets for 19 yards in the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Nix’s only incompletion when targeting Sutton resulted in the veteran receiver getting rocked over the middle of the field on a ball Nix led him directly into oncoming contact. Sutton vented his frustration by repeatedly pounding the ground following the hit, with it unclear whether it was due to the hit or the incompletion on third down on a night the Broncos struggled to move the football to the tune of only 168 yards of total offense. Fantasy managers likely aren’t utilizing Sutton as a weekly option, but will want to track his practice status ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the Cardinals if bye week fill-ins are required.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 2-of-3 targets for 18 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: It’s the first touchdown for Sutton on the season, and it tied the game at 17-17. The 31-year-old was unable to find room versus the Chargers’ secondary, and for the fifth-straight week, Sutton was held under 50 yards. His size could give the smaller Seahawks’ defensive backs trouble, but he’s essentially a touchdown-dependent FLEX for Week 6 against Seattle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 1-of-6 targets for four yards in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Sutton was the recipient of a couple off-target intermediate looks from Bo Nix, who struggled to place the ball against the 49ers secondary. Sutton could see an expanded role in the Denver offense if Pat Bryant is out long term following his leg injury in Week 4. Sutton has been targeted on 16 percent of his pass routes this season; he has nine receptions through four games. Sutton should only be rostered in deeper leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 3-of-7 targets for 46 yards in the Broncos’ Week 3 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Sutton tied for the team lead in targets while pacing the offense in yards, which highlights the struggles that persist in Davis Webb’s offense through three games. He will be off the FLEX radar ahead of a Week 4 showdown against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 3-of-4 targets for 25 yards in the Broncos’ Week 2 win against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Sutton’s lone end zone target was intercepted on a poor throw from Bo Nix. Last week Sutton had just 11 yards on five targets in the Broncos’ season-opening loss to the Chiefs. Jaylen Waddle, with 148 yards in Week 2, has established himself as the clear-cut WR1 in the Denver offense. Sutton will be a touchdown-dependent WR3/4 option in Week 3 against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Bo Nix called the Broncos’ Week 1 offensive performance “pretty pitiful.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: Nix during his postgame presser defended offensive play caller Davis Webb, who took over for head coach Sean Payton this offseason. “The players did not make it easy on [Webb] today,” said Nix, who completed 17-of-28 passes for 131 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in Monday night’s loss to Kansas City. “Pretty pitiful, actually.” Denver had the league’s second lowest drop back EPA of Week 1; only the Falcons were worse. Nix, meanwhile, ranked 28th out of 32 qualifying QBs in Week 1 accuracy. “We called exactly what we prepared for and what we wanted to get to and we just didn’t execute,” Nix said. “Then we were behind.” Webb and the Broncos will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a tough Jaguars defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.headline: Courtland Sutton caught 2-of-5 targets for 11 yards in the Broncos’ Week 1 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/courtland-.analysis: The good news for Sutton’s fantasy managers is that he tied for second on the team in targets. The bad news is everything else. Sutton was locked down by the aggressive Kansas City secondary, failing to generate separation as the offense struggled to move the football. It is difficult to count on Sutton as being any higher than third on the team’s pecking order for targets following the addition of Jaylen Waddle this offseason. The veteran incumbent turns 31 in October and appears likely to struggle when he’s not finding the end zone. Sutton is a low-upside WR4 ahead of a pass-funnel matchup against the Jaguars in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marvin-mim.headline: Marvin Mims caught 2-of-3 targets for 10 yards in the Broncos’ Week 8 win over the Chiefs, adding two carries for 19 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marvin-mim.analysis: Sean Payton talked earlier this week about getting the ball in Mims’ hands more. Mims had two catches in each of his previous three games. He had two catches today. Maybe you can point to Mims’ two catches as a reason to believe Payton was telling the truth, but the role itself was almost completely unchanged. There’s nothing for fantasy managers to see here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marvin-mim.headline: Broncos coach Sean Payton, asked about Jonah Coleman, said touches were “something you earn and he’s done a good job of that.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marvin-mim.analysis: He also noted that Coleman’s touches were explosive. It’s hard to sit here with much certainty about what looks to be a three-headed Broncos running back room where every back has their niche, but Coleman probably enters Week 8 as the favorite of the three to crack 10 touches. Payton added, for the 17th time since he became Broncos coach, that he needed to get more touches for Marvin Mims on offense. We’ll believe that when we see it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marvin-mim.headline: Marvin Mims caught both of his targets for 53 yards in the Broncos’ Week 7 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marvin-mim.analysis: Mims also added three rushing yards on his lone carry. Troy Franklin and Mims split the WR3 role in this game, but the former failed to reel in either of his two targets. Mims, on the other hand, picked up 47 yards on a catch-and-run that saw him juke an Arizona defender out of his cleats. With Jaylen Waddle banged up, the WR2 role might be up for grabs next week. That would put both Mims and Franklin in the FLEX mix versus Kansas City, though we would look to aim higher on the waiver wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marvin-mim.headline: Marvin Mims caught 1-of-3 targets for ten yards in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marvin-mim.analysis: Mims also lost a fumble in the loss. Mims has been virtually invisible in the Broncos offense through four games, though that could change if Pat Bryant’s injury proves to be the long-term variety. Even in that case Mims would be nothing more than an ultra deep league option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marvin-mim.headline: Marvin Mims (foot) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marvin-mim.analysis: Mims aggravated his foot injury back in Week 1 and has been inactive on game day since. The Broncos’ volatile performer is back, but is not on the FLEX radar in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marvin-mim.headline: Marvin Mims (foot) is practicing in full for Week 4 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marvin-mim.analysis: Mims went down with a foot injury in Week 1 and hasn’t played or practiced since. A full session on Wednesday means he’s good to go for Week 4. He could push Troy Franklin for the WR4 job, but his biggest contributions will come in the return game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marvin-mim.headline: Broncos declared WR Marvin Mims, WR Lil’Jordan Humphrey, QB Sam Ehlinger, OL Kage Casey, TE Dallen Bentley, DL Sai’vion Jones, and DT Tyler Onyedim inactive for Week 3 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marvin-mim.analysis: Mims will be inactive for the second consecutive week while Humphrey’s presence is not required with the four receivers ahead of his on the depth chart active. Defensive lineman Sai’Vion Jones will have to wait to at least Week 4 to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marvin-mim.headline: Marvin Mims (foot) is questionable for Denver’s Week 3 game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marvin-mim.analysis: Mims re-aggravated his preseason foot injury in Week 1 and did not play in Week 2. He was able to get three limited sessions in ahead of Week 3, but has no fantasy value at this point in Denver’s deep wideout room. He’d provide considerable real-life value as a punt returner.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marvin-mim.headline: Broncos WR Marvin Mims (foot) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marvin-mim.analysis: Mims has a chance to return this week, but his availability is not yet guaranteed. Regardless, he is not fantasy-relevant in 12-team leagues. He more so functions as a slight target share problem for other Broncos pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marvin-mim.headline: Broncos WR Marvin Mims (foot) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marvin-mim.analysis: Mims is still working his way back after aggravating his foot injury in Week 1 against the Chiefs. Although his early participation is a good sign for his Week 3 availability, the Broncos will likely play things extra cautiously this time around.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich caught 4-of-6 targets for 43 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 8 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Three of Dulcich’s catches occurred on the final two drives, and his first catch occurred in the two-minute drill at the end of the first half. Malik Willis seemingly only looks his way when playing quickly. Maybe the coaching staff should address that, because Dulcich played effectively in those situations. The Dolphins face the Lions’ fantasy-friendly pass defense next week, potentially elevating Dulcich to high-end TE2 status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich is not on Miami’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: The fringe TE2 life awaits Dulcich against the Patriots on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich (ankle) remained limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Still, back-to-back practices are a good sign that Dulcich will be ready to go for Week 8’s game against the Patriots. That isn’t necessarily an endorsement of using him in fantasy football — even after last week’s surprise 5/86 against the Jets — but hey, the Dolphins will be glad he’s around.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: The Dolphins’ tight end finally had a decent game, only to tweak an ankle along the way. He should be fine for Week 8 against the Patriots, but he is barely in the TE2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich caught all five of his targets for 86 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Dulcich made the most of National Tight Ends Day with a 32-yard catch on the Dolphins’ opening drive and two more gains of 15+ yards throughout the contest. He led the team in catches and targets. Dulcich now has at least four receptions in three of his past four games. Miami’s run-first approach is preventing him from finding spike weeks, but Dulcich has worked himself into the TE2 conversation ahead of Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich caught 4-of-5 targets for 37 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Dulcich also added a two-point conversion to his total. It was a low-efficiency passing offense for the Dolphins once again, leading to Dulcich averaging under 10 yards per reception. The 26-year-old tight end is a fantasy TE3 as the Dolphins head into a Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich caught 5-of-7 targets for 55 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 3 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Held under 20 yards in each of the Dolphins’ first two games, Dulcich finally had something of a pop-up effort as the ‘Fins tried in vain to match points with the Chiefs. It was nice to get some proof of TE2 concept, but it is going to be exceptionally difficult for Dulcich to carve out streamer value in a low-volume passing attack focused on seeing what it has in its intriguing rookie receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: Greg Dulcich caught 2-of-2 targets for 18 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 1 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Both of Dulcich’s targets occurred on the third drive. One was a six-yarder via play action. The other was a delayed screen pass, which Dulcich admirably ran for 12 yards, picking up a first down along the way. The fact that he was barely involved in a pass-heavy game script bodes poorly for his TE1 viability. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues heading into Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: The South Florida Sun Sentinel’s David Furones believes Jalen Tolbert “appeared to be” one of Malik Willis’ top targets in OTAs and minicamp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Furones also lists Greg Dulcich as a player that was a primary receiver for Willis, but we’ve done plenty of offseason hype on Dulcich. Tolbert appears to be a potential “someone has to catch a ball here” deep league pick, as he’s well off the fantasy radar at this point. He’s not off the board among the top-100 wideouts in ADP. The ceiling is likely low, but if he can emerge as the top option amongst Miami’s wideouts, Tolbert could be a viable WR3/WR4 at points this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.headline: ESPN’s Marcel Louis-Jacques reports Greg Dulcich was “one of the primary targets” for Malik Willis in spring practices.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/greg-dulci.analysis: Dulcich turned into a nice contributor for the Dolphins during the second half of last season. He didn’t play his first snaps until Week 8 due to an injury that landed him on injured reserve, but in 10 games, Dulcich caught 26 passes for 335 yards and one touchdown on 33 targets, earning four or more targets in five of those games. This isn’t the first time we have heard Dulcich has flashed in practice, and given the thin receiver room in Miami, it’s easy to envision a meaningful role for him in 2026. Dulcich is a former third-round pick who posted a 33-411-2 line as a rookie back in 2022 in 10 games with the Broncos, but injuries have slowed him in recent years. Now that he’s healthy and making a strong early showing this offseason, Dulcich could make for an intriguing late-round draft pick in fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught 3-of-6 targets for 13 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: With Rashee Rice back after missing two games because of a hamstring issue, Worthy was relegated to WR2 duties once again. Per usual, he didn’t do much while Rice racked up PPR-friendly receptions. Worthy was, however, the intended target on a pair of red zone attempts in the third quarter. Pat Surtain easily broke up one pass that was left a bit short and Worthy actually fought to knock another one down that should have been intercepted by Riley Moss. Worthy has topped 25 yards in one game with Rice again. He’s simply not a part of the Chiefs’ plans on offense when they’re at full strength. Fantasy managers can feel free to cut him loose on this week’s run of waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught 3-of-6 targets for 11 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 7 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Worthy struggled to separate from primary coverage of the Seahawks throughout, also committing a drop in a crucial situation in the second half. The Chiefs continue to show hesitancy in utilizing Worthy in a downfield role, which is of particular concern for his fantasy managers considering the absence of Tyquan Thornton. Worthy is better left on fantasy benches ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the stingy Broncos, particularly if Rashee Rice returns from injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught all seven of his targets for 73 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: The Chiefs, with Rashee Rice (hamstring) sidelined, made every effort to force feed Worthy near the line of scrimmage in this one. That resulted in Worthy leading the KC offense in both targets and receiving yards, with a long reception of 19 yards. Most of his Week 6 touches were of the gadget variety. Increased usage should give Worthy a sturdy PPR floor for now. He should be considered a flex play next week against the tough Seattle secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Rice appeared to have a good chance at suiting up for Week 6 when Andy Reid spoke about it after Week 4’s win over the Raiders. Reid only said he “tweaked” his hammy. Even with a bye week to rest, it looks like Rice is now on the wrong side of questionable for Week 6. With Tyquan Thornton on IR, Xavier Worthy may be tasked with WR1 duties this week. He totaled four catches for 70 yards in his last outing and would be a solid FLEX play versus the Chargers if Rice can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught 4-of-7 targets for 70 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 4 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Worthy saw a season-high seven targets in this one after Rashee Rice (hamstring) exited just a few plays into the game. Worthy came up with a handful of key plays for the Chiefs, with his biggest coming on a 41-yard reception that put the Chiefs in position for a short touchdown pass to Tyquan Thornton a few plays later. The Chiefs now head into their Week 5 bye, but they could be down multiple receivers, with Rice and Thornton (ankle) both suffering injuries in this one. While we don’t yet know the extent of Rice’s injury, Thornton’s ankle injury looked like a potential season-ender. Worthy could well be worth a stash in leagues where he is still available, as he could soon be the top receiver for the Chiefs when they return in Week 6 to face the Chargers. Second-year receiver Jalen Royals, who ran 21 routes in this game, could also see an expanded role in the coming weeks.
