https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught 2-of-2 targets for 20 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 3 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Worthy was also shaken up by a big hit but was never announced with an injury. Patrick Mahomes attempted only 24 passes this afternoon, but that’s still a disappointing target total for the third-year pro. 23-year-old Worthy is now sitting on just 10 catches for 63 yards through the Chiefs’ first three games. Even with this offense showing major year-over-year improvement, it’s getting harder to keep the WR4 faith with Worthy. The Raiders are a plus Week 4 matchup in Vegas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught 5-of-7 targets for 25 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 2 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Worthy’s score came from one yard out on a fourth-down play at the end of the second quarter. The play followed three consecutive failed rush attempts from Kenneth Walker from one yard out, with the veteran receiver leaking to the flat on a Mahomes bootleg for his first score of the young season. Worthy remains a shaky WR5 ahead of a cake matchup with the Dolphins in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught 3-of-6 targets for 18 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 1 win over the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: The entire Kansas City pass offense appeared stuck in the mud, with little ability to attack deep against one of the league’s best defenses. Worthy struggled to gain separation on targets beyond five yards of the line of scrimmage, something the Chiefs have struggled with the previous two seasons. Further hampering their downfield pass game was an inconsistent and adjusting Patrick Mahomes in his first game since tearing his ACL. The return of offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy saw the Chiefs lean on new running back Kenneth Walker, who out-gained the entire Denver offense on his own, leaving little in the way of additional motivation to air the ball out. Worthy enters a Week 2 matchup with the Colts as a low-upside WR5, likely best left on fantasy benches, for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Chiefs WR Xavier Worthy (shoulder) is practicing in full for Week 1 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Worthy’s range of potential outcomes remains quite wide. The team attributed his lackluster 2025 season to the significant shoulder injury he suffered in Week 1. He missed time in training camp with a shoulder issue as well. He can be treated as a volatile FLEX playing in a top-tier offense against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Chiefs WR Xavier Worthy (shoulder) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: On Monday, Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Worthy should resume practicing at some point this week. The Chiefs have another practice tomorrow, so Worthy technically still has 24 hours to prove Reid right, but his continued absence is slightly concerning regardless. Last Saturday, Worthy sprained the same shoulder that was surgically repaired this offseason. He dislocated his right shoulder in Week 1, causing a full labral tear and badly impacting his season. It would be great to see him resume practicing fully tomorrow or early next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Ollie Gordon rushed 19 times for 69 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 8 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Gordon continues to look like a powerful, capable interior runner, deserving of the Dolphins’ starting role. He, frustratingly, had a 15-yard run erased by a holding penalty and failed to catch his lone target. Gordon celebrated a bit too enthusiastically after a five-yard run on the Dolphins’ seventh drive and was flagged for a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. The young player was extremely upset about the call and required one-on-one conversations with coach Jeff Haffley, another unidentifiable coaching staff member and Malik Willis before regaining composure. Gordon will likely end up in the mid-to-high RB2 ranks against the Lions next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Ollie Gordon rushed 25 times for 103 yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: The Dolphins took an early lead and never looked back, allowing them to lean on their ground game for the better part of four quarters. Gordon, in turn, set new career highs in rushes and yards. In four starts sans De’Von Achane, Gordon has 69 carries for 332 yards and four touchdowns. He has finished as a top-20 fantasy option at his position in all four starts. Gordon’s role on one of the most run-heavy offenses in the league is too good to ignore. He will be in the RB2 mix when the Dolphins take on the Patriots next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Ollie Gordon rushed 18 times for 88 yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Gordon continued to operate as the Dolphins’ No. 1 running back, scoring a touchdown for the second straight week. He took all of Miami’s red zone backfield touches and was tackled at the one yard line in the third quarter, coming close to his second touchdown of the day. He lost two yards the next play and the Dolphins did not convert. Gordon saw 42 snaps on the day and will be a low-end fantasy RB2 for Week 7 against the Jets after a Week 6 bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Ollie Gordon rushed nine times for 100 yards and one touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Gordon entered the game on the Dolphins’ second drive, generating one yard and two receptions on three touches during that possession. Things improved from there. After letting nominal starting RB Jaylen Wright and Gordon each play their own drives, the Dolphins eventually began rotating them in and out until Gordon separated on the first drive after halftime. Gordon notched three carries in a row, breaking off a 53-yarder on the second one by navigating traffic and making his way to the left sideline, shedding a jersey grab along the way. On the seventh drive, he had what could have been a breakaway touchdown run blown dead by officials, who thought Gordon was down by contact as he stumbled through the box. It was a close call. He then touched the ball on two-of-four plays on the ensuing drive, including a touchdown run up the middle from 12 yards out, in which Gordon acrobatically vaulted over a downed lineman. Tentatively expect Gordon to be the Dolphins’ starter in Week 5 against the Bengals and treat him as an RB2/FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: The South Florida Sun Sentinel’s David Furones reports that Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright is lining up with the first-team offense during pre-game warmups.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Dolphins RB Ollie Gordon is rotating in behind Wright, confirming Wright is the team’s current starter. That said, the Dolphins could still split the backfield workload almost evenly. We won’t know what the plan is until the game is underway. For now, Wright should be viewed as the slightly safer FLEX, though both running backs could get bottled up by the Vikings’ defense today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright (foot) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Wright sits atop the Dolphins’ depth chart with De’Von Achane (knee) done for the year. He will likely split touches with new No. 2 running back Ollie Gordon in a very difficult matchup against the Vikings this week. Both players are worth rostering, but they are shaky FLEX starters this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said Jaylen Wright (foot) should be good to go for Week 4 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Wright was a full participant in Thursday’s and Friday’s practices, which is a good sign for his Week 4 availability. If he doesn’t draw a questionable tag later in the day, we’ll go ahead and assume that the third-year back will be on the field when the Dolphins visit the Vikings. Wright should be in line for a decent day as far as volume is concerned, but it’s hard to invest much hope in him or Ollie Gordon, who will split work with De’Von Achane (knee) out for the remainder of the season. It’s hard to know how the touches could be distributed here, but fantasy managers shouldn’t be rushing to put either back in their lineups against a stout Vikings defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright (foot) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Wright should be rostered in 12-team leagues. He is now on track to play in Week 4 against the Vikings and is still listed ahead of RB Ollie Gordon on the Dolphins’ depth chart. The Vikings’ defense could bottle up this running back, but things might get a tad easier in Week 5 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright (foot) said he was “very close” to playing in Week 3 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Wright and RB Ollie Gordon are expected to split backfield touches moving forward, though this could be a fluid situation if one running back simply outplays the other. Gordon profiles as a burly grinder, while Wright may offer more big-play potential. It sounds like Wright has a strong chance of playing in Week 4 against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot) was limited during practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ollie-gord.analysis: Wright was inactive with his foot injury last week against Kansas City. De’Von Achane went down with a season-ending ACL injury and Ollie Gordon took over as the team’s workhorse with no other running back on the active roster. Dolphins coaches have implied that both Gordon and Wright will get work in the Miami backfield with Achane out. An even backfield split would make both Wright and Gordon nothing more than deep-league flex plays.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Kenneth Walker rushed 21 times for 69 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Broncos, adding four catches for 15 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Emmett Johnson stole the show today with 128 yards and a touchdown on five receptions. Johnson blew by the Broncos’ defense for a 73-yard touchdown, which alone would have been enough for a breakout performance. The good news for Walker drafters is that Johnson only carried the ball once. Walker also matched him in targets at five apiece. Walker is now coming off his two worst rushing performances of the year in tandem with the Chiefs’ first two losses. It’s safe to assume the two are related. With a down-bad Jets defense on deck, we fully expected Walker to get back on track as a top-end RB1 in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Kenneth Walker rushed 14 times for 36 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 7 loss to the Seahawks, adding 21 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Walker was held to below 4.9 yards per carry for only the second time this season while also failing to find the end zone for the second time through six games, with his longest rush going for a meager seven yards. Seattle had all the answers on the defensive side of the ball as they held the Chiefs to just 213 yards of total offense. One of fantasy’s breakout stars in the early going of the 2026 season will face another difficult matchup on the road against the Broncos in Week 8, where he remains an elite RB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Ken Walker had 19 rushes for 128 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers, adding two catches for 11 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: The Chiefs once again leaned hard on the rushing attack, running the ball 24 times while attempting 30 passes on the day. Walker breezed through a lifeless LA defense from start to finish. On many of his carries Walker was not touched until he was five or six yards beyond the line of scrimmage. Walker, who accounted for 19 of the team’s 24 rushing attempts, is perhaps the most important player in fantasy football through Week 6. He’ll be an RB1 in Week 7 against his former mates in Seattle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Kenneth Walker rushed 22 times for 177 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs’ Week 4 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Walker found the end zone twice in 19 seconds in this one. After scoring on a two-yard run in the fourth quarter, Walker then broke free for a 22-yard run on his next play after the Chiefs recovered a fumbled kickoff by the Raiders. Walker’s longest run of the game was an explosive burst down the right sideline that saw him pick up 76 yards, but he was tackled at the Raiders eight-yard line and lost out on a scoring opportunity two plays later when Tyquan Thornton came down in the end zone with an eight-yard reception. Walker has now scored multiple touchdowns in three of four games this season and has 621 yards from scrimmage and seven total touchdowns. He’s been more than fantasy managers could have hoped for through the first four weeks, but they will have to manage without him next week as the Chiefs enter their bye week. He’ll be firmly in the RB1 mix in Week 6, however, when the Chiefs play host to the winless Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Kenneth Walker rushed 18 times for 70 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 3 win over the Dolphins, adding two receptions for three yards and a second score.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: The two-touchdown outing was Walker’s second in three games as a Chief after he had only one such effort for the Seahawks last season. His 20 touches were a rather remarkable total seeing as the Chiefs were limited to 49 plays with the Dolphins attempting to play keep away. He was not efficient, but Patrick Mahomes was. That’s the new reality for defenses facing the Chiefs, as this is no longer a stop Mahomes at all costs team. You now have to pick your poison, which is going to lead to many more blow-up efforts for KWIII. Perhaps that will include Week 4 in Vegas against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said RB Emmett Johnson “will continue to get more snaps.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Johnson has turned 14 touches into 103 scrimmage yards thus far. Evidently pleased with his fifth-round rookie, Reid wants to keep “allowing Emmett to grow,” in turn taking “a little bit of load off” starting RB Kenneth Walker. Reid notes that Walker wants the ball on every play and is not asking for a lighter workload, but Reid is seeking “a nice balance with those two in there,” which “keeps them even more fresh as the season goes on.” Walker, of course, remains an elite RB1. Johnson, however, should be rostered in all 12-team leagues as a high-upside bench stash that could return standalone value before long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Kenneth Walker rushed 24 times for 117 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 2 win over the Colts, adding 61 yards on six receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Walker has now notched 178 combined yards or more in each of his new team’s first two games to start the season. In addition to the gaudy yardage numbers, Walker saw 10 targets on 47 Patrick Mahomes pass attempts in the overtime victory, while accounting for all but four running back opportunities. His backfield opportunity share, touchdown equity, and pass game involvement make Walker a top-tier fantasy asset for those that invested a second-round pick in his services this offseason. The only micro-blemish on his record against the Colts was a sequence of carries at the end of the second quarter in which he was stuffed from the one-yard line on three straight plays, with the team eventually scoring on fourth down via a touchdown pass to Xavier Worthy. Walker remains a top-tier RB1 ahead of a road date with the much more forgiving Dolphins in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Kenneth Walker rushed 23 times for 173 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 1 win over the Broncos, adding 18 yards and a touchdown on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Walker single-handedly out-gained the entire Denver offense on the evening as he was the clear point of emphasis in Patrick Mahomes’ first game back after tearing his ACL in 2025. He was fed seven carries on the team’s first nine offensive plays run from scrimmage, a drive that would result in a 15-yard Mahomes rushing touchdown on the team’s first possession. The highlight of the game for the explosive back was a 60-yard touchdown run on fourth-and-one, in which he bounced the football outside and dusted the secondary on his way to the end zone. He would add a receiving score on a “Kansas City Special” later in the game, taking a Mahomes shuttle pass to the end zone from two yards out to further bolster his counting stats. What’s more, walker played all but five offensive snaps in the first half with the game still within reason, highlighting a massive ceiling for the remainder of the season. Walker is a locked-in RB1 ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: The Athletic’s Jesse Newell reports the Chiefs view Kenneth Walker as a potential three-down back.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: What is clear in the wake of the Chiefs waiving Emari Demercado is that they don’t really have another player that qualifies as a passing-down back besides Walker without squinting. The other backs they kept are Emmett Johnson, a Day 3 rookie, and Brashard Smith, a gadget player without enough size to really block. Perhaps the Chiefs will address this in street free agency ahead of the season, but as things stand, it certainly seems like Walker will be involved on all three downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: ESPN’s Nate Taylor reports that the Chiefs are counting on RB Kenneth Walker to help build a “more potent offense” this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Chiefs coach Andy Reid and QB Patrick Mahomes believe last season’s run game failed to make defenses respect their play-action run fakes. With Walker now on board, the Chiefs believe both the run game and play-action game will improve. The staff has catered to Walker by installing more plays from under center, which Walker prefers to shotgun. “One way Walker can help transform the offense,” per Taylor, “is by becoming a true dual-threat player.” Reid believes Walker’s “receiving skills and ability to make defenders miss” will allow Reid to incorporate “one of his favorite passing concepts: the variety of plays where a play-action fake to the running back is executed before a short screen pass is thrown back to the same running back.” Walker should be expected to handle a high-end, dual-threat workload. He is a locked-in RB1 with immense upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.headline: Kevin Coleman caught 3-of-3 targets for 46 yards and one touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 8 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.analysis: Coleman led the Dolphins in receiving yards today. Although that outcome may be unlikely in the coming weeks, he looks like a capable contributor. Coleman scored a 35-yard touchdown on the Dolphins’ 10th drive, shaking his coverage defender along the sideline with a false step and a dramatic upper-body fake, before racing downfield and hauling in the pass in stride before crossing the plane. He nearly scored earlier, on the Dolphins’ fifth drive, snagging a six-yard pass on a quick out route on 1st-and-goal from the Patriots’ six-yard line, but he was unable to stay inbounds. Coleman could warrant boom-bust FLEX treatment in 14-team leagues against the Lions next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.headline: Kevin Coleman caught 3-of-7 targets for 30 yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.analysis: Coleman was heavily involved in the Dolphins’ second-half gameplan, seeing the second-most targets among Miami pass-catchers on the day. He scored on a Malik Willis red zone pass in the fourth quarter and was tackled at the one-yard line on a reception towards the end of the game. Coleman is a fifth-round rookie and unlikely to see this much volume moving forward but is an intriguing deep-league stash in case Malik Washington were to suffer an injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.headline: Kevin Coleman caught 1-of-4 targets for three yards in the Dolphins’ Week 4 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.analysis: This is Coleman’s second consecutive week catching 1-of-4 targets for three yards. He earned two targets on the second drive, which was encouraging. He should have had a double-digit gain on the fifth drive, but Malik Willis’ off-target throw was far too low. Willis targeted him again on the sixth drive, but the pass clanged off Coleman’s hands as he slid toward the sideline in the end zone. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats, but he is worth keeping an eye on for later in the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said there will be no “pitch count” for starting receiver Chris Bell, and that he trusts both Bell and fellow rookie starter Caleb Douglas.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.analysis: “We believe those guys deserve to start, and we’re gonna start them,” was Hafley’s matter-of-fact Wednesday statement. His words come after the ‘Fins officially listed the third-round rookies as starters on Tuesday. His “pitch count” comments pertain to Bell’s summer stint on the NFI list as he completed his recovery from torn ACL suffered last season at Louisville. Starting a pair of Day 2 receivers in Week 1 is far from ideal for anybody, but no less so than trotting out Jalen Tolbert. The Dolphins are fully committed to their rebuild, and rookies like Bell, Douglas and Kevin Coleman are the biggest potential beneficiaries. Bell and Douglas belong on 12-team league watch lists, with Coleman worth a dynasty stash.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.headline: The Miami Herald’s Omar Kelly believes Dolphins rookie WR Kevin Coleman Jr. should be the team’s starting slot receiver this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.analysis: Responding to readers on social media this week, Kelly said he believes Coleman is the Dolphins’ best rookie wide receiver, and linked to an article of his from May 8. In the piece, Kelly argues that Coleman should be the team’s front-runner for the starting slot role. If Coleman can pull it off, he may only get on the field when the Dolphins are in three-wide receiver sets, giving him a limited upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.headline: Dolphins selected Missouri WR Kevin Coleman Jr. with the No. 177 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kevin-cole.analysis: Coleman (5’10/179) spent his college career with four teams in four seasons, starting at Jackson State with Travis Hunter and Deion Sanders. After Hunter and Sanders left for Colorado, he hopped to Louisville and Mississippi State before finishing at Missouri. Coleman spent much of his college career as a slot receiver with some punt return ability mixed in. He is undersized but has acceleration and agility to make him an effective ball-carrier in space. Coleman is limited in his route tree with shallow receptions littered across his college production. Despite the lack of vertical receptions and touchdown production, Coleman got the ball a combined 153 times on offense between Mississippi State and Missouri in his final two seasons. He has a chance to stick on an NFL roster as a gadget slot receiver and special teams return man.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell caught 4-of-5 targets for 31 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 8 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: The third-round rookie was limited to short-area work in today’s loss to the Patriots, but his five targets and four receptions both tie for career highs. He also lost two yards on a run play. Bell has had a few gaffes this year, but he is seemingly recovering well from last year’s ACL surgery. He is a player worth stashing on benches in many 12-team leagues, and could warrant WR5 treatment against the Lions next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell caught 3-of-4 targets for 25 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: Bell finished second on the team in targets but fourth in receiving yards. Caleb Douglas was finally healthy this week and stole the spotlight with 70 yards and two touchdowns despite seeing just three targets. After being held without a catch in back-to-back games, Bell’s modest Week 7 showing is still a step in the right direction. On the other hand, he simply isn’t seeing enough targets to be a weekly fantasy consideration right now. He should remain on the waiver wire in most fantasy leagues this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell caught neither of his two targets in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals, adding one carry for 26 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: Bell was targeted just twice on the day, catching neither target. He did see a carry on an end-around play, rushing for 26 yards on his sole touch of the game. He has ramped up to a starting receiver’s workload of snaps, ranking second among Dolphins receivers with 41 snaps. Though Bell is the field more, he has yet to be a key part of the Dolphins offense and will see less opportunities once Caleb Douglas (ankle) returns. Bell is best left on fantasy benches when the Dolphins come out of their Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell (knee) is not on Miami’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: He’ll be a FLEX dart throw against the Bengals. Bell continues to get listed with his knee injury as the Dolphins bring him along slowly, but he seems wheels up for Sundays as things currently stand.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell (knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: The Dolphins have been managing Bell’s practice reps for a few weeks, but it hasn’t been an issue on Sundays. He ran 85 percent of the routes in Week 4 and his route share has gone up in every game. He is in the WR5 range headed into Week 5 versus the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell caught 0-of-3 targets in the Dolphins’ Week 4 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: Bell’s Week 4 outing was heartbreaking. His near-68-yard touchdown on the Dolphins’ third drive will live with him, and fantasy managers alike, for a while. Malik Willis rolled right out of the pocket, facing pressure and lobbed a wobbly pass to Bell downfield. The rookie wide receiver caught it, took off downfield, stumbled through a leg grab and ran into the end zone. Unfortunately, the officials determined Bell had stepped out of bounds, along the right sideline, during the scramble drill. Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley did not challenge it. Upon replay, one can make the case that his pinky toe’s shadow grazed the white line, but it was an awfully close call. Aside from that, Willis sent him a wobbly, incomplete overthrow beyond the sticks on the Dolphins’ first drive and later tried to force a fadeaway jumper to him 25 yards downfield. The pass was contested and fell incomplete. The talent is there. Despite the rough outing, Bell warrants FLEX consideration against the Saints in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Chris Bell (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: Bell posted a 4/67 receiving line last week, though the Dolphins are still managing his reps. The Vikings’ blitz-based defense poses problems for Miami, limiting Bell to WR4 status this week. The rookie wide receiver should be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) will not play in Week 4 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: Douglas will miss his second straight game with an ankle injury, paving the way for fellow rookie Chris Bell to build on his Week 3 performance in which he went for 4-67-0 on eight targets. Bell and all Dolphins pass-catchers will be tough for fantasy managers to trust as anything more than WR4s on the road against a Vikings defense that could give them fits all afternoon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Dolphins WR Chris Bell (knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: The Dolphins’ ascending rookie wide receiver is on track to face the Vikings this week, although he continues to be limited by his surgically repaired knee. Bell should be viewed as a FLEX starter with an admittedly tough matchup against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/elijah-sar.analysis: We expect to see Douglas listed with a second DNP next to his name today, putting him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 4 against the Vikings. Were he indeed to miss this week’s game, WRs Chris Bell (knee) and Malik Washington would benefit. Washington’s target volume is somewhat intriguing, but Bell looks like the far more talented player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen caught both of his targets for eight yards in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: With Colby Parkinson sidelined with a rib injury, Allen played behind Tyler Higbee and wasn’t all that involved in the Rams’ run-first offense. Fresh off catching two touchdowns from Matthew Stafford on just 12 routes in Week 7, Allen didn’t get so lucky in Week 8. He shouldn’t be rostered in 12-team formats for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Parkinson will have one more chance to get back no the practice field Friday to avoid an injury designation entering the weekend. The veteran tight end was in and out of the team’s Week 7 game with the injury but managed to finish it, apparently feeling much worse after the adrenaline wore off. Fantasy managers of Parkinson and Tyler Higbee will want to track Parkinson’s status closely to end the week. An absence from Parkinson could also bring Davis Allen into the fantasy spotlight after the young tight end scored twice against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen caught 4-of-5 targets for 20 yards and two touchdowns in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: The Rams in Week 7 resorted to a heavy dose of three tight end sets with Davante Adams sidelined with a long-term hamstring injury. That led to 12 pass routes for Allen, fewer than both Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee. He caught two red zone touchdowns from Matthew Stafford, however, seeing a look on 33 percent of his routes. Allen will be tough to trust as a fantasy option unless or until his snaps and routes increase. He could be a deep league option in Week 8 against the Chargers, however.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen (foot) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: He got in a limited session and the Rams apparently trust him to play despite a pair of missed practices on Wednesday and Thursday. Colby Parkinson (shoulder) also avoided the final report. Tyler Higbee is the Rams tight end you should be using at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Allen remains out, and Parkinson (shoulder) remains limited. Tyler Higbee has played productively in the Rams’ No. 1 tight end role, and he should be expected to do so again this week against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Allen is dealing with a foot injury and is listed as a DNP on the Rams’ estimated practice report. Fellow tight end Colby Parkinson (shoulder) was listed as limited, though he has been dealing with the shoulder injury for a few weeks now and the Rams are likely managing his workload. Parkinson is trending to play. Allen’s potential absence may lead to the Rams activating rookie Max Klare to play alongside Parkinson and fantasy streaming option Tyler Higbee in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen is being evaluated for a concussion.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Allen has one catch for 13 yards, and likely is done for the day. The 25-year-old backup will need to clear protocol to play in Week 2 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Rams TE Davis Allen (quadricep) missed practice Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Speaking to media Monday, head coach Sean McVay relayed that it would be “some time” before Allen returns to the practice field considering the nature of the soft tissue injury. McVay added, “You don’t want to rush him back, Davis is going to be a big part of what we do this year.” Allen set career highs in his third professional season in 2025, catching 24 passes for 208 yards and three touchdowns, ranking second on the team in offensive snaps behind only Colby Parkinson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: ESPN’s Matt Bowen believes TE Kenyon Sadiq could be a “matchup player” in the Rams offense.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Sadiq out of Oregon is widely expected to be a first round pick after setting record at the NFL Combine. Bowen believes the hyper-athletic tight end could be a situation matchup player for Sean McVay, who used three tight end sets at the NFL’s highest rate in 2025. “With his frame and 4.39 speed, Sadiq could be a seam stretcher for quarterback Matthew Stafford. Plus, McVay could use Sadiq as a backside X receiver/power slot to draw favorable man matchups.” Sadiq, who had 80 receptions over three seasons at Oregon, could fit the LA offense “as a catch-and-run target on boot action concepts,” Bowen said. Stafford last season led the NFL with 75 pass attempts on designed rollouts. It’s a crowded tight end room in LA, with Colby Parikson, Tyler Higbee, Terrance Ferguson, and Davis Allen on the roster. Sadiq would likely function as a rotational player if he lands with the Rams, who have the 13th pick in the 2026 draft.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.headline: Davis Allen was not targeted in Los Angeles’ NFC Championship loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davis-alle.analysis: Allen went untargeted in the playoffs despite a strong snap share — he’s clearly the blocking tight end of the four-headed 3TE attack the Rams run. He enters the final year of his rookie contract in 2026 looking like a solid use of a roster spot for the Rams and someone fantasy managers should never, ever call on.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre Harris caught all three of his targets for 31 yards in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris was the team’s WR3 behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston, as usual. When McConkey is healthy, Harris operates as a part-time player without much of a fantasy floor. He should remain on waiver wires ahead of LA’s Week 9 game against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) will play in Week 8 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris returns to the lineup after missing Week 6, with the team’s bye week providing enough time for the veteran receiver to get back to the active game-day roster. That doesn’t mean he should be inserted into fantasy lineups after such a slow start to the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris missed Week 6 before the team’s Week 7 bye but could be held out for an additional week given the nature of his injury. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his status on the team’s final injury report Friday to gauge the viability of entering him back into lineups for Week 8. Fellow wide receiver Ladd McConkey (concussion) got in his second consecutive full session and should be good to go for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) will practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris was labeled week-to-week early in Week 6 and was unable to face the Chiefs that weekend. After resting and rehabbing through the Chargers’ Week 7 bye, Harris has a chance to resume playing in Week 8. We expect to see him listed as a limited participant, but an update will be provided if he practices in full. Brenen Thompson (quad) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 6 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: He did not practice this week and Jim Harbaugh called him “week to week.” Harris stands a chance at returning after Los Angeles’ Week 7 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Tre’ Harris (hamstring) is “more of a week-to-week [thing].”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris will probably have a real chance to play in Week 8, after the Chargers’ Week 7 bye. He thudded to a 16-yard outing in his big chance last week with Quentin Johnston and Ladd McConkey out and doesn’t necessarily need to be rostered if you’re in a bye week crunch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tre Harris caught 2-of-4 targets for 16 yards in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harris was a complete non-factor even against the depleted Broncos’ secondary. The second-year wideout was the top target with Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston unavailable, and that extra attention didn’t help. Harris will try and bounce back in Week 6 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Ladd McConkey (foot) is not expected to play in Week 5 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: McConkey did not practice at all this week but was still given a questionable tag on Friday. He was always a long-shot to play after aggravating his foot injury in Week 4. With Quentin Johnston out this week as well, Tre’ Harris will be Justin Herbert’s No. 1 receiver. That puts him in the WR3 mix despite the Chargers’ dismal offensive performance through four weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) won’t play in Los Angeles’ Week 5 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Johnston got in limited sessions on Thursday and Friday, so it was surprising to see him sent straight to “not playing.” Tre’ Harris figures to step in as Los Angeles’ top outside receiver by snaps this week and is a worthwhile FLEX play, even against a formidable Broncos defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Johnston and TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) both remained limited today, though WR Brenen Thompson (quad) downgraded. He did not practice, nor did Ladd McConkey (foot). Tre’ Harris could end up being the Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver, but he would only be a FLEX against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas caught 4-of-6 targets for 43 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 8 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Malik Willis did not throw a pass to Douglas until just over a minute left in the first half. The talented rookie came down with both two-minute drill targets for a total of 24 yards. He caught two more passes in the second half, seemingly injuring his right ankle while being tackled on the first. He managed to return for the next drive and helped set up Kevin Coleman’s 35-yard touchdown with a 12-yard reception. Douglas should be rostered in most 12-team leagues. He is a WR4/FLEX against the Lions next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas caught 2-of-3 targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Douglas was active for the first time since suffering an ankle injury in Week 2. Though he logged a measly 14 percent target share, Douglas was involved early, turning a first-quarter red zone target into his first NFL touchdown. Douglas turned his second catch of the day, a short out route, into a 63-yard touchdown by toe-tapping his way along the sideline for a game-sealing score. His role is only going in one direction after the breakout performance. He will be in the WR3 mix when the Dolphins take on the Pats next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Dolphins WR Caleb Douglas (ankle) will play in Week 7 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Douglas hasn’t played since Week 2 against the 49ers, but the rookie caught five passes for 94 yards in his pro debut against the Raiders and has been targeted on 16.4 percent of his routes. Stuck in a Dolphins offense that currently ranks 31st in scoring and passing yards, Douglas will be hard to trust as anything more than a fringe WR3/WR4 this week against a top-five Jets pass defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) remained limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: That’s back-to-back limited sessions from Douglas as he attempts to come back from an injury suffered in Week 2. We’d bet on him getting to the questionable line at this point given the significant layoff, but he does have a real chance to play against the Jets in Week 7 and be a WR4/FLEX candidate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Douglas told reporters that he has finally progressed to being “day-to-day,” giving him a real chance to suit up in Week 7 against the Jets. Douglas should be added in 12-team formats. He played very well early on and will likely warrant FLEX consideration upon his return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) won’t play in Miami’s Week 5 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Douglas has not practiced or played since Week 2. If only there were some sort of “injured reserve list” he could be placed on. Ah well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Dolphins coach Jeff Halfey said Douglas is “doing better” but is not ready to practice yet. It sounds like the rookie will miss another week. Malik Washington will continue to operate as the Dolphins’ No. 1 receiver, putting him in the WR3 mix for Week 5. Fellow rookie Chris Bell has seen his role grow every week, but the fantasy numbers aren’t there to match. He was held without a catch on three targets in Week 4. Bell is a solid long-term stash but barely cracks the WR5 ranks for Miami’s matchup with the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said the team is taking it “one day at a time” with Caleb Douglas’ ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: It’s hard to know what to make of this, but Douglas has missed back-to-back games with his injury and could be at risk of missing a third straight game if he can’t get on the practice field ahead of Week 5’s game against the Bengals. Douglas did not practice at all last week, so even getting on the field in a limited capacity would be an improvement. His name will be one to keep an eye on when the Dolphins release their first injury report on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Dolphins declared WR Caleb Douglas, QB Brady Cook, CB Marcellas Dial, EDGE Rob Beal, OG DJ Campbell, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick and TE Justin Joly inactive for Week 4 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: The Dolphins will be without Douglas, one of their two talented rookie wide receivers, against the Vikings’ top-tier defense today. He is sidelined by an ankle injury. Joly, the Dolphins’ rookie tight end, is inactive after making his debut last week. Cook wil serve as the team’s emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) will not play in Week 4 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Douglas will miss his second straight game with an ankle injury, paving the way for fellow rookie Chris Bell to build on his Week 3 performance in which he went for 4-67-0 on eight targets. Bell and all Dolphins pass-catchers will be tough for fantasy managers to trust as anything more than WR4s on the road against a Vikings defense that could give them fits all afternoon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden II caught all five of his targets for 52 yards in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden led LA tight ends in targets and trailed only Ladd McConkey in receiving yards on the day. Operating as a big slot receiver, Gadsden could have some fantasy value if he were to get more snaps and routes in the Chargers offense. In Week 9 against the Texans he’ll be a decent streaming option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden II caught 3-of-5 targets for 17 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Both Gadsden and Charlie Kolar had five targets on the day. (Kolar caught three of those targets for 20 yards.) Gadsden logged 28 pass routes to 24 for Kolar. The split-up tight end role will make it next to impossible for either player to be fantasy relevant without catching a touchdown. The Chargers are on bye next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden failed to haul in his only target in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden had another disappointing outing for the Chargers and his fantasy managers on Sunday. He’s now been held without a catch in two of his last three games and has yet to exceed 36 receiving yards in any game this season. Playing in one of the worst offenses in the league certainly doesn’t help things, but Gadsden can’t be trusted by fantasy managers at this point and won’t be on the fantasy radar in Week 6 when the Chargers visit the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden II caught 5-of-8 targets for 36 yards in the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden did make a spectacular catch on fourth down to set up a touchdown, but oustide of that, the tight end — while finishing tied for the most catches on the day with Keaton Mitchell — was unable to find any room against the Seahawks’ defense. The 23-year-old was more involved than he has been in previous weeks, but that’s less compliment to this effort than insult to the first few. He’ll be back at it in Week 5 against another tough defense in the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Chargers TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) won’t play in Los Angeles’ Week 4 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: He did rejoin practice today, making it plausible he’ll be up for the Chargers’ Week 5 game against the Broncos. Second-year receiving TE Oronde Gadsden was unable to seize the moment with Kolar and TE David Njoku (knee) sidelined last week, catching 0-of-3 targets. The once-promising youngster must do something on Sunday if he wishes to remain re-draft-relevant in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden didn’t catch any of his three targets in a Week 3 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden’s first target of the day was on a third-down pass that hit off his hands and landed on the grass. Neither of his other two targets was particularly close to being caught. He did play on 39 of the team’s 69 snaps, more than any other tight end, and ran a route on 31 of their 43 dropbacks, which was the third-most of any player on the Chargers. We guess you can talk yourself into his role based on those numbers, but the results weren’t there, and the Chargers look discombobulated on offense. It’s hard to trust Gadsden in fantasy going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: ESPN’s Kris Rhim reports that Chargers TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) will not be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Kolar’s surgery earlier this week reportedly changed his prognosis. Kolar was expected to land on short-term injured reserve and miss at least four games. Apparently, the team expects him back sooner than that. Backup TE Oronde Gadsden is still set to start, given Kolar and TE David Njoku’s (knee) injuries, but Gadsden’s audition window has evidently shrunk. He remains a worthwhile add and can be started by TE-needy fantasy managers in what should be a productive game environment against the Bills this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden caught both of his targets for 18 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 2 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: David Njoku left the game early with a knee injury and Charlie Kolar followed him to the locker room much later because of a forearm injury. As a result, Gadsden’s route rate jumped from 14 percent in Week 1 to 48 percent today. He still managed just two catches, but Gadsden at least found the end zone for the first time this year. The Chargers offense has looked defunct through two weeks, so even a full-time role for Gadsden could result in middling fantasy numbers. Still, he is worth a look off the waiver wire for teams in need of tight end production.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Chargers OC Mike McDaniel said the team plans on utilizing TE Oronde Gadsden’s skillset.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: McDaniel was asked why Gadsden only played eight snaps in Week 1. The Chargers’ offensive coordinator said he expected Gadsden to get more involved last week, but the game “didn’t play out” that way. McDaniel closed by saying he expects Gadsden “to be more involved outside of an unforeseen situation where the game and the parameters with which you’re playing change — and therein lies the problem. Gadsden is not a full-time player. Projecting his weekly usage will be challenging. He is currently not worth starting in 12-team leagues, though that could change if McDaniel decides to feature him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden II caught both of his targets for 32 yards in the Chargers’ Week 1 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden hardly saw the field against Arizona. He ran just seven pass routes while David Njoku logged 17 routes and caught all five of his targets. Gadsden is clearly an afterthought in the Chargers passing offense for now. He should remain on waiver wires ahead of the Bolts’ Week 2 game against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington caught 5-of-6 targets for 40 yards and one touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 8 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington continues to play well as a short-area pass catcher, though he did haul in a 23-yarder downfield. He got leveled on the Dolphins’ fifth drive, and Patriots LB Christian Ellis received an unnecessary roughness penalty for the act. It briefly seemed like Washington’s day might be over, but he returned a few plays later to score a one-yard touchdown via a quick out route after going in motion pre-snap. Today’s stat line allowed Washington to clear the century mark in career catches (103). Among NFL wide receivers with at least 100 receptions from 2021-26, Washington’s 8.4 yards per reception ranks dead last. He is a WR4/FLEX against the Lions in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington (knee) is not on Miami’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington’s WR4 status will continue aplomb against the Patriots in Week 8, though Caleb Douglas’ return probably has capped his ceiling case for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Back-to-back limited sessions probably leave Washington in a good spot for Week 8. He’s more likely than not to be cleared off the injury report on Friday as long as there’s not a sudden downgrade.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington has cooled off in recent weeks. Although his knee injury is unlikely to keep him out of the Dolphins’ Week 8 matchup against the Patriots, he is barely a WR5 in fantasy football. Washington does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington caught all three of his targets for 27 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 7 win over the Jets, adding two carries for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington’s previous season-low in targets was five. He had also reached at least 43 receiving yards in every game before today. It shouldn’t come as a surprise that his worst box score of the season came in Caleb Douglas’s first game back from a month-long absence. With more competition for targets on a team that doesn’t want to pass the football, Washington is trending in the wrong direction headed into Week 8. He will be a low-end WR4 versus the Patriots next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington caught 6-of-8 targets for 43 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals, adding one carry for 19 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington was the most involved Dolphins receiver, leading the team in targets and receiving yards. He started things off with an 18-yard rush and saw a steady peppering of low-depth targets. Though he led all Dolphins skill-position players in snaps, Washington doesn’t see many scoring opportunities in the Miami offense. After a Week 6 bye, The 25-year-old is a volume-based FLEX play Week 7 against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington caught 5-of-5 targets for 67 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 4 loss to the Vikings, adding two rushes for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Washington remains one of the Dolphins’ primary returners despite his increased receiving involvement. His day began with a muffed punt that he successfully recovered in the end zone for a touchback. Things improved from there. Washington delivered multiple double-digit gains, functioning effectively as a weapon behind the line of scrimmage and in the flats. He also turned in a 17-yarder via a corner route on play action. Rookie WR Caleb Douglas (ankle) may return for next week’s game against the Saints. If he remains sidelined, Washington should be FLEX-viable, though his ceiling is questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: We expect to see Douglas listed with a second DNP next to his name today, putting him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 4 against the Vikings. Were he indeed to miss this week’s game, WRs Chris Bell (knee) and Malik Washington would benefit. Washington’s target volume is somewhat intriguing, but Bell looks like the far more talented player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Douglas, who has shown flashes in limited action so far this season, did not suit up in Week 3 against the Chiefs and looks like a long shot for Week 4 against the Vikings. Douglas’ absence would be a potential boost for Malik Washington, who leads the Dolphins in targets and air yards through Week 3. Minnesota’s defense, while elite, has allowed the fourth most air yards this season and profiles as a pass-funnel.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.headline: Malik Washington caught 5-of-10 targets for 56 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 3 loss to the Chiefs, adding two carries for five yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-wash.analysis: Every total was a new season high for Washington, including the carries. It briefly appeared Washington might be the Dolphins’ emergency lead back, as De’Von Achane was knocked out with a knee injury and Ollie Gordon was cramping. With Achane seemingly set for a long absence, Washington could indeed be in line for more rushing usage. That makes him a slightly more viable WR4, but rookies Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas still offer more overall upside heading into Week 4 against the Vikings. That’s, of course, if Douglas returns from his ankle injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Kimani Vidal had eight rushes for 23 yards in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams, adding two catches for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: Vidal was second on the team in rushing attempts behind Omarion Hampton (9) and ran the second most pass routes behind Keaton Mitchell. Vidal won’t be a legit fantasy option unless Hampton misses time in the coming weeks. He’s a decent stash in deeper formats for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Kimani Vidal had seven rushes for 21 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs, adding three catches for 19 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: Vidal got much of his work in the first quarter before Omarion Hampton worked into the backfield later in the game. Hampton ended up leading the Bolts backfield in both routes and targets, with Vidal a close second in both categories. When the Chargers return from the bye week, Vidal could see an increased role as the team looks elsewhere for production. He should be rostered in most deep formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Kimani Vidal rushed eight times for 57 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: Vidal showed off his potential to be a big-play back on a 42-yard touchdown that gave the Chargers a 17-10 lead. The 25-year-old did nothing outside of that carry, but in a game where offense was limited — limited is putting it nicely — it stood out. Vidal was more effective than Omarion Hampton (33 yards on 14 carries) and Keaton Mitchell (11 on six) but still seems likely to be behind both for Week 6 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Kimani Vidal caught two passes for 11 yards and a touchdown while rushing four times for 16 yards in the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: Vidal took a flip pass from Justin Herbert for a touchdown to get the Chargers to within two scores. The 25-year-old saw plenty of reps as Los Angeles is clearly committed to the committee approach — no running back had more than ten carries — but outside of that score, he didn’t do much with them. The Chargers take on the Broncos in Week 5 and Vidal remains off the fantasy radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Chargers RB Keaton Mitchell rushed three times for minus-one yard in Thursday’s preseason game against the 49ers, adding one reception for 11 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: Mitchell’s box score would have looked a lot better if his 21-yard reception on a route out of the backfield had not been called back due to a penalty. Chargers starting RB Omarion Hampton played all three snaps on the opening drive before giving way to Mitchell, who played 10-of-10 snaps on the second and third drives. Fellow backup RB Kimani Vidal took the field as the Chargers’ kick returner to begin the game. He made his first appearance on offense on the Chargers’ fourth drive. Mitchell could return standalone FLEX value with big-play upside in this role. He reportedly visited the blue medical tent, but was allowed to return to the sideline. Hopefully, this is a non-issue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Chargers RB Kimani Vidal rushed five times for eight yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: Vidal stayed in for two drives and did not catch his only target. Tonight’s start suggests Vidal is behind RB Keaton Mitchell on the depth chart. Mitchell did not play, nor did starting RB Omarion Hampton. Vidal is a proven, capable fill-in starter, but he should only be drafted as the Chargers’ RB3 at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Speaking on NFL Daily about his backfield rotation, Chargers OC Mike McDaniel said, “if a player is playing really well, I’m not going to take them out.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: Earlier this week, McDaniel said he plans to employ a hot-hand approach at the running back position and plans to “use all three of those guys probably every game.” NFL Daily co-hosts Gregg Rosenthal and Jourdan Rodrigue helpfully followed up on those comments, specifically regarding their fantasy football implications. McDaniel encouragingly prefaced his response by saying, “no one has to worry,” adding that benching productive players is “bad business.” If you were already bullish on one or more of Omarion Hampton, Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal, these comments can be taken positively. Reading between the lines, if Hampton, the starter, proves his value as the team’s RB1, he should receive a fantasy-friendly workload.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Chargers OC Mike McDaniel said “I’ll use all three of those guys probably every game” when asked about the backfield.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: Speaking to reporters Monday, Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel said that all three of Omarion Hampton, Keaton Mitchell, and Kimani Vidal will be featured in the backfield this season. “Good news is I see all three of those guys performing at a very high level,” McDaniel said. “Kinda play hot hand once you’re into games.” While that’s not the best news for fantasy managers that invested second round picks into Hampton, the opportunity for the Chargers to turn heads on the scoreboard could result in a case of “a rising tide raises all ships.” McDaniel famously, and recently, made two backs top-six producers in fantasy points per game in the same season, with both Raheem Mostert and De’Von Achane finishing 2023 in that range. Whether a similar situation transpires in Los Angeles remains to be seen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Chargers OC Mike McDaniel said he could use all three RBs in a game and that usage may depend on who has the “hot hand.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: It’s the kind of thing fantasy managers hate to hear. When speaking about his running backs on Monday, McDaniel said, “I see all three producing at a very high level,” while saying the workload for each back could depend on the opponent and who has the “hot hand.” While it’s certainly concerning on the surface, we feel pretty confident in Omarion Hampton having the safest role as far as fantasy is concerned, while Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal could prove a bit more volatile. Their volatility has been baked into their ADP all offseason, as Mitchell is often going in the 12th or 13th round of drafts while Vidal often goes undrafted. It may take some time to get a good sense of McDaniel’s plans for the backfield, but we would expect a clear-cut RB1 and RB2 to emerge this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: The Athletic’s Daniel Popper expects Keaton Mitchell to beat out Kimani Vidal for Chargers’ RB2 role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: Per Popper, the Chargers really like Mitchell’s ability to “press the edge and get explosives to the outside.” That said, Popper believes Vidal will “give Mitchell a push” for the role. He also believes that both players will make the final roster, regardless. If this is how the depth chart shakes out, one wonders whether Vidal could sneak onto the field in certain passing situations, potentially reducing Mitchell’s standalone viability. Mitchell was seen working in the passing game last week, though — something he rarely did in Baltimore — so it is too early to tell.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston caught all four of his targets for 37 yards in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: It was yet another down game for Johnston, who did his work underneath in this one. He now has one game this season with more than two receptions in a Chargers offense that can be described as utterly dysfunctional on every level. Johnston should not be rostered in most fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-3 targets for 57 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston’s lone catch was a fantastic grab over tight coverage in the fourth quarter. He nearly scored on the play. Even with Ladd McConkey out with a head injury, Johnston did not function as the Chargers’ top wideout, as DeAndre Lambert-Smith led the team with ten targets. Johnston will be nothing more than a deep league flex option going forward. He should not be rostered in most 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Stark difference from last week’s limited-limited-rule out. Jim Harbaugh would not commit to putting it on the record that Johnston would be on a snap count. Playing through the injury with Los Angeles’ sad sack offensive line would seem to have Johnston as more of a sketchy FLEX play than a WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston is on track to play, but this wide receiver corps is very banged up. KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring) and Brenen Thompson (quad) remained limited as well. Marquez Valdes-Scantling (ribs) upgraded to full.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston, KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring), Brenen Thompson (quad), and Marquez Valdes-Scantling (rib) were all limited Wednesday. Lambert-Smith currently has his practice window for return from IR open while the others are dealing with a varying level of ailments. Johnston is the best fantasy option out of this group, but he is only worth FLEX consideration in the deepest of leagues. With Ladd McConkey (foot) also limited, the Chargers have several “maybes” ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Quentin Johnston (chest) will “probably be limited this week like last for the practice.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: “We’ll see where he’s at the end of the week,” Harbaugh added. Johnston practiced on both Thursday and Friday so he likely has the best chance of being active among Los Angeles’ main three wideouts. Unfortunately this passing game is in rough shape, and even a higher volume, healthy load probably wouldn’t get Johnston above the FLEX line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) won’t play in Los Angeles’ Week 5 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston got in limited sessions on Thursday and Friday, so it was surprising to see him sent straight to “not playing.” Tre’ Harris figures to step in as Los Angeles’ top outside receiver by snaps this week and is a worthwhile FLEX play, even against a formidable Broncos defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston and TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) both remained limited today, though WR Brenen Thompson (quad) downgraded. He did not practice, nor did Ladd McConkey (foot). Tre’ Harris could end up being the Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver, but he would only be a FLEX against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Chargers WR Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: In addition to Johnston, TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) and WR Brenen Thompson (quad) were also limited. Johnston has played in every game this season, but pops up on the practice report with a chest issue on Wednesday. He is not yet in danger of missing Week 5, barring setbacks later in the week. Neither Thompson nor Kolar have played since Week 2 but both have a chance to return this week against the Broncos. With Ladd McConkey (foot) not practicing, Johnston may have fantasy value as the Chargers’ No. 1 wideout this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-2 targets for 44 yards in the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston at least made the most of his only catch, as it was on 4th-and-7 and kept the Chargers in the game. He also saw a redzone target, but Justin Herbert overthrew him. Johnston simply cannot be trusted even with the potential to make big plays in Week 5 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Corey Kiner rushed seven times for 38 yards in the Patriots’ Week 8 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kiner’s most notable usage note is that he was trusted with a carry on 3rd-and-1 during the Patriots’ eighth drive. He was unable to convert it for a first down. Kiner was involved today because TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was inactive. Kiner does not need to be stashed on fantasy football benches in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Corey Kiner rushed 11 times for 57 yards in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Even with Rhamondre Stevenson active and TreVeyon Henderson surprisingly playing through his ankle injury, Kiner was called on as the Patriots’ “closer,” with all 11 of his handles coming in the final 16:30 of the contest. The Patriots were winning, but the game was still in doubt. Kiner responded by continually turning his short-yardage opportunities into first downs, while he ended up leading the team in rushing. It wasn’t easy to see that one coming, but it might be difficult for coach Mike Vrabel to un-see it as neither Stevenson nor Henderson impress in their No. 1 or 2 jobs. Kiner is worth an end-of-bench stash in 14-team leagues but is not yet 12-team league relevant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) will miss multiple weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Henderson suffered his latest ankle injury in Week 5 against the Raiders. Schefter said Henderson is “regarded as a quick healer, so the Patriots are hoping his return is sooner rather than later.” Still, he could be sidelined for the next few weeks, leaving Rhamondre Stevenson as the team’s clear lead back. Corey Kiner, meanwhile, appears to be in line as the Patriots’ RB2 after seeing seven touches last week against the Raiders. Kiner should be stashed in most 12-team fantasy leagues for now. Stevenson profiles as a top-12 play until Henderson returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Corey Kiner had six rushes for 52 yards in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders, adding one catch for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kiner’s seven touches came after TreVeyon Henderson went down with what could be a serious ankle injury in the second quarter. While much of his work came in garbage time, Kiner could work as the Patriots’ No. 2 back behind Rhamondre Stevenson if Henderson is sidelined in Week 6. Kiner is worth a look on waiver wires this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Corey Kiner rushed six times for 11 yards in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kiner served as Rhamondre Stevenson’s backup with TreVeyon Henderson out this week. He was the only other Pats running back to see a carry in this game, though practice squad call-up Lan Larison was targeted twice, both of which he caught. Kiner did not see a look through the air. As a backup running back without any pass-catching value, Kiner is not on the fantasy radar heading into Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Mike Reiss reports that Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is not present for the media-access portion of practice on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The injury has sidelined Henderson since August 24. The Patriots face the Seahawks on Wednesday. At this point, Henderson must be considered questionable to play. Even if he were active, he would be slated for No. 2 duties behind starting RB Rhamondre Stevenson, and it is fair to wonder if the team would keep Henderson on a snap count. Reiss reported this morning that RB Lan Larison and/or RB Hassan Haskins would likely be elevated from the practice squad if Henderson cannot play, joining Stevenson and backup RB Corey Kiner on game day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots acquired RB Corey Kiner from the Cardinals in exchange for a seventh-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The trade was first reported by ESPN’s Adam Schefter. The draft pick going to the Cardinals is a seventh-round pick in 2028. Kiner was buried on the depth in Arizona, but should immediately step in as the RB3 behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson with the Patriots. A former UDFA who appeared in four games with the Cardinals last year, Kiner is only worth a stash in deeper formats and has no standalone fantasy value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Emari Demercado rushed five times for 30 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 16 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Demercado failed to snag his only target and he was out-touched 6-to-5 by fellow backup RB Corey Kiner. Cardinals RB Michael Carter is the clear-cut starter and Kiner’s presence reduces Demercado’s bench-stash value. This looks like a three-player committee with one FLEX-viable player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cardinals signed RB Corey Kiner off the Vikings’ practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Cardinals released RB Jermar Jefferson in a related move. We’d love to say this doesn’t matter, but sadly, all Cardinals running back news is real news. Kiner spent time with the 49ers in training camp before getting hurt, he was a priority UDFA signing this offseason. It’s possible he may be fantasy-relevant at some point given how banged up the Cardinals RB room is.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan said RB Patrick Taylor (shoulder) will miss a couple of weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Taylor exited Saturday’s preseason game against the Raiders with the injury and did not return to the field. Rookie UDFA Corey Kiner also exited with a high-ankle sprain and is expected to miss a couple of weeks. The 49ers are already dealing with injuries to Isaac Guerendo (shoulder) and rookie Jordan James (knee). Behind Christian McCaffrey is journeyman Ke’Shawn Vaughn and the recently re-signed Jeff Wilson, who rushed for 8-16-1 against the Raiders while adding another catch for 16 yards. Both Vaughn and Wilson could spell McCaffrey in Week 1 against the Seahawks if Guerendo, James, and Taylor are all sidelined. That said, none of these players carry much fantasy upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed 19 times for 82 yards in the Patriots’ Week 8 win over the Dolphins, adding three receptions for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson was held out of the end zone against the Dolphins, but comfortably paced his team with 22 touches and was handed the ball on each of the Patriots’ first three plays. Stevenson ran hard on inside runs and played well as a receiver, as usual. A fake pitch from inside the Dolphins’ five-yard line had at least one Dolphins defender convinced that Stevenson was headed for the end zone, but Drake Maye kept the ball and ran it into the end zone himself. Stevenson remains firmly in play as an RB2 next week against the Packers.
