https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed six times for 22 yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears, adding 93 yards and a touchdown on five receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson scored one of the more improbable touchdowns you will see late in the second quarter. After taking possession with just 14 seconds remaining on the clock, Drake Maye completed an 18-yard pass to A.J. Brown to place the ball near midfield with three seconds remaining before the half. Instead of heaving the ball deep on a Hail Mary, Maye dumped the ball off to Stevenson in the flat with blockers out front. Stevenson would do the rest on his way to a 48-yard score as time expired in the second frame on a score that never really should have happened. The six carries go down as a season-low for the veteran back, although 11 opportunities handily led the team. Stevenson has not seen more than 14 carries since Week 1 and is not finding paint frequently enough to remain a consistent RB2, making him a shaky weekly start moving forward. That holds true ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed 14 times for 36 yards in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson was not targeted in the passing game. He didn’t make any big mistakes — that would be TreVeyon Henderson with his third quarter fumble — but like Hendo, Stevenson found himself mostly on the bench late as the Pats surprisingly rode No. 3 back Corey Kiner in closeout mode. Kiner received 11 carries in the game’s final 16:30. Speaking afterward, coach Mike Vrabel literally called it a hot-hand situation. The “hot hand” is something Stevenson rarely develops, so he can ill afford this backfield becoming a three-man committee. For now, Stevenson is still the Pats’ No. 1 running back. but things just got a little dicier heading into Thursday’s short-week matchup with the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson had 13 rushes for 64 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders, adding three catches for 21 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson was splitting the backfield workload with TreVeyon Henderson before Henderson sustained a potentially serious ankle injury in the second quarter and did not return. Stevenson was somewhat efficient with his opportunities, breaking a few tackles against a low-energy, low-effort Raiders defense. His touchdown came on a goal line carry in the first half. It was his second score of the year. Stevenson will be a top-12 fantasy option next week against the Jets if Henderson is sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson already told reporters on Friday that he was “ready to go”, so this news item doesn’t come as much of a surprise. Stevenson will continue to operate as the Pats’ top option in high-leverage situations, though he could cede more work between the 20s to TreVeyon Henderson. Both backs are stuck as low-ceiling RB3 options this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is questionable for New England’s Week 5 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson told Mike Reiss that he’s “ready to go” and that he just got “rolled up on” late in Week 4’s win over the Bills. We’d be surprised if he didn’t play on Sunday and he should be regarded on the optimistic side of questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson is on track to play in Week 5 against the Raiders. It would be great to see him upgrade to full participation tomorrow. Regardless, Stevenson should at least be available for FLEX-viable duties on game day, if not his normal RB2-worthy workload.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Patriots RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: This one is a surprise considering head coach Mike Vrabel said earlier Wednesday that Stevenson would not practice. Instead, the 28-year-old is listed as a limited participant on Wednesday’s official practice report. Stevenson seemingly tweaked his knee towards the end of Week 4 but he has a chance to play in Week 5 against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said Rhamondre Stevenson (leg) is not expected to practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson tweaked his knee or ankle on his last touch of Week 4. The game ended shortly after that, so we didn’t get an official update on his injury from the team. Vrabel told reporters there is a chance he plays in Week 5, but it sounds like the veteran is on the wrong side of questionable as of Wednesday. TreVeyon Henderson’s role was dwindling in recent weeks, but Stevenson’s absence will thrust him right back into a workhorse role. He would be a high-end RB2 if Stevenson is unable to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed 13 times for 47 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 4 win over the Bills, adding 27 yards receiving on 3-of-5 targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson also hauled in a crucial two-point conversion catch on the late fourth-quarter drive that gave the Patriots the lead. Stevenson didn’t have any huge gains on the day, but he consistently gained yardage through the middle of the Bills’ defense and was the clear top option in the red zone. However, when the Patriots were trying to run out the clock, Stevenson got hit at the line of scrimmage and limped off the field with a knee injury. The game ended just two plays later, so this will have to be a situation fantasy managers monitor during the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell had four rushes for six yards in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams, adding three catches for 17 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Mitchell, as usual, was third in rushing attempts, behind Omarion Hampton (9) and Kimani Vidal (8). His three targets led the backfield but didn’t amount to much. With the Bolts’ backfield being split three ways, Mitchell is going to struggle to get anything going without an explosive play or two. He should remain on most waiver wires ahead of Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell had two rushes for four yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Mitchell did not catch his only target on the day. He was third among Bolts running backs in pass routes, behind Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal. The sad state of the Chargers offense and injuries to the team’s offensive line make it nearly impossible for Mitchell to post fantasy relevant numbers for now. The Chargers are on bye in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell rushed 6 times for 11 yards in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos while adding three receptions for 18 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: The only positive here was that Mitchell was somewhat involved in the pass game, but it was all of the check-down variety. The injuries to the Los Angeles offensive line just won’t open many holes right now, and even if Mitchell has looked more spry than Omarion Hampton, there’s more risk than reward having him in a lineup right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel said he has not lost “any faith” in Omarion Hampton.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: “I don’t see any change in terms of the depth chart at all. I felt I was underutilizing a strength,” McDaniel said about the increased usage of Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal. McDaniel’s statement is good for Hampton in the sense that we know Hampton will retain a reasonable role. And it’s bad because McDaniel is all but confirming the pecking order will remain the same. Expect more low-end RB2/FLEX nonsense from Hampton.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell rushed 10 times for 39 yards while catching five passes for 24 yards in the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Mitchell, Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal were both equally involved in the rushing attack, and that’s not really a compliment to anyone in this group.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell (foot) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 4 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: He practiced all three days this week, upgrading to full on Friday, and should be a lower-end FLEX option against a tough Seahawks run defense. The good news for Mitchell is that the proof-of-concept of “the Chargers can’t run block so they should just use someone fast” worked in Week 3. He should see a reasonable amount of touches in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: The Chargers’ speedy RB2 was seen wearing a walking boot after practice on Wednesday, but that didn’t keep him from practicing today. Mitchell scored a touchdown on a red zone carry last week and could continue rotating in against the Seahawks this week. He should be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: ESPN’s Kris Rhim reports Keaton Mitchell was wearing a walking boot on his left foot after practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: He was eventually added to the injury report as “limited” with an ankle issue. Per Rhim, Mitchell told reporters in the locker room he was okay. Mitchell was not initially on the injury report. This obviously flared up during practice but he didn’t have it looked at until after the report was posted. We will get more clarity on the situation tomorrow. Mitchell’s role grew in Week 3 with 11 touches, but a foot or ankle injury would likely limit any further progress.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell rushed eight times for 52 yards in a Week 3 loss to the Bills, adding three catches and a receiving touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Mitchell’s touchdown was on a “pass” from Justin Hebert that was really a jet sweep where Herbert let go of the ball, and Mitchell rushed it in off the edge. Regardless, it was a nice run by Mitchell, who made Deone Walker miss in the backfield and is a clear example that the Chargers want to get him the ball in space. Mitchell did see about half as many carries as Omarion Hampton, but he played just three fewer snaps and ran a route on nine more dropbacks. Considering he was also seeing some work in the red zone, Mitchell needs to be rostered in all formats right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell rushed five times for 24 yards in the Chargers’ Week 2 loss to the Raiders, adding one catch for 145 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: The Chargers deployed Mitchell sparingly once again. He touched the ball four times in his LA debut last week and that number only improved to six this time around. Omarion Hampton logged 23 carries and two catches today. On the other hand, Hampton coughed up a game-losing fumble, so the Chargers may want to see more from Mitchell next week versus the Bills. He is buried in the RB5/6 ranks for now, but fantasy managers can hold onto him for at least one more week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Eli Raridon caught 1-of-4 targets for five yards in the Patriots’ Week 8 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Patriots’ rookie tight end got involved early, chipping in a five -yard catch on the team’s first drive. He earned a target at the Dolphins’ five-yard line on the next play, but the pass was thrown inaccurately by a scrambling Drake Maye. Hunter Henry suffered a foot injury in the first half, which allowed Raridon to run as the Patriots’ top tight end. Although he earned a few more targets as the game progressed, unfortunately, Raridon’s lone box score contribution thereafter was a false start on the Patriots’ eighth drive. Despite Raridon’s quiet Week 8 outing, he will warrant streaming TE1 treatment next week against the Packers if Henry is unable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Eli Raridon caught 5-of-5 targets for 57 yards in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Raridon, who was out last week, was very much involved in the revived New England passing attack. Hunter Henry, meanwhile, had three grabs for 44 yards and a touchdown. The Patriots have used two tight end sets at a high rate when Raridon is healthy. Unless Henry misses time, Raridon should remain on waiver wires in most 12-team formats. He had been targeted on ten percent of his routes headed into Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Eli Raridon is questionable to return in Week 4 against the Bills with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Raridon was questionable coming into this game with a thigh injury. He caught one of two targets for 12 yards before leaving this game with another injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Eli Raridon (thigh) is active for Week 4 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Raridon was questionable heading into the weekend, but he was able to get in three limited practice sessions this week, so he had been trending towards a return. He will back up Hunter Henry but could cut into Henry’s snaps enough to make Henry just a TE2 in deeper formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots TE Eli Raridon (thigh) is questionable for New England’s Week 4 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: He got in three limited sessions this week. If active, Raridon would cut into Hunter Henry’s ceiling a bit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots TE Eli Raridon (thigh) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Patriots’ rookie tight end has a chance to play this week. He is not yet involved enough to warrant TE1 treatment though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots TE Eli Raridon (thigh) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Raridon is tentatively on track to play in Week 4 against the Bills, though he cannot be started as anything more than a touchdown-dependent TE2. His return could squeeze TE Hunter Henry’s access to targets though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots declared TE Eli Raridon, QB Behren Morton, OT Dametrious Crownover, DT Leonard Taylor III, EDGE Dre’Mont Jones, and S Craig Woodson inactive for Week 3 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Raridon’s absence should provide a small bump for Hunter Henry, who has run a route on 63 percent of the Patriots’ drop backs and seen a target on 16 percent of those routes through Week 2. Raridon had been running around 20 percent of the team’s routes. Henry profiles as a deep league option for Week 3 against Jacksonville’s pass-funnel defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots TE Eli Raridon (thigh) is questionable for New England’s Week 3 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The second-string tight end’s absence may open up more opportunities for New England slot wideout Pop Douglas. The Patriots also ruled out Dre’Mont Jones (shoulder) for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots TE Eli Raridon (thigh) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Raridon worked off to the side yesterday and ended up being listed as a limited participant. He is not seen with the team again today, so either a light, limited session or a total absence is possible. Either way, Raridon remains firmly in the questionable column, though a second limited session would theoretically put him on track to play in Week 3 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey caught 4-of-6 targets for 86 yards in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey was fully back from various injuries that kept him sidelined for much of the season’s first month and a half. He led the Chargers in all receiving categories, and had the team’s biggest play of the game — a 54-yard gain on a nicely thrown ball from Justin Herbert. McConkey will have a solid matchup in Week 9 against a struggling Houston secondary and should remain in 12-team league lineups. It remains to be seen whether he has any sort of ceiling in a pitiful LA offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (concussion) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 8 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey’s concussion was always unlikely to hold him out for Week 8 with the team coming off their bye, with Friday’s injury report confirming that notion. The Chargers have under-performed offensive expectations more than any team through their first six games, leaving McConkey in the FLEX range for Week 8, a far cry from the WR2 range he was drafted in this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Tre’ Harris (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: Harris missed Week 6 before the team’s Week 7 bye but could be held out for an additional week given the nature of his injury. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his status on the team’s final injury report Friday to gauge the viability of entering him back into lineups for Week 8. Fellow wide receiver Ladd McConkey (concussion) got in his second consecutive full session and should be good to go for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (concussion) will practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: The Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver could resume practicing in full today, after recovering during the team’s Week 7 bye. If McConkey is limited, an update will be provided. Exactly one week ago, The Athletic’s Noah Furtado reported that the Chargers will try to “simplify” the team’s offense in the coming weeks. They face an underperforming Rams defense in Week 8 and could (maybe) generate a bounce-back performance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: The Athletic’s Noah Furtado reports the Chargers will try to “simplify” the team’s offense in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: Justin Herbert and the flailing Chargers skill position players have appeared almost comically confused about all the pre-snap motion OC Mike McDaniel uses. That came through in the team’s embarrassing Week 6 loss to the Chiefs when players were bumping into each other during pre-snap motion calls from Herbert. Head coach Jim Harbaugh acknowledged the team is considering narrowing the offensive playbook during their bye week. “Definitely looking at volume and where you can make it to where the players can understand,” Harbaugh said when asked about how Chargers players were adjusting to McDaniel’s complex offense. The Chargers have used pre-snap motion on 74 percent of their snaps, the fourth highest rate in the NFL. Last year they used motion on 56 percent of their snaps. Hopefully these adjustments lead to some production for the NFL’s worst offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (head) was ruled out in Week 6 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey exited the game after a 17-yard reception in the first quarter and was seen entering the blue medical tent before being helped to the locker room. The quickness with which he was ruled out could mean the injury is on the severe side. The Chargers are down to their fifth and sixth wideouts on the depth chart. Justin Herbert likely won’t be fantasy relevant for the rest of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (foot) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said he did not know if McConkey or Quentin Johnston would be on snap counts on Sunday. Cool. What we do know is that the Chargers desperately need a win and McConkey is their best receiver, so the incentives are certainly aligned to get McConkey into the fantasy WR3 discussion even with a pitch count.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (foot) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey is on track to once again be active on game day, but it is unclear how involved he will be. Two limited sessions are a good sign, but it would be great to see him practice fully tomorrow. In that instance, starting him as a WR2 would be far more palatable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said he expects Ladd McConkey (foot) to practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: We, in turn, expect McConkey to be listed as a limited participant. An update will be provided if he practices in full. The Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver was an emergency active last week, goose-egging in the box score. His early-week return to practice puts him on track to play in Week 6 against the Chiefs, but it would be great to see him practice in full by the end of the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said it’s “possible” that Ladd McConkey (foot) is “working back in this week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey was active last week but an emergency-only player and played zero snaps. With the Chargers having a Week 7 bye, we’d be surprised if they pushed McConkey to play unless they really needed him. Unfortunately, since he was already active last week, we know that they may really need him. His status is up in the air ahead of Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Efton Chism caught 5-of-5 targets for 37 yards and one fumble lost in the Patriots’ Week 8 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Chism drew the start opposite Kyle Williams in the Patriots’ victory over the Dolphins. Dolphins LB Jacob Rodriguez punched the ball out of Chism’s possession on the wide receiver’s first catch, during the Patriots’ second drive, but the wide receiver corps’ short-staffed state meant coach Mike Vrabel could not bench him. Chism chipped in three catches on the Patriots’ touchdown-scoring eighth drive, including a clutch eight-yard catch on 1st-and-goal from the Dolphins’ 15-yard line that helped set up Drake Maye’s end zone plunge. Chism will be FLEX against the Packers next week if A.J. Brown (knee) remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Efton Chism was held without a catch in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Coming off a two-game stretch where he surprisingly popped up for 99 combined yards, Chism was held under two receptions for third time in five 2026 appearances. This, as A.J. Brown returned to the lineup. Romeo Doubs (shoulder) did depart, but Chism is never going to have the advantage on Pop Douglas for slot/short-area looks. He is not a realistic consideration in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Efton Chism caught 5-of-6 targets for 57 yards in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Chism came down with some big catches to keep the chains moving. He seems to have earned the trust of the Patriots coaching staff and Drake Maye in recent weeks. Even so, his route participation has been limited and his role could shrink next week if A.J. Brown returns from his high ankle injury. For now he’s an OK stash in deeper fantasy leagues in case he carves out a bigger role in the rejuvenated New England passing offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Efton Chism III caught 2-of-4 targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 4 win over the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Chism III’s touchdown was a spectacular diving one-handed touch in tight coverage that gave the Patriots a late lead over the Bills. It was an unreal grab on a third-down play in the biggest moment of the game. His only other catch was also on a third-and-long to keep a drive alive. With Mack Hollins (calf) leaving this game early, Chishm III played on 30 of the team’s 70 snaps and ran a route on 18 of their 43 dropbacks. The 24-year-old came into today with just five career catches, but he could be in for a bigger role in Week 5. He is still not a priority add in fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots declared WR Efton Chism, CB Kobee Minor, OLB Bradyn Swinson, OT Marcus Bryant, G Caedan Wallace, TE C.J. Dippre and QB Tommy DeVito inactive for Super Bowl LX against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Chism, an undrafted free agent rookie, was active in the Divisional Round and Wild Card Round but did not play in the AFC Championship Game. He caught 3-of-3 targets for 75 yards and one touchdown in the regular season and caught his lone postseason target for a 20-yard gain. DeVito will serve as the Patriots’ emergency third quarterback today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Drake Maye completed 17-of-29 targets for 268 yards, one touchdown, one interception and lost one fumble in the Patriots’ 16-3, Wild Card win over the Chargers, rushing 10 times for 66 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Maye led the team in rushing, but he got the most out of RB Rhamondre Stevenson, efficiently linking up with him three times via the passing game for 75 yards. Maye was nearly on the receiving end of an explosive pass play, but rookie WR Efton Chism overthrew him, wide open, running down the right sideline. Chism made up for it with a 20-yard reception. Maye’s 37-yard scramble on the Patriots’ final drive before halftime was the longest rush of the game. He connected with TE Hunter Henry for a 28-yard, third-quarter touchdown against Chargers S Derwin James. The Patriots face the winner of the Texans-Steelers game tomorrow night. Maye’s elite fantasy upside remains intact no matter the opponent, though the Steelers field a far more fantasy-friendly defense than the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Efton Chism caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 17 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Chism hasn’t played much this year after surprisingly making the Pats’ roster after a strong training camp. New England was without Kayshon Boutte and Mack Hollins this week, giving Chism an opening. He took the opportunity and ran with it, pulling in his first grab of the day for 30 yards and his second for a 10-yard score. Boutte should be back next week, meaning Chism isn’t guaranteed a spot on the gameday roster for Week 18. Still, his Week 17 spike should earn him more playing time in the long run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said DeMario Douglas (hamstring) is questionable for New England’s Week 17 game against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: If Douglas doesn’t play, New England’s only three healthy wideouts on the roster will be Stefon Diggs, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism. Chism would fit best in the slot, so he may get a chance to have a moment against the Jets if Douglas is ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots declared QB Tommy DeVito, LB Robert Spillane, OT Marcus Bryant, TE CJ Dippre, and WR Efton Chism inactive for Week 16 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: All of Carlton Davis, Marcus Jones, Harold Landry, and Christian Barmore are active for the Patriots after coming into the weekend listed as questionable. Tommy DeVito will continue to serve as the emergency quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots declared WR/KR Efton Chism III, OLB Bradyn Swinson, TE C.J. Dippre, OT Marcus Bryant, DT Eric Gregory, and QB Tommy DeVito inactive for Week 15 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: No real surprises here. The Patriots come into this game relatively healthy, except for defensive tackle Milton Williams being on the IR.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Noah Gray caught both of his targets for 15 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray extended his streak of catching at least two (but no more than three) passes to five games. He also got in the end zone for the first time this year on a four-yard strike from Patrick Mahomes. Gray is a solid real-life tight end, but his role is too limited to be worth a look, even in deep fantasy leagues. He is not on the fantasy radar headed into Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Noah Gray caught all three targets for 44 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 7 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: The fact that the team’s top two tight ends tied for the most production through the air at a modest 44 yards tells the story of how the game went against the Seahawks, who limited the Chiefs to just 213 yards of total offense. The absences of the team’s top two receivers continue to place stress on an offense with no true vertical threat, although their primary downfield option was lost for the season prior to their bye. Gray remains unlikely to return weekly fantasy value for as long as Kelce remains healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Noah Gray caught all three of his targets for 53 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: The Chiefs used more two tight end sets with Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton sidelined. Gray ran a route on around half of KC’s drop backs and matched Travis Kelce with 53 yards. If Kelce struggles to play through the ankle injury he picked up against the Bolts, Gray could step in as the team’s TE1 in Week 7 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Noah Gray caught 3-of-5 targets for 30 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 18 loss against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray led the Chiefs in targets for 30 receiving yards in another miserable offensive outing for the Mahomes-less KC offense. It was a season-best game for Gray, who once again played behind Travis Kelce and had just five games with more than 20 receiving yards. He had 21 receptions for 178 yards in 2025. Gray, 26, is signed through the 2027 season and could have an increased role in the team’s passing offense if Kelce retires this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Noah Gray (concussion/shoulder) practiced in full on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray missed last week’s game with the concussion. The shoulder issue is a new addition to his practice report, though a full practice means it won’t stop him from suiting up this week. Gray isn’t on the fantasy radar for Week 14 but does bring plenty to the table as an extra blocker and a backup tight end for the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Chiefs TE Noah Gray (concussion) has been ruled out for Week 13 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray sustained a head injury last week against the Colts and entered the league’s concussion protocol. He won’t suit up on a short week. It could mean a slight target bump for TE Travis Kelce. Gray had five receptions on seven targets over his past two games as a rotational tight end in the KC offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Chiefs TE Noah Gray (concussion) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray has slowly seen his role in the passing game grow over the past month, accumulating 12 targets in Kansas City’s last four games. It looks very unlikely he’ll be up for Thursday’s game against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Noah Gray caught a two-yard pass in the Chiefs’ Super Bowl LIX loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray’s short grab was his lone target in a blowout loss. Coming off back-to-back solid seasons as the Chiefs’ No. 2 seam stretcher, Gray signed a new three-year deal on the eve of Week 1 and proceeded to post a career-best slash of 40/437/5 as Travis Kelce continued to decline. Gray’s five scores tied for ninth amongst tight ends, though his modest eight red zone targets suggest that number was a fluke. It was still an encouraging campaign for the 25-year-old with Kelce looking like a retirement candidate. Were that to transpire, Gray would suddenly be in the lower-end TE1 mix for a Chiefs skill corps that remains undermanned despite its continued Super Bowl appearances.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Noah Gray caught 1-of-1 targets for one yard and rushed once for negative-four yards in the Chiefs’ Week 18 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray logged just four total snaps in this one, indicating the Chiefs value him as a capable passing-game contributor. Most skill position starters rested in this one though some, like Gray, remained active in a reserve capacity. Gray could be an interesting leverage option in playoff DFS tournaments.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Chiefs declared Travis Kelce inactive for Week 18 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: The Chiefs listed numerous healthy, core players as doubtful to play this week with Kelce of course among them. His deactivation was fully expected. Backup tight end Noah Gray is an intriguing, if volatile, dart throw. The fourth-year veteran is having a career-best season and the Chiefs could use the opportunity to see what they have in Gray for the long-term. It is possible Andy Reid already views Gray as an important passing-game contributor though so he may have a limited role, with the playoffs in mind.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 3-of-3 targets for 76 yards and one touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 8 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: The Patriots rolled with 12 personnel on their first play from scrimmage, so Douglas began his day on the sideline. Hunter Henry suffered an apparent foot injury early on, which likely afforded Douglas extra snaps via 11 personnel. He made his opportunities count. Douglas critically picked up a first down, powering through contact on 4th-and-2 on the Patriots’ eighth drive. He showed up again on the Patriots’ ninth drive, securing a play-action pass along the right sideline before juking a Dolphins safety and slipping a shoestring tackle attempt from JuJu Brents before racing into the end zone for a 48-yard touchdown. Douglas is a FLEX option against the Patriots next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 3-of-4 targets for 23 yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: The magic of the previous two games quickly evaporated for the diminutive slot receiver as Hunter Henry and Rhamondre Stevenson stepped into the primary security blanket role for Drake Maye, the latter of whom faced consistent pressure from the aggressive Dennis Allen Bears defense. Starting Douglas on a weekly basis is akin to reaching your hand into a brown paper bag found on the side of the road. It feels exhilarating at the time but you never know what you’re going to get.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 7-of-8 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets, also losing a fumble.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Douglas followed up his best game of the season with another best game of the season, as well as the third most receiving yards of his career. His touchdown was a nine-yarder in the second quarter where the Jets’ defense simply afforded Drake Maye too much time. Things could not have been going better for “Pop” until his fourth quarter fumble at the end of a 39-yard catch-and-run. He was the victim of a classic “Peanut punch” from behind. Rather ominously, he was not targeted thereafter, though the Patriots were also in ball-control mode as they worked on draining the clock. That today’s effort came as A.J. Brown was returning from a five-week absence was promising, but the reality is that Douglas’ big box scores are likely to remain pop-up efforts rather predictable and/or weekly occurrences. He’s a shaky WR4 even with byes and injuries in full swing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 4-of-5 targets for 65 yards and two touchdowns in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Douglas had his first two touchdown grabs of the season as Drake Maye sliced and diced a lifeless Vegas defense from start to finish. Douglas was wide open standing in the end zone by himself for his first score, and broke out of a bunch formation inside the ten yard line for his second score. Douglas has run significant routes in the New England offense since A.J. Brown (ankle) went down to injury. When Brown returns — perhaps this week — Douglas will take on a smaller role in the Pats pass game. He should remain on waiver wires in most formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 1-of-5 targets for 38 yards in the Patriots’ Week 3 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Douglas was second on the team in targets behind only Mack Hollins, who saw nine looks from Drake Maye. Douglas got open and made a nice grab for his 38-yard gain — one of the only big plays for the struggling New England offense on Sunday. Though Douglas is playing a decent snap share, he should remain on waivers in most formats ahead of the Patriots’ Week 4 game against Buffalo.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports A.J. Brown (ankle) is expected to miss 6-8 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Schefter and other reporters previously called it a 4-6 week injury, which now seems unlikely. Schefter did add that Brown is moving “pretty well” and could come back on the faster side of his updated timeline. Still, it looks like Brown will miss at least half of the regular season. Romeo Doubs will operate as the team’s No. 1 receiver until he returns, though it will likely be a group effort to replace Browns’ production. Mack Hollins and Demario Douglas will also be more involved.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Patriots’ Week 2 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Douglas made the first catch of the game for the Patriots, but was silent the rest of the day. The 25-year-old is a low-yardage slot receiver who tends to get schemed targets when he is on the field. Douglas tallied the third-most snaps of all Patriots wide receivers on the day but will find it hard to achieve fantasy relevancy in an offense that utilizes multiple receivers in several different ways. Second-year receiver Kyle Williams also saw a pair of targets, catching one for 10 yards. Neither Williams or Douglas are anything more than deep league dart throws for Week 3 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the “preliminary diagnosis” for A.J. Brown is a high-ankle sprain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Garafolo added, “MRI today after X-rays were negative.” That’s a good sign, but there is currently no timeline for Brown’s return. It will ultimately be a multi-week injury that could linger well into the season. Demario Douglas led the Pats with seven targets last night, though his looks are generally low-value check-downs. Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs will serve as the team’s primary outside receivers until Brown is healthy. Hollins led the Pats in receiving yards at a modest 51. Hollins is worth adding in deeper leagues, but it’s hard to imagine him putting up anything more than WR4 numbers while Brown is sidelined. Doubs should improve in Week 2 after failing to catch any of his three targets versus the Seahawks. He will get another shot at WR3 numbers against Pittsburgh next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: Demario Douglas caught 5-of-7 targets for 20 yards in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Seattle shut down the Patriots’ deep passing game, forcing Drake Maye to pepper Douglas with low-value check-downs. Douglas wound up leading the Pats in targets and catches. He finished fifth in receiving yards. With A.J. Brown banged up, Douglas could be in line for another smattering of targets next week versus the Steelers. Even with Brown out, Douglas would barely register as a PPR WR5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: A.J. Brown suffered an ankle injury in Week 1 against the Seahawks and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: A Seattle defender landed on Brown’s leg in the third quarter and the former Eagle clutched at his ankle as soon as he hit the ground. Brown eventually made his way off the field and limped to the locker room. He was listed as questionable for roughly a quarter, but the team has now ruled him out. The immediate worry will be that Brown suffered a dreaded high ankle sprain. That would sideline him for multiple weeks, though it’s too early to say much about the injury. Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs, and Demario Douglas will all see some extra routes sans Brown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed seven times for 13 yards in the Broncos’ Week 8 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins got the Bronocs’ first touch on offense and immediately took a backseat to Jonah Coleman. The rookie tallied 11 carries and five targets. He also became the first Bronocs running back to hit 100 yards from scrimmage in a game this year. Dobbins was not targeted and was not on the field at the goal line, where Coleman was heavily involved. Coleman ultimately punched in a goal line touchdown for the game-winning score after setting himself up with a 51-yard catch. The short-yardage role used to belong to Dobbins, but the rookie appears to have taken that as well. Without any high-value touches to work with, Dobbins is a between-the-20s grinder averaging a little over three yards per carry this season. He is falling back into the RB4 ranks for his Week 9 date with the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed six times for 23 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 7 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins was the team’s preferred option at the goal line, allowing him to save a bust of a fantasy day with a one-yard score in the second half. He was initially stood up at the goal line but made it in the paint by driving his legs through the contact for six. Dobbins was held under 10 points even with the touchdown. Jonah Coleman returned this week and led the team in carries with nine. Harvey ran the ball just three times. This backfield is a messy, three-man committee and Dobbins doesn’t get to pad the stats with PPR-friendly targets. He will shuffle to the back of the RB3 ranks for his Week 8 date with the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: Broncos designated Jonah Coleman (ankle) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Coleman can return to practice this week and the team now has 21 days to bring him off injured reserve. He could be back on the field as soon as Sunday. With the Broncos’ offense struggling and two backs already seeing work in the backfield, it’s hard to imagine Coleman having much fantasy value in his first game back. He’s worth stashing in deeper leagues, but it might be a while before fantasy managers want him in their lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed 17 times for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins found little room to run on a night the Broncos gained only 168 yards of total offense but handily led the backfield in opportunities in what was a consistently positive game script due to the dominance of their defense. Dobbins has now failed to eclipse a modest 50 yards on the ground in four of five appearances but might be useful as a bye week fill-in when the Broncos travel to Arizona to face the Cardinals in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed 18 times for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins was the most effective offensive player for both teams, which isn’t quite the compliment you’d think it is. The 27-year-old was the bellcow for the Broncos, however, and he was able to keep the chains moving enough to give Denver the victory over the winless Chargers. Dobbins will likely find the sledding tougher in Week 6 when the Broncos face the Seahawks on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: JK Dobbins had 11 rushes for 40 yards in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers, adding two catches for 12 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins, as usual, led the Denver backfield in carries but lost out to RJ Harvey on pass routes and targets. In fact, Harvey led the Broncos with ten catches on ten targets in a check-down heavy game plan for Bo Nix and OC Davis Webb. Dobbins has been touchdown-reliant as the Broncos’ lead back, and sensitive to game script, as we saw in Week 4. Dobbins can be used as a flex next week against a vulnerable Chargers run defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins (hip) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins practiced in full this week, so he should be ready to handle his typical workload against the 49ers this week. The Broncos’ lead rusher has played very unproductively this season, failing to hit 7.0 PPR points each week. The Broncos’ defensive line has been hit hard by injuries. Perhaps Dobbins can steady himself in the RB2/FLEX ranks against them.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins (hip) is practicing in full for Week 4 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: RJ Harvey was checked for a concussion in Week 3 and is not on the injury report today, meaning both backs are good to go for Week 4. Dobbins saw 17 carries versus the Rams compared to just two for Harvey, though the latter caught six passes. Dobbins caught one pass. The rushing advantage will keep Dobbins in the RB3 mix for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed 17 times for 49 yards in the Broncos’ Week 3 win over the Rams, adding four yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: Dobbins and the rest of the Denver offense have been subject to poor situational tendencies from first-time play caller Davis Webb’s offense through three weeks. Dobbins is the player arguably hit the hardest with poor play sequencing as the bulk of his work comes on early downs. Even so, Dobbins now has a higher share of the backfield opportunities following the placement of Jonah Coleman on IR Saturday. Dobbins is a shaky RB3 ahead of a Week 4 showdown with the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.headline: J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) is not on Denver’s final Week 3 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/j-k-dobbin.analysis: He’ll form a committee with RJ Harvey, who was also cleared for Week 3, against the Rams. Dobbins is a low-end RB2 at best in this role against a tough Los Angeles defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Kyle Williams caught 1-of-1 targets for 43 yards and one touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 8 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Good things happen when the Patriots get Williams involved downfield. He only caught one pass, but he made it count. Williams got open on a post route way downfield and was able to haul in the well-aimed pass from Drake Maye for a 43-yard score. The play was initially ruled incomplete because Williams accidentally kneed the ball out of his own possession as he entered the end zone, but coach Mike Vrabel smartly challenged the ruling of the play and won. Williams indeed crossed the plane before losing control of the ball. Williams’ workloads are frustratingly unreliable. He’s a boom-bust FLEX next week against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Kyle Williams caught a 12-yard pass in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Romeo Doubs departed early in the proceedings with a shoulder injury, but Williams was still held under two receptions for the fifth time in six appearances. We know Williams can pop up for big plays like a northeastern Isaac TeSlaa, but the Patriots’ coaching staff doesn’t trust him for anything else. He’s off the radar in all but the deepest of formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Kyle Williams caught all three of his targets for 91 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams caught a beautifully thrown 49-yard score from Drake Maye, who had four touchdown passes to go along with 376 yards through the air in the blowout victory. Williams ran a route on 19 of the team’s 42 drop backs with Mack Hollins on injured reserve. He also came down with a long grab in the second half that put the Pats in position to take a four-score lead. A.J. Brown’s eventual return to the New England offense — as soon as this week against the Jets — will further limit Williams’ snaps and routes. He won’t be playable in most formats going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Kyle Williams caught his lone target for 34 yards in the Patriots’ Week 3 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams logged a pass route on 16 of the Patriots’ 29 drop backs on the day and had one of the longest plays of the game for a struggling New England passing attack. Williams will need more playing time if he’s going to be viable for fantasy purposes. For now Mack Hollins appears to be the top wideout in the Patriots offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Patriots’ Week 2 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Douglas made the first catch of the game for the Patriots, but was silent the rest of the day. The 25-year-old is a low-yardage slot receiver who tends to get schemed targets when he is on the field. Douglas tallied the third-most snaps of all Patriots wide receivers on the day but will find it hard to achieve fantasy relevancy in an offense that utilizes multiple receivers in several different ways. Second-year receiver Kyle Williams also saw a pair of targets, catching one for 10 yards. Neither Williams or Douglas are anything more than deep league dart throws for Week 3 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: The Athletic’s Chad Graff believes getting WR Kyle Williams more involved will help the Patriots generate explosive plays.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The issue is that Williams “didn’t display much craftiness in his route running during training camp this summer.” He ended up “buried on the depth chart” and played just 12 snaps in the opener. Still, Graff notes, Williams has shown an ability to “release off the line of scrimmage with ease, and run straight, deep routes for big completions.” Getting Williams more involved makes sense, but the Patriots have been reluctant to do so thus far in his career. He can be stashed on deep-leagues benches for a week or so, but positive results are not guaranteed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots WR Kyle Williams caught 2-of-2 targets for 55 yards and one touchdown in Thursday’s preseason game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This is the performance Williams needed to have following WR Kayshon Boutte’s trade to the Texans. The Patriots still have a crowded wide receiver room, but at least one competitor has been removed from the equation. Williams delivered a 10-yard catch on a curl route on the Patriots’ third play from scrimmage. Three plays later, he shook his defender at the line of scrimmage and took off down the left sideline. He hauled in the pass from QB Tommy DeVito in stride and waltzed into the end zone for a 45-yard score. Williams does not yet need to be drafted in 12-team leagues, vying for the third wide receiver spot on the Patriots’ depth chart. He could be a worthwhile waiver wire add early on, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: The Athletic’s Chad Graff believes Kyle Williams is “going to have a role” in the Patriots’ offense this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It’s hard to imagine Williams having a fantasy-relevant role given the fact that the Patriots went out and added A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs this offseason, but Graff believes the second-year receiver will have some sort of role in the offense this season. As a rookie, Williams caught 10 passes for 209 yards and three touchdowns, and he went for 2-37-1 on three targets in last week’s preseason game against the Colts. Williams’ role in the offense could be worth monitoring in-season, but there’s no reason to rush to add him to your draft day plans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots WR Kyle Williams hopes to improve his play over the middle of the field this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams also focused on building lower-body strength this offseason, adding five to eight pounds in the process. He believes this strength could help him develop as a centerfield target, which is the primary thing to note for fantasy purposes. A 2019 Rotoworld study showed that targets thrown over the middle, 10-plus yards downfield, are more valuable than those thrown along the sideline at an equivalent depth. Williams went 0-for-5 on centerfield targets as a rookie. Improving his play over the middle will help him challenge for a role in the Patriots’ starting three-wide receiver set. Williams also said he hopes to be more consistent, build chemistry with QB Drake Maye and master the playbook this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Kyle Williams caught 1-of-2 targets for seven yards in the Patriots’ Super Bowl LX loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: A third-round rookie hype merchant in an offense many were expecting to be better, Williams ended up struggling to get on the field, catching just two passes across his first nine games. He was more involved down the stretch, but still finished the regular campaign with all of 10 grabs. He turned that limited work into more than 20 yards per catch and three touchdowns, but Williams was a strict role player in an offense that has fellow field-stretchers Mack Hollins and Kayshon Boutte. With both those wideouts likely back for 2026, Williams could have a difficult time commanding a bigger role. He turns 24 in November, making him a lower-upside hold in dynasty leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Harrison Butker converted 1-of-2 field goal attempts in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: Butker missed a 54-yard field goal late in the fourth quarter. It would have made the game a one-point deficit instead of four for the Chiefs’ final drive. Kansas City was ultimately rebuffed at the goal line and lost the game. Having missed a field goal in all but one game this year, we suspect Andy Reid will throw in the towel on Butker after today’s performance. Justin Tucker, recently signed to the Chiefs’ practice squad, will likely get called up for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Chiefs special teams coach Dave Toub said Harrison Butker is “our kicker.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: “He went 10-for-10 yesterday, with Justin Tucker right there. ... We’re going to keep working it,” Toub continued. It sounds like despite signing Tucker, Butker will continue to kick for the Chiefs. At least this week, anyway.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Chiefs signed Justin Tucker, formerly of the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: Tucker will start on the Chiefs practice squad. His signing comes a few days after Harrison Butker missed two field goal attempts against the Seahawks. On the season Butker has missed five of his 16 attempts, and over his past 11 games he’s missed seven kicks. Tucker, who recently competed for the Dolphins kicker job, hasn’t kicked since 2024 in Baltimore, when he missed eight of his 30 field goal tries. The Ravens released Tucker in 2025 after 16 massage therapists accused him of sexual misconduct.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Harrison Butker converted both of his field goal attempts in the Chiefs’ Week 15 loss against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: Butker bounced back from his Week 14 miss against the Texans in a close loss. He’s missed just four of his 28 field goal attempts through Week 15. Butker’s fantasy prospects might be affected by Patrick Mahomes’ potential absence after Mahomes went down with a knee injury near the end of KC’s loss to the Bolts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Harrison Butker went 1-for-2 in field goal attempts in the Chiefs’ Week 14 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: He connected from 36 yards and made his only point after attempt, missing from 43 yards at the end of the second quarter when his kick hit off the right upright. That missed field goal contributed to the Chiefs being shut out in the first half for only the third time in quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ career, making the failed conversion slightly more meaningful.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Chiefs activated K Harrison Butker from injured reserve ahead of Week 15’s matchup with the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: Matthew Wright was waived in a corresponding move. The Chiefs designated Butker, who missed a month with a knee injury, to return from injured reserve earlier this week and deemed him good to go after logging three limited practices. He has plenty of time to shake off the rust before the playoffs, but may be difficult to trust in his first game back in the fantasy playoffs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Harrison Butker (knee) is questionable for Week 15 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: Butker practiced in a limited capacity all week, logging his first practice repetitions since undergoing a mid-season meniscus trim in his left knee. Given the Chiefs’ Super Bowl aspirations, the team is unlikely to let him suit up this week if his re-injury risk is significant. If he plays, it stands to reason that he is good to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Chiefs designated Harrison Butker (knee) for return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: Butker underwent a meniscus trim on his left knee in November, as he was sent to injured reserve. The talented kicker could play as early as Week 15, however, he understandably makes for a slightly less certain K1 than fantasy managers are used to. It would be unsurprising to see him turn in an up-and-down performance in his first game back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Chiefs K Matthew Wright will start in Week 14.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: The journeyman kicker made four of his five field goal tries last week in a win against the Raiders and will get at least one more start before Harrison Butker returns from a knee injury that landed him on injured reserve. The Chiefs put K Spencer Shrader on IR this week. Wright is a solid fantasy option with the Chiefs sporting an implied Vegas total of 23.5 points against LA.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.headline: Chiefs placed K Harrison Butker (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/harrison-b.analysis: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero was the first on the scene, reporting that Butker is expected to miss 3-4 weeks due to a meniscus injury in his left knee — which is his non-kicking knee. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport later reported that Butker is expected to have surgery to trim his meniscus, which is why the team went ahead and placed him on injured reserve. In a corresponding move, the Chiefs have already signed kicker Spencer Shrader off the Jets practice squad. Shrader is a rookie who went undrafted out of Notre Dame earlier this year. During his five years of college, he converted on 43-of-62 field goals while making 98.7 percent of his extra point attempts. He’ll now be tasked with replacing one of the most reliable kickers in the league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Jonah Coleman rushed 11 times for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 8 win over the Chiefs, adding four catches for 63 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman out-carried Dobbins 11-7 and was the only Broncos running back to earn a target, of which he saw five. Most importantly, Coleman was on the field for goal line duties, and he cashed in with a touchdown late in the fourth quarter. Though he only averaged 3.7 yards per carry, Coleman was a handful for Chiefs defenders to bring down, routinely creating missed tackles while racking up yards after contact. Coleman’s best rep of the day was a 51-yard catch-and-run to set up his touchdown on the next play. Coleman saw all of the high-value touches in the backfield while leading the way in carries and targets. The takeover is all but complete, putting Coleman in the RB2 ranks for Week 9 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: RJ Harvey (knee) was ruled out for Week 8 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Harvey was added to the injury report Thursday with a knee injury before being unable to practice Friday, ultimately ruled out for the team’s divisional clash against the Chiefs. Expect Jonah Coleman to serve as the primary rusher in addition to the possibility he sees his pass game involvement tick up in the absences of both Harvey and Tyler Badie, the latter of whom is on injured reserve. The increase in opportunity is enough to vault Coleman into viable FLEX territory for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Broncos coach Sean Payton, asked about Jonah Coleman, said touches were “something you earn and he’s done a good job of that.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: He also noted that Coleman’s touches were explosive. It’s hard to sit here with much certainty about what looks to be a three-headed Broncos running back room where every back has their niche, but Coleman probably enters Week 8 as the favorite of the three to crack 10 touches. Payton added, for the 17th time since he became Broncos coach, that he needed to get more touches for Marvin Mims on offense. We’ll believe that when we see it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Jonah Coleman rushed nine times for 54 yards in the Broncos’ Week 7 win over the Cardinals, adding two catches for 15 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman returned to action after missing a month because of an ankle injury. He was immediately in the mix for touches and saw three opportunities before RJ Harvey got his first look. Coleman went on to lead the Broncos in carries. Both he and Harvey earned two targets apiece. Unfortunately for Coleman, he was the only Denver back who didn’t find the end zone in Week 7. Coleman has made a mess of a backfield that had just begun to stabilize. Now all three Denver backs will be low-end FLEX options for Week 8 versus the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Jonah Coleman (ankle) is active for Week 7 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper is also active. Coleman hasn’t played since Week 2, when he turned 10 carries into 39 yards and a score. The Broncos were banged up at running back that week. They have since established a stable two-man rotation with JK Dobbins operating between the tackles and RJ Harvey handling passing downs. Coleman will likely take a backseat to those two this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Broncos activated Jonah Coleman (ankle) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman missed the minimum four games as he tended to an ankle injury suffered in Week 2. He led the team in snaps in that contest and could return to the primary rushing role considering the inefficient play of J.K. Dobbins in his absence, making him worthy of a start in fantasy circles in a plus matchup against the Cardinals in his first game back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Jonah Coleman (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman practiced in full all week, but the Broncos could technically give him another week to rehab the ankle. If active, there are too many unknowns regarding Coleman’s potential workload to start him in the FLEX, but he must be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Jonah Coleman (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman is trending toward returning for the Broncos’ Week 7 game against the Cardinals. His teammate, RB Tyler Badie (thumb), remains sidelined. Coleman makes for a risky start if active, but the Broncos’ coaching staff likes him. He should be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Broncos designated Jonah Coleman (ankle) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman can return to practice this week and the team now has 21 days to bring him off injured reserve. He could be back on the field as soon as Sunday. With the Broncos’ offense struggling and two backs already seeing work in the backfield, it’s hard to imagine Coleman having much fantasy value in his first game back. He’s worth stashing in deeper leagues, but it might be a while before fantasy managers want him in their lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Broncos placed RB Jonah Coleman (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: That escalated quickly. Coleman was potentially in line to serve as the starter in Week 3 with both J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey nursing various injuries. Coleman missed practice throughout the week with an ankle injury that wasn’t revealed until Wednesday’s practice report, with the injury now taking the next four games, at minimum, from the talented rookie. Both Harvey and Dobbins have been cleared to play in Week 3, forming a backfield tandem in the wake of Coleman’s injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 16-of-20 passes for 199 yards and two touchdowns in the Patriots’ 24-19, Week 8 win over the Dolphins, adding eight rushes for five yards and one touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye’s two-yard touchdown run was a thing of beauty. The Patriots quarterback took off to the right side of the field, faking a pitch to Rhamondre Stevenson, which caused a Dolphins defender to fully bite on it, running right past Maye while the Patriots’ quarterback darted into the end zone. Maye’s first touchdown pass was thrown to Kyle Williams on a post route. It was well-placed, allowing Williams to secure the ball in stride just before entering the end zone. Maye later linked up with DeMario Douglas via play action for his second score. The Patriots’ quarterback is a QB1 against the Packers next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 24-of-31 passes for 321 yards, two touchdown, and one interception in the Patriots’ 30-24, Week 7 loss to the Bears, adding 26 yards and a touchdown on four carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye and the Patriots struggled to tame an unrelenting Chicago pass rush and were unable to move the football on the ground effectively, two cariables that led to an early deficit against the Bears. Their first half possessions went turnover on downs, three-and-out, three-and-out, touchdown, interception before a wild series to end the second quarter. Caleb Williams led a touchdown drive that left only 14 seconds on the clock. After an 18-yard completion to A.J. Brown, just three seconds remained with the ball near midfield. That’s when Maye dumped the ball off to Rhamondre Stevenson in the flat underneath deep prevent coverage, and Stevenson did the rest on a touchdown that never should have happened to bring the game to a one-possession game. Maye’s other touchdown toss was a beautiful bread-basket throw to rookie tight end Eli Raridon up the seam, adding a score on a grit-play rushing touchdown early in the second quarter. It goes down as Maye’s fourth consecutive QB1 fantasy performance after starting the season leading the league in turnovers through three weeks. The 4-3 Patriots get a mini-bye ahead of a divisional meeting against the Dolphins in Week 8, where Maye will remain an upside QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 18-of-32 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns in the Patriots’ 26-19, Week 6 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye added four carries for 24 yards rushing. The three-score passing effort was his third in as many weeks, while he is now up to 11 total touchdowns during his three-game hot streak. Good stuff, though it could have been much better. Maye lost No. 2 receiver Romeo Doubs to an early shoulder injury after he housed a 42-yard touchdown, while returning “No. 1" A.J. Brown had a nightmarish day with 4-5 drops, including several long gains and a potential score or two. Pop Douglas also lost a fumble at the end of a long catch-and-run. Unfortunate, but Maye is at least playing well enough again that those miscues merely held back his final box score instead of ruining it. He now has a likely short-week shootout in Thursday’s Bears road tilt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 26-of-34 attempts for 374 yards and four touchdowns in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders, adding seven rushes for 25 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye had all day to operate in the pocket against a Raiders front seven that entered Week 5 with the league’s ninth highest pressure rate and fourth highest quick pressure rate. He attacked the Vegas secondary downfield from start to finish, hitting Kyle Williams and Pop Douglas for long touchdowns, and Williams for another long gain that put the Pats inside the five yard line. Maye’s rushing score came on a green scramble in the third quarter. Fully emerged from his early-season struggles, Maye is once again carving up opposing coverage units and causing fits with his scrambling ability. Maye, with eight total touchdowns over his past two outings, should be locked into lineups next week against a middling Jets secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 22-of-37 passes for 269 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception in a 29-26, Week 4 win over the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye also added 53 yards rushing on eight carries. This was easily the best game of Maye’s season. The Bills had pressure in his face often, but Maye was frequently able to evade pass rushers and pick up chunk gains with his legs. When he did have time to throw, he ripped off big passes downfield and could have even had a bigger day after a potential 40+ yard pass slipped through Romeo Doubs’ hands in the fourth quarter. Maye did wince and grab his right shoulder on one hit, so that will be something to watch during practice this week, but we don’t expect him to miss any time. The bad news is that Maye figures to be without Mack Hollins (calf) in Week 5, and A.J. Brown (ankle) is not yet ready to return, so Maye will play with limited options next week against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Bills declared CB Christian Benford, WR Skyler Bell, OL Jude Bowry, OL Ar’maj Reed-Adams, DL T.J. Sanders, OLB Mike Danna, and S Jalon Kilgore inactive for Week 4 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: No real surprises here. Benford was listed as questionable heading into the day, but he didn’t practice at all this week so he was never likely to play. Rookie Davison Igbinosun is likely to step into his spot opposite Maxwell Hairston, which makes the Bills young and inexperienced on the boundary. Perhaps Drake Maye could finally take advantage of that on the way to his first truly good fantasy game of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye (right shoulder) is practicing in full for Week 4 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: We are happy to see that the Patriots’ quarterback is practicing fully, but this is a new injury for Maye. He notably dealt with a throwing shoulder injury during the Patriots’ playoff run last season. His listing raises questions as to whether there might be a lingering issue. We expect a follow-up report on this in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: The Athletic’s Chad Graff believes Drake Maye’s confidence is “shot.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye, after another meltdown in Week 3 against the Jaguars, has now posted a negative drop back EPA in six dtraight outings dating back to last season. Against Jacksonville on Sunday he posted a meager 40 percent drop back success rate, the fifth lowest of the week. “What’s fallen apart with Maye looks like it’s between the ears as much as anything physical,” Graff said. “He looks like a quarterback whose confidence is shot.” Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said this week that Maye needs to calm down if things are going to turn around. “We need to stop trying to choke the life out of every single play,” Vrabel said during his Monday radio appearance. “We need to relax.” Maye through Week 3 ranks 32nd in fantasy points per drop back, below the likes of Daniel Jones and Cam Ward. It will be tough to start Maye in Week 4 against Buffalo if there are other viable QB options on the waiver wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 14-of-29 attempts for 199 yards and two interceptions in the Patriots’ Week 3 loss to the Jaguars, adding four rushes for 18 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: He fumbled twice, losing one to the Jags defense. Maye was under duress and missing routine throws for most of this game. He also had a long touchdown throw and a rushing touchdown called back on penalties. Without A.J. Brown (ankle) in the lineup the Patriots have no one to threaten secondaries, allowing opposing defenses to stack the box, shut down the run game, and leave the Pats a one-dimensional offense. Though Maye’s rushing could keep him afloat as a top-12 quarterback in Week 4 against the Bills, he should be considered a shaky option for now. New England’s offensive line might be able to hold up against a Buffalo front seven that has struggled to pressure the passer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 14-of-22 passes for 208 yards and an interception in the Patriots’ 20-3, Week 2 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: It was a defensive slugfest for the Patriots and Steelers in Week 2, with neither team passing for a touchdown on the day. Maye added 17 rushing yards on four carries but took three sacks, including one in the red zone in the second quarter. His interception was a floater in Steelers territory in the third quarter, tossed right to Patrick Queen to end a drive. He ends the day with 44-percent of his passing yards coming on two third-quarter chunk plays to Romeo Doubs. Maye has had a rough start to the season, following up a three-interception Week 1 with a scoreless, one-interception Week 2. He faces another solid defense in the Jaguars for Week 3; Maye’s rushing upside keeps him in the low-end QB1 territory for next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Emmett Johnson caught all five of his targets for 128 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: He added one carry for 15 yards. Johnson racked up the bulk of his production on a 73-yard touchdown grab in the first half. The Broncos sent pressure and Patrick Mahomes perfectly lofted the ball to Johnson, who saw nothing but green grass ahead of him.
