The turf monster nearly took him down at the 10-yard line, but Johnson stayed upright enough and lost one final defender on his way into the end zone. He also picked up a 38-yard catch just before halftime to set up a last-second field goal. Johnson had more than two touches in just one of his previous three games headed into Week 8. Though he’s not going to challenge Kenneth Walker for RB1 duties anytime soon, this breakout performance should earn him a few more touches in Week 9. He will be have some value as a boom/bust FLEX play versus the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Emmett Johnson had three rushes for six yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: It was another Ken Walker explosion game (128 yards, two touchdowns on the ground) with Johnson serving as the breather back. Johnson should be rostered as a high-upside contingency option in case Walker misses any time in the coming weeks or months.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Emmett Johnson rushed six times for 17 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 3 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Johnson was not targeted in the passing game. His six carries were nothing to sneeze at on an afternoon where the Chiefs were limited to 49 total plays, but that was compared to 20 Kenneth Walker touches. Johnson will have some pop-up standalone value behind workhorse Walker, but he is primarily a contingency option heading into the meat of the fantasy campaign.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said RB Emmett Johnson “will continue to get more snaps.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Johnson has turned 14 touches into 103 scrimmage yards thus far. Evidently pleased with his fifth-round rookie, Reid wants to keep “allowing Emmett to grow,” in turn taking “a little bit of load off” starting RB Kenneth Walker. Reid notes that Walker wants the ball on every play and is not asking for a lighter workload, but Reid is seeking “a nice balance with those two in there,” which “keeps them even more fresh as the season goes on.” Walker, of course, remains an elite RB1. Johnson, however, should be rostered in all 12-team leagues as a high-upside bench stash that could return standalone value before long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Chiefs waived RB Emari Demercado.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Demercado’s departure leaves rookie RB Emmett Johnson and second-year RB Brashard Smith to back up starting RB Kenneth Walker. The Chiefs also waived DE Vincent Anthony, LB Kam Arnold, WR Andrew Armstrong, WR Wesley Bissainthe, DT Cole Brevard, WR Jason Brownlee, WR Jacob De Jesus, OT Ethan Driskell, WR Omari Evans, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick, LB Cam Jones, WR Xavier Loyd, S Tanner McCalister, DT Amari McNeill, C Pete Nygra, RB Jaydn Ott, DT Damon Payne, CB D’Arco Perkins-McAllister, TE Mason Pline, S DeShon Singleton, CB Melvin Smith, EDGE Tyreke Smith, OG Josh Thompson, CB Zelmar Vedder, TE Tre Watson and WR Jeff Weimer. The Chiefs released LB Cole Christiansen, CB Kaiir Elam, CB Kader Kohou and EDGE Emmanuel Ogbah. The Chiefs placed DT Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) on the reserve/physically unable to play list and WR Jimmy Holiday on injured reserve. The Chiefs also waived OG C.J. Hanson, QB Chris Oladokun and RB EJ Smith with injury designations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Emmet Johnson rushed seven times for 39 yards in the Chiefs’ preseason game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Johnson added two catches for 15 yards and had another chunk gain through the air called back because of a penalty. Kenneth Walker didn’t play in this contest, allowing Johnson to draw the start with some of KC’s first-team offense on the field. Johnson split reps with Emari Demercado over the team’s first three drives, then left the game for good. He looks like the team’s No. 2 back, though all three backs have been the next man up behind Walker at some point during the preseason. Johnson isn’t guaranteed the backup job, but he’s now the favorite, putting him in the mix as a late-round flyer in deeper fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Emmett Johnson was “one of the positives coming out of” their first preseason game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Johnson had 12 carries for 59 yards and three catches for 10 yards against the Rams. While we’ve seen a little camp buzz about Johnson, The Athletic’s Jesse Newell presents this as a step forward for Johnson who “has been running with the fourth-string offense most of training camp.” He’s still probably the best back to have rostered in the event of a Kenneth Walker injury, but this isn’t such an important role that the backup necessarily needs to be rostered in standard redraft leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that Chiefs RB Emmett Johnson “is swiftly earning a role as an explosive, decisive runner.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Breer refers to RB Kenneth Walker as an “every-down” player, says RB Brashard Smith “has already shown he can be a weapon in space,” and notes RB Emari Demercado adds depth. Perhaps taking on a change-of-pace rushing role is in play for Johnson this season. The rookie back has pass-catching experience as well, but Smith and Demercado could offer more in that department at the moment. Johnson could be the next player up if Walker were to miss time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano believes Emmett Johnson “has a shot” to be Kansas City’s No. 2 back.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: The currently-murky situation behind Kenneth Walker includes the rookie Johnson, veteran receiving back Emari Demercado, and Player Who Is Nominally A Running Back Brashard Smith. The fifth-round pick sure seems like the best play here over the long-term, but if Johnson can win the No. 2 role out of camp, he’d hold some stash fantasy value behind Walker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: A to Z Sports’ Charles Goldman believes Emari Demercado “is closer to RB2 in Kansas City than any other prospect.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Goldman added that the team is “very high” on Demercado before noting his spot as the No. 2 back in every drill of note during OTAs. The Chiefs signed Demercado to a one-year deal this offseason to back up Kenneth Walker. They also added Emmet Johnson in the fifth round of the draft, but it sounds like the veteran has the inside track to backup duties right now. Demercado could also operate as the team’s primary back on passing downs, giving him some extra juice in PPR formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 30-of-41 passes for 321 yards and three touchdowns in the Chiefs’ 28-24, Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes posted a strong box score for fantasy managers and took care of the football with zero turnovers. He also took just two sacks, but the second was one that will haunt Chiefs fans for a while. After marching the offense down to the goal line under the two-minute warning, the Chiefs found themselves on fourth-and-goal. They initially got the score via a strike to Rashee Rice, but the play was blown dead via a false start. The Broncos’ pass-rush got to him on the second try, taking Mahomes down for a game-ending sack. On the whole, it was another dink-and-dunk game plan from Mahomes, who failed to get the deep ball going once again. Luckily for him, Emmet Johnson averaged 25.6 yards per catch and turned a short toss into a 73-yard touchdown in the first half. The Chiefs get a bounce-back spot against the Jets next week in a game where Mahomes will be just inside the QB1 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 19-of-33 passes for 165 yards and one interception in the Chiefs’ 20-3, Week 7 loss to the Seahawks, adding 14 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: The three points tied the fewest scored in a start in Mahomes’ career as the Chiefs suffered their first defeat of the season. Mahomes faced consistent pressure and a shrinking pocket as the Seahawks held the Chiefs to just 213 yards of total offense. Mahomes also had an ill-advised turnover as he tried to escape pressure, over-throwing his intended receiver on the run. The Chiefs fall to 5-1 with the defeat, leaving only the Vikings as the lone unbeaten team through seven weeks. Mahomes gets little time to lick his wounds with the division rival Broncos on the horizon in Week 8, where he’ll be a low end QB1 in another difficult matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 23-of-30 attempts for 272 yards and one interception in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers, adding five rushes for 16 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes had multiple touchdown tosses in every game this season headed into Week 6. Kansas City’s offense didn’t have to do much against a sleepy Chargers offense that could barely move the ball once again on Sunday. The Chiefs leaned on Ken Walker, who went for 128 yards and two touchdowns on the day. With Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton out, Mahomes relied heavily on Xavier Worthy and Travis Kelce. Until Rice is back and fully healthy, Mahomes will be more of a top-15 option. He gets the Seahawks in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 15-of-30 passes for 225 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs’ 30-27, Week 4 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes was under duress throughout this one. He took multiple hits and was sacked twice, but managed to come up with just enough plays to pull off the road win against a spry Raiders team. Mahomes threw his first touchdown of the day in the first quarter, finding Tyquan Thornton for a two-yard score, then connected with Thornton again in the fourth quarter for an eight-yard touchdown near the back of the end zone. Mahomes’ longest play of the game also went to Thornton, when the speedster broke free down the left sideline to make a 55-yard catch. Unfortunately, Thornton exited the game with a gruesome ankle injury after the play, but he did set up Kenneth Walker for a two-yard touchdown run on the ensuing play. Mahomes and the Chiefs are now 4-0 as they enter their Week 5 bye week. They’ll play host to the Chargers, who are 0-4 when they return in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 20-of-24 passes for 246 yards, two touchdowns and an interception in the Chiefs’ 24-10, Week 3 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: With the Dolphins playing ball-control offense, the Chiefs were limited to just 49 total plays, but Mahomes and company compensated with extreme efficiency. That included long catch-and-run gains to Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice, with Mahomes also finding the former for an end zone score. Mahomes has now posted multiple passing scores in each of his first three starts. It took him seven games to accomplish that feat last year. There was a scary moment when Mahomes got “body weighted” by DL Chop Robinson, but Mahomes shook it off as Robinson was flagged for roughing. Currently averaging 8.3 yards per attempt after that number was 7.1 a year ago, Mahomes is looking at home in this “new look” Chiefs attack once again coordinated by Eric Bieniemy. He has another soft Week 4 matchup in the Raiders before the Chiefs head on early-season bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 32-of-47 passes for 382 yards and three touchdowns in the Chiefs’ 33-30, Week 2 win over the Colts, adding 17 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes looked much more like himself against the Colts than he did against the Broncos in Week 1, with his typical mobility in the pocket on full display as he extended plays. He even escaped the pocket twice to pick up crucial first downs with his legs in key situations, looking closer to how he did before tearing his ACL in 2025. Mahomes managed to complete two passes greater than 30 yards, one to Tyquan Thornton and one to Rashee Rice, an area of his game that he has not excelled in over the previous two seasons. Even so, it took the Chiefs two possessions in overtime to finally sneak by the tenacious Colts, moving to a 2-0 record ahead of a road date with the Dolphins in Week 3. Mahomes has returned to weekly QB1 status, although the team could look to continue its dominance on the ground against a week opponent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes ran the ball seven times for 23 yards and one touchdown last week before practicing in full this week. Both factors are encouraging. The Chiefs’ star quarterback warrants QB1 treatment against the Colts in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes (knee) is practicing in full for Week 2 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Rashee Rice (knee) is also practicing in full. Both players underwent offseason knee procedures and had slow ramp-ups during the summer. Both players were active for Week 1 and found the end zone. Mahomes did so on the ground, putting the notion that he would be hampered by the knee issue to rest. The passing attack still looked shaky in Week 1, but there are no health concerns for either player. Mahomes will be a low-end QB1 versus the Colts, and Rice will hold a spot in the WR2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 15-of-27 passes for 184 yards, two touchdowns, and one interceptions in the Chiefs’ 31-10, Week 1 win over the Broncos, adding 23 yards and a touchdown on seven carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: A rushing score on the team’s first possession appeared to calm fantasy owners’ nerves as that was the area of Mahomes’ game most in question coming off the injury, but concerns grew as he completed just two of his first 12 pass attempts in his first start since suffering a torn ACL in 2025. A passing score to Rashee Rice at the end of the first half elevated his counting stats further before a shuttle pass touchdown to Kenneth Walker after the break took him into fantasy QB1 territory. Even so, the outing was far from perfect as Mahomes missed numerous open receivers on his way to a paltry 6.8 yards per pass attempt. Mahomes’ lone interception was a badly overthrown ball on a miscommunication in the third quarter that could have been much more damning had the Kansas City defense not held the Broncos to a field goal on the resulting possession. With games against the Colts, Dolphins, and Raiders on tap the next three weeks, the Chiefs could continue to lean on Walker after the recent addition out-gained the entire Denver offense by himself in Week 1. Mahomes will be difficult to trust until he proves to be more accurate through the air.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes (knee) is practicing in full for Week 1 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Earlier this week, Chiefs coach Andy Reid said there is a “good chance” that Mahomes starts in Week 1. At this point, we would be surprised if he didn’t. The Chiefs’ quarterback is coming off season-ending ACL and LCL tears and will likely scramble less frequently than he did last year, potentially hurting his expected fantasy football output. He is a borderline QB1/2 against the Broncos’ elite defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Willliams had 16 rushes for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers, adding one catch for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: The more efficient Blake Corum had 11 rushes for 73 yards and did not see a target in a run-heavy Rams offense. Williams led the LA backfield in routes but only had one look from Matthew Stafford. He was stuffed at the line of scrimmage a handful of times in the first half. The rushing volume in the Rams offense of late should make both Williams and Coum fantasy relevant every week, including next week against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams had 16 rushes for 99 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders, adding two catches for 22 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: After complaining about the team’s backfield split last week, Williams was out-carried by Blake Corum, 17 to 16, with Corum scoring a touchdown and having two others called back on penalties. Though Williams lost a fumble in the second half, the Rams leaned on him late in the fourth quarter following a short-lived Vegas comeback. He ran 18 pass routes to eight routes for Corum — a season long trend that makes Williams less sensitive to game script than Corum. Williams will be a locked-in top-15 running back option next week against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 10 times for 50 yards in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals, adding three receptions for 17 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams played for the duration of the first and third drives, ceding the second to Blake Corum, who played well right out of the gate. The duo rotated during drives thereafter. Williams looked like his normal, capable self, showcasing a slick spin move off contact on the Rams’ fourth drive. Unfortunately for him, Corum fought hard to convert a first down just inside the red zone and coach Sean McVay kept him out there for the scoring-position sequence, which ended in a 15-yard receiving score for Corum. Williams quietly continued his high-end receiving involvement, earning six targets against the Cardinals today. Williams belongs in the RB1 tier next week against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 16 times for 49 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills, adding 27 yards on six receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams has yet to see more than the 16 carries he saw against the Bills this season but the team’s recent pass-heavy nature has left the veteran lead back with six or more receptions in three straight games, including 27 total targets in that span. The elite-level aerial volume made it three consecutive games with 20 or more opportunities for Williams, who continues to return RB1 fantasy weeks while playing in one of the league’s top offenses. Williams remains a middling RB1 ahead of a Week 6 divisional showdown against the Cardinals at home.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 16 times for 80 yards in the Rams’ Week 4 win over the Eagles, adding 10 receptions for 66 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams’ 10 receptions were a new career high, while his 26 touches were tied for his seventh most. This, as Blake Corum handled the ball only six times. With Matthew Stafford having trouble against a stout Eagles defense in the rain, he focused on Williams checkdowns, and the strategy actually paid off as the Rams erased a 20-10 halftime deficit. Williams now has 47 touches over the past two weeks after that number was 28 for Weeks 1 and 2. With the Rams off to a shaky start, it’s not surprising they’ve started concentrating touches on their most established weapons. Corum is going to hang around as a nuisance, but Williams has returned himself to the low-end RB1 mix ahead of a likely Week 5 shootout with the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams need more from Blake Corum in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Atkins believes Puka Nacua’s (groin) impending return will lighten the box, in turn making life easier on the run game and preventing the opposition from blitzing as frequently as the Broncos did last week. Corum has not established himself as a reliable weekly contributor in fantasy. Perhaps positive impacts from Nacua’s return trickle down to the Rams’ No. 2 running back. Kyren Williams remains a locked-in starter. Keep Corum stashed for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 15 times for 88 yards in the Rams’ Week 3 loss to the Broncos, adding 70 yards on six receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams’ 70 yards through the air were a career-high mark in receiving for a single game, returning yet another RB1 fantasy performance despite sharing backfield work with Blake Corum. Corum managed only 15 yards on six carries and caught two passes for zero additional yards. Furthermore, Corum has still not seen a carry inside the red zone through three games of the 2026 season. Williams remains a surefire RB1 ahead of a difficult matchup against the Eagles in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 12 times for 85 yards in the Rams’ Week 2 win over the Giants, adding 12 yards and a touchdown on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams has opened the season with touchdowns in consecutive games after hitting pay dirt 15 times or more the previous two seasons. The difference this season is that he’s doing it while Blake Corum has been much more involved in the weekly game plan. Williams continues forward with an elevated weekly floor due to his robust red zone role, albeit with a shakier ceiling than in recent years due to the presence of Corum. He remains a back-end RB2 when the Rams travel to Colorado to face the Bronco in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 11 times for 41 yards with a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 1 loss to the 49ers while adding three catches for 24 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams’ day was salvaged with a short-yardage score. He finished with one more rushing attempt than Blake Corum, but Corum did look spryer with 54 yards on those attempts. The Rams’ offense just didn’t have it in the Australian showdown, and Williams should see a better box score in Week 2 against the Giants; even if Corum remains a fantasy adversary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay said Blake Corum will “be a big factor” in the offense this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Corum took a nice leap in his second season as a pro, posting a 145-746-6 rushing line over 17 games while competing with Kyren Williams for touches every step of the way. Like Corum, Williams was also healthy for 17 games, but that didn’t stop Corum from popping up for a few top-24 PPR finishes last season. Corum’s 9.4 opportunities per game weren’t enough to make him a reliable option in start/sit leagues, as he managed only one double-digit PPR performance from Weeks 1-12, but his production could pave the way for a more even split with Williams this season. It may take some time to determine whether or not we can view Corum as a player who has standalone value this season, but he remains one of the best handcuffs in fantasy playing in an elite offense that could feature him in a high-volume role should Williams ever miss time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said OC Mike McDaniel will continue to call plays after the team’s 9-24, Week 8 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: Harbaugh is standing by the organization’s biggest offseason hire. The Chargers at least got a little passing production going today, though obviously the results continue to fall short of expectations. The Chargers, now 0-6, face the Texans, 2-5, in Week 9. Houston’s underperforming defense could give the Chargers a chance to improve their standing next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will continue calling plays.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: McDaniel gets the bye week to recalibrate after six weeks of disgraceful football from his unit, but it’s clear McDaniel’s leash is incredibly short. PFT’s Mike Florio reported a week ago that the Chargers could ultimately replace McDaniel with Adam Gase, who currently holds the title of pass game specialist. They currently rank dead last in points and 28th in yards. If the results are no different versus the Rams this week, McDaniel may be out of a job by Monday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio reports that there is “growing buzz” that the Chargers could fire OC Mike McDaniel “soon,” and potentially replace him with pass game specialist Adam Gase.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: According to Florio, Gase “is expected to take over if McDaniel is fired.” The Chargers go on bye in Week 7, so this is the best time to install a new offense if they really intend to do so. Gase previously served as head coach of the Jets and Dolphins, though those stints are hardly reassuring. His offenses have frequently fallen short of expectations. The 0-6 Chargers are searching for answers, though, and the McDaniel-Justin Herbert pairing does not seem to be working out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: When asked if Chargers OC Mike McDaniel is going to continue calling plays, coach Jim Harbaugh said the team is “going to look at everything.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: Harbaugh made clear that his team has to “address everything,” especially the offense, and acknowledged that the Chargers aren’t scoring enough points. He added that the plan is to watch today’s game tape and “get with our offensive coaches” to figure things out. Although McDaniel could end up losing play-calling duties, Harbaugh owned the team’s offensive woes, saying it “starts” with him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said he doesn’t plan to intervene in the offense if it continues to struggle.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: When asked if he had any plans of intervening, Harbaugh offered his endorsement of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, saying, “No. We trust Mike. We believe in Mike.” The 0-3 Chargers have struggled mightily out of the gate to start the season, failing to score more than 16 points in a game while also turning the ball over six times. Even in a game where the Chargers forced five turnovers off of Josh Allen and the Bills and registered four sacks, they were unable to capitalize on multiple opportunities to take the lead in the 24-16 defeat. We’ll see how long Harbaugh can go continuing to let McDaniel run the show, but it wouldn’t be surprising if the team decided to make a change if things continue in this direction.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: Chargers hired Max McCaffrey as their new running backs coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: McCaffrey is a former undrafted free agent NFL wide receiver who spent time with five different NFL teams. He joined the college coaching ranks as a wide receivers coach at Northern Colorado in 2020. He added offensive coordinator to his title in 2021 and held both roles for two seasons. McCaffrey joined the NFL coaching ranks as a member of former Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel’s coaching staff in 2023, serving as an offensive assistant through the 2025 season. McCaffrey’s new role reunites him with McDaniel, who was hired as the Chargers’ offensive coordinator in January. 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey and Commanders WR Luke McCaffrey are Max’s younger brothers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: Chargers hired former Dolphins HC Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: McDaniel continued to entertain head coaching offers even after it was rumored he would join the Chargers. Now, after much deliberation, McDaniel is officially joining the Chargers to pair with Justin Herbert and company. McDaniel’s offense finished 11th or better in points scored in two of his four seasons with the Dolphins, but his final two seasons proved forgettable as Tua Tagovailoa’s limitations became apparent and defenses took advantage. McDaniel gets a top-flight QB and talent young playmakers in Ladd McConkey and Omarion Hampton to help guide his offense into 2026. All will make for enticing fantasy picks, and Herbert should enjoy a bounce back if his offensive line can stay healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports former Dolphins HC Mike McDaniel is “still in the mix” for the Raiders’ head-coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: According to Rapoport, McDaniel is ultimately expected to take the Chargers’ offensive coordinator role, but until the Raiders officially rule him out as a candidate, he will remain an option for the Silver and Black. McDaniel most recently canceled his interview with the Bills on Friday and withdrew his name for consideration for the Browns before that. McDaniel has made several rounds this coaching cycle to speak with teams, but the Chargers seem like the most likely fit barring a team sweeping in to hand him a head coaching gig.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reports former Dolphins HC Mike McDaniel canceled his interview with the Bills to discuss the team’s head coaching position on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: While the Bills are just beginning their search for a new head coach after dismissing Sean McDermott earlier this week, McDaniel has already withdrawn his name from the Browns head coaching search and interviewed for multiple offensive coordinator positions before agreeing to sign on with the Chargers. Schultz says McDaniel and the Bills remain in contact for a potential interview, but there’s a “strong possibility” he moves forward with the Chargers. McDaniel’s presence in Los Angeles would be massive as fantasy managers could expect the 42-year-old coach to get the most out of Justin Herbert and the rest of the Chargers’ offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: Bills are expected to interview former Dolphins HC Mike McDaniel for their head-coaching vacancy on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: McDaniel is expected to take the job as the Chargers’ offensive coordinator, but he’ll still take time to speak with the Bills about their head-coaching opening before settling for a coordinator role. McDaniel withdrew his name from the Browns’ head-coaching search earlier this week in favor of the Chargers’ job, but having the chance to lead a team with one of the best quarterbacks in the game in Josh Allen could be too much for McDaniel to pass up should the opportunity present itself. The Bills are early in their head-coaching search and still have other potential suitors to meet over the weekend, but for now, McDaniel is in the mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Puka Nacua caught 11-of-12 targets for 80 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nacua, with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined, again dominated targets in the newly run-heavy LA offense. No other Rams pass catcher saw more than four targets on the day. Nacua’s touchdown came on a well-designed screen in the second half at the end of a long drive for the run-first Rams offense. Nacua, who had 41 targets over his prior four games, is among the safest players in fantasy football. He matches up against the Commanders in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Puka Nacua caught 8-of-10 targets for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders, adding two rushes for ten yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nacua, dealing with a calf injury, didn’t appear to be 100 percent but still got by just fine against a beatable Vegas secondary. He caught one of Matthew Stafford’s three touchdowns and led the Rams offense with ten targets. Nacua has a good chance of leading the NFL in targets for the remainder of the season with Davante Adams (hamstring) out indefinitely. His role in the LA offense makes Nacua one of the most dangerous fantasy options in the game. He gets the Chargers secondary in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Puka Nacua (calf) is active for Week 7 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Start him. The Rams clearly feel comfortable with their superstar playing today, and we should too. Nacua’s upside is too high for him to remain on fantasy football benches. Reporting on Nacua’s ailment suggests he is not necessarily dealing with a strain. It can perhaps be best described as muscle fatigue, though we are doctors here at Rotoworld. Re-injury is possible, but we can safely expect him to handle a large workload whenever he is on the field. Nacua is a high-end WR1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Rams are “confident” Puka Nacua (calf) will play in Week 7 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nacua is going to test out his calf issue in warmups. Rapoport said Nacua isn’t necessarily dealing with a calf strain. He simply didn’t feel he could explode like he needed to. Nacua’s groin injury was described similarly earlier this year. Fantasy managers will want to keep an eye on this injury ahead of kickoff. If Nacua can’t go, Jordan Whittington will take on a larger role in the offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Puka Nacua (calf) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: The fact that Nacua is not practicing today is a bad sign for his Week 7 availability. Ever the injury-related optimist, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported earlier today that Nacua’s injury is “more minor than anything else,” though he quickly balanced the scales by then saying that he would not call Nacua’s quick trip to the imaging room “precautionary, because it’s not nothing.” If active, Nacua should be in fantasy football lineups because his talent and workload are almost unparalleled. Unfortunately, coach Sean McVay told reporters that Nacua felt that “he wasn’t able to have some of the power and full explosion.” Nacua is on the wrong side of questionable, and the Rams obviously do not want his injury to worsen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Puka Nacua’s calf injury is not considered “a significant injury.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: As far as Nacua’s long-term status goes, this sounds like good news overall. However, Rapoport also noted that Nacua’s status for Sunday’s game against the Raiders could be “up in the air.” With Friday’s practice still to go, Nacua’s status will be one to look for later in the day, as will his designation entering the weekend. If he draws a questionable tag, fantasy managers should treat him as a true game-day decision and have a backup plan in place should be unable to play this week. Given the 4:25 PM EST start time for this game, Rams WR Konata Mumpfield could be on a short list of players worth stashing until we know more about Nacua’s availability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Puka Nacua left practice early after suffering a calf injury on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Brutal. The Rams lost Davante Adams to a hamstring tendon rupture in Week 6 against the Cardinals, and now they could be without Nacua in Week 7 against the Raiders. The Rams have handled star-player injuries smartly this season. Consider Nacua highly questionable to play, and seek out a backup plan. Konata Mumpfield would serve as the de facto No. 1 wide receiver if Nacua is unable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Puka Nacua caught 6-of-7 targets for 80 yards in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: The Cardinals’ pass rush derailed the Rams’ offensive game plan early on, and Nacua was held without a target until just under 11 minutes remaining in the second quarter. Heartbreak struck on the Rams’ sixth drive. Nacua shook his coverage defender on a hitch-and-go and had no one between him and the end zone. Matthew Stafford let it rip, but was hit during the throw. Nacua dove for what should have been a 65-yard touchdown, but the pass fell incomplete. Nacua had another close call late in the game, dragging a defender for half of his downfield route, on what was ultimately flagged for DPI, but the defender’s unscrupulous tactic prevented Nacua from hauling in a 45-yarder at the Cardinals’ 10-yard line. Fortunately, Nacua and Stafford linked up for 42- and 16-yard gains on their lone touchdown-scoring drive at the end of the game, salvaging Nacua’s box score. He’s an elite WR1 against the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Puka Nacua caught 17-of-24 targets for 138 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills, adding nine yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nacua operated as the primary option through the air for a Rams team that attempted more than 50 passes for the third straight game. The veteran alpha was mostly confined to short-area work, something that could be attributed to the groin injury that continues to have his name on the injury report in practice, but that would not keep Nacua from returning another elite WR1 performance. Nacua was also inches away from padding his stat line further after failing to come down with what would have been a 51-yard touchdown reception on the final play of the first half. Nacua and the Rams fall to 2-3 ahead of a Week 6 divisional showdown against the Cardinals, where he will remain one of the top fantasy assets in the league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Puka Nacua caught 9-of-12 targets for 125 yards in the Rams’ Week 4 win over the Eagles, adding a two-yard rushing touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nacua’s rushing score came on a second quarter end-around. Out there for the first time since Week 1, Nacua did what he always seems to do when active and post a dominant statline. We say “active” rather than “healthy,” as FOX’s Erin Andrews confirmed during the broadcast Nacua is dealing with some sort of sports-hernia situation. That could make him something of a week-to-week proposition but hopefully the superstar wideout has found some way to manage the pain for the rest of the season. He has a Week 5 smash spot in the Bills’ shootout-prone defense. He will also have an extra day to get healthy with the game taking place on Monday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Tyler Higbee caught 1-of-2 targets for 14 yards in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: It was another disappointing outing for Higbee. This one came with Colby Parkinson (ribs) sidelined. Davis Allen had two catchers on two targets for eight yards. Higbee now hasn’t had more than 25 yards receiving in a game since the beginning of October, and has lost opportunities with the Rams going run heavy in recent weeks. Higbee won’t be a fantasy option in Week 9 against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Rams declared TE Colby Parkinson, QB Ty Simpson, LS Joe Cardona, OT Keagan Trost, and DE Desjuan Johnson inactive for Week 8 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Parkinson will miss at least one game with a rib injury he sustained last week against the Raiders. His absence could have a big impact on playing time for both Davis Allen — who had two touchdown grabs last week — and Tyler Higbee, the de facto TE1 in the LA offense. Both tight ends are better options against the Chargers with Parkinson sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Parkinson will have one more chance to get back no the practice field Friday to avoid an injury designation entering the weekend. The veteran tight end was in and out of the team’s Week 7 game with the injury but managed to finish it, apparently feeling much worse after the adrenaline wore off. Fantasy managers of Parkinson and Tyler Higbee will want to track Parkinson’s status closely to end the week. An absence from Parkinson could also bring Davis Allen into the fantasy spotlight after the young tight end scored twice against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Parkinson has meaningfully contributed to the Rams’ offense in each of the last two weeks, but he is now at risk of missing his team’s Week 8 game against the Chargers. Were Parkinson to sit out on Sunday, Tyler Higbee would likely benefit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Davis Allen caught 4-of-5 targets for 20 yards and two touchdowns in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: The Rams in Week 7 resorted to a heavy dose of three tight end sets with Davante Adams sidelined with a long-term hamstring injury. That led to 12 pass routes for Allen, fewer than both Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee. He caught two red zone touchdowns from Matthew Stafford, however, seeing a look on 33 percent of his routes. Allen will be tough to trust as a fantasy option unless or until his snaps and routes increase. He could be a deep league option in Week 8 against the Chargers, however.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Tyler Higbee caught 2-of-3 targets for 14 yards in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: It was Davis Allen who caught two of Matthew Stafford’s three touchdown tosses as the Rams leaned into heavy three tight end-set usage with Davante Adams sidelined indefinitely with a hamstring injury. Though Higbee led Rams tight ends in pass routes, his lack of red zone involvement left him out in the statistical cold. Trying to figure out which LA tight end is going to go off in a given week is going to be a continual headache for fantasy gamers in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Tyler Higbee caught 4-of-4 targets for 22 yards and one lost fumble in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Higbee lost volume to Colby Parkinson in this one. Higbee also had the ball ripped from his possession by Cardinals LB Cody Simon while trying to fall forward for extra yards on the Rams’ seventh drive, further reducing his fantasy output. With Parkinson playing well, Higbee is a shakier, low-end TE1 against the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Davis Allen (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Allen remains out, and Parkinson (shoulder) remains limited. Tyler Higbee has played productively in the Rams’ No. 1 tight end role, and he should be expected to do so again this week against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Tyler Higbee caught 5-of-6 targets for 83 yards in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Higbee continued to operate as the primary pass-catching tight end against the Bills, something that must please fantasy managers considering Colby Parkinson returned from a one-game absence. Furthermore, the team carried only three tight ends on the active game-day roster after being at either four or five through the first month of the 2026 season. Higbee is a middling TE2 in fantasy circles ahead of a juicy matchup against the divisional rival Cardinals in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Colby Parkinson (knee/shoulder) practiced in full on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Parkinson is unlikely to be startable as a TE1 if he plays on Monday night, but his return will likely reduce Tyler Higbee’s snap share. Higbee has been TE1-viable in each of the last two weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor caught 4-of-4 targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor’s touchdown was his first as a Raider. It went down for all of two yards. In addition to the score, Nailor posted new seasons highs in yards and receptions, which obviously tells you all you need to know about his WR4 value. He doesn’t have any heading into Week 9 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor caught 2-of-5 targets for 14 yards in the Raiders’ Week 7 loss against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor ran a route on 42 of the team’s 49 drop backs but wasn’t all that involved. Tre Tucker remains the Raiders’ top wideout, leaving Nailor without much in the way of air yards or targets. He should remain on waiver wires ahead of the Raiders’ Week 8 game against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-4 targets for nine yards in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: After missing Week 5’s game against the Patriots due to a concussion, Nailor was back on the field this week to face the Bills. Unfortunately for the 2026 free-agent signee, the results looked all too familiar. Nailor managed only one reception for nine yards and is now sitting on a 6-61-0 receiving line through his first five games of the season. Fantasy managers shouldn’t be counting on him to provide anything in next week’s game against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor (concussion) will play in Las Vegas’ Week 6 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: This per coach Klint Kubiak, so we assume Nailor has passed protocol. He’s only a FLEX play at this point as it’s hard to trust any weapons in the Vegas offense beyond Brock Bowers, even in a good matchup against a struggling Bills defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor (concussion) resumed practicing in a red non-contact jersey.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor will likely end up being listed as a limited participant today. He has a chance to play in Week 6 against the Bills, but his odds would be better if he had returned yesterday. If active, Nailor would only be a boom-bust WR5/FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor suffered a concussion in the Raiders’ Week 4 loss to the Chiefs, missing Week 5 against the Patriots while still in the protocol. He starts out the week not practicing, indicating he is not close to clearing protocol. Though he still has a chance to play this week, Nailor does not need to be stashed for fantasy purposes amid a murky wide receiver corps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Raiders ruled out Jalen Nailor (concussion) for Week 5 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: The Raiders entered the season with a thin wide receiver corps, and the unit just got thinner. Tre Tucker will continue functioning as the team’s top wide receiver and second pass catcher, backed up by Cody White (ankle) and rookie Malik Benson. Nailor does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Raiders WR Jalen Nailor (concussion) did not participate in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor will almost assuredly sit out the Raiders’ Week 5 game against the Patriots. Fellow WR Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) is practicing in full, and WR Cody White (ankle) remains limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Raiders WR Jalen Nailor (concussion) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor suffered a concussion against the Chiefs in Week 4 and starts out the week not practicing. This indicates he is on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5 against the Patriots. Fellow WR Cody White (ankle) was limited as well, though Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) returned to practice, giving the Raiders some reinforcement with Nailor still in concussion protocol.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor (concussion) will not return in Week 4 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor took a hard hit from Chiefs S Nohl Williams in the second quarter and was forced to go to the sideline to be evaluated. The team has now announced that Nailor will not be returning for Sunday’s game. Nailor will end the day with zero receptions on zero targets and will need to clear concussion protocol if he hopes to return in Week 5 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 5-of-6 targets for 53 yards in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: This was Mayer’s fourth five-catch outing of the season. Only Brock Bowers caught more passes this afternoon. It could have been a bigger day in fantasy, but Mayer’s unconverted look was an inaccurate goal-line pass he short-armed. Mayer has a reasonable enough PPR TE2 floor, but his spiked week potential remains limited enough that he is not a very exciting streamer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught all three of his targets for 32 yards in the Raiders’ Week 7 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer benefited from a pass-heavy second half for the Raiders as they once again faced a big deficit. He ran a pass route on 38 of the Raiders’ 49 drop backs. With four games of at least five targets, Mayer profiles as a desperation play in tight end premium games and a 12-team option if Brock Bowers misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 7-of-9 targets for 95 yards in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: This is the second time in three weeks that Mayer has popped up for a big performance. With Brock Bowers blanketed for much of the first half, Mayer stepped up to catch five passes for 52 yards in the first half, and he ripped off an impressive 28-yard reception in the second half on a drive that ended with a Matt Gay field goal. Playing behind Bowers continues to make Mayer a risky fantasy bet, but he’s averaging 6.7 targets in his last three games, which is buoyed by this week’s nine-target game and a 10-target outing in Week 4 against the Chiefs. With a few reliable tight ends on bye in Week 7, Mayer could have some viability as a dart throw next week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught his lone target for two yards in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer and the rest of the Vegas pass catchers took a backseat to Brock Bowers, who had a team-leading ten targets for 110 yards and a touchdown before the Raiders pulled their starters in the fourth quarter of this blowout loss. Mayer was fresh off an 82-yard outing (on ten targets) against Kansas City. He should remain on waivers ahead of Week 6’s game against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 8-of-10 targets for 82 yards in the Raiders’ Week 4 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer’s 10 targets were just one fewer than what Brock Bowers (11) saw on the day. Mayer made the most of his opportunities, racking up 82 yards—the second most in his career and saw four of his receptions come on the Raiders’ first four drives of the game. On the Raiders’ fourth drive, Mayer hauled in passes of two, seven, and 17 yards, with his longest catch setting up a 48-yard field goal just before halftime to put them up 13-10. We shouldn’t expect this level of production from Mayer on a weekly basis, but the Raiders’ underwhelming WR corps could pave the way for more opportunities for Mayer going forward after this solid outing. There’s a lot to like here, but Mayer will be a boom-or-bust TE2 next week against the Patriots until we see reliable target totals on a more consistent basis, while he shares the field with Brock Bowers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 3-of-3 targets for 32 yards and one touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 3 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer scored with just under six minutes left in the first half. Coach Klint Kubiak sent Brock Bowers in motion, back and forth across the formation, behind the line of scrimmage, before Kirk Cousins executed the play-action fake. Mayer ran an out route from the slot and shook Saints defender Justin Reid on the cut before quickly hauling in the pass. Mayer’s other two catches both went for double-digit yardage gains. He will be a viable TE2 moving forward, with defenses focused on stopping Bowers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 3-of-4 targets for 23 yards in the Raiders’ Week 2 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Brock Bowers missed his second game of the year while recovering from a mensicus trim procedure, giving Mayer another opportunity to start. He led the Raiders in routes but failed to make a big impact in the box score, logging a measly 14 percent target share. Mayer is generally in the TE2 mix when Bowers is out, but even then he isn’t a particularly high-upside option. With Bowers expected to return next week, Mayer can be sent back to the waiver wire on the upcoming waivers run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 6-of-7 targets for 32 yards in the Raiders’ Week 1 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer was seemingly set for a sizable workload, going 3-of-3 for 21 yards on the Raiders’ first drive. He caught his fourth pass on the second drive, which was punched out and recovered by the Dolphins, but the play was overturned. For his part, Mayer looked good on short in-breakers and out routes, and his six receptions tie for a team-high. The Raiders simply got up to a 10-0 lead early in the second quarter and controlled the game thereafter, leaving the passing offense to take a backseat role to the Raiders’ ground game. Mayer can be started as a TE1 again next week against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Raiders signed TE Michael Mayer to a three-year, $45 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: The deal was first reported by NFL Insider Ian Rapoport. Mayer’s deal includes $30 million guaranteed and his $15 million average annual value is third among tight ends. The Raiders selected Mayer in the second-round (35th overall) of the 2023 NFL Draft. He had 300 yards as a rookie and the Raiders drafted Brock Bowers 13th overall the following year. Mayer is firmly on the fantasy radar for Week 1 against the Dolphins with Bowers (knee) sidelined, but his value is unstable as the Raiders’ second tight end.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Raiders ruled out TE Brock Bowers (knee) for Week 1 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Earlier today, Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said he was initially optimistic that Bowers could play in Week 1, even after undergoing a recent meniscus trim, which is surprising. Kubiak, however, declined to discuss an updated return timeline for his star tight end. We do not yet know when he is expected back. In the meantime, Michael Mayer is a TE1 this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Kyren Willliams had 16 rushes for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers, adding one catch for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: The more efficient Blake Corum had 11 rushes for 73 yards and did not see a target in a run-heavy Rams offense. Williams led the LA backfield in routes but only had one look from Matthew Stafford. He was stuffed at the line of scrimmage a handful of times in the first half. The rushing volume in the Rams offense of late should make both Williams and Coum fantasy relevant every week, including next week against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum had 11 rushes for 73 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Kyren Williams led the LA backfield with 16 carries for 56 yards. Corum was much more efficient as a rusher against the Chargers, regularly bursting through the line of scrimmage and shedding tacklers on a couple second half runs. The Rams have been run heavy since Davante Adams went down with a serious hamstring injury a few weeks ago. That’s generated more opportunity for Corum, who last week had 17 rushes. He ranks 44th among running backs in expected fantasy points per game in 2026. That kind of usage should make Corum flex-viable for now. He gets the Commanders in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum had 17 rushes for 93 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders, adding one catch for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum had the lead in carries until the final drive of the game, when the Rams turned to Kyren Williams to seal the victory following a short-lived Raiders comeback. Corum’s fantasy day could have been much bigger if he hadn’t had two touchdowns called back on penalties along with another chunk gain. Despite running cold on luck, Corum’s role continued to grow even after Williams complained publicly about the backfield workload split last week. Williams logged 18 routes against the Raiders while Corum ran just nine. Look for the Rams to be more run heavy in the coming weeks with Davante Adams out indefinitely with a hamstring injury, putting Corum in play as a weekly flex. He gets the Chargers in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed nine times for 42 yards in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals, adding two receptions, 18 yards and one touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum got the Rams’ second drive all to himself before re-entering the game on the fourth drive and splitting reps with Kyren Williams thereafter. Rams coach Sean McVay seemingly rewarded Corum for powering through contact on a third-down conversion from the Cardinals’ 19-yard line by allowing him to remain on the field for the scoring-position sequence. Two plays later, Corum was scampering upfield for a 15-yard receiving score after hauling in a pass in the flats. He ran hard the rest of the way, but the Rams got off just 20 rushing attempts today, surprisingly playing in a trailing game script for the entire second half, as the Cardinals achieved victory via voluminous field goals. Corum is an RB3/FLEX against the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed five times for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills, adding 53 yards on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum provided a much needed spark in relief of lead back Kyren Williams, contributing three clutch receptions that kept drives alive in addition to a third quarter touchdown. That said, his modest volume continued while Williams turned in a third straight game with 20 or more opportunities, including 28 total targets in that stretch. Corum remains a top fantasy handcuff but is unlikely to return useful fantasy weeks for as long as Williams is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed five times for 14 yards in the Rams’ Week 4 win over the Eagles, adding a seven-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum was employed as a pure breather back this afternoon, as he got out-touched 26-6 by Kyren Williams. Four of Corum’s handles came on one first quarter series. With the 1-2 Rams staring down the barrel of 1-3 as they trailed by two scores for several quarters, they circled the wagons around their most established players, and that does not yet include Corum. The third-year pro will undoubtedly pop up for more 10-12 carry afternoons, but he’s fading from FLEX relevance as Williams gets re-established in the low-end RB1 mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams need more from Blake Corum in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Atkins believes Puka Nacua’s (groin) impending return will lighten the box, in turn making life easier on the run game and preventing the opposition from blitzing as frequently as the Broncos did last week. Corum has not established himself as a reliable weekly contributor in fantasy. Perhaps positive impacts from Nacua’s return trickle down to the Rams’ No. 2 running back. Kyren Williams remains a locked-in starter. Keep Corum stashed for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 15 times for 88 yards in the Rams’ Week 3 loss to the Broncos, adding 70 yards on six receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Williams’ 70 yards through the air were a career-high mark in receiving for a single game, returning yet another RB1 fantasy performance despite sharing backfield work with Blake Corum. Corum managed only 15 yards on six carries and caught two passes for zero additional yards. Furthermore, Corum has still not seen a carry inside the red zone through three games of the 2026 season. Williams remains a surefire RB1 ahead of a difficult matchup against the Eagles in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed 12 times for 79 yards in the Rams’ Week 2 win over the Giants, adding 13 yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum was kept out of the end zone for the second straight game to open the 2026 season but continues to display elite per-touch efficiency. The scoring woes could persist considering the robust red zone role of cohort Kyren Williams, the latter of whom found pay dirt for the second consecutive game to open the season. Corum continues to be a difficult weekly start outside of deeper leagues for as long as he is taken off the field where it matters most to fantasy production, and will remain a borderline FLEX start when the Rams face the Broncos in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed 10 times for 54 yards in the Rams’ Week 1 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum was unable to find the end zone while Kyren Williams did, but Corum was the more efficient tailback between the 20s with Williams only tallying 41 yards. He was also a non-factor in the passing game, but the Rams were basically a non-factor in the passing game with Matthew Stafford struggling to figure out the 49ers’ defense. Corum could see more touches in Week 2 against the Giants, but there’s no guarantee.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker was held without a catch in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Coming off 10/200/3 over the past two weeks, Tucker somehow commanded only one target in a game where the Raiders scored 38 points. It was the first time since the opener he caught fewer than four passes. Tucker has definitely benefitted from some garbage time production, but he is not typically going to be a zero waiting to happen. He can still be trotted out there as a low-end WR3 for a Week 9 matchup where the Raiders are going to have to pass to compete with the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 5-of-12 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 7 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: It was a quiet day for Tucker until the Raiders once again found themselves down by three scores in the fourth quarter. Kirk Cousins — as he did last week against Buffalo — let it rip and peppered Tucker with late downfield targets, one of them resulting in an impressive 37-yard touchdown. Tucker led all Vegas pass catchers with a dozen targets and dominated air yards as usual. Last week against the Bills, Tucker went for 97 yards and two scores on five receptions. The miserable Raiders defense should lead to plenty of runaway negative game script for the team’s offense in the coming weeks, and Tucker’s role as the team’s lone deep ball option gives him weekly upside. He’ll be a WR3 option in Week 8 against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 5-of-7 targets for 97 yards and two touchdowns in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Tucker found the end zone on an 11-yard touchdown pass from Kirk Cousins in the fourth quarter to tie the game at 23-23. Later in the game, with the Raiders down by 10, Tucker found himself on the receiving end of a Kirk Cousins moon ball in the end zone, which he hauled in for a 44-yard touchdown to cut the Bills’ lead to 33-30 with just over a minute left in the game. Tucker is the closest thing the Raiders have to a fantasy-viable wide receiver, and he has proven to be a volatile player throughout his four-year career. Fantasy managers shouldn’t view him as anything more than a boom-or-bust WR4 in next week’s game against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 4-of-5 targets for 41 yards in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots, adding two rushes for -7 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Tucker’s two rushing attempts were blown up in the backfield. He was third on the team in targets, trailing Brock Bowers and Ashton Jeanty. Tucker, who usually operates as the team’s primary downfield option, should have some appeal in Week 6 against Buffalo in what could be a high-scoring game. He has at least four receptions in four of five games this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 4-of-8 targets for 44 yards in the Raiders’ Week 4 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Tucker’s longest catch came on a 23-yard reception late in the fourth quarter as the Raiders looked to drive and tie up the game. Had the replay officials called for a review of the play in time, the catch likely would have been overturned, but the play was upheld, much to the disappointment of the Chiefs and head coach Andy Reid. The eight targets Tucker saw in this one set a new season high. He’s totaled 44 or fewer yards in three of four games this season and will be hard to trust as anything more than a dart-throw WR4 in Week 5 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 4-of-4 targets for 43 yards in the Raiders’ Week 3 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Tucker had a bigger impact in real life than he did in fantasy. On the plus side, he helped set up a field goal and a touchdown, first by finding the soft spot in the Saints’ zone coverage in the two-minute drill. Later, his 15-yard gain on a deep crossing route helped set up the Raiders. He also committed a holding penalty, which erased a short gain for RB Ashton Jeanty. Tucker is a WR4/FLEX against the Chiefs next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 5-of-7 targets for 119 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 2 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Kirk Cousins got the deep ball going in this game after settling for mostly check-downs in Week 1. Tucker caught two passes of 40+ yards, the first of which was a second-quarter touchdown. He also tied Ashton Jeanty with a team-high seven targets, so it wasn’t just a one-off deep shot for the veteran wideout. Brock Bowers is expected to return next week, meaning Tucker’s target share should take a hit the next time we see him. Even if he is relegated to field-stretching duties in Week 3, Tucker will remain a high-ceiling FLEX bet versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 2-of-4 targets for 27 yards in the Raiders’ Week 1 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Despite receiving clear-cut No. 1 wide receiver treatment late in the preseason, Tucker was not the clear-cut No. 1 wide receiver in Week 1. He nabbed a nice 21-yard gain and had another downfield pass broken up by DPI, but Raiders coach Klint Kubiak didn’t have a focal target here. Treat Tucker as a boom-bust FLEX against the Chargers next week, in what should be a back-and-forth game environment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said the team is still trying to find a wide receiver who is “accountable and can help us on Sunday.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: He punctuated his point by saying only, “still looking.” Kubiak’s ambiguous phrasing could suggest that the Raiders are seeking a wide receiver via trade, but it can also be read simply as an indictment of players like Jalen Nailor, Jack Bech and Malik Benson. None of the three turned in a great game last night, while Tre Tucker was given the night off. Tucker makes for a boom-bust FLEX option in an underwhelming position group.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Raiders WR Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-3 targets for 22 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Both Nailor and WR Jack Bech played tonight while WR Tre Tucker took the night off. Bech failed to earn a target and played into the fifth drive. Nailor called it a night after the third drive. The Raiders’ top-three wide receivers appear to be Tucker, Nailor and Bech, in that order. Tucker might warrant matchup-based FLEX treatment in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Seth McGowan rushed five times for 29 yards in the Colts’ Week 8 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: McGowan actually out-gained Jonathan Taylor on the ground in a game the Colts trailed 28-0 at halftime and 42-7 heading into the fourth quarter. No. 3 back DJ Giddens was called upon for six carries, which he turned into 43 yards. Fantasy managers are stuck in a holding pattern as they await Taylor’s Colts fate ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, but McGowan remains worth a speculative stash in most 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts are open to trading RB Jonathan Taylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: Multiple teams are interested in acquiring the 27-year-old Taylor and talks are active and ongoing, according to Schefter. The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reported that the Colts already turned down an offer for Taylor that included a 2027 second-round pick and another pick. While previous reports stated the Colts weren’t interested in trading Taylor, who signed an extension before the season, Indianapolis appears to be holding out for the best offer they can get. Taylor would see a slight boost in fantasy value if acquired by another team while Seth McGowan would likely take over the Colts’ backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Jonathan Taylor has not requested a trade.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: The Colts this week dealt DeForest Buckner to the 49ers and Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks in what looks like a fire sale ahead of the NFL’s trade deadline. Taylor could be next if the Colts are ready to go all in on a rebuild in 2027 and beyond. A contender would likely have to part with a second round draft pick if they want Taylor in the coming weeks. Teams that could be suitors for Taylor include the Bengals, Vikings, and Seahawks, all of whom have backfield issues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Seth McGowan rushed 11 times for 46 yards in the Colts’ Week 7 loss to the Vikings, adding one reception for two yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: With Jonathan Taylor trade possibilities swirling, McGowan quietly saw an increase in usage against the Vikings. He turned 12 touches into 48 yards, seeing 20 offensive snaps to Taylor’s 41. Though Taylor is still the definitive RB1, it is notable that the rookie 25-year-old is getting more opportunities, including a couple red zone snaps. McGowan has not quite achieved standalone fantasy value but should be added as a bench stash. He would be the Colts’ RB1 should Taylor be traded later this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: ESPN’s Stephen Holder reports that several teams are interested in trading for Jonathan Taylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis:
According to Holder, multiple teams would be open to trading for Taylor, but it remains unclear whether the Colts are ready to be sellers before the trade deadline. Colts GM Chris Ballard was recently fired, and “it is widely expected that significant organizational changes might be coming” after the eventual hiring of a new general manager.
Seth McGowan
should be stashed on benches at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Seth McGowan rushed six times for 31 yards in the Colts’ Week 4 win over the Commanders, adding one catch for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: McGowan got a whole drive to himself early in the second quarter. Three of his carries and one of his two targets came on this drive. He was otherwise tasked with normal backup duties. McGowan is the only backup of note on the team, but he doesn’t have a standalone fantasy role right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Seth McGowan rushed four times for 14 yards in Indianapolis’ Week 3 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: It was McGowan’s first real taste of snaps with Jonathan Taylor, as he had 11 to Taylor’s 60 while the Colts were trying to grind clock with a lead against a hapless Texans offense. We doubt there’s much to this extra usage, it was likely just Taylor managing something minor on the sideline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: Colts RB DJ Giddens (knee) was added to the injury report and did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: He did not play behind Seth McGowan in Week 1 and neither of them have fantasy value while Jonathan Taylor is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: The Athletic’s James Boyd left DJ Giddens off his 53-man roster projection.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: It’s been hard to find a good word from a beat on Giddens this offseason, so this isn’t an overly surprising conclusion to see listed out. He’s been sidelined for most of camp with a hamstring injury. The Colts look like they’ll keep Seth McGowan as their main backup to Jonathan Taylor. In this projection, Giddens loses the third running back spot to Ulysses Bentley IV.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.headline: The Athletic’s James Boyd believes Seth McGowan has “flashed” in training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/seth-mcgow.analysis: Describing his style as “decisive and violent,” Boyd believes McGowan is “building his case” to overtake DJ Giddens for the No. 2 role on the Colts depth chart behind Jonathan Taylor. Neither player will have a major role as long as Taylor is healthy, but it wouldn’t be stunning if McGowan won this battle in the preseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 24-of-32 attempts for 257 yards and two interceptions in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams, adding four rushes for 15 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Coming off their bye week, the Chargers looked worse than ever on offense, with Herbert apparently confused as to where to throw the ball or how to conduct OC Mike McDaniel’s complex pre-snap motion scheme. Herbert had a negative EPA per drop back. Both of his picks were of the mind blogging variety, thrown directly to Rams defenders in the open field. Frustrated and dejected, Herbert continues his worst pro season for the winless Bolts. As usual, Herbert — who ranks 33rd in fantasy points per game — won’t be a fantasy option in Week 9 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: The Athletic’s Noah Furtado reports the Chargers will try to “simplify” the team’s offense in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Justin Herbert and the flailing Chargers skill position players have appeared almost comically confused about all the pre-snap motion OC Mike McDaniel uses. That came through in the team’s embarrassing Week 6 loss to the Chiefs when players were bumping into each other during pre-snap motion calls from Herbert. Head coach Jim Harbaugh acknowledged the team is considering narrowing the offensive playbook during their bye week. “Definitely looking at volume and where you can make it to where the players can understand,” Harbaugh said when asked about how Chargers players were adjusting to McDaniel’s complex offense. The Chargers have used pre-snap motion on 74 percent of their snaps, the fourth highest rate in the NFL. Last year they used motion on 56 percent of their snaps. Hopefully these adjustments lead to some production for the NFL’s worst offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 22-of-37 attempts for 205 yards and one interception in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs, adding five rushes for 26 yards.
