https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Herbert’s hellish season continued unabated on Sunday against a Kansas City defense that swamped the beleaguered Bolts quarterback on seemingly every drop back. After throwing exactly one touchdown in each of his first five outings, Herbert didn’t have any against the Chiefs. He had a negative EPA per drop back and was 10 percent below his expected pass rate in the loss. Ladd McConkey was ruled out with a head injury in the first half, further complicating OC Mike McDaniel’s efforts to stop the bleeding for the LA offense. The team’s wideout injuries and the predictability of the offense means Herbert should be dropped in most one-QB fantasy formats ahead of the Chargers’ Week 7 bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter said the Chargers would not consider trading Justin Herbert.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Schefter reached out to the team after a league source told him the Chargers could get upwards of three first-round draft picks in exchange for Herbert. The Chargers source told Schefter the team has “never” discussed the idea of dealing Herbert, even as the Chargers start the season 0-5 and rank near the bottom in almost every offensive category. It would seem unlikely that the Chargers would consider trading Herbert even if they go all in on a rebuild following the 2026 season. Herbert, 28, who ranks 33rd out of 34 qualifying quarterbacks in EPA per drop back this year, is signed through the 2029 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 14-of-24 passes for 121 yards with a touchdown and interception while rushing for 54 yards and losing a fumble in the Chargers’ 23-17, Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Herbert was without his top wideouts, his top offensive lineman, and the fact he was able to put up even this type of statline is somewhat impressive, if you squint very hard. The 28-year-old quarterback was constantly under pressure, and was at his best when he was able to escape the pocket and use his underrated wheels. That being said, he could have had more turnovers than this, and his interception was an inexcusable throw right into the hands of the Broncos defender. Even if Herbert gets his weapons back, fantasy managers should be looking elsewhere in Week 6 in standard leagues with a tough matchup against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Rashawn Slater suffered a high ankle sprain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: The injury, sustained during the Bolts’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, will cost Slater between four and six weeks, Rapoport said. It’s yet another massive blow for the struggling Chargers offense. Through Week 4 the Chargers rank 30th in ESPN’s pass blocking win rate and fifth in run blocking win rate. Justin Herbert’s weekly prospects take a hit with the oft-injured Slate sidelined, as do the prospects of LA’s pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 19-of-31 passes for 189 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions in the Chargers’ 30-23, Week 4 loss to the Seahawks while adding 40 yards on the ground on six attempts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: It really wasn’t this close. Herbert and Sam Darnold became the first quarterbacks since 1991 to throw interceptions on their first throws of their game. Things didn’t get less weird, nor less shaky for the now 0-4 Chargers. He threw both his picks to linebackers, and outside of a 26-yard scramble, there just wasn’t much there from a quarterback who had (much) loftier expectations coming into the year. His only touchdown was a flip to Kimani Vidal that left Los Angeles down two scores. There’s a lot of football left, but this is ugly. Herbert will try and get going in Week 5, but the Broncos make for a tough team to get that ship righted.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Justin Herbert must “be better.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: It’s hard to write these quotes without sounding “clicky,” but Harbaugh was forthright at his Monday press conference when asked about Herbert’s decision-making. “Be better. Be better,” Harbaugh said before attempting to soften the blow. “And that drives Justin, that drives me, that drives his position coach, that drives (OC Mike [McDaniel). I mean, drives us all.” Harbaugh also said the team could look to simplify McDaniel’s complex scheme. “As far as the scheme going forward, all options are open,” Harbaugh claimed. When asked what that might entail, the coach responded “run, pass, up the middle, motion, no motion.” Alrighty then. It’s shocking to hear a coach talk this frankly — especially Harbaugh about Herbert — but the situation really is that dire in Los Angeles. Herbert is in the crossfire, but it could be McDaniel who is on something of a hot seat with his play-calling. Sitting at 0-3, the Chargers face the unwelcome prospect of a “must win” Week 4 contest against defending Super Bowl champion Seattle, itself coming off a rough loss. We will be benching Herbert in fantasy for that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 20-of-34 passes for 226 yards, one touchdown and one interception in the Chargers’ 24-16, Week 3 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: On one hand, Herbert was under constant pressure in this game behind a beat-up offensive line and was able to evade pressure regularly and extend plays. On the other hand, he really wasn’t able to get anything going down the field. His one touchdown “pass” was on a handoff where he essentially let go of the ball and Keaton Mitchell took the “forward pass” into the end zone on a jet sweep. Herbert’s interception was a terrible pass in the end zone when the Chargers were up 13-10 and looking to put the game away. The Bills also dropped two other potential interceptions. Herbert looks pretty firmly like a QB2 here, and it’s hard to get overly excited about playing him next week against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 15-of-27 passes for 192 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the Chargers’ 24-14, Week 2 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: The Chargers were an uncoordinated mess in this one. They committed loads of procedural penalties on offense, had several drops, and botched multiple handoffs or snaps. Their final penalty was holding in their own end zone, resulting in a safety. David Njoku handed Herbert’s first interception to a defender, but the second pick was all his fault. Herbert fired into a non-existent window on a deep shot and was easily intercepted by the Vegas secondary. Herbert also committed two fumbles, though both were recovered by the Chargers. Sitting at 0-2 with murderer’s row of opponents on deck, something has to change in a hurry for the Chargers. Herbert will shuffle into the QB2 ranks for his Week 3 date with the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 7-of-7 targets for 67 yards in the Colts’ Week 8 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: As is now the case every week, Allen easily lead the Colts in most every receiving category. That did not include targets — a returning Tyler Warren commanded 10 looks — but Allen out-gained him 67-18. Now Allen and fantasy managers must sit and wait to see what kind of moves the tanking Colts make ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline. That could include non-personnel changes like the benching of Daniel Jones. For now a low-end WR3, Allen could be valued much differently 10 days from now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 3-of-3 targets for 31 yards in the Colts’ Week 7 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen was second on the team in targets while leading in receptions and yards against the Vikings. He saw just 30 snaps but operated as a quick release valve over the middle of the field for Daniel Jones against a blitz-happy Vikings defense. In an otherwise low-volume day, Allen had another game with a high share of the Colts’ receiving output. He will be in the WR3 ranks ahead of a Week 8 matchup against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 8-of-11 targets for 82 yards in the Colts’ Week 6 loss to the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Each of Allen’s targets, receptions and receiving yards were new personal bests for his embryonic Colts career. Allen is doing what he’s supposed to be doing in Indy, but that’s not true for many of his teammates. Then again, we don’t really care in fantasy football, as Allen’s WR3 checks are clearing all the same. Allen’s short-area looks will be in high demand in Week 7 as Daniel Jones tries to survive the Vikings’ onslaught of blitzes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen caught 5-of-9 targets for 45 yards in the Colts’ Week 5 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen did not play a full complement of snaps in his first week back from a groin injury. He played 32 of the team’s 71 snaps and ran a route on 28 of their 47 dropbacks. That makes him leading the team with nine targets even more impressive. Of course, the Colts were forced to throw almost 50 times because the Steelers made it a priority to contain Jonathan Taylor. It’s highly unlikely Daniel Jones throws that much going forward, but Allen remains the top target in the offense. The issue is that most of his targets are in the short-yardage areas of the field, so he is more of a fringe-FLEX option unless you’re in a full PPR league. Next week against the Titans is a good matchup for the Colts, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen (groin) is active for Week 5 against the Steelers
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen got in a full practice on Friday, so he seemed to be trending towards being active, but now we know for sure. With Jamel Dean out this week and Joey Porter Jr. now in Dallas, the Colts’ passing game gets a slight bump, which is good news for Daniel Jones, who really needs to get back on track. The Colts inactives are: LB Jaylon Carlies, WR Ashton Dulin, QB Riley Leonard, WR Darius Slayton, and G Dalton Tucker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Keenan Allen (groin) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen missed Week 4 with the groin issue but returned to practice this week and even managed a full session on Friday. The team still listed him as questionable, though he appeared to be on the right side of that designation heading into the weekend. Allen will be a low-ceiling WR4 for his date with the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen (rest/groin) is questionable for Indianapolis’ Week 5 game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: He did upgrade to a full practice today so he’s at least likely on the optimistic side of questionable. Still, we were hoping he’d be cleared off the line entirely today, so it does give us a little hesitation that he could practice all three times this week, including one full, and still be questionable. The Colts don’t really have much else behind him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen (rest/groin) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Two straight practices, albeit limited ones, should put Allen on the right side of questionable on Friday barring something new popping up. Allen will be an unexciting FLEX play against the Steelers in Week 5 if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Keenan Allen (groin) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen suffered a groin injury in practice last week and was unable to play in Week 4 against the Commanders. His early-week return puts him on track to play in Week 5 against the Steelers, but he can likely only be viewed as a touchdown-dependent FLEX at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.headline: Colts WR Keenan Allen (groin) is out for Week 4 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keenan-all.analysis: Allen was limited in practice throughout the week and listed as questionable. Now he’s been ruled out for Week 4 against the Commanders. Josh Downs is locked in as the Colts top wide receiver this week and Tyler Warren should also see a boost in value with Allen sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington rushed 25 times for 83 yards in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: At least for one week, the Raiders formalized Washington’s early-down takeover, as the rookie out-carried a doghoused Ashton Jeanty 25-2. However, Washington got routinely stood up on his ample goal-line opportunities, and only out-gained Jeanty 83-73 thanks to Jeanty’s involvement in the passing game. A 45-yard reception where Jeanty literally fell down to catch an inaccurate Kirk Cousins pass only to get up and rumble nearly half the length of the field was by far the biggest play by a Raiders running back in this one. Although Washington now has to be considered the favorite for early-down work, he was uninspiring enough this afternoon that it’s not going to be an open-and-shut case against the 49ers. We would still rather start Jeanty in fantasy because of his pass catching.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington, Jr. had six rushes for 27 yards in the Raiders’ Week 7 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: As usual, Washington was far more efficient than lead back Ashton Jeanty, who had 15 yards on eight carries while catching eight passes for 61 yards and a touchdown. Washington can be stashed for now in case Jeanty misses time in the second half of the season. Washington likely won’t get the pass-catching work if Jeanty misses time, however.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington (foot/back) is active for Week 7 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Whether Washington plays all that much remains to be seen. He is not a recommended FLEX starter. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak has misdirected at times with injury-related comments. The Raiders declared DT Thomas Booker IV, DE Cian Slone, S Dalton Johnson, DT Jonah Laulu, G Bryan Cabeldue, S Tristin McCollum and QB Aidan O’Connell inactive for Week 7 against the Rams. O’Connell will serve as the emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Mike Washington (foot/back) is a game-time decision for Week 7 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Washington Jr. didn’t practice on Thursday or Friday but still received a questionable designation for Week 7. Fowler added that there is “some optimism” that he plays this week, but the pre-game workout will be the determining factor. Washington saw an uptick in carries last week with nine totes for 43 yards. We don’t expect as much work to go this way given the injury situation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington (foot/back) is questionable for Las Vegas’ Week 7 game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Washington didn’t practice on Thursday and was not spotted at practice on Friday. It would seem that he’s a very tenuous questionable at this point. Dylan Laube would be next up for backup duties behind Ashton Jeanty if Washington were ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington (foot/back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Dang. This suggests Washington suffered one or both injuries yesterday in practice. He is firmly in the questionable camp and may have only a long shot at suiting up in Week 7 against the Rams. Without him, Ashton Jeanty should handle a solid workload. Dylan Laube could end up serving as the No. 2 running back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington Jr. (foot/back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: In a semi-surprising twist of fate, the Raiders running back on the practice report with injuries is Washington, who was limited with foot and back injuries on Wednesday. Ashton Jeanty was not listed on the practice report. A limited practice indicates Washington is still trending to play Week 7, but with him appearing on the injury report and Jeanty off, any hopes for Washington achieving standalone fantasy value will have to wait.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington rushed nine times for 43 yards in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Washington’s nine carries were only one fewer than the 10 Ashton Jeanty saw on the night, but Washington was by far the more productive back. The rookie fourth-rounder averaged a solid 4.8 YPC in this one and ripped off an 18-yard run in the fourth quarter on a drive that ended with a Tre Tucker touchdown. Jeanty is dealing with a foot/ankle injury that is clearly limiting him on the field. Washington should continue to spell Jeanty in Week 7 against the Rams, but he doesn’t have much to offer fantasy managers as far as reliable production is concerned. He continues to be nothing more than a stash as long as Jeanty is active and on the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington, Jr. had one rush for five yards in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots, adding one catch for five yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It was odd usage for Washington, who had at least five carries in three of four games headed into Week 5. Even Ashton Jeanty being limited with his ankle and foot injuries did nothing to bolster Washington’s involvement in the Vegas offense. In fact, Dylan Laube was the team’s clear No. 2 back behind Jeanty on Sunday. Laube had four carries and three receptions and punched in a short touchdown in the second half of the blowout loss. It raises serious questions about what Washington’s workload might look like if Jeanty misses time this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Ashton Jeanty (ankle, foot) is active for Week 5 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Jeanty will play through his foot and ankle injuries against New England. It wouldn’t be surprising if he cedes some backfield work to a healthy and much more explosive Mike Washington, however. Jeanty should be considered a top-24 option this week while Washington is a desperation flex. Raiders declared WR Jalen Nailor, QB Aidan O’Connell, S Tristin McCollum, RB Roman Hemby, S Dalton Johnson, OL Trey Zuhn, and DT JJ Pegues inactive against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught a 22-yard pass in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Sadiq’s third quarter reception went down as one of just two targets for the rookie tight end. He was once again out-caught by Mason Taylor, though Taylor provided just 19 yards across his three grabs. Sadiq’s reception was an impressive, leaping catch against single coverage, but therein lies part of the problem: It’s taking spectacular acts for Sadiq to create fantasy value. He is sadly off the radar for the time being in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught his only target for six yards in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: The first-round rookie was held to one catch for the second week in a row. He has four catches over his past four games. It wouldn’t be surprising for his role to expand as the season wears on, but there were no signs of that happening this week. He isn’t worth holding onto in most fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught 1-of-3 targets for 12 yards in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Although there was an injury-shortened appearance mixed in, Sadiq now has just three catches for 15 yards over his past three games. This, as Mason Taylor has caught nine balls for 57 yards over the past two weeks. Sadiq’s big-play ability is going to come back into play sooner rather than later, but he is unsurprisingly maxing out as a zero-floor TE2 in fantasy for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is active for Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Sadiq made quick work of the league’s concussion protocol, for better or worse. With Omar Cooper Jr. also active vs. the Pats, Sadiq isn’t much more than a low-end TE2 prayer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Sadiq left Week 5 with a concussion. He was upgraded to a full practice on Friday and seemingly cleared the league’s concussion protocol over the weekend. With Mason Taylor and Omar Cooper Jr. back for Week 6, there will likely be fewer targets to go around in a Jets offense that has regressed heavily over the past two weeks. Sadiq is a low-end TE2 for his date with New England.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is questionable for New York’s Week 6 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: He did upgrade to a full practice and Aaron Glenn told reporters he expects Sadiq to play. Sadiq’s fantasy upside is well-known, but with Mason Taylor back and Omar Cooper Jr. also pushing to play, his target volume has shrunk quite a bit from some of the early-season scenarios we’ve seen. He’s likely a TE2 at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: He has been limited twice and doesn’t look close to clearing concussion protocol. It’s become rarer for players to launch a Friday comeback to get off protocol, but it’s not unprecedented. Sadiq looks like he’s on the doubtful side of questionable heading into Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq remains in the league’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: The good news is that Sadiq was able to practice in a limited capacity on Wednesday. Sadiq suffered the head injury in Week 5 against Cleveland and did not return to action. Mason Taylor led the team’s tight ends with a 59 percent route rate against the Browns, catching all three of his targets for 23 yards. If Sadiq remains in the protocol tomorrow, he would be a long shot to play in Week 6. Taylor in that case would be a desperation streaming option in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq suffered a concussion in the Jets’ Week 5 game against the Browns and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: To make matters worse, Sadiq suffered the injury in the process of losing a fumble. Targeted on a 3rd-and-9 near the goal line in the third quarter, Sadiq was short of the first down and got “Peanut punched” for the giveaway. With neither side getting anything going in rainy New Jersey conditions, Sadiq had just two receptions for three yards before going down, getting out-produced by a returning Mason Taylor in the process. Now highly questionable for Week 6 against the Patriots, Sadiq will not be on the streamer radar if given the go-ahead.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Jets TE Mason Taylor (thumb) is practicing in full for Week 5 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Taylor’s return could be problematic for rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq. Sadiq posted a 7/105/1 receiving line two weeks ago before goose-egging last week. Taylor is not a serious receiving threat, but he can eat into Sadiq’s snap share. Sadiq likely remains a viable TE1, but his volatility just increased a tad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.headline: Broncos S Brandon Jones suffered a hamstring injury and will not return in Week 8 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.analysis: With Talanoa Hufanga also sidelined heading into this game, both of Denver’s starting safeties from Week 8 are out. Luckily for Denver, Pat Surtani is back this week, giving them some extra firepower in their secondary. Jones has two interceptions and five pass breakups this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.headline: Broncos placed S Brandon Jones (pectoral) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.analysis: Jones suffered the injury in Sunday’s win over the Packers. The decision to place Jones on IR came after an MRI, which could indicate something more serious, although the team has not suggested that at this time. Jones has totaled 78 tackles, seven pass breakups, and one interception in 14 games for the Broncos this season. Safety Devon Key is listed behind him on the depth chart and will presumably take over in Jones’ absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.headline: Broncos CB Riley Moss and S Brandon Jones were listed at “DNP” on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.analysis: The team did not hold a practice on Monday ahead of their Week 10 meeting with the Raiders on Thursday Night Football, but the fact two additional members of the secondary appeared on the injury report as non-participants is concerning considering the absence of Pat Surtain. Absences from either could improve the schematic matchups for Jakobi Meyers and Tre Tucker, with tight end Brock Bowers expected to see a good deal of coverage from standout safety Talanoa Hufanga.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.headline: Free agent S Nico Bolden will work out for the Broncos on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.analysis: The report comes from the Denver Gazette’s Chris Tomasson. The Broncos are now without three safeties following Brandon Jones’ Friday hamstring strain, though Jones is expected to return in two weeks. Bolden’s initial NFL dreams were dashed by a torn meniscus suffered at his 2023 pro day. He played in seven games with the UFL’s St. Louis Battlehawks this season, earning a 68.2 PFF defense grade for his efforts. Bolden functions primarily as a box safety but has some free safety versatility.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.headline: Broncos S Brandon Jones suffered a hamstring strain at training camp on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.analysis: The training staff has yet to determine the injury’s severity but the Broncos are already in a tough spot at safety. The front office released four-time second-team All-Pro S Justin Simmons this offseason and both S Caden Sterns (patellar tendon) and S Delarrin Turner-Yell (ACL) are currently on the active/physically unable to perform (PUP) list. P.J. Locke is the only active Broncos safety who logged triple-digit defensive snaps last year, though he worryingly earned a 55.2 PFF coverage grade.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Broncos and S Brandon Jones have agreed to a three-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.analysis: According to Bleacher Report’s Jordan Schultz, Jones’ deal is worth $20 million, with a chance for him to move up to $22.5 million. The former Dolphin totaled 48 tackles and two interceptions last season and should have a chance to step in and replace Justin Simmons, who the team made a cap casualty last week. Jones was a third-round pick of the Dolphins back in 2020 and has started 30 of the 54 games he’s appeared in for his career.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.headline: Dolphins S Brandon Jones (ACL) is out for the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.analysis: Jones suffered the injury Sunday night against the Steelers. It’s a blow to an injury-riddled Dolphins secondary graded by PFF as the league’s fifth worst. Miami’s secondary should be as vulnerable as any in the NFL for the remainder of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.headline: Dolphins signed third-round S Brandon Jones to a four-year, $4.873 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.analysis: And with that, Miami officially puts pen to paper with their entire draft class. Jones (5’11/198) was a four-star recruit and three-year starter at Texas who earned second-team All-Big 12 honors as a senior. He moved across the defensive formation but was best away from the line of scrimmage where his overaggressiveness would bite him. A decent athlete with high-end competitiveness, Jones should be a nice special teamer in the NFL and could compete for a starting spot at box or free safety. His 86 tackles in 2019 were among the best in the safety class, but he’s just average when the ball is in the air.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.headline: Dolphins selected Texas S Brandon Jones with the No. 70 overall pick in the 2020 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.analysis: Jones (5’11/198) was a four-star recruit and three-year starter at Texas who earned second-team All-Big 12 honors as a senior. He moved across the defensive formation but was best away from the line of scrimmage where his overaggressiveness would bite him. A decent athlete with high-end competitiveness, Jones should be a nice special teamer in the NFL and could compete for a starting spot at box or free safety. His 86 tackles in 2019 were among the best in the safety class, but he’s just average when the ball is in the air.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.headline: Dolphins selected Texas S Brandon Jones with the No. 70 overall pick in the 2020 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brandon-jo.analysis: Jones (5’11/198) was a four-star recruit and three-year starter at Texas who earned second-team All-Big 12 honors as a senior. He moved across the defensive formation but was best away from the line of scrimmage where his overaggressiveness would bite him. A decent athlete with high-end competitiveness, Jones should be a nice special teamer in the NFL and could compete for a starting spot at box or free safety. His 86 tackles in 2019 were among the best in the safety class, but he’s just average when the ball is in the air.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-bates.headline: Jake Bates made two of his three field goal attempts in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-bates.analysis: Bates boinked one off the uprights in the second half, his first field goal miss of the 2026 season. One of the most reliable kickers in the NFL, Bates doesn’t get much opportunity thanks largely to Dan Campbell’s fourth down aggressiveness. Bates, who has just one game with multiple field goal tries this year, will be an iffy option in Week 9 against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-bates.headline: Lions tendered exclusive rights free agent K Jake Bates.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-bates.analysis: Bates’ numbers took a hit in 2025 compared to his previous year. He connected on just 79 percent of his attempts compared to 90 percent in 2024. Five of his seven misses came from at least 50 yards out and he was perfect within 40 yards. Even after the down season, Bates is still an above-average kicker and the ERFA tender costs Detroit next to nothing. Bates will remain a strong fantasy option in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-bates.headline: Jake Bates made 3-of-4 field goal attempts and all five of his extra points in the Lions’ Week 14 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-bates.analysis: Bates’ longest field goal on the day came on a 47-yarder late in the second quarter. The field goal came only a few minutes after Bates took a hard hit on a kick return and appeared to briefly get checked out by the medical staff. Bates has attempted seven field goals in his last three games and will remain a high-end fantasy option in Week 15 against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-bates.headline: Jake Bates made both of his field goal attempts and all four of his extra points in the Lions’ Week 12 win against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-bates.analysis: Bates drilled a 59-yard field goal to send this one into overtime. The kick came after the Lions lost five yards on an ill-advised screen pass. Bates had struggled from deep this season, making just three of his six field goal tries of more than 50 yards entering Week 12. Bates should remain in fantasy lineups next week against the Packers. He has multiple field goal attempts in eight games this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-bates.headline: Lions K Michael Badgley suffered a torn hamstring and is out for the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-bates.analysis: According to Lions beat writer, Tim Twentyman, Badgley “suffered a severe injury getting ready for practice” on Thursday. The veteran kicker converted on all four of his field goal attempts for the Lions last season, and was expected to compete with UFL star Jake Bates for the kicking job this summer. Bates now appears to be the frontrunner to land the job, but NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the team plans to bring in other kickers for added competition .

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-bates.headline: Lions signed K Jake Bates to a two-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-bates.analysis: It was reported earlier that the Lions were expected to sign Bates at the end of the NFL season. Now, ESPN’s Adam Schefter has confirmed that the kicking phenom will sign a two-year deal for a chance to compete with Michael Badgley for the starting job in camp. Bates was 6-of-10 on field goals of 50-plus yards during the UFL regular season and blasted a 64-yard game-winner in Week 1 for the Michigan Panthers. Before signing with the Lions, Bates also met with the Commanders and Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-bates.headline: KPRC2’s Aaron Wilson reports K Jake Bates is expected to sign with the Lions at the conclusion of the UFL season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-bates.analysis: Bates visited with the Commanders last week but appears set to join the Lions. Currently kicking for the UFL’s Michigan Panthers, Bates has turned into a spring football phenom after making multiple field goals of 60-plus yards and going 6-of-10 on field goals of 50-plus yards on the season. Bates converted on 17 of his 22 attempts (77.3 percent) in the regular season and first caught the attention of football fans when he converted a 64-yard game-winning field goal in Week 1 of the UFL season. He’ll have a chance to compete for the Lions starting kicker job against incumbent Michael Badgley, who made all four of his field goal attempts in his four games with the team. Badgley is a career 82.4 percent kicker and has made just five field goals of 50-plus yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers caught 7-of-10 targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: The multi-score start was Bowers’ first of the season but third of his career. He won a first quarter end zone hand fight for a 12-yarder before later contributing a two-yarder where he broke some tackles. He is now up to five touchdowns in six games and has yet to finish below 70 yards. That is league-winning type stuff out of the tight end position. The 49ers are on deck as a tough matchup up the seam for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers caught 6-of-8 targets for 73 yards in the Raiders’ Week 7 loss against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Bowers seemed to be battling some sort of minor injury for most of the game, missing a few high leverage plays while staying loose on the sideline. Bowers was second on the team in targets behind Tre Tucker (12), who did most of his damage in garbage time. Bowers, who has at least nine targets in every game this season, has as high a weekly floor as any tight end in recent memory. Hopefully he’ll be able to explore some of his upside in Week 8 against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (hamstring/calf) is not on Las Vegas’ final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: A Friday afternoon tradition unlike any other, Bowers was cleared after getting in two full sessions on Thursday and Friday. He can be played as an elite TE1, as usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (hamstring/calf) practiced in full on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Phew. Seeing Bowers return to full participation today is heartening. The star tight end appeared on the injury report as a limited participant yesterday, leaving some questions as to when the injuries occured, and how severe they are. Ideall, he remains full tomorrow and can be started as an elite TE1 as usual against the Rams this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (hamstring/calf) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Bowers is usually a limited practice participant due to his knee injury, before upgrading to full and eventually playing. However, this week is notable as he was listed with hamstring and calf injuries instead of a knee injury. He was still limited as usual on Wednesday but the new designations are something to keep an eye on throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers caught 4-of-9 targets for 70 yards in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.i
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: After being held without so much as a target in the first half of Sunday’s loss, Bowers still managed to finish the day with 70 receiving yards on a team-high nine targets. The Bills effectively shadowed Bowers with cornerback Christian Benford for much of the game but Bowers took advantage of a few holes in the Bills’ zone defense to make a few plays, which included back-to-back catches of 18 and 29 yards in the fourth quarter. Bowers did in one half what most tight ends need a full game to do, which speaks to his ability as one of the top play-making tight ends in the league. He’ll remain on the TE1 radar next week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: One of these days, Bowers will be removed from the injury report for good. For now, we will continue to let you know that the Raiders’ star player gets a half day on Wednesday before practicing in full for the rest of the week. Bowers is the overall TE1 in fantasy football each week. Start him accordingly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (knee) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: The Raiders continue managing Bowers’ practice reps early in the week, though he plays unrestrictedly on game day. The Raiders face the Bills in Week 6, likely facilitating a fantasy-friendly game environment. Bowers should be treated as the overall TE1 as usual this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers (knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Bowers continues his trend of practicing limited to open the week before upgrading to a full practice later in the week and getting cleared off the injury report. Fantasy managers can again expect to see Bowers return top-five fantasy tight end value in Week 6 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.headline: Brock Bowers caught 8-of-10 targets for 110 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brock-bowers/0.analysis: Bowers was again unstoppable both from the slot and from the boundary. The injury-ravaged New England secondary had no chance of stopping Bowers, whose ten targets led the Raiders. Bowers had three receptions of over 20 yards. His day could’ve been bigger if the Raiders had not rested their starters in the fourth quarter of the lopsided loss to the Patriots. With outrageous usage in Klint Kubiak’s offense, Bowers has as much upside as any player in fantasy for now. He gets the Bills in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 5-of-9 targets for 76 yards in the Titans’ Week 8 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm saw career-highs in targets and receiving yards in a high-scoring game against the Bengals. He saw a few targets in the flats but was targeted downfield multiple times, catching two passes of at least 24 yards. Helm also caught a two-point conversion in the fourth quarter. He is the Titans primary pass-catching tight end and saw heavy usage in a pass-heavy game script. Fantasy managers should not anticipate more game scripts like this for the Titans but Helm is a deep league streaming tight end option once the Titans come out of a Week 9 bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 3-of-4 targets for 24 yards in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Running a route on 23 of the team’s 34 drop backs, Helm was a little more involved than usual in the Titans’ low-octane passing attack. With fewer than 30 receiving yards in every game this season, Helm should not be rostered in any fantasy format for now. He’s been targeted on just 12 percent of his routes in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm failed to catch his only target in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: 45 snaps, one target. Helm has somehow grown less relevant than his 4/28 Week 1 showing would have even suggested. He can be dropped in most leagues at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 2-of-4 targets for 14 yards in the Titans’ Week 3 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm continued to split reps with Daniel Bellinger, who also caught two passes today. Helm hasn’t topped 30 yards in a game this year and his four catches in Week 1 remain a high-water mark. He isn’t even in the TE2 mix for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 2-of-2 targets for 13 yards in the Titans’ Week 2 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm is now sitting on a scoreless 6/41 through the Titans’ first two contests. Helm is an intriguing second-year pro, but there’s not going to be much intrigue in the Titans’ offense for the time being. 24-year-old Helm is best left on 12-team league waiver wires head of Week 3 vs. the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Gunnar Helm caught 4-of-5 targets for 28 yards in the Titans’ Week 1 loss to the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm gobbled up snaps as he tied Carnell Tate for the second most Titans receptions on an afternoon where Cam Ward completed just 19 passes. Helm is looking heavily involved in the offense, it’s just unclear if that will even amount to anything in this situation. Week 2 is going to be tough against the Eagles before a slightly more forgiving Week 3 date with the Giants. For now, Helm is not a recommended TE2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans TE Gunnar Helm (toe) will not play in Tennessee’s Week 18 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm finishes a successful rookie season with a 44/357/2 slash line, and looked to be making a climb up Tennessee’s target pecking order before injuries largely derailed his final month. It’s hard to rely on anything in Tennessee’s offense until we see exactly what happens with the coaching staff, but there are offseason runouts that will put Helm as a high-end TE2 with Chig Oknokwo slated for free agency.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans TE Gunnar Helm (toe) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm is now on the wrong side of questionable, which benefits TE Chig Okonkwo, who has scored a touchdown in consecutive weeks. Okonkwo is scheduled to enter free agency at the end of the season and has a chance to earn a decent payday with another strong showing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans TE Gunnar Helm (toe) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 17 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Helm is good to go, which is nice for QB Cam Ward. The promising rookie tight end has made good on his fourth-round draft capital, though the Titans’ distributive offense makes him too dicey a start for Week 17. Helm is up to 52 targets on the year, while averaging 1.58 yards per route run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans TE Gunnar Helm (toe) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Titans have been distributing the ball across the skill position corps in recent weeks, and we see no reason for that to change in Week 17 against the Saints. Helm is a touchdown-dependent fantasy-starter in re-draft formats. His rookie season showings have been encouraging overall.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.headline: Isaac TeSlaa did not have a catch in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.analysis: TeSlaa has been effectively phased out of the Detroit passing attack. he has one catch over his past three games, and against the Vikings on Sunday he ran 13 routes on 35 Lions drop backs and did not see a target. He can be dropped in most formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.headline: Isaac TeSlaa caught 0-of-2 targets in the Lions’ Week 5 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.analysis: Jared Goff gave TeSlaa two chances to contribute today. The first was a 3rd-and-13 pass on the Lions’ second drive, just beyond the sticks, in which TeSlaa went aerial and fully horizontal, trying to make the diving catch. The pass, unfortunately, fell incomplete. Goff went back to him on the fifth drive, firing a pass — just a touch too high — to the second-year wide receiver who was wide open on a crossing route, racing across the back of the end zone. TeSlaa leapt for it and got a hand on it, but he couldn’t come down with it. TeSlaa takes his goose egg into the Lions’ Week 6 bye. With any luck, it hatches into a FLEX-relevant stat line against the Packers in Week 7, though he remains a boom-bust pass catcher.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.headline: Isaac TeSlaa caught all three of his targets for 66 yards in the Lions’ Week 3 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.analysis: TeSlaa led the Lions in receiving on the back of a 49-yard grab late in the game. He was otherwise an afterthought in the offense, finishing the game with a nine percent target share. TeSlaa is averaging three targets per game, which simply isn’t enough to get him into the FLEX mix. He is buried in the WR6/7 range headed into Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.headline: Isaac TeSlaa failed to catch his only target in the Lions’ Week 1 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.analysis: TeSlaa did his usual wind sprinting in this game and failed to bring in his only target on the day. With stars at nearly every skill position in Detroit, there simply isn’t any room for a meaningful TeSlaa role. He is not on the fantasy radar heading into Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.headline: Lions HC Dan Campbell told reporters WR Isaac TeSlaa is going to be just fine.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.analysis: Even after TeSlaa’s training camp struggles extended into the Lions’ first preseason game, Detroit doesn’t seem worried about the 24-year-old receiver. TeSlaa had his first target go through his hands and off his helmet for an interception and later couldn’t hang on to a fourth down pass in the loss to the Bengals on Thursday. Still, his only competitor for the WR3 role is Greg Dortch, a journeyman receiver who also failed to catch a pass in the first preseason game. The Lions WR3 isn’t likely to be a fantasy-relevant role when everyone else in the offense is healthy, but Detroit would still like to see more development from their third-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.headline: Lionis WR Isaac TeSlaa caught 0-of-3 targets in Thursday’s preseason game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.analysis: The Lions’ established starters did not play. Lions WR Greg Dortch could be challenging TeSlaa’s WR3 role, although Dortch went 0-for-1 as a receiver as well. TeSlaa out-snapped him 15-7 on the first three drives. TeSlaa took two more snaps on the fourth drive, sans Dortch, which ended in a turnover. This is a position battle to keep an eye on.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.headline: The Athletic’s Colton Pouncy reports a lot of targets to Isaac TeSlaa in the early portion of training camp have been broken up “due to a lack of separation.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.analysis: We weren’t expecting a major target share for TeSlaa anyway in this offense, and he makes his living making contested catches, but it’s still a little disappointing that he hasn’t taken more of a step forward from his rookie season so far. TeSlaa is probably only a consideration in deeper leagues at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.headline: Lions coach Dan Campbell said Isaac TeSlaa has “looked like a consistent veteran this offseason” and he is “excited about where he’s trending.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.analysis: TeSlaa looks to be penciled into the three-wide set next to Jameson Williams and Amon-Ra St. Brown. It’s hard to understand how TeSlaa will generate much in the way of targets — he sure didn’t last year when he was on the field — but the Lions could have a good enough offense that TeSlaa finds his way on the WR4 radar this year either way. TeSlaa notched six touchdowns on 27 targets last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.headline: The Athletic’s Colton Pouncy believes Isaac TeSlaa should be a “full-time starter” in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.analysis: TeSlaa played sparingly for most of the season until Kalif Raymond started dealing with an ankle injury near Thanksgiving. TeSlaa’s numbers boomed to an average of 44 snaps a game for the rest of the season. The target rate wasn’t exactly fantasy-friendly, but TeSlaa managed six touchdowns on just 27 targets last year and figures to be an interesting fantasy football player in 2026, if not a downright useful one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.headline: Isaac TeSlaa caught his only target for 18 yards in the Lions’ Week 18 win over the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaac-tesl.analysis: TeSlaa emerged as a primary option for the Lions in Week 13 after Amon-Ra St. Brown departed with injury, finishing off the back half of his rookie season as the clear WR3 for the Lions. That effectively shifted Kalif Raymond into a situational role, something likely to carry forward into the 2026 season. TeSlaa ends his rookie year with 16 catches for 239 yards, flashing abilities in the red zone through six touchdowns. Although unlikely to immediately see his role grow while playing alongside St. Brown and Jameson Williams, TeSlaa appears likely to step into a bigger role when one of the main receivers goes down. That gives him legitimate best ball upside considering he will be playing for an offense that has finished in the top five in scoring in each of the previous four seasons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-mcla.headline: Chase McLaughlin converted 3-of-3 field goal attempts in the Bucs’ Week 8 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-mcla.analysis: McLaughlin also nailed his only PAT try. The Bucs forced a trio of turnovers in the first half. Their ensuring drives didn’t amount to much, but the field position alone allowed McLaughlin to put the ball through the uprights on two of them. With the Faclons accomplishing nothing on offense, the Bucs were comfortable taking the points throughout the contest, resulting in another strong fantasy outing for McLaughlin. He entered Week 8 as a top five fantasy option and will remain near the top of the kicker ranks for Week 9 versus the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-mcla.headline: Chase McLaughlin (groin) will play in Week 5 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-mcla.analysis: McLaughlin had a hip/groin issue pop up during practice this week but has since been cleared to play on Thursday. With the offense struggling to move the ball under Jalon Daniels, McLaughlin is not on the fantasy radar for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-mcla.headline: Buccaneers kicker Chase McLaughlin (right groin/hip) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-mcla.analysis: It was an addition to the report. Never a great sign, especially on a short week. The Buccaneers aren’t carrying a practice-squad kicker, so expect some workouts as they try to find someone you won’t be starting in fantasy football with Jalon Daniels under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-mcla.headline: Chase McLaughlin converted 1-of-2 field goal attempts in the Buccaneers’ Week 17 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-mcla.analysis: McLaughlin had a 55-yard field goal attempt blocked at the end of the first half. He ultimately made a 33-yard field goal in the second half and sunk both of his extra points, but the Bucs offense did not yield too many opportunities for him. McLaughlin should see a similar amount of scoring opportunities in Week 18 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-mcla.headline: Buccaneers re-signed K Chase McLaughlin to a three-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-mcla.analysis: The Bucs brought in McLaughin to replace former long-time kicker Ryan Succop. In his lone season with the team, McLaughlin converted 29-of-31 field goal attempts and nailed 100 percent of his extra points. Now under contract through the 2026 season, McLaughlin is just the latest Buccaneer to re-up with the team in hopes of winning their fourth-straight NFC South title.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-mcla.headline: Buccaneers signed K Chase McLaughlin, formerly of the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-mcla.analysis: McLaughlin made 30-of-36 field goals for Indianapolis last year without missing an extra point, and has played 16 games in each of the last two seasons despite playing for five different teams between 2019 and 2020. He’ll be Tampa’s replacement for Ryan Succop at kicker after they moved on from Succop to save cap space.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-mcla.headline: Colts elevated K Chase McLaughlin from the practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-mcla.analysis: He will kick Sunday against the Jags with the Colts operating as three-point road favorites in a 45-totaled affair. After starting for the Browns in 2021, McLaughlin was eventually released after the team drafted Cade York out of LSU in the 2022 draft. He then lost the preseason kicker battle in Indianapolis to recently released kicker Rodrigo Blankenship but gets a fresh start with the recent transaction. McLaughlin struggled in 2021 with the Browns, missing 6-of-10 field goal attempts between 40-49 yards. Consider McLaughlin nothing more than a low end streaming option in deep leagues that still include kickers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-mcla.headline: Browns released K Chase McLaughlin.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-mcla.analysis: The Browns also released kicker Chris Blewitt. After drafting LSU kicker Cade York in the fourth round, the team had no plans of holding a kick-off in training camp. York joins a team that should be an elite offense in 2022, making him an intriguing fantasy option for leagues that still utilize the kicker position.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-mcla.headline: Browns re-signed K Chase McLaughlin.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-mcla.analysis: The team in March didn’t tender McLaughlin as a restricted free agent, but the sides came together and McLaughlin is likely to return as Cleveland’s starter despite missing six of his 21 field goal tries in 2021. He made all four of his kicks of more than 50 yards while making just four of his ten attempts between 40 and 49 yards. McLaughlin could have some fleeting fantasy appeal for the Deshaun Watson-led Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-mcla.headline: The Browns did not tender restricted free agent K Chase McLaughlin, making him a free agent.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-mcla.analysis: 25-year-old McLaughlin was amongst the league’s worst kickers last season, making just 71.4 percent of his field goals. His experience will probably keep him on the workout circuit, but his odds of a long NFL career are not looking terribly great.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Travis Hunter was held without a catch in the Jaguars’ Week 8 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: Hunter did add a five-yard “rush” on what sure looked like a pass attempt from Trevor Lawrence, but that’s neither her nor there. What is here is a rather predictable letdown after Hunter went into the Jaguars’ Week 7 bye with a pop-up effort in London. Although it was good to see Hunter contribute at all on offense, his role is too limited in an attack with too many mouths to feed to treat him as even a boom/bust WR4. That includes for Thursday’s short-week date with a Ravens team now missing starting quarterback Lamar Jackson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Travis Hunter caught 4-of-4 targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: In London, where Travis Hunter’s best games live, Hunter both caught a touchdown and picked off C.J. Stroud (his first of the season), becoming the first player to do both in the same game since Brian Dawkins in 2002. Hunter did all this on just nine offensive snaps. The skill is there to do this on offense, but the Jaguars have really been defense-first with his snaps this year. Depending on the post-bye buzz, Hunter could be a reasonable pick-up in fantasy leagues ahead of Week 8’s games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said the Jaguars are “looking at continuing to find different ways” to get Travis Hunter involved.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: Coen talked about getting Hunter involved more on both sides of the ball, so it’s unclear how much of an uptick in offensive snaps we can expect in Week 3. Hunter has a 58 percent snap share on defense and a pitiful nine percent snap share on offense through two games. Even if he isn’t likely to hit the fantasy radar anytime soon, it would be shocking for the No. 2 overall pick to play this infrequently every week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Travis Hunter caught his lone target for eight yards in the Jaguars’ Week 1 win over the Browns, adding one carry for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: Hunter saw just four offensive snaps to 39 defensive snaps against the Browns. With a good wide receiver room, Hunter was not playing offense as much and his utilization overlapped with Jakobi Meyers. It’s unlikely the 23-year-old achieves much fantasy relevancy without an injury to Meyers moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley reports that Travis Hunter “is expected to be the Jaguars’ No. 1 cornerback in Week 1 and beyond.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: Shipley leaves the light on for offensive contributions, entertaining the idea that Hunter can chip in “a few hundred yards and a few touchdowns” this season as well. That said, the early indications for Hunter’s FLEX viability in managed leagues are pretty bleak. Stash him if you wish, but understand that starting him in Week 1 against the Browns could result in zero points.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley reports that Jaguars CB/WR Travis Hunter has taken reps “almost exclusively at cornerback” for the last two weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: Shipley estimates that Hunter has logged fewer than 10 reps at wide receiver in team drills during that span. Shipley said, “it seems like” the Jaguars are treating Hunter like their CB1. He also still thinks “there will be games where he logs 50 percent of the offensive snaps,” though. The biggest takeaway is that Hunter has an extremely wide range of potential outcomes, and he cannot be counted on to be FLEX-viable at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: ESPN’s Mike DiRocco reports that Jaguars WR Brian Thomas Jr. and CB/WR Travis Hunter “have shared reps” in 11 personnel packages.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: To be clear, Thomas is the starting X-receiver and Hunter is rotating in behind him. Hunter has also been taking more defensive snaps lately, so if he is going to maintain an offensive role, a simplified downfield role makes sense. Regarding Thomas, DiRocco adds that he “was arguably the best player on the field” during organized team activities, has had a “great” training camp and is “showing some of the toughness and ball security that seemed to be missing last season.” With all of that in mind, losing snaps in three-wide receiver sets is a bit surprising. Thomas is extremely talented, but obvious questions remain as to his usage in the upcoming season. A boom-bust WR3 season could be on the way.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Travis Hunter took zero 11-on-11 reps on offense on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: It was suggested by Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley that the Jaguars could be “tipping their hand” here, as he writes “it is clear the Jaguars believe they need to devote more practice time with Hunter before Week 1 at cornerback, which could be the biggest signal yet that the majority of his snaps against the Cleveland Browns on Sept. 13 will be at cornerback.” Hunter will likely still be involved in the offense — he has worked with the offense every day before this — but it is notable that there was a shift here. Hunter will likely be just a dart throw WR5/WR6 in most standard leagues this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe believes Brian Thomas Jr. will play the X receiver role in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: That would mean Thomas is set to play on the outside at the line of scrimmage. Parker Washington will presumably play in the slot with Jakobi Meyers and Travis Hunter fighting for flanker duties. As Wolfe notes, Liam Coen learned last year that going over the middle of the field and taking hits isn’t BTJ’s thing. Instead, he will likely be tasked with winning deep and beating man coverage. Wolfe noted Liam Coen’s roots in the Rams’ offense and compared BTJ’s role to that of Brandin Cooks and Sammy Watkins when they played in LA. Cooks topped 1,200 receiving yards in his first season with the Rams but fell below 600 in his second and final season with the team. Watkins, meanwhile, played just one season in LA and was also held under 600 yards. All signs point to Washington being the team’s No. 1 receiver this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said, “He will do it,” when asked if Travis Hunter would play offense and defense in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: Talking with Peter Schrager on his podcast, Coen almost laughed at the idea that Hunter might play exclusively on one side of the ball this year. Early offseason reports suggested Hunter might play primarily on defense after suffering a season-ending injury during his rookie season. Every subsequent report from local beats and all the quotes from the coaching staff have made it clear that Hunter remains a two-way player. Coen did note that they are still determining how much he will play on both sides of the ball, but it sounds like a part-time role on offense is the floor. Given the barrage of information suggesting Hunter will play on offense, a WR57 price tag for last year’s No. 2 overall continues to look absurdly cheap.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Chimere Dike caught 5-of-6 targets for 71 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 8 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Dike saw 58 snaps with Carnell Tate out, second among Titans wide receivers. He scored on an 11-yard reception in the fourth quarter. It was Dike’s first game with over three receptions and second game over one target this season. Dike is mostly utilized as a kick returner but is in line to see increased opportunities on offense if Tate misses additional time. For now, Dike should be off the fantasy radar heading into the Titans’ Week 9 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Chimere Dike caught 4-of-5 targets for 55 yards in the Titans’ Week 17 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Dike also had a carry of seven yards and drew a 50-yard defensive pass interference. He finished the day tied for team-highs in catches and yards. With some help from his punt and kick returns, Dike set the record for all-purpose yards by a rookie at 2,344. Dike has his limitations as a receiver, but he is a force to be reckoned with when the ball is in his hands. He will be in the FLEX mix for his Week 18 date with the Jags.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Chimere Dike caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 16 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: In addition to his fourth receiving score of the season, Dike set the Titans’ single-season record for kick return yardage. The 24-year-old has been a legitimate all-purpose weapon, even if it hasn’t quite translated to weekly WR4 value. Maybe that will be on tap for 2026, but Dike still lacks either the floor ceiling to be a trusted fantasy option for finals week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Chimere Dike caught 4-of-5 targets for 17 yards in the Titans’ Week 15 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Dike had the most targets of any Titans wide receiver, but that’s not much to write home about. The Titans love to run screen passes, and Dike is really shifty after the catch, so you figure he’d be a good option on those plays. The Titans don’t seem to agree. The rookie also had a brutal drop in the fourth quarter on a play where Cam Ward evaded three rushers and escaped to the sideline before throwing a dart that hit Dike in the chest. He needs to make those catches, and the drop is a good example of why he’s hard to trust in fantasy leagues right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Chimere Dike caught 5-of-8 targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 14 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: That’s a highly disappointing yardage total considering Dike’s catches and targets, but the looks matched a season high. The score was also his second in three weeks. The Titans have followed through on their pledge to get Dike more involved down the stretch. It has been difficult for it to translate to real fantasy value because of Cam Ward’s ongoing struggles, but Dike is still looking like someone who could be an eventual fantasy WR3. That will not include for Week 15 against the 49ers. Fantasy managers simply have too many other higher-ceiling options with the playoffs beginning.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Titans WR Chimere Dike (quad) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 14 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Dike has been quite the volatile scorer as of late. In his late six games, he has finished as the half-PPR WR15-18 three times. In his other three showings, he finished as the WR75 or worse. Facing the Browns’ elite defense, he makes for a very risky FLEX option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Titans WR Chimere Dike (quad) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Dike had a calamitous Week 13 showing with just eight yards on four targets, as well as a fumbled kick return. He’s not a super desirable FLEX option against a strong Browns defense in Week 14.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Titans WR Chimere Dike (quad) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Dike has delivered volatile results while playing through small injuries in recent weeks. Although his limited session on Wednesday puts him on track to play, he faces the Browns’ elite defense in Week 14. He is not a recommended FLEX starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Chimere Dike caught 1-of-4 targets for eight yards in the Titans’ Week 13 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: Dike also gained one yard on a rush and fumbled on a kick return in the first quarter. His explosiveness makes Dike an intriguing fantasy option, but he does not get consistent usage in a low-ceiling Titans offense. With Elic Ayomanor back in the lineup, Dike was still second on the team in wide receiver snaps, indicating he is still a large part of the pass-catching lineup. Dike is a shaky boom-or-bust play for Week 14 against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.headline: Chimere Dike caught 5-of-7 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 12 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chimere-di.analysis: In addition to tying for the team lead in targets, Dike notched a second score when he housed a third quarter punt for a 90-yard special teams touchdown. It was Dike’s second return TD in three games, though fantasy managers will be more heartened by his second best reception total of the season. With Calvin Ridley (broken leg) done for the year, there should be more where that came from, though both floor and ceiling are difficult to come by in this bottom-three offensive environment. The Jaguars are not a great Week 13 matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.headline: Wan’Dale Robinson caught 6-of-7 targets for 57 yards, a touchdown and a fumble in the Titans’ Week 8 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.analysis: Robinson led Titans wide receivers in targets and snaps with Carnell Tate out, seeing seven targets. He was involved in his usual short-yardage role out of the slot, averaging 9.5 yards per reception with a 15-yard fourth quarter touchdown boosting his fantasy production. He was credited with a fumble on a screen pass that controversially could have been ruled an incomplete pass. Robinson is consistently a checkdown target for Cam Ward, with intermediate targets sparsely sprinkled in. Tate may return out of the Titans’ Week 9 bye, leaving Robinson to fend for fantasy production in the fantasy WR4 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.headline: Wan’Dale Robinson caught 4-of-6 targets for seven yards in the Titans’ Week 7 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.analysis: The checkdowns for Robinson will continue until morale improves. Running a pass routes on 27 of 34 Titans drop backs, Robinson was third in targets among Tennessee pass catchers and couldn’t make anything happen after the catch on each of his four grabs on the day. He now has two games of more than 50 receiving yards on the season with an average depth of target below six. Robinson should remain on waiver wires ahead of Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.headline: Wan’Dale Robinson caught 3-of-7 targets for 22 yards in the Titans’ Week 6 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.analysis: We suppose 3/22 isn’t an awful outcome on a day where the quarterback completed only 11 passes, but supposed targets hog Robinson is falling further and further behind No. 4 overall pick Carnell Tate, who is suddenly stacking impressive box scores and highlight-reel plays. You would like for that to eventually add an extra element to this anemic offense — and perhaps more play volume — but until it does, Robinson is looking like little more than a last-gasp WR4 in fantasy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.headline: Wan’Dale Robinson caught 6-of-7 targets for 53 yards in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.analysis: Unbelievably, that’s the most efficient Robinson has looked all season. He remains ticketed as the undercard to Carnell Tate and should only be viewed as a FLEX option. A matchup against the Colts next weekend at least is a lot more interesting of a spot than one against Houston’s defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.headline: Wan’Dale Robinson caught 3-of-5 targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 4 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.analysis: Robinson was bailed out of a disappointing fantasy day when he hauled in a three-yard touchdown pass from Cam Ward late in the fourth quarter. Robinson was heavily out-targeted by Carnell Tate in this one, but he and Tate continue to be the only fantasy-viable receivers in this Titans offense. Robinson could be in play as a desperation FLEX play in next week’s game agains the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.headline: Wan’Dale Robinson caught 7-of-11 targets for 57 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 3 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.analysis: Robinson got in the end zone for the first time as a Titan on a quick out route late in the fourth quarter. He comfortably led the team in targets and catches, though Carnell Tate beat him by one yard. Robinson and Tate are the only game in town for receiving opportunities on this team, but Cam Ward’s struggles make it hard to trust either for fantasy purposes. Robinson is a FLEX consideration in deeper leagues for his Week 4 matchup with the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.headline: Wan’Dale Robinson caught a nine-yard pass in the Titans’ Week 2 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.analysis: Robinson’s third quarter reception was his lone official target, though he had a second catch wiped out by penalty in the fourth frame. 25-year-old Robinson is highly paid to be a compiler over the middle of the field, but he’s somewhat predictably looking like a poor fit with Cam Ward’s scattershot skill-set. He did at least catch five balls in Week 1. He is now heading on the road for a “revenge game” with his former team the Giants in Week 3. He will be a low-end WR4 for that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.headline: Wan’Dale Robinson caught 5-of-6 targets for 38 yards in the Titans’ Week 1 loss to the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.analysis: It’s a standard-issue Robinson statline for his Titans debut. Ominous, since this should have been an 8-9 reception Robinson outing with the Titans spending the entire game in comeback mode. Cam Ward and company simply could not sustain drives. In theory, Robinson could form a compelling inside-out duo with Carnell Tate, but Ward did not look like a player ready to break out on Sunday. Things could get worse before they get better with the Titans forced to take on the Eagles’ tough defense in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Titans WR Wan’Dale Robinson “is not believed” to have suffered a concussion.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.analysis: This is good to hear. New Titans OC Brian Daboll brought Robinson with him from the Giants to serve as a reliable go-to option for QB Cam Ward, particularly on third down. Robinson has a chance to lead the Titans in targets this season, though questions about the offense’s overall effectiveness could keep him stuck in FLEX spots, rather than the WR3 tier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.headline: Team reporter Jim Wyatt reports that Titans WR Wan’Dale Robinson is being evaluated for a concussion on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/wandale-ro.analysis: FOX Sports’ Ben Arthur reported earlier that Bears DB Xavier Woods “laid out Wan’Dale Robinson over the middle of the field” during today’s joint practice, which “justifiably” prompted a response from the Titans’ sideline. Titans coach Robert Saleh called the hit “cheap.” The NFL reviews practice footage when available. We’ll see if anything comes of it. Losing Robinson for Week 1 would be consequential for QB Cam Ward, and would likely shift more work toward rookie WR Carnell Tate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-5 targets for 95 yards in the Falcons’ Week 8 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: The bulk of Dotson’s production came on a single, 76-yard gain in the fourth quarter. Michael Penix lobbed him a ball on the boundary and two Bucs defensive backs collided, leaving Dotson uncovered with room to run. He bolted down the sideline but didn’t have the speed to take it to the house. That play alone accounted for over half of Penix’s passing output. Dotson has made the occasional splash play while running as Atlanta’s WR2, but his fantasy prospects are not that intriguing headed into Week 9. He will be in the WR5/6 range when the Falcons take on the Bengals next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 1-of-3 targets for six yards in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson was also targeted on three different deep passes that resulted in San Francisco penalties.
