That doesn’t help your fantasy team, but it is indicative of his role in this offense. Dotson did run the second-most routes of any receiver on the Falcons; however, he is really only targeted on deep shots down the field, which will make his production inconsistent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 3-of-5 targets for 87 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson, whose season-high yardage coming into the week was 54 — his total in both of the past two weeks — got loose a couple times in this one, mostly when the Falcons ditched their usual run-heavy offense in favor of a fast-pace pass-heavy approach while facing a multiple touchdown second half deficit. Running a route on 32 of the Falcons’ 38 drop backs, Dotson led the team in receiving yards thanks largely to a 41-yard grab. Dotson could be a deep league play in Week 7 against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-4 targets for 54 yards in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson’s 54 yards finished second on the team behind alpha Drake London but his four targets finished behind London, Kyle Pitts, and Bijan Robinson. His status as the starting wide receiver opposite London likely means little in the wake of modest volume games that continue to stack up. He can safely be left on, or returned to, the waiver wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-3 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson continues to operate as the team’s WR2 opposite Drake London but remains unlikely to return consistent fantasy production in an offense heavily concentrated on its top two options in London and Bijan Robinson. Dotson’s touchdown came in the fourth quarter with the team cruising, pushing the lead to 21 points with under 10 minutes to play. Fantasy managers can safely keep Dotson on the bench ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Ravens in Atlanta.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-4 targets for 11 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson saw four targets for the second week in a row. He went for 19 yards on one catch last week and didn’t look any different this time around. Dotson is the team’s No. 2 receiver by routes, but there aren’t enough targets to go around after Drake London, Kyle Pitts, and Bijan Robinson all get theirs. Dotson is not on the fantasy radar for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 1-of-3 targets for 19 yards in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson actually operated as the second receiver for the Falcons in this one, running a route on 20 of the team’s 29 dropbacks. He also played 38 snaps, while Olamide Zaccheaus played just 18. That didn’t amount to much, but it’s something for fantasy managers in deeper leagues to keep in mind when Michael Penix eventually gets back onto the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: ESPN’s Marc Raimondi believes Falcons WR Zachariah Branch could start the season as a “gadget guy,” before later earning a starting role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Branch was a screen game dominator in college, with speed to spare. Raimondi thinks the Falcons will attempt to replicate his Georgia game early on, but Branch has a chance to become “the No. 3 guy, maybe even the No. 2 guy at some point.” Falcons WRs Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus sit in those two spots. Branch is unlikely to contribute meaningfully in fantasy early in the year, but he is worth keeping an eye on in-season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: The Athletic’s Josh Kendall believes that if the Falcons make a “random offseason move,” it might come at wide receiver.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: The Atlanta depth chart at wideout is sparse even after we account for third-round pick Zachariah Branch in the draft. The No. 2 receiver right now might be Jahan Dotson. Olamide Zaccheaus is also in the picture. The Falcons still have $27 million in cap space but we’ve rarely heard them mentioned by national reporters as interested in the Stefon Diggs/Deebo Samuel/Keenan Allen best veteran free agent wideout tier. Those guys aren’t mentioned in this report either, but they do make plenty of sense from a roster standpoint.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: The Athletic’s Josh Kendall believes Jahan Dotson “may be” Atlanta’s No. 2 receiver this year.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: The Falcons released Darnell Mooney and KhaDarel Hodge, leaving them with a depth chart behind Mooney of Olamide Zaccheaus, Casey Washington and Deven Thompkins. The Falcons, who lost their first-round pick in the ill-fated James Pearce trade, also don’t have many draft picks this year and could be less likely than most teams to draft a wideout that could challenge Dotson for a role. We’re not quite at “sleeper” status here, but we’re at least late-round Best Ball curious.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones had five rushes for 22 yards in the Vikings’ Week 8 loss to the Lions, adding two catches for 18 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jordan Mason led the Minnesota backfield with eight rushes (for 20 yards) while Jones remained the team’s preferred pass-catching option out of the backfield. Jones was battling a knee injury headed into the game and did not appear to be 100 percent against Detroit. He’ll be a deep league flex option in Week 9 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) is active for Week 8 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones was able to practice in full on Friday after battling the lingering knee issue all week. He could be somewhat limited against Detroit, creating a potentially bigger workload for Jordan Mason, who profiles as a flex option in 12-team leagues. Vikings declared Jakobe Thomas, Charles Demmings, Demond Claiborne, Caleb Tiernan, Elijah Williams, and Max Brosmer inactive against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) will play in Week 8 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones departed the team’s Week 7 win over the Colts after aggravating an existing knee issue. He was held out of practice Wednesday before retaking the practice field on consecutive days to end the week, ultimately deemed healthy enough to play against the division rival Lions in Week 8. Fantasy managers are likely best off finding a suitable alternative considering Jones is struggling through a sprained MCL and the team got Jordan Mason back a week ago, although managers in a bind can safely expect him to be on the field come Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones was forced from the team’s Week 7 win over the Colts due to an aggravation of an existing knee injury. The fact he was able to return to the practice field in any capacity after missing Wednesday’s session is good news for his potential availability against the Lions. We would expect him to form a loose committee with Jordan Mason, if active Sunday. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his level of participation Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones has reportedly been playing through a sprained MCL in one knee since Week 2. He seemingly aggravated it in Week 7 and left the game early in the fourth quarter. On Monday, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported that Jones is considered “day-to-day.” Jones could once again play through the issue this week against the Lions. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Aaron Jones is considered “day-to-day” after suffering a knee injury in Week 7’s win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones’ status will be one to watch this week as the Vikings prepare for their Week 8 matchup against the Lions. While the team calling him day-to-day is encouraging, Jones was already dealing with a knee injury entering Week 7, so it wouldn’t be surprising if the Vikings opted to sit him this week to give him some additional time to recover. Jordan Mason, who rushed 15 times for 68 yards in Sunday’s win over the Colts could be in line for a busy day against the Lions if Jones is unable to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones rushed eight times for 26 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts, adding one reception for zero yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones got the start in the Vikings backfield, ripping off four straight carries for nine yards on Minnesota’s first possession. Outside of the opening possession, Jones took a backseat to Jordan Mason, seeing a mix of passing-down snaps and short-yardage carries. He caught his only target in the red zone but had it punched out for a fumble out of bounds. Jones left in the fourth quarter with a knee injury; he had been playing through an MCL injury and may have aggravated the issue. Prior to the injury, Jones was getting out-snapped by Mason and ends with 15 snaps to Mason’s 38, while getting six fewer touches. Jones is a low-end fantasy RB2 if healthy for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) is questionable to return Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones suffered a knee injury after a fourth quarter run against the Colts. He has notably been playing through an MCL injury and may have re-aggravated it here. Jones struggled to walk and spent time in the medical tent. Jordan Mason is the team’s top running back while Jones is out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: The Athletic’s Alec Lewis believes the Vikings could target a running back with ‘home-run burst’ in a move for the trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Lewis connects the Vikings to Chargers backs Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal as well as Tennessee’s Tony Pollard, Tampa Bay’s Kenneth Gainwell, and Arizona’s Tyler Allgeier. These are just whispers at the moment, but any kind of costly trade acquisition would cut into the playing time and fantasy value of Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones. The Vikings have clearly already been shuffling depth pieces around so we believe there could be more urgency there as the trade deadline gets closer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.headline: Aaron Jones rushed 25 times for 113 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints, adding three catches for four yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-jone.analysis: Jones had been seeing elite workloads ever since Jordan Mason was placed on IR with a thumb injury. He hadn’t done all that much with the opportunities but finally got going downhill today. Jones ran right over a New Orleans defender for a short touchdown early in the fourth quarter. He then salted the game away with a handful of chunk gains late in the contest. Mason is eligible to return after the Vikings’ Week 6 bye, so this may be the last we’ve seen of Jones in a three-down role for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley caught 1-of-3 targets for 20 yards in the Titans’ Week 8 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley was active after dealing with a hip injury this week, seeing the fourth-most snaps among Titans wide receivers. He finished the game with a drop and one reception. The veteran is a candidate to be traded but has not been offering much by way of fantasy production. Ridley can be left on fantasy benches heading into the Titans’ Week 9 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) is active for Week 8 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley entered the week questionable due to a hip injury but will be active after getting in a full practice on Friday. The Titans declared WR Carnell Tate, RB Tyjae Spears, P Tommy Townsend, CB Jaylon Jones, OT Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, TE Kylen Granson, and DT Jackie Marshall inactive for Week 8 against the Bengals. Ridley will be one of the Titans’ top pass-catchers with Carnell Tate (shoulder) already ruled out, but is not more than a touchdown-dependent fantasy WR4 this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter named Calvin Ridley as a potential trade candidate.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Schefter threw out several names, many of whom have already been bandied about as trade candidates. Among the lesser-discussed options, he included Jerry Jeudy and Jauan Jennings in addition to Ridley. All three are veteran wideouts who have simply disappeared in the current iterations of their respective offenses. Even with new landing spots in the cards for the trio, none of them are worth holding onto in standard fantasy leagues. Ridley has five catches for 81 yards this year. He is expected to play through his hip injury today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 8 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: He got in a full session on Friday and would seem to be trending towards playing. With Carnell Tate down this week, Elic Ayomanor is probably the Titans dart throw wideout for the desperate against the Bengals if you’re choosing between him or Ridley.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) returned to practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley did not practice once last week. He was listed as questionable on Friday but never appeared likely to suit up and was eventually ruled out ahead of kickoff. Elic Ayomanor popped up for 44 yards on three catches and seven targets in his absence. Ridley’s return will prevent Ayomanor from building any momentum.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 7 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: He didn’t practice Thursday or Friday, and we’d consider him on the pessimistic side of questionable. Not that you were thinking about playing him anyway.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Firmly off the fantasy radar when healthy, Ridley downgraded from a limited session on Wednesday and does not seem likely to play in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: The 31-year-old player has a hip injury. Ridley mostly runs cardio and game day and is not fantasy-relevant at this time. Were he to sit, Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike could get more playing time — which would be a positive outcome for the offense as a whole.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley caught 2-of-3 targets for 33 yards in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Is this doing anything for anybody? Ridley had a 23-yarder to open the game and vanished thereafter. He has not cracked more than two catches or three targets all year and does not need to be in fantasy consideration in the vast, vast majority of leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley failed to catch his only target in the Titans’ Week 3 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley has been held without a catch in 2-of-3 games this year. He’s losing routes to Elic Ayomanor and not earning targets when on the field. He can be cut even in the deepest of leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason had eight rushes for 20 yards in the Vikings’ Week 8 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason led the team in carries, as Aaron Jones — who came into the game with a knee issue — saw five rushing attempts on the day. Jones remained the team’s pass-catching option out of the backfield while Mason could not get anything going on the ground against a middling Lions rush defense. Mason, who had 15 carries last week, will remain a touchdown-dependent RB3 option in Week 9 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Aaron Jones is considered “day-to-day” after suffering a knee injury in Week 7’s win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Jones’ status will be one to watch this week as the Vikings prepare for their Week 8 matchup against the Lions. While the team calling him day-to-day is encouraging, Jones was already dealing with a knee injury entering Week 7, so it wouldn’t be surprising if the Vikings opted to sit him this week to give him some additional time to recover. Jordan Mason, who rushed 15 times for 68 yards in Sunday’s win over the Colts could be in line for a busy day against the Lions if Jones is unable to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason rushed 15 times for 68 yards in the Vikings’ Week 7 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason did not start for the Vikings, but out-touched and out-snapped Aaron Jones. He was the primary early-down back and saw two targets as well, though he did not catch either of them. Jones (knee) exited the game in the fourth quarter, leading to Mason finishing out the game for the Vikings. Even before the Jones injury, Mason was the the back with the highest utilization. Mason is a low-end fantasy RB2 heading into a soft Week 8 matchup against the Lions; he could emerge as a top-15 option if Jones misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason (thumb) is active for Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: The Vikings activated Mason off injured reserve and he is officially active for the first time since suffering a thumb injury in Week 1. He will split backfield touches with Aaron Jones, with Jones likely getting more of the passing-down work and Mason more the early-down work. Mason is a fantasy RB3 in his return. The Vikings declared S Jakobe Thomas, QB Max Brosmer, CB Chuck Demmings, RB Demond Claiborne, DL Elijah Willliams and OT Caleb Tiernan inactive for Week 7 against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Vikings plan to activate Jordan Mason (thumb) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason came into the season as the presumed lead back in a timeshare with Aaron Jones, the latter of whom has performed as a true workhorse in Mason’s absence. Although it could take a week or two for Mason to fully regain the lead back role, his presence significantly mutes the potential of Jones. Expect a near-even split when the Vikings take on the Colts in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason (thumb) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason practiced in full all week. He seemingly has good odds of suiting up, but sometimes NFL teams will give players extra time off when they are returning from injured reserve. If Mason plays this weekend, he should be able to handle his normal lead-rushing role. In that case, he can be started as an RB2/FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason (thumb) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason is firmly on track to play in Week 7 against the Colts. He should tentatively be expected to lead the backfield in carries right away, with Aaron Jones potentially settling into a 1B role. The Colts’ defense is not an imposing unit, so both running backs are FLEX-viable this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Vikings designated Jordan Mason (thumb/IR) to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: His 21-day practice window will open; most of the reporting is that the Vikings expect him to play in Week 7. Assuming that’s the case, we expect to see him hit the ground running on the Wednesday practice report with at least a limited session and perhaps a full.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: The Athletic’s Alec Lewis believes the Vikings could target a running back with ‘home-run burst’ in a move for the trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Lewis connects the Vikings to Chargers backs Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal as well as Tennessee’s Tony Pollard, Tampa Bay’s Kenneth Gainwell, and Arizona’s Tyler Allgeier. These are just whispers at the moment, but any kind of costly trade acquisition would cut into the playing time and fantasy value of Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones. The Vikings have clearly already been shuffling depth pieces around so we believe there could be more urgency there as the trade deadline gets closer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Vikings “hope” to get Jordan Mason (thumb) back from injured reserve for Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Late last week, Fowler’s colleague, Kevin Seifert, reported that Mason is expected to return in Week 7 as well. Add him if he is available. Mason is not involved much as a receiver, but his expected rushing workload makes him a reliable FLEX with RB2 upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 2-of-5 targets for six yards in the Falcons’ Week 8 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts’ 20 percent target share would have been good for at least TE2 fantasy numbers on a normal day. This game was anything but normal. Pitts and Jahan Dotson were the only Falcons pass-catchers with multiple receptions. Michael Penix only completed eight passes, so there simply wasn’t enough production to go around. He was intercepted four times and the Falcons were shut out. Pitts role as a PPR merchant should tick back up in Week 9 versus the Bengals. He will be back in the TE2 mix for that contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught all five of his targets for 22 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: The touchdown is nice to see, and Pitts finished tied for second on the team in both catches and targets. However, preliminary snap counts say he played on 37 of the team’s 67 snaps and ran a route on 20 of their 37 dropbacks. Charlie Woerner ran a route on 11 dropbacks and Austin Hooper ran a route on 10 dropbacks, so the Falcons continue to get tons of tight ends on the field. That makes Pitts more of a high-end TE2 option, really solely because of good touchdown equity.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 5-of-7 targets for 60 yards and two touchdowns in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts was one of the beneficiaries of a pass-heavy second half for a Falcons offense that was forced to abandon the run game facing a multi-touchdown deficit. Pitts took advantage of single coverage a couple times, including on his first touchdown grab. He now has three touchdowns over his past two games as Michael Penix brings some stability to the Atlanta offense. Pitts, who ran a route on 26 of the team’s 38 drop backs against Chicago, will be a viable play in Week 7 against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 5-of-6 targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts remained largely confined to short area work with his game-long reception going for only 13 yards. A second quarter touchdown from five yards out gave the veteran tight end his first trip to paint through five games and his five receptions doubled that of his previous four appearances. Pitts remains a difficult weekly start for as long as Drake London and Bijan Robinson remain healthy. A Week 6 meeting with the Bears in Atlanta should see him remain in the TE2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught all three targets for 47 yards in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts played just one snap on the team’s first two possessions before seeing modest usage the rest of the game. His counting stats were padded in the second half with a 28-yard, catch-and-run reception on a play action pass out of the flat. Pitts isn’t getting the snaps or route participation to return consistent fantasy production and is best left on fantasy benches for as long as Drake London remains healthy. That won’t change ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 1-of-2 targets for five yards in the Falcons’ Week 3 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts was the recipient of Michael Penix’s first completion of the 2026 season, with the latter making his season debut following ACL surgery. The return of his starting quarterback was not enough to give Pitts his first fantasy-relevant performance of the season as he watched blocking tight end Austin Hooper score the lone receiving touchdown of the evening from five yards out in the second quarter. Fantasy managers are stuck in the constant hype cycle with Pitts with very little to show for it through three games, making Pitts a difficult start on the road against the Saints in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 1-of-3 targets for 15 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Cooper Rush was a disaster once again, tanking the fantasy prospects of every Falcon. Pitts narrowly avoided his second straight bagel with a lone catch late in the second quarter. He failed to catch his only target last week. There’s not much to say about Pitts and the entire offense when Rush simply shuts down all production from the jump. Pitts will reclaim a spot in the TE1 ranks if Michael Penix is back for Week 3. He is not on the fantasy radar if Rush is under center once again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowlers reports Michael Penix (knee) is “not yet ready for live game action.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Fowler said Penix, still recovering from his 2025 ACL injury, “wants to be fully confident before stepping onto the field. And my understanding is the Falcons are leaving the comfort level part of his recovery up to him.” “Penix is coming off his third ACL reconstruction, which is a lot of ACL reconstructions,” ESPN’s Dan Graziano added. “I believe it takes a lot of mental work to convince yourself it’s OK to go back out there and play. If Penix needs more time, I’m sure the Falcons will give it to him, though I believe we will see him on the field at some point this season.” That would leave Tua Tagovailoa as the team’s presumed starter if Tua can play through the oblique strain that sidelined him in Week 1 against the Steelers. If Tua can’t go, the Falcons could be forced to start Cooper Rush for another game or two. Rush, who had the lowest drop back EPA of any QB in Week 1, makes Drake London and Kyle Pitts iffy starts in 12-team fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts Sr. had no catches on one target in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts owes most of this to a poor performance by Cooper Rush under center. Pitts played on 39 of the team’s 61 snaps and ran a route on 22 of their 29 dropbacks. He simply wasn’t a factor with Rush struggling to move the ball down the field. We should note that the Falcons were very run-heavy with Rush at quarterback, and Charlie Woerner played 38 snaps and was on the field for 22 run-blocking snaps to just 16 for Pitts. If the Falcons are going to continue to be so focused on rushing the ball, that could cut into some of Pitts’ snaps and usage.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Falcons TE Kyle Pitts caught 3-of-3 targets for 59 yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts ripped off multiple double-digit gains, moved well and looked tough to bring down. He delivered a 37-yard catch on the Falcons’ first drive, securing the pass on a quick out route from bunch formation before taking off down the right sideline. He later had a 16-yard gain on a sort crossing route, where he again chewed up yards after the catch. Pitts is a mid-tier TE1 entering the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren caught 4-of-10 targets for 18 yards in the Colts’ Week 8 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: As if that inefficiency was not enough, Warren also batted a late second quarter target into the air for an “interception” that turned into a 92-yard Jaguars touchdown. Brutal stuff, not that it’s anything new in a season where Warren has only two touchdowns and is averaging an abysmal 6.8 yards per reception. Daniel Jones is not playing well, but his seemingly inevitable benching would only make things worse with Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard as the “alternatives.” Warren will be a low-end TE1 for Week 9 against the Cowboys. That is at least an A+ matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Tyler Warren (groin) is “good to go” for Indianapolis’ Week 8 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Warren was limited in practice on Thursday and Wednesday and will return to a rough receiver corps against a Jaguars defense coming off bye. Warren remains a startable TE1, but it’s hard to forge much of a ceiling case for him at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren (groin) was limited in practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: It was his second consecutive limited showing following two missed games, with his level of activity Friday likely to be telling as it pertains to a potential return in Week 8. Warren’s absence has been felt hard by a Colts offense that has struggled to move the football consistently. He would likely return to a sizable role over the middle of the field against the pass-funnel Jaguars, if active in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren (groin) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: This is Warren’s first practice in two weeks, indicating he’s close to making a return. With Josh Downs failing to step up in his absence, the Colts desperately need Warren back in the lineup as their de facto WR1. Downs has also requested a trade, which would open up even more work for him. If all goes well in practice this week, Warren will be back in the TE1 mix for his Week 8 matchup with the Jags.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Colts declared TE Tyler Warren, LB Bryce Boettcher, LB CJ Allen, CB Sauce Gardner, TE Tyler Warren, WR Anthony Gould, G Dalton Tucker, and QB Riley Leonard inactive for Week 7 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Warren was declared out earlier in the week due to a groin injury. Sauce Gardner (calf) and Anthony Gould (concussion) were also already declared out while Bryce Boettcher (groin) and CJ Allen (ankle) were declared out after having a questionable tag. Riley Leonard will serve as the team’s emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren (groin) will not play in Week 7 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Warren was a DNP throughout the week and has now been ruled out for this week’s game against the Vikings. This will be the second straight missed game for Warren, who first suffered the injury in last Friday’s practice. The Vikings have allowed the fewest fantasy points to opposing tight ends this season, meaning fantasy managers are best off avoiding Will Mallory and Mo Alie-Cox as streaming options this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren (groin) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: He’s firmly on the wrong side of questionable. The media attention in Indianapolis this week has been spent on the firing of Chris Ballard rather than chasing down Warren’s status, but he does seem very unlikely to play and hasn’t practiced since last Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Tyler Warren (groin) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Warren suffered a groin injury during Friday’s practice last week. He was listed as questionable for Sunday’s game. Though he was reportedly considered a game-time decision over the weekend, the Colts shut him down on Sunday. A DNP today suggests he will miss at least one more game. Keenan Allen led the Colts with eight catches for 82 yards last week. He remains an unfortunately viable PPR scam as long as Warren is out versus the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: Colts TE Tyler Warren is inactive for Indianapolis’ Week 6 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Warren suffered a groin injury during Friday’s practice and was put on the questionable line; this is not great news for his chances of playing in Week 7’s game. Fantasy managers relying on Warren must immediately pivot elsewhere. Also inactive for the Colts are WR Ashton Dulin, LB Jaylon Carlies, QB Riley Leonard (third quarterback), and G Dalton Tucker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Tyler Warren (groin) is a game-time decisions for Week 6 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyler-warren/0.analysis: Warren suffered the groin injury during Friday’s practice. He was added to the injury report and listed as questionable for Week 6. Of note, Warren also dealt with a groin injury late in training camp, though he was ready to go for Week 1 and had not appeared on the injury report again until this week. Even if he does suit up, Warren will be at far less than 100 percent. Expect Josh Downs and Keenan Allen to take on more work whether or not Warren is active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-endri.headline: Jack Endries caught his sole target for one yard and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-endri.analysis: Endries got his first career catch and touchdown at the goal line in the second quarter against the Titans. The 22-year-old saw 11 snaps, getting a few increased opportunities with Tanner Hudson hitting injured reserve a few weeks ago. Endries should not be rostered for fantasy purposes, but enters the scene with his first career touchdown in a win over the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-endri.headline: Bengals selected Texas TE Jack Endries with the No. 221 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jack-endri.analysis: Splitting his time with two years at Cal and one at Texas, Endries (6’4/245) started all three of his college seasons. He caught 56 passes for 623 yards and two touchdowns with the Golden Bears in 2024 but saw a reduced receiving role after transferring to Texas. Finishing 2025 with a 33/346/3 line, Endries mostly lined up in-line with the Longhorns. As a blocker, he has the versatility to block inside and out but needs more physicality to be a consistent run blocker. Endries lacks elusiveness and red zone utility, but has consistent receiving production and profiles as an “F” tight end who could eventually develop into a low-level starter in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 4-of-6 targets for 76 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Gesicki has been a high-value red zone target for the Bengals all season long. His score against the Titans came from outside of the red zone, catching a 25-yard pass for the score in the fourth quarter. It’s Gesicki’s sixth-straight game with a touchdown and seventh score of the season. Pass-heavy game scripts will lift all boats in the Bengals offense but Gesicki remains a high-end fantasy TE2 due to his high amount of touchdown opportunities.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught his lone target for six yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Gesicki’s lone target came on an end zone target from Joe Burrow that resulted in a six-yard touchdown. The 31-year-old tight end has now scored in all five games he has appeared in this season, but has managed just 10 yards on two receptions in his last two games. Fellow tight ends Erick All and Drew Sample combined to catch five passes for 45 yards and one touchdown on five targets. Gesicki has run 15 routes in each of his last two games and is purely a touchdown-dependent option in Week 8 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 1-of-2 targets for 4 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: The Bengals utilized all of their tight ends against the Dolphins, with Gesicki catching just one pass on the day. His sole reception was a touchdown on the Bengals’ opening drive, totaling four on the season and salvaging some fantasy value for those who streamed him at tight end this week. Gesicki’s value is lowered when Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are active; his red zone utilization makes Gesicki a low-end fantasy TE2 heading into the Bengals’ Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Bengals’ Week 4 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Gesicki caught a third quarter touchdown against the Jaguars, his third score of the year. He saw just five targets on a day where Joe Burrow threw 54 passes and Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) exited early. However, Gesicki has a clear red zone role and he led all Bengals tight ends in snaps on the day. If Chase and Tee Higgins (adductor) miss any time, Gesicki is a tight end streaming option for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 3-of-3 targets for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 3 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: After going without a target last week, Gesicki made the most of his three targets in this one. His most notable reception came in the fourth quarter on a fourth-and-two when he broke free across the middle of the field for a wide-open 25-yard touchdown to put the Bengals up 27-24. Gesicki has now scored in two of his first three games this season, but is averaging just 3.3 targets per game. Fantasy managers should be rushing to add him to their lineups for next week’s game against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki was not targeted in Cincinnati’s Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: The rollercoaster ride that is “tertiary target in a Tee Higgins/Ja’Marr Chase-centric offense.” Erick All (2/5 on three targets) lead Bengals tight ends in receptions. Drew Sample (36 of 60) led Bengals tight ends in snaps. Starting Gesicki will pay off at times, but this wasn’t one of them. He’s a TE2 in Week 3 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 5-of-7 targets for 78 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 1 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Gesicki led the Bengals in catches, targets and yards and was the only pass catcher to score on an afternoon where the Bucs’ defense was funneling Joe Burrow to the middle of the field. Gesicki’s score was a two-yarder where he rolled in to the end zone in the first quarter. Gesicki’s yardage total would have been his second highest of 2025. He’s a valuable real-life contributor, but he is going to have trouble cracking the top 18 tight ends on a regular basis with Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown all usage monsters for the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: ESPN’s Ben Baby reports that Bengals rookie WR Colbie Young is competing for OC Dan Pitcher’s “passing target No. 3" role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Baby’s practice notes indicate that incumbent No. 3 WR Andrei Iosivas and No. 1 TE Mike Gesicki are the other two competitors for the role, and both players “had productive springs.” Pitcher also said RB Chase Brown “can sometimes be viewed as a slot receiver,” but those types of comments are common in the summer and rarely pan out in the fall. Iosivas and Gesicki have been helpful contributors, but the fact that the team is searching for an answer at the No. 3 receiving role is indicative of their ceilings. Pitcher believes Young is “going to fight and battle” this summer, and thinks there are things Young “can do quickly and help us.” If he can actually become the team’s third-most voluminous target earner, he could pay off as a late-round best ball pick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught both of his targets for 13 yards in the Bengals’ Week 18 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: Hot off a rebound 2024 season, Gesicki inked a three-year, $25.5 million contract to stay in Cincinnati in the offseason. It became apparent early in the year that Gesicki would not be giving Bengals fans an encore in 2025. He was held under 20 receiving yards in each of his first six games before a pec injury sent him to injured reserve. Gesicki started to turn things around after coming off IR, totaling 35 yards on four grabs in Week 12. At the time, it was his best game of the year. He eventually popped for a few other meaningful games, though he ultimately topped 50 yards just once on the year. He posted a 28/307/2 receiving line in total. The Bengals could save $3.3 million in cap space with a $4.3 million dead cap hit if they move on from him after the year. Either way, we don’t expect him to be on the fantasy radar in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.headline: Mike Gesicki caught 2-of-2 targets for 47 yards in the Bengals’ Week 17 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-gesic.analysis: This is close to Gesicki’s standard statline when the Bengals’ offense is at full strength, which it is at the current moment. They have a rough Week 18 matchup in the Browns, meaning Gesicki probably won’t be much of a DFS play even with the usual final Sunday chicanery primed to be more insane than ever this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 3-of-5 targets for 33 yards in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta had a quiet day against a Minnesota defense that has shut down opposing tight ends for much of the season. He had at least 80 receiving yards in each of that past two Detroit games. LaPorta had been a serviceable starting tight end headed into Week 8, and should have a better outlook in Week 9 against the Bills. He’s been targeted on 18 percent of his routes on the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 1-of-2 targets for 18 yards in the Lions’ Week 7 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: While Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams combined for 244 yards and two touchdowns, LaPorta was an afterthought in the Lions’ offense on Sunday. LaPorta’s first target didn’t come until late in the fourth quarter, and his first catch came in the fourth quarter on an 18-yard play. It was an uncharacteristically underwhelming game by LaPorta, who entered the day coming off two-straight games in which he topped 80 yards and found the end zone. Despite the dud performance, LaPorta will be in the TE1 ranks next week at home against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports “it’s more likely than not” that the Lions work out an extension with TE Sam LaPorta before free agency.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: According to one of Jones’ sources, Lions GM Brad Holmes “does not like losing his draft picks, especially high ones.” A second-rounder in 2023, LaPorta made waves earlier this week when he expressed frustration with his lack of a contract extension on the Pardon My Take podcast. While those frustrations persist, the 25-year-old tight end clarified some of his comments to local Detroit media Friday, reiterating his desire to stay with the Lions long-term. Jones notes that other extensions the Lions have handed out have taken some time to get done. He also cautions that the team shouldn’t wait too long to sign LaPorta as the Raiders are unlikely to waste time making Brock Bowers the highest-paid tight end in football when he becomes extension-eligible after the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta said he wants to continue playing for the Lions long-term.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: Earlier this week, LaPorta expressed frustration in an interview about his contract negotiations stalling in-season. The Athletic’s Colton Pouncy asked him a few follow-up questions today on the matter today, and LaPorta made clear that he hopes to remain a Lion long-term and is excited about the prospect of raising a family in Detroit. LaPorta seemed extremely earnest, saying he felt bad about his comments potentially causing a distraction for his team, but he knows his teammates care for him and want him to be happy and compensated. He handled the issue well and appears to be ready to play hard for a lucrative contract extension, which is good news for fantasy managers. LaPorta is a locked-in TE1 against the Packers this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 5-of-5 targets for 88 yards and one touchdown in the Lions’ Week 5 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta got involved on the Lions’ third drive, making a clutch 12-yard grab on 4th-and-3 while suffering what the officials deemed an unnecessarily rough hit by LB Mack Wilson at the end of the play. He chipped in two catch-and-run plays on the following drive. The first being an 11-yard play that was controversially ruled down in front of the sticks. Coach Dan Campbell called his number on the next play, resulting in an effortless 38-yard touchdown down the right side of the field. LaPorta tacked on an eight-yard catch and a 19-yard catch in the second half as the Lions cruised to a blowout win. He goes on bye next week but returns to the TE1 ranks in Week 7 against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 8-of-13 targets for 84 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 4 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta was the primary beneficiary against the single-high-heavy Panthers, which was interesting considering both of Carolina’s top two corners were absent from this game. The 13 targets were easily a season high for the veteran tight end, primarily the result of 52 Jared Goff pass attempts in what would become a negative game script. LaPorta routinely found space behind the linebackers as the primary outlet through pressure for Goff, and while it remains unlikely he repeats the lofty target totals, LaPorta’s red zone acumen keeps him a fantasy TE1 ahead of a very different matchup in the two-high-heavy Cardinals in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Sam LaPorta and the Lions “have broken off contract talks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: Rapoport did note that the Lions could make another push to sign LaPorta later this year, so the door isn’t entirely closed. LaPorta is set to become a free agent next offseason. The team could, however, place the franchise tag on him. He has gotten off to a quiet start with 14 catches for 144 yards and one score. LaPorta is currently on pace for a career-low in yards per game. He would still have plenty of suitors in free agency, even if the counting stats don’t improve this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 3-of-4 targets for 44 yards in the Lions’ Week 3 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta was a secondary piece of the passing attack in this game, taking a backseat to Jhamyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown. The two superstars combined for 16 targets while LaPorta and Jameson Williams were held to a combined eight looks. LaPorta has at least 44 yards in every game this year but no more than 52. With a solid floor established, all that’s left is for LaPorta to hit on a ceiling game. He remains a mid-range TE1 for Week 4 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 6-of-7 targets for 52 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 2 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta combined with Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs to be the primary targets for quarterback Jared Goff on a night where relentless pressure from the Bills forced the offense to primarily attack the intermediate areas of the field. That could be the norm for this offense moving forward considering the mounting injuries along their offensive line, which are likely to be felt the most against opponents with a legitimate pass rush. That may not be the case in Week 3 when the Lions host the Jets, a team that is likely to also utilize elevated rates of zone coverage. LaPorta has had stark man-zone splits throughout his career and could see less volume due to matchup. He’ll be a low-end TE1 against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 5-of-8 targets for 48 yards in the Lions’ Week 1 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: Week 1 was business as usual for LaPorta, who finished second on the team in catches and yards. After missing time in the offseason recovering from a season-ending back injury and later a minor hip issue, this goes down as a big win for the young tight end, even if fantasy managers aren’t thrilled with his score. LaPorta will project for TE1 numbers when the Lions take on the Ravens next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins caught 10-of-11 targets for 155 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins led the team in receiving yards while trailing Ja’Marr Chase in receptions and targets. He was Joe Burrow’s primary target over the middle of the field in the intermediate and deep areas. Higgins caught a pair of second half touchdowns, catching an 18-yard score to tie the game towards the end of regulation. Pass-heavy game scripts will lead to a high amount of fantasy production for Higgins and Chase, who saw a combined 56-percent target share from Joe Burrow. Higgins is a high-end WR2 for Week 9 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins caught 6-of-7 targets for 148 yards and one touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins came up big multiple times for the Bengals in the second half after they were shut out 13-0 in the first half. He hauled in passes of 10 and 19 yards on the Bengals’ opening drive in the second half to help set up an eventual six-yard touchdown pass to Mike Gesicki, and hauled in a 13-yard touchdown of his own on the following drive. He would also make two catches of 40-plus yards, and came up six yards short of a second touchdown on an impressive 44-yard grab — his longest play of the day. Higgins has gone for 140-plus yards in two of his last three games and has topped 90 yards in four of six games this season. He profiles as a high-end WR2 in next week’s game against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins caught 2-of-4 targets for 22 yards in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins saw just four targets against the Dolphins after seeing 16 targets in Week 4. The adductor/neck injuries didn’t limit his playing time as much, seeing 45 snaps on the day, No. 2 among Bengals receivers. With Ja’Marr Chase back on the field, Higgins’ target volume decreased considerably and he totaled just 22 yards in a more run-favorable game script. Despite the dud, Higgins still belongs in the WR2 ranks and gets a mediocre Ravens defense in Week 7 after a Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Bengals WR Tee Higgins is active for Week 5 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins suffered an adductor injury in Week 4 against the Jaguars and was a full practice participant Friday after DNPs the two days before. Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) both declared active. Though NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports he will play mostly “meaningful plays”, Higgins is in the WR2 ranks while Chase is back in the WR1 ranks this week. The Bengals declared S Kyle Dugger, C Connor Lew, OT Myles Hinton, TE Jack Endries, WR Colbie Young, and DT Landon Robinson inactive for Week 5 against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Tee Higgins (groin/neck) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) will also play. Higgins is likely suiting up at less than full strength, but fantasy managers have to keep him in their lineups versus a Miami defense that is giving up explosive passing plays at the second-highest rate in the league this year. He will be a boom/bust WR2 for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said Tee Higgins (groin/neck) is questionable for Week 5 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins missed the first two practices of the week but practiced in full on Friday. We would consider him to be truly questionable given his one day of practice, meaning fantasy managers will want to check his official game status when the team announces inactives 90 minutes before kickoff. If he can’t go, Dohnte Meyers, who saw nine targets last week, could be on the fantasy radar as a WR4 in deeper leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) was seen practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Chase still needs to clear concussion protocol if he hopes to suit up for Week 5’s game against the Dolphins. That said, he appears to be trending toward being able to play after logging back-to-back practices to close out the week. Tee Higgins (groin/neck), who was a DNP on Wednesday and Thursday was also seen sprinting and running routes on Friday, which suggests he could also be good to go for Sunday’s game. We will check back in with official game day statuses in the coming hours when the team releases its final injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins (adductor/neck) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins is sporting a T-shirt and shorts at today’s practice. We expect to see him listed as a non-participant at the end of the day. Consecutive absences put him on the wrong side of questionable for the Bengals’ Week 5 game against the Dolphins, though he still has at least a small chance of turning things around tomorrow. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins (adductor/neck) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Head coach Zac Taylor told reporters before practice that Higgins would be listed as limited. Not only did he not practice, but the team listed him with a neck injury on top of his adductor issue. He went down with the adductor injury late in Cincy’s Week 4 loss to the Jags. It’s unclear when the neck issue cropped up. With multiple injuries holding him out of practice, Higgins looks unlikely to play in Week 5. With Ja’Marr Chase potentially out as well, Dohnte Meyers could be Joe Burrow No. 1 receiver this week. He should be added in all fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.headline: Tee Higgins (adductor) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tee-higgin.analysis: Higgins went down with the injury in the fourth quarter of Week 4. He tried to play through it but ultimately ended the game on the sidelines. A limited practice today is a good sign for his Week 5 availability. That will be doubly important with Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) also questionable for Sunday’s game. If Chase can’t clear protocol in time, Higgins will operate as the Bengals’ No. 1 receiver. Even at less than full strength, he would be a fringe WR1 play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 1-of-6 targets for eight yards in the Falcons’ Week 8 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: Bucs defenders caught more passes on London’s six targets than he did. It was that bad of a day. Michael Penix was intercepted four times and only completed eight attempts. He managed just 125 yards, over half of which came on a 76-yard throw to Jahan Dotson that was the result of a coverage miscue. There’s simply not much to take away from a game where London’s quarterback plays this poorly. London had gone for at least 60 yards on four catches in every previous Penix start. We fully expect him to get back on track as a WR1 versus the Bengals next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 7-of-10 targets for 66 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London fought through a tackle on a 21-yard catch in the fourth quarter for his first touchdown catch of the season. He was also open for a touchdown earlier in the game, but Michael Penix Jr. sailed the pass over his head. London had twice as many targets as any other pass catcher in Atlanta and should continue to get elite usage in this offense. He did leave the game to be evaluated for a concussion, and while he was able to return to the field, it’s a situation to monitor for early practice reports next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 4-of-10 targets for 62 yards in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London couldn’t get much going against Chicago’s middling secondary outside a 39-yard grab in the second half, with the Falcons abandoning the run game as they faced a three-touchdown deficit. Michael Penix missed London in the first half on what could have been a fairly easy 30-yard score with a better-placed throw from Penix. London almost came down with an end zone target too. No other Atlanta pass catcher had more than seven targets on the day. London will remain a top-10 option in Week 7 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 7-of-11 targets for 118 yards in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London started slow along with the rest of an Atlanta offense that gained just 37 total yards on their first three possessions before a 78-yard scoring drive to end the half. He would add six receptions after the break to push his season average to 127 yards per game in games started by Michael Penix. Penix departed late in the fourth quarter with a ribs injury, suddenly making London’s fantasy managers skittish after the veteran receiver managed a meager 80 total yards in two games without Penix to begin the season. Fantasy managers will want to monitor Atlanta’s starting quarterback’s status in the coming days ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Bears, where London will be a WR1 with Penix or an upside WR3 in his absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 5-of-6 targets for 96 yards in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London turned in his second consecutive usable fantasy week with Michael Penix under center. The low volume can primarily be attributed to just 20 Penix pass attempts in a game Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson combined for 207 yards and five touchdowns on the ground on 33 carries. London could be tasked with more volume when the Falcons host the Ravens in Week 5, for which he will remain an unquestioned WR1 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 9-of-10 targets for 194 yards in the Falcons’ Week 3 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: To make the stat line more impressive, London didn’t catch his first pass until three minutes into the second quarter following a 1-of-5 start from Michael Penix. He would catch his final nine targets on his way to a massive fantasy day, combining with Bijan Robinson to set the NFL record for a wide receiver and running back duo to both go over 150 yards in the same game with three such occurrences. London continues to excel with Penix under center and returns to the WR1 ranks in fantasy circles ahead of a Week 4 meeting with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 4-of-5 targets for 51 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London also had a 25-yard grab called back by penalty. As expected, the Falcons simply rolled out a dead-on-arrival offense with Cooper Rush under center. Rush turned the ball over three times before being benched in the third quarter. Things didn’t get any better with Jack Strand under center. He threw an immediate pick-six and the Falcons promptly pulled the bulk of their starters from the game. With Michael Penix expected to play next week, London should return to the WR2 ranks next time we see him. If Penix isn’t available once again, London will barely register as a WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowlers reports Michael Penix (knee) is “not yet ready for live game action.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: Fowler said Penix, still recovering from his 2025 ACL injury, “wants to be fully confident before stepping onto the field. And my understanding is the Falcons are leaving the comfort level part of his recovery up to him.” “Penix is coming off his third ACL reconstruction, which is a lot of ACL reconstructions,” ESPN’s Dan Graziano added. “I believe it takes a lot of mental work to convince yourself it’s OK to go back out there and play. If Penix needs more time, I’m sure the Falcons will give it to him, though I believe we will see him on the field at some point this season.” That would leave Tua Tagovailoa as the team’s presumed starter if Tua can play through the oblique strain that sidelined him in Week 1 against the Steelers. If Tua can’t go, the Falcons could be forced to start Cooper Rush for another game or two. Rush, who had the lowest drop back EPA of any QB in Week 1, makes Drake London and Kyle Pitts iffy starts in 12-team fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: Drake London caught 2-of-4 targets for 29 yards in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: London also added six yards on one rush as the Falcons looked to do anything to get the ball in the hands of their best receiver. The 25-year-old was an absolute non-factor in this one, largely because Cooper Rush was highly inefficient and ineffective under center. The role is not in question though. London played 60 of the team’s 61 snaps and ran a route on 28 of their 29 dropbacks. However, he will be tough to trust with Cooper Rush (and probably even Tua Tagovailoa) under center. London has a much better matchup next week against the Panthers, but there is some fear that he’s more of a WR2 option until Michael Penix (knee) returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.headline: ESPN’s Marc Raimondi believes Falcons WR Jahan Dotson will “probably” be the team’s No. 2 wide receiver.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drake-lond.analysis: Raimondi believes Dotson’s ability to stretch the field from the perimeter adds an element to the Falcons’ offense that they lacked in recent seasons. Although WR Drake London has been regularly deployed as a part-time slot weapon, Dotson’s presence helps reinforce London’s slot opportunities this season. Great news for all involved.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.headline: Brevyn Spann-Ford caught 4-of-5 targets for 31 yards in Dallas’ Week 8 loss to Arizona.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.analysis: With Jake Ferguson (ankle) felled early, Spann-Ford played 65-of-74 snaps for the Cowboys and was second on the team in targets as Dallas tried to find a solution for the blitz. Spann-Ford would likely factor into the TE2 ranks next week if Ferguson were unable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.headline: Jake Ferguson caught 2-of-3 targets for 13 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.analysis: Ferguson has now been out-targeted by the team’s WR3, Ryan Flournoy, in five of six games, even being out-targeted by fellow tight end Brevyn Span-Ford in this one. The latter caught 4-of-5 targets for 35 yards on a night quarterback Dak Prescott attempted 54 passes. Any fleeting fantasy value is quickly evaporating as the fourth option, at best, through the air. Ferguson can safely be left on fantasy benches ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the Eagles on the road.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.headline: Cowboys signed TE Brevyn Spann-Ford to a three-year extension through 2029.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.analysis: Spann-Ford initially signed on with the Cowboys as a 2024 undrafted free agent. He has caught 18 passes for 178 yards and one touchdown since then. The front office is evidently pleased with his development. He is not worth rostering in 12-team leagues. The deal is worth $18 million with $12.075 million guaranteed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.headline: Cowboys TE Brevyn Spann-Ford was taken to the locker room with an apparent leg injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.analysis: ESPN’s Todd Archer described the play on which Spann-Ford was injured, saying, it “looked like he got rolled up on a run play.” Roll-up mechanisms can impact the knee and/or ankle, but specifics on the injury event are unknown and players are often sent for further examination during training camp out of an abundance of caution. The Cowboys should update Spann-Ford’s status in the near future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.headline: Cowboys ruled out Jake Ferguson (concussion) for Week 12 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.analysis: Ferguson logged his third straight DNP on Friday and will be forced to try again next week. Backup tight ends Luke Schoonmaker and Brevyn Spann-Ford split repetitions in Week 11, with Schoonmaker astonishingly finishing second on the team in targets (10) and Spann-Ford respectably tying for third with five of his own. Schoonmaker can be streamed as a low-end TE1 if need be but be warned: The Commanders’ linebacker corps is one of the league’s best. This will not be an easy matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Cowboys TE Jake Ferguson “could miss some time” with an MCL sprain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.analysis: Ferguson’s Week 1 injury against the Browns appeared much more serious. It looks like he avoided a season-ending injury and could return later this season, though a timeframe has yet to be detailed. Luke Schoonmaker and Brevyn Spann-Ford should split tight end pass-catching duties while Ferguson is sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.headline: Cowboys sign Minnesota TE Brevyn Spann-Ford.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.analysis: After redshirting his first season at Minnesota in 2018, Spann-Ford (6’7/260) caught five passes over his next two seasons. He rotated into the starter role during the 2021 season, starting all 24 of his games in his last two seasons. Spann-Ford finished his six years at Minnesota with a 25-239-2 line for the 2023 season. Though he struggles with drops and physicality, Spann-Ford’s size can allow him to be a mismatch in the passing game. Similarly, he can be a big blocker for the run game. His combine numbers show a subpar athletic profile, running a 4.77 40-yard dash and jumping a 31.5-inch vertical, both bottom-two among participating tight ends. Spann-Ford’s size will be an asset at the NFL level, though he will need to get more physical to make up for a lack of athleticism.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.headline: Minnesota redshirt senior TE Ko Kieft (undisclosed) is available to play in Saturday’s game against Wisconsin.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.analysis: Kieft (6'5/265) was among the many offensive linemen/tight ends who were sidelined in recent weeks, and the exact reason for those absences remains unknown. The redshirt senior is one of two tight ends who will be back in the fold, as Bryce Witham has also been cleared to play. Brevyn Spann-Ford is also in the mix, and that trio will split the tight end reps with Jake Paulson (undisclosed) being sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.headline: Minnesota redshirt sophomore TE Brevyn Spann-Ford (undisclosed) participated in warmups ahead of Saturday’s game vs. Nebraska.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.analysis: Spann-Ford (6'7/270) has been sidelined for nearly a month, with his most recent game action coming in Minnesota’s Nov. 13 loss to Iowa. The redshirt sophomore has been more valuable as a blocker than as a pass-catcher throughout his collegiate career, catching four passes for 25 yards and a touchdown in 12 appearances last season. Spann-Ford has yet to catch a pass this season, but his return will give the Golden Gophers additional depth at the tight end position.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.headline: Minnesota redshirt senior TE Ko Kieft has been ruled out for Saturday’s game at Illinois due to an undisclosed injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brevyn-spann-f.analysis: Kieft (6'5/265) started the Golden Gophers’ season opener vs. Michigan, but was held out of last weekend’s loss at Maryland due to an undisclosed injury. With the redshirt senior set to miss a second straight game, redshirt sophomore Brevyn Spann-Ford’s reps will increase. Kieft caught two passes for 29 yards and a touchdown in the loss to Michigan.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught 4-of-6 targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: Williams scored the Lions’ lone passing touchdown on a short corner-of-the-end-zone grab in the first half. Williams was second behind Amon-Ra St. Brown in targets, functioning as the primary downfield threat with a nice 46-yard catch on a Jared Goff shot down the middle. Williams, who came into Week 8 with the 16th most air yards among wide receivers this season, should remain in lineups next week against a vulnerable Buffalo secondary that has struggled against boundary wideouts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught 5-of-9 targets for 91 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 7 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: Williams wasted little time getting involved early in this one. On the Lions’ fifth play of the game, he ripped off a 24-yard gain to the Packers’ 16-yard line. On the next play, Williams came in motion and snuck out of the Lions’ backfield to turn a short pass into a 16-yard score, giving the Lions their first points of the day. Williams would find the end zone again in the third quarter on a 10-yard touchdown, and on the following drive, he nearly scored again. Were it not for a Packers defender knocking him out of the back of the end zone on a catch, we would have seen a hat trick. Williams’ big-play ability was on display all night, as three of his five receptions went for 15-plus yards. Williams now has back-to-back two-touchdown performances to his name and has gone for 90-plus yards in two of his last three games. His volume continues to be inconsistent, but Williams is capable of breaking any game open at a moment’s notice. He will be a fringe WR2 in what could be a tough Week 8 matchup against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught 2-of-4 targets for 47 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ Week 5 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: The Lions’ speedster only caught two passes today, but he made them count. Williams’ first catch was a nine-yard, fourth-down touchdown on the Lions’ fifth drive. He nearly hauled in a 25-yarder via a play-action target on the sixth drive, but Cardinals CB Max Melton batted it away. He was open for an explosive gain on the next drive, but Jared Goff checked down to Sam LaPorta about 10 yards beneath Williams. A few plays later, Williams dusted his coverage defender for a 39-yard score from bunch formation, hauling in the touchdown pass in stride in the end zone. Goff later gave him another touchdown chance on a downfield throw targeted inside the Cardinals’ five-yard line, but Williams couldn’t secure it. He’ll now take a week off with the Lions’ Week 6 bye, but return as a WR2 against the Packers in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught 6-of-8 targets for 102 yards in the Lions’ Week 4 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: Fantasy managers had suffered through three down games with the middle-round pick before Williams was able to take advantage of a Carolina secondary missing its top two corners. He was kept out of the end zone for the fourth consecutive contest to start the 2026 season but returned his first fantasy-viable outing on the backs of 52 Jared Goff pass attempts. While that level of volume is unlikely to be the norm for the Lions, a Week 5 meeting with the Cardinals provides another opportunity for Williams to return value in a potential shootout. Williams will be an upside WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: The Detroit Free Press’s Dave Birkett reports Jameson Williams will not face assault charges stemming from an incident with a woman on August 6th.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: The incident was reported to the police earlier this month. Jeff Wattrick, spokesman for the Oakland County Prosecutor, told Birkett, “Based on the facts presented to us at this time, the Novi Police and our office jointly concluded that there is no cause to file charges against Mr. Williams.” Williams has been an off-field headache for the Lions since entering the league, but it doesn’t sound like this latest incident will be an issue. He will be on the field for the team’s Week 4 date with Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in the Lions’ Week 3 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: Drew Petzing schemed up a few short and intermediate looks for Williams, but he still finished with a measly 12.5 percent target share. Both Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown saw eight targets. Williams has topped out at four catches through three weeks. His 49 yards today are a season-high. Williams closed the 2025 season as an every-week WR2, maybe even more. That usage has all but disappeared to start the 2026 season. He is tumbling back into the WR3 ranks heading into the Lions’ Week 4 game against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught 2-of-4 targets for 33 yards in the Lions’ Week 2 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: Williams continues to be primarily utilized as a deep threat in the Detroit offense, which is not the development fantasy managers were expecting following offseason reports that his route tree would be expanded in the new year. The mounting injuries along the offensive line have limited Goff’s time in the pocket to the point where Williams rarely has enough time for his routes to develop, leading to the down production through two weeks. Whether either of those two variables changes in the immediate future remains to be seen, leaving us to treat Williams as nothing more than an upside WR3 in the interim. He will be a difficult start in Week 3 when the Lions host the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Lions head coach Dan Campbell said he’s “not concerned” with Jameson Williams’ drops.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: At least a couple times a year Campbell has to tell reporters that he’s not worried about Williams’ sometimes-egregious drops, and that his playing time won’t suffer as a result. “I mean, look, nobody’s more frustrated than he is about it, but what I love is this just shows his growth,” Campbell said. “He bounced back, he gets back in the huddle. He’s not sulking, he’s not pouting about it, he’s not letting it go in the tank.” Williams in Week 1 against the Saints had two drops, one of which could have gone for a long score. He led the Lions with 128 air yards (a 56 percent share) and was second on the team with a 23 percent target share. Williams ran a route on 37 of Detroit’s 40 drop backs. He should be locked into lineups for Thursday night’s matchup against the Bills.
