https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: Jameson Williams caught 4-of-9 targets for 45 yards in the Lions’ Week 1 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: Williams posted a semi-usable fantasy score, but the film was hard to watch. He dropped a perfectly thrown deep shot from Jared Goff early in the game and bungled a pitch later, resulting in a loss. Williams has had these types of games in the past and he generally rebounds well. Fantasy managers can keep him in their lineups for a likely shootout with the Bills next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano believes Jameson Williams could lead the Lions in receiving this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jameson-wi.analysis: Graziano said the “Lions offense is going to hum this season, and Williams is the player poised to take the biggest leap.” That leap, he said, could come as Detroit coaches push Jamo “to expand his route repertoire and contribute as more than just a deep threat.” That in turn could create more short-area and intermediate opportunities and make Williams something more than a boom-bust WR3 play. Williams’ splits with and without Sam LaPorta are concerning, but he should be a high-upside swing in fantasy drafts, especially for those who fade receivers in the first couple rounds.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase caught 11-of-16 targets for 141 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase was heavily involved in a pass-heavy game script, seeing 16-of-48 Joe Burrow pass attempts. He was targeted downfield several times, catching a 30-yard touchdown but being the intended target on a pair of interceptions. It was Chase’s first 100-yard receiving day as he led the team in targets and receptions. The Bengals have a pass funnel to Chase and Tee Higgins, leading to extremely productive fantasy days in high scoring games. Chase is once again squarely in the fantasy WR1 ranks for Week 9 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase is not on Cincinnati’s final Week 8 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: He will play and be on the overall WR1 line against the Titans. Zac Taylor spoke earlier today and said he had no concerns about Chase. Everyone has downplayed concerns about Chase’s ankle for the majority of the week. He will be a smash play against a Jeffrey Simmons-less Titans defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase (ankle) practiced in full Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase quickly puts his fantasy managers’ worries to rest, returning to a full session Thursday after being limited Wednesday. The Bengals will be playing without two tight ends and their WR3 in Andre Iosivas, but their primary contributors remain one of the healthier units as we approach the half way point in the regular season. Chase can be started as a top tier WR1 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Ja’Marr Chase’s ankle injury “is not considered a major deal.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Rap isn’t breaking much news here. Chase didn’t practice on Wednesday, but the Bengals listed him as getting a rest day on top of the ankle issue. It was just a maintenance day for one of the league’s best wideouts. Chase remains in the WR1 overall mix for his Week 8 game against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase (NIR-rest/ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: The rest aspect suggests Chase’s ankle injury can effectively be treated as a non-issue, but NFL teams have played games with the injury report at times this season, so we are cataloguing it here to be safe. Assuming Chase resumes practicing tomorrow, he can be started as an elite WR1, as usual, in Week 8 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase caught 5-of-7 targets for 62 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase caught just two passes for 23 yards in the first half, but he popped up for a 30-yard gain in the fourth quarter on a drive that he capped with a two-yard touchdown to save the day for his fantasy managers. His seven targets tied Tee Higgins for the team-high this week, but Higgins had the far more productive day. He’s still in search of his first 100-yard performance of the year, but Chase has now found the end zone five times and has gone for 60-plus yards in four of six games this season. He’ll be on the WR1 radar next week against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase caught 6-of-10 targets for 77 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase returned from a concussion he suffered last week, seeing 10 targets in a productive fantasy day. He saw a goal-line fade target on the Bengals’ first drive and was later tackled at the one-yard line towards the end of the first half. Joe Burrow missed Chase for a 70-yard touchdown in the second half but Chase made a miraculous catch with his right arm for a 45-yard touchdown later in the half. He finishes with a successful fantasy day and is squarely in the WR1 ranks heading into the Bengals’ Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) will play in Week 5 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase cleared the league’s concussion protocol over the weekend. With Tee Higgins (neck/groin) also expected to play, it’s business as usual for the Bengals this week. Higgins could be on a pitch count, while Chase won’t have any restrictions. Facing a pitiful Miami defense, Chase is in the running for WR1 overall this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) is questionable for Cincinnati’s Week 5 game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: He did fully practice today — it feels like this is trending in the right direction, but it’s hard to know without detailed reporting of where he is in the protocol how likely he is to sit. We’re sure there will be many more report on Chase over the next 24-36 hours. He enters the weekend a true question mark.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.headline: Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) was seen practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jamarr-cha.analysis: Chase still needs to clear concussion protocol if he hopes to suit up for Week 5’s game against the Dolphins. That said, he appears to be trending toward being able to play after logging back-to-back practices to close out the week. Tee Higgins (groin/neck), who was a DNP on Wednesday and Thursday was also seen sprinting and running routes on Friday, which suggests he could also be good to go for Sunday’s game. We will check back in with official game day statuses in the coming hours when the team releases its final injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane caught his lone target for 13 yards in the Ravens’ Week 8 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane hauled in a 13-yard reception from Joe Fagnano in the second quarter after Fagnano came in to replace Tyler Huntley (toe). Lane has yet to live up to the training camp hype he drew all offseason and seems even less likely to hit his stride with Lamar Jackson’s (thumb) in jeopardy. Fantasy managers stashing Lane in deeper leagues can move to drop him at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane caught 3-of-5 targets for 25 yards in the Ravens’ Week 7 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane had a relatively forgettable day through the air, but just missed finding the end zone on a short pass from Tyler Huntley in the second quarter. The rookie receiver ran 30 routes, which were second only to Zay Flowers, but he’s caught just seven passes for 65 scoreless yards in his two games since returning from injury. Lane’s involvement in the offense is encouraging, but there’s not enough here to warrant starting him in Week 8 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane caught 4-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Ravens’ Week 6 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane was immediately involved in the offense after missing the previous four weeks with a wrist injury. The rookie third-rounder caught two of his four passes on the Ravens’ opening drive that ended with a short touchdown pass to Josh Cuevas and ran 22 routes on the day. Zay Flowers (34) and Devontez Walker (26) both ran more routes than Lane on the afternoon, but Lane has been targeted on 21.1 percent of his routes in limited action this season. Fantasy managers shouldn’t be looking to start him in Week 7 against the Bengals, but the early volume is encouraging for a player who was hyped up throughout training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Ravens WR Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is “good to go” and should be activated for Week 6 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: While nothing is official yet, Lane practiced in full all week, which is another good sign for his availability against the Browns this weekend. Lane was one of the most impressive rookies this offseason and preseason. Rashod Bateman isn’t on the injury report, but missed practice during the week with a shoulder. Lane could conceivably operate as the second option in the Ravens passing game behind Zay Flowers as early as this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is questionable for Baltimore’s Week 6 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane practiced in full all week, lending credence to the idea that he’ll be activated. Ravens coach Jesse Minter stopped short of saying Lane would play when given a chance, saying they’d “figure that out,” but said he had a great week of practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Bateman played through the shoulder injury last week. He was limited yesterday, but coach Jesse Minter said he wasn’t worried. Downgrading to a DNP is not a good sign. Meanwhile, Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is practicing fully this week and could hop right into WR2 duties for the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Earlier today, NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported that Lane has “a shot” to face the Browns in Week 6. His full participation furthers that notion. The talented rookie drew rave reports all summer before suffering an unfortunate wrist fracture in Week 1. While he makes for a dicey FLEX if Tyler Huntley is under center, Lane should at least be safely stashed on fantasy football benches in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) has “a shot” to play in Week 6.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Lane, who injured his wrist in the season opener against the Colts, will return to practice this week and could suit up this weekend against the Browns. Lane had impressed Ravens coaches and beat writers through training camp and in Week 1 he caught one of three targets for 11 yards before exiting with the wrist injury. Lane’s return to the Baltimore lineup could limit snaps and routes for Rashod Bateman Devontez Walker. Lane should be picked up in 14-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ravens placed WR Ja’Kobi Lane on injured reserve with a wrist injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane underwent surgery to address a fracture in his wrist and will now miss at least four games on short-term injured reserve. He will be eligible to return in Week 6. Ravens No. 1 WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) is also nursing an injury. Theoretically, fellow rookie WR Elijah Sarratt should be active in Week 2 against the Saints, though it is unclear if he would have a meaningful role if Flowers plays.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Ravens WR Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is expected to undergo surgery “in the coming days.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane fractured his wrist in the Ravens’ Week 1 victory over the Colts, catching one pass for 11 yards in his rookie debut. The 22-year-old operated as a top-three receiver in the Ravens offense and was set for a sizeable role prior to the injury. He was seeking multiple opinions on the injury as of Monday, but Zenitz now reports Lane is expected to have surgery on his wrist very soon. Zenitz adds that the hope is for the rookie to be able to return in a month. Injured reserve will be a consideration for Lane, which would be a four-game absence at the minimum.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 3-of-4 targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in Dallas’ Week 8 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: He added a DPI at the two-yard line to set up another score, and dropped another pass in the red zone. It’s clear that he’s cutting into George Pickens’ production at this point; Flournoy has gone over 90 yards or scored in three of his last four starts. He’ll be a reasonable FLEX play next week against the Colts, although the Cowboys may abandon the pass at some point in that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught all four targets for 70 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 7 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Flournoy is not typically going to see elite volume while playing alongside two true alphas in CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, but he continues to outproduce tight end Jake Ferguson as the preferred third option through the air. His big play potential showed against the Eagles as he caught a 35-yard dime early. Flournoy is, at minimum, worthy of a bench spot and could work his way into viable FLEX territory with another solid outing against the downtrodden Cardinals in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 7-of-9 targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: While the yardage totals continue to remain modest for the third-year receiver, his emergence as a trusted WR3 in the offense has led to him out-targeting tight end Jake Ferguson in five of six games through the first third of the season. That’s a role that can return usable FLEX production in the right matchups in the typically high-powered Cowboys offense, adding to his high-end handcuff value. Fantasy managers can continue to stash FLournoy ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the division rival Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 3-of-4 targets for 90 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 5 loss to the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Flournoy continues to operate as the clear WR3 behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, typically incapable of returning viable fantasy production in their shadows. He hit for a 48-yard reception at the end of the second quarter to set up a go-ahead field goal entering the break, otherwise remaining about as quiet as we would expect. This was the first game in 2026 over a modest 37 yards for Flournoy, who could be tasked with additional emphasis in the immediate future after Lamb departed with a quad injury in the fourth quarter. He could be worth a speculative add ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the reeling Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 4-of-5 targets for 37 yards in Dallas’ Week 4 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Flournoy has been held to exactly 22 or 23 yards in each of his first three games of the season, but the trend of Dallas passing more is pretty good for him. He’s got 21 targets over his last three games. It’s not anything beyond FLEX production yet but Thursday night games can be weird and that’s where Dallas will be next week against the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 2-of-4 targets for 22 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 1 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: The veteran receiver inked a one-year contract extension this offseason to retain his supporting role in the high-powered Dallas offense, but the early returns were less than inspiring. Flournoy played 41 of 58 snaps, nearly every-down work, but the Cowboys just didn’t get enough play volume to let him spike a ceiling week. It’ll be hard for Flournoy to return consistent fantasy production for as long as both CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens remain healthy. He’ll be a boom-bust WR4 in a plus matchup against the Commanders in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Cowboys signed Ryan Flournoy to a one-year, $6 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Flournoy is now under contract through the 2027 season. The 26-year-old receiver caught 40 passes for 475 yards and four touchdowns last season, while finishing third among Cowboys receivers in routes run (273) and fourth on the team in targets. It was reported earlier this summer that he was seeing more snaps in the slot, but it’s hard to imagine Flournoy making enough of an impact to be fantasy-relevant as long as CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, and Jake Ferguson are healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: ESPN’s Todd Archer reports Ryan Flournoy “has worked in the slot more” this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Archer mentioned Flournoy as the biggest surprise for the Cowboys so far this offseason. The third-year receiver totaled 40 catches for 475 yards and four touchdowns last season, and played 34.4 percent of his snaps in the slot. The Cowboys ran the fourth-most plays from 11 personnel last season, per TruMedia. While it’s possible that Flournoy’s increased slot role leads to more production, fantasy managers should take this with a grain of salt. As long as CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, and Jake Ferguson are healthy, Flournoy will face an uphill climb to improve on the 3.8 targets per game he averaged last season. That said, if either Lamb or Pickens were to miss time, Flournoy could have some streaming upside in deeper leagues after he posted a few 100-plus yard games last season in games where either Pickens or Lamb were sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said he really thinks WR Ryan Flournoy “is taking the next step.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Schottenheimer believes the 2024 sixth-round pick “has a chance to be a terrific receiver in this league.” He currently projects as the Cowboys’ WR3 and will likely carry that distinction into the regular season. Flournoy is a worthwhile best ball pick right now, but it remains to be seen whether he will warrant consideration in 12-team re-draft leagues late in August. Flournoy posted a 40/475/4 receiving line last season, while upping his yards per route run average from 1.06 to 174. It will be difficult for him to be anything more than a volatile WR5/WR6, but he will deliver a few spiked weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: The Athletic’s Jon Machota believes Ryan Flournoy will be Dallas’ No. 3 receiver in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: In other words, he expects Flournoy to confine KaVonate Turpin to a gadget role. Flournoy produced in his limited chances last year and, if a surprise George Pickens trade comes to fruition, could have real fantasy upside in 2026. As is, he’ll have WR5/WR6 appeal in what profiles as the third or fourth option (alongside tight end Jake Ferguson) in a good passing offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 19 times for 76 yards in the Falcons’ Week 8 loss to the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson dropped his only target of the day. He has quietly been held under 100 rushing yards in four straight games. Robinson normally papers over that with strong receiver numbers, but that disappeared today as well. Michael Penix only completed eight passes and threw four interceptions. Robinson should have better luck in Week 9 against the Bengals, but the odds of him repeating as the RB1 overall are shrinking by the week. He will sit just outside the top tier of fantasy options in Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Brian Robinson (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Bijan Robinson handled 20 carries and five targets with his backup, Brian Robinson, sidelined in Week 7. The backup should be considered questionable to play at this time, though he could make a late-week return. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 20 times for 63 yards in the Falcons’ Week 7 win over the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson did add 59 yards receiving on five catches to help salvage his fantasy day, but this is the third straight week he has delivered a modest fantasy return after explosive performances in Weeks 3 and 4. In fact, this is now five of seven games this season that Robinson has been held under 90 yards rushing. He’s contributing as a pass-catcher, and he looks elusive when he can get beyond the line of scrimmage, but the Falcons may need to make an adjustment on offense with defenses clearly keying on stopping Robinson. We’d expect them to focus on getting him going next week against the Bucs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: The Falcons’ No. 2 running back was limited yesterday. This series of events suggests Robinson strained his hamstring on Wednesday, putting him on the wrong side of questionable for the Falcons’ Week 6 game against the 49ers. Bijan Robinson would handle a few extra touches in Robinson’s absence. The team does not have a third running back on the active roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson had nine rushes for 61 yards in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears, adding two catches for -8 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson couldn’t get anything going against a Chicago defense allowing the fifth highest rate of yards before contact. The Bears were intent on snuffing out the Atlanta rushing attack and forcing Michael Penix to move the ball through the air. It worked for much of the game. Robinson, who had 425 rushing yards in his previous three games, remains the engine of the run-heavy Falcons offense and should get back on track in Week 7 against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 17 times for 86 yards in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens, adding 32 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson suffered through poor offensive efficiency in the first half, finally breaking loose for a 38-yard carry on the team’s first possession of the third quarter. Although the receiving production and yardage total were enough to salvage a usable fantasy week, it was only the second time in five games in which Robinson failed to find the end zone. Robinson remains an elite fantasy RB1 ahead of a Week 6 showdown against the Bears in Atlanta.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 19 times for 145 yards and two touchdowns in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints, adding two yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Week 4 marked Robinson’s second consecutive game going over 100 yards with two touchdowns on the ground, this time aided by a 59-yard touchdown run on his first touch of the game. The Falcons tied a franchise record with five rushing scores, with backfield mate Brian Robinson adding three to the two of Bijan. The return of quarterback Michael Penix has given the Falcons the threat of passing after dropping their first two games of the season behind suboptimal play from the position, and nobody has benefited more from reduced numbers in the box than Robinson. He’ll look to keep the momentum going as a top-tier RB1 when the Falcons host the Ravens in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 29 times for 194 yards and two touchdowns in the Falcons’ Week 3 win over the Packers, adding 19 yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson single-handedly out-gained the Packers in the first half after clearing the century mark on the ground early in the second quarter. His patience and burst through the gap were on full display, routinely gaining chunk yardage on first down while making the Green Bay defensive front look like Swiss cheese. A 55-yard scamper on a wide zone carry in the first quarter got the All Pro back off to a blazing start, adding his first of two touchdowns to cap the drive. He would take on a second score late in the fourth quarter to send the Packers to their first home opener loss in 14 years. Robinson remains an elite RB1 ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the division rival Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 16 times for 72 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers, adding three catches for nine yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: Robinson did what he could in the midst of a Cooper Rush meltdown, but it’s hard to expect much when his team puts up a grand total of three points. Atlanta also pulled their starters early, allowing Brian Robinson Jr. to rack up 13 touches of his own. Robinson is a volume-based RB1 even when Rush is under center, and he’ll move back into the top three once Michael Penix takes over. That could happen next week versus the Packers on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 21 times for 83 yards in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers, adding 90 yards receiving and one touchdown on eight catches.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bijan-robi.analysis: To say Bijan Robinson was the majority of the team’s offense would be an understatement. He had 173 of the team’s 238 total yards and 29 of the 43 touches by any skill player. He played on 47 of the team’s 61 total snaps and only lost carries to Brian Robinson because the team couldn’t possibly continue to ride Bijan Robinson any more than they were. His involvement in the short passing game, especially given who will be at quarterback, makes Bijan Robinson seemingly matchup-proof for fantasy purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 18-of-25 attempts for 176 yards, a touchdown, and an interception in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: Goff, like all quarterbacks against the Vikings, seemed lost from start to finish, unable to decipher to intricate Vikings blitz scheme. He was sacked four times and saw pressure on seemingly every drop back before the Lions abandoned the pass game for the run game in the second half. Sunday marked only the second game this season in which Goff did not have multiple touchdown throws, and the first time he has not eclipsed 200 passing yards. Goff should be able to get back on track next week against a bad Dolphins defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 22-of-32 passes for 303 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ 20-17, Week 7 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: In a game that felt like it should have featured far more points, Goff and the Lions narrowly walked away with the win. He led an explosive opening drive that included a 28-yard pass to Amon-Ra St. Brown and a 24-yard pass to Jameson Williams, and ended with a 16-yard touchdown pass to Williams to put the Lions up 7-0 early. Goff would again connect with Williams for a 10-yard touchdown pass in the third quarter, and narrowly missed linking up with him for a third touchdown when Williams was forced out of the end zone on a catch on fourth-and-five from the Packers’ six-yard line. Goff did lose a fumble in this one on a botched snap exchange with his center, but it was an overall strong outing for the Lions’ signal-caller. Goff has yet to throw an interception this season and has now thrown for over 300 yards in three of his six games this season. He’ll be a fringe QB1/QB2 next week at home against the 6-0 Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 19-of-30 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in the Lions’ 45-21, Week 5 win over the Cardinals, adding one rush for a one-yard touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: Sacks and a few errant throws under pressure derailed the Lions’ first three drives. Goff got things back on track after that, guiding the offense to seven straight scoring drives, including six touchdowns. He even punched in a one-yard rushing touchdown via a quarterback sneak, marking his first rushing score since 2023. Goff could have boosted his passing yards total with a likely explosive gain by targeting an open Jameson Williams on the first drive after halftime, but he instead checked down to Sam LaPorta in the flats for an eight-yard pickup. The Lions are on bye in Week 6, but Goff will be a locked-in QB1 against the Packers in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 32-of-52 passes for 412 yards and one touchdown in the Lions’ 32-26, Week 4 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: Goff has now thrown a touchdown pass in 27 straight contests, a streak that started in the team’s Thanksgiving day contest against the Bears in 2024. He could move into sixth on the all-time list for consecutive games with a touchdown pass should he throw for at least one touchdown in each game this season. He came within four minutes of breaking that streak against the Panthers, needing a late touchdown to tight end Sam LaPorta to keep it alive in a game the Panthers dictated with their defense throughout. Goff also maintained his clean sheet of no interceptions thrown to start the season but it wasn’t enough to overcome a defense that ceded 445 yards of total offense to a Panthers team without two of their top three wide receivers in Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette. The Lions fall to 2-2, now two games behind the division-leading Vikings through the first month of play. Goff remains a surefire QB1 ahead of a potential shootout against the Cardinals in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 25-of-32 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ 31-24, Week 3 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: Goff and the Lions got off to a slow start with just three points over their first three drives. Things started to click before halftime and Goff rode that momentum to 21 points after the break. Excluding a few kneel-downs to end the game, Detroit scored on five of their final six drives. The Lions have scored exactly 31 points in all three of their games this year. That may be a bit higher than their projection for Week 4 against the Panthers, but not by all that much. Goff will remain in the QB1 mix versus Carolina next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 26-of-38 passes for 327 yards and four touchdowns in the Lions’ 41-31, Week 2 loss to the Bills, adding seven yards on three carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: The Lions staked the Bills to a 21-point lead early in the second quarter, eventually taking a 27-10 deficit into the break. The closest they would get the rest of the game was a 10-point deficit, but the offense finally came alive in the final two frames. Goff tossed a pair of touchdowns to alpha wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and one each to Sam LaPorta and Jahmyr Gibbs, salvaging the poor team performance with an elite fantasy score for managers brave enough to start him on the road in the elements. The Lions fall to 1-1 ahead of a much more forgiving home matchup against the Jets in Week 3, where Goff will look to return another QB1 performance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Jared Goff completed 26-of-39 passes for 206 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions’ 31-30, Week 1 overtime win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: Goff struggled to get much going early on this game, putting up seven points in the first half. The Lions quickly dropped 14 in the third quarter but took their foot off the gas with the Saints struggling to do much of anything. That nearly came back to bite them as Tyler Shough led a frantic comeback while the Lions amassed three points in the final frame. An overtime touchdown to Amon-Ra St. Brown proved to be just enough to come home with the win, though it required a failed two-point conversion from the Saints. Despite the slow start, Goff should return to the QB1 ranks when he squares off with the Ravens next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: The Athletic’s Robert Mays said new Lions OC Drew Petzing spent “the first couple of weeks after he got the job” learning the offense from QB Jared Goff.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: The Lions are retaining “all” of last year’s play-calling verbiage, and “it was on Drew Petzing to learn the offense,” not the other way around. Goff apparently “had as much of a hand in getting Petzing familiar with the offense as the offensive staff did.” Mays believes these developments speak to the command, agency and autonomy that Goff possesses at this stage in his career. We agree. For those who were concerned about the Lions scrapping the tactics that coach Dan Campbell employed as the Lions’ play caller in Weeks 10-18 last year, it sounds like those concepts aren’t going anywhere. Will Petzing be allowed to add his own elements to that playbook? Yes, we assume so. At the end of the day, this year’s offense could look a lot like last year’s fantasy-friendly unit, though. Draft accordingly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: Lions restructured QB Jared Goff’s contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: The move lowers Goff’s 2026 salary cap hit from $55 million to just $15 million and adds a void year in 2030. It allows the team to get under the salary cap before today’s deadline. In 2024 Goff, 32, signed a four year extension that included $170 million in guaranteed money — one of the richest contracts in the history of the NFL. Since the start of the 2024 season, Goff ranks fifth among all QBs in EPA per drop back and sixth in completion rate over expected. He has at least 30 touchdown passes in each of this past three seasons in the Lions’ efficient offensive system.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.headline: The Lions will play a regular season game in Munich, Germany in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jared-goff.analysis: This will be the sixth regular season NFL game played in Germany as part of the league’s international series. It will feature Lions WR Amon-Ra St. Brown, a German-American and the centerpiece of the Detroit offense. Last year St. Brown was fifth in receiving yards and fourth in wideout receptions. The Lions will be looking to bounce back from a relatively disappointing 2025 campaign after losing OC Ben Johnson to the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed 4 times for 10 yards in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans, adding one reception for nine yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine took a backseat to Chase Brown against the Titans, seeing 26 snaps to Brown’s 50. He was still involved in the red zone, but was not utilized as much as Brown as a pass-catcher. Perine’s path to fantasy production will be touchdown opportunities. He is a fantasy handcuff with some desperation RB4 value in Week 9 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed four times for 16 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine saw only four carries in this one, but he turned his lone goal-line touch into a one-yard touchdown to barely salvage what was still a relatively disappointing day. Perine was out-snapped by Chase Brown 38-12, with Brown also leading the way with 11 rush attempts. Perine will be hard to trust as anything more than a desperation RB4 play next week against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Bengals OC Dan Pitcher said the team will “continually assess how that touch share between [Perine] and Chase Brown should play out.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Pitcher suggested that when they run the ball more from shotgun — as they did last week against the Dolphins — Perine’s a better fit for those kinds of plays. The Bengals spent a lot of time this offseason working on an under center run game to get Brown more explosives, but that has gone for naught early on in the season. We may indeed see more Perine in Cincinnati’s running game after they return from the bye week, lowering Brown into the RB2 range.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed 14 times for 68 yards in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins, adding 2 receptions for 10 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine was involved heavily against the Dolphins, a surprising development given his lack of touches to open the season. He trailed Chase Brown by just five snaps on the day, getting involved in short-yardage situations and seeing an increase in red zone snaps after Brown’s red zone fumble in the second quarter. He caught a touchdown running a route out of the backfield and finished with 78 total yards. We don’t expect Perine to consistently see this kind of usage, but he is back on the radar as a deep-league FLEX value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed three times for seven yards in the Bengals’ Week 4 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine only saw three touches on the day, though he had a rushing touchdown called back for holding in the second quarter. He has generally held a pass-catching role throughout his career but ceded all the backfield pass-catching opportunities to Chase Brown on the day. Perine remains a handcuff in the event of a Brown injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed two times for six yards in Cincinnati’s Week 2 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: He added 16 yards on his only catch, making him the third-leading receiver for the game. Perine has 42 snaps in the first two games of the season and looks like a decent stash in case of a Chase Brown injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed eight times for 42 yards in the Bengals’ Week 18 loss to the Browns, adding three catches for 10 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine returned to Cincinnati on a two-year deal in the offseason. He easily took the RB2 gig over rookie Tahj Brooks and eventually parlayed that into a committee role. Perine didn’t log a single carry over the first two weeks but was stacking 10-touch games by November. He finished the year with 84 carries for 382 yards and three scores while adding 17 grabs for 87 yards. Perine was a staple of the RB4 ranks over the final two months of the year. He will likely keep his No. 2 role with the Bengals into the 2026 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed seven times for 25 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 16 win over the Dolphins, adding two receptions for 16 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine got the Bengals’ backfield scoring started with a four-yard touchdown run in the second quarter, but then Chase Brown got the next three. Wild. Brown ended up out-touching his veteran backfield mate 16-9. Perine has been much more involved of late, but it’s not creating standalone fantasy value, and it’s somehow not affecting Brown’s. Brown has a plus Week 17 matchup in the Cardinals while Perine remains off the radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine rushed 14 times for 42 yards in the Bengals’ Week 15 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: Perine saw one more carry than Chase Brown, but averaged just three yards per carry on the day with his longest gain coming on an eight-yard pickup. Perine briefly left the game in the fourth quarter due to a knee injury, and was carted to the locker room at one point. Despite all of this, he returned to finish out the day and should be good to go for Week 16 against the Dolphins. Even if he is active, fantasy managers can avoid him next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.headline: Samaje Perine returned in the fourth quarter of Week 15’s game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/samaje-per.analysis: It’s not often we see a player carted to the locker room only to return later in the game. That said, Perine did exactly that in the fourth quarter after exiting earlier with a knee injury. Perine didn’t even miss a drive despite the injury, and returned to take more carries from Chase Brown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell caught 7-of-9 targets for 142 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Looking to bounce back from a Week 7 doughnut in his return from a marathon injury absence, Mitchell responded with by far the best game of his career. This, even as one of his two missed connections was a heinous deep drop. Geno Smith never stopped looking his way, however, and the quarterback was rewarded with multiple chunk gains. Smith once again failed to get fully in sync with Garrett Wilson. Smith also targeted Omar Cooper Jr. zero times. That was hard to see coming, and will be difficult to sustain going forward, keeping Mitchell as more of a boom/bust WR3/4 than weekly must start. This blow-up effort confirmed he still has life in 12-team leagues, however. That will include for Week 9 against a Chiefs defense that is admittedly much better than Vegas’ porous unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell failed to catch any of his three targets in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: To add insult to injury, Mitchell had a two-point conversion catch called back because of a penalty. Omar Cooper Jr. once again stole the show, reeling in several long catches en route to his second 100-yard game in a row. Playing in his first game in over a month, Mitchell did not appear awfully involved in the team’s game plan. The hope will be that he earns more opportunities next week, but Cooper Jr. may have already cemented himself as the team’s No. 2 receiver. Mitchell will be stuck in the WR5 ranks when he takes on the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Adonai Mitchell (finger) will play in Week 7 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell has been sidelined since injuring his finger in preparation for the Jets’ Week 3 game against the Lions. It was incredibly unfortunate time for Mitchell and his fantasy managers, as his injury came just days after he went for 6-63-0 on 12 targets against the Packers. Mitchell’s return could complicate things for Omar Cooper’s fantasy managers after Cooper broke out for 6-103-1 against the Patriots last week. The Jets rank 13th in the league in plays run from 11-personnel (209) through the first six weeks of the season, which means both Mitchell and Cooper should see plenty of snaps. That said, neither player should be viewed as anything more than a WR3/FLEX play until we see how the target distribution looks with both players active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: It is too early to say whether Mitchell and his surgically repaired finger will be ready to face the Dolphins this week. He is a worthwhile bench stash, though. Mitchell played well early in the year, pre-injury and pre-breakout from rookie Omar Cooper. It is unclear whether Mitchell will return to the No. 2 wide receiver role or if he will be asked to unseat the youngster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell has missed the past four weeks with a finger injury that required a “small procedure” to fix. Though a limited practice today doesn’t guarantee he will be back for Week 7, it’s a big step in the right direction. Mitchell had nine catches for 123 yards in his first two appearances this year. If he’s able to return this week, he would at least earn a spot on the WR3/4 border versus the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) will not play in Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: It was reported earlier this week that Mitchell underwent a “small procedure” on the finger he injured in practice ahead of Week 3. Given that news, it doesn’t come as much of a surprise to learn that Mitchell will miss his fourth straight game with the injury. With rookie Omar Cooper Jr. set to play in his first game since Week 1, Mitchell could face additional competition for targets when he finally returns to the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said Adonai Mitchell underwent a “small procedure” on his hand.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: As expected, he did not practice today. Per Glenn, Mitchell remains week to week. This explains the lengthy absence for Mitchell, who hasn’t played since injuring his finger in practice ahead of Week 3. According to Glenn, Mitchell is moving his fingers around well, which is hopefully a sign that he will be back soon. With Omar Cooper Jr.'s practice window now open, Mitchell could return to a rather crowded receiver room once he is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) will not play in Week 5 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell will miss his third straight game with the finger injury he sustained in practice, ahead of Week 3’s game against the Lions. During Mitchell’s absence, Isaiah Williams has run 59 routes, the second-most of any Jets receiver, but has seen just five targets. Garrett Wilson is the only reliable receiver in this passing game, while rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq is a boom-or-bust option against a defense that has allowed the ninth-most fantasy points to tight ends this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Adonai Mitchell (finger) remains week to week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell will likely miss his third straight game with the finger issue. He suffered the injury just as he was coming on as the team’s clear No. 2 wideout behind Garrett Wilson. With Mitchell sidelined last week against the Bears, Isaiah Williams was second on the team in pass routes, saw three targets, and caught a 58-yard touchdown from Geno Smith. Williams will have some deep-league viability in Week 5 against a Browns defense allowing the most air yards in the NFL. Adonai was officially a non-participant on Wednesday’s injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Jets declared WR Adonai Mitchell, RB Breece Hall, CB Nahshon Wright, LB Kiko Mauigoa, DE Kingsley Enagbare, OL Dylan Parham, and TE Mason Taylor inactive for Week 4 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell will miss another game with his finger injury and Hall will be sidelined with a quad injury he sustained last week against the Lions. Garrett Wilson, with Mitchell out, should continue dominating air yards and targets in the balanced Jets offense. Braelon Allen will take over as New York’s lead back for now and should be in all fantasy lineups against a suspect Chicago run defense. Kenyon Sadiq has some streaming appeal with Mitchell out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 7-of-11 targets for 58 yards in Dallas’ Week 8 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb’s most memorable play from this game was evading three tacklers on a screen to finally find a first down. He had two of Dallas’ six red zone targets but turned them into just one catch for four yards. Arizona’s aggressive defense simply clouded Lamb and dared the other receivers to win. He’ll remain on the WR1 line next week against the hapless Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 5-of-12 targets for 74 yards and two touchdowns in the Cowboys’ Week 7 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: It wasn’t a clean game for the alpha wide receiver by any stretch, who committed two drops and caught only five of his team-leading 12 targets. Despite the poor efficiency, Lamb made the plays he needed to when it mattered most, scoring from nine yards out on a fade to the back corner of the end zone and from 16 yards out on a similar play to the opposite sideline. Lamb has now seen 56 targets in his previous four games, with 12 or more in three of his last four. That level of volume keeps him in elite company near the top of rest-of-season wide receiver rankings in fantasy circles, where he will remain ahead of a Week 8 matchup against the Cardinals at home.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 9-of-18 targets for 70 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb was targeted relentlessly against the match-zone-based Green Bay defense but suffered through an up-and-down connection with quarterback Dak Prescott on his way to middling fantasy returns. The Cowboys managed under 100 yards in the first half and were victimized by two Prescott interceptions deep in Green Bay territory, leading to a game environment that required 55 Prescott dropbacks. Even with a second consecutive middling-to-poor performance from a fantasy first round pick, Lamb is still pacing for a 1,500-yard, 11-touchdown season, plenty to provide a solid return on investment for fantasy managers that used their top pick on his services. Lamb could be busy again in Week 7 against the inside-funnel nature of the Philadelphia defense, where he will once again be a fantasy WR1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb (quad) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb played through a quad bruise last week but exacerbated the issue and left the game late in the fourth quarter. The injury is not believed to be serious and a full practice today means Lamb isn’t at risk of missing Week 6. Despite burning fantasy managers with two catches for nine yards last time around, Lamb remains one of the best fantasy football wideouts in play this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports CeeDee Lamb’s quad injury is not believed to be serious after Week 5’s loss to the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb was on the field for a few more plays in Thursday’s loss to the Buccaneers after his injury was announced. Rapoport reports that Lamb is believed to be dealing with a quad bruise, which is not believed to be serious. Lamb and the Cowboys now have over a week to rest up before facing the Packers on Sunday Night Football in Week 6. Barring an unexpected development, we would expect Lamb to be good to go for next week’s game against the Packers at Lambeau Field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb (quad) is questionable to return to Week 5 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb departed in the fourth quarter with a quad injury. He tried to return but managed one snap before making his way back to the sideline, coming back on the field later in the drive for a two-point attempt. He was shown on the sideline in visible discomfort following the additional two snaps. Lamb managed to catch just 2-of-5 targets for nine yards prior to departing. Fantasy managers will want to track his status in the coming week, although the additional recovery time could allow him to avoid any missed games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 17-of-21 targets for 189 yards and a touchdown in Dallas’ Week 3 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: He simply could not be stopped the way the Texans were playing defense. Lamb feasted on the sideline and against zone coverages — his longest catch went just 30 yards — and he had the go-ahead touchdown with less than 30 seconds left that had FOX’s Greg Olsen wondering why any defense would play him that way when he’d been that productive over the course of the game. He’d never managed more than 17 targets in a game before today. Obviously he won’t do this again, but Lamb has delivered for those who lucked into him in the late first-round mix and will again be a plug-and-play alpha WR1 against the Bucs on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 7-of-8 targets for 112 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 3 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: That makes it back-to-back games of 100-plus yards for Lamb. Lamb didn’t officially find the end zone on this one, but he did come up with a catch on a two-point reception in the third quarter to cut the Ravens’ lead to 24-21. He came up with a few big plays in the fourth quarter, with his biggest being a 49-yard reception on a drive that ended with a KaVontae Turpin rushing touchdown to briefly give the Cowboys the lead. Despite being out-targeted 11 to 8 by George Pickens in this one, Lamb has looked like the unquestioned WR1 for the Cowboys through the first three weeks. He’s totaled 15 receptions for 265 yards and two touchdowns over the last two weeks and is a high-end WR1 in next week’s game against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 8-of-9 targets for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the Cowboys’ Week 2 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb caught three passes on the Cowboys’ opening drive, picking up gains of 15 and 23 yards before connecting with Dak Prescott on a three-yard score. Lamb gave the Commanders fits all day, but strung together another massive drive late in the fourth quarter when he hauled in a 35-yard pass from Prescott, who went right back to him five plays later for a 24-yard touchdown on a pass Lamb had to fight to come down with. Lamb has now scored in each of his first two games this season and will be firmly on the WR1 radar in next week’s game against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 5-of-8 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 1 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Although he lead the team in both targets and receiving, Lamb got off to a slow start while committing an early drop. He would score from one yard out in the second quarter after a Javonte Williams touchdown was ruled short of the goal line and also draw a defensive pass interference penalty in the second half that would lead to a Williams score, but the Cowboys simply had problems creating the chunk plays that ruled the roost in 2025. Better days are likely ahead for the perennial WR1, which starts in a Week 2 home showdown against another divisional opponent in the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Tyler Goodson rushed seven times for 14 yards in Dallas’ Week 8 loss to Arizona, adding two catches for 19 yards on his only two targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: He found 20-of-74 running back snaps against the Cardinals; not bad work but nothing that is making you consider a waiver claim either. Goodson should be held in deeper leagues as a contingency stash.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Cowboys waived RB Emari Demercado.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: Tyler Goodson has had the RB2 role for the past couple of weeks and is set to continue now that Demercado was waived to make room for Tyler Smith to come off injured reserve. Demercado has now been waived twice in two months, and though he may be claimed again, he could also wind up on a practice squad next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: KPRC2’s Aaron Wilson reports the Cowboys are signing RB Tyler Goodson off the Falcons’ practice-squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: Goodson will backfill the roster spot lost to placing Malik Davis on IR at the end of last week. It’s unclear whether Emari Demercado or Goodson would be the head of a committee if Javonte Williams were injured, as both of them showed up with the Cowboys after last cuts. Neither player is a must-roster as things stand.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Falcons released RB Tyler Goodson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: Goodson made an impact as part of the Falcons’ running back room in the preseason but ultimately Brian Robinson Jr. will keep the backup job. Also waived/released by the Falcons were CB Darnay Holmes, DT Eric Johnson II, TE Nick Muse, OLB Azeez Ojulari, DE Cam Sample, LB Channing Tindall, DT Marlon Tuipulotu, OL Brandon Walton, DL Chris Williams, LB Josh Woods, DT Carlos Allen, WR Vinny Anthony, OL James Brockermeyer, CB Cobee Bryant, RB Nate Carter, OL Kam Dewberry, WR Dylan Drummond, RB Cash Jones, OL Riley Mahlman, WR Keelan Marion, DT Devonnsha Maxwell, OT Wanya Morris, LB Daveren Rayner, OL Jaeden Roberts, TE Joshua Simon, DB Keidron Smith, OL Andrew Stueber, LB Bralen Trice, TE Jack Velling, WR Antwane Wells Jr., and CB A.J. Woods.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Falcons signed RB Tyler Goodson, formerly of the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: Goodson was slated to be a restricted free agent, but the Colts balked. He’s a decent third-down back, but behind Bijan Robinson he figures to offer little fantasy value in his age-26 season. At least his last name isn’t also “Robinson,” unlike some backups in this backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: DJ Giddens rushed eight times for 30 yards in the Colts’ Week 18 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: It was the first time Giddens saw any real work since Week 1, where he spelled Jonathan Taylor late in a blowout win over the Dolphins. With Tyler Goodson (one carry, three yards) set to become a restricted free agent in 2026, Giddens will enter the offseason No. 2 on the depth chart. He hasn’t shown much so far, but how could he? He had only 18 carries all season before this game as Taylor stayed incredibly healthy, and those 18 carries were the most among Indy’s backup runners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Colts WR Ashton Dulin (chest) is practicing in full for Week 8’s game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: With Josh Downs (concussion) expected back, Dulin will only be Indy’s WR4. He may see more snaps than usual if the Colts create a(nother) blowout of the Titans, but Dulin won’t be a recommended FLEX play in this scenario. Tyler Goodson (groin) also practiced in full on Wednesday and Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Colts RB Tyler Goodson (groin) is questionable for Indianapolis’ Week 7 game against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: Goodson has been healthy enough to suit up for two weeks this season and recorded four offensive snaps in each game. Even if he does finally shake off this groin injury, you can do better.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Colts WR Ashton Dulin (chest) did not participate in Wednesdays’ practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: Dulin took over the WR4 role for the Colts in Week 6, though he did not record a target against the Cardinals. Interestingly enough, he did record a pass rush rep on defense. He starts out this week not practicing due to a chest injury. With Josh Downs (concussion) also out, Adonai Mitchell might find his way back into the lineup Week 7 against the Chargers. Also out for Wednesday was RB Tyler Goodson (groin).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.headline: Colts CB Kenny Moore (Achilles) won’t play in Indianapolis’ Week 6 game against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-good.analysis: That makes it three weeks in a row for Moore, who has not practiced since the Thursday ahead of Week 5. He’s a potential IR candidate over the weekend. With Mike Hilton on practice squad IR, the Colts cornerback corps shouldn’t be able to limit what little there is to limit of the Raiders passing attack. Backup RB Tyler Goodson (groin) joined Moore on the rule-out list.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Braelon Allen rushed 21 times for 147 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Allen added two receptions for six yards. With Breece Hall a surprising weekend ruleout with an aggravation of his long-running quad injury, Allen got another start and once again made the most of it. Allen’s career-high 147 yards on the ground included a 24-yard rush and 21-yard touchdown where he got the edge and was then not touched en route to the house. In between, he got shaken up on a big hit but appeared no worse for the wear. Although Hall is supposedly in play for Week 9, he was never even supposed to be in doubt for Week 8. For now we will consider Hall on the wrong side of questionable to face the Chiefs’ strong defense on the road. Even if Hall goes, Allen will maintain FLEX appeal. If Hall sits, Allen will be a must-start RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Breece Hall (quad) is inactive for Week 8 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Hall seems to have suffered a rather serious setback with the quad injury that has been dogging him since September. This is easily said in hindsight, but it would seem Gang Green did not handle the issue particularly well. Hall is supposedly “hoping for next week,” but we would consider him on the wrong side of questionable until further notice. Isaiah Davis will serve as Braelon Allen’s breather back. Joining Hall on the shelf are EDGE David Bailey, WR Tim Patrick, CB Nahshon Wright, ED David Bailey, OL Kohl Levao and OL Max Mitchell.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Breece Hall (quad) is “hoping for next week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported an hour ago that Braelon Allen will get the start, but he didn’t explicitly rule out Hall for Week 8. Fowler’s report makes things relatively black and white. Hall will miss today’s game versus the Raiders. He got in three practices this week before being listed as questionable on Friday. Though a Week 9 return is on the table, the Jets’ failure to put Hall on IR, only for him to miss at least five games, suggests his injury is worse than they initially expected. It’s possible he’s held out beyond today’s game. Braelon Allen will continue to dominate the Jets’ backfield touches until Hall returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Braelon Allen is expected to start for the Jets in Week 8 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Rapoport mentioned that Breece Hall is still dealing with his quad injury, though he didn’t explicitly say that Hall will not play this week. For now, fantasy managers should assume he is out, marking his fifth absence because of the injury. Allen is averaging 20.8 touches and 105 yards from scrimmage without Hall this year. He is back on the RB1/2 border for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Braelon Allen (ankle) will play in Week 8 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Allen ended the week of practice with consecutive full showings after being limited Wednesday, while backfield mate Breece Hall officially drew the questionable tag following a week full of limited sessions. Allen would remain an upside RB2 in a solid matchup should Hall be held out for another week, likely maintaining FLEX status should Hall play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) will be limited in Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: This will be the third straight limited practice for Hall, which is an encouraging sign as he looks to return to action since last playing in Week 3 against the Lions. If he’s active, Hall will likely find himself in a bit more of a timeshare with Braelon Allen, who has rushed for 357 yards and a touchdown on 72 carries in Hall’s absence while averaging a solid 5.0 YPC. We will provide an update on Hall’s Week 8 availability when the team announces it, but at worst, we would expect him to carry a questionable tag entering the weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Braelon Allen (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: It’s an upgrade from a Wednesday limited session. We’re pretty sure Allen will play this week and was just being managed on Wednesday, but how often he’ll be playing will depend on how Breece Hall’s situation shakes out on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Breece Hall (quad) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Hall returned to practice last week for two limited sessions. He was listed as questionable on Friday but didn’t seem to be in the running to play by Sunday morning. The Jets ultimately ruled him out before kickoff. That ramp-up period suggests he should be back to face the Patriots this week. Braelon Allen has likely played himself into a large role even once Hall is healthy, but the latter should still operate as the team’s clear No. 1 back this week, putting him in the RB2 mix versus Las Vegas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Braelon Allen rushed 17 times for 104 yards in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins, adding six catches for 30 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Allen almost turned a solid fantasy outing into an RB1 performance in the fourth quarter, but the Dolphins stonewalled him at the goal line. Geno Smith was sacked on the next play and the Jets settled for a field goal. Allen appeared to get banged up late in the game and missed a few snaps on the Jets’ final drive, but he ultimately got back on the field just before the team’s last snap on offense. With Breece Hall expected to return next week, Allen’s days as low-end RB1 might be at an end. Fantasy managers should still hold on to him in case he forces a committee in Week 8 against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Breece Hall (quad) is “unlikely” to play in Week 7 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Rapoport added that Hall might work out to see if he can go, but it’s “a bit early” for him to return. That means he won’t be playing this week. Hall returned to practice on Wednesday but never got in a full session. The team will give him another week to ramp up. He should be back for Week 8 versus the Raiders. Braelon Allen will draw the start again this week, putting him near the top of the RB2 ranks versus Miami.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. was not targeted in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Coming off back-to-back 100-yard efforts since rejoining the Jets’ lineup in Week 6, it was Cooper’s turn to take a zero after Adonai Mitchell had that unfortunate distinction in Week 7. Today it was Mitchell blowing up for a 100-yard day, going 7/142/1 on nine looks. This, as Garrett Wilson still commanded a team-leading 12 targets. Wilson’s unmovable presence combined with Mitchell’s target competition means Cooper is going to be a volatile WR3 going forward, but “volatile” does at least denote upside. He might not be particularly likely to tap into it for Week 9 against the Chiefs. Especially with only two teams on bye next weekend, Cooper is probably best treated as a WR4 rather than WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. caught 5-of-6 targets for 115 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 7 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper was an electric deep threat once again, bringing down catches for 60 and 52 yards, neither of which was his touchdown. He scored shortly after the 52-yard grab by lining up as a running back and cruising past his defender for an easy three-yard touchdown reception. Cooper Jr. is the first rookie in franchise history with back-to-back games with 100+ receiving yards and a touchdown. While we can’t say he has overtaken Garrett Wilson already, this is looking like, at worst, a co-WR1 situation. Cooper will flirt with a WR2 ranking when he takes on the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Adonai Mitchell (finger) will play in Week 7 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Mitchell has been sidelined since injuring his finger in preparation for the Jets’ Week 3 game against the Lions. It was incredibly unfortunate time for Mitchell and his fantasy managers, as his injury came just days after he went for 6-63-0 on 12 targets against the Packers. Mitchell’s return could complicate things for Omar Cooper’s fantasy managers after Cooper broke out for 6-103-1 against the Patriots last week. The Jets rank 13th in the league in plays run from 11-personnel (209) through the first six weeks of the season, which means both Mitchell and Cooper should see plenty of snaps. That said, neither player should be viewed as anything more than a WR3/FLEX play until we see how the target distribution looks with both players active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. caught 6-of-7 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Active for the first time since Week 1, the No. 30 overall pick shook off his ankle issue by recording the first 100-yard outing of his now two-game career. It was a much needed effort with No. 1 Garrett Wilson getting tangled up in Christian Gonzalez’s coverage. The highlight was a 48-yard touchdown where Cooper got behind the entire defense then came back to an underthrown deep ball for six. This was after he had a shorter touchdown called back by a dubious Tim Patrick OPI penalty. Now firmly in the mix for No. 2 status even when Adonai Mitchell comes back from his seemingly never-ending finger injury, Cooper is worth rostering in a majority of fantasy leagues with injuries mounting and bye weeks raging. The Jets have a plus Week 7 matchup in the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper (ankle) is active for Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Up for the first time since Week 1, Cooper should immediately slide in as the Jets’ No. 2 wideout with Adonai Mitchell (finger) still somehow on the shelf. He’s a dart throw WR4 for a contest where the Jets should be playing from behind. Joining Mitchell on the shelf for Gang Green are RB Breece Hall, CB Nahshon Wright, LG Dylan Parham, DT Jack Heflin and EDGE Joseph Ossai.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. will play in Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper had his 21-day practice window opened earlier this week, but is officially set to return after logging a full practice on Friday. The rookie receiver could step into an immediate role for the Jets with Adonai Mitchell (finger) out for at least one more week, but he could still be a few weeks away from fantasy relevance. Cooper played on just five snaps in Week 1 before his injury, but did catch one pass for 30 yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Jets opened the 21-day practice window for Omar Cooper (ankle).
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper has been on injured reserve since sustaining a high ankle sprain in Week 1. He could return as soon as this week against the Patriots, though he could see his snaps and routes limited. Cooper can be rostered in deeper 12-team formats. Garrett Wilson’s domination of the New York passing offense makes it tough for anyone else to post fantasy-relevant numbers for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Jets placed WR Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: The news was first reported by NFL Insider Ian Rapoport. Cooper is going on injured reserve for an ankle sprain. He’ll be sidelined for at least four games with a designation to return. Rapoport mentions that Cooper should be back “shortly.” Cooper could still make an impact in the second half of his rookie season, but he isn’t worth holding in most fantasy formats at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper (ankle) will not play in Week 2 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: This was always expected to be the case, but head coach Aaron Glenn said on Friday, while speaking with the media, that Cooper, RB/KR Kene Nwangwu (back), S Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin), and EDGE Joseph Ossai (foot) will all miss Sunday’s game against the Packers. It was reported earlier this week that the Jets are hoping to have Cooper back “within the next four weeks,” so it wouldn’t be surprising if he also missed Week 3’s game against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) is “week to week, with the hope that he returns within the next four weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: The phrasing at the end of that sentence makes it clear the Jets are pondering not sending him to injured reserve. Fantasy managers who took the plunge in non-dynasty leagues do not necessarily have to hold on to Cooper through the early weeks if something catches their eye on the wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 12 times for 55 yards and a fumble in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans, adding 8 receptions for 46 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Brown saw most of his fantasy production come from the passing game, seeing nine targets in a pass-heavy game script. He fumbled on a handoff from Joe Burrow and also had a receiving touchdown called back for holding in the first half. Despite the dampened fantasy production, Brown saw most of the backfield opportunities for the Bengals, out-touching Samaje Perine 20-to-5. Brown’s production has been underwhelming the first half of the season but fantasy managers should hold tight given his large share of opportunities in pass-heavy game scripts. Brown’s production should regress to see more touchdowns the second half of the season. He is in the RB2 ranks for Week 9 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 11 times for 39 yards in the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens, adding four receptions for 19 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: The Ravens held Brown in check both on the ground and through the air, with his longest play coming on an eight-yard reception. Even with the Bengals scoring 35 unanswered points in the second half alone, Brown was unable to find the end zone, and watched from the sidelines as Samaje Perine vultured a one-yard touchdown run from him down near the goal-line. Brown out-snapped Perine 7-to-3 in the red zone, but that won’t help fantasy managers much. This continues to be a tough season for Brown, who has just one touchdown on the year and has yet to surpass 82 yards from scrimmage in any game this season. He shouldn’t be considered as anything more than an RB2 next week against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Bengals OC Dan Pitcher said the team will “continually assess how that touch share between [Perine] and Chase Brown should play out.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Pitcher suggested that when they run the ball more from shotgun — as they did last week against the Dolphins — Perine’s a better fit for those kinds of plays. The Bengals spent a lot of time this offseason working on an under center run game to get Brown more explosives, but that has gone for naught early on in the season. We may indeed see more Perine in Cincinnati’s running game after they return from the bye week, lowering Brown into the RB2 range.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.headline: Chase Brown rushed 13 times for 39 yards and a fumble in the Bengals’ Week 5 win over the Dolphins, adding 3 receptions for 21 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chase-brow.analysis: Brown took a surprising backseat to Samaje Perine in the Bengals’ win over the Dolphins. He still out-snapped Perine 38-to-33, but a red zone fumble hurt his fantasy production while splitting backfield touches 50/50.
