Las Vegas lines up Brock Bowers as a wide receiver most of the time. Missing both starting coverage defenders would make life tough on the defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Gonzalez has been sidelined with a shoulder injury since last week, missing the Patriots’ Week 4 win over the Bills. Also not practicing were Carlton Davis (neck) and Karon Prunty (hamstring). We’ll see if any of these corners can practice enough to play for Week 5, but Raiders WR Tre Tucker is headed for a good matchup against a banged up Patriots secondary this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots CB Carlton Davis (neck) is inactive for Week 2 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Davis did not practice all week due to a neck injury and was officially ruled out on Saturday. The Patriots will look for reinforcements in the secondary for Week 2 against the Steelers. Also inactive for the Patriots are OT Dametrious Crownover, OT Walter Rouse, TE Tanner Arkin, DT Leonard Taylor, and QB Behren Morton.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Brian Branch left Week 8’s game against the Vikings with an apparent head injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Branch tried to spear a Vikings ball carrier with his helmet but hit teammate DJ Wonnum in the head. Wonnum was later carted off with a head injury and Branch was able to leave to field under his own power. It would be a surprise if Branch returned to the ballgame.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions activated Brian Branch from the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: The team also activated center Cade Mays from the reserve/injured list. Week 7 will be the first game of the year for both players. Branch tore his Achilles in Week 14 last year and has been out ever since. Currently in last place in the NFC North, the Lions desperately needed this infusion of talent to get their season back on track.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Brian Branch (Achilles) is questionable for Detroit’s Week 7 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: After three full sessions this week, Branch is expected to be activated off reserve/PUP and should have no snap count per DC Kelvin Sheppard. He can be welcomed back to IDP lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Brian Branch (Achilles) is practicing in full ahead of Week 7’s game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: He seems likely to be activated off injured reserve after getting the Week 6 bye to get acclimated. Lions DC Kelvin Sheppard has said that Branch will not be on a snap count.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions ruled out C Cade Mays (wrist) for Week 5 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Mays and S Brian Branch (Achilles) are not yet ready to return from their injuries. Starting CB Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring) has been ruled out as well, and DL Tyleik Williams (foot) is questionable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions coach Dan Campbell said it will take a few weeks for S Brian Branch (Achilles) to ramp up before playing on game day.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Branch has officially resumed practicing, but he has a 21-day practice window to bring himself up to speed. The team has handled Branch’s recovery responsibly thus far. He is unlikely to be rushed out there, no matter how poorly the Lions’ defense is playing. We do not expect him to face the Cardinals in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions S Brian Branch (Achilles) has a “really good chance” to return to practice next week, reports the Ringer’s Tom Pelissero.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Branch is still on the PUP list after tearing his Achilles last season. Lions HC Dan Campbell said Branch was close to returning to practice on Friday, though he wouldn’t disclose when exactly the Lions will open the 21-day practice window for the 24-year-old safety. According to Pelissero, there’s a really good chance Branch returns to practice next week. He’ll undoubtedly help a Lions pass defense that has been torn to shreds in the first three weeks of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions head coach Dan Campbell said Brian Branch (Achilles) is “close” to returning to the field.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Campbell didn’t say when he expects Branch to return, but said the fourth-year safety “looks really good” as he continues to recover from a torn Achilles he suffered in Week 14 last season. The Lions haven’t opened Branch’s 21-day window for return, which will be the first sign that he’s nearing a comeback. Branch totaled 75 tackles, five TFLs, and 2.5 sacks for the Lions in 12 games last season and will be a welcome addition to a secondary that has allowed the most passing yards in the league through the first three weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions coach Dan Campbell said S Brian Branch (Achilles) “has a chance” to resume practicing sooner than S Kerby Joseph (knee), “but it won’t be this week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Campbell spoke in a dejected tone when asked about the Lions’ safety duo returning to practice, particularly when discussing Joseph’s outlook. Campbell said Joseph did not suffer a setback, but stopped short of fully explaining the situation. It sounds like Joseph’s recovery stalled. The training staff was focused on strengthening Joseph’s knee, “but there was a little time there where we weren’t able to do everything we needed to do.” The Lions will not ask Joseph to play until he gets his knee as strong as it can possibly be, “and he feels comfortable.” Branch could return to practice in the coming weeks, but at this point, Joseph’s career status seems like it might be up in the air.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions place S Brian Branch on the reserve/physically unable to perform list with an Achilles injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Branch ruptured an Achilles tendon in Week 14 last year. He is still recovering. The Lions also placed C Cade Mays (wrist) on the injured reserve/designated for return list due to his summer injury. Both players will be eligible to return after missing four games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marcus-har.headline: Marcus Harris (ankle) is questionable to return Week 8 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marcus-har.analysis: Harris suffered an ankle injury and limped off the field with trainers in the first half of the Titans’ Week 8 game against the Bengals. He spent time in the blue tent and was subsequently carted to the locker room. Harris is questionable to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.headline: Jaguars DT DaVon Hamilton suffered a knee injury in Jacksonville’s Week 8 game against the Colts and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.analysis: Hamilton got rolled up in ugly fashion in the second quarter and required the assistance of a cart. He was then quickly ruled out for the remainder of the game. That, it goes without saying, is never a good sign. It’s a huge loss for the Jags’ stout defense up front, as seventh-year pro Hamilton has been arguably having his best season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes that the Jaguars could use the 2026 NFL Draft to “boost” their defensive line.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.analysis: The front office could invest heavily in the defensive line, which currently includes three projected starters who have just one year remaining on their contracts. Former No. 1 overall pick, EDGE Travon Walker, is among them and is coming off a four-sack season, matching his 2022 rookie season total. He recorded 10 in 2024 and 11 in 2023. The team could draft an EDGE to groom behind Walker just in case they don’t complete an extension before the season. The Jaguars’ projected starting DTs are Arik Armstead, 32, and DaVon Hamilton, 29. Both players are scheduled to enter free agency next offseason. Given their age, it is reasonable to assume the Jaguars draft at least one interior defender in April. The team is returning every member of their offensive line this year. Shipley believes the Jaguars will use “at least one pick on a developmental offensive lineman.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.headline: Jaguars designated DT DaVon Hamilton (back) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.analysis: This is welcome news for the Jaguars, who have been without their starting defensive tackle through the first five weeks. Hamilton was signed to a three-year extension this offseason after setting career-highs in tackles (56), TFLs (5), and sacks (2.5). The team has officially opened his 21-day window for a return and can activate him whenever they feel he is ready.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.headline: Jaguars placed DL DaVon Hamilton (back) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.analysis: Hamilton will miss at least the next four games with the injury, which is something he’s been dealing with for the last two weeks. The Jaguars signed Hamilton to a three-year extension earlier this offseason after he set career-highs with 56 tackles, five TFLs, and 2.5 sacks. A key member along the offensive line, his absence is a slight downgrade for the Jags’ run defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.headline: Jaguars DT DaVon Hamilton is sidelined indefinitely with a back issue.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.analysis: Hamilton suffered the injury away from the team. Signed to a three-year extension in April, Hamilton is coming off something of a breakout season under coach Doug Pederson. A two-down run-plugger, Hamilton’s regular season absence would be no small issue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.headline: Jaguars signed DT DaVon Hamilton to a three-year, $34.5 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.analysis: A third-round pick in 2020, Hamilton is coming off the best year of his career. He set career-highs in tackles (56), TFLs (five), and sacks (2.5). Hamilton also forced and recovered a fumble. After taking a leap in his third season, the Jags chose to reward the all-purpose tackle with a hefty contract that includes $23 million fully guaranteed. Hamilton can tack on $1.5 million through incentives over the course of the deal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.headline: Jaguars declared DT DaVon Hamilton, CB Shaquill Griffin, TE Jacob Hollister, DE/LB Jordan Smith, and OL KC McDermott inactive for Week 13 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.analysis: Nothing to see here. James Robinson (heel, knee) is officially available as the team’s starting running back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.headline: Jaguars DT DaVon Hamilton (knee) is out for Week 13 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.analysis: Third-round rookie Hamilton was carted off in Week 12 and didn’t practice all week. He’s week to week. It’s poor timing with the tanking Jaguars facing Dalvin Cook on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.headline: Jaguars DT DaVon Hamilton was carted off the field in the fourth quarter of Week 12 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.analysis: The Jaguars selected Hamilton out of Ohio State in the third round of the draft this year. Hamilton recorded his first career sack two weeks ago and entered the week with five QB hits. He has played on half of the Jaguars’ defensive snaps in a majority of his games this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.headline: Jaguars activated OL Jawaan Taylor from the Reserve/COVID-19 list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davon-hami.analysis: He only ended up missing four days of training camp. Taylor started all 16 games as a rookie and should make a leap in his second year. Jacksonville also activated TE Charles Jones and rookie DT DaVon Hamilton.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Browns declared QB Dillon Gabriel, QB Taylen Green, LB Justin Jefferson, CB Noah Igbinoghene, RB Audric Estime, and C Parker Brailsford inactive for Week 8 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Gabriel was activated off of injured reserve at the beginning of the week and will serve as the team’s emergency third quarterback ahead of rookie Taylen Green. The Browns enter Week 8 with a relatively healthy depth chart, making their inactives healthy scratches against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Browns activated Dillon Gabriel from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: In a corresponding move, the Browns waived TE Carsen Ryan to make room for Gabriel, now the fourth quarterback on the team’s 53-man roster. Gabriel is buried on the depth chart behind Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders, and would need a lot to break right for him to have a chance to play this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Browns designated QB Dillon Gabriel (back/IR) for return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: His 21-day practice window will open up. There’s obviously no rush to promote him to the active roster with the Browns already dressing three quarterbacks every week, so this is probably just starting a ticking clock on a trade or cut from the quarterback room.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Browns placed QB Dillon Gabriel (back) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Reporting had the Browns set to keep four quarterbacks on their initial 53-man roster, but this makes a little more sense. Gabriel was not spotted throwing at practice today, and now we know why. Supposedly he suffered the back injury in the midst of shredding in the final preseason game; he’ll miss at least the first four weeks of the season. The team also announced the final roster cuts to get down to the final, 53-man roster. Waived or released were DT Travis Bell, RB Davon Booth, DT Elijah Chatman, G Kinsley Eguakun, DE Logan Fano, WR Luke Floriea, WR Gage Larvadain, T K.T. Leveston, RB Ahmani Marshall, P Wes Pahl, DT Tyreak Sapp, DE Khordae Sydnor, LB Edefuan Ulofoshio, S Zion Washington, LB Nathaniel Watson, and WR Kole Wilson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Dillon Gabriel is “set” to make the Browns’ 53-man roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Browns also reportedly want to keep rookie Taylen Green, and it’s hard to imagine them keeping four quarterbacks on the roster, so something has to give. Our money is on the Browns ultimately trading Gabriel for a late-round pick. Gabriel looked good in his final preseason outing, throwing for 186 yards and three scores. That alone might be enough for a team to give him a shot at a backup job this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Browns HC Todd Monken declined to say whether or not he would keep four QBs on the roster after the Browns’ preseason finale on Thursday against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: In fairness to Monken, it’s not often we see teams keep four QBs on a roster. With Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders already locked into their roles, the question becomes whether or not both Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green make the 53-man roster or if one could be cut/traded. Gabriel turned in a solid outing in the Browns’ final preseason game, throwing for 186 yards and three touchdowns in one half of play, while Green threw for 27 scoreless yards but also rushed for 88 yards on six carries and helped orchestrate a 98-yard touchdown drive in the fourth quarter. With roster cutdown day set for Sunday, Monken and GM Andrew Berry still have a few days to decide the makeup of their QB room before Week 1’s game against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Daniel Oyefusi believes it’s a “likely outcome” that the Browns will make a quarterback trade at last cuts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Dillon Gabriel is the player left off their 53-man roster projection by Oyefusi entering camp, with Taylen Green getting the QB3 gig for the Browns. There’s been smoke around dealing Gabriel for most of the offseason, but it doesn’t seem like anyone is all that interested in the 2025 third-round pick just yet. It does seem likely he’ll be the one available here given the role that former head coach Kevin Stefanski had in the selection.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Dillon Gabriel was second in line in quarterback snaps during team drills on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It might not mean much for the forgotten man in the Browns quarterback room this offseason. Deshaun Watson continues to operate as the team’s starter in offseason practices. Shedeur Sanders is expected to compete for the starting gig, though he’s expected to be an underdog to begin the regular season under center for a revamped Cleveland offense. Head coach Todd Monken appears enamored with Watson, who has played in 19 regular season games since 2021. Gabriel had the NFL’s lowest EPA per drop back in 2025, just ahead of Sanders. The Browns have insisted they would not trade Gabriel this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Speaking on The Ken Carman Show, Browns HC Todd Monken said he “would love” to know who his QB1 is before training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Monken also says he’s “not there yet” when it comes to naming his QB, but it doesn’t sound like he’s against the idea of naming his preferred starter before camp. Recent reports have suggested that Deshaun Watson “looks healthy” and has the inside edge to win the QB battle over Shedeur Sanders, who struggled mightily his rookie season. The Browns have been on the field for three days during their first mini camp, with Watson leading the QB room thus far. The last time we saw Watson, he threw for 1,148-5-3 in seven games for the Browns, but missed all of last season due to a torn Achilles. He’s in the final year of his record-setting five-year, $230 million contract, and could earn the early nod if he impresses enough before camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter said the Browns have “no plans to trade QB Dillon Gabriel.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The reports comes in the wake of the team drafting Arkansas quarterback Taylen Green at pick No. 182, bringing the total number of quarterbacks on the roster to four alongside Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders, and Gabriel. Watson enters 2026 as the presumed starter considering the hefty financials invested in his services, but to say the situation isn’t fluid is a vast understatement, particularly after the team drafted three quarterbacks in the previous two drafts. Stay tuned, sports fans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/seth-mclaughli.headline: Lions declared C Seth McLaughlin, TE Jackson Meeks, DL Mekhi Wingo, EDGE Ahmed Hassanein, and S Bishop Fitzgerald inactive for Week 8 against the Vikings.
Bengals signed C Seth McLaughlin.
https://www.nbcsports.com/seth-mclaughli.analysis: McLaughlin (6’4/304) spent time at Alabama and Ohio State. He transferred to OSU for the 2024 season and started 34 collegiate games at center, including 10 for the Buckeyes in 2024. He is extremely quick off the ball, and shows a high motor, especially in the run game. As a run blocker, McLaughlin is consistent with his hands and aggressive at the point of attack. As a pulling guard, he’s fluid with his hips and well-balanced. He does play high at times, which causes him to lose leverage, and some of that lower body strength. As a pass blocker, McLaughlin is quick at the line of scrimmage, posting a 74.1 overall PFF grade. He allowed just one sack throughout his career, and played over 1,800 snaps. McLaughlin also missed Ohio State‘s playoff run because of a torn Achilles he suffered in November. McLaughlin shows plenty of potential at the pivot, but the Achilles injury likely cost him a shot to get drafted.

https://www.nbcsports.com/seth-mclaughli.headline: Alabama sophomore center Seth McLaughlin is taking the first snaps to QB Bryce Young.
https://www.nbcsports.com/seth-mclaughli.analysis: McLaughlin (6'4"/295) came in the second half against Auburn for normal starter Darrian Dalcourt and played very well. He has started the subsequent two games against Georgia and Cincinnati and excelled in both, so it’s no surprise to see him take the first snaps even if he wasn’t the starter to begin the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/seth-mclaughli.headline: Alabama received a verbal commitment from three-star 2020 T Seth McLaughlin.
https://www.nbcsports.com/seth-mclaughli.analysis: McLaughlin is the rare three-star commit for the Crimson Tide, as there class is usually littered with four-and-five star prospects. He certainly has offers that suggest that a three-star ranking might be too low, however, with Clemson, Auburn, Florida State and -- of course -- Alabama offering the 6-foot-4, 270-pound tackle. He ranks 88th among offensive tackles in the class on 247 Sports list, and 84th among prospects out of the state of Georgia.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/avieon-ter.headline: Avieon Terrell (illness) is active for Week 8 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/avieon-ter.analysis: Starting linebacker Divine Deablo is out with a forearm injury. Terrell, the No. 48 overall pick, made his first start in Week 6 before missing the following game with a groin issue. Also inactive for the Falcons are S Billy Bowman, QB Andy Dalton, LB Drake Jackson, CB Robert Longerbeam, RB Brian Robinson, QB Jack Strand.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/avieon-ter.headline: Falcons signed No. 48 overall pick CB Avieon Terrell to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/avieon-ter.analysis: Terrell becomes the lowest-drafted player in NFL history to receive a fully-guaranteed deal. The brother to Falcons corner A.J. Terrell, Avieon Terrell put together a solid career during his time at Clemson, playing almost exclusively on the outside while forcing three interceptions and breaking up another 17 passes. He’s expected to earn an early starting role on the perimeter in his rookie season and should help improve a defense that was already 13th in net YPA allowed (5.8) last season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/avieon-ter.headline: Falcons selected Clemson CB Avieon Terrell with the No. 48 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/avieon-ter.analysis: Terrell (5’11/180) delivered a strong second season as Clemson’s boundary corner, logging 375 coverage snaps and holding opponents to 21 completions on 43 targets (48.8 percent) for 216 yards while flashing improved patience and route recognition on the perimeter. Despite allowing three touchdowns, Terrell countered with nine pass breakups and an 18.6 percent forced incompletion rate, illustrating how often he played through the hands and stayed connected at the catch point. His PFF coverage grade landed at a respectable 76.9, supported by favorable efficiency indicators such as 5.0 yards per target, 0.58 yards per coverage snap, and a 76.0 opposing QBR, all of which sit in the “quality starting corner” neighborhood. Terrell’s vertical defense showed stability, surrendering only two completions of 20-plus yards and just 9.4 air yards per attempt against him, signaling that offenses rarely succeeded pushing the ball downfield. Poor testing has raised concerns about his upside, as a dreadful 4.64 40 (29th percentile) and 45th percentile 34” vertical are red flags regarding his athletic potential. He didn’t turn sticky coverage into turnovers as often as you would like to see, and he has trouble with physical X-WR types in coverage. However, Terrell’s smooth movement profile and improved zone coverage acumen position him as a potential immediate contributor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/avieon-ter.headline: Clemson has received a verbal commitment from 2023 four-star DB Avieon Terrell.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/avieon-ter.analysis: Terrell (6'0/170) is the 32nd ranked DB of the 2023 class and the 300th ranked player nationally. The younger brother of Atlanta Falcons DB A.J. Terrell, who also played at Clemson, Avieon appears ready to stick with family tradition. Terrell is a native of Atlanta, Georgia and tallied five interceptions in his freshman season at Westlake High School -- where he started for the varsity squad. Prior to committing to Clemson, Terrell had also received offers from Arizona State, Cincinnati, Colorado, Florida, Florida State and Georgia, among other top programs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: Anthony Gould (concussion) won’t play in Indianapolis’ Week 8 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: The biggest news for fantasy purposes with the Colts inactives is simply that Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs are up, but that isn’t exactly surprising. Gould practiced in full the last two days of the week before being ruled out and stands a chance at being ready for Week 8. Inactive for the Colts are: LB Bryce Boettcher (groin), TE Pharaoh Brown, DT Kevin Givens, T Charlie Heck, QB Riley Leonard (third quarterback) and CB Justin Walley (knee).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: Sauce Gardner (calf) will not play in Week 7 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: Gardner was never expected to play this week after it was announced on Monday that he would be week-to-week with his calf injury. His absence could be a good sign for Vikings pass-catchers this week in what should be a plus matchup against a Colts defense that ranks 14th in fantasy points allowed to receivers this season. In addition to Gardner, the Colts also ruled out WR Anthony Gould (concussion).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: Colts ruled out RT Braden Smith (concussion/neck) for Week 15 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: The Colts will be without their starting right tackle for Sunday’s road game against a stout Seahawks defense. Backup Jalen Travis is expected to draw the start in his place and will be tasked with keeping one of either Riley Leonard or Philip Rivers upright. In addition to Smith, the Colts also ruled out WR Anthony Gould (ankle) and CB Sauce Gardner (calf).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: WR Adonai Mitchell caught 1-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Colts’ preseason game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: Mitchell started in place of injured slot receiver Josh Downs (high-ankle sprain), though Mitchell was curiously subbed out for fellow rookie Anthony Gould on third downs, as noted by PFF’s Nathan Jahnke. Mitchell promisingly logged perimeter snaps opposite Alec Pierce in 12 personnel with the second-team offense. Gould averaged 22.0 yards per return on three total kickoff returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: The Athletic’s James Boyd believes Colts WR Anthony Gould could see starting snaps with Josh Downs (ankle) sidelined.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: According to Boyd, Gould “has flashed more as a receiver than as a returner during camp.” The rookie fifth-rounder made a name for himself as a returner during his time at Oregon State, but with Downs sidelined for multiple weeks, there’s now a hole that needs to be filled at the slot position. Gould blazed a 4.39 40-yard dash at the combine this spring and totaled 44-711-2 in his final season of college. He played just 33.5 percent of his college snaps from the slot but had a 90.5 percent slot rate in 2021. We wouldn’t expect Gould to offer much fantasy upside, but this is worth monitoring as the team figures out a temporary replacement for Downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.headline: Colts selected Oregon State WR Anthony Gould with the No. 142 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-go.analysis: Gould (5’8/174) is an undersized receiver who surprisingly played 92.4 percent of his snaps out wide in his final year at Oregon State. Last season was undoubtedly Gould’s best, as the 44 receptions and 711 yards he posted were more than the he totaled in his previous four seasons combined. Despite his size, Gould’s 4.39 40-time and elite vertical and broad jumps were exactly what he needed to catch the attention of scouts. Gould ran only 601 routes during five years in college and spent most of his time in the slot before last season. He may return to the slot as a pro, but the former First-team All-Pac-12 return specialist may be better served on special teams. Gould averaged 16.3 yards per punt return and returned 14 punts for two scores in 2022.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) is inactive for Week 8 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Steelers declared WR Ben Skowronek, QB Drew Allar, QB Will Howard, CB Brandin Echols, RB Eli Heidenreich, and CB Doneiko Slaughter inactive for Week 8 against the Browns. Skowronek will miss this game with a calf injury while Echols and Slaughter deal with hamstring injuries. Howard will serve as the emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 8 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: He was limited all three days. Skowronek carries no standalone value but could eat into snaps for the other Steelers receivers if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Skowronek is not fantasy-relevant and should not be picked up in 12-team formats. His potential return provides Aaron Rodgers with a trusted target. Skowronek also serves as a reliable run blocker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) will not play in Pittsburgh’s Week 7 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Ruled out on Thursday before traveling, Skowronek probably has a real chance to get back in Week 8. With Marquez Valdes-Scantling now on the roster, Skowronek has likely lost whatever desperation fantasy value he might have had either way.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Ben Skowronek (leg) has been ruled out for Week 6.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: We weren’t exactly worried about Skowronek siphoning many targets away, but with him out of the pecking order entirely Germie Bernard should be a wheels-up WR3 for Week 6 now that both Skowronek and Roman Wilson have been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek has been ruled out for Week 5 against the Colts with a calf injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: There hasn’t been a lot of word on what happened to Skowronek. He went into the blue medical tent in the second quarter to have his leg looked at and then headed into the locker room. When the Steelers returned the kickoff to start the second half, Skowronek, who is a key special teamer, was not on the field. He was ruled out shortly after. With Michael Pittman Jr. already out, the Steelers are getting a little thin with their wide receiver depth.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek caught his only target for 22 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 1 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: It was a play-action pass where Skowronek went against the flow of the defense and it almost operated like a screen, with Steelers receivers blocking downfield to create an easy crease for the 28-year-old receiver. Skowronek doesn’t need to be chased in fantasy leagues after only playing 10 of 53 snaps for the Steelers in this one. He’s operating more-or-less in a timeshare for Pittsburgh’s third receiver role with Roman Wilson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers re-signed WR Ben Skowronek to a two-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Skowronek caught five passes for 69 yards with the Steelers last season while playing in a very limited role. Skowronek’s 46 routes run and five targets marked the second fewest amongst any receiver on the team in 2024. A good blocker and willing special teamer, Skowronek probably has an inside track to a roster spot even if what he does isn’t worthy of fantasy interest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers WR Ben Skowronek (hip) is questionable to return to Week 16 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Skowronek was involved early, catching both targets for 25 yards, but departed early in the second quarter with a hip injury and was deemed questionable to return by the team. Already shorthanded at wide receiver due to the continued absence of George Pickens, it will be up to Calvin Austin, Van Jefferson, and Mike Williams to step up for a team fighting to clinch the AFC North against their great division rivals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers elevated WR Ben Skowronek for Week 2 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: The team also elevated Skowronek in Week 1, but he wasn’t a factor against the Falcons and shouldn’t be one this week either. If anything, it’s likely not a good sign for the chances that rookie WR Roman Wilson makes his NFL debut this weekend. Skowronek will have most of his value of special teams this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.headline: Olamide Zaccheus (shoulder) is active for Week 8 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.analysis: Zaccheus and Zachariah Branch will split the WR3 duties for Atlanta today. Neither player is on the fantasy radar for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.headline: Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.analysis: Zaccheaus’ shoulder injury caused him to miss the Falcons’ Week 7 game against the 49ers. Although he is not fantasy-relevant, his absence reduces the target competition for the remaining pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.headline: Falcons declared WR Olamide Zaccheaus, QB Jack Strand, QB Andy Dalton, RB Brian Robinson Jr., LB Divine Deablo, CB Avieon Terrell, and DB Billy Bowman Jr. inactive for Week 7 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.analysis: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) was ruled out earlier in the week, and Zaccheaus is dealing with a shoulder injury and will not be able to suit up for this one. That could mean more work in the receiving game for rookie Zachariah Branch, who might be worth a stash in deeper formats in case a solid game today earns him a bigger role moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Za’Darius Smith (neck) is expected to play in Week 7 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.analysis: The same is true of Gervon Dexter, who is dealing with a hamstring injury. Rapoport added that there is “much less optimism” for Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). That could mean an uptick in snaps for rookie wideout Zachariah Branch. He’s worth an add in deep leagues, but this offense isn’t likely to support another fantasy-relevant pass-catcher.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.headline: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.analysis: Robinson is the immediate backup to Bijan Robinson in the Falcons’ backfield, seeing his best usage in run-heavy game scripts. He was limited with a hamstring injury on Wednesday but is still trending to play Week 7 against the 49ers, barring setbacks. Also limited was Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). Both players are depth options at best behind the Falcons’ star-studded skill players.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.headline: Olamide Zaccheaus caught 1-of-3 targets for three yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.analysis: Zaccheaus has caught exactly one pass in each of his first two games as a Falcon. With Jahan Dotson ahead of him on the depth chart and Zachariah Branch fighting for more work, Zaccheaus is not in the FLEX mix for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.headline: Olamide Zaccheaus caught his only target for five yards in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.analysis: Zaccheaus was on the field for 18 of the team’s 61 snaps and ran a route on 11 of their 29 dropbacks. Rookie Zachariah Branch ran a route on eight dropbacks. Neither player appears to be a major factor on an offense that really wants to run the ball, especially with Cooper Rush at quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.headline: ESPN’s Marc Raimondi believes Falcons WR Zachariah Branch could start the season as a “gadget guy,” before later earning a starting role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.analysis: Branch was a screen game dominator in college, with speed to spare. Raimondi thinks the Falcons will attempt to replicate his Georgia game early on, but Branch has a chance to become “the No. 3 guy, maybe even the No. 2 guy at some point.” Falcons WRs Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus sit in those two spots. Branch is unlikely to contribute meaningfully in fantasy early in the year, but he is worth keeping an eye on in-season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.headline: Falcons agreed to terms with WR Olamide Zaccheaus, formerly of the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.analysis: It’s far from a splashy free agent signing, but the Falcons have work to do to shore up a receiver room that is glaringly thin behind Drake London. Zaccheaus caught 39 passes for 313 yards and two touchdowns in his lone season with the Bears while playing on 580 snaps — his most since 2022. Zaccheaus’ ability to play both out wide and in the slot will give some versatility to the Falcons’ offense, but we would expect more receivers to join the mix in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.headline: Olamide Zaccheaus caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Bears’ Divisional round loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olamide-za.analysis: Zaccheaus signed a one-year deal with the Bears this offseason and wound up being a thorn in the side of Luther Burden’s fantasy managers for the first half of the season. The veteran receiver occupied his normal role in the slot early in the year, but later saw more work on the outside. Zaccheaus caught 39 passes for 313 yards and two touchdowns in the regular season, and finished the year with the third most routes run (335) of any Bears receiver, per PFF. Whether he’s back with the Bears in 2026 or playing elsewhere, Zaccheaus seems destined to play out the rest of his career on one-year deals and will likely ink another deal similar to his current one this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.headline: Bengals declared S Kyle Dugger, C Connor Lew, OT Myles Hinton, WR Mitch Tinsley, and DT Landon Robinson inactive for Week 8 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.analysis: Dugger is ruled out after not practicing all week due to a quad injury. The rest of the Bengals’ inactives consist of healthy scratches and they enter Week 8 against the Titans with a relatively clean bill of health.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.headline: Bengals signed S Kyle Dugger.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.analysis: Dugger was a full-time starter for years in New England before falling out of favor under new head coach Mike Vrabel, starting four of seven games before the Patriots traded him to the Steelers. Now the 30-year-old safety is on his way to Cincinnati, where he’ll presumably start once again. Dugger had 59 total tackles, five passes defended and two interceptions in 16 games (13 starts) in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.headline: Steelers acquired S Kyle Dugger and a 2026 seventh-round pick from the Patriots in exchange for a 2026 sixth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.analysis: The Patriots continue to deal defensive players that have fallen out of favor in their current scheme, sending Dugger to the Steelers just minutes after sending Keion White to the 49ers. Both deals were structured the same, with the Pats swapping late-round picks in exchange for giving up the defensive player. Dugger had started all 45 games played for the Patriots from 2022-2024, but started four out of seven games played this season. The veteran has nine career interceptions, 24 passes defended, and 25 tackles for loss over a six-year career. The Steelers had a need at safety with DeShon Elliott week-to-week due to a knee injury suffered in Week 8. Dugger will mix into a Steelers secondary that needs improvement if they are to make a playoff push.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.headline: Patriots declared DE Keion White, S Kyle Dugger, LB Caleb Murphy, DT Eric Gregory, OL Caedan Wallace, WR Efton Chism, and QB Tommy DeVito inactive for Week 8 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.analysis: Dugger is set to miss Week 8 with a knee issue that kept him limited in practice and landed him with a questionable tag heading into Sunday. Meanwhile, White is a surprise healthy scratch. Both White and Dugger could be on the trade block ahead of the November 4th trade deadline, but for now the Pats make both inactive against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that the Patriots are “shopping” S Kyle Dugger.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.analysis: Rapoport’s report backs up what Jordan Schultz reported on August 20. The Patriots’ new coaching staff is hoping to move on from Dugger. Earlier today, ESPN’s Mike Reiss reported that it has been a “challenging year” for Dugger, who underwent offseason ankle surgery and has played “deep into preseason games” this month.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Patriots are open to trading S Kyle Dugger.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.analysis: Schultz said the Patriots are keen on getting rid of Dugger ahead of the regular season, and are willing to eat part of his hefty contract to get a deal done. Dugger has been unhappy with his reduced role this offseason. There are several teams interested in acquiring Dugger, graded by Pro Football Focus in 2024 as the league’s fourth worst safety. Dugger last year allowed a completion on 79 percent of the passes that came his way. There’s a good chance he’s on another roster by Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.headline: The Athletic’s Chad Graff believes Patriots S Kyle Dugger “may not make the team.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.analysis: Dugger was playing deep into the fourth quarter with third-stringers in New England’s second preseason game, and he finished 2024 with a ghastly 34.8 PFF coverage grade — by far the worst of his five-year career. The Patriots wouldn’t get much cap relief from releasing Duggar, who is making $14.5 million a season, but Graff believes “they might do it anyway.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.headline: Patriots S Kyle Duggar (ankle/quad) is questionable for Week 17 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.analysis: Duggar did not practice on Tuesday or Wednesday but was upgraded to a limited participant on Thursday. The veteran safety played through an ankle injury in last week’s loss to the Bills, but the quad injury appears to be something new. In addition to Duggaer, the Patriots also listed safety Jabrill Peppers, LB Sione Takitaki, and offensive tackle Caedan Wallace as questionable, while ruling out cornerback Marcus Jones (hip).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.headline: Patriots declared S Jabrill Peppers (hamstring) inactive for Week 16 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.analysis: The Patriots also declared CB Marcus Jones, G Tyrese Robinson, OL Lecitus Smith, QB Joe Milton III (3rd QB) and RB JaMycal Hasty inactive. Peppers and Jones are notable losses for the Patriots’ starting DB group. Fellow starting S Kyle Dugger (ankle/illness) will suit up after practicing in a limited capacity on Thursday and Friday. The Bills’ passing offense should still be able to pick on the Patriots’ short-staffed secondary though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.headline: Patriots S Kyle Dugger (ankle/illness) is questionable for Week 16 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-dugge.analysis: Dugger closed the week with two limited sessions, putting him on the right side of questionable as Sunday approaches. Fellow starting safety Jabrill Peppers is also listed as questionable for Week 16. Healthy or not, the Patriots will be easy targets for Josh Allen and a red-hot Bills offense. Allen remains the QB1 overall heading into Week 16.

https://www.nbcsports.com/max-melton/000.headline: Max Melton (knee) is active for Arizona’s Week 8 game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/max-melton/000.analysis: Melton is one of three questionables for the Cardinals that will suit up on Sunday, along with Hjalte Froholdt (knee) and Andrew Wingard (knee). Walter Nolen (ankle) and Jon Gaines (ankle/knee) were ruled out on Friday. Also inactive for the Cardinals are QB Carson Beck (emergency 3rd QB), OL Albert Reese, CB Starling Thomas V, RB Evan Hull and LB Eku Leota.

https://www.nbcsports.com/max-melton/000.headline: Cardinals CB Garrett Williams (Achilles) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/max-melton/000.analysis: The Cardinals lost their top perimeter CB Will Johnson (neck) to injured reserve this week. Fellow perimeter CB Max Melton (toe) is questionable to play. Williams suffered a season-ending Achilles tendon rupture last year, and returns this week to man the slot.

https://www.nbcsports.com/max-melton/000.headline: Cardinals placed CB Will Johnson (neck) on injured reserve
https://www.nbcsports.com/max-melton/000.analysis: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said on Monday that Johnson (neck) could miss the remainder of the season. ESPN’s Adam Schefter broke the news today about Johnson being placed on injured reserve, though he did not specify whether Johnson’s season is for sure over. Cardinals slot CB Garrett Williams (Achilles) and perimeter CB2 Max Melton (toe) are also dealing with injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/max-melton/000.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said he does not think CB Will Johnson (neck) and CB Max Melton (toe) suffered serious injuries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/max-melton/000.analysis: The Cardinals are already without slot CB Garrett Williams, who has not yet returned from last season’s Achilles tendon rupture. Johnson and Melton start on the perimeter. Losing one or both could be consequential against the 49ers next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/max-melton/000.headline: Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison Jr. (heel) is active for Week 16 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/max-melton/000.analysis: The Cardinals reportedly plan to “ease” Harrison back into action today. Teams often cast aside snap-count plans if their recently injured star player is feeling good early in their return, but Harrison has not yet established himself as a player who regularly exceeds expectations. The prudent move is to treat WR Michael Wilson as a fantasy football WR2 and view Harrison as a WR4/FLEX. Cardinals WR Xavier Weaver (hamstring) is also active. The Cardinals declared CB Max Melton (heel), CB Elijah Jones, CB Darren Hall (concussion), S Jalen Thompson (hamstring), OL Evan Brown (personal) and LT Paris Johnson Jr. (knee) inactive for Week 16 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/max-melton/000.headline: Cardinals CB Will Johnson (back/hip) will not play in Arizona’s Week 10 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/max-melton/000.analysis: Neither will (inhale): CB Max Melton (concussion), LB BJ Ojulari (knee), or LB Mack Wilson (ribs) — the good news is that Budda Baker (hamstring) upgraded to full today and has been removed from the injury report. Arizona’s defense looked good against the Cowboys on Monday night, but their cornerback depth will be tested against Jaxson Smith-Njigba and Rashid Shaheed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/max-melton/000.headline: Cardinals CB Will Johnson (back/hip) will not play in Week 10 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/max-melton/000.analysis: It’s a brutal blow to a Cardinals defense that will also be without starting cornerback Max Melton (concussion). The Cardinals will need to make due with backups Kei’Trel Clark and Elijah Jones against a Seahawks offense that is fresh off a dominant performance against the Commanders in which Sam Darnold threw for 330-4-1 while completing 70.4 percent of his passes. In addition to Johnson and Melton being out, the Cardinals will also keep LB BJ Ojulari (knee) sidelined for at least one more week after he was limited in every practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/max-melton/000.headline: Cardinals CB Max Melton (concussion) did not participate in Wednesday’s walkthrough.
https://www.nbcsports.com/max-melton/000.analysis: Melton suffered a hit to the head in the Cardinals’ Week 9 Monday victory over the Cowboys. He is listed as a non-participant on Wednesday with a concussion. It will be difficult for Melton to pass concussion protocol on a short week heading into a Week 10 matchup against the Seahawks. LB Mack Wilson Sr. (ribs) also was listed with a DNP designation. Both players will need practice time later this week to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/max-melton/000.headline: Cardinals declared CB Max Melton, LB Xavier Thomas, DL Darius Robinson, OL Evan Brown, OL Demontrey Jacobs, OL Josh Fryar, WR Xavier Weaver inactive for Week 5 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/max-melton/000.analysis: Melton will miss Week 5 with a hamstring injury, though Will Johnson (groin) will return to the secondary. Darius Robinson (pectoral) and Evan Brown (hamstring) are also out due to injury. DT Bilal Nichols (neck) and OL Will Hernandez (ACL) are both active for the first time this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/max-melton/000.headline: Cardinals CB Garrett Williams (knee) will be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/max-melton/000.analysis: Williams suffered the knee injury in Week 2 against the Panthers and will be sidelined for the near future. Head coach Jonathan Gannon said Williams will be placed on injured reserve with a chance to return. Meanwhile, CB Max Melton (knee) was a limited practice participant. Losing Williams and potentially Will Johnson (groin) for Week 3 is a tough blow to the secondary, but Melton at least has a shot to play against an equally banged-up 49ers receiving group.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.headline: Raiders WR Jack Bech (forearm) is active for Week 8 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.analysis: Coming off injured reserve, Bech is active for the first time since Week 3. He was a small part of the offense before going down, but with this new coaching staff in evaluation mode, perhaps he will see more work down the stretch. He is nevertheless currently off the radar in 12-team leagues. Inactive for the Silver and Black are WR Dont’e Thornton Jr., WR Malik Benson, S Tristin McCollum, S Dalton Johnson, OG Bryce Cabeldue, DT JJ Pegues and QB Aidan O’Connell.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Raiders are expected to activate WR Jack Bech (forearm) from injured reserve ahead of Week 8.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.analysis: Bech has been on the shelf since fracturing his arm in Week 3, missing the minimum required four games due to the injury. He returns to a passing offense that has been heavily concentrated amongst Brock Bowers and Tre Tucker, unlikely to be a usable weekly fantasy asset. Fantasy managers can stash the youngster in hopes of a growing role moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.headline: Jack Bech (forearm) is questionable for Las Vegas’ Week 8 game against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.analysis: He practiced in full all three days. Klint Kubiak was evasive when asked if he would be activated, but players that practice in full three days in a row while trying to come off injured reserve rarely aren’t activated. Bech will be restored to the roster on Saturday if he’s going to play. He doesn’t need to be proactively rostered outside of the deepest leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.headline: Jack Bech (forearm) was a full participant in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.analysis: That’s back-to-back full practices for Bech after the Raiders opened up the 21-day window for the wideout. He’s worth monitoring in redraft leagues in part because the options ahead of him aren’t exactly elite, but fantasy managers don’t need to consider a stash just yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.headline: Raiders designated Jack Bech (forearm) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.analysis: His 21-day practice window will open this week. Bech could, in theory, start eating into Jalen Nailor and Tre Tucker’s snap counts. The Raiders are probably pretty happy with how Tucker has played, though, and Nailor is more of a fit as an outside receiver than Bech is. The 2025 second-rounder is worth monitoring but not exactly someone you should be stashing ahead of his return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.headline: Raiders placed WR Jack Bech (forearm) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.analysis: He’ll miss at least the next four weeks. Bech had five catches for 48 yards and a touchdown in the first two weeks of the season, but played just 11 snaps in Week 3 before fracturing his forearm. The Raiders signed Cody White — he of the three touchdowns in the last two weeks — to the active roster as his replacement.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.headline: Raiders ruled out Jack Bech in Week 3 against the Saints with a forearm injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.analysis: Bech reportedly fractured his forearm against the Saints. Bech earned an end zone target on the Raiders’ fourth drive. The pass was overthrown and ruled incomplete, but Bech was hit by a defender late, resulting in a personal foul. The Raiders accepted it, erasing Bech’s target from the box score along the way. He finished the game with zero statistics and will likely miss a few weeks due to injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.headline: Jach Bech caught both of his targets for 25 yards in the Raiders’ Week 2 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.analysis: Bech got in the end zone last week but was still held to three catches for 23 yards. Without a touchdown to his name in Week 2, there wasn’t much fantasy production to be had. Bech is the WR3 on an offense centered around Ashton Jeanty and eventually Brock Bowers. He is not on the fantasy radar for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.headline: Jack Bech caught 3-of-4 for 23 yards and one touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 1 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.analysis: Bech scored a 15-yard touchdown, running a post route from the slot, on the Raiders’ first drive, bouncing off contact before running into the end zone. Bech’s day was largely quiet outside of that, although Kirk Cousins overthrew him on another post route, and the ball was picked off by a Dolphins safety. Bech remains a touchdown-dependent FLEX against the Chargers next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said the team is still trying to find a wide receiver who is “accountable and can help us on Sunday.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/jack-bech/0000.analysis: He punctuated his point by saying only, “still looking.” Kubiak’s ambiguous phrasing could suggest that the Raiders are seeking a wide receiver via trade, but it can also be read simply as an indictment of players like Jalen Nailor, Jack Bech and Malik Benson. None of the three turned in a great game last night, while Tre Tucker was given the night off. Tucker makes for a boom-bust FLEX option in an underwhelming position group.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Ravens declared WR Elija Sarratt FS Jaylinn Hawkins, CB Chandler Rivers, OG Emery Jones, OG Vega Ioane, DT Aeneas Peebles, and QB Joe Fagnano inactive for Week 8 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: The Ravens will be without rookie guard Vega Ioane, who suffered a knee injury in last week’s loss to the Bengals. While it’s yet another blow to an already banged-up offensive line, the Ravens do have Lamar Jackson returning from his three-game absence after he suffered a high-ankle sprain in Week 4. Hopefully, Jackson’s return can provide a much-needed spark to an offense that has managed just 23 points combined in its last two games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Vega Ioane (knee) won’t play in Baltimore’s Week 8 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Ioane got in limited sessions on Thursday and Friday but was evasive when asked if he’d go at his locker yesterday. In the end, it would have been very impressive for him to play through a sprained MCL one week later. Ioane’s practice augurs well for his chances of playing in Week 10, at the very least. Week 9, on Thursday Night, might be too big of an ask.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Roquan Smith (knee) and Vega Ioane (knee) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Both players missed practice Wednesday, with their return Thursday a good step in the right direction for their availability in a marquee matchup against the Bills in Week 8. Quarterback Lamar Jackson and safety-linebacker Kyle Hamilton were also present at practice Thursday as the team inches closer to full strength.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said he is not ruling out Vega Ioane (knee) for Week 8 against the Bills yet.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: The Ravens’ mauling rookie guard suffered an MCL sprain in Week 7 against the Bengals. He is likely on the wrong side of questionable for Week 8, but Minter said he has been impressed by Ioane’s resilience and thinks he could recover quickly. In the meantime, OL Emery Jones Jr. and OT Andrew Vorhees will compete for the potential starting role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Vega Ioane suffered an MCL injury and will miss time.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Ioane went down with a knee injury on Sunday against the Bengals and did not return to the game. Though Rapoport said the injury is not considered long term, Ioane — an impressive rookie — will be sidelined for a while. Baltimore’s offensive line ranks 20th in pass block win rate and 19th in run block win rate, according to ESPN.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Ravens OG Vega Ioane (knee) will not return in Week 7 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Ioane exited late in the first quarter of Sunday’s game and was ruled out shortly after halftime. The rookie first-rounder appeared on 16 snaps and has started every game for the Ravens this season, splitting time between right guard and center. He was replaced by Emery Jones.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Ravens C Jovaughn Gwyn (fibula) will miss 2-3 months.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Gwyn went down with a serious leg injury in Week 3 against the Cowboys and will require surgery in the coming days, per Fowler. That will leave Lamar Jackson and the Ravens offense without their starting center for at least the next couple months. Rookie first-round pick Vega Ioane will likely start at center for the Ravens in Week 4. It’s a blow to a Baltimore offensive line that ranks 29th in ESPN’s pass blocking win rate and third in run blocking win rate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Ravens signed No. 14 overall pick OG Olaivavega Ioane to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Ioane gets a fully guaranteed $24.2 million deal with a $14.1 million signing bonus and a fifth-year team option. Ioane is expected to start in year one. He primarily played left guard at Penn State, but should be able to line up at right guard, if need be. Vega (6'4/320) earned an 87.0 PFF pass-blocking grade and a 78.6 PFF run-blocking grade last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.headline: Ravens selected Penn State OG Olaivavega Ioane with the No. 14 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/olaivavega.analysis: Ioane (6’4/320) is a powerful interior blocker who delivered one of the cleanest pass-protection seasons among Big Ten linemen in 2025. The 6-4, 328-pound guard allowed zero sacks and just a 0.7 percent pressure rate across 294 pass-blocking snaps, posting a 99.7 percent pass-block efficiency and an outstanding 87.1 PFF pass-blocking grade while committing only one penalty. Ioane also logged 306 run-blocking snaps with a 78.6 PFF run-block grade, finishing the year with only a 1.6 percent blown-block rate on run plays, illustrating his consistent execution in Penn State’s physical rushing attack. Built like a prototypical power-scheme guard, Ioane wins with thick limbs, core strength and excellent contact balance, using strong hands and hip roll to generate displacement on base blocks and double teams. His firm punch and sturdy anchor allow him to absorb power rushers effectively, while his vice-like grip strength helps him stay connected through the rep. With elite pass-protection acumen and the most complete resume of any interior lineman in the class, Ioane projects as a high-floor guard who can step into a starting role on day one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maxx-crosb.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Raiders “currently have no plans” to trade Maxx Crosby.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maxx-crosb.analysis: Crosby was the subject of rampant trade rumors as the deadline approached last year. Nothing materialized then, but the team ultimately found a partner in the Ravens during the offseason. The deal was signed and Crosby had his flight to Baltimore booked, but the Ravens backed out at the last minute after Crosby failed his physical. Crosby’s baulky knee was a long-term concern for the Ravens, though it hasn’t even been mentioned this year. Schefter added that Crosby no longer wants to be traded, which was not a foregone conclusion this time last year. Even in the midst of a four-game losing streak, the Raiders are still contenders in the AFC West, giving them reason enough to hold onto their star pass-rusher.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maxx-crosb.headline: Raiders HC Klint Kubiak told reporters that QB Kirk Cousins and EDGE Maxx Crosby are being held out of practice Saturday for violating team rules for fighting.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maxx-crosb.analysis: Cousins and Crosby got into it Friday with the 37-year-old quarterback taking exception after multiple hits from Crosby. Cousins got in Crosby’s face and grabbed his jersey as the two exchanged words before it was broken up. Both will sit out practice Saturday, but should be back on the field soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maxx-crosb.headline: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said EDGE Maxx Crosby (knee) is ready for the start of training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maxx-crosb.analysis: Crosby underwent meniscus surgery in January after playing through a left knee injury for much of last season. His health and failed physical were infamously the reason for a failed trade with the Ravens, but new Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said the 28-year-old is ready for the start of training camp. He will not have the same limits as he did for the offseason program; Crosby is on track to be a full-go heading into the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maxx-crosb.headline: The California Post’s Vincent Bonsignore reports that the 49ers’ 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second-round pick and EDGE Mykel Williams form the “framework for a suitable offer” in a potential trade for Raiders EDGE Maxx Crosby.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maxx-crosb.analysis: Multiple league sources tell Bonsignore that the Raiders would revisit the idea of trading Crosby away “if the right offer was made.” According to Bonsignore’s sources, the 49ers could make a play for him if they so desire. The Raiders nearly traded Crosby to the Ravens earlier this offseason, but the Ravens cancelled the deal due to concerns over a “degenerative issue” in his knee. Per Bonsignore, if Crosby “returns to terrorizing Raiders’ practices during training camp, he’ll put all concerns to rest,” and “the Raiders will be flooded with calls from interested teams.” The 49ers hope to make a Super Bowl run this season. Adding Crosby to their pass rush makes sense. Williams, the 49ers’ EDGE in reference, is currently recovering from a torn ACL and it is unclear whether he will be able to play in Week 1. At 22 years old, he is more of a long-term option anyway, and the Raiders are currently rebuilding. This framework is interesting and could work well for both sides. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maxx-crosb.headline: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said the goal is to have EDGE Maxx Crosby (knee) “out there for training camp.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maxx-crosb.analysis: Crosby underwent knee surgery at the start of the offseason and has been working his way back since. The Ravens were set to acquire the 28-year-old pass rusher before a failed physical due to concerns with his knee nixed the deal. Crosby is instead back with the Raiders and continuing to rehab after the knee ended his 2025 season early. New head coach Klint Kubiak said the goal is to have Crosby back and healthy by training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maxx-crosb.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams could consider trading for Raiders EDGE Maxx Crosby in October.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maxx-crosb.analysis: Atkins believes the Raiders have mended their relationship with Crosby, and currently plan to keep him, but “the organization’s approach could change if the Raiders hit another tough start to a season.” Per Atkins, the Rams also “want to be one of the rare teams willing to trade from an expectedly loaded 2027 draft class” as they pursue a Super Bowl this year. If the rest of the NFL is set on keeping their 2027 picks, it could give the Rams an opportunity to exploit the market. Many things can change between now and this season’s trade deadline, so this scenario should not be considered likely to happen. If a big, pre-deadline move has been on the Rams’ mind, it could partially explain why they used the 2026 NFL Draft’s No. 13 overall pick on a developmental player, rather than an immediate starter, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maxx-crosb.headline: ESPN’s Ryan McFadden reports the Ravens believed Maxx Crosby had “a degenerative issue” in his knee.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maxx-crosb.analysis: In a lengthy breakdown about how the trade failed to come to fruition, the Ravens ultimately weren’t concerned about Crosby’s 2026 season, but about his “durability after a couple of seasons.” Crosby has said that he’s a “Raider for life” since on his own podcast, but Fowler notes that teams continue to check on Crosby’s availability, that the asking price remains high, and that teams are reluctant to meet it. It is possible that “a window of opportunity opens closer to the draft,” so we’re probably not out of the Crosby trade rumor blurb business just yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maxx-crosb.headline: NFL Network’s Gerald McCoy reports Maxx Crosby said “I’ll be 200 percent ready” by the start of training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maxx-crosb.analysis: Crosby said the world will “get the best version of 98" in 2026 after the Ravens failed him on his physical just days after agreeing to a trade with the Raiders. The star pass-rusher recently declared himself “a Raider” on social media, suggesting he’s hoping to remain with the team this upcoming season, and it’s been reported that the asking price for Crosby hasn’t changed despite the Ravens reneging on the deal. Crosby suffered a knee injury last season that he played through, but he still underwent offseason surgery to repair a torn meniscus. One of the true Iron Men of the league, Crosby is no doubt motivated to prove the Ravens made the wrong move in sending him back to Vegas. He’ll have a sizable chip on his shoulder and a lot to prove if he is ready for training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maxx-crosb.headline: Maxx Crosby declared himself “a Raider” on social media.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maxx-crosb.analysis: Prior reports indicated that Crosby was unwilling to play for the Raiders ever again. He has seemingly changed his mind, telling Raiders fans, “I’m back.” Crosby was nearly traded to the Ravens in exchange for two first-round picks, but the Ravens withdrew from the deal yesterday, citing a failed physical. Earlier today, The Athletic’s Dianna Russini reported that the Raiders’ asking price for Crosby had not changed. Trading away Crosby for draft picks makes sense for a team that is ostensibly beginning a rebuild. Whether the Raiders’ front office has changed its mind about jettisoning him remains unknown. But Crosby, for his part, appears ready to don the Silver and Black once again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maxx-crosb.headline: Ravens GM Eric DeCosta said he wanted to pair Maxx Crosby with Trey Hendrickson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/maxx-crosb.analysis: He added that the team started contract talks with Hendrickson after the team lost center Tyler Linderbaum in free agency. For those out of the loop: Baltimore agreed to trade two first-round picks for Crosby earlier this week, only to back out of the deal at the last minute, citing a failed physical. They then inked Hendrickson to a four-year deal just over 12 hours later. Multiple reports have suggested NFL staffers around the league found the series of moves detestable. Given that Crosby underwent offseason meniscus surgery, DeCosta does have a reasonable alibi for calling off the trade. Now Baltimore will move forward with Hendrickson and their full allotment of first-round selections over the next two drafts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Broncos placed RB RJ Harvey (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Whoa, that escalated quickly. Harvey reportedly suffered a knee injury in practice this week that initially caused the Broncos to rule him out for Week 8, with the team then making the procedural move of placing him on injured reserve Saturday. Harvey will now miss the next four games, at minimum, as he rehabs the injury, leaving rookie Jonah Coleman and veteran J.K. Dobbins to handle primary backfield duties with Tyler Badie also on injured reserve. Coleman warrants weekly FLEX status, at minimum.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey (knee) was ruled out for Week 8 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harvey was added to the injury report Thursday with a knee injury before being unable to practice Friday, ultimately ruled out for the team’s divisional clash against the Chiefs. Expect Jonah Coleman to serve as the primary rusher in addition to the possibility he sees his pass game involvement tick up in the absences of both Harvey and Tyler Badie, the latter of whom is on injured reserve. The increase in opportunity is enough to vault Coleman into viable FLEX territory for Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harvey was added to the injury report Thursday after being limited in practice due to a knee injury, something fantasy managers will want to monitor as the weekend approaches. Either way, Harvey now has two healthy backs to compete with for touches with the return of Jonah Coleman in Week 7, keeping him on the fringes of FLEX consideration entering a difficult matchup against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey caught two passes for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 7 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harvey only ran the ball three times for six yards. Jonah Coleman, who was active for the first time since Week 2, ran nine times and also caught a pair of passes. Harvey’s role took a hit, but he made the most of his limited opportunities with a 52-yard screen in the third quarter. Sean Payton’s play-call schemed half of the Cardinals’ defense out of the play and Harvey blew by the other half on his way to the end zone. Despite the spike week for fantasy managers, Harvey’s declining role will have him tumbling down the running back ranks for Week 8. He will be on the RB3/4 border versus Kansas City next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Broncos designated Jonah Coleman (ankle) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Coleman can return to practice this week and the team now has 21 days to bring him off injured reserve. He could be back on the field as soon as Sunday. With the Broncos’ offense struggling and two backs already seeing work in the backfield, it’s hard to imagine Coleman having much fantasy value in his first game back. He’s worth stashing in deeper leagues, but it might be a while before fantasy managers want him in their lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey rushed six times for 25 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks, adding 31 yards on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The fact that the 31 yards through the air led the team in receiving is a comment on the state of an offense that gained only 168 yards of total offense against the defending Super Bowl Champions. Even so, a relentlessly aggressive defense willed the team to victory behind a consistently positive game script, which allowed J.K. Dobbins to handily lead the backfield in opportunities. Harvey remains a matchup-dependent fantasy option best utilized in trailing game environments, which is unlikely to be the case when the Broncos face the struggling Cardinals in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey picked up seven yards on three carries in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Harvey was a non-factor in this one, and a week after his big receiving game, he was held without a catch with just one target. The second-year tailback was clearly the backup to JK Dobbins, and was unable to make the most of his limited opportunities. He’s off the radar for Week 6 versus the Seahawks on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: JK Dobbins had 11 rushes for 40 yards in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers, adding two catches for 12 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Dobbins, as usual, led the Denver backfield in carries but lost out to RJ Harvey on pass routes and targets. In fact, Harvey led the Broncos with ten catches on ten targets in a check-down heavy game plan for Bo Nix and OC Davis Webb. Dobbins has been touchdown-reliant as the Broncos’ lead back, and sensitive to game script, as we saw in Week 4. Dobbins can be used as a flex next week against a vulnerable Chargers run defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: RJ Harvey had seven rushes for 25 yards in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers, adding ten catches for 68 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Playing against a 49ers defense allowing the league’s highest target share to running backs, Harvey led the Broncos in targets and receptions — thanks in part to negative game script that forced Denver to go pass heavy in the second half. It was a nice little PPR cheat code outing for Harvey, who now has 20 receptions in three games this year. JK Dobbins, meanwhile, led the Denver backfield with 11 rushes in Week 4. Harvey could be a PPR flex play next week against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: J.K. Dobbins (hip) is practicing in full for Week 4 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: RJ Harvey was checked for a concussion in Week 3 and is not on the injury report today, meaning both backs are good to go for Week 4. Dobbins saw 17 carries versus the Rams compared to just two for Harvey, though the latter caught six passes. Dobbins caught one pass. The rushing advantage will keep Dobbins in the RB3 mix for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.headline: Chiefs placed CB L’Jarius Sneed (knee) on inured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.analysis: That was somewhat unexpected. Sneed missed Wednesday’s practice for personal reasons and was limited Thursday and Friday. He was moved to injured reserve a day later. The Chiefs are now down their top two corners after Mansoor Delane was ruled out for Week 8, creating a much softer matchup for the Broncos on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.headline: The Kansas City Star’s Pete Sweeney reports that Chiefs WR Rashee Rice is participating in warmups and play installations, but is not yet participating in team drills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.analysis: The Chiefs are doing the same thing with CB L’Jarius Sneed. There is nothing to be worried about here. Chiefs coach Andy Reid said the team is “just building them up,” which will “take a little bit of time.” Rice is still working on conditioning at this point, but once his cardio is good to go, we should see him practicing fully. He was cleared to practice on July 24th after undergoing an offseason clean-up procedure on his knee. Rice is a WR2 with WR1 upside.
