https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.headline: Chiefs signed CB L’Jarius Sneed, formerly of the Titans, to a one-year, $5 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.analysis: NFL insider Jordan Schultz was first to report the reunion between the Chiefs and Sneed. The veteran corner last played for the Chiefs in 2023 and was traded to the Titans in the 2024 offseason. Over the last two seasons, Sneed has struggled with multiple injuries, limiting him to just 12 games. Sneed, 29, will also reunite with defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo, which could bode well for him as he returns to a familiar environment and a team he helped lead to two Super Bowl titles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.headline: Free agent CB L’Jarius Sneed visited with the Chiefs on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.analysis: Clearly there was no rush to add him to the roster. It’s the first sniff of NFL interest we’ve seen for the former star cornerback since he was released by the Titans, and unsurprisingly it was with his former employers in Kansas City. We suspect this has a chance of happening at some point this offseason, but the 29-year-old Sneed is likely to sift through options ahead of training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the criminal charges against L’Jarius Sneed have been dismissed.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.analysis: Sneed had been “charged with aggravated assault that was reduced by the grand jury to the misdemeanor offense of failure to report the commission of a felony,” according to Schefter. That could clear the way for the mega-bust to sign on with a cornerback-needy team in the coming weeks. Sneed, 29, was released by the Titans in March after signing four-year, $76.4 million deal in 2024 that included $55 million in guaranteed money. He will probably have to settle for a prove-it deal for 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.headline: Titans released CB L’Jarius Sneed.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.analysis: Sneed’s contract will go down as one of the worst in recent memory. The 29-year-old corner joined the Titans in 2024 on a four-year, $76.4 million deal that included $55 million in guaranteed money, and appeared in just 12 games during his two seasons with the team. Knee injuries plagued the majority of Sneed’s time with the Titans, but it was a quad injury that landed him on season-ending IR last October. Sneed was one of the top corners in the league during his time with the Chiefs, but his recent string of injuries begs the question of how much is left in the tank at this stage of his career. If he wants to continue playing, he will likely need to do so on a one-year prove-it deal to show he can stay healthy for a full season while still contributing at a high level.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.headline: Titans placed CB L’Jarius Sneed on injured reserve with a quad injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.analysis: A balky knee has impeded Sneed’s play for much of the year. The 28-year-old perimeter cornerback is currently allowing 17.2 yards per reception, 5.3 more than his prior career-worst average. Adding a quad issue to the mix was only going to make things worse. Sneed will now miss at least four games and will be eligible to return in Week 13. The team’s bye occurs in Week 10. CB Darrell Baker Jr. is listed as his backup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.headline: Titans interim head coach Mike McCoy said DT Jeffery Simmons (hamstring) is considered week to week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.analysis: Cornerback L’Jarius Sneed is expected to miss some time with a quad injury. McCoy didn’t rule out Simmons for Week 8, but it doesn’t sound like he is expected to play this week. Simmons has been one of the few bright spots for the Titans this year with 4.5 sacks and a forced fumble through eight games. The Titans’ defense will continue to struggle in his absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.headline: Titans DC Dennard Wilson said “guys will have to step up” without L’Jarius Sneed (quad) against the Colts in Week 8.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.analysis: Sneed left Week 7’s game against the Patriots and was quickly ruled out. This seems to confirm he has little chance to play this week. Frankly, with how poorly Sneed has been playing in his limited snaps, the Titans could probably use those snaps to evaluate younger players. The Sneed contract has been a boondoggle for Tennessee through two years.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.headline: Titans declared DL Shy Tuttle, CB Jalyn Armour-Davis, S Kevin Winston, CB Samuel Womack, OL Jackson Slater, OL Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, and DL CJ Ravenell inactive for Week 1 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ljarius-sn.analysis: La’Jarius Sneed, struggling with a knee issue, will suit up for the Titans for Cam Ward’s first NFL regular season game. Even with Sneed healthy and active, the Titans defense should struggle to stop Bo Nix and the Denver offense. It could be a running theme in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Chargers placed S Derwin James (hamstring) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: Previous reports indicated the team was considering a stint on injured reserve following an aggravation of his hamstring injury, with Saturday’s transaction confirming those suspicions. James will now miss the coming four games, at minimum, as the Chargers look to reverse course on a sinking season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Derwin James (hamstring) will not play in Week 8 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: James reportedly suffered a setback with his hamstring injury, with the team now considering injured reserve. His absence is a big hit to their defense as a primary interior defender against the heavy personnel sets from the Rams, upgrading the matchup for Tyler Higbee and company.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Derwin James (hamstring) is a candidate for injured reserve after suffering a setback.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: Brutal. This team cannot catch a break. Losing James makes the center of their defense fairly vulnerable. The Chargers’ stalwart safety plays a do-it-all role. If James lands on injured reserve this week, he will be eligible to return for the Chargers’ Week 12 game against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Derwin James (hamstring) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 6 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: That is back-to-back weeks of no James. Donte Jackson (hamstring) was also ruled out. We’re almost through the Chargers blurbs. We think they should just put some people on injured reserve too. Keep reading.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Joe Alt (neck) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: Chargers OG Kayode Awosika (fibula), S Derwin James (hamstring) and CB Donte Jackson (hamstring) also remained sidelined. The Chargers take on the division-rival Chiefs this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Derwin James (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: CB Donte Jackson (hamstring) also did not practice. Neither player played in Week 5 and both will need at least a limited practice before they can be considered questionable for Week 6 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Donte Jackson (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: Derwin James was also held out because of a hamstring injury. He is considered week-to-week. We don’t anticipate him suiting up on Sunday. A DNP for Jackson puts him on the wrong side of questionable as well. LA’s secondary will be an easy target for Bo Nix as he looks to bounce back from a lackluster Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said S Derwin James (hamstring) is “week to week” but not an injured reserve candidate.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: Sounds like we should be counting James out for Week 5’s game against the Broncos, and perhaps Week 6 as well. The safety did not play in Week 4’s loss to the Seahawks, leaving Tarheeb Still as the main slot cornerback with 2026 fourth-rounder Genesis Smith seeing an elevated role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Derwin James (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 4 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: James sandwiched a Thursday absence with two limited sessions. The veteran safety plays through injuries whenever possible, and the Chargers will need all hands on deck to get their season back on track.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.headline: Derwin James said he will play the rest of the season in a cast after suffering a fractured pinky finger in Week 2’s loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/derwin-jam.analysis: James will look to play out the Chargers’ final 15 games of the season with a cast. The Chargers are off to an 0-2 start and will be desperate to turn things around in Week 3 against the 2-0 Bills on the road in Buffalo. The veteran safety has totaled 10 tackles and one pass breakup in the first two games of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Tytus Howard (concussion) cleared protocol and will play in Week 8 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: Howard gains clearance just in time to be charged with slowing an aggressive Pittsburgh pass rush, likely in line to handle his fair share of T.J. Watt on Sunday. There should be no reason for Howard to see a decline in snaps or performance after suffering a concussion in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Tytus Howard (concussion) is questionable for Week 8 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: Howard returned to the practice field Friday after missing both sessions to start the week, keeping the door open for him to clear concussion protocol in time for Sunday’s game against the Steelers. Howard will need to remain asymptomatic and gain clearance from an independent neurologist to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Elgton Jenkins and Jared Verse practiced Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: Both players emerged from their Week 7 win a bit banged up, with their return to practice Thursday a positive development toward an active game-day status. Right tackle Tytus Howard (concussion) remained sidelined, who will have one more opportunity to get on the practice field and remain asymptomatic to have a chance at playing against the Steelers in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Tytus Howard (concussion) is questionable to return in Week 7 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: Howard left the game in the first half with a head injury and had not returned as of the start of the fourth quarter. Losing Howard would be a tough blow for a Cleveland offensive line that has been solid in both run and pass blocking in 2026. Look for Howard to enter the league’s concussion protocol in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Tytus Howard (knee) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: His Wednesday DNP suggested worse, but Howard will try to play through the knee injury that cost him roughly half of Cleveland’s snaps against the Jets last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Tytus Howard (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: It’s good progress after he had a Wednesday DNP. Howard should have a real chance at playing on Sunday as long as his Friday status stays neutral or trends positively.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Tytus Howard (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: The Browns acquired Howard from Houston in the offseason. Howard left Week 5 with the knee issue and a DNP today suggests he will miss at least one week. Dawand Jones took his spot in the lineup on Sunday and would presumably draw the start at right tackle if Howard is out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Browns acquired RT Tytus Howard from the Texans in exchange for a fifth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: This is the first big move the Browns have made to address their offensive line. The acquisition of Howard gives them an experienced right tackle who has started all 16 games he has appeared in for each of the last two seasons, and he has allowed just five sacks on 1,175 pass blocking snaps per TruMedia. Shortly after trading for Howard, the Browns announced they would be signing him to a three-year, $63 million extension, keeping him with the team through the 2029 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Texans G Ed Ingram (knee) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: After missing each of the last two games with a knee injury, Ingram looks likely to go on Thursday night. Ingram has posted back-to-back full practices this week. Tytus Howard (ankle/knee) and Trent Brown (hand/knee) were both limited participants on Monday and Tuesday and also look to be trending towards playing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.headline: Texans OL Ed Ingram (knee) is questionable for Houston’s Week 11 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tytus-howa.analysis: Ingram, one of Nick Caserio’s better OL scrapheap finds this year, missed last week’s game with the injury but had limited practices on Thursday and Friday after a full on Wednesday. Juice Scruggs wound up seeing most of the time at right guard after an ugly debut series from Sidy Sow. Tytus Howard (concussion) cleared protocol and will start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Jets placed NT T’Vondre Sweat (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The vaunted Jets run defense takes a major blow as Sweat is moved to injured reserve. Defensive end David Bailey is also doubtful to play in Week 8, boosting the matchup for Ashton Jeanty on Sunday. Sweat will be sidelined for four games, at minimum, as the Jets struggle to cling to another lost season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: T’Vondre Sweat suffered a knee injury in Week 7 against the Dolphins and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Sweat went down in the second quarter. He walked off the field under his own power but immediately went into the medical tent. The team ruled him out after halftime. Sweat has 15 combined tackles and two TFLs this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Jets acquired DT T’Vondre Sweat from the Titans in exchange for EDGE Jermaine Johnson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: As Schefter notes, the deal won’t become official until the new league year, which starts in a few weeks. Johnson was the subject of trade rumors at the deadline last year, but nothing materialized. He now gets a new home in Tennessee. Sweat, a former second-round pick, had a quiet rookie season with one sack and four TFLs. Despite appearing in five fewer games, Sweat upped his sack total to two in 2025. Pro Football Focus also charted him as a markedly improved player. He ranked fourth in run defense grade and top-20 in pass-rush grade among defensive linemen. Sweat has two more years on his rookie contract.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans activated NT T’Vondre Sweat (ankle) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Sweat makes his return to a roster that has allowed the fourth most fantasy points per game to opposing backfields this season. Sweat has continually graded as a top performer against the run throughout this career, making his return a significant boost to a struggling unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans placed NT T’Vondre Sweat (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Titans will now be without their big man against the run for the next four games, at minimum. Expect Shy Tuttle to fill in in his absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans DT T’Vondre Sweat (ankle) will not play in Week 3’s game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Rejoice, Jonathan Taylor fantasy managers, as Sweat is one of the best young nose tackles in the game. Sweat was a Friday downgrade to not participating, opening up the possibility that he’s had a setback. At the very least, he should be considered extremely questionable for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans OT JC Latham (hip) will not play in Week 2 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Neither will T’Vondre Sweat, who has been sidelined with an ankle injury. Oli Udoh looks to be next in line for snaps at right tackle for Tennessee. It’s a big downgrade for Cam Ward’s protection as the rookie quarterback continues to fight against his supporting cast to produce aesthetically pleasing statistics.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans RB Kalel Mullings (ankle) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: That makes two absences for Mullings this week. If the sixth-round rookie cannot suit up for Week 2, that would leave the Titans with just Tony Pollard and Julius Chestnut as the available running backs on the active roster. Pollard totaled 19 touches against the Broncos last week, with Tyjae Spears (ankle) on injured reserve. He is likely to do so again against a slightly softer Rams defense. Titans OT JC Latham (hip) and DT T’Vondre Sweat (ankle) were also not seen practicing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans OT JC Latham (hip) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Latham aggravated a preseason hip injury in Week 1 against the Broncos. The 22-year-old tackle played 45 snaps before exiting, with Oli Udoh replacing him at right tackle. Latham’s status for Week 2 and the foreseeable future remains in doubt. Also not practicing for the Titans Wednesday were S Quandre Diggs (hand) and DT T’Vondre Sweat (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans DT T’Vondre Sweat (eye) left Week 16 against the Colts and returned.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Sweat was poked in the eye in the first half of the Titans’ Week 16 matchup against the Colts. He left the game and went to the locker room, but returned to the sideline. Sweat returned late in the second quarter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.headline: Cowboys activated S P.J. Locke (plantar fascia) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.analysis: Locke spent the previous five weeks on injured reserve with a plantar fascia issue and is expected to be active for the team’s Week 8 game against the Cardinals. He brings a veteran presence to a defense that struggled mightily to start the season as the Cowboys continue inching closer to full health.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.headline: Cowboys placed S P.J. Locke (plantar fascia) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.analysis: The team had already ruled him out for multiple weeks and will now make the administrative move of sending him to injured reserve. He will first be eligible to return for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.headline: Cowboys HC Brian Schottenheimer said CB Cobie Durant (hamstring) and S P.J. Locke (plantar fascia) will miss “a few weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.analysis: Durant suffered a hamstring strain and Locke suffered a torn plantar fascia in the team’s Week 2 win over the Commanders. Both players are reportedly going to miss multiple weeks, while a stint on injured reserve is not yet being ruled out for either player. In what has become somewhat of a yearly tradition in Dallas, the secondary is suddenly extremely thin on healthy bodies after the team invested significant capital re-tooling the back end this offseason. Expect Markquese Bell and Shavon Revel to enter the starting lineup for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.headline: Cowboys agreed to terms with S P.J. Locke, formerly of the Broncos, on a one-year, $5 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.analysis: After starting all 15 games he appeared in during the 2024 season, Locke made just three starts in 16 games last season, totaling 16 tackles and three pass breakups. The former UDFA became a major contributor for the Broncos in 2023 when he emerged to total 53 tackles, three sacks and five pass. Locke will join former Broncos DB coach Christian Parker in Dallas, and is capable of lining up from multiple spots. Even if he doesn’t earn a “starting” role in Dallas, Locke will likely see plenty of work for the Cowboys next season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.headline: Broncos S P.J. Locke said he underwent spinal fusion surgery after the team’s playoff loss in January.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.analysis: Locke is one of the first NFL players to undergo spinal fusion surgery, sharing his journey in a personal documentary YouTube video. He dealt with the pain from the surgery early on, but says he does not feel pain now. Locke started 15 games and the playoff loss for the Broncos and is a key member of a daunting secondary. The 28-year-old missed offseason workouts due to rehab and is preparing to be ready for the regular season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.headline: Broncos declared S P.J. Locke (thumb), QB Zack Wilson, CB Kris Abrams-Draine, T Alex Palczewski, TE Greg Dulcich, LB Dondrea Tillman and DL Eyioma Uwazurike inactive for Week 8 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.analysis: Locke was considered doubtful for the bout against the Panthers, and will unsurprisingly miss the contest. Wilson will operate as the emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.headline: Broncos S Brandon Jones suffered a hamstring strain at training camp on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.analysis: The training staff has yet to determine the injury’s severity but the Broncos are already in a tough spot at safety. The front office released four-time second-team All-Pro S Justin Simmons this offseason and both S Caden Sterns (patellar tendon) and S Delarrin Turner-Yell (ACL) are currently on the active/physically unable to perform (PUP) list. P.J. Locke is the only active Broncos safety who logged triple-digit defensive snaps last year, though he worryingly earned a 55.2 PFF coverage grade.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.headline: Broncos re-signed S P.J. Locke to a two-year, $9 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.analysis: Locke played sparingly his first three seasons in the league but became one of the standouts of the defense while filling in for the injured Kareem Jackson in 2023. Locke returns to a secondary now devoid of Justin Simmons after the latter’s release, creating the opportunity for Locke to see a significant bump in playing time in the immediate future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.headline: Broncos re-signed QB Brett Rypien, ILB Jonas Griffith, and S P.J. Locke to one-year contracts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.analysis: All three were exclusive rights free agents. Rypien had a four-interception start against the Jets in 2020, but only attempted two passes in 2021 as a backup. He may be in line to be Russell Wilson’s backup in 2022 unless the Broncos sign someone else, as they’ve traded Drew Lock and Teddy Bridgewater is a free agent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.headline: The Athletic’s Dane Brugler projects Texas S P.J. Locke to Round 7 or as an undrafted free agent.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/p-j-locke/.analysis: Locke (5'10/200) entered the draft mix after his senior season, but it’s been a really quiet draft season for the former Longhorn. However, as a senior, Locke racked up an impressive 58 solo tackles with a career-high 5.5 tackles for loss. That level of production is nice to see for a deep sleeper.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Daron Payne suffered a season-ending Jones fracture.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.analysis: Payne suffered the injury during Friday’s practice. A previous report from Ian Rapport stated the 29-year-old defensive tackle suffered a significant foot injury and would be out for the foreseeable future. Payne will be placed on injured reserve as he’s set to miss the rest of the season. He recorded a sack, a forced fumble and 14 tackles in six games with the Commanders this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Daron Payne suffered a “significant foot injury” in practice Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.analysis: Rapoport adds that the injury is likely to sideline the standout defensive tackle “for the foreseeable future,” with a stint on injured reserve appearing likely. The Commanders continue to be dealt significant injuries, this time on the defensive side of the ball, as they fight to remain in contention in a fragile NFC East division. The team will know more about the extent of the injury when Payne undergoes further testing Saturday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.headline: Commanders EDGE Odafe Oweh (calf) will play in Week 1 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.analysis: The Commanders will also have Daron Payne (knee) and K’Lavon Chaisson (knee) on the field for Sunday when they travel to Philly to take on the Eagles. Washington made several defensive additions this offseason in hopes of improving a unit that ranked among the league’s worst last season in its second year under Dan Quinn.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.headline: Commanders RB Chris Rodriguez Jr. (illness) is inactive for Week 17 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.analysis: Rodriguez was a late add to the injury report with an illness and is now officially inactive for the Commanders’ Christmas afternoon game against the Cowboys. Jacory Croskey-Merrit is an RB3 with Rodriguez out. The Commanders also declared QB Jayden Daniels, QB Marcus Mariota, QB Sam Hartman, LT Laremy Tunsil, LB Nick Bellore, and DT Daron Payne out against the Cowboys. Payne did not practice all week with a back issue. Jeff Driskel is Josh Johnson’s backup while Sam Hartman is the emergency third quarterback for Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.headline: Commanders DT Daron Payne has been suspended for one game after punching Amon-Ra St. Brown in Week 10’s loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.analysis: Payne could appeal this, but the tape doesn’t exactly work in his favor. Payne took a blatant, cheap shot at St. Brown during the second quarter of Sunday’s game and was immediately ejected for his actions. Assuming this holds up, which it should, Payne will miss Week 11’s game against the Dolphins in Spain and will be eligible to return in Week 13 after the Commanders’ bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.headline: Commanders DT Daron Payne was ejected from Week 10 against the Lions after committing an unnecessary roughness penalty.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.analysis: Payne was flagged after a hard-fought 13-yard touchdown run made by Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs. Payne can be clearly seen punching Lions WR Amon-Ra St. Brown on the left side of his facemask. Astonishingly, Commanders DT Javon Kinlaw was not ejected after striking a referee in the forehead, though he was penalized, after Payne was ejected. The Commanders also may have lost CB Trey Amos, who entered the game with a hip injury, and required two trainers’ assistance to leave the field after injuring his ankle on the play. Amos is currently questionable to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.headline: Commanders ruled out DT Daron Payne (knee/finger) for the NFC Championship game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.analysis: Payne came into the weekend listed as questionable but will ultimately miss the team’s NFC Championship game against the Eagles. The Commanders have struggled mightily against the run and will now be without one of their top run defenders on the interior of their defensive line. That could spell trouble against Saquon Barkley and Jalen Hurts after the two ran wild in both of these teams’ previous meetings this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.headline: Commanders DT Daron Payne (knee/finger) is questionable for the NFC Championship Game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.analysis: Linebacker Bobby Wagner was removed from the report and will play. Payne did not practice at all this week, putting him on the wrong side of questionable heading into the weekend. However, with a Super Bowl berth on the line, he will be doing everything in his power to get on the field. Payne has four sacks and five TFLs this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.headline: Daron Payne (knee/finger) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.analysis: Payne suffered his finger injury in the team’s wild card win over the Buccaneers. He was limited in two of three practices last week but appears to have picked up a knee injury in the divisional round win over the Lions. Back-to-back DNPs to open the week is a concerning sign for Payne’s availability, but the team could be exercising caution for their star tackle. We’ll see where things stand come Friday when the Commanders release their final injury report before the weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.headline: Commanders DT Daron Payne is questionable to return to the wild card game against the Bucs with a finger injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daron-payn.analysis: This is a big blow for the Commanders. The 320-pound defensive tackle has 42 tackles, four sacks, and five tackles for a loss on the season while soaking up attention from blockers in the middle of the defensive line. Payne injured his finger early in the second quarter of the game and seemed to be in immense pain on the sideline. It would be a huge boost for the Tampa Bay running game if Payne can’t come back in.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.headline: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports Giants HC John Harbaugh called Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk about trading for DT Jeffery Simmons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.analysis: With Giants GM Joe Schoen stonewalled, Harbaugh broke with traditional NFL trade-talk norms and called the Titans owner himself. Unfortunately for the Giants, the message was the same, that Simmons was off limits in trade talks. Previous reporting from Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer stated that Bears GM Ryan Poles’ long-standing relationship with Titans GM Mike Borgonzi played a huge role in Simmons ending up in Chicago. Poles and Borgonzi first met in 2007 when Poles was a guard at Boston College and Borgonzi was a recruiting assistant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.headline: Connor Hughes reports Giants head coach John Harbaugh is expected “to be aggressive in targeting ex-Ravens in free agency.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.analysis: After coaching the Ravens for 18 years, it’s no surprise Harbaugh would try to get the band back together in New York. That could include C Tyler Linderbaum, who played under Harbaugh in Baltimore from 2022 to 2025. Linderbaum, 26, is an unrestricted free agent this offseason and a potential upgrade for a Giants offensive line that struggled throughout 2025. Harbaugh could also pursue Patrick Ricard and Isaiah Likely in free agency. Harbaugh could also bring in coaches he had during his time in Baltimore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.headline: The Athletic’s Ian O’Connor reports that John Harbaugh “needed it in writing that he would report to John Mara, and not to [GM Joe] Schoen.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.analysis: “This wasn’t about Schoen; the coach definitely feels he can work with the GM. Harbaugh wanted the ability to impact the entire operation, from security to training to analytics to media relations to staff size to assistant salaries to relocation expenses to you name it. And yes, in the unlikely event there’s a stalemate on draft day between Harbaugh and Schoen, there’s no longer any question who will prevail,” O’Connor writes. Well then. Joe Schoen begins the Harbaugh Era as a convenient scapegoat the second it takes more than a year to get things going in the right direction. What could go wrong for him?

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.headline: Giants signed former Ravens HC John Harbaugh to a five-year contract to be their next head coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.analysis: And... it’s done. After numerous delays amidst contract minutiae, the two sides have agreed on a five-year contract to make Harbaugh the team’s next head coach. The former Ravens head coach was one of the longest tenured head coaches in the league before being fired last week, quickly landing on his feet with one of the more desirable head coaching vacancies in the league. He’ll be tasked with turning around a franchise that has had little success in the post-Eli era.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.headline: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan speculates the holdup with John Harbaugh’s five-year contract to be the Giants next head coach involves the organization’s chain of command.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.analysis: Duggan reports that while Harbaugh coached the Ravens for 18 seasons, the 63-year-old head coach reported directly to owner Steve Biscotti and not the general manager. While that has not been the Giants’ chain of command historically, it appears Harbaugh prefers that same setup rather than reporting to Giants GM Joe Schoen. Harbaugh is the first major domino to fall in this offseason’s coaching carousel, which gives the Giants some options if this deal were to fall through, though that’s not seen as likely at this point. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the negotiations are heading in the right direction, according to a source, and the Giants hope to introduce Harbaugh at a press conference on Tuesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.headline: The Giants are still expected to sign former Ravens head coach John Harbaugh to a five-year contract to be their next head coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.analysis: Over the last few hours, multiple reports have indicated that the two sides are still expected to come to an agreement. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said it “seems like something was lost in translation” during early negotiations, specifically regarding the “reporting structure” and decision-making powers. He adds that the Titans are still “interested and waiting” to find out what happens, while noting that former Browns head coach Kevin Stefanski could be “the one” for the Giants if things fall through with Harbaugh.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Giants are finalizing a five-year contract with John Harbaugh to be their next head coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.analysis: Per Rapoport, the Giants will spend the morning hammering out the details, but Harbaugh has accepted the job. We should get confirmation on the deal later today. He will become one of the league’s highest-paid coaches once the ink is dry. Things have been moving in this direction for a while. Harbaugh visited the Giants’ facility yesterday, met with the New York brass, and even talked with Jaxson Dart in person. There were reports that he would meet with the Titans today, but those plans have likely been called off. The Giants have won more than eight games just twice in the past 13 seasons. Harbaugh, on the other hand, never won fewer than eight games during his 18-year run as the team’s head coach. He will bring an unmatched floor and cultural shift to the organization. The question now will be what kind of ceiling he can achieve. That was ultimately his issue at the end of his Baltimore days, and it will be the determining factor in whether or not his Giants tenure is a success.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Giants are expected to hire John Harbaugh as their next head coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.analysis: That’s “barring setbacks.” Things have been trending this way for the past few days, though the Titans and Falcons were still hoping to make a race of it. The Giants have the quarterback and the seeming pure desperation to put them over the top in the fight for Harbaugh’s services. We would expect official word to arrive some time on Thursday, likely early in the day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.headline: The Athletic’s Dianna Russini reports the Titans interview former Ravens head coach John Harbaugh on Thursday for their head coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.analysis: The Giants reportedly made a “massive push” to get Harbaugh to sign with them today. Of note, Harbaugh met with the Giants at their facility, toured the grounds, and even met with Jaxson Dart today. The Titans, on the other hand, are meeting him at his home. While it does seem like the Giants are in pole position to land the cycle’s hottest name, Harbaugh is still going to talk to the Titans. He will likely meet with Atlanta before making a decision as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.headline: SNY’s Connor Hughes reports the Giants are making a “massive push” to sign John Harbaugh for their head coaching vacancy today.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/john-harba.analysis: Harbaugh is currently in New York, meeting with Giants ownership, and they clearly don’t want him walking out of the building without a deal. Per Hughes, “They’re willing to not only pay him, but also whatever his staff wants.” A blank check plus a roster with the quarterback position already figuired out will be hard to turn down. Harbaugh, however, is also being pursued by the Titans and Falcons. Neither job looks as enticing on paper, but it would make sense for him to hear them out, even if that is just to drive up his asking price for the Giants.
